title: download: conflates binary upgrades with destructive repo regeneration — upgrade block unreachable on its own
description:
## Context

Discovered 2026-08-01 while updating binaries on `zig` (the Mac) after a 723-commit pull.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cd ~/azigler/dotfiles`
2. Run `./download.sh cursor` on a machine with FEWER Cursor extensions than the tracked
   list — observe `cursor/install_extensions.sh` shrinks, silently, and no upgrade runs.
3. Run `./download.sh` with no argument — observe it DOES run the binary upgrades, but also
   re-runs every destructive case from step 2.
4. There is no third invocation that does the upgrades alone.

## The defect (two parts)

**1. The upgrade block is unreachable on its own.**

`download.sh` with NO argument runs the binary upgrades (brew / rustup / bun / deno /
pnpm / claude / uv) AND THEN loops `for dir in */ .*/` running every `download()` case.
`download.sh <arg>` runs ONLY that case and skips the upgrades entirely. You either get
both or neither.

**2. Several of those cases are lossy writes against TRACKED files.**

- `cursor` / `vscode` — regenerate the tracked `install_extensions.sh` from whatever is
  installed ON THE CURRENT BOX. Running on a machine with a subset of extensions silently
  DELETES entries from the canonical list. The worst one: a silent, lossy,
  machine-dependent overwrite of shared state.
- `fonts` — re-downloads and extracts the Nerd Font tarball into tracked `fonts/`.
- `gnupg` / `ssh` — write `$(hostname -s).asc` / `.pub` into the repo. Public keys, not
  secrets, but repo churn on a PUBLIC repo.
- `zsh` / `tmux` / `blightmud` — `rm -rf` + re-clone. All gitignored, so harmless to git,
  but destroys live oh-my-zsh / antigen / tpm installs.

## Also stale

Last touched 2026-01-25 (`93cff5e`); `sync.sh` is 2026-07-27. It upgrades none of the
tooling added since: `br`, `bv`, biome, ruff, golangci-lint, gitleaks, goose, cursor,
nix / nix-direnv, oh-my-zsh, or the bun/npm globals.

## Resolution direction

Zig, 2026-08-01: move the upgrade block OUT into `mac.upgrade.sh`, leaving `download.sh` as
a pure vendor/fetch script. Consider also making the vendor cases opt-in rather than swept
by the bare `for dir` loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `download.sh` no longer performs binary upgrades
- [ ] the cursor/vscode extension-list regeneration is removed, made additive, or gated
      behind an explicit flag — a subset machine must not be able to silently shrink the
      tracked list
- [ ] README / CLAUDE.md reflect the new split
delete_reason: wrong prefix — created before .beads/config.yaml issue_prefix was uncommented; recreated as dotfiles-*

title: pulse-stall-reconcile reads the TIMER's LastTrigger, not whether the SERVICE ran — 'enable --now' manufactures phantom stall rows
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Re-arm a pulse timer: `systemctl --user enable --now pulse-autonoveld-mail.timer`
2. Wait for pulse-stall.timer (every 10m).
3. A `{"outcome":"stalled","reconciled":true}` row is appended for every row on that
   timer -- for a fire that never happened.

Live instance, 2026-08-01: re-arming autonoveld's four timers at 19:05:30 produced
FOUR phantom stall rows at 21:13:59, all carrying `"fire_ts":"2026-08-01T19:05:30Z"`.
Zig saw them and asked why "all my autonoveld pulses today stalled."

## Root cause
`_last_trigger()` reads `systemctl show <unit>.timer -p LastTriggerUSec`. **`enable
--now` STARTS THE TIMER UNIT and stamps LastTriggerUSec, without ever running the
service.** The discriminator the script never checks:

  pulse-autonoveld-mail.timer   LastTriggerUSec      = Sat 2026-08-01 19:05:30 UTC
  pulse-autonoveld-mail.service ExecMainStartTimestamp = <EMPTY -- never ran>

## The worse half: the note ASSERTS THREE THINGS IT NEVER CHECKED
Verbatim from the emitted row:
  "STALLED -- {timer}.timer fired at {fire} and pulse-inject REPORTED THE TICK
   INJECTED, but no ledger row landed in the {waited}m since. The tick DID NOT BOUNCE
   (it was typed into a ready window) and DID NOT BLOCK (nothing chose to park on
   Andrew) -- it started and died without reporting."
The script reads LastTriggerUSec and the ledger. It never reads an inject marker,
never checks for a bounce, never checks for a block. All three clauses are invented.

This is the SAME DEFECT CLASS as the open dotfiles-kel5 ("pulse-dispatch-remote: the
preflight block message asserts a cause it never checked") and belongs to the
dotfiles-cxle class (the consumer reports something the step never established).
Second confirmed instance in the same subsystem.

## Why it matters beyond four bad rows
- It fires on EVERY timer re-arm, install, or rename -- exactly the moments an
  operator is already unsure whether a loop is healthy.
- harnessd renders `stalled`, so the dashboard shows a red loop that is actually fine.
- It teaches the operator to distrust `stalled`, which is the one row that should
  always be believed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Treat a fire as real only if the SERVICE ran: compare the .service's
      ExecMainStartTimestamp against the .timer's LastTriggerUSec. Empty, or older
      than the trigger, means the timer was activated but nothing executed -> NOT a stall.
- [ ] Rewrite the note so every clause is something the script actually established.
      If it did not read an inject marker, it must not claim one. Prefer naming what
      was checked ("no ledger row since <ts>; service start not observed").
- [ ] Regression test: simulate `enable --now` (timer stamped, service never run) and
      assert ZERO stall rows; simulate a real fire with no ledger row and assert
      exactly ONE. The second case must FAIL before the fix -- a green suite proves
      nothing (repo rule 1).
- [ ] Consider retracting the 4 phantom rows of 2026-08-01, or leaving them with a
      follow-up note -- they are historical record either way.
close_reason: FIXED (both halves), commits 9064c81 + cc5b8c7. (1) A timer TRIGGER is not a FIRE: gate on the .service's ExecMainStartTimestamp — 'enable --now' stamps LastTriggerUSec without running the service. (2) The start must BELONG to that trigger: a 15-min attribution window, because a manual 'systemctl start' hours later was blamed on the stale stamp — which happened minutes after shipping half (1). Note rewritten so every clause is established and it names what it did NOT check. Suite test-pulse-stall-reconcile.sh, 7 cases incl. an over-correction guard; mutants killed both ways.

title: consul: session-only one-shot cron fired 3h56m late (09:47Z -> 13:43Z) — REPL-idle gating can starve a time-critical gate
description:
## Context
2026-08-10, consul session c417e95a (demesne). The qwq9 post-drain gate was re-armed as a CronCreate one-shot for 09:47Z. It fired at 13:43Z — 3h56m late. CronCreate docs say jobs fire only while the REPL is idle; the session's last turn ended ~05:0x, yet the fire slipped ~4h. The dotfiles peer independently observed 'your 02:47 PT cron gate never fired — it couldn't while you were blocked on the question', suggesting an open AskUserQuestion (or other input-pending state) suppresses firing for the whole window it is open.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In an interactive session, CronCreate a one-shot for T+few hours.
2. End the turn via AskUserQuestion (or leave any input-pending state), with the answer arriving before T.
3. Observe fire time vs T: expected within jitter of T; observed ~4h late on 2026-08-10 (armed 09:47Z, fired 13:43Z).

## Why it matters
Seat gates are time-critical by design (post-drain merges, timer re-arms). A gate that silently slips hours degrades to 'on wake, if later' every time — that fallback clause in the handoff note was load-bearing today.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Measured: which session states suppress session-cron firing (idle, open AskUserQuestion, mid-turn), with a reproduced timeline
- [ ] Standing guidance recorded (AGENTS.md or the relevant skill): time-critical gates use transient systemd timer -> pulse-inject (works-gate pattern); session crons only for best-effort nudges
- [ ] The qwq9-gate instance cross-referenced as the motivating case

## Write target
~/demesne — refs/probes/ (client CronCreate behavior probe + documented finding; may end as a vendor-behavior note only).

title: model: wake-time settings-vs-COMMITTED-default divergence alarm (SessionStart, alarm-never-convert)
description:
## Context
dotfiles-cpqi AC5, deliberately NOT implemented in that wave: session-start.sh is shared
infra with its own blast radius, and the cpqi fix (the seat-aware expectation in
post-tool-model-guard.sh) already removes the cascade. What it does NOT do is notice the
flip: the shared `model` key can sit wrong for hours with every seat happily on its pin
and nothing saying so. On 2026-08-10 it stood ~15 minutes and was caught only because a
guard mis-fired at a consul that went and checked the roster by hand.

## The design constraint that kills the obvious version
"Alarm when settings.json disagrees with MY SEAT PIN" is WRONG and must not be built.
seats.yml is default-up/pin-down: `dive` and `autonoveld` pin opus, `digestd`/`az3`/
`hevyd`/`picod`/`tinker` pin sonnet, while the machine default is fable. So that comparison
is TRUE on roughly a third of the seats at all times, forever — a wake banner that cries
wolf on every one of them gets ignored within a day, which is the failure mode dotfiles-lstn
already paid for once (see the settings-drift alarm's once-per-session design).

The comparison that CARRIES SIGNAL is the key against ITS OWN COMMITTED VALUE:

    git -C ~/demesne show HEAD:claude/settings.json | jq -r .model     # the intended default
    jq -r .model "$(readlink -f ~/.claude/settings.json)"              # what is live now

A difference there means the key was PERSISTED BY A CLIENT ACTION (a /model, or an accepted
limit-degrade dialog) rather than by a reviewed commit — precisely the cpqi/lstn shape, and
exactly the check the consul performed by hand to conclude "uncommitted client dirt".

## Task
Add that check to agents/hooks/session-start.sh, after the seat-identity block (which
already resolves the seat and pays that cost once per wake). ALARM ONLY:
- print a wake banner naming BOTH values, the resolved real path (never a hardcoded repo
  path — ~/.claude/settings.json has pointed at two different repos on this box), and the
  sentence "do NOT /model to it — that re-persists the flip machine-wide (dotfiles-cpqi)"
- one ledger row (reuse the model-guard ledger's `settings-drift` conventions)
- NEVER write settings.json, never emit a /model instruction, never exit non-zero
- fail open on every unresolvable input: no repo, no git, no jq, a dirty tree, a detached
  HEAD, no ~/.agents. A wake hook that dies takes every session on the machine with it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Divergence between live and HEAD's `model` value alarms at wake, once, with both values
- [ ] A seat whose PIN differs from the machine default (opus/sonnet seats) does NOT alarm —
      the false-positive case above, asserted explicitly
- [ ] Every fail-open path is a case (no repo / no jq / no settings file), all silent exit 0
- [ ] Nothing in the change can write settings.json or emit a /model instruction
- [ ] Cases in agents/hooks/test/test-session-start-*.sh, made-to-fail proven

title: vps-repo-refresh: 'oob-exclude' manifest directive kills every refresh, so no receipt is written and every remote dispatch blocks
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 while verifying dotfiles-wv2a (the step-1 tunnel adopt fix) with
a live --dry-run against marketing-vps. The tunnel fix works, and the dispatch
then blocks one step later on THIS, which is a separate and equally silent
tick-killer.

`oob-exclude` was added to vps-repo-manifest.txt on 2026-07-28 (bead
dotfiles-f5tg) and taught to pulse-dispatch-remote.sh's manifest reader. It was
NEVER taught to vps-repo-refresh.sh, whose parser is strict:

    *) die "manifest: unknown directive '$kind' in $MANIFEST" 65 ;;

So the refresh dies with exit 65 on the box, writes NO receipt, and vps-preflight
then blocks fail-closed ("no receipt ... the checkout is UNVERIFIED"). That is
every remote pulse dispatch, every row, since 2026-07-28. Measured: the box's
last receipt was 81593s (~22.6h) old.

Note the sibling directive `require-oob-untracked` IS handled there, with a
comment saying exactly why ("so an unknown-directive death cannot take the whole
refresh down") — the same reasoning applies to `oob-exclude` and was simply
missed. This is the "a refactor propagates to ALL surfaces" lesson again: the
manifest has THREE readers, not two.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. ssh marketing-vps 'bash -lc "~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh --self-update"'
2. Observed: `REFRESH-FAIL: manifest: unknown directive 'oob-exclude' in
   /home/andrew/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/vps-repo-manifest.txt 65`
3. Any dispatch then blocks: PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=failed-preflight (73).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] vps-repo-refresh.sh accepts `oob-exclude` (a no-op there — the exclusion is
      meaningful only to pulse-dispatch-remote.sh's complement enumeration).
- [ ] A test asserts that an unknown-to-the-refresh but known-to-the-dispatcher
      directive does not kill the refresh; the shape of this bug recurs.
- [ ] A live `vps-repo-refresh.sh --self-update` on the box writes a receipt.
- [ ] Consider whether the strict `die` on unknown directives is right at all for
      a script that is only one of three readers of a shared manifest.
close_reason: done

title: brew: outdated returns clean rc=0 while tap-sourced formulae are invisible — yabai and skhd are frozen behind an untapped tap
description:
## Context

`brew outdated` on `zig` returns **no output and rc=0** — which reads as "everything is
current". It is not. Formulae installed from a third-party tap that is no longer tapped are
**excluded from the check entirely**, with no warning.

Measured 2026-08-01, immediately after a successful `brew upgrade` of 40 formulae:

```
$ brew outdated ; echo rc=$?
rc=0                          # looks clean

$ brew tap
asmvik/formulae
dicklesworthstone/tap
felixkratz/formulae
homebrew/services
nanobot-ai/tap                # koekeishiya/formulae is NOT here

$ brew list --versions yabai skhd
yabai 7.1.16
skhd 0.3.9                    # both installed FROM koekeishiya/formulae

$ brew outdated --verbose koekeishiya/formulae/yabai
Error: No available formula or cask with the name "koekeishiya/formulae/yabai".
This command requires the tap koekeishiya/formulae.
```

So yabai and skhd are installed, running, and **permanently frozen** — brew cannot see a
new version and will never report one.

## Why this matters beyond two formulae

It breaks the assumption every upgrade script makes. `mac.upgrade.sh` (new, `85000d4`) and
any human running `brew upgrade` will conclude the box is current when tap-sourced tools
are silently pinned. It is the `dotfiles-cxle` class again: **the consumer reports success
while the step stopped working.** A clean `brew outdated` is not evidence.

`mac.upgrade.sh` already gained a `--trust-taps` flag from the same investigation; this bead
is the residual — the tap is missing entirely, so trusting is not enough, it must be
re-tapped.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the four commands in the Context block on any Mac whose taps have drifted from what
`mac.setup.sh` installed.

## Fix direction

- Re-tap `koekeishiya/formulae`, confirm `brew outdated` then sees yabai/skhd, upgrade them
  deliberately (both are running window-manager services — expect a restart).
- Have `mac.upgrade.sh` **verify the taps its formulae came from are present** and fail
  loudly if not, rather than inheriting a false-clean `brew outdated`.
- `mac.setup.sh` should tap explicitly rather than relying on `brew install user/tap/formula`
  leaving the tap behind.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `koekeishiya/formulae` re-tapped; `brew outdated` visibly reports yabai/skhd status
- [ ] yabai + skhd upgraded, or their current pin recorded as deliberate
- [ ] `mac.upgrade.sh` fails loudly when a formula's originating tap is absent
- [ ] a check exists that distinguishes "nothing outdated" from "nothing was examined"

title: gdoc: the proxy read-back prints a markdown length as if it were a char count
description:
## Context
Found while fixing dotfiles-aoyz (2026-08-04), verified live against the proxy but deliberately NOT fixed there, to keep that fix to one thing.

`render_styled_blocks.mjs` ends every run with:

    warn(`verified: sent ${text.length} chars, read back ${back}`)

On the **direct** transport those two numbers are comparable and now agree (21,843 sent vs 21,844 read back, the difference being the implicit trailing newline). On the **proxy** transport `readBackChars` returns `data.markdown.length` from `GET /api/gdoc/docs/:docId`, which is the length of a MARKDOWN RENDERING, not of the inserted text. Measured: 226 against 211 sent / 212 actual.

So the line reads as a comparison and is not one. It is only ever consumed as `if (!back) fail(...)`, a zero/non-zero liveness check, which is legitimate. The defect is purely that the printed number invites a comparison that is meaningless on that path, and a reader diffing 211 against 226 would go hunting for a truncation that is not there.

The proxy response already carries a truer `chars` field.

## Fix options
Either use `data.chars` when present, or label the number for what it is (`read back N chars of markdown`) so nobody diffs the two. Do not make the guard stricter than zero/non-zero on that path without checking what `chars` actually counts.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Render any spec with `GDOC_TRANSPORT=proxy`.
2. Compare the two numbers in the `verified:` line. They differ by the markdown syntax overhead and always will.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The proxy path's `verified:` line either compares comparable numbers or names the unit it is reporting
- [ ] The zero/non-zero liveness guard still fires on a genuinely empty proxy render
close_reason:
Fixed by LABELLING, not by swapping the number. readBackChars -> readBack, returning { n, unit }; the proof line prints the unit.

The bead's first suggested option (use data.chars) is WRONG and I only know because I measured it before implementing: against a 21,843-char insert the proxy's markdown length is 22,832 and its own chars field is 22,945, so chars is not the segment length either. Swapping it in would have traded one incomparable number for another while looking like a fix. The measurement is recorded in the transport comment so the next reader does not retry it.

Direct now returns { n, unit: 'chars' } (exactly comparable to the insert, +1 for Docs' implicit trailing newline). Proxy returns { n, unit: 'chars of markdown' } with a comment saying why not chars. Zero/non-zero liveness semantics unchanged, which is all this proof needs.

Both transports EXERCISED, not reasoned about:
  direct: verified: sent 21843 chars, read back 21844 chars
  proxy : verified: sent 21843 chars, read back 22896 chars of markdown
Both fired clear (segment end index=21845). Target doc still 22,325 chars with its title appearing exactly once after three re-renders, so no duplication. node --check clean, 8/8 doc_content tests still pass, no readBackChars identifier remains.

dotfiles-gklx fixed in the same commit 0f522d4.

title: pulse-inject.sh note() append is not concurrency-safe — two timers firing the same second interleave the log
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while re-verifying the warm-session claim (explore-qd0l).

Nine pulse ticks APPEARED lost — fired with no corresponding row. All nine were hand-verified as having injected correctly and warm. The apparent loss is a log-interleaving artifact: `pulse-inject.sh`'s `note()` append is not concurrency-safe, so when two timers fire in the same second their lines interleave and a tick's record is mangled into unreadability.

This matters beyond tidiness: "fired but no row" is EXACTLY the condition the stale-loop detector (harnessd-h14z, just un-silenced) alerts on. An unsafe append therefore manufactures false stale-loop alerts, and false alerts are how a just-restored detector gets ignored and re-silenced.

## Steps to Reproduce

Arrange two pulse timers to fire in the same second and inspect the resulting note lines.

## Design

Make the append atomic — `flock` on the note file, or write via a single `printf` under O_APPEND with a line-sized write, and stagger the timer minutes so same-second fires are rare (the scheduler already avoids :00/:30 for a related reason).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Concurrent note() appends from two processes never interleave within a line
- A regression test drives two concurrent writers and asserts every line parses
- Timer schedules are checked for same-second collisions
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent note() appends from two processes never interleave within a record; a regression test drives two concurrent writers against the SHIPPED note() and asserts every record is correctly attributed; timer schedules checked for same-second collisions.
close_reason: done

title: worktrees: a plain 'merge=union' line is re-added in every agent worktree, overriding jsonl-union
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-26 while orchestrating four parallel worktree subagents in
`~/autonoveld`. Every one of the four worktrees had independently committed:

    :wrench: config: add gitattributes for JSONL merge

adding a second line to `.gitattributes`:

    .beads/*.jsonl merge=jsonl-union     <- the repo's committed line
    .beads/*.jsonl merge=union           <- added in the worktree

`session-start.sh` is NOT the culprit — the installed copy is the fixed one
(it strips legacy union, appends jsonl-union, and skips in worktrees), and its
commit message is different (":wrench: config: jsonl-union merge driver for
.beads JSONL (dedupe by ID, keep newer)"). The observed message matches a much
older form last seen in March 2026 debug logs, so the writer is something else
in the worktree-creation path — likely the harness's own native worktree setup
rather than a dotfiles hook. Identifying the writer is part of this bead.

## Steps to Reproduce

Empirical, in a scratch repo — this is the whole bug in four lines:

    git init -q . && mkdir -p .beads
    printf '.beads/*.jsonl merge=jsonl-union\n.beads/*.jsonl merge=union\n' > .gitattributes
    git check-attr merge -- .beads/issues.jsonl
    # => .beads/issues.jsonl: merge: union

Reverse the two lines and it resolves to `jsonl-union`. **Last match wins**, and
the added line always sorts last because it is appended.

To see it live: dispatch any worktree subagent and run
`git -C .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> show HEAD:.gitattributes`.

## Why this matters

This is the exact resurrection bug `lin-eqh` fixed on 2026-06-10, reintroduced.
`session-start.sh` even documents the mechanism in its own comments:

> The previous setup — git's BUILT-IN `merge=union` — was the resurrection bug
> itself: union keeps BOTH sides' lines on conflict, so a stale "open" line from
> a worktree branch survives next to main's "closed" line and br's auto-import
> can flip the bead back open. Any plain union line is therefore REMOVED (it also
> overrides jsonl-union when it sorts later, since last gitattributes match wins).

The hook strips the line in the main worktree and deliberately skips worktrees —
but something re-adds it *in* the worktree and commits it, so the harmful line
rides the merge back into the project. The fix's own stated failure mode is
restored, and nothing reports it: the bead store just quietly grows duplicate
ids and resurrected-open beads after a conflicting merge.

Every project on this box that uses `isolation: "worktree"` is affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Identify what writes the `merge=union` line inside agent worktrees
- [ ] Stop it, or strip the line on the worktree side before the agent's first
      commit, so a merge can never carry it back
- [ ] A test asserts `git check-attr merge -- .beads/issues.jsonl` resolves to
      `jsonl-union` inside a freshly created agent worktree — not merely that the
      jsonl-union line is present, which is what makes this invisible today
- [ ] **Negative control:** append the union line, watch that test fail
- [ ] Audit existing repos for the line already merged into a default branch
      (`git grep -n 'merge=union' $(ls -d ~/*/ ) -- .gitattributes`) and strip it
- [ ] `/orchestrator`'s merge checklist mentions it until the root cause is fixed

## Workaround in use

The autonoveld orchestrator strips the line during each wave-1 merge.

## See also
- `lin-eqh` — the original fix this silently undoes
- `agents/hooks/session-start.sh` lines 273-331 — the correct handling, and the
  comment block that predicted this exact failure
notes:
DIAGNOSED AND FIXED 2026-07-27 (autonoveld a69be6b). The writer is identified,
and this bead's two central hypotheses were both WRONG — worth recording, since
they are what kept it open.

THE WRITER: `~/autonoveld/hooks/session-start.sh:34-37`, a PROJECT-LOCAL
SessionStart hook dated 2026-03-27:

    if [ -d ".beads" ] && ! grep -q 'merge=union' .gitattributes 2>/dev/null; then
      echo '.beads/*.jsonl merge=union' >> .gitattributes
      git add .gitattributes && git commit -q -m ":wrench: config: add gitattributes for JSONL merge" 2>/dev/null
    fi

That is the exact observed commit message, which this bead correctly dated to a
"much older form last seen in March 2026" — the vintage was right, the location
was not.

CORRECTION 1 — it is NOT the harness's native worktree setup. This bead said
"likely the harness's own native worktree setup rather than a dotfiles hook".
There is no WorktreeCreate hook configured in settings.json, and the global
`~/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` is the FIXED implementation (strips plain
union, appends jsonl-union, skips worktrees, commits with a different message,
logs failures). Neither was ever the writer.

CORRECTION 2 — it is NOT fleet-wide. This bead said "Every project on this box
that uses isolation: worktree is affected." Checked: `~/*/hooks/session-start.sh`
exists in exactly ONE project, autonoveld. That over-scoping is probably why the
bead sat at P1 unfixed — it framed the fix as a risky fleet-wide change when it
was a five-line deletion in one repo.

WHY IT SURVIVED SIX CONSECUTIVE WORKTREES — three faults stacked:

1. The guard cannot fire. `grep -q 'merge=union'` does NOT match
   `merge=jsonl-union` (that substring is not present), so the "already
   configured?" test was false forever and the line was appended EVERY session.
2. Last-match-wins means the appended line OVERRODE the committed jsonl-union
   line — the resurrection bug lin-eqh fixed, reintroduced by a hook whose
   comment claimed to prevent it.
3. It COMMITTED its own write, under `2>/dev/null`. So `git status` stayed
   clean, nothing was ever dirty to notice, and the only signal was
   autonoveld's own `tests/test_gitattributes.py` going red inside a worktree.

THE FIX: the block is DELETED (not repaired) — the global hook already owns the
merge driver, so this was duplicated fleet capability in its broken original
form. A comment stands in its place saying why. Added
`test_no_project_hook_writes_a_gitattributes_merge_line`, which greps the
project's hooks for the WRITER rather than asserting the resolved attribute
after the damage; negative-controlled both directions.

VERIFIED BY NATURAL EXPERIMENT, not by inspection: the next worktree subagent
dispatched after the fix (autonoveld-18o) was the first worktree created since,
and its `.gitattributes` held only `.beads/*.jsonl merge=jsonl-union`. Nothing
to strip, and its merge into master was the first this session that did not
carry the bad line.

FLEET FOLLOW-UP, none of it blocking: any project that later acquires a
project-local SessionStart hook could reintroduce this class. The guard that
caught it is autonoveld-local. If it is wanted fleet-wide, the honest place is a
dotfiles-side check that no project hook appends to .gitattributes — filed
separately if Zig wants it, deliberately NOT done here on the evidence that
exactly one project ever had the file.

title: a decide-and-proceed bead that says 'fail hard' must enumerate WHO dies
description:
## Context
Promoted out of the 2026-08-04 handoff (offboard Step 2.6), earned by a real outage.

`dotfiles-ucl4` decided that a gateway tunnel failure fails HARD with no silent fallback.
The reasoning was sound and I still stand by it. The blast radius was not reasoned about
at all: I weighed a dead TUNNEL (marketing-vps only) and never weighed a dead GATEWAY.
pico is a fleet-wide single point of failure, so when pico lost internet for ~6.5 hours on
2026-08-04, `claude` died on EVERY host and a scheduled pulse tick was injected into an
API-dead session and lost.

"Fails hard" is not one property. It is one property per dependent, and the set of
dependents is exactly what a reviewer cannot reconstruct from the decision text later.

## The practice
AGENTS.md already requires a decide-and-proceed record with Context / Decision / Why /
Reversibility. Add: when the decision makes something fail CLOSED, name **who fails with
it** — the dependents, not just the component. One line. If the honest answer is "I do not
know what depends on this", that is the finding, and it belongs in the bead.

`ucl4` would have read: "fails hard — marketing-vps loses claude" ... and writing that
sentence is what surfaces the question "only marketing-vps?", whose answer is no.

## Where it might live
AGENTS.md "The counterpart: when you decide-and-proceed, leave a durable record" is the
natural host — it owns the required shape. `/beads` documents bead types but not this
field. Zig picks; it is a rules change to the always-loaded global tier, which is why this
is a bead and not an edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the requirement lands in exactly one place, in the existing Context/Decision/Why/
      Reversibility list rather than as a new section
- [ ] it stays one line — this is a field, not a methodology
- [ ] `dotfiles-ucl4` is cited as the worked example, including that the author still
      thinks the decision was right and only the blast-radius framing was missing

## Write target
~/demesne — AGENTS.md decide-and-proceed practice (always-loaded tier: running sessions need a cycle to see it).

title: fix: give gdoc skill its own package.json — retire the ~/node_modules band-aid (and the $HOME project-root hazard it creates)
description:
## Context

`agents/skills/gdoc/render_styled_blocks.mjs` does a bare `import { google } from
'googleapis'` with **no manifest of its own**. It had been resolving out of bun's
GLOBAL store, where `googleapis` was an ORPHAN (never a declared global dep).

On 2026-07-25 the overnight upgrade ran `bun install -g` for 4 CLIs, which
re-hoisted `gcp-metadata` down to 6.1.1 while `google-auth-library@10.5.0` requires
`^8.0.0`. The renderer died with `ENOENT while resolving package 'gcp-metadata'`,
taking the daily-digest's styled-tab delivery with it. It failed SILENTLY until
something tried to run it.

**Stopgap applied** (decision bead `explore-kbqe`): `bun add googleapis` at
`/home/ubuntu`, creating `~/node_modules` + `~/package.json`. Node/bun resolution
walks up `gdoc/ -> skills/ -> agents/ -> dotfiles/ -> ~/` and finds it. Delivery
works again. Note `bun add -g googleapis` alone did NOT fix it — the renderer still
resolved from a bare cache path.

## Why the stopgap must be retired

1. **The script is still structurally fragile.** It now depends on a `$HOME`-level
   install that any stray `npm install` / `bun install` run with `cwd=$HOME` would
   rewrite — the same class of accident that broke it in the first place.
2. **`~/package.json` is a latent hazard.** Every tool that walks up to find a
   "project root" — `tsc`, `biome`, `vitest`, `bunx` — will now stop at `$HOME` for
   any file not inside a real project. Not currently causing failures; worth
   removing rather than living with.

## The correct pattern already exists in-house

`~/explore/bin/` is the model: its own `package.json`, its own `node_modules`, a
pinned version, and explicit `createRequire` resolution with a documented fallback.
`headless-fetch.mjs` was verified working through the whole upgrade precisely
because of this.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `agents/skills/gdoc/package.json` created, pinning `googleapis` (match the working version, currently 173.0.0 / google-auth-library 10.9.1 / gcp-metadata 8.1.2)
- [ ] `agents/skills/gdoc/node_modules/` installed and **gitignored** (dotfiles/.gitignore currently has NO node_modules entry — add one)
- [ ] `render_styled_blocks.mjs` verified to resolve from the skill dir with `$HOME` fallback removed from the equation (test by running it from several unrelated cwds)
- [ ] `ops/digest-to-gdoc.sh` end-to-end run still succeeds (it is the real consumer; a styled tab render is the proof)
- [ ] ONLY THEN remove the band-aid: `rm -rf ~/node_modules ~/package.json ~/bun.lock`, and re-verify delivery still works afterwards
- [ ] committed + pushed
notes:
## DONE — 2026-07-25 (commit 372396c, pushed)

agents/skills/gdoc/package.json created pinning googleapis 173.0.0 (+ committed
lockfile, deliberately: freezing transitive deps IS the point of this bead —
gcp-metadata drifting is exactly what broke it). node_modules/ added to
dotfiles/.gitignore, which previously had NO entry (the tree is 226M).

BAND-AID SUCCESSFULLY REMOVED. ~/node_modules, ~/package.json, ~/bun.lock all gone;
orchestrator confirmed. Resolution verified from 4 unrelated cwds (/tmp, /,
~/explore, ~) — all four land in the skill's own node_modules. Consumer verified
end-to-end AFTER removal: digest-to-gdoc.sh EXIT=0, 68 blocks / 362 textReqs.

## Flags raised

1. gdoc.sh is a SECOND googleapis consumer the criteria never named. It cds to
   $GDOC_AGENT_DIR (default ~/linearb/agent-factory/agents/lb-agent-di) and runs
   `bun -e`, which resolves from CWD — so it WOULD have walked up to ~/node_modules.
   It survives only because that LinearB dir has its own install. Verified working
   post-removal. The skill dir is now a viable portable default for GDOC_AGENT_DIR;
   documented but NOT changed (behavior change to a working path, outside the bead).
2. ~/explore/ops/digest-to-gdoc.sh had a stale header comment claiming resolution
   came from bun's global store. FIXED by the orchestrator in the explore repo.

title: model-canon: the roster keeps aliases; canonicalisation happens at the launch/restore boundary
description:
## Context
dotfiles-lstn had to decide WHERE the alias -> canonical mapping lives. Two forks:
rewrite agents/seats.yml's 14 `model:` values to the full canonical ids
(`claude-fable-5[1m]`, …), or keep the aliases in the roster and canonicalise at
the boundary — pulse-inject.sh's launch-string splice and
post-tool-model-guard.sh's /model instruction.

## Decision
**The roster keeps the four aliases (`fable`/`opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`); a single
shared table, `agents/lib/model-canon.sh`, is applied at the boundary.**

## Options
Canonical ids IN the roster
  + one fewer indirection at the launch site; what you read is what runs
  - agents/lib/validate-seats.py gates `model:` against KNOWN_MODELS = the four
    aliases, so this needs that validator changed too
  - agents/bin/hall renders the model column at SIX cells (`W_MODEL=6`); every
    canonical id truncates to the indistinguishable string `claude`, so the
    court view stops answering "which tier is this seat on"
  - 14 copies of a fact that moves whenever Anthropic ships a model — the
    two-copies defect, at the speed of the vendor's release cadence

Aliases in the roster, canonicalised at the boundary  <- CHOSEN
  + the long id exists once, in a file that also carries the probe evidence
  + validate-seats.py and the hall are untouched
  + the /model instruction and the launch string are the only places the
    literal actually has to be right, and both are now tested + mutated
  - one indirection: reading seats.yml no longer tells you the exact id
  - a missing model-canon.sh silently degrades to the alias (mitigated: it is a
    logged WARN in pulse-inject, and the guard falls back to naming EXPECTED)

## Consequences
Reversibility: HIGH. Flipping to canonical-in-roster later means widening
KNOWN_MODELS, widening `W_MODEL`, and deleting the canonicalise step — no data
migration beyond seats.yml itself.

title: impl: ss14-wrapper Go daemon — satisfy qts test contract per spec 9g1
description:
## Context

Implementation wave for spec dotfiles-9g1 (Approach C2). Test wave qts
shipped 35 Go test functions + Bash integration test + SS14 C# test
design sketch, all under ss14-wrapper/ in dotfiles. Tests currently
26 FAIL / 9 PASS (assertion-level failures — the expected TDD baseline,
since all wrapper functions are stubs returning ErrNotImplemented).

This bead implements the Go wrapper daemon to satisfy that test
contract.

## Scope

- `ss14-wrapper/main.go` — daemon entry; wires config → start UDP/TCP/UDS
  loops → graceful shutdown
- `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/proxy.go` — PROXY v1/v2 autodetect parsing,
  per-datagram header peel (UDP), per-connection header peel (TCP)
- `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/session.go` — concrete SessionStore with TTL,
  per-tuple lookups, allocator hook for testability
- `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/api.go` — UDS server (LOOKUP, ENUMERATE, HEALTH
  verbs per docs/ss14-patch-tests.md wire format)
- `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/config.go` — env-var loading, defaults, validation

## Out of scope (separate dispatches)

- SS14 C# patches (live in vacation-station-14, separate repo + worktree)
- nginx config deployment (handled by /impl when we reach the cutover bead)
- LaunchAgent install for the wrapper on pico (handled at cutover time)
- A wider integration test that exercises the live wrapper (the qts
  Bash script's "wrapper present" stage extension)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go test ./...` from ss14-wrapper/ → all 35 test functions PASS
- [ ] `go vet ./...` clean
- [ ] `gofmt -l .` empty
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./...` clean
- [ ] `go build ./...` produces a binary at ./ss14-wrapper (or main pkg)
- [ ] Tests file UNCHANGED — verify via `git diff --stat HEAD~1
      ss14-wrapper/wrapper/*_test.go` returns empty (the impl agent
      must NOT modify the contract)
- [ ] No source files modified outside ss14-wrapper/ or in
      ~/vacation-station-14/
notes:
## Scrutiny — 2026-05-24 (general-purpose subagent)

**Verdict: SHIP**

### Re-run results (all independently verified)
- go test: 35 PASS / 0 FAIL (matches impl claim)
- go test -race: clean
- go vet, gofmt, golangci-lint: clean
- go build: 3.6MB ELF binary

### Stub-body audit
Every function in the hunt list confirmed REAL impl: ParseProxyHeader,
ServeUDP, ServeTCP, SessionStore.{LookupOrCreate, LookupByPort,
EvictExpired}, HandleAPIRequest + handlers, Run. Bodies have
defensive guards (panic recovery, alloc-failure paths, double-checked
locking), not type-check-satisfier stubs.

### Delegation-assertion confirmed genuine
TestHandleAPIRequest_Lookup_DelegatesToStore (api_test.go:157-187)
seeds two real stores with different IPs, asserts responses differ.
A stub returning hardcoded values would fail this. The oracle is
distinguishing, not tautological.

### Spec drift: faithful with one documented narrowing
ENUMERATE returns UDP sessions only (TCP is short-lived) — comment-
documented in session.go:188-192. Doesn't break the C# wire-format
contract (LOOKUP / MISS / OK formats exact match).

### Findings (non-blocking, see /fix candidates below)
1. **go.mod cosmetic**: go-proxyproto under `// indirect` block but
   is a direct import. `go mod tidy` fixes.
2. **session.go:97-107 narrow race**: LookupOrCreate fast→slow path
   drops RLock then re-acquires Lock without re-checking map presence.
   EvictExpired runs every TTL/4 (30s); race window is sub-millisecond.
   Outcome: one dropped datagram in the worst case; next datagram
   spawns a fresh session. Degraded-but-safe, not data-loss.
3. **proxy.go:113-114,164-168 slow leak**: `pumps[port]` cancel-func
   map grows per session; pump goroutine self-terminates on FanOut
   close (correct) but the cancel entry leaks. Bounded by ephemeral
   port wraparound (~28K sessions). Not load-bearing at SS14 scale
   (~256 concurrent max).
4. **README.md doc rot**: still says "implementation has NOT landed
   yet" and labels every .go file "stub". Trivial sed fix.

### Production safety
Zero files touched outside ss14-wrapper/. Confirmed via
`git diff --name-only 730a950^..730a950 | grep -v '^ss14-wrapper/'`
returning empty.

### Recommendation
SHIP. Findings 2 + 3 worth a small /fix wave (regression tests +
narrow fixes). Findings 1 + 4 are housekeeping (no bead needed).
Ready for next dispatch: SS14 C# patches in vacation-station-14.

title: installers write into symlinked dotfiles — bun upgrade re-added a hardcoded path the repo had deliberately removed
description:
## Context

`sync.sh` symlinks `~/.zshrc` -> `dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc`. So any installer that "helpfully"
appends to `~/.zshrc` is **writing into the tracked repo**, and the change shows up as an
unexplained dirty file rather than as anything attributable to the installer.

Observed 2026-08-01 during the upgrade pass on `zig`. `bun upgrade` (1.3.9 -> 1.3.14)
appended:

```bash
# bun completions
[ -s "/Users/zig/.bun/_bun" ] && source "/Users/zig/.bun/_bun"
```

Two things wrong with that:

1. It **re-introduced a hardcoded absolute path** that this repo had deliberately replaced
   with `$HOME`. The tracked file already carries the portable form, with a comment
   explaining why: "$HOME, not a hardcoded /home/ubuntu — identical on zig-computer, and no
   longer a dead path on every other box". The installer silently undid a considered fix.
2. It was **redundant** — `zsh/.zshrc` already sources `_bun` twice (lines 14 and 70), both
   portable. The append made it three.

Reverted on `zig`; the tracked file is clean again. But `bun upgrade` will re-add it every
time, on every machine.

## Why this is a class, not a bun quirk

Every tool in `mac.setup.sh` that offers shell integration is a candidate: nvm, pnpm, deno,
uv, cargo, pyenv, conda. Each one's installer appends to a shell rc that is a symlink into
this repo. The failure is quiet — a dirty tracked file after an unrelated upgrade — and on
a box where someone runs `git add` broadly it gets committed and propagates fleet-wide.

Related: `bash/.profile` currently sources `$HOME/.cargo/env` **unguarded** (noted in
`dotfiles-1r6k`), which is likely the same mechanism from an earlier rustup run.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
grep -c _bun zsh/.zshrc     # 2
bun upgrade
git -C ~/azigler/dotfiles status --short zsh/.zshrc   # M
grep -c _bun zsh/.zshrc     # 3, the new one hardcoded
```

## Fix direction

- `mac.upgrade.sh` / `ubuntu.upgrade.sh` should **detect and report** a tracked dotfile that
  an upgrade step dirtied, rather than leaving it for someone to notice. That is the cheap,
  high-value half: make it loud.
- Where an installer supports it, suppress the rc edit (bun honours `BUN_INSTALL` /
  no-modify flags in some versions; uv, pnpm and nvm have their own).
- Consider a post-upgrade assertion: `git diff --name-only` over the dotfiles repo must be
  empty after an upgrade run, else fail with the diff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] an upgrade run that dirties a tracked dotfile fails or warns loudly, naming the file and the step
- [ ] `bun upgrade` no longer leaves `zsh/.zshrc` modified (suppressed, or reverted automatically)
- [ ] the other shell-integrating installers in `mac.setup.sh` audited for the same behavior
- [ ] `bash/.profile`'s unguarded `$HOME/.cargo/env` source guarded (it breaks on any box without cargo)

title: lb-granola commit swallows a rejected push — 8 days of deliveries stayed local while the timer reported success
description:
## Context
Found 2026-08-05 during the retreat data-loss audit. **11 commits (2026-07-30 → 2026-08-05)
existed only on zig-computer.** Rescued by a manual fetch+merge+push; the root cause is not.

## Steps to Reproduce
It reproduces itself hourly. The state that caused it:

    # lb-granola README line 170 documents the contract:
    #   `commit` | flock`d, idempotent `git add data/ && commit && push`, then `check`
    ssh zig-computer "cd ~/linearb/lb-granola && git log --oneline --branches --not --remotes | wc -l"
      -> 11
    ssh zig-computer "cd ~/linearb/lb-granola && git log -1 --format=%ci 3b97979"
      -> 2026-07-28 22:05:39      # the last time the remote advanced
    systemctl --user list-timers | grep granola
      -> lb-granola-commit.timer, ran 12 min ago, GREEN

## Root cause — two writers, then silence
`3b97979` is a commit **marketing-vps** pushed to lb-granola on 2026-07-28 22:05 (its
machine-scoped handoff note). zig-computer local never had it, so from that moment every
hourly `git push` was rejected **non-fast-forward** — and the binary swallowed the error.
Verified: my own `git push` hit the identical rejection until I merged.

`commit` then ran `check`, `check` passed, the unit exited 0, the timer stayed green for
**8 days**. Meanwhile marketing-vps `lb-granola-pull` (a self-described read-only consumer,
every 2 min) kept pulling week-stale data and also reporting success.

Both ends green, no data moving. This is dotfiles-cxle CLASS ("the consumer reports success
while the step stopped working"), and the unit file itself states the intended mechanism —
"the timer is not the safety net, the non-zero exit is" — which is exactly the mechanism
that failed.

## Why it will recur even after the retreat
Removing marketing-vps removes THIS divergence source, not the swallow. Any second writer
(a future box, a GitHub-side edit, a rebase) re-arms it, and the failure is silent by
construction.

## Fix direction (not prescribed — the binary is compiled Go, source may not be here)
Cheapest loud fix: an `ExecStartPost` on `lb-granola-commit.service` that asserts
`git rev-parse HEAD` == `git ls-remote origin main` and FAILS the unit otherwise — the
same push-proof /commit already mandates. Better: fetch+merge before pushing, and exit
non-zero on a refused merge (two writers genuinely conflicting) rather than on every
divergence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a rejected/absent push makes the UNIT fail, visibly, not exit 0
- [ ] demonstrated: force a divergence, run the unit, watch it go red
- [ ] the assert compares against `ls-remote`, not a local tracking ref (a stale tracking
      ref is what made my first audit report a phantom unpushed commit)
- [ ] `lb-granola-pull` on any consumer can tell stale-because-nothing-published from
      stale-because-broken, or the pull side is documented as unable to
- [ ] the README contract (`... && push`) and the actual behaviour agree
notes:
## ⚠️ ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED — my original diagnosis was WRONG (2026-08-05)
This bead said the binary SWALLOWED the push error. It does not. The agent found the Go
source (`internal/gitcommit/commit.go`), which returns the push error; `main.go` exits 1.
Verified in the journal:

    Aug 05 19:29:45  ! [rejected]  main -> main (fetch first)
    Aug 05 19:29:45  Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

So the unit DID go red. The real defect is **a red that erases itself**: `commit` only
reaches its push when something is STAGED. Granola deliveries are sporadic, so the next
no-op tick returns early, never touches the remote, passes `check` — C3 asserts
COMMITTED, not PUBLISHED — and exits 0:

    Aug 05 23:37:02  commit: nothing staged; no-op
    Aug 05 23:37:02  Finished lb-granola-commit.service

A oneshot unit has ONE state bit and the next success overwrites the failure. The unit was
red for about a minute at a time, repeatedly, for 8 days — and green whenever anyone
looked. My "stayed green for 8 days" was very nearly true and wrong about the mechanism.

That is a more interesting bug than the one I filed, and it generalizes: **any oneshot
whose real work is conditional can erase its own failure on the next no-op run.** Worth
checking the other oneshot timers for the same shape.
close_reason: Fixed by agents/scheduler/lb-granola-publish-guard.sh (b481caa), wired as ExecStartPre (healing, '-' prefixed) + ExecStartPost (fatal assert) on lb-granola-commit.service. The guard runs EVERY tick — including no-op ticks — which is precisely the hole: the old red only appeared on ticks with something staged and was erased by the next no-op success. Compares against git ls-remote, not a tracking ref (the stale-tracking-ref trap that made my own audit report a phantom unpushed commit elsewhere today); a refused merge aborts and FAILS rather than papering over a genuine two-writer conflict. MY ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG and the agent corrected it — the Go binary does not swallow the error, it exits 1 and the unit does go red; the defect is a red that erases itself. See the notes. Two things the agent got right that I had not specified: it edited BOTH the installed unit and ~/linearb/lb-granola/ops/lb-granola-commit.service, because ops/ is the source 'make install-units' copies from (Makefile line 30, verified) — an installed-only edit would have been silently reverted by the next install; and it flagged that its pre-deployed untracked copy of the guard would block the dotfiles pull on zig-computer even though byte-identical, which it did (sha af1df68c), and which I cleared before pulling. Evidence: RED demonstrated twice (diverged remote -> 'publish-guard: FAIL — main local 4b8d411 is not on origin'; refused merge -> 'merge of origin/main REFUSED', HEAD unmoved, nothing pushed). GREEN: local == ls-remote at 1b91a7d, unpushed 0, check rc=0, commit idempotent twice. 46 test cases, 3 mutants killed each on the case it names (the tracking-ref mutant dies only on S8). Orchestrator independently confirmed the journal evidence for the corrected root cause and that install-units exists. Left open by the agent and worth a follow-up: lb-granola-pull consumers still cannot distinguish stale-because-unpublished from stale-because-broken, and C3 could become a published-check in Go.

title: mac.setup.sh: tooling parity audit against ubuntu.setup.sh
description:
## Context

`mac.setup.sh` is a flat, mostly-uncommented sequence of installers. `ubuntu.setup.sh` and
`ubuntu.upgrade.sh` have drifted ahead with tooling the Mac never got. Audit both and
reconcile.

## Suspected gaps on the Mac side

VERIFY EACH — this list was assembled by READING the scripts, not by running anything on
the box. Check what is actually installed before acting on any line of it.

- **gitleaks** — foundational to the secret-hygiene system (`explore-r2iq`); `mac.setup.sh`
  does not install it
- **goose** — installed on ubuntu, and `bash/.bash_aliases` carries a goose-jail alias that
  assumes the binary exists
- **biome / ruff / golangci-lint** — the lint toolchain the repo's own `/lint` skill assumes
  is present
- **lazygit, fzf, ripgrep** — present on ubuntu via apt, absent from the Mac `brew install`
  line
- **bun globals** — @google/gemini-cli and @openai/codex are bun-installed on ubuntu; the
  Mac line only has `npm install -g @github/copilot wrangler`

## Structural gap

`mac.setup.sh` has no `set -euo pipefail` and no section / warn / fail structure, so a
failed installer mid-script is silent — the script reports success while a tool never
landed. This is the `dotfiles-cxle` failure class (consumer reports success while the step
stopped working) instantiated in a provisioning script. `ubuntu.upgrade.sh`'s helper block
is the pattern to copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a written per-tool table — mac / ubuntu / pico, present or absent — derived by
      PROBING the boxes, not by reading the scripts
- [ ] each gap either closed in `mac.setup.sh` or explicitly recorded as deliberate
- [ ] `mac.setup.sh` gains `set -euo pipefail` and the section/warn/fail helper block, so a
      failed installer stops being silent
notes:
Empirical findings from the 2026-08-01 upgrade pass on `zig` — add these to the audit:

1. **cargo AND rustup are both ABSENT** on this Mac, yet `bash/.profile` sources
   `$HOME/.cargo/env` and `sync.sh` symlinks `cargo/config.toml` to `~/.cargo/config.toml`.
   The repo expects a Rust toolchain that `mac.setup.sh` never installs.
   (`ubuntu.upgrade.sh` installs rustup on missing; the Mac has no equivalent.)

2. **bv is dual-managed and the brew copy shadows the newer one.**
   `mac.setup.sh` installs it via `dicklesworthstone/tap/bv` (brew), while
   `ubuntu.upgrade.sh` uses the curl installer. On this box:
     which bv              -> /opt/homebrew/bin/bv   (brew, v0.13.0)
     ~/.local/bin/bv       -> v0.18.0
   So running the curl installer on a Mac is a silent no-op — brew wins on PATH.
   Pick ONE manager per tool and make both scripts agree.

3. **br was 0.1.7** until this session (now 0.2.19). The hooks reference "verified br
   0.2.16" behavior, so this box was running hooks against a br that predated the
   behavior they document.

All three are the same root shape: a tool the fleet assumes is present-and-current on the
Mac, with nothing that checks.
close_reason: Done in db183e0 — all three boxes probed (none UNKNOWN), 12 tools added to mac.setup.sh, set -euo pipefail + section/warn/fail added, three brew-shadows-curl traps resolved.

title: session-start: sed -i -E is a BSD no-op — the merge=union migration silently fails on every Mac and litters .gitattributes-E
description:
## Context

`agents/hooks/session-start.sh:318` runs:

```bash
sed -i -E '/^\.beads\/\*\.jsonl[[:space:]]+merge=union[[:space:]]*$/d' .gitattributes
```

GNU sed treats `-i` as "in place, no backup" and `-E` as "extended regex". **BSD sed
(macOS) requires `-i` to take a backup-suffix argument**, so it consumes `-E` as that
suffix. Two consequences, both silent:

1. The regex runs in **BRE** mode, where `+` is a literal plus, not a quantifier. The
   pattern never matches, so the legacy `merge=union` line is **never deleted**. The
   migration this line exists to perform has never once run on a Mac.
2. Every invocation writes a backup named **`.gitattributes-E`** into the repo root.

Found 2026-08-01 on `zig` via a stray untracked `.gitattributes-E` whose contents were
byte-identical to `.gitattributes`.

## Why it went unseen

Two gaps compounded:

- `agents/hooks/test/test-session-start-merge-driver.sh:115-118` **does** assert the union
  line is removed. That assertion would fail on macOS. It presumably only ever runs on
  Linux.
- `core.hooksPath` was **UNSET** on this clone, so `tools/githooks/pre-commit` — the thing
  that would run that suite — had never executed here at all. CLAUDE.md documents that a
  fresh clone starts ungated; this is that gap producing a real miss. (Set to
  `tools/githooks` on `zig` 2026-08-01.)

This is repo rule #1 territory: a hook bug that runs in every session, fleet-wide.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS:

```bash
cd /tmp && rm -rf sedtest && mkdir sedtest && cd sedtest
printf '%s\n' '.beads/*.jsonl merge=union' '.beads/*.jsonl merge=jsonl-union' > .gitattributes
sed -i -E '/^\.beads\/\*\.jsonl[[:space:]]+merge=union[[:space:]]*$/d' .gitattributes
cat .gitattributes   # both lines still present — deletion did NOT happen
ls -a | grep gitattributes   # .gitattributes AND .gitattributes-E
```

Observed 2026-08-01, verbatim: both lines survived, and `.gitattributes-E` was created.

## Fix direction

Do not reach for `sed -i '' -E`, which fixes macOS and breaks Linux. Use an idiom with no
in-place flag at all — filter to a temp file and `mv` — so one code path is correct on both:

```bash
if [ -f .gitattributes ] && grep -qE '^\.beads/\*\.jsonl[[:space:]]+merge=union[[:space:]]*$' .gitattributes; then
  grep -vE '^\.beads/\*\.jsonl[[:space:]]+merge=union[[:space:]]*$' .gitattributes > .gitattributes.tmp \
    && mv .gitattributes.tmp .gitattributes
fi
```

Audit the rest of `agents/` for the same `sed -i` shape while in there — this is a class,
not an instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the migration deletes the legacy `merge=union` line on **macOS and Linux**, verified
      by running the reproduction above on both and pasting output
- [ ] no `.gitattributes-E` (or any `-E` suffixed backup) is produced
- [ ] `grep -rn 'sed -i' agents/` audited; every hit is either portable or documented as
      GNU-only with a guard
- [ ] `test-session-start-merge-driver.sh` demonstrably FAILS against the old line on macOS
      and passes after — a green suite that never ran on the affected platform is not
      evidence
- [ ] the stray `.gitattributes-E` on `zig` is removed
close_reason: Fixed in ce5f531 — sed -i replaced with temp-file+mv. Verified: main FAIL 1/14, fixed 14/14 on macOS; agent confirmed 14/14 on Linux via docker.

title: CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 does not bypass the gateway in any fresh zsh — .zshenv re-exports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and inherited-wins defeats the hatch
description:
Found while building dotfiles-ogkz (surfaced by the dotfiles-v93v agent, independently reproduced by the orchestrator).

## Context
claude-identity-wrapper.sh precedence is documented as:
  1. inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL wins (explicit per-call override)
  2. CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 -> the escape hatch
  3. re-derive from ~/.<host>.zshenv

Rules 1 and 2 are in the wrong order for any FRESH zsh. zsh sources ~/.zshenv on
EVERY invocation, which sources ~/.<host>.zshenv, which EXPORTS ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.
So by the time the wrapper runs, rule 1 has already matched and rule 2 is unreachable.

The hatch only works in a shell where the var happens to be unset — i.e. bash, or a
zsh where the per-host file is absent. That is the opposite of where it is needed.

## Steps to Reproduce
    env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 zsh  -c 'echo ${ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL:-<unset>}'
    # -> http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude      (hatch DEFEATED)

    env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 bash -c 'echo ${ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL:-<unset>}'
    # -> <unset>                              (hatch works)

## Why it matters now
This is the documented recovery when the gateway o11y body-size limit 503s a large
request — context compaction being the usual victim, i.e. exactly when a session is
long and expensive and least able to absorb a failure.

It gets worse with dotfiles-ogkz: marketing-vps moves behind the gateway with a
deliberate FAIL-HARD policy (dotfiles-ucl4). A VPS whose tunnel is down then has no
working claude AND a hatch that does not fire in its own login shell.

Note the wrapper header comment asserts CC_NO_GATEWAY "REPLACES the old
`unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL && claude` hatch" — a documented example that does not work,
which CLAUDE.md rule 2 says is an executable defect in a prompt-driven harness.

## Candidate fix
Check CC_NO_GATEWAY BEFORE honoring an inherited value: if the hatch is armed, clear
_base unconditionally. The subtlety is not clobbering a genuine deliberate override —
but an explicit CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 is itself the more specific intent, so it should win.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 bypasses in a fresh zsh -lc, a fresh bash, AND a durable pane
- [ ] a deliberate inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL still wins when the hatch is NOT armed
- [ ] the wrapper header comment corrected to describe what actually happens
- [ ] regression test in the new agents/lib/test-claude-identity-wrapper.sh
- [ ] a mutant reverting the fix is OBSERVED to fail that test
close_reason: Fixed, and the fix had TWO halves — the bead only named one. (1) Ordering: CC_NO_GATEWAY is now checked BEFORE an inherited value. (2) STRIPPING, which the agent found only because its test went red after half 1 landed: clearing the wrapper's internal _base bypasses nothing, because ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is EXPORTED by the calling shell and the child inherits it regardless of what the wrapper computes. Hatched launches now run 'env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL claude' — env, not unset, so a per-call hatch does not become sticky in a pane whose shell lives for days. Orchestrator verified live on main: hatch armed -> child sees UNSET; hatch unarmed -> child gets the gateway; caller shell unchanged. Independently re-ran mutant M9 (ordering kept, strip reverted) with the mutation asserted applied: 4 failures, hitting exactly the armed-hatch cases T9/T11/T12. Suite blind spot also fixed: run() launched under 'env -i HOME=$FAKEHOME', a shape that exists nowhere in production, which is why T6/T6b passed in BOTH shells and this was never a zsh-vs-bash gap; a $STARTHOME fixture now models a shell that starts with the var exported, and T9pre asserts the fixture fires so T9 cannot pass vacuously.

title: sketchybar: hook dispatch derives a function name with a hyphen, so any hyphenated hook file registers nothing
description:
## Context

`sketchybar/sketchybarrc` loaded hooks with:

```bash
source "$hook"
register_$(basename "$hook" .sh)
```

A shell function name **cannot contain a hyphen**. So a hook file named
`zig-computer.sh` must define `register_zig_computer` (underscores) — which it does — while
the dispatch derived `register_zig-computer` and invoked a command that does not exist.

Net effect: the hook was sourced successfully and then **registered nothing**. The bar came
up looking fine, minus one item, with the only signal a `command not found` on a stderr
nobody reads.

## How it got broken

`zig` carried a local uncommitted edit that hardcoded `register_zig_computer` in place of the
dynamic line — a correct workaround for exactly this. During the 723-commit fast-forward on
2026-08-01 I reviewed that hunk and advised taking origin's version, reasoning that "the
dynamic dispatch already handles the case where only zig-computer.sh exists." **That was
wrong** — it handles the file being found, not the hyphen-to-underscore translation. The
workaround was dropped and the item disappeared.

Worth recording because the local edit *looked* like drift-for-no-reason. It was load-bearing
and its reason was invisible from the diff.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
hook=sketchybar/hooks/zig-computer.sh
source "$hook"
type -t register_zig-computer   # nothing — not a function
type -t register_zig_computer   # function
sketchybar --query bar | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([i for i in json.load(sys.stdin)['items'] if 'zig' in i])"
# -> []   before the fix
```

## Fix

`976710f`+ — derive with `| tr '-' '_'`, and guard with `declare -F`, emitting a message when
a hook defines no matching function. Re-hardcoding would have fixed this one hook and broken
the next one; the guard is the part that matters, since a silently-unregistered hook is
indistinguishable from one that ran.

Verified: `sketchybar --query bar` went from no `zig*` item to `['zig-computer']` after
`sketchybar --reload`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] hyphenated hook filenames resolve to their underscored `register_*` function
- [x] a hook with no matching function reports itself instead of failing silently
- [x] `zig-computer` item present in the live bar after reload, demonstrated
- [ ] decide whether `sketchybar/hooks/` should be tracked — it is currently UNTRACKED, so
      this hook exists on no other machine and a fresh clone has an empty hook dir
close_reason: Fixed in 2e4f792 — dispatch derives register_$(basename | tr '-' '_') with a declare -F guard that reports an unmatched hook. Verified: sketchybar --query bar went from no zig* item to ['zig-computer'] after --reload, still present after merging 44 upstream commits. Tracking of sketchybar/hooks/ left as an open question for Zig.

title: decision: pico runs WITHOUT a host firewall — not internet-exposed (Zig, 2026-08-01)
description:
## Context
The 2026-08-01 pico audit filed the missing firewall as a finding: macOS ALF disabled
(`socketfilterfw --getglobalstate` -> State = 0), pf disabled (`pfctl -s info` ->
Status: Disabled), and ~13 of ~24 listeners wildcard-bound (`*:port`). On
zig-computer, ufw's INPUT DROP is what makes a wildcard bind merely a documentation
smell; pico has nothing in front of anything.

Offered: file-and-dont-touch / enable ALF / audit the 13 binds first.

## Decision (Zig)
"pico is not exposed to the public internet so we dont need a firewall on it."

No firewall on pico. Not deferred, not a TODO -- a settled threat-model call.

## Why it is defensible
pico sits at home behind NAT with no inbound port-forwarding, and is reached over
tailscale (WireGuard, authenticated at the mesh layer) or the home LAN. A host
firewall would defend only against other devices on that LAN. The wildcard binds are
therefore reachable by household devices, not by the internet -- a materially
different exposure from zig-computer, which IS a public VPS on 51.81.33.136 and where
the same posture would be a live P0 (see dotfiles-2smz on marketing-vps, which is
exactly that shape and is under 10k brute-force attempts/day).

## THE CONDITION THIS RESTS ON — re-open if it changes
The decision is sound ONLY while pico stays un-port-forwarded behind NAT. It should
be re-opened if any of these become true:
  - a port is forwarded to pico on the home router
  - pico moves to a public IP or a co-lo
  - pico joins an untrusted network (café / conference wifi) with wildcard binds live
  - the tailnet ACLs widen such that untrusted peers can reach it
An auditor finding "no firewall on pico" should read THIS bead and check the four
conditions above, not re-file the finding.

## Reversibility
Fully reversible: `sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw
--setglobalstate on` enables ALF. Deliberately NOT done from here -- pico is headless
and reached only over tailscale, so a firewall change with no console access is a
lockout risk with nobody at the keyboard.

title: hooks: built-in merge=union resurrects closed beads on worktree merges — replace with jsonl-union driver (dedupe by ID, keep newer updated_at)
description:
Built-in git merge=union keeps BOTH sides' lines on conflict. When a worktree branch carries a stale 'open' line for a bead that main has since closed, the merged JSONL contains both lines and br auto-import can flip the bead back open. Observed 3x on 2026-06-09 in ~/linearb (lin-bgd, lin-r5m, lin-lc8). Compounding bug: the old hook block greps for the plain union token, which does NOT match the jsonl-union token, so it appended the weak line into agent-dev-interrupted, overriding the custom driver there (last gitattributes match wins).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Repo with gitattributes mapping .beads/*.jsonl to the built-in union driver; bead X open, committed.
2. Branch a worktree; commit a touch to issues.jsonl (stale open line for X).
3. On main, close X, commit.
4. Merge the worktree branch: merged JSONL contains BOTH open and closed lines for X; br import may resurrect X.
(Automated: agents/hooks/test/test-merge-jsonl.sh reproduces this end-to-end.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Custom driver merges by union + dedupe-by-bead-id, newer updated_at wins.
- Malformed JSONL or missing jq: driver exits 1, visible conflict, never silent corruption.
- Hook sets the driver config idempotently per session and removes plain union lines.
- Regression test passes 9/9 incl. live merge repro.
close_reason: Fixed: custom union driver dedupes by bead ID keeping newer timestamp; hook wires config idempotently each session; regression test 9/9 including a live merge repro.

title: skills: three SKILL.md bodies hand agents GNU-only stat/date snippets that silently no-op on macOS
description:
## Context

`agents/skills/{offboard,pulse,desk}/SKILL.md` contain copy-paste shell snippets using
`stat -c` and/or `date -d`. Both are GNU-only. On macOS they fail, and in each case the
snippet has a fallback that makes the failure look like a legitimate empty result.

Hit live 2026-08-01 running `/offboard` on `zig`. The decision-harvest step:

```bash
export SINCE_EPOCH=$(stat -c %Y "$(last_offboard_path .)" 2>/dev/null || date -d 'today 00:00' +%s)
```

**Both branches are GNU-only**, so on macOS `SINCE_EPOCH` ends up empty or garbage and the
harvest silently reports no decisions. The skill even documents a receipt line to catch a
silent-empty query (`0 … (0 scanned)`) — but that receipt cannot distinguish "no decisions"
from "the cutoff was never computed", because the cutoff failure happens upstream of it.

## Why this is worse than the hook instances

This is CLAUDE.md rule #2 territory: **a documented EXAMPLE is executable in a prompt-driven
harness.** Agents copy these snippets verbatim. A wrong example is a defect that replicates
itself, is invisible to code review and to tests, and *scales with adoption*. Rule #2 already
lists four confirmed instances; this is a fifth class, in the always-loaded skill tier.

Sibling of `dotfiles-5vz2` (hooks, fixed in `6a46488`) and `dotfiles-6fmx` (scheduler).
Those were code; this is instructions to agents, which is a wider blast radius.

## Steps to Reproduce

macOS:

```bash
stat -c %Y ~/.zshrc                  # illegal option -- c
date -d 'today 00:00' +%s            # illegal time format
grep -rn 'stat -c\|date -d' agents/skills/
```

Then run `/offboard` and observe the harvest cutoff.

BSD equivalents: `stat -f %m FILE`; `date -v0H -v0M -v0S +%s`.

## Fix direction

The shim from `6a46488` (`agents/hooks/lib/portable.sh`: `_p_mtime`, `_p_epoch`,
`_p_date_since`) already solves this — the skills should **source it** rather than inline
raw coreutils, so there is one implementation and the snippets stop teaching the wrong idiom.

Where a snippet must stay standalone, use a form correct on both, and never let a fallback
silently substitute for a failed probe.

Also worth checking: `agents/doclint/doc-example-lint.py` exists to catch bad documented
examples. It did not catch these — determine whether it can, and extend it if so. That
would make the class mechanically enforced rather than periodically audited.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] all `stat -c` / `date -d` in `agents/skills/` are portable or source the shim
- [ ] the `/offboard` decision harvest computes a correct cutoff on macOS, demonstrated
- [ ] a failed cutoff probe is visibly distinct from "no decisions found"
- [ ] `doc-example-lint.py` extended to flag GNU-only coreutils in documented snippets, or a note recorded explaining why it cannot

title: the scrutinize proof has no binding to the work — a tick can point proof.bead at any bead that shipped months ago and earn a 'done' row forever
description:
## Context

`dotfiles-8aj5` fixed the *matcher* — the gate no longer accepts the letters `SHIP`
anywhere in a bead. It did not, and cannot, fix what sits behind it.

The agent that shipped that fix probed its own result and found **four ways the FIXED
gate still returns rc 0**:

1. A bead whose body quotes the required format **inside a fenced code block** —
   `Verdict: SHIP` on its own line between fences. Any bead documenting the format
   (including the skill docs, or `lib/scrutiny-verdict.sh`'s own comments if pasted into
   a bead) is a valid proof token.
2. `The reviewer wrote "Verdict: SHIP".` — same class.
3. `Verdict: SHIP` followed on the next line by `Actually, on reflection: do NOT SHIP.`
   That is the documented line-wise negation working as designed, and it is also a
   retraction the gate cannot see.
4. **The real one: nothing binds the proof bead to the work.** The gate asks *"does some
   bead say SHIP"*. It never asks *"is this the bead this tick worked on"*, *"is the
   verdict recent"*, or *"was the reviewer someone other than this tick"*.

Items 1-3 are inherited by `pre-bead-close.sh` too — a bead self-certifies from its own
notes. Not a regression introduced by the fix; the same contract, now visible.

## Why this is the interesting one

`explore-len0` built the proof-token gate on the principle of **verifier distance**: a
`done` row needs proof a hook can re-run, and `artifact`/`commit` were rejected as
zero-distance no-ops a stub passes. For `kind:cmd` the design holds — the hook genuinely
re-executes the command.

For `kind:scrutinize` **the distance is claimed by the design and not enforced by the
code.** A tick with any reachable bead id gets a permanent `done`. That is `artifact`
wearing `scrutinize` vocabulary, and it survived because nothing tested this branch at
all until 2026-08-01.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Append to a pulse ledger:
   `{"outcome":"done","proof":{"kind":"scrutinize","bead":"<any bead with a real SHIP verdict>"}}`
   — a bead from months ago, on unrelated work, already closed.
2. `git commit` → **allowed**. The gate cannot tell it apart from a genuine proof.
3. Positive control: point `proof.bead` at a bead with no verdict → correctly blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pick and implement a binding. Candidates, from the finding: require the proof bead's
      verdict line to **postdate the tick's previous ledger entry**; require the bead id to
      appear in the tick's own commit; or require `Verdict:` to be in the bead's **notes**
      field specifically rather than anywhere in `br show`.
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, state what it does **not** cover — none of the three closes
      items 1-3, and a design that implies otherwise is worse than one that says so.
- [ ] A test per accepted and rejected shape, and a mutant in
      `agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh` that dies on the new binding
      specifically.
- [ ] Decide whether `pre-bead-close.sh` gets the same treatment; it has the same
      self-certification property.

Related: `dotfiles-8aj5` (the matcher fix that surfaced this), `explore-len0` (the
verifier-distance principle this branch does not honour), `explore-fxb8` (the composing
verification-stage spec — this is a concrete instance of its separation axis being
asserted rather than enforced), `dotfiles-jm1c`.

title: fix: lint-on-write.sh runs bare rustfmt — fails open on edition-2024 and swallows stderr
description:
## Problem

`agents/hooks/lint-on-write.sh` (~line 61) runs:

    rustfmt "$FILE_PATH" 2>/dev/null

Bare — **no `--edition` flag** — so rustfmt defaults to **edition 2015**. On an
edition-2024 crate it cannot parse let-chains:

    error: let chains are only allowed in Rust 2024 or later
       --> .../holt_agent/src/agent.rs:387:12

It exits 1, but stderr is discarded and **the exit code is never checked** — so
the hook reports success while having formatted nothing. Every edition-2024 Rust
file silently goes unformatted.

Reproduced on `~/explore/smalltalk` (edition 2024), verified on a COPY not the
original.

## Notes

- **Pre-existing, NOT caused by the 2026-07-25 upgrade** — bare rustfmt has always
  defaulted to 2015. Found during the post-upgrade diagnostic sweep.
- This is a live instance of the harness's own documented anti-pattern
  ("Don't blanket-suppress stderr" in AGENTS.md): `2>/dev/null` on a command whose
  errors we need turned a real failure into a silent no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rustfmt` invoked with an `--edition` derived from the crate's Cargo.toml (fall back to a sane modern default when it can't be determined)
- [ ] stderr no longer blanket-suppressed — filter known noise if needed, but real errors must surface
- [ ] the exit code is checked; a formatting failure is reported, not swallowed
- [ ] verified against an edition-2024 file (e.g. a copy from ~/explore/smalltalk) AND an edition-2021 file
- [ ] committed + pushed
notes:
## DONE — 2026-07-25 (commit 166705a, pushed)

lint-on-write.sh now derives --edition by walking up to the nearest Cargo.toml with a
LITERAL edition — workspace members say `edition.workspace = true`, so continuing up
to [workspace.package] is the correct resolution. stderr kept, exit code checked
(failure exits 2, matching the biome/ruff branches).

Fallback is 2021, deliberately NOT 2024: `--edition 2024` on a pre-1.85 toolchain is
a hard error that would block every write.

VERIFIED through the live ~/.claude/hooks/ path, on COPIES (smalltalk original mtime
untouched at 2026-02-27):
  [2024] exit=0 reformatted=1 let-chain-intact=1
  [2021] exit=0 reformatted=1
  [broken] exit=2
  OLD path on the same 2024 file: rustfmt exit=1, ugly line STILL present after the
  old path reported success — i.e. the silent no-op reproduced, then fixed.
bash -n and shellcheck clean.

NOTE — mild behavior change beyond formatting: a .rs file that is syntactically
invalid mid-edit now exits 2 and BLOCKS, where it previously no-op'd silently. That
matches the biome/ruff branches but will be newly visible. /tmp, */scratch/*,
*/sandbox/* and *.scratch.* remain exempt.
