title: break-glass cards are untracked $HOME copies — install them from the tracked runbook instead
description:
## Context
2026-08-04, at Zig's request, a break-glass card was written to ~/.break-glass.txt on both
marketing-vps (/home/andrew) and zig-computer (/home/ubuntu). It carries the gateway
kill-switch procedure so it is findable when the harness is down and grepping is not an
option. It is deliberately a REAL file, not a symlink into ~/dotfiles, so it still works if
the repo is mid-anything.

That robustness has a cost, and this bead is the cost: the cards are untracked. They are
lost if a box is rebuilt, and they can silently diverge from the authoritative runbook in
agents/infra.md ("The kill switch"). Each card's header says infra.md wins on any
disagreement, which is the cheap mitigation, but nothing regenerates or checks them.

The two cards are NOT identical — each carries its own host's facts (gateway URL, failure
shape, whether a tunnel timer exists, whether pico is reachable directly). So this is not a
straight copy; whatever installs them has to be host-aware, the same way the per-host
zshenv files are.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The card content is generated from, or checked against, a tracked source rather than
      existing only in $HOME
- [ ] sync.sh (or an equivalent provisioning step) installs it, so a fresh machine gets one
- [ ] The host-specific sections stay correct per host — a single shared blob that claims
      marketing-vps can `ssh pico` is worse than no card (that exact error was caught and
      fixed by hand on the day the cards were written)
- [ ] Whatever ships still works with the repo unavailable — do NOT reduce it to a symlink

title: expected-gap primitive: declare an intentional silence with an expiry, so watchers can tell a planned gap from an outage
description:
## Context

Three live incidents share ONE shape — a signal goes quiet and the harness cannot tell
'planned' from 'broken' (Zig's framing 2026-08-14: declare an expected gap with an
expiry; design the primitive once):

1. POST-MOLT STALL (plan §2.3): the seneschal molted 2026-08-13, its first command died
   on a gateway error, and it sat frozen until Zig found it by hand. Silence after a
   molt is EXPECTED for minutes, an outage after that.
2. INTENTIONAL SEAT SHUTDOWN (dotfiles-c6k5): Zig deliberately closed seven seats;
   seat-liveness correctly classed them dead and paged for a planned action. Its AC
   already asks for exactly this: WHO/WHEN/EXPECTED-BACK, and suppression that EXPIRES.
3. GRANOLA STARVATION: the corpus committer goes quiet on meeting-free days (weekends);
   freshness checks read that as breakage. A declared gap with an expiry describes it
   exactly.

In all three, silence and success are indistinguishable today (plan §2.3's note). The
fix is a shared primitive, not three bespoke watchers.

## Design

agents/lib/expected-gap.sh + state at ~/.local/state/harness/expected-gaps.jsonl
(append-only JSONL; a row is superseded by a later row for the same entity+kind).

Verbs (exit codes per house three-valued convention where a check crosses state):
- declare --entity <seat|unit|feed> --kind <liveness|molt|freshness|...> \
          --until <ISO8601> --reason <text> --by <who>
  Appends the declaration. Refuses (loud) a missing --until: NO UNBOUNDED GAPS —
  expiry is the whole point (c6k5: a permanent deny-list entry is an unwatched seat
  nobody knows is unwatched).
- check --entity X --kind K → 0 = active gap (suppress; prints the row), 1 = no gap,
  3 = state unreadable (callers must fail closed, i.e. treat as no-gap and alarm).
- resolve --entity X --kind K --by <who>: entity returned before expiry; closes the gap.
- expired: list gaps past --until with no resolve — THE STRONGEST SIGNAL: something
  declared 'back by T' and is still gone. Watchdog consumers act on this.
- list: human/agent-readable current state.

Last-stdout-line verdict marker EXPECTED_GAP_RESULT=... on every terminal path
(dotfiles-cxle contract). stdlib-only (bash + jq or python3), no network.

Consumers (each its own bead/change, NOT this one): the post-molt stall watcher
(dotfiles bead filed alongside this one), seat-liveness (c6k5), granola freshness.
This bead ships the primitive + tests only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] declare/check/resolve/expired/list behave as specified, including supersession
      (re-declare extends) and the no-unbounded-gaps refusal.
- [ ] check exits 3 (never 0) when the state file is unreadable/corrupt — a broken
      suppression store must fail toward ALARMING, not toward suppressing.
- [ ] Concurrent-writer safe (two seats declaring simultaneously): append-only +
      atomic append, documented.
- [ ] test-expected-gap.sh in the demesne suite set, wired through tools/githooks;
      MUTANTS DIE on named cases (at minimum: expiry honored — a gap past --until no
      longer suppresses; fail-closed on unreadable state).
- [ ] EXPECTED_GAP_RESULT= marker on every terminal path.

## Notes

Home: ~/demesne (agents/lib + suite). Keep the primitive policy-free: it stores and
answers declarations; consumers decide what suppression means for them. Do not touch
seat-liveness or any timer in this bead.
close_reason: Landed on demesne main 68c691f (merge of a435bea atop Works' ed1ebbe; ancestor-verified; pushed + ls-remote confirmed). Second-pusher protocol run: all pre-commit arms grep-verified intact post-merge, three suites green on merged main (post 26/26, tap-alarm 28/28, expected-gap 24/24), 9/9 mutants killed on main. Scrutiny FIX-FIRST (M3 mislabeled) fixed with measured evidence, recorded on bead. CLI + exit contract documented in lib header; consumers (cbfc watchdog, c6k5 seat-liveness, granola freshness) are separate beads. Known deliberate omission, needs its own bead: append-only store compactor (write-new + os.replace, never in-place).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Scrutiny — FIX-FIRST then fixed, verdict effectively SHIP (2026-08-14, fresh fable-context gate on the opus build). 10 claims verified with real runs: exit contract (corrupt/truncated/chmod-000/dir-at-path all exit 3; missing store exits 1 by design — absent-is-not-corrupt, case 6), --until mandatory + 30d horizon boundary-measured, supersession + reopen + no cross-entity leakage, O_APPEND single-writer with case 16 re-run 3/3 deterministic, verdict marker on every path (16-path case-14 sweep + independent 9-path probe, no hole), all 9 mutants re-killed with applied-ness guard proven real (stale-target and syntax-broken replacements both HARNESS ERROR rc=2 not kills), hermetic (live store never created), case 19 genuinely extracts the doc example from file bytes, UTC-normalized (offset form measured to flip active->lapsed at the exact Z instant), scope clean. THE FINDING: mutant M3's injected fallback was TAB-separated while the parser splits on US (0x1F), so M3 landed as exit 1 — a near-duplicate of M2, not the named fail-open; the 'opposite directions' narrative was false (dotfiles-77s4 class). Suite itself proven sound: a hand-built genuine fail-open mutant reds 7/7b/14 and case 7 asserts rc==3 literally. title: SECURITY P0: marketing-vps is under active SSH brute force with password auth ON, NO firewall, NO fail2ban, and 2 NOPASSWD-root accounts
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
All verified independently on 2026-08-01 (agent found it; orchestrator re-ran every check):

  sudo sshd -T | grep passwordauth        -> passwordauthentication YES
  sudo ufw status                         -> Status: inactive
  sudo iptables -S INPUT                  -> policy ACCEPT, 0 rules
  systemctl is-active fail2ban            -> inactive  (not installed)
  journalctl -u ssh --since "24 hours ago" | grep -cE "Failed password|Invalid user"
                                          -> 10,635   (agent measured 14,600 earlier
                                             the same day -- window drift, same order)
  top sources: 91.92.42.172 (1354), 91.92.40.217 (1354), 192.227.224.88 (924),
               45.156.87.254 (896)   <- two are the same /22, coordinated
  shell accounts: ubuntu, kevin, andrew, mike, ben
  NOPASSWD:ALL sudo: **ubuntu** AND **andrew**
  /etc/shadow: ALL FIVE accounts have a usable password -> all brute-forceable

Host is internet-facing on 15.204.114.210, NOT on the tailnet (plain SSH).

## NOT COMPROMISED (checked, and this is the load-bearing negative)
  - successful logins, last 7 days: ONLY `publickey andrew from 51.81.33.136`
    (= zig-computer; the hourly refresh + today's audit). Zero from attacker ranges.
  - successful PASSWORD logins, last 30 days: 7, ALL from 192.184.211.228 (one
    consistent IP, almost certainly a teammate) or 51.81.33.136:
      Jul 17 x3 ubuntu, Jul 17 kevin, Jul 20 andrew(from zig-computer), Jul 24 x2 kevin
  - /etc/cron.d: only e2scrub_all, dated Feb -- no persistence added
  - no unexpected authorized_keys (ubuntu 1, kevin 2, andrew 1, mike 0, ben 0, root 0)

So: an at-risk host, not a breached one. The window to act is now.

## Why it is P0
Password auth + no rate limiting + no firewall + 10k attempts/day + two accounts with
passwordless root = one weak password away from instant root on an internet-facing
box that also holds LinearB material and is a WRITER on shared git repos. A cracked
`ubuntu` or `andrew` is root without a second step.

## The constraint that shapes the fix
Password auth is IN REAL USE: kevin logged in by password as recently as Jul 24, and
ubuntu on Jul 17 -- both from 192.184.211.228. Four LinearB teammates have accounts.
So `PasswordAuthentication no` risks locking out real people, which is why this is
gated on Zig rather than fixed on sight.
Mitigating detail: kevin has 2 authorized_keys and ubuntu has 1, so the two accounts
that actually used passwords ALSO have keys -- but whether those keys are current is
unverified, and mike/ben have NO keys at all (password is their only way in).

## Acceptance Criteria — ordered by (risk reduced / chance of lockout)
- [ ] **fail2ban installed + enabled** -- bans brute-forcers by IP; CANNOT lock out a
      user with correct credentials. Highest value, lowest risk. Do this first.
- [ ] **ufw enabled** allowing 22/80/443 (+ `ufw limit 22/tcp` for rate limiting).
      Standard remote-enable lockout risk -- allow 22 BEFORE enabling, and keep a
      session open while doing it.
- [ ] Decide on `PasswordAuthentication no` -- requires confirming mike/ben have
      working keys first, or they lose access. Zig's call, needs teammate coordination.
- [ ] Re-check whether `ubuntu` and `andrew` both need NOPASSWD:ALL
- [ ] Root cause of the `yes`: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf overrides
      60-cloudimg-settings.conf's `no`, because sshd takes the FIRST value read.
      Fixing the file without understanding that ordering will silently not work.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS ACCEPTED RISK — Zig's call, 2026-08-01: 'fail2ban is enough, close the bead', and leave both NOPASSWD accounts as-is.

MITIGATION APPLIED AND VERIFIED WORKING: fail2ban 1.1.0 installed, sshd jail on the
systemd backend, active + enabled. Measured effect: 7 IPs banned and the attack rate
fell from ~440/hr (10,635 in 24h when found) to 66 in the last hour -- roughly an 85%
reduction, from a mechanism that CANNOT lock out a user who types the right password.
ignoreip carries 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and 51.81.33.136 INSIDE [sshd] (a [DEFAULT] entry is
not inherited at runtime) so zig-computer can never self-ban and kill the hourly refresh.

NOT BREACHED, established before deciding: every successful login in 7 days was
publickey andrew from 51.81.33.136; all 7 password logins in 30 days came from one
consistent teammate IP or zig-computer; /etc/cron.d unchanged since February; no
unexpected authorized_keys.

RESIDUAL RISK, accepted knowingly and stated plainly: PasswordAuthentication is still
YES, ufw is still inactive, and ubuntu + andrew still hold NOPASSWD:ALL. A cracked
password on either is still root. The reason not to close that gap today is real and
not laziness -- mike and ben have ZERO ssh keys, so disabling password auth locks two
teammates out of a shared box, and that needs coordination rather than a unilateral
edit during an active campaign.

TRIGGERS TO REOPEN (this is the part a future reader needs):
  - fail2ban stops keeping up: the ban list saturates, or the failed-auth rate returns
    toward its pre-fix level despite banning
  - ANY successful password login from an IP that is not the known teammate address
  - mike/ben acquire ssh keys -> the lockout objection disappears and
    PasswordAuthentication no becomes free
  - the box gains anything more sensitive than it holds today
Root cause for whoever does that work: the 'yes' comes from
/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf overriding 60-cloudimg-settings.conf's 'no',
because sshd takes the FIRST value read. Editing the wrong file silently does nothing.

title: post-tool-model-guard restore instruction is tap-blind — it orders a restore to a model whose pool is exhausted
description:
## Context

The guard's escalation ladder (post-tool-model-guard.sh, RESTORE SEAM comments ~lines
51-106) instructs the session to /model back to the declared id, then verifies. It never
consults tap state. On 2026-08-13 it ordered a restore to claude-fable-5[1m] SEVENTEEN
times (37 blocks at the seneschal desk by 2026-08-14 01:30Z) while the primary fable
pool sat at 1.0000 — the seat was on opus DELIBERATELY because its pinned pool was
exhausted. The instruction was not merely useless, it was harmful: obeying it would burn
a restore into a dead pool, and the ladder ends at /model, which PERSISTS MACHINE-WIDE
(one obedient seat re-points the shared default for every window started after). Two
seats refused on their own judgement; an unattended marshal builder would not.

The reader exists: agents/lib/tap-headroom.sh (pool=... u5h= u7d= fable= rows,
TAP_HEADROOM_RESULT verdict marker). agents/scheduler/taps.conf maps seats to pools
(seat_home.*). Nothing joins them to the guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Exhaust (or simulate via a stubbed reader) the pool that serves a seat's pinned
   model — e.g. primary fable at 1.0000.
2. Run the seat on a fallback model so the guard sees a mismatch.
3. Observe: every block instructs '/model <pinned>' with no acknowledgment that the
   target pool has no headroom; nothing in the ledger records the tap state at fire.

## Design

Before composing a restore instruction, resolve the target model's pool for this seat
(taps.conf seat_home, else the pool→model mapping) and read tap-headroom for it. If the
pool is exhausted (fable=1.0000 for a fable target, u7d=1.0000 generally — define the
predicate precisely against tap-headroom.sh's output contract):
- do NOT instruct a restore; emit a DIFFERENT, once-per-episode message: pin
  unsatisfiable, pool exhausted, hold current model, no /model
- ledger the fire with the tap reading it acted on
Reader failure (TAP_HEADROOM_RESULT != ok) must DEGRADE to the current behaviour
(instruct, but say tap state was unreadable) — a broken reader must not silence the
guard entirely.

Also fold in (observability, same fix): ledger EVERY fire including try-1 — the
2026-08-13 defect was invisible in model-degradation-ledger.jsonl because early tries
were not ledgered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the target pool exhausted, no emitted block instructs /model to that model;
      the unsatisfiable-pin message appears instead, once per episode.
- [ ] With the target pool healthy, behaviour is unchanged (restore instruction).
- [ ] With the reader failing, the guard still fires and names the degradation.
- [ ] Every fire, including try-1, writes a ledger row; rows carry the tap reading.
- [ ] Proven by MUTANTS THAT DIE on the cases they name (exhausted-pool case at
      minimum), mutation-application asserted first; suites green before and after.

## Notes

Sibling beads, same file: dotfiles-9qyk (escalation cap), dotfiles-rlpm (frozen memo).
Independent fixes — keep separate; coordinate merges (same file). Cost note: the
tap-headroom read should be memoised/cooldowned like the seat resolution — never a
per-tool-round network/oauth read. This is a marshal prerequisite (plan §8: the maiden
drain must not dispatch builders that are each told to re-point the machine default).
close_reason: Landed on demesne main c6dd96a (same rehearsed merge as rlpm). The guard can no longer order a restore into an exhausted pool: seat-resolved expectations gate on tap headroom (memoised 900s, bounded timeout, oauth source only), exhausted => once-per-episode hold message naming pool+reading, reader failure => named degrade never silence, ledger every fire incl. try-1 with the tap reading. Marshal prerequisite satisfied on the guard side (plan §8). Scrutiny F4 accepted as-is: HOLD_TAIL full-volume escalation is nearly unreachable when ceiling from try 1 — consistent with once-per-episode design, recorded here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Scrutiny — SHIP (2026-08-14, same trio gate). Verified: ceiling => hold-pin-unsatisfiable with NO /model instruction anywhere (hand-inspected, RESTORE_CLAUSE flips the tail too); unavailable => ladder unchanged + named degrade; ok => literally byte-identical to pristine modulo the intended roster note (diffed); 900s memo proven by counting stub; TAP_HEADROOM_SOURCE=oauth forced (no SSH from a hook); every ledger row incl. try-1 carries the tap reading. Hand-applied M24: confident restore block while the ledger's own tap field reads ceiling 1.0000 — the exact 2026-08-13 incident, caught. Builder additionally verified against the REAL reader: seneschal->primary ceiling fable=1.0000 rc10; linearb->unavailable. Post-scrutiny F2 fix: copyable tap-headroom command backtick-terminated, extracted-from-emitted-bytes and run verbatim (rc10, real pool line).

## Guard — test-post-tool-model-guard-seat.sh S17-S21 + mutate-model-guard.sh M24/M25/M26/M27/M32.

## Context
~35 stale sockets sit in /tmp/tmux-1000/ (pulseseat-*, pulseseatleak-*, fcsuite*, ska5-*) — hook-test fixtures that were never reaped; only 'default' is the real server. The sweep agent exported TMUX_TMPDIR for a demo dir and ran a BARE `tmux kill-server` — but the inherited $TMUX env var takes PRECEDENCE over TMUX_TMPDIR, so the client connected through the live default socket. - [ ] The sweep also removes the incident's own debris (probetest, sweep-demo leftovers; socket count is now 42, worse than the 35 it started with)

Offenders fixed at source: test-pulse-inject + test-fleet-creds now use env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR + explicit -L everywhere and traps rm -f their socket files (kill-server measured to leave its own socket special file behind). Reusable agents/bin/tmux-fixture-sweep.sh (structural leaks from SIGKILLed runs bypass EXIT traps — demonstrated live: 16 fresh dead sockets from concurrent harness runs cleaned by second pass). Incident 2026-08-09 01:06 (the killed live server) fully remediated: env precedence root cause, guard at the right layer this time.

title: fix: ~/.claude/settings.json symlink was broken — template had drifted 5 settings behind live
description:
## What was wrong

`~/.claude/settings.json` was a REGULAR FILE, not a symlink to `claude/settings.json`,
even though `sync.sh` (`sync_source`) creates it with `ln -s` and every sibling is
correctly linked (CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, agents, statusline.sh).

Consequence: the tracked template had silently drifted **5 settings behind** the live
file, and the drift was invisible until it mattered. Today it mattered twice —
the template still pinned `effortLevel: xhigh` (the Opus 5 WebSearch-killer) and
would have reinstalled it on any fresh machine.

## When it broke, and why

* Last `sync.sh` run 2026-06-10 — its backup shows the target WAS a symlink then.
* Template received real commits 2026-07-04 / 07-07 / 07-10 — writes still flowing through the link.
* `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` was NEVER committed to the template (`git log -S` finds nothing), so it was added to the live file AFTER the link broke.
* => broke sometime after 2026-07-10. Claude Code shipped 2.1.218/219/220 in that window.

Mechanism: Claude Code writes settings.json **atomically (temp file + rename)**, and
`rename()` REPLACES a symlink with a regular file. The live file had accumulated
exactly the content Claude Code writes itself — a `permissions.allow` entry (the
"accept a permission" flow) and `effortLevel` (the effort menu).

## The 5 settings the template was missing

  env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL              <- the agentgateway proxy: ALL API traffic
  env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL    <- claude-opus-5[1m]
  PostToolUse/PushNotification        -> post-push-fallback.sh
  PreToolUse/Agent                    -> pre-tool-use-require-isolation.sh
  permissions.allow                   <- Read(conduit state dir)

A naive symlink would have DESTROYED all five. Verified live was a strict superset
first (diff had only `<` lines), then made template := live before linking.

## Also done

Removed `effortLevel` entirely. Verified empirically it is a no-op: with the field
absent a fresh session reports `EFFORT=[high]` and WebSearch succeeds. `high` is the
Opus 5 vendor default, identical to omitting the parameter.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [x] Diagnosed when and why the symlink broke, with evidence rather than a guess
* [x] Confirmed live was a strict superset before overwriting the template (nothing lost)
* [x] Template updated to contain all 5 previously-missing settings
* [x] `effortLevel` removed, and the no-op claim VERIFIED (fresh session reports high, search works)
* [x] `~/.claude/settings.json` is a symlink to `dotfiles/claude/settings.json` again
* [x] Proxy URL and both hooks verified readable through the link
* [x] committed + pushed
design:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ls -l ~/.claude/settings.json` — it was a REGULAR FILE, while every sibling
   (`CLAUDE.md`, `skills`, `hooks`, `agents`, `statusline.sh`) is a symlink into
   dotfiles.
2. `diff <(jq -S . ~/.claude/settings.json) <(jq -S . ~/dotfiles/claude/settings.json)`
   — output contained ONLY `<` lines, i.e. live was a strict superset: 5 settings
   existed live and were absent from the tracked template.
3. `grep -n -A25 '^sync_source()' sync.sh` — confirms the intended state is `ln -s`,
   so a regular file there is a broken invariant, not a design choice.
4. `git log -S'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL' -- claude/settings.json` — returns NOTHING, proving
   that setting never reached the template and so was added after the link broke.
5. `ls -la .backup/*/home/ubuntu/.claude/settings.json` — the 2026-06-10 backup shows
   the target WAS a symlink at that time, bounding the break to after 2026-07-10 (the
   template's last content commit).

## Root cause

Claude Code writes global settings atomically: temp file + `rename()`. `rename()`
replaces the symlink itself rather than writing through it. The live file had
accumulated exactly the content Claude Code authors — a `permissions.allow` entry
(accept-a-permission flow) and `effortLevel` (the effort menu) — which is the
fingerprint confirming the mechanism.
close_reason: done

title: guard: refuse worktree removal while a live agent owns the tree — the premature-reap incident
description:
## Context
INCIDENT 2026-08-09 (~04:00 UTC): the orchestrator dispatched a 3-task batch agent (bi2i+o9vi+v8k8), saw task 1's commit merge cleanly, and included the worktree in a cleanup pass — git worktree remove --force --force succeeded against a LIVE agent mid-task-2. The agent's fully-verified o9vi diff (built, mutation-tested 5/5, never committed) was destroyed; the agent's remaining calls all refused ('isolation worktree appears to have been removed'). Root causes: (1) doctrine gap — cleanup keyed on 'branch merged' not 'agent completed'; batch agents commit incrementally so the signals diverge; (2) mechanism gap — nothing refuses removal of a tree with a live owner. The doctrine half is fixed (AGENTS.md cleanup-gates-on-completion callout cites this bead). This bead is the MECHANISM half.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A PreToolUse guard (or a pre-flight inside the documented cleanup sequence) that REFUSES git worktree remove when live processes are rooted under the target path (the orphan-reaper's /proc scan inverted: reaper kills the dead, this guard protects the living) — override requires an explicit flag naming the incident class
- [ ] The guard distinguishes 'live agent processes' from 'reapable debris' (a dead tmux server or stale zsh must not block cleanup — that is the reaper's job, run first)
- [ ] Test + >=2 mutants per repo rule 1 (refusal-removed must die on the named case; debris-blocks-cleanup inverse must die too)
- [ ] The lost o9vi work is re-landed (separate re-dispatch, tracked on o9vi itself)
close_reason: Guard LIVE (merge, agent branch a12c13d6; wired into claude/settings.json PreToolUse, 0.35s on a 405-process box after a 7s->0.35s fork-elimination pass). Debris-vs-live heuristic (conservative by argued asymmetry): debris = shell/tmux comm AND <200 lifetime CPU ticks AND no non-debris descendant at any depth; everything else LIVE; unknown resolves LIVE because a false-debris destroys verified work (it did — incident reproduced as evidence: bare git worktree remove --force --force exits 0 SILENTLY against a live tree, task file gone, zero commits; guard exits 2 naming pids + this bead + the two legitimate paths incl. WORKTREE_REMOVE_OVERRIDE_LIVE=1 with loud echo). Cumulative-CPU chosen over sampling: honest sampling needs a sleep in a PreToolUse hook, and cumulative only over-reports liveness — the cheap test is the conservative one. Fails OPEN on scan errors with announcement (blocking all cleanup fleet-wide is the worse failure; inverse of the outward gate's choice, both argued in headers). ## Guard: 19/19; 4 mutants killed on named cases w/ must-pass isolation (refusal-removed, debris-blocks-cleanup, override-ignored, path-boundary-dropped). Documented not-caught: rm -rf, aliased git, script-internal removals, macOS no-/proc (fails open, noted). Doctrine half landed earlier (AGENTS.md completion-notification callout). o9vi re-land tracks the recovered work.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIRST LIVE FIRING (2026-08-09, hours after landing): the guard blocked the orchestrator's own removal of the o9vi worktree — correctly conservative. The occupants were the agent's self-documented lingering poll shells (zsh+sleep loops it said 'can be left to self-terminate'), which read as LIVE under the shell-with-active-child rule rather than debris. Completion notification was in hand + the agent's report named the processes -> textbook override path 2, used with the loss accepted (loss = nothing; polls were watching already-exited pids). CALIBRATION NOTE, not a defect: sleep-poll loops are the first observed false-live class; if it recurs often, a future refinement could classify 'shell whose only descendants are sleep' as debris — but the asymmetry argument says leave it conservative until the annoyance is measured, and the override cost was one env-var. The guard's block message carried the incident story and both paths exactly as designed.

title: mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh does not meet the rule it is now governed by — partial applied-check, no named-case assertion
description:
Found by the dotfiles-3afr agent while landing the rule, and confirmed by the orchestrator. Filed rather than fixed — it is a behaviour change to a gated harness, not part of writing the rule.

## Context
dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1 now requires of any mutation harness:
  1. assert the mutation actually APPLIED before the suite result means anything
  2. a killed mutant must fail the case(s) it NAMES

agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh implements both and is cited as the
reference. agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh PREDATES both clauses and does
not meet them:

    named-case assertions   mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh : 0
                            mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh: 4
    applied-check matches   mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh : 2  (a single count(frm))
                            mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh: 10

So the older harness can report a kill for a mutation that never applied, or for one
that reddened the suite somewhere unrelated. It is wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit
for the scrutiny-verdict guards, so a false kill there reads as "the guard bites" on a
guard that may not.

This is the ordinary consequence of writing a rule from the newer implementation: the
older sibling is now non-conforming. Better to have it named than silently tolerated —
an unenforced rule is the shape CLAUDE.md rule 1 exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh asserts each mutation applied (target present before,
      replacement present after, bytes changed, file still parses)
- [ ] each mutant declares the case(s) it should kill, and a kill on a DIFFERENT case is
      reported as MIS-KILLED rather than counted
- [ ] an unapplied mutation exits as a harness error, distinct from a kill
- [ ] demonstrated: feed it a deliberately stale target and watch it report the harness
      error rather than a kill
- [ ] pre-commit still passes on a clean tree, and the added runtime is measured
close_reason: mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh brought up to CLAUDE.md rule 1 (30efbf4), modelled line-for-line on mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh — same MUTANT_OK/HARNESS_ERR/FAILED vocabulary and 0/1/2 exits, so the two harnesses read alike as the rule intends. A pristine snapshot is taken once and every assertion compares against it, not the live tree. mutate() asserts target-exactly-once-in-pristine, replacement-absent-before, bytes-changed, replacement-once-after, and bash -n clean; remove_file() asserts the analogous three for the file-deletion mutant. A declared case name absent from the suite source is itself a HARNESS ERROR, so a typo cannot pass as coverage. tools/githooks/pre-commit needed no change — its trigger regex already named this file. THE HEADLINE: a LIVE FALSE KILL was demonstrated on the old harness. The same unparseable mutant (a stray fi) produced 'killed M2 empty-cmd-proof-accepted' at exit 0 under the OLD harness, with none of M2's named cases red; under the NEW one it is 'HARNESS ERROR: the mutant is not valid bash', exit 2. That is a gate wired into pre-commit reporting that a guard bites when it had not been tested at all — exactly what rule 1 predicts, found on a real guard rather than argued. Orchestrator verified independently: clean run green with all 6 mutants killed on their named cases, and the HARNESS ERROR path reproduced by staging a copy whose M1 target no longer exists in the source ('target text occurs 0x (want exactly 1)... the line this mutant aims at has MOVED or CHANGED', M1 reported NOT RUN rather than killed). Runtime delta ~+3s, inside the ~9s measurement spread.

title: task: --fresh's post-/clear settle is an unguarded race the readiness marker cannot cover
description:
Found by the dotfiles-mrta fix agent, 2026-07-26; documented in-code, unresolved.

pulse-inject's --fresh path issues /clear and then waits for the session to
settle. It CANNOT use the readiness marker that dotfiles-mrta hardened, because
the composer footer never disappears during a repaint — so the marker matches
INSTANTLY and the wait is a no-op.

That leaves the post-/clear settle as an unguarded race: a tick injected into a
session still repainting can land its keystrokes into a composer that is about to
be redrawn.

--fresh is LIVE on pulse-dive (shipped after the warm-session-collapse finding),
so this races on a real loop today, roughly 4x/day.

Fix direction: find a signal that is genuinely absent-then-present across a
/clear (not one that survives the repaint), or gate on a settle interval measured
from real /clear timings rather than a marker match.

Relates: dotfiles-mrta (closed), dotfiles-6ycc (--fresh).

title: seneschal: the spawn verb — a Zig directive raises the owning seat's session with guaranteed onboard/offboard, never beads
description:
## Context

Today this is impossible by charter: agents/skills/seneschal/SKILL.md declares 'This seat has no hands... never dispatches an agent, never touches another window, no send-keys, no state.' That prohibition exists to prevent an UNREVIEWED dispatcher — but a Zig-directed spawn has Zig in the loop, which IS the review. This bead is a narrow charter amendment plus the procedure, NOT a general dispatch power: the daily brief still never dispatches; only a direct Zig instruction triggers the spawn verb.

Mechanism already exists — do not build a second one: pulse-inject.sh --fresh creates the window if absent (it created the marshal window 2026-08-09), resolves the seat's model pin from agents/seats.yml (dotfiles-pulse-row-model-seat-d0bk), refuses 🔔 windows, and emits PULSE_INJECT_RESULT= verdicts the seneschal must read from the LAST STDOUT LINE (never the exit code — dotfiles-q0qi). Onboard/offboard guarantee, the part Zig stressed: a spawned seat must (1) onboard — the injected command carries the seat's own entry (its tick command, or '/onboard' followed by the directive as the work item) so the fresh context reads its handoff, seat header, and skill material (interacts with dotfiles-as1p's TOOLKIT fix — sequence after or alongside it); (2) offboard — the window-scoped .offboard-pending machinery (handoff-path.sh + session-end.sh) must fire for spawned windows exactly as for durable ones; verify, don't assume, since these windows are created ad-hoc. Note ie5a's superseding shape (handoff notes moving to demesne) — land compatibly.

- [ ] Spawned-window lifecycle verified with a REAL spawn: evidence that the spawned seat onboarded (handoff/seat header read in its transcript) and that its offboard machinery is intact (marker present after a deliberate no-offboard end, honored at next start).
- [ ] Verdict handling: bounced-not-ready / deferred-blocked-on-human / failed-* each have a stated seneschal behavior (report to Zig; never retry-loop into a blocked window).
- [ ] One spawn implementation fleet-wide: coordinated with 9z3o's raise rung (shared helper or explicit reuse), recorded on both beads.

The fork: (a) summon Zig (machine-level incident, AskUserQuestion + push); (b) wait for systemd-tmpfiles aging (10d rules — days away); (c) find an execution path that does not create /tmp files. Self-recover via the hook seam rather than summoning Zig, with age-guarded deletion only after two diagnostic rounds attributed the files.

The blocked state was itself accumulating damage (all seats + the 14:09Z zf2q verify run would brick); the deleted artifacts were provably ubuntu-owned leaked test fixtures (contents + mtime evidence logged before deletion to /home/ubuntu/.local/state/harness/tmp-inode-recovery.log); the hook edit was scoped (idempotent, bounded, logged, no stdin interference) and held for ~3 minutes.

title: CLAUDE.md rule 1: a mutant must die of the BUG IT NAMES, not merely make the suite red
description:
Standing-practice proposal promoted out of the 2026-08-03 handoff note (offboard Step 2.6). Do NOT leave this in a snapshot file — it is durable guidance.

## Context
CLAUDE.md rule 1 already says: "A green suite is not evidence that a guard bites; only
a mutant that dies is." That is right and it is not sufficient. Six times in one session
(dotfiles-ogkz arc) a mutant "died" or was about to be believed for the WRONG reason:

- dotfiles-47nf: the agent's first mutant over-escaped a sed pattern so it matched
  NOTHING. The suite failed. By exit code alone that is indistinguishable from a mutant
  that died properly.
- dotfiles-77s4: the ORCHESTRATOR's own first ownership mutant broke the script
  globally — unrelated preflights failed with verdict "<none>". It "died", of the wrong
  cause. Redone surgically it died on the right assertion.
- dotfiles-u9kw: a mutant killed case 19 via the header, leaving 19's base-URL half
  unproven; a third mutant was needed to isolate it.
- dotfiles-adf5: an over-broad grep matched a COMMENT, caught only by the applied-check.

## The refinement
Two clauses, both mechanical:
1. **Assert the mutation actually applied** before interpreting the suite result (target
   present exactly once pristine; replacement absent before and present after; bytes
   changed; the file still parses). A mutation that did not apply is a HARNESS ERROR,
   not a kill.
2. **A killed mutant must fail the case(s) it NAMES.** Red-somewhere is not evidence for
   the specific guard under test — it is often evidence the mutant broke something else.

## Where this already exists in code
agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh implements BOTH (five applied-checks, plus
a named-case requirement, rc 2 for harness error). It is the reference implementation;
the rule should point at it rather than re-describe it.

## Open question for Zig
Which tier: dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1 (project, where the existing sentence lives), or
/scrutinize (which owns the post-impl audit)? Rule 1 is the natural home for the
sentence it refines, but it is a rules change to a file every session in this repo
loads, which is why this is a bead and not an edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the two clauses land in exactly ONE place, pointing at mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh
- [ ] no second copy of the guidance is created (the two-copies defect, dotfiles-x1fn)
- [ ] the worked example cited is one that actually happened, with its real symptom
close_reason: Landed in dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1 (ecbe235), the tier decided in dotfiles-dkmc. Two clauses, placed immediately after the sentence they refine: assert the mutation actually APPLIED before the suite's exit code means anything (an unapplied mutation is a HARNESS ERROR, not a kill), and a killed mutant must fail the case(s) it NAMES (red-somewhere is frequently evidence the mutant broke something else). Each grounded in a real incident from this arc — dotfiles-47nf's over-escaped sed pattern that matched nothing, and dotfiles-77s4's ownership mutant (the orchestrator's own) that broke the script globally so unrelated preflights failed with verdict <none>. It POINTS at agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh rather than restating its checks; orchestrator verified no second copy exists (the applied-check mechanics grep to 10 hits in that one script and 1 in CLAUDE.md, which is the HARNESS ERROR label being defined, not an enumeration). Cited path resolves — the harness was run: baseline 28/28, all five mutants killed on their named cases.

title: mac.setup.sh: note Tailscale variant trade-off (headless vs GUI on macOS)
description:
## Context
Phase 1 testing surfaced a macOS Tailscale architectural constraint we missed during /spec + /scrutinize: you can't have both Tailscale SSH server AND MagicDNS on the same macOS install. The brew formula (CLI/headless) gives the server but runs in userspace networking (no DNS). All GUI variants (App Store, "Standalone" download, brew cask) give DNS via Network Extension but are sandboxed and refuse to run Tailscale SSH server.

`mac.setup.sh` installs the formula via brew (correct for headless servers like pico). The script doesn't document the trade-off, so anyone reading it for a workstation Mac (metis-style) would get the wrong variant for that role.

## Task
1. Add a comment block above the zig-zone bring-up section in `mac.setup.sh` explaining:
   - This script installs the FORMULA (headless tailscaled)
   - Right for HEADLESS SERVERS (Tailscale SSH server works)
   - For WORKSTATIONS: swap to cask post-install with explicit commands (including the `sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/tailscale*` step for cleaning up the formula's symlinks)
   - Reference to runbook gotcha #12 for the full rationale
2. Add a note at the END of the script reminding users about the `/etc/hosts` shim for outbound MagicDNS

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Comment block above zig-zone section explains variant trade-off
- [x] Explicit cask-swap commands for workstation use case
- [x] Reference to runbook gotcha #12
- [x] /etc/hosts shim note at end of script

title: mac.upgrade.sh: create it, mirroring ubuntu.upgrade.sh — then move the upgrade block out of download.sh
description:
## Context

`ubuntu.upgrade.sh` and `pico.upgrade.sh` exist. There is NO `mac.upgrade.sh`. The Mac's
only upgrade path is the no-argument branch of `download.sh`, which is both incomplete and
inseparable from destructive repo regeneration (see sibling bug `dotfiles-7bij`).

Build `mac.upgrade.sh` modeled on `ubuntu.upgrade.sh` — the mature reference: `set -euo
pipefail`, `section` / `warn` / `fail` helpers, reinstall-on-missing fallbacks, per-tool
guards.

## Coverage delta — what ubuntu.upgrade.sh does that the Mac path does NOT

- beads_rust (`br`) + beads_viewer (`bv`) installers
- biome, ruff (`uv tool upgrade ruff`), golangci-lint, gitleaks
- goose
- oh-my-zsh (`$OMZ/tools/upgrade.sh`)
- nix + nix-direnv
- cursor (`curl https://cursor.com/install`)
- bun/npm globals: @google/gemini-cli, @openai/codex, @github/copilot, vercel, wrangler

## Mac-specific substitutions

- `brew update && brew upgrade` in place of apt. Decide whether `brew upgrade --cask` is in
  scope.
- gitleaks / goose asset names are darwin+arm64, NOT `linux_x64` / `linux-amd64`. The
  ubuntu script hardcodes Linux assets; copying it verbatim fetches the wrong binary.
- agentgateway / agctl — this box does NOT serve it, and `zig` has no `.zig.zshenv` so it
  is not gateway-routed at all. Decide whether the Mac needs the client binaries before
  porting that section.
- **tmux is the live hazard.** Measured 2026-08-01: brew has `tmux 3.6a < 3.7b` pending.
  Upgrading the binary while a server is running leaves the old server in memory; a NEW
  client cannot attach across a protocol-version bump. Zig lives in tmux over SSH and the
  durable pulse windows (dive/digest/desk/dream) hold sessions for DAYS. An unguarded
  `brew upgrade` in this script can therefore cost real work. Pin it, prompt on it, or
  document the recovery path — do not let it ride in silently.
- `brew services` restarts: yabai, skhd, sketchybar, borders, tailscale, ollama will bounce
  on upgrade. None were outdated on 2026-08-01, but that is luck, not a guarantee.
- If the agentgateway section IS kept, carry the prerelease gotcha comment over verbatim:
  `/releases/latest/download/` silently installs betas because upstream mis-flags them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `mac.upgrade.sh` exists, is executable, covers every tool `mac.setup.sh` installs
- [ ] darwin/arm64 asset names verified for gitleaks and goose — not copied from Linux
- [ ] the tmux protocol-version hazard is explicitly handled, not ignored
- [ ] the `brew services` restart set is warned about up front or handled deliberately
- [ ] the upgrade block is removed from `download.sh`, closing `dotfiles-7bij`
- [ ] the script has actually been RUN and its output pasted into the bead — a script that
      has never been executed is not done
close_reason: mac.upgrade.sh created in 85000d4 — 19 sections, --dry-run/--only/--list, darwin assets verified, executed for real (gitleaks 8.30.1, goose 1.45.0, golangci-lint 2.12.2, biome 2.5.6, ruff 0.16.1).

title: guard: block/warn variable-rooted rm without the :? idiom — rm -rf "$VAR/..." degrades to a root-path delete on empty expansion (Zig, 2026-08-14)
description:
## Context
Zig's live catch, 2026-08-14 ~02:40Z: a permission gate intercepted a session command (a scrutiny subagent's cleanup) where rm took a path ROOTED IN A VARIABLE — empty variable would have made it a delete rooted at /. His instruction: do that safely, mechanically. The template source is already fixed (demesne 4f556d3: /dispatch's cross-repo block now uses ${WT:?} with the ruling documented inline) — this bead is the MECHANICAL rung: prose idioms don't survive contact with generated commands.

## Design sketch
A PreToolUse Bash guard (family of pre-bash-stderr-guard.sh): flag rm (and rm -r/-rf) invocations whose first path argument begins with an UNGUARDED variable expansion — $VAR/ or "$VAR/ without :? or :- — and block with a message that names the fix (${VAR:?}/...). Notes: (a) command-STRING inspection is the right seam here, unlike C1's case — the :? idiom is visible in the string by construction, no resolution needed; (b) allow ${VAR:?} and ${VAR:-default} forms and absolute-literal paths; (c) same treatment for rmdir and find ... -delete rooted at a bare variable is worth considering, but scope rm first; (d) mind the compound-kill property — the block message must say the whole Bash call died.

## Sweep
Also sweep existing house scripts for the unguarded shape (grep -rn 'rm -rf "\$' over demesne agents/) and convert hits to :? — post.sh:161 and marshal-garden.sh:365,406 use mktemp-derived $WORK (scrutiny-verified derivation, still cheap to convert).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Guard blocks rm -rf "$EMPTY/x" shape and passes ${VAR:?} form, literal paths, and rm of plain files (test both directions + a mutant that removes the check and dies)
- [ ] Block message names the :? fix and the whole-call kill
- [ ] House sweep done; converted sites listed here
- [ ] Consul/works lane ownership settled before build (guards are the consul's charter tonight)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CLAIMED by the CONSUL (2026-08-14 ~02:55Z, via direct session message) — dispatching its builder: new hook + tests + mutants + dedicated pre-commit harness block. Sweep coordination agreed: consul's builder converts unguarded variable-rooted rm only in files on main and unowned by in-flight lanes (exclusions: post-tool-model-guard.sh, seat-molt.sh, seat-cycle.sh, pulse-inject.sh, marshal-garden.sh); post.sh:161 goes to the consul (works confirmed no conflict — z4ib rebases onto it); marshal-garden.sh's two rm sites convert in the works' garden fix wave. Skipped hits get listed in the consul's handoff and relayed to owners.

title: hall: court view renders every seat idle after ylw2 — read @glyph, not the name prefix
description:
## Context

Discovered during dotfiles-ylw2 impl (2026-08-11). agents/bin/hall derives every seat's
status glyph from the tmux WINDOW NAME: hall_status_glyph (agents/bin/hall:182-197)
strips the lexicon prefix off the name and treats whatever it removed as the state,
falling back to the idle glyph when it removed nothing.

After the ylw2 ruling the name is ALWAYS bare, so hall_status_glyph always removes
nothing and every live seat renders idle — a court view that says "nothing here wants
Zig" while a seat sits on an open AskUserQuestion. This is the `prefix W` surface, i.e.
the one Zig actually looks at.

hall is READ-ONLY on tmux, so the fix is a read-source change only.

## Steps to Reproduce

On a scratch tmux server (NOT zig-computer), after the ylw2 change lands:

    tmux -L t -f /dev/null new-session -d -s scratch -n marshal
    tmux -L t set-option -w -t '=scratch:marshal' @glyph "$(printf '\U1F514')"
    HALL_TMUX_SOCKET=/tmp/tmux-1000/t hall

The seat renders with the idle glyph, not the blocked one.

## Task

hall_live_windows already lists windows with a -F format string; add
#{@glyph} as a field and have hall_status_glyph prefer it, keeping the
name-prefix derivation as the transition fallback for a window no hook has touched yet.
Note hall_status_glyph must stay NEVER-EMPTY (its own comment explains why: the records
are tab-separated and read with IFS=$'\t', so an empty middle field shifts columns).

Sibling of dotfiles-u1g1 (the send-keys safety guards); same root cause, different
consequence — this one is cosmetic-but-load-bearing, u1g1 is a safety guard, so they
are filed separately and u1g1 is the P1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] hall reads @glyph for a bare-named window and renders the right seat glyph
- [ ] A still-glyphed (not yet normalized) window keeps rendering correctly — fallback
- [ ] test-hall.sh covers both, and hall_status_glyph is still never empty
- [ ] Made-to-fail: break the @glyph read and the bare-name case goes red

title: pulse: a new-row setup dispatch must carry step 5.5 (harnessd registration) and the seed row
description:
## Context

2026-07-31, standing up `biweekly-content`. The subagent built the skill, the
script, the routing row, the CLAUDE.md entry, and the timer — everything
committed and armed — and the row was still **invisible to harnessd**, because
nothing registered it in `~/harnessd/refs/harness-manifest.json`. The DI project
had 5 loops; the 6th was scheduled and unwatched. A missed or stalled tick would
never have surfaced as STALE.

Zig caught it by asking "is it listed in the harness and everything?" — not by
any check firing.

Root cause is an orchestrator omission, not an agent one: `/pulse` step 5.5
specifies the registration, but the dispatch brief never mentioned it, so the
agent had no reason to look. The brief listed the row, the timer, the skill and
the docs — the four visible artifacts — and silently dropped the one that makes
the loop *observable*.

Registering it then hit the documented sibling failure: a brand-new row has no
ledger history, so `harness-assert-registration` reports `NO_LEDGER_TS` even with
a correct manifest entry, compounded by the pre-created systemd stamp file making
`last_fire` point at setup ("fired 24m ago, tick in flight" for a row that had
never run). Fixed with the prescribed seed `outcome:"quiet"` row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/pulse` "setup" gains an explicit **orchestrator checklist** for standing
      up a NEW row, enumerating every artifact including the two easy to forget:
      the harnessd manifest entry, and the seed `quiet` ledger row that must
      precede the first real fire.
- [ ] The checklist is phrased so it survives being copied into a dispatch brief
      — that is the failure path it exists to close.
- [ ] Cross-reference the new-row sibling failure already documented at step 5.5
      so the two are read together rather than discovered in sequence.
- [ ] Consider whether `harness-assert-registration` should be run by the setup
      flow itself rather than left to the orchestrator to remember.

## Note

Not urgent — `biweekly-content` is now registered and asserting clean. This is
about the NEXT new row, which will hit the identical gap.

title: guarded merge: sanction the FF tree-identity assertion as suites-on-main equivalence — codify in AGENTS.md Delegation sequence
description:
## Context
Used twice this session (d5ez/u1g1 landing, nit-commit avoidance context): when the guarded merge fast-forwards, `git rev-parse main^{tree}` == `<branch-tip>^{tree}` proves main's tree is bit-identical to the worktree HEAD the scrutinizer already ran the full suites on — so re-running every suite on main re-proves a proven artifact. The practice: assert tree identity; if identical, cite the scrutiny run as the suites-on-main evidence and run one fast smoke; if it DIFFERS (true merge), full suites on main remain mandatory. Saves ~10-30 min per FF landing; the ckst-era rationale (a green worktree proves nothing about the merge RESULT) is fully preserved because the assertion is exactly about the merge result.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Delegation" merge sequence gains the tree-identity clause (assert-identical -> smoke + cite; differs -> full suites), a few sentences, no restructure
- [ ] The close-reason convention notes citing the scrutinized HEAD when the clause is used

title: scrutinize: the write-only-your-own-critique pattern, from a 4-round adversarial design review
description:
## Context
2026-08-01, ifcompd wave 3. Four adversarial critics were run against a game
design in parallel isolated worktrees, each with a distinct lens (the player who
does everything wrong / the bored judge / the craft critic / the implementer).

Two constraints made it work, and both are generalizable beyond this project:

1. **Each critic could write ONLY its own critique file and was explicitly
   forbidden from modifying the artifact under review.** Rationale given in the
   dispatch: "a critic who fixes things stops being a critic, and the orchestrator
   needs to see findings, not silent edits." Result: 4 critiques, zero
   modifications to the reviewed spec, verified by counting changed paths per merge.
2. **Isolation from each other.** No critic saw another's findings. They did NOT
   converge — four genuinely different failure classes. Convergence would have
   signalled the lenses were not independent, i.e. an orchestrator failure.

Two further things emerged that are worth writing down:
- Both critics that finished first **deliberately filed no beads**, reasoning that
  filing before the other rounds reported would front-run synthesis and produce
  duplicates from four isolated agents. That instinct was right and is not
  currently stated anywhere.
- The critic given TOOL ACCESS (compile probes) produced by far the most
  actionable findings — including a defect in the harness itself. /scrutinize
  already says "EXECUTE & OBSERVE" for user-facing surfaces; this is evidence the
  same applies to design review, where it is much less obvious.

## The proposal
/scrutinize gains a short section on multi-lens adversarial review of a DESIGN or
SPEC (as opposed to an impl wave): distinct named lenses, mutual isolation, write
only your own critique, no bead-filing before synthesis, and give at least one
lens real tool access.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /scrutinize SKILL.md carries the pattern
- [ ] The no-bead-filing-before-synthesis rule is stated
- [ ] Non-convergence is named as the success signal, convergence as a dispatch smell

title: decision: gateway-outage hardening — recovery charters, no auto-flip, targeted kickstart
description:
## Context
2026-08-09 gateway outage (dotfiles-kviw), hardening seat proceeding without Zig on four calls someone might have made differently.

## Decision
1. gateway-health recovers ONLY the gateway job, not every dead pico LaunchAgent — pico-health stays the read-only detector for the rest; a keep-side script mass-kickstarting pico services on a probe blip is too much blast radius for a 2-min timer. The incident's other services were kickstarted by hand this once.
2. No guard ever auto-runs gateway-switch.sh (fleet re-route to direct API). A running claude cannot be re-routed anyway (exec-time env), and a flapping auto-flip is worse than a 2-min recovery gap. Flip stays an operator call.
3. Session recovery = a NEW injected turn via send-keys (the pulse-inject mechanism), not any attempt to resurrect the dead turn; 3-digit-code API errors are deliberately excluded (harnessd bells those; a settled 4xx/5xx may need a human).
4. pico reboot-survival root cause (Tahoe BTM 'needs LWCR update', runs=0) is NOT patched on pico now — kickstart recorded the LWCR, next reboot may be clean, and the keep-side guard covers the gap within ~2 min either way. Verify at the xh18 restart window instead of engineering blind.

## Why
Charters stay narrow and testable; recovery latency (≤2 min) is acceptable against fleet-wide blast radius of broader autonomous actions.

## Reversibility
All four reversible: widen the kickstart set, add an auto-flip threshold, include coded errors, or add a pico-side boot sweeper later — each is an extension, not a rewrite.

title: reaper: processes rooted in removed worktrees/scratchpads outlive their trees — 42 found in one sweep
description:
## Context
2026-08-09: hevyd-c9h's orphan (*:14877, 13 days, wildcard-bound, hammering a real API on a stale key — and the entire cause of drift bug dpbn) turned out to be one instance of a CLASS: a follow-up scan found 41 MORE processes running from deleted worktree/scratchpad cwds (node preview servers ~57MB each ≈2.2GB, a watch loop, a stale shell), some 6 days old. Worktree removal deletes the TREE; nothing reaps the PROCESSES. Builders legitimately start servers to test; the leak is structural.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reap at the right layers: (a) worktree removal path (the orchestrator merge-cleanup sequence and/or WorktreeRemove hook) kills processes whose cwd/exe is under the tree being removed, verified-negation style; (b) a periodic sweep on the keep (agents/bin/, pattern: cwd matches .claude/worktrees/*(deleted) or */scratchpad/*) — candidate to fold into the keep-side health watcher family
- [ ] The sweep NEVER matches live worktrees or the session's own processes (the deleted-cwd + scratchpad-path predicates are the safety); test proves a live-worktree process survives

title: a1111: inpaint NaN crash on MPS — missing --upcast-attn
description:
## Context

A1111 install on pico (dotfiles-rp0) shipped without enabling the
"Upcast cross attention layer to float32" setting. User attempted SDXL
inpainting immediately after install and hit:

```
NansException: A tensor with NaNs was produced in Unet. This could be
either because there's not enough precision to represent the picture,
or because your video card does not support half type. Try setting the
"Upcast cross attention layer to float32" option in Settings > Stable
Diffusion or using the --no-half commandline argument to fix this.
Time taken: 13.8 sec.
```

Known MPS issue with SDXL inpainting — the cross-attention layer
underflows to NaN at fp16 precision.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh A1111 install on Apple Silicon via mac.setup.sh (as shipped
   in rp0)
2. Load SDXL base 1.0 model
3. Open Img2Img tab → Inpaint sub-tab
4. Upload any image, draw a mask, run generation
5. After ~14 seconds, NansException raised; no output produced

## Fix

The error message itself recommends two options: (a) Settings > Stable
Diffusion > "Upcast cross attention layer to float32" toggle, or
(b) `--no-half` CLI arg. The Settings toggle is targeted (~minor
perf hit on the cross-attention layer only); --no-half is heavy
(doubles model memory).

A1111 1.10 has NO CLI flag for the Settings toggle — only the toggle
itself, which lives in `config.json` as `upcast_attn: true`. Created
`~/dotfiles/a1111/config.json` with the toggle pre-set; mac.setup.sh
installs it on fresh-Mac rebuild (only if config.json doesn't already
exist — preserves UI-saved settings on re-runs). Synced to pico's live
config.json + kickstarted LaunchAgent.

(Initial attempt added `--upcast-attn` to COMMANDLINE_ARGS; A1111
rejected it as unrecognized. Reverted to config.json-based fix.)

## Regression guard

- **Structural**: `~/dotfiles/a1111/config.json` is the seed file
  mac.setup.sh installs on fresh-Mac bootstrap. Future installs get
  the upcast_attn toggle automatically.
- **Documentation**: README.md in `~/dotfiles/a1111/` lists config.json
  in the files table with the reason.
- **Code comment**: `webui-user.sh` notes that the Settings toggle (no
  CLI flag) is needed for SDXL inpainting on MPS and points at
  `a1111/config.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] config.json seeded with upcast_attn=true in dotfiles
- [x] mac.setup.sh installs the seed (idempotent: only when missing)
- [x] Pico's live config.json updated
- [x] LaunchAgent kickstarted; A1111 boots cleanly with new config
- [x] README documents the file + reason
- [ ] User verifies SDXL inpainting now succeeds (their re-test confirms)
close_reason: done

title: ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh: generalize to --target / --probe-path / --expect so it can keep the pico agentgateway tunnel too
description:
Parent: dotfiles-ogkz.

ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh hardcodes three things that make it fleet-proxy-only:
  - target `127.0.0.1:$PORT` (line ~160, the -L spec)
  - probe path `/api/health` (probe(), line ~82)
  - success code 200 (three case statements)

The gateway tunnel needs target=100.72.47.4:17017, path=/claude/v1/models, expect=401.

Add --target HOST:PORT, --probe-path PATH, --expect CODE. Defaults MUST keep the
existing fleet-proxy behavior byte-identical (127.0.0.1:$PORT, /api/health, 200).

Preserve every existing guard, they are all load-bearing and each was paid for:
  - the three-valued probe and the "capture then substitute only when EMPTY" comment
    (a naive `|| echo 000` prints 000 TWICE and lands in the blocked branch)
  - FORWARD_PAT ownership + pidfile + pgrep re-adoption. NOTE: FORWARD_PAT embeds the
    target, so it must be built from the new --target or two tunnels will see each
    other as their own and kill each other. This is the single most important
    correctness point in this bead.
  - ExitOnForwardFailure=yes (without it ssh exits 0 on a failed bind)
  - never kill a listener we did not start

Also extend agents/scheduler/test-*.sh coverage (or add one) for: defaults unchanged,
--expect 401 treats 200 as BLOCKED, and two concurrent tunnels with different targets
do not adopt each other's pid.

⚠️ pre-commit runs the matching suite; core.hooksPath must be set in the worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] --target / --probe-path / --expect implemented; defaults byte-identical in behavior
- [ ] FORWARD_PAT is target-derived and two-tunnel isolation is TESTED, not asserted
- [ ] test suite green, and a mutant (break the isolation) is OBSERVED to fail it
- [ ] shellcheck + bash -n clean
notes:
## Scrutiny — 2026-08-03: FIX-FIRST (independent general-purpose reviewer, read-only)

IMPLEMENTATION SOUND — no code change required. The reviewer could not construct a
cross-kill. Verified: defaults byte-identical (NEWPAT == the old literal, and both
live callers pulse-dispatch-remote.sh:794,1302 pass --port 7100 only); pidfile
transition safe (old local-forward.pid orphaned, never read, pgrep re-adopts via the
identical pattern); :1701 vs :17017 isolate under real pgrep (delimiters both sides);
--target/--port in either order give identical pattern+pidfile; IPv6 and space-bearing
targets rejected exit 64; same-port-different-target hits ExitOnForwardFailure exit 1,
never a kill; re_escape itself correct over 13 metachars with negative fuzz;
trichotomy + --expect 000 rejection + ExitOnForwardFailure mutants each die of the bug
they name; harness claim true (only curl/ssh shimmed, pgrep/kill real).

THREE TEST/DOC DEFECTS:

1. re_escape has ZERO coverage. Neutering it to an identity function: PASS 26/26.
   The property is real — with real pgrep on a real process table, an unescaped
   pattern for 100.72.47.4:17017 also matched a DIFFERENT forward (3210491 3210539)
   where the escaped one matched exactly one. No live cross-kill today only because
   127.0.0.1 and 100.72.47.4 differ in LENGTH. Guard gap, repo rule 1.

2. Cases 24/25/26 degenerate-passable: A_PID/B_PID re-read with no -n assertion, so
   `alive ""` reads dead. The author self-reported case 25 and was CONFIRMED. But 25
   is NOT unfailable — under M5 (hardwire only our_pid discovery, leaving NEWPID
   correct) case 25 was the SOLE detector with the right symptom. Keep it, de-vacuum
   it.

3. The header mutant->case map is wrong in BOTH entries: it credits case 23 with
   "down B" but 23 is down A, and the real down-B case (25) is exactly what M2 does
   not kill. Measured M1 kills 22/23/24/25/26; M2 kills 22/23/24/26. Repo rule 2.

4. Also folded in: --expect "" silently defaults to 200 while --port "" is loud —
   binding because dotfiles-xp57 writes systemd units passing these flags.

Out of scope, left alone: pgrep not -u scoped (pre-existing, so an identical ssh -L
from another of the five VPS accounts is adopted; the kill then fails EPERM = safe,
unless same UID); missing-flag-value rc=1-not-64.

Agent resumed. Gate NOT cleared until the re_escape mutant is observed dying.
close_reason: Flags --target / --probe-path / --expect added; defaults byte-identical for the fleet proxy (verified live on main: 'status' -> exit 0, up (200)). Scrutiny FIX-FIRST resolved: the re_escape guard gap is closed by new case 28 (two same-length targets, pidfiles removed so only the pgrep pattern decides) — the orchestrator independently re-verified the neutered-re_escape mutant DYING at case 28, with the mutation asserted applied before interpreting the result. Cases 24-28 de-vacuumed with -n assertions on both pids; the mutant->case map re-measured rather than recalled; empty flag values now exit 64 naming the systemd-unit hazard they prevent. 28/28 on main.

title: zig (Mac): tailscale binary absent despite mac.setup.sh installing it and two aliases depending on it
description:
## Context

`zig` (this Mac) has **no `tailscale` binary at all**, confirmed 2026-08-01 while probing
the fleet for the `dotfiles-1r6k` parity audit.

That contradicts three things in the repo:

1. `mac.setup.sh` lists `tailscale` in its `brew install` line and later runs
   `sudo brew services start tailscale`.
2. `bash/.bash_aliases` defines `ssh-zig` and `ssh-pico` as
   `ssh ...@$(tailscale ip -4 <host> || echo <host>)`. With no binary the substitution
   falls through to the bare hostname every time — the aliases "work" only because of the
   fallback, and only where DNS happens to resolve.
3. `agents/infra.md` describes the tailnet as the path to `zig-computer` and `pico`.

Concrete consequence measured during the audit: reaching `zig-computer` over the tailnet
address `100.98.174.21` **timed out**, and the probe had to fall back to the public IP
`51.81.33.136`; `pico` was only reachable via an SSH hop through `zig-computer`.

Note `dotfiles-406` records "zig (work laptop) deferred from tailnet at user's discretion".
**If that is still the intent, this is not a bug — it is an undocumented deliberate state,
and the three references above are the thing to fix.** Resolve which it is before acting.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
command -v tailscale        # -> nothing
ssh-zig                     # silently uses bare hostname, not the tailnet address
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] decide and record: is `zig` deliberately off the tailnet, or is this drift?
- [ ] if deliberate — `mac.setup.sh`, the `ssh-*` aliases, and `agents/infra.md` are
      updated to say so, and the aliases stop pretending to resolve a tailnet address
- [ ] if drift — tailscale installed and the box rejoined, with `ssh-zig` / `ssh-pico`
      demonstrated working over the tailnet
- [ ] `dotfiles-406` updated or closed to match the outcome

title: spec: THE CONDUIT — boundary questions route to the seneschal; Zig gets only the remainder
description:
## 1. Overview
THE CONDUIT — boundary-question routing through the seneschal. Zig's directive
(2026-08-10 ~09:15 PT, via seneschal): seats that end a molt, finish a pulse
tick, or complete a deliverable currently raise their "what next?" / "review?"
questions at Zig directly (AskUserQuestion) or push him (P1 `human:` bead +
push). Route the ROUTABLE portion to the seneschal instead: the seat asks the
conduit; the seneschal answers what docket order, standing rulings, and brief
context can answer, and brings only the genuine remainder to Zig. "You should
be the one receiving that and handling what makes sense and bringing the rest
to me... the central conduit."

Sources (1.1): the directive relay (seneschal peer message, consul session
c417e95a); AGENTS.md "Surfacing to Zig" + autonomous-loop exception; seneschal
charter + /seneschal skill; dotfiles-7fik (the POST — R2 message shape, R3
delivery-at-wake); dotfiles-h1oa + its Zig-ruled OQs (docket tick, ALWAYS-FIRE,
dispatch allowed); pulse-escalate.sh ladder; pulse-inject.sh spawn-if-absent;
agents/hooks/pre-ask-user-question-seat-guard.sh (interactive:false blocking).

NOT covered: outward-facing approval (htqt owns it); the POST substrate itself
(7fik owns it); seneschal dispatch authority (unchanged: none); laurels;
mid-task questions inside a live Zig conversation (unchanged — a seat talking
to Zig asks Zig).

## 2. Current State / Baseline
- Interactive seats at a boundary: AskUserQuestion at Zig (AGENTS.md "Surfacing
  to Zig") — 🔔 in the lexicon; PushNotification alongside when he may be away.
- Unstaffed ticks: NEVER block on AskUserQuestion — file P1 `human:` bead +
  push Zig, end the tick (AGENTS.md autonomous-loop exception; enforced for
  interactive:false seats by pre-ask-user-question-seat-guard.sh).
- Escalation machinery: pulse-escalate.sh (bounce floor, molt-refusal watcher)
  files P1 `human:` beads + pushes Zig directly.
- The seneschal: daily 06:44 PT brief from live cross-repo reads; ends on
  AskUserQuestion at Zig when items are blocked; NO dispatch authority; writes
  only refs/seneschal-brief.md. Today it is a pull-based daily surface — seats
  do not push questions to it.
- spawn-if-absent: pulse-inject.sh creates the target window per tick if
  missing and injects a real user turn (the --cmd grant); hevyd-inject reuses
  the pattern. Transient works-gate timers prove ad-hoc spawn works.
- Cross-session SendMessage: live P2P, exists, used fleet-wide today.
- dotfiles-h1oa (ruled): consul's daily docket tick resumes the lane without
  Zig — the sibling mechanism that REMOVES a class of "what next" asks by
  making the docket self-driving. The conduit handles the asks that remain.
- dotfiles-7fik (spec'd, unbuilt): mail spools + delivery-at-wake; R3 forbids
  injection into running contexts; message shape {ts, from-seat, to|channel,
  body, ref?}.

## 3. Changes and Decisions
- C1 ROUTING RULE (the directive): at a boundary (molt-end/offboard, tick-end,
  deliverable-complete), a seat classifies its pending question ROUTABLE vs
  ZIG-ONLY (table in §4). Routable → the seneschal. Zig-only → exactly today's
  paths. Why: Zig's attention is the estate's scarcest resource; most boundary
  questions are answerable from recorded state.
- C2 GRACEFUL LADDER (constraint 1): seneschal live → SendMessage; absent →
  spawn-if-absent (pulse-inject pattern, real user turn carrying the
  question-delivery prompt); spawn fails → FAIL-OPEN to Zig via today's path.
  Never silent, never a lost question.
- C3 TICK DOCTRINE PRESERVED (constraint 2): unstaffed ticks still never block.
  Their escalation gains a seneschal-notify branch for routable items; Zig-only
  items keep P1 bead + push-Zig unchanged.
- C4 SENESCHAL ANSWERS ONLY FROM RECORD (constraint 3): an answer must cite its
  source — a docket position, a standing ruling (bead id), a brief section, a
  prior Zig decision. No citable source → escalate to Zig. If the answer would
  require NEW dispatch, the seneschal names the owning seat and the bead; it
  spawns no builders. This keeps the charter: route, never dispatch, never
  invent policy.
- C5 POST CO-DESIGN (constraint 4): the conduit message shape IS the 7fik R2
  mail shape ({ts, from-seat, to:seneschal, body, ref}). Phase A (now): live
  SendMessage + durable fallback recorded on the asking seat's bead/handoff.
  Phase B (when 7fik lands): mail to the seneschal spool is the durable record,
  SendMessage remains the live nudge; dedupe by ref. One channel doctrine, no
  competing second substrate.
- C6 SEAMS (constraint 5, Works implements): seat-molt/onboard opening-prompt
  templates; /pulse tick-end; /offboard "What's next"; pulse-escalate.sh +
  escalate.conf; /seneschal skill + charter text; pre-ask-user-question-seat-
  guard.sh redirect text; AGENTS.md "Surfacing to Zig" section.

## 4. Formal Specification
CLASSIFICATION (routable → seneschal):
  what-next / docket-order at a boundary; questions a standing ruling already
  answers; cross-seat coordination (who owns X); review-requests whose
  acceptance is mechanical/recorded; "may I proceed" where authority is already
  granted in writing.
ZIG-ONLY (today's paths, unchanged):
  taste calls; irreversible or outward-facing (htqt); security-sensitive; new
  spend/authority beyond a recorded grant; scope changes; anything the
  seneschal cannot answer WITH A CITATION (default-escalate — uncertainty fails
  toward Zig, never toward autonomy).

MESSAGE (Phase A live / Phase B mail body, same fields):
  {ts, from_seat, boundary: molt-end|tick-end|deliverable|other,
   question, options?: [..], refs: [bead ids / handoff path], urgency: now|wake}

LADDER (asking-seat side, pseudocode):
  if in live conversation with Zig: ask Zig directly (out of scope).
  classify(question) == zig_only → today's path (AskUserQuestion or bead+push).
  else:
    if seneschal reachable (ListAgents / socket) → SendMessage(question)
    elif spawn_if_absent(seneschal) succeeds → deliver via the spawn prompt
    else → FAIL-OPEN: today's path + loud record of the conduit failure.
  molting seats DO NOT WAIT for an answer: record the question durably
  (bead comment / handoff / Phase-B mail), then molt; the successor reads the
  answer at onboard. Only staffed interactive seats may block awaiting reply.

SENESCHAL ANSWER CONTRACT:
  answer := {verdict, citation (bead id | ruling | brief section | docket pos),
             remainder?: what goes to Zig and when (immediate vs next brief)}
  uncited answer is INVALID — the asking seat treats it as escalate-pending.
  Zig-remainder batching: urgency=now → immediate AskUserQuestion/push from the
  seneschal session; urgency=wake → next daily brief.
  Every routed question + answer leaves a durable trace (Phase A: comment on
  the asking seat's bead or handoff; Phase B: the mail spool is the trace).

LOOP SAFETY: the seneschal's own boundary questions go directly to Zig (never
route to self). The conduit adds no new authority anywhere: it changes WHO
FIELDS the question first, not who may decide anything.

## 5. Test Cases (>=10)
TEST T1 routable-molt-what-next
INPUT: seat ends molt with docket question; seneschal live
EXPECTED: SendMessage delivered; answer cites docket/ruling; Zig not pinged
RATIONALE: the core routing path.
TEST T2 taste-call-passthrough
INPUT: boundary question classified taste
EXPECTED: today's Zig path used; seneschal not consulted
RATIONALE: Zig-only class bypasses the conduit entirely.
TEST T3 spawn-if-absent
INPUT: seneschal session absent; routable question
EXPECTED: spawn fires (pulse-inject pattern); question delivered as real user
turn; answered post-onboard
RATIONALE: constraint 1 graceful path.
TEST T4 fail-open
INPUT: spawn itself fails (tmux/unit error)
EXPECTED: direct Zig path fires + loud conduit-failure record; question never lost
RATIONALE: never silent, never lost.
TEST T5 tick-routable
INPUT: unstaffed tick ends with routable item
EXPECTED: seneschal notified; NO AskUserQuestion in tick window; tick ends per
ledger discipline
RATIONALE: constraint 2 — tick doctrine intact.
TEST T6 tick-zig-only
INPUT: unstaffed tick hits Zig-only item
EXPECTED: P1 human: bead + push Zig, unchanged
RATIONALE: the conduit narrows nothing about Zig's channel for his items.
TEST T7 citation-required
INPUT: seneschal answer lacking a citation
EXPECTED: asking seat treats as escalate-pending; question stays open
RATIONALE: C4 — no invented policy.
TEST T8 no-dispatch
INPUT: routable what-next whose real answer is "build X"
EXPECTED: seneschal names owning seat + bead; spawns nothing
RATIONALE: charter unchanged.
TEST T9 molt-no-wait
INPUT: molting seat sends question, molts immediately
EXPECTED: question durably recorded; successor finds answer at onboard; no
wedged pre-molt context
RATIONALE: molt latency must not grow; delivery-at-wake semantics.
TEST T10 phase-b-dedupe
INPUT: mail + SendMessage nudge both carry ref R
EXPECTED: seneschal answers once (dedupe by ref)
RATIONALE: C5 — one channel doctrine across the seam.
TEST T11 self-loop
INPUT: seneschal's own boundary question
EXPECTED: routes to Zig directly
RATIONALE: loop safety.
TEST T12 seat-guard-compat
INPUT: interactive:false seat (marshal) at tick end with routable item
EXPECTED: guard still blocks AskUserQuestion; seneschal-notify branch used;
no behavioral regression for Zig-only items
RATIONALE: C3/C6 — the guard's redirect text gains the conduit, loses nothing.

### 4.b DECIDED SHARPENINGS (/check 2026-08-10, trail dotfiles-en86 — full rationale in bead comments)
- BOUNCE VERDICT (OQ-02): the seneschal re-classifies every arrival; zig-only
  arrivals are bounced to the asker with the class citation + logged to the
  brief. Answer contract verdicts: answered | bounced | escalated.
- CITATION ROOTS (OQ-03): a conduit answer is NEVER an admissible root; every
  chain terminates in a Zig ruling, decision bead, or committed doc.
- DEADLINE / FLOOR (OQ-04, Zig-adjacent): seneschal-notify runs BESIDE the
  pulse-escalate floor — P1 human: bead files immediately; push-to-Zig deferred
  conduit_answer_deadline_minutes (escalate.conf, default 60) for urgency=now,
  next-brief for wake; unanswered past deadline → push fires as today. Clock
  lives in pulse-escalate's conduit watcher, never the asking seat.
- ADVISORY HEADER (OQ-07): every answer carries 'advisory: routing /
  authority: none', machine-readable.
- QUEUE (OQ-08): oldest-first drain, per-turn cap 5, molt-safe cursor;
  spawn-if-absent serialized by has-window check under flock.
- AGING (OQ-09): answers carry as-of ts; a successor re-validates the citation
  when >6h old or the cited bead changed status.
- ZIG-LIVE PREDICATE (OQ-10): a real Zig turn in THIS window within the
  current session = live conversation; else unstaffed for routing.
- REF (OQ-13): bead id when one exists, else <seat>-<session8>-<seq>.

TEST T13 misclassified-arrival
INPUT: zig-only question sent to conduit
EXPECTED: bounced with class citation; brief logs it; Zig path then used
RATIONALE: OQ-02 — receiving side owns classification.
TEST T14 wedged-seneschal-deadline
INPUT: delivered question; seneschal 🧠 never answers
EXPECTED: P1 bead exists from t0; push fires at deadline; nothing swallowed
RATIONALE: OQ-04 — deferred, never suppressed.
TEST T15 burst-drain
INPUT: 8 questions land in one window
EXPECTED: oldest-first, cap 5 per turn, none orphaned across a seneschal molt
RATIONALE: OQ-08 queue semantics.
TEST T16 superseded-citation
INPUT: successor acts on 7h-old answer whose cited bead closed
EXPECTED: re-validation fires (br show) before acting
RATIONALE: OQ-09 aging.
TEST T17 phase-cutover-dedupe
INPUT: question in flight via SendMessage as Phase B mail goes live; same ref
EXPECTED: answered once
RATIONALE: OQ-13 ref + C5 one-channel doctrine.
TEST T18 concurrent-spawn-race
INPUT: two seats find seneschal absent simultaneously
EXPECTED: one spawn wins (flock); both questions reach the surviving session
RATIONALE: OQ-08 spawn serialization.

## 6. Open Questions — ALL DECIDED (/check 2026-08-10)
14/14 decided. OQ-01/05/06 ruled by Zig (AskUserQuestion via seneschal,
2026-08-10 ~09:30 PT): narrow charter amendment YES (append-only cited
comments on conduit-question beads only); urgency=now = PushNotification +
brief entry, NO standing AskUserQuestion from the conduit. OQ-02/03/04,
07-12, 13-14 decided per author recommendations (OQ-14 modified: baseline
pre-impl, review +2w). Full decisions with rationale: bead comments +
trail bead dotfiles-en86. Readiness: this bead's --notes.

## 7. Future Considerations
- Standing-rulings INDEX the seneschal answers from directly (Phase C).
- 7fik channels as ruling-broadcast rooms.
- THE MAILMAN (sibling spec, Zig directive 2026-08-10 ~10:15 PT): the reverse
  direction — seneschal-curated delivery of arriving mail to RUNNING seats at
  safe boundaries. Specced separately; shares the message shape, the
  deferred-never-suppressed doctrine, and the source registry.
- The pattern generalizes (Works fielding build questions) only after the
  seneschal instance proves citation discipline holds.
- h1oa's docket tick + this conduit should shrink consul boundary questions
  toward zero; measure per OQ-14 before generalizing.
