title: pulse-dispatch-remote --dry-run is not dry: it creates a real tmux window on marketing-vps, types into it, and makes a paid claude call
description:
Investigated 2026-08-03 after Zig noticed `di-monday` and `di-wednesday` windows on marketing-vps that he had not opened and that were not due to run.

## Context
Zig hypothesized unit tests. The tests are NOT the cause and are clean:
  - test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh stubs ssh (records to ssh.log) and uses a FAKE row
    name `di-tuesday`, so it can never create a real di-monday/di-wednesday window.
  - test-pulse-inject.sh drives a real tmux binary but only ever creates throwaway
    sessions `pulse-test-$$` / `pulse-ready-$$` / …, and its header explicitly notes
    real injection happens "only in the `work` and `zig-computer` tmux sessions".

The real cause is `--dry-run`.

## Evidence
Run dirs on the box match the pane shell start times almost exactly:

    ~/work/pulse-dispatch/20260731T234006Z-di-monday      -> shell started 23:40:36 (+30s)
    ~/work/pulse-dispatch/20260731T235721Z-di-wednesday   -> shell started 23:57:54 (+33s)

Each contains ONLY `claude-probe.txt` (18 bytes: "claude\nPROBE_RC=0"), the artifact
of preflight A4 — i.e. these runs stopped before dispatching. And the timers did NOT
fire them: pulse-di-monday.timer last ran Mon 2026-07-27, pulse-di-wednesday.timer last
ran Wed 2026-07-29. Jul 31 was a FRIDAY.

Transcripts show many `--row di-monday … --dry-run` / `--row di-wednesday … --dry-run`
invocations from the dashboard-dev-interrupted sessions.

## The actual defect
`--dry-run` stops before INJECTING, but everything before that point is real. The
script says so itself (line 1459: "Everything above ran for real"), yet the flag NAME
promises the opposite, and the side effects outlive the run:

    line 528   REMOTE_WINDOW="$ROW"
    line 1369  tmux new-window -d -P -F ... -n "$REMOTE_WINDOW"   <- creates work:<row>
    line 1371  note "created remote window ..."
    line 1436  tmux send-keys -t "$PANE"  (the A4 probe, typed into the pane)
    line ~1414 A7: timeout 90 claude -p "reply with exactly: PONG"   <- a REAL, PAID call
    line 1463  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then ... exit

So a dry run: opens the tunnel, refreshes four tiers of repos, CREATES A PERSISTENT
TMUX WINDOW on a shared production box, types a command into it, and spends tokens.
The window is never cleaned up, so every dry run leaves litter that looks to a human
like a scheduled tick fired early — which is exactly how this surfaced.

## Steps to Reproduce
    agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh --row di-monday \
      --dir /home/ubuntu/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted --dry-run
    ssh marketing-vps "tmux list-windows -t =work"   # work:di-monday now exists

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a --dry-run leaves NO window it created (create -> probe -> remove), OR the flag
      is renamed to something that does not promise inertness (e.g. --preflight)
- [ ] the A7 paid call under --dry-run is either documented at the call site as a real
      cost or gated behind an explicit opt-in
- [ ] --dry-run output NAMES every mutation it performed, so the operator can see the
      window was created rather than discovering it days later
- [ ] a regression test asserts the window count on the box is unchanged across a
      --dry-run (or that the creation is explicitly announced)
- [ ] the mutant (restore the leak) is OBSERVED to fail that test
close_reason: A --dry-run now removes the tmux window it created, and ONLY that one. release_dry_run_window() gates on DRY_RUN=1 AND REMOTE_WINDOW_CREATED=1 AND a well-formed @N id captured AT CREATION — it kills by id, never by name, because the tmux-status hook rewrites names and a row can legitimately own two windows. The agent found a SECOND ownership door I had not named in the brief: 'new-session -d -s work -n <row>' creates the row's window ALONG WITH the session, so list-windows then FINDS it and a created-only-via-new-window flag would have left a whole session behind; that branch was fire-and-forget and now reports PULSE_SESSION=created|existed, with anything unparseable leaving ownership UNCLAIMED. Idempotent, and called from the normal exit, from fail() before emit_result (preserving marker-is-last), and from the EXIT trap. When the control master is already down it does not fail silently — it warns 'DRY RUN LEFT LITTER' with the exact manual kill command. A7 kept and its cost stated in --help and in the run's mutation block: gating the billed probe would rebuild the blind spot it exists to close (the 2026-07-27 outage survived A4 for a day precisely BECAUSE every run that day was --dry-run, and any gate would default off in timer units). Suite 239 -> 267 assertions. Orchestrator re-verified independently: my first ownership mutant was INVALID (it broke the script globally, failing unrelated preflights with verdict '<none>' — a mutant dying of the wrong cause); redone surgically (created-gate removed, id captured unconditionally, bash -n clean) it dies 264/3 on exactly 'a dry run NEVER kills a window it did not create' plus the unclaimed-ownership case.

title: bug: gdoc.sh returns exit 0 on failure — a bogus doc id, and a read of a tabbed doc, both look like success
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while verifying dotfiles-dt6c, by running a negative control on
the probe rather than trusting a clean-looking result.

TWO FAILURES, BOTH EXIT 0:

1. BOGUS DOC ID -> exit 0.
     gdoc.sh tabs 1ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ
   dumps TypeScript SOURCE LINES from the error-mapping code (case 401 /
   GoogleConfigError / case 403 / GooglePermissionError) and exits 0. A caller
   checking the exit code concludes the doc exists.

2. READ OF A TABBED DOC -> empty output, exit 0.
     gdoc.sh read 1YF_JiO3pcvcFR4x72NNJozGmsB8FMiv30PliJmZqEJk
   returns NOTHING and exits 0. The doc is real and has content — `gdoc.sh tabs`
   on the same id returns [OLD, "Jul 22"]. `read` presumably needs a tab id on a
   tabbed doc, but it reports absence rather than saying so.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ANNOYANCE: this is dotfiles-cxle's class, in a tool
the weekly-report skill DEPENDS ON to publish. An automated caller cannot
distinguish "doc is empty" from "doc does not exist" from "credentials failed" —
all three are exit 0 with no usable stderr. The weekly-report pipeline publishes
through this shim on a live Tuesday timer.

It is also generator (a) from dotfiles-cxle exactly: EXIT CODE != EFFECT.

FIX: map every error path to a nonzero exit and a one-line human-readable stderr
message (never a source dump). For `read` on a tabbed doc, either default to the
first tab or fail loudly telling the caller to pass a tab — silence is the one
unacceptable option.

Relates: dotfiles-cxle (the failure class), dotfiles-dt6c (found during its
verification), dotfiles-gify (the sibling silent-drift in the same skill).

title: decision: AGENTS.md's fetch+merge wins over /commit's pull --rebase — by recency and by mechanism (Zig, 2026-08-01)
description:
## Context

dotfiles-mjln found /commit and AGENTS.md giving opposite git instructions, both in
the loaded tier. Zig's call: "i think agents.md wins. check which one is most recent
and side with that one."

Recency checked with `git log -S` on both strings:
  AGENTS.md  "merge, never rebase, NEVER stash"  -> 1f23c02, 2026-08-01 (TODAY)
             ":lock: hooks: make the shared-working-tree hazard unreachable"
  /commit    "Always pull --rebase, THEN push"   -> a2f9e8d, 2026-07-28
             ":lock: commit: pull --rebase before every push - multi-machine fleet now"

AGENTS.md's rule is 4 days newer. It is also the one with a mechanism behind it
(pre-shared-tree-guard.sh, 422 lines) and a measured 3-row table, and 1f23c02's whole
purpose was to make this exact hazard unreachable.

## Decision

AGENTS.md wins. `git fetch origin && git merge --no-edit origin/main` is the fleet
rule. /commit's `pull --rebase` guidance is removed.

## Why -- and what must NOT be lost

/commit's rule was not wrong about its OWN problem. a2f9e8d was written for
multi-machine push races ("never push blind") after commits were stranded on
marketing-vps. That concern is real and survives: fetch+merge satisfies it just as
well as rebase did. So this is a change of VERB, not the abandonment of the
discipline. The /commit fix must keep:
  - never push blind; a rejected push means another machine committed
  - the detached-HEAD push proof (compare against `git ls-remote`, never
    `git rev-parse HEAD`) -- unrelated to rebase, and the densest local fact
    in that skill
  - the linear-history preference stated as a preference, not an instruction to rebase

## Reversibility

Prompt-wording only, fully reverted by `git revert`. The hook is unchanged either
way -- pre-shared-tree-guard.sh already blocks the destructive verbs regardless of
which prose won.
close_reason: done

title: download: conflates binary upgrades with destructive repo regeneration — upgrade block unreachable on its own
description:
## Context

Discovered 2026-08-01 while updating binaries on `zig` (the Mac) after a 723-commit pull.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cd ~/azigler/dotfiles`
2. Run `./download.sh cursor` on a machine with FEWER Cursor extensions than the tracked
   list — observe `cursor/install_extensions.sh` shrinks, silently, and no upgrade runs.
3. Run `./download.sh` with no argument — observe it DOES run the binary upgrades, but also
   re-runs every destructive case from step 2.
4. There is no third invocation that does the upgrades alone.

## The defect (two parts)

**1. The upgrade block is unreachable on its own.**

`download.sh` with NO argument runs the binary upgrades (brew / rustup / bun / deno /
pnpm / claude / uv) AND THEN loops `for dir in */ .*/` running every `download()` case.
`download.sh <arg>` runs ONLY that case and skips the upgrades entirely. You either get
both or neither.

**2. Several of those cases are lossy writes against TRACKED files.**

- `cursor` / `vscode` — regenerate the tracked `install_extensions.sh` from whatever is
  installed ON THE CURRENT BOX. Running on a machine with a subset of extensions silently
  DELETES entries from the canonical list. The worst one: a silent, lossy,
  machine-dependent overwrite of shared state.
- `fonts` — re-downloads and extracts the Nerd Font tarball into tracked `fonts/`.
- `gnupg` / `ssh` — write `$(hostname -s).asc` / `.pub` into the repo. Public keys, not
  secrets, but repo churn on a PUBLIC repo.
- `zsh` / `tmux` / `blightmud` — `rm -rf` + re-clone. All gitignored, so harmless to git,
  but destroys live oh-my-zsh / antigen / tpm installs.

## Also stale

Last touched 2026-01-25 (`93cff5e`); `sync.sh` is 2026-07-27. It upgrades none of the
tooling added since: `br`, `bv`, biome, ruff, golangci-lint, gitleaks, goose, cursor,
nix / nix-direnv, oh-my-zsh, or the bun/npm globals.

## Resolution direction

Zig, 2026-08-01: move the upgrade block OUT into `mac.upgrade.sh`, leaving `download.sh` as
a pure vendor/fetch script. Consider also making the vendor cases opt-in rather than swept
by the bare `for dir` loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `download.sh` no longer performs binary upgrades
- [ ] the cursor/vscode extension-list regeneration is removed, made additive, or gated
      behind an explicit flag — a subset machine must not be able to silently shrink the
      tracked list
- [ ] README / CLAUDE.md reflect the new split
close_reason: Fixed in 85000d4 — upgrade block removed from download.sh (now vendor-only); cursor/vscode regeneration is additive with --prune opt-in, refuses on empty/missing CLI.

title: spec: the POST — mail, channels, broadcasts; IRC for the estate, delivery at wake
description:
## Context
Zig, 2026-08-09: 'we want broadcasts and channels and channel discovery and usage... channels are basically like IRC for them. peer-to-peer live messaging fills the rest of the gap.' The comms stack's durable middle layer, between beads (work) and SendMessage (live). Substrate spec; the hall's verbs (dy5o) and the skill (d54d) are surfaces consuming it.

## Formal Spec v1 (Fable, 2026-08-09)

R1 — SUBSTRATE: append-only files under ~/.local/state/harness/post/ (flows to demesne-side backup via the existing pull). mail/<seat>.jsonl (directed spool); channels/<name>.jsonl (topic log, the IRC room with history); channels/<name>.subs (subscriber seats, one per line); channels/INDEX.jsonl (the DISCOVERY registry: name, purpose, owner-seat, created — 'post channels' lists it). Per-seat read cursors (cursors/<seat>.json: per-spool offsets) — reading is catch-up-from-cursor, exactly IRC rejoin semantics.

R2 — VERBS (one lib, agents/lib/post.sh; hall + skills wrap it): post send <seat> <msg> (mail) · post publish <channel> <msg> (broadcast = append once, every subscriber sees it at next read — fan-out is a READ-side join, never N copies) · post channel create|join|leave|list (discovery via INDEX) · post read [--seat] (unread mail + subscribed channels since cursor, advances cursor) · post peek (no cursor advance). Message shape: {ts, from-seat, to|channel, body, ref?} — ref optionally cites a bead/commit so mail can point at work without BEING work.

R3 — DELIVERY AT WAKE, NEVER INJECTION. A seat reads its post at /onboard (a post read step beside the laurels head) and at natural boundaries. NOTHING pushes into a running context — reading is the seat's own act (the hall-never-types principle generalized). Live urgency uses SendMessage (P2P, exists) or push-to-Zig; the POST is durable, not immediate. The marshal reads mail at window start (d54d AC) — directives like 'focus harnessd tonight' re-weight the night.

R4 — THE COURT'S 📬: unread count = spool length minus cursor, computed by the hall directly from files (dumb glass, no daemon dependency; harnessd's mail_unread field — lman R-F named it nullable for exactly this — gets fed by the same computation when the bus wants it).

R5 — WHAT THE POST IS NOT: not a work queue (beads own claim semantics — Yegge's stack lacks a bead store, ours does not; recorded refusal, reversal trigger = a real non-work queue need); not real-time (SendMessage is); not outward (htqt governs anything leaving the estate); not unbounded (channels declare retention in INDEX; the ledger-trim idiom applies).

R6 — HYGIENE: channels are low-volume announcement/topic rooms (freeze notices, campaign coordination, a seat's findings feed). Creating a channel is cheap but REGISTERED (INDEX entry with purpose — an unregistered spool file is a finding). The Remembrancer reads channel logs during dreams (cross-seat patterns in conversation, not just handoffs).

## Test cases
T1 send->read advances cursor, peek does not. T2 publish once, three subscribers each see it once (read-side fan-out, file appears once on disk). T3 join mid-history: catch-up from join point (cursor initialized at join, not zero — IRC rejoin). T4 discovery lists INDEX with purpose. T5 unread count matches spool-minus-cursor; hall renders it. T6 an unregistered channel file is a validator/audit finding. T7 marshal window-start reads mail and the directive reaches the night plan (integration, marshal build). T8 retention trims per INDEX declaration, cursor stays valid. T9 a ref-bearing message renders its bead pointer. T10 concurrent send+read: append-only + cursor semantics never lose a message (flock or O_APPEND argument).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] post.sh + suite + >=3 mutants (cursor-not-advanced, fanout-copies-per-subscriber, unregistered-channel-invisible), pre-commit wired
- [ ] /onboard gains the post-read step; hall's 📬 goes live (consumes this, dy5o)
- [ ] d54d's skill teaches the verbs + layer doctrine; TOOLKIT entry
- [ ] Impl beads author-marked Fleet: yes — the POST is ideal drain work (internal, crisp, testable)
notes: AMENDMENT (Zig, 2026-08-09, mid-migration session): the channel model is closer to BBS / forums / newsgroups than IRC — durable topical boards with threaded/append posts agents catch up on at wake, not ephemeral realtime chat. Reframe the spec's channel section around that: persistence and catch-up-at-wake are the primitives, presence is not. Keep 'IRC for the estate' only as the discovery/naming vibe, not the delivery semantics. Related: the comms SKILL bead (see dotfiles-d54d + the new comms-skill bead filed today) covers the behavioral layer — find/swarm/create channels.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CORRECTION (Zig caught it, 2026-08-09): R5's clause 'Yegge's stack lacks a bead store, ours does not' is FALSE — Yegge BUILT beads; his stack runs queues ALONGSIDE beads, using queues for high-frequency transient flow (pipeline handoffs, merge items) where issue-per-item is too heavy. The refusal therefore stands on OUR deliberate collapse of work-flow into the bead store (one store one truth; beads carry evidence/deps/history that queue messages lack), NOT on Yegge's architecture. SHARPENED REVERSAL TRIGGER replacing the vague one: build a queue layer when we hit flow too high-frequency for issue-per-item — first visible candidate is the drain's own merge queue (69qr, currently in-memory serialization); if it ever needs durable cross-restart state, derive it from bead state rather than a second store. Read R5 with this comment; the description's clause is superseded.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: TAXONOMY SETTLED (Zig, 2026-08-09, final): Yegge's queue is a MERGE QUEUE — build machinery, not a communication layer at all. The comms coverage is exactly THREE layers and is COMPLETE with this spec: (1) BROADCAST = the IRC-like channels (this spec's R1/R2); (2) PEER-TO-PEER = Claude Code's own SendMessage (exists, nothing to build); (3) MAIL = directed spools (this spec). The merge queue lives where it always did — 69qr R2/R3's serialization point in the drain. This supersedes both the original R5 clause AND the earlier correction's reversal-trigger framing: there is no future 'queue layer' to trigger — a queue question is a DRAIN question, routed to 69qr.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: R3 FORK RESOLVED (Zig, 2026-08-10, AskUserQuestion via seneschal — the sf86 walk): DELIVERY-AT-WAKE stands as written; push-on-active and the urgent-flag hybrid are both REJECTED. The interaction contract, explicit per sf86's AC: live urgency is SendMessage (P2P, exists) or push-to-Zig — never the POST; the marshal's window-start mail read stands (a window start IS a wake, so directives like 'focus harnessd tonight' arrive with zero injection machinery); nothing ever pushes POST content into a running context. With this plus the BBS amendment and the settled 3-layer taxonomy, the spec has no open forks: /check-clear for build. Readiness child + cross-ref: see the bead named in the next comment.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Cross-ref per sf86 AC: the R3 walk's outcome lives in the previous comment; Implementation Readiness child = dotfiles-5z5n (build may proceed; d54d skill scope rides on it).

title: pulse-inject: make the verdict END-TO-END — send-keys failure still reports 'injected'
description:
## Context
Follow-up to dotfiles-q0qi, which added `PULSE_INJECT_RESULT=` to every terminal
path. That change is PATH-accurate: it truthfully reports which branch the script
took. It is not yet EFFECT-accurate.

Residual seam, flagged by the implementing agent and deliberately left open: if
the final `tmux send-keys` fails (the pane vanished between the readiness check and
the injection), the script still emits `injected` and exits 0. The verdict is then
wrong in exactly the direction the whole contract exists to prevent.

## Why it was scoped out (and why that was right)
Closing it means evaluating a condition the script has never evaluated, across ~20
live pulse timers. A false `failed` would make picod's daemon file a spurious P1
`human` bead on a dispatch that actually landed — trading a rare silent success for
a recurring false alarm, which is worse. dotfiles-q0qi was constrained to "purely
additive, exit codes unchanged," and this would have broken that.

picod is not exposed today: its verifier (ha-portal/src/verify.ts) independently
probes tmux for the window and a live claude pane after every dispatch, so a
send-keys failure that left no agent running is still caught on the picod side.
This bead is about making the PRIMITIVE honest for every other consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `send-keys` failure produces a distinct verdict (e.g. `failed-send-keys`) rather
  than `injected`
- The exit code for that path is decided deliberately and documented: staying 0
  keeps the fleet's current behaviour; a non-zero is more honest but changes it for
  ~20 live units. State which and why; do not change it incidentally.
- A test drives the failure (kill the pane between readiness and injection, or stub
  the tmux seam to fail only on send-keys) and asserts the new verdict
- NEGATIVE CONTROL: remove the new check, watch that test fail
- Watch the pulse ledgers for a week after rollout — if spurious `failed-*` verdicts
  appear, revert rather than tune

## Related — a latent test flake found in passing by dotfiles-q0qi
`tmux list-panes -a` IGNORES `-t` and lists the whole server, so the older cases
(PANE2, PANE3) in test-pulse-inject.sh match whichever session sorts first and pass
by luck of naming. The new cases use an explicit session_name match; the older
lookups were deliberately not refactored. They will flake if anyone renames those
test sessions.

title: safe_remote: macOS self-match — pgrep -af inside zsh -c wrapper matches its own cmdline (eviction probe false-positives, aborts matrix pre-flight)
description:
## What happened
First live bench-matrix pre-flight (cohort 1, 2026-06-11) aborted: safe_pkill_remote(pico,llama-server) reported survivors with a DIFFERENT PID each retry, while ssh pico pgrep -fl llama-server returns rc=1 (no real process).

## Root cause
safe_remote.sh runs: ssh HOST "pgrep -af 'PATTERN' ...". The remote command executes as zsh -c "...PATTERN..." — the wrapper's own cmdline contains the literal pattern. On Linux pgrep -a = print cmdline (harmless; pgrep excludes self/parent). On macOS/BSD pgrep -a = INCLUDE ANCESTORS in the match list — the wrapper shell (pgrep's parent) becomes matchable. Every probe matches its own ephemeral wrapper → infinite survivors → pre-flight abort. Unreachable in the bats suite (ssh mocked, Linux semantics).

## Steps to Reproduce
ssh pico 'pgrep -af "llama-server"' with no llama-server running → returns its own zsh -c wrapper PID. Repeat → different PID. bench-matrix.sh pre-flight eviction then aborts (log /tmp/bench-cohort1.log).

## Fix
In safe_remote.sh, neutralize self-match by bracketing the first alphanumeric char of the pattern before embedding: llama-server → [l]lama-server (regex matches real processes; the wrapper cmdline now contains the bracketed literal which the regex does not match). Apply in both safe_pgrep_remote and the pkill command. Drop nothing else.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] safe_pgrep_remote pico llama-server returns 0 (no match) with no real process, repeatedly
- [ ] Real-process detection still works (launch llama-server, probe finds it, pkill kills it)
- [ ] bats regression test: embedded pattern is bracket-neutralized (assert the ssh command string contains [l]lama-server)
- [ ] Full bats suite green
notes: Fixed orchestrator-direct (time-boxed unblock of the user-approved cohort-1 launch; deviation from delegation default noted). _safe_remote_neutralize brackets first alnum char of each |-branch; applied in pgrep+pkill embeddings. Live-verified on pico both directions; 14/14 bats (4 new regression tests pin the neutralized embedding + branch-wise bracketing + real-survivor detection). dotfiles d4703ea.

title: decision: accept agentgateway :17017 LAN exposure on pico (Zig, 2026-07-25)
description:
Context: pico's agentgateway `claude` listener binds *:17017 — reachable from
the home LAN, not just the tailnet. Verified: `curl http://192.168.1.149:17017/`
from pico's LAN address returns a gateway response; macOS application firewall
is DISABLED and pf is DISABLED. Anything joining the home wifi can proxy
requests through Zig's Anthropic account.

It CANNOT be fixed in config. Proven by `--validate-only` against BOTH v1.3.1
and v1.4.0-beta.1: `binds[]` accepts only `port`, `listeners`, `tunnelProtocol`
(+`mode` in 1.4). There is no listener- or config-level bind-address field. The
admin listener binds 100.72.47.4 only because `adminAddr` is a dedicated field.

Alternatives offered to Zig:
  (a) a macOS pf anchor allowing :17017 only from 100.64.0.0/10 / utun* —
      closes it without touching gateway config or breaking any session, but
      requires enabling pf, currently disabled
  (b) accept the exposure
  (c) an apiKey policy on the listener — expressible today, but breaks EVERY
      routed Claude Code session on zig-computer until each presents a key

DECISION (Zig): (b) — accept the LAN exposure. The home LAN is a trusted-enough
boundary and this is his own network.

Reversibility: HIGH and cheap. Option (a) remains available at any time and is
additive — a pf anchor can be added later without touching agentgateway, its
config, or any client. Nothing has been done that makes the fix harder.

Recorded rather than left implicit because a future audit WILL re-flag this;
this bead is the answer to "why is a public-ish listener still open." It is an
accepted risk with a named owner and a known remedy, not an oversight.

Distinct from the retained :7575 exposure (dotfiles-6wdw / dotfiles-ks1u), which
is INTERNET-facing and is being closed via the granola->linearb migration.
That one is NOT accepted; only this LAN-scoped one is.
notes:

Decision bead, enacted. Superseded in part by dotfiles-13qu.

Verified by an independent read-only recon agent against live system state, not
from the bead body. Closing as confirmed-resolved.

title: dispatch: tell long-running worktree subagents to commit incrementally
description:
## Context
2026-08-01, ifcompd wave 2. A worktree subagent writing a 6-file design spec was
killed by a server-side API error mid-write ("API Error: Server error
mid-response"). It had written 2 files (~18 KB) and committed NOTHING — the
default shape, since /dispatch's template says "commit on your worktree branch"
as a single end-of-task step.

Recovery worked (SendMessage resumed it with context intact, and it finished),
but only because the worktree still existed. Had cleanup run, or had the crash
been harder, the work was gone.

The resumed agent was told to commit after each file. It then produced 7 clean
incremental commits, all correctly trailered — no downside observed.

## The proposal
/dispatch's "Commit + push" block should add: for a dispatch expected to produce
multiple substantial artifacts, commit after each one rather than once at the end.
A crash then costs at most one artifact.

Deliberately a JUDGMENT CALL, not a blanket rule — a one-file surgical edit should
stay one commit, and "one bead = one commit" is the standing convention this has
to sit beside without contradicting. The framing that resolves it: incremental
commits on a WORKTREE branch are checkpoints, and the orchestrator's merge is what
makes them one unit of work in main's history.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /dispatch SKILL.md "Commit + push" block carries the guidance, scoped to
      multi-artifact dispatches
- [ ] The one-bead-one-commit convention is explicitly reconciled, not silently contradicted

## Write target
~/demesne — agents/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md (Commit + push block).

title: note: /pulse — the TIMER must express the cadence; a check is a guard, never the schedule
description:
## Context

Live failure in `~/investd`, 2026-08-01/02. Proposing this as an addition to the
global `/pulse` skill because it is a general loop-design trap, not an investd
quirk — filing rather than editing the fleet-wide skill unilaterally.

**What happened.** investd's row needed a 6-week cadence. systemd cannot express
"every 6th Wednesday", so the timer was set to poll **weekly** and the 6-week
cadence was placed in the row's `check`. Everything local passed: ledger lint
clean, proof token re-ran green, `harness-assert-registration` healthy.

The next morning Zig looked at his harnessd dashboard and asked: *"why does the
rebalance-tradfi pulse say next fire in 3 days? its every 6 weeks."*

**Root cause.** harnessd reads systemd's `NextElapseUSecRealtime` directly
(`internal/gen/parse.go` -> `internal/gen/loop.go:174`). It has no way to
distinguish a POLL from a FIRE. So the dashboard faithfully reported the poll,
while the real schedule lived only inside a bash string that nothing outside the
tick could read. **The timer was lying to every observer** — the dashboard,
`systemctl list-timers`, `systemd-analyze`, and the human.

## The rule worth adding to /pulse

**THE TIMER MUST EXPRESS THE CADENCE. A `check` is a safety gate, never the
schedule.** If anything has to read a row's `check` to learn when the loop runs,
the schedule is in the wrong place.

For a cadence systemd cannot express (any n-week period that is not 1, 2, or 4
weeks), **enumerate the dates** in the unit — `OnCalendar=` accepts explicit
timestamps and repeats freely. investd now lists 47 dates through 2031-12-24 and
`list-timers` reports the truth.

Enumeration has a real failure mode that must be guarded: when the list runs out
the timer **silently stops**. So the row's `check` keeps a `LAST` date and returns
**exit 3 (blocked)** past it, and the action files a `human:` bead once fewer than
3 slots remain. Silence is the one failure mode a loop must never have — which is
the same principle as the three-valued check the skill already teaches, applied to
the schedule rather than the trigger.

Side benefit, non-trivial: the poll design woke a full Claude session ~5 times per
cycle to do nothing.

## The general shape (worth naming in the skill)

This is the second instance in two days, in one project, of the same class:
**a component passing every local gate while being wrong about something only an
outside observer could see.** The other was a `done` proof token asserting
`count(*) >= 8 WHERE asof = current_date` — which passed for the WRONG REASON
(8 tickers had been fetched, but not the 8 the loop actually tracks, and one was a
day stale). Both were caught only by asking *what does the consumer see?* rather
than *does my assertion pass?*

Suggested placement: an anti-pattern bullet plus a short subsection under the
existing three-valued-check material, which is where the "silence is the enemy"
reasoning already lives.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/pulse` SKILL.md gains the timer-expresses-cadence rule with the enumeration
      recipe and the exhaustion guard
- [ ] Anti-pattern list gains "cadence hidden in the check / timer that polls"
- [ ] Cross-reference the proof-token distance material with the passed-for-the-
      wrong-reason instance
- [ ] TOOLKIT.md entry for /pulse updated if the anti-pattern line changes

title: pre-commit-checks: the done-proof scrutinize branch uses a bare grep -q 'SHIP' — the false-accept pre-bead-close already fixed and hoisted a shared matcher for
description:
## Context

`agents/hooks/pre-commit-checks.sh:347` accepts a pulse `done` proof of `kind:scrutinize`
if `br show <bead>` contains the substring `SHIP` **anywhere**:

```bash
if [ -z "$B" ] || ! { command -v br &>/dev/null && br show "$B" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'SHIP'; }; then
```

The sibling hook **in the same directory** already solved this. `pre-bead-close.sh:25-33`
holds a hardened matcher — `SCRUTINY_VERDICT_RE` anchored to a verdict line, plus a
line-wise `SCRUTINY_NEGATED_RE` for `NOT SHIP` — and it was deliberately hoisted into a
shared function, with this comment:

> *"Hoisted so --selftest and the gate itself share one definition — the 2026-06-09
> over-tightening shipped because the pattern was inline with no regression test to
> contradict it."*

The pulse gate never adopted it. So the fix, the reasoning, and the shared function all
already exist, ten lines away, in a file the same author wrote.

**Why it matters:** this is the gate enforcing `explore-len0`'s proof-token invariant —
that a `done` row carries proof with real verifier distance. A pulse tick can currently
self-certify `done` by pointing its scrutiny proof at **any bead whose text contains the
four letters SHIP**, including "needs scrutiny before we SHIP" and "Verdict: do NOT SHIP"
— both of which `pre-bead-close.sh`'s own `--selftest` matrix explicitly lists as FAIL.

Found 2026-08-01 by a cross-repo fleet audit dispatched from `~/explore`.

## Steps to Reproduce

Verified end-to-end against the live hook, unmutated, with `br` shimmed to replay real
`br show` output so a missing beads DB is not the variable:

1. Temp git repo with `refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl`; append
   `{"outcome":"done","proof":{"kind":"scrutinize","bead":"explore-89uu"}}`.
2. Shim `br show` to emit the real `br show explore-89uu` text — an **OPEN** bead with no
   scrutiny verdict of its own, whose body merely *quotes another bead's* SHIP.
3. Pipe the `git commit` PreToolUse JSON to `pre-commit-checks.sh` → **rc 0, COMMIT ALLOWED.**
4. **Positive control:** same run with `explore-6g3l` (no `SHIP` substring anywhere) →
   **rc 2, blocked.** The gate is live and firing; the matcher is what fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The scrutinize branch calls the same verdict logic as `pre-bead-close.sh` — source
      the shared matcher; do **not** re-inline a third copy.
- [ ] `test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` gains scrutinize cases: `Verdict: SHIP` → ALLOW;
      `do NOT SHIP` → BLOCK; `needs scrutiny before we SHIP` → BLOCK; empty `cmd` → BLOCK.
      All four are currently absent (cases 13-20 cover only artifact/commit/cmd/quiet).
- [ ] Mutating `grep -q 'SHIP'` to `true` makes the suite RED. It is currently green at
      58/58 with that mutation applied — that is the finding, and the regression test.
- [ ] The empty-`cmd`-proof mutant (also a survivor) is killed by a test.

Related: `explore-len0` (built this gate), `explore-a3zc` (a green suite is not evidence
the guards bite — this is a textbook instance), `dotfiles-cxle` (the class).
notes:
## Correction 2026-08-01

The close reason above names the follow-up bead as `dotfiles-mjf3`. **That id does not exist** — I wrote it before creating the bead and beads assigns ids at creation. The real id is **`dotfiles-2dez`** ("the scrutinize proof has no binding to the work").

Recording rather than quietly repairing, because a dangling bead citation is the exact class this session spent the day on (`explore-89uu`, `explore-6g3l`): a confidently-written reference that reads as valid until someone follows it.
close_reason:
FIXED and pushed (cf15d6c, in b918e153 verified via git ls-remote).

PRE-FIX REPRO WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, against the unmutated hook — three false-accepts, one control:
  an OPEN bead merely QUOTING another bead's 'Verdict: SHIP'  -> rc 0 ALLOWED
  '## Scrutiny — 2026-08-01: Verdict: do NOT SHIP'            -> rc 0 ALLOWED
  'needs scrutiny before we SHIP this'                        -> rc 0 ALLOWED
  CONTROL: no SHIP substring anywhere                         -> rc 2 BLOCKED
The control is what makes it a finding rather than a guess: the gate was live and firing, and the matcher was what failed. All three now rc 2; the two genuine forms (Verdict: SHIP, ## Scrutiny — OVERRIDE:) still rc 0.

THE FIX. agents/hooks/lib/scrutiny-verdict.sh — 44 lines, pure definitions, the matcher moved VERBATIM out of pre-bead-close.sh. Both hooks source it; no third copy. A dedicated lib rather than the existing lib/hook-helpers.sh because that is a 258-line command lexer and pre-bead-close.sh's --selftest branch runs BEFORE it sources anything; pulling a lexer in ahead of the selftest to get a 4-line matcher is the wrong dependency, and a small file lets the new runner key precisely on the matcher.

Both loaders FAIL CLOSED AND SCOPED: a missing lib defines a stub that returns 1 with a diagnostic naming the cause, so it can never read as 'verdict accepted', and it does not brick the unrelated git-add / push / trailer / lint gates. Mutant M5 asserts this.

ONE MORE FREE 'done' FOUND IN THE SAME FAMILY: the kind:cmd empty check is now [ -z "${C//[[:space:]]/}" ], because bash -c '   ' exits 0 exactly like bash -c ''. A whitespace-only cmd was also a free done.

VERIFIED BY ME, not taken on report: sourced the shared lib and ran the matcher over seven cases in BASH (the grep -qv zsh/bash trap). Verdict: SHIP and OVERRIDE accept; do NOT SHIP, prose mentioning SHIP, a bead quoting a FOREIGN verdict, empty input, and FIX-FIRST all reject. My own expectation table had the quoted-foreign-verdict case labelled ACCEPT — that was my error, and its rejection is precisely the original bug being fixed.

MUTANTS, each killed on the case written for it (names printed, not trusted): M1 the historical grep -q 'SHIP' restored verbatim -> 4 cases die; M2 empty-cmd check -> if false -> 3 cases die; M3 SCRUTINY_NEGATED_RE neutered -> dies in the pre-commit suite, the pre-bead-close suite AND --selftest. Byte-identical restores by md5 each time. Suites 58 -> 69 and 60 -> 61.

STILL OPEN AND DEEPER, filed as dotfiles-mjf3: four ways to defeat the FIXED matcher (a verdict inside a fenced block; a quoted verdict; a verdict retracted on the next line) and, the real one, NOTHING BINDS THE PROOF BEAD TO THE WORK — a tick can point proof.bead at any bead that shipped months ago and earn a done row forever. Verifier distance is claimed by the design and not enforced by the code. A matcher cannot reach that.

title: reef: hardcoded /home/ubuntu/reef paths break macwhisper + calendar on pico
description:

 - the calendar UI logs a scandir ENOENT and degrades to 200/empty

## Steps to Reproduce

- both sites resolve their paths from the reef root rather than a hardcoded absolute
- a grep gate rejects any new hardcoded /home/ubuntu path in reef source
- macwhisper webhook returns a success code on pico, and the calendar UI renders real content

title: scheduler: gate the shared manifest against ALL THREE of its parsers at commit time
description:
## Context

`vps-repo-manifest.txt` is read by THREE independent components, each with its
own hand-maintained directive vocabulary and no gate tying them together:

  1. `vps-repo-refresh.sh`  — strict parser, `*) die … 65`
  2. `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` — its own pre-scan (e.g. `oob-exclude` at ~line 750)
  3. `vps-preflight.sh` — its own reading of the required/oob tiers

On 2026-07-28 `oob-exclude` was added to the manifest and taught to parser 2
only. Parser 1 then died `exit 65` on every run, wrote no receipt, and
`vps-preflight.sh` fail-closed — silently blocking EVERY remote pulse row on
every project for ~28 hours. Found 2026-07-29 only because Zig asked why
di-wednesday had no window (dotfiles-0bf2, dotfiles-wv2a).

The per-instance fix shipped. This bead is the CLASS. The strict `*) die` is
correct and should NOT be relaxed — a typo'd directive means a manifest that
does not mean what its author thinks, and `test-vps-repo-refresh.sh` case 11b
now pins that behavior deliberately. The defect is not strictness; it is that
nothing checks the three vocabularies agree, so the disagreement is discovered
at 07:00 on a box nobody watches instead of at commit time on the machine Zig
does watch.

Credit: identified by the subagent that fixed dotfiles-0bf2/h13q, as the
follow-up it deliberately did not implement because it is cross-file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test on zig-computer feeds the SHIPPED `vps-repo-manifest.txt` to all
      three readers and asserts each one accepts it. Not a fixture — the real
      file, so adding a directive to the manifest without teaching every parser
      fails here.
- [ ] Each reader is exercised through its real parse path, not a
      reimplementation of it. A copy of the vocabulary in the test is the same
      bug one level up.
- [ ] Runs in the existing scheduler test suites (or a new one wired the same
      way), so it executes wherever those already run. Zero runtime cost — this
      is a commit-time gate, nothing new in the tick path.
- [ ] The failure message names WHICH parser rejected WHICH directive, so the
      fix is obvious without bisecting.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: add a directive the manifest's parsers do not know, watch the
      gate fail, remove it, watch it pass. Paste both.

## Also worth folding in (cheap, same file family)

- [ ] The manifest header documents `require-oob` but NOT `require-oob-untracked`
      or `oob-exclude` — which is precisely how the next reader gets surprised.
      Document all current directives there.
- [ ] `~/.cache/vps-repo-refresh/last-failure.txt` on the box is append-only and
      never rotated (18 KB already, mostly the `oob-exclude` deaths). Bound it
      the way the old `~/bin` script bounds its own log, so the next real
      failure is findable by eye.

## Notes — a known coverage trade, recorded not fixed

`--ignore-submodules=all` (dotfiles-h13q) is non-lossy only for submodules that
also carry their own `readonly` manifest line. `dashboard-dev-interrupted` and
`weekly-reporting` have one; `pipeline-website` does not, so its contents are
now unchecked by the refresh. Same trade `vps-preflight.sh` already makes, and
no live pulse row reads that path — recorded here so it is a known trade rather
than a later surprise.

title: doclint: concurrent runs poison each other's sandbox — second run cascades to 1504 phantom hook-block errors
description:
## Context
2026-08-10, during 79zy close-out: a full doc-example-lint.py run overlapping builder D's --rule pruned-path verification runs produced errors=1504, every added error 'hook could not be evaluated: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: PosixPath(/tmp/doc-example-lint-sandbox-4a8ptag0)' — the run's own sandbox disappeared mid-flight. A solo run minutes earlier returned errors=25 warnings=43; warnings matched (43) across both, so the delta is pure sandbox-loss cascade. Hypothesis to verify at fix time: sandbox cleanup globs /tmp/doc-example-lint-sandbox-* (or equivalent shared-path teardown) rather than removing only the run's own directory, so any concurrent invocation destroys the other's sandbox. Note doclint is now wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit (79zy) AND run ad hoc — concurrency is the NORMAL case going forward, not an edge.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a full run: cd /home/ubuntu/demesne && python3 agents/doclint/doc-example-lint.py (takes ~9 min)
2. While it runs, invoke a second run in another shell: python3 agents/doclint/doc-example-lint.py --rule pruned-path (or any invocation that triggers sandbox setup/teardown)
3. Observe the first run's subsequent hook evaluations fail with 'No such file or directory: /tmp/doc-example-lint-sandbox-<its-suffix>' and per-line hook-block errors cascade (observed: 25 → 1504 errors, warnings stable at 43)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause confirmed (not assumed): reproduce with two overlapping runs, identify the exact teardown path
- [ ] Concurrent runs isolated (per-run sandbox teardown only, or lockfile with a clear queued/refused message — no silent cascade)
- [ ] Regression guard made-to-fail: a test that runs two overlapping invocations and asserts both finish with sane per-run results
- [ ] A hook-could-not-be-evaluated condition reports as its own DISTINCT verdict class, not as per-line errors that inflate the count 60x (evaluability != document defect)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Second evidence set (builder C follow-up, 2026-08-10 ~19:3xZ): the doclint SUITE's sandbox-cleanup assertion is a GLOBAL find over ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} -name 'doc-example-lint-sandbox-*' — any other run's leftover fails it regardless of ownership. Measured during the allowlist commit: two foreign sandboxes (uvk38oh7 mtime 19:24:55, oum6r2ue 19:32:52) and FOUR live doc-example-lint processes belonging to another session, i.e. concurrent doclint is already routine across seats today. Confirmed workaround that fixes the VIEW without weakening the assertion: per-run isolated TMPDIR (builder C used it for both lint runs and the hook-bearing git commit). Fix shape sharpened: (a) narrow the suite's find to the run's own sandbox; (b) per-run teardown or lock per the original ACs. Nothing was deleted; foreign sandboxes left in place.

title: tailscale: drop SSH `check` re-auth to unblock pico→zig granola webhook
description:

Compromised user-owned device can SSH within the user's tailnet without browser re-verify, but the attacker already has full tailnet identity and could do anything else within the ACL anyway — no material blast-radius increase.

title: finding: the buggy hook blocked the merge of its own fix (pre-merge-worktree cwd bug, observed live)
description:
Observed 2026-07-25, worth recording because it is the cleanest possible
demonstration of why the hook layer needed this pass.

`pre-merge-worktree.sh` had (among three defects) a bug where it never read
`.cwd` from the hook stdin JSON, so it evaluated the HOOK PROCESS's cwd rather
than the SESSION's. The orchestrator session was cwd'd to ~/explore while
merging a branch in ~/dotfiles.

Two branches shared the name `worktree-agent-ad28b48474f7ce8b4`: the empty one
in ~/explore (0 commits — the agent had been given an explore worktree but the
target files were in dotfiles, so it correctly created a dotfiles worktree
instead) and the real one in ~/dotfiles (7 commits).

The hook, evaluating in the wrong repo, reported:
  "Blocked: worktree-agent-ad28b48474f7ce8b4 has no commits beyond main."
...and refused the merge OF ITS OWN FIX.

Resolved by removing the empty explore worktree + branch first, then merging.

THE THIRD DEFECT, which no audit found and only writing the test surfaced:
check 2 used `--pretty=format:`, which omits the trailing newline, so the
`while read` loop hit EOF without a delimiter and SKIPPED THE LAST COMMIT. On a
single-commit branch — the normal subagent worktree shape — the Bead-trailer
gate therefore examined ZERO commits and NEVER FIRED. A gate that silently
passed everything it was built to check.

THE LESSON: two of the three defects here were invisible to reading the code and
only appeared when someone wrote a test that exercised the real shape. The
existing 12-file hook suite passed 100% throughout — every bug found in this
pass was outside its coverage. Coverage that is green is not coverage that is
complete.

Post-fix: 17 test files, 266 cases, all green, verified independently by the
orchestrator on the merged tree (not merely reported by the agent).
notes:
## Verification — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

The pre-merge-worktree cwd bug is fixed in the hook.

Verified by an independent read-only recon agent against live system state, not
from the bead body. Closing as confirmed-resolved.

title: model-guard: the cold-start rounds the 1s re-read cannot win
description:
## Context
dotfiles-8x8l fixed the BLINDNESS ATTRIBUTION: a first-tool-round read that finds no
assistant row is now ledgered as `check-skipped / no-assistant-row-yet` with the seat's
expected model attached, and a re-read (MODEL_GUARD_RETRIES=4 x MODEL_GUARD_RETRY_SLEEP=0.25,
a 1s ceiling) recovers the round when the client's batched assistant rows land inside it.

Measured live on 2026-08-09 across 9 fresh interactive sessions, shipped hook vs fixed hook
side by side on the same first tool round:
  * 22:01:35 — the re-read WON: t0 lines=12 assistant=0 -> t1 lines=14 assistant=2 after
    0.413s, and the round produced a real `detected / restore` verdict instead of nothing.
  * 22:02:40 — the re-read LOST: t0 12/0 -> t1 12/0 after 5.8s. The assistant batch had not
    been written at all, so no wait short enough for a PostToolUse hook would have helped.

So a residual remains: on some sessions the guard still makes no verdict on tool round 1.
The cost is low (round 2 catches it seconds later) EXCEPT for a session whose entire life is
one tool round — a pulse tick that fails fast, a headless run.

## Task
Decide whether that residual is worth closing, and if so on which seam. Candidates:
  * a Stop / SessionEnd hook that makes the check once the turn's rows are durable
  * reading the served model from somewhere that is not the transcript (agentgateway
    request logs are ground truth per AGENTS.md, but off-box for some seats)
  * accepting it, and having whatever counts the ledger treat `check-skipped` as expected
    background rather than a defect

Note for any counting surface (dotfiles-7pbn): the ledger vocabulary GREW in 8x8l. `event`
is now detected | recovered | check-failed | check-skipped, and `action` on a blind round is
one of no-transcript, transcript-empty, transcript-unparseable, no-assistant-row-yet,
assistant-rows-carry-no-model, assistant-rows-all-synthetic, assistant-rows-all-sidechain.
A surface that greps for the old literal `no-served-model` will now match nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision recorded (close-with-rationale is a fine outcome) on whether round-1 misses
      are worth another seam.
- [ ] If anything counts the ledger, it knows check-skipped from check-failed.

title: spec: SS14-on-pico via Approach C2 — nginx + wrapper-pair + minimal Robust.Server patches
description:
## POST-jc5 CORRECTION (2026-05-25) — nginx UDP PROXY cadence

**This spec was wrong about nginx UDP PROXY-protocol cadence.** Multiple sections claim nginx 1.28 emits a PROXY header on EVERY UDP datagram. **That is false in production traffic.** Caught live during the dotfiles-oxe cutover; fixed in dotfiles-jc5.

**Correct behavior**: nginx `stream { proxy_protocol on; }` on UDP emits the PROXY-v1 header **ONCE per nginx-UDP-session**, where a session is keyed by client `<src-ip, src-port>` and persists for `proxy_timeout` (default 10m; this spec uses 120s). Subsequent datagrams from the same client tuple arrive at the upstream **without** a PROXY header. The wrapper must maintain session state keyed on the wrapper-side src tuple (= nginx's outbound socket addr) and route headerless follow-up datagrams via that lookup.

**Why the original conclusion was wrong**: /check dotfiles-9cj's synthetic test used `nc` invocations that allocated a fresh ephemeral src port per datagram. On loopback, nginx therefore created a separate UDP session per datagram, each getting its own header — making the per-session-only behavior invisible. Real Lidgren clients use ONE src port for the entire handshake → ONE nginx session → ONE PROXY header total. Generalization rule for future test work: any UDP test that sends multiple datagrams MUST pin the src port (single socket, multiple `sendto`) to honestly exercise session-reuse paths.

**Sections affected by this correction** (read in light of the above, not as originally written):

- **§1.3** ("PROXY v1 text on UDP — per /check dotfiles-9cj empirical test") — true that v1 text is the right format, false implication that headers are per-datagram
- **§3.6** ("matters on every UDP datagram in the connect handshake") — outdated framing of cost; only the FIRST datagram per session bears the header
- **§3.8** ("on EVERY UDP datagram of a 'UDP session'") — **DIRECTLY WRONG**; correct is ONCE per nginx session, not per datagram
- **§3.8** ("re-populates lazily from incoming per-datagram PROXY headers") — wrapper actually populates on first datagram per session, then routes headerless follow-ups via `LookupBySrcTuple`
- **§4.1** nginx config inline comment ("PROXY v1 text header prepended to EACH UDP datagram") — wrong, prepended to first datagram per session
- **§4.2** wrapper pseudocode comments ("we parse on every datagram", "header is per-datagram") — wrong; parse-failure on a follow-up datagram is a routing signal (look up established session), not a drop signal
- **§5 TC03** ("a second datagram from `203.0.113.5:54321` arrives — and ALSO carries a PROXY v1 text header") — **DIRECTLY WRONG**; should split into TC03a (first datagram, header-bearing) and TC03b (follow-up datagram, headerless, routes via `LookupBySrcTuple`)
- **§6 OQ-03 resolution** ("the header is emitted on EVERY UDP datagram (per-datagram)") — **DIRECTLY WRONG**, the basis was a synthetic test that didn't pin src port
- **§6 OQ-03 spec impact bullet 3** ("§4.2 wrapper pseudocode — remove the 'First packet: parse PROXY v2 header' branching since header is per-datagram") — wrong direction; the branching needed was per-session, not per-datagram. jc5 reintroduced session-bound routing via a parse-failure classification (`ErrNoProxyHeader` = routing signal, `ErrMalformedProxyHeader` = drop signal).

**Architectural impact**: zero — Approach C2 still works. The fix is contained to `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/proxy.go` (ServeUDP parse-failure branch) and `ss14-wrapper/wrapper/session.go` (added `LookupBySrcTuple`). The C# patches in vacation-station-14 are unaffected. The `proxy_timeout 120s` decision from OQ-01 is unchanged and is what governs nginx's session lifetime on the corrected understanding.

**Audit trail**: see dotfiles-jc5 for the live-cutover diagnosis (nginx error log + tcpdump), the fix sketch, and the regression-guard test that pins down the corrected contract. /check dotfiles-9cj's OQ-03 conclusion is retracted with a SUPERSEDED pointer in that bead's --notes.

---

## 1. Overview

### 1.1 Sources

This spec is informed by:

- Parent bead `dotfiles-52c` (explore: SS14-on-pico via TPROXY or GRE) — full rationale for why DNAT was rejected (exposes home WAN IP) and why TPROXY (`dotfiles-r8k`) and GRE/IPIP-over-Tailscale (`dotfiles-jjd`) were ruled out.
- The zig-zone runbook at `~/explore/.claude/skills/zig-zone/SKILL.md` — 22 production gotchas, Phase 4 ATTEMPTED+ROLLED-BACK history, Colima/Tailscale/macOS networking quirks, the `/etc/hosts` shim for headless tailscaled on pico, the established convention that LaunchAgents live at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.<service>.plist`.
- The `vacation-station-14` source tree at `~/vacation-station-14/` (community fork; `git log -1` shows `b8c8c54d48`). Specific moderation-path locations grepped and confirmed (see Section 2).
- The Robust.Server vendored copy at `~/vacation-station-14/RobustToolbox/Robust.Server/` and `Robust.Shared/Network/` — confirms `INetChannel.RemoteEndPoint` is the universal IP-source; confirms Lidgren has zero PROXY-protocol parsing.
- nginx 1.28.0 on zig-computer (`apt-cache policy nginx`) built `--with-stream=dynamic --with-stream_realip_module` — stream module + PROXY protocol support both present.
- Phase 4 build artifacts on pico (per `dotfiles-52c`): `/Users/pico/ss14-watchdog/` instance dir, darwin-arm64 binaries preserved, two LaunchAgent plists on disk but unloaded.

### 1.2 Goal

Move SS14 (game server + watchdog + replay-rotate) from zig-computer to pico (Mac Studio on the tailnet) **while preserving real client source IPs** in every SS14 moderation-subsystem code path AND keeping zig-computer's IP `51.81.33.136` as the only publicly-known address.

### 1.3 Approach (C2) in one paragraph

nginx `stream{}` on zig-computer accepts UDP+TCP on public `:1212`, then forwards each connection to a **wrapper daemon** on pico over the tailnet, with a PROXY-protocol header prepended to convey the real client IP+port (PROXY v1 text on UDP — per /check dotfiles-9cj empirical test of nginx 1.28; PROXY v2 binary on TCP per nginx default). The wrapper listens on pico's tailnet IP `:1212`, peels the PROXY header, forwards the stripped UDP/TCP payload to `127.0.0.1:1213` where Robust.Server binds. The wrapper maintains a 5-tuple → real-client-IP map and exposes it over a localhost Unix Domain Socket (UDS) at `/Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock`. Robust.Server is patched (in two places: the connect-time `NetConnectingArgs.IP` synthesis in `NetManager.ServerAuth.cs`, and the `NetChannel.RemoteEndPoint` property in `NetManager.NetChannel.cs`) to consult the wrapper's UDS map and override the apparent peer IP. All downstream moderation paths (`BanManager`, `ConnectionManager`, `IPIntel`, `ServerApi`, `PlayerLocator`, `AdminAlertIfSharedConnection`) read the corrected IP transparently because they all funnel through those two override points.

### 1.4 In scope

- nginx `stream{}` config on zig-computer with UDP+TCP `proxy_protocol on` + `proxy_pass` to pico's tailnet IP `:1212`.
- Wrapper daemon design + implementation (single binary, single config file).
- Two minimal patches to vendored Robust.Server (NetManager.ServerAuth.cs synthesis site + NetChannel.RemoteEndPoint property).
- The wrapper's `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-wrapper.plist` (KeepAlive=true, follows zig-zone naming convention).
- Updates to `~/dotfiles/vs14/` plist templates for ss14-watchdog (port flip 1212 → 1213) and the new wrapper plist.
- zig-zone runbook update: Phase 4 transitions from "rolled back" to "SHIPPED via Approach C2" with a new section + 1–2 new gotchas.
- Cutover playbook on zig-computer (stop ss14-watchdog, reload nginx with stream block) + on pico (load LaunchAgents in the right order).

### 1.5 Out of scope

- Anything touching Lidgren-Network internals (no PROXY parsing INSIDE Lidgren — that's why C2 has a wrapper).
- Upstream-PR work to space-wizards/RobustToolbox (vacation-station-14 is a community fork already; the patches stay in our tree).
- The A1111 / Ollama / Phoenix / vs14-web / postgres / observability stack on pico — those are untouched. Only port allocations are coordinated (Section 4.5).
- vs14-mapserver port :44880 — this spec does NOT consume that. Wrapper allocates ports outside the existing taken set.
- IPv6 dual-stack handling beyond "IPv4 ships first; IPv6 is a separately-tracked follow-up." Robust.Server's default `net.bindto = "0.0.0.0,::"` means dual-stack matters eventually; first ship is IPv4-only with the IPv6 path documented as a follow-up bead.
- DDOS protection at the wrapper layer (relies on nginx upstream + tailnet ACL).

## 2. Current State / Baseline

### 2.1 SS14 runtime topology (post-Phase 4 rollback)

- Robust.Server + Content.Server + SS14.Watchdog all live on **zig-computer**, bound on `0.0.0.0:1212` (UDP + TCP, IPv4 + IPv6 — 4 listeners total per `ss -tunap | grep :1212`).
- Pico has **preserved** darwin-arm64 build artifacts under `/Users/pico/ss14-watchdog/` (instance laid out, binaries published, Resources/ + Content.Client.zip intact, `config.toml` already patched for `pg_host=localhost` + `loki=http://localhost:3100` + `UpdateType=Dummy`).
- LaunchAgents `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist` + `com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist` exist on pico but are **unloaded**.
- Zig-computer has nginx 1.28.0 with the stream module installed (`/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` includes `stream { include /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/*; }`) but `/etc/nginx/streams-enabled/` is currently empty.

### 2.2 SS14 moderation code paths that consume `RemoteEndPoint.Address`

Grep results in `~/vacation-station-14/`:

**Content.Server (the fork's content layer):**
- `Content.Server/Connection/ConnectionManager.cs:115` — commented-out `HandleApproval`, reads `eventArgs.Connection.RemoteEndPoint.Address`.
- `Content.Server/Connection/ConnectionManager.cs:137` (LIVE) — `var addr = e.IP.Address` inside `NetMgrOnConnecting`; addr is then passed to `_db.AddConnectionLogAsync(...)` and `_db.GetBansAsync(...)` via `ShouldDeny` (line 214).
- `Content.Server/Connection/ConnectionManager.cs:184` — `var addr = newSession.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address` inside `AdminAlertIfSharedConnection`.
- `Content.Server/Connection/IPIntel/IPIntel.cs:110` — `var ip = e.IP.Address` inside `IsVpnOrProxy`; this drives `_db.GetIPIntelCache(ip)` (the `ipintel_cache` table the parent bead names).
- `Content.Server/Administration/Managers/BanManager.cs:75` — `netChannel.RemoteEndPoint.Address` inside `CachePlayerData` (role-ban lookup).
- `Content.Server/Administration/Managers/BanManager.cs:203` — `player.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address` inside `BanMatchesPlayer` (live ban-check).
- `Content.Server/Administration/PlayerLocator.cs:154` — `session.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address`.
- `Content.Server/Administration/PlayerPanelEui.cs:182` — `s.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address` for shared-connection count display.
- `Content.Server/Administration/ServerApi.cs:371` — `info.AddAddress(player.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address)` for the admin API response.
- `Content.Server/Administration/Managers/AdminManager.cs:505` — `var ep = player.Channel.RemoteEndPoint`.
- `Content.Server/Info/RulesManager.cs:32` — `IPAddress.IsLoopback(e.Channel.RemoteEndPoint.Address)` for the local-host bypass.

**Robust.Server / Robust.Shared (vendored engine, the override point):**
- `RobustToolbox/Robust.Shared/Network/INetChannel.cs:27` — interface contract `IPEndPoint RemoteEndPoint { get; }`.
- `RobustToolbox/Robust.Shared/Network/NetManager.NetChannel.cs:40` — implementation `public IPEndPoint RemoteEndPoint => _connection.RemoteEndPoint` (proxies through to Lidgren's `NetConnection`).
- `RobustToolbox/Robust.Shared/Network/NetManager.ServerAuth.cs:231` — `var endPoint = connection.RemoteEndPoint` then `new NetConnectingArgs(userData, endPoint, type)` — this is where `NetConnectingArgs.IP` is born. Override here = `e.IP.Address` in Content.Server gets the real client IP.

### 2.3 Network topology pieces

- Tailnet IPs at time of writing (per gotcha #17 / `/etc/hosts` shim): zig-computer `100.98.174.21`; pico `100.95.4.73` (was `100.72.47.4` during the GRE test 2026-05-24; tailnet IPs are stable per-device but check `tailscale ip -4` at install time).
- zig-computer public IP `51.81.33.136` is the only publicly-known game endpoint (DNS: `ss14.zig.computer`).
- Players currently dial `ss14.zig.computer:1212`. After C2, the dial target is the same — only the back-end moves.

### 2.4 Pico port usage inventory (must not collide)

Per the zig-zone runbook + dotfiles-52c context, pico already runs:

| Service | Bind |
|---|---|
| ssh | :22 |
| nginx (pico-side internal) | 0.0.0.0:8080 |
| Phoenix | tailnet-IP:6006 + tailnet-IP:4317 |
| Ollama | tailnet-IP:11434 |
| postgres | *:5432 |
| vs14-web | tailnet-IP:3300 |
| Colima docker workload | various 0.0.0.0 ports (mapserver, ss14-admin, prometheus, loki, grafana, cdn) |
| reef-router (when Phase 3 deferred bead lands) | tailnet-IP:7575 |
| A1111 | :7860 |
| (deferred from Phase 3) timers / cron — no ports |

**C2 allocations** (must not collide):
- Wrapper public-facing UDP+TCP listener: tailnet-IP:1212 (NEW — was free).
- Robust.Server internal UDP+TCP listener: `127.0.0.1:1213` (NEW — was free).
- Wrapper UDS for API: `/Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock` (filesystem, not a port).

### 2.5 What ruled out earlier approaches (for the file)

- **DNAT (parent's pre-pivot plan)**: exposes home WAN IP via DDNS resolution.
- **TPROXY (`dotfiles-r8k`)**: asymmetric routing — return path requires `tc nat egress` (Linux-only) on the backend; macOS has no equivalent that scales beyond per-client routes (O(connected players)).
- **GRE/IPIP-over-Tailscale (`dotfiles-jjd`)**: Tailscale's WireGuard drops non-TCP/UDP/ICMP IP protocols (upstream issue tailscale/tailscale#14006, unresolved since 2024-11-02). GRE/IPIP-over-public-IP would re-expose pico's home WAN IP.

C2 is the escalation path the parent flagged as "biggest engineering scope but most likely to actually deliver the goal."

## 3. Changes and Decisions

### 3.1 Change — Add an nginx stream block with PROXY-protocol on zig-computer

- **Why**: nginx's `proxy_protocol on` directive prepends a PROXY-protocol header to the outbound stream (TCP or UDP) carrying the original client's IP+port. nginx 1.28 (Ubuntu's questing-shipped stable) supports PROXY-protocol for UDP since nginx 1.27.x. **Empirically verified via /check (dotfiles-9cj) on 2026-05-24: nginx 1.28 emits PROXY v1 (text format), not v2 (binary), on UDP** — both formats convey the same real-client IP+port info; the wrapper consumes either via the `go-proxyproto` library's autodetecting reader. No build flag changes — `--with-stream=dynamic` is already present.
- **How**: New file `/etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf` (see §4.1).

### 3.2 Change — Introduce a wrapper daemon on pico

- **Why**: Lidgren does not parse PROXY headers (`grep -rn "PROXY\|proxy_protocol\|ProxyProtocol"` in `RobustToolbox/` returns zero hits). Adding parsing INSIDE Lidgren is a fork of the network library, with much larger blast radius than a sidecar daemon. The wrapper isolates PROXY-protocol handling from the game engine, lets Robust.Server believe it's still receiving plain UDP/TCP from `localhost`, and gives us a clean local API for the moderation override.
- **How**: Single-binary daemon written in **Go** (decision below in §3.6) at `~/dotfiles/ss14/wrapper/`. Reads PROXY-protocol headers (v1 text or v2 binary — autodetected via `go-proxyproto` library), forwards stripped payloads to `127.0.0.1:1213`, exposes a session-lookup API over a UDS.

### 3.3 Change — Patch vendored Robust.Server in two places to consult the wrapper API

- **Why**: The cleanest minimum-surface override. Every IP-reading site downstream funnels through one of:
  - `INetChannel.RemoteEndPoint` (NetChannel.cs:40)
  - `NetConnectingArgs.IP` (synthesized in NetManager.ServerAuth.cs:231)
  Override these two and every Content.Server moderation read becomes honest with zero changes in Content.Server itself.
- **How**: Inject a small `IRemoteAddressOverride` service into NetManager; service is implemented by a class that talks to the wrapper's UDS API. Default (no-wrapper-running) behavior: pass-through — returns `_connection.RemoteEndPoint` unchanged. Fork-fail-safe.

### 3.4 Change — LaunchAgent for the wrapper

- **Why**: All other persistent pico services follow the `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.<service>.plist` pattern (gotcha #15 — never use `brew services`, write our own plist with envs baked in).
- **How**: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-wrapper.plist`, KeepAlive=true, `RunAtLoad=true`, `EnvironmentVariables` includes `SS14_WRAPPER_LISTEN=$(tailscale ip -4):1212`, `SS14_WRAPPER_UPSTREAM=127.0.0.1:1213`, `SS14_WRAPPER_SOCK=/Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock`. Template sed-substitutes `TAILSCALE_IP_PLACEHOLDER` at install time (per Phase 2 Ollama plist precedent).

### 3.5 Change — ss14-watchdog config flip to bind 1213, not 1212

- **Why**: The wrapper owns `:1212` on pico's tailnet IP; Robust.Server moves to `127.0.0.1:1213`.
- **How**: Patch the instance's `config.toml` with `[net] port = 1213` and `bindto = "127.0.0.1"`. Update `~/dotfiles/vs14/` templates accordingly. Also patch `status.connectaddress` to remain pointing at the **public hostname** `ss14.zig.computer:1212` (NOT pico's tailnet IP — the launcher must reach the public face).

### 3.6 Decision — Wrapper language is Go

- **Tradeoffs considered**:
  - **Go** (chosen): single static binary, excellent stdlib for net/UDP + Unix sockets, established PROXY-protocol library at `github.com/pires/go-proxyproto`, cross-compiles cleanly to darwin-arm64, no runtime install. Builds in `dotnet`-installer-free CI. Familiar to the user (reef-router is bun/TS, but ops tooling on pico is comfortable Go-or-anything).
  - **Rust** rejected: more dev-time for marginal runtime gains; UDP-forward + UDS-server is solved-problem territory where Go's stdlib is genuinely good enough.
  - **Python** rejected: GIL + GC pauses on a UDP-hot-path are risk. Phase 4 already observed `MsgEntity Diff: -4250` mystery disconnects we couldn't fully isolate; the wrapper should add zero new GC sources.
  - **C#** rejected: another whole dotnet runtime on the box for one process, AND a managed sidecar to a managed server doesn't simplify the deployment story.

### 3.7 Decision — Wrapper API is UDS (not HTTP)

- **Tradeoffs**:
  - **UDS** (chosen): no port allocation, no firewall question, no localhost-binding question, sub-millisecond round-trip, dirt-simple permission model (filesystem mode 0660 + group). Robust.Server already runs as `pico:staff`; wrapper plist drops privileges to same user; both can read/write the socket.
  - **HTTP loopback**: simpler to debug (`curl http://127.0.0.1:NNNN/lookup/...`), but requires a port allocation and the cost is the round-trip latency that matters on **every UDP datagram in the connect handshake**. With UDP at 30 Hz + ~50ms ban-check budget, even 1ms HTTP overhead × N calls during a connect storm adds up.
  - **In-memory shared file** (mmap): pure-speed winner but the synchronization design surface (multi-process atomic writes) is non-trivial; UDS is good enough and the protocol is much simpler to evolve.

### 3.8 Decision — Session key is `(client-5-tuple)` keyed by Lidgren's view

- **Why this matters**: Lidgren multiplexes many "Net peers" over the single UDP socket. The wrapper has to map "this incoming UDP packet" to "this real client IP." nginx provides the PROXY header ONCE per stream (TCP) or **on EVERY UDP datagram** of a "UDP session" (nginx's term — keyed on client 5-tuple with a configurable timeout; per-datagram header behavior verified empirically via /check dotfiles-9cj 2026-05-24). After header strip, the payload reaches the wrapper and gets forwarded to Robust.Server bearing the wrapper's loopback source.
- **The mapping** the wrapper maintains: `(wrapper-loopback-port-it-just-allocated, Robust.Server-port-1213)` → real client IP. Robust.Server, when it wants to know "who is this peer?", asks the wrapper API: `LOOKUP <5-tuple-as-seen-by-Robust>` and the wrapper answers with the real client IP.
- **Why this works for the multiplex problem**: nginx stream's `proxy_upload_rate`/UDP-session model already keys by client 5-tuple. The wrapper inherits that key. For each unique (client-5-tuple), the wrapper allocates a unique outbound source port (call it the "fan-out port"), forwards to Robust.Server, and Robust.Server sees `127.0.0.1:<fan-out-port>` as the peer. Lookup by that 5-tuple gives the real client.
- **Wrapper is stateless across restarts** (ratified by /check dotfiles-9cj on OQ-02): no session-map persistence to disk; each wrapper process starts with an empty map and re-populates lazily from incoming per-datagram PROXY headers. Wrapper restart costs every active player a Lidgren `ConnectionTimeout`-driven reconnect window (~25s with default settings; see OQ-02).

### 3.9 Decision — Failure semantics: wrapper crash leaves Robust.Server up but moderation becomes pass-through

- **Why**: Robust.Server must not crash because the wrapper crashed. If the IRemoteAddressOverride service's UDS connect fails, it must fall back to `_connection.RemoteEndPoint` (the proxy's IP) and continue serving. Moderation degrades to "every player looks like 127.0.0.1" for the duration. The wrapper's LaunchAgent KeepAlive will restart the wrapper within ~1 sec. Players already connected see no interruption; new connects during the gap have wrong IPs in `ban_address` etc.
- **Counter-design considered**: hard-fail Robust.Server on UDS connect error. Rejected because (a) Phase 4's rollback was driven partly by avoiding "single point breaks the game"; (b) cached moderation data already loaded covers most cases; (c) the alert path can be a log-only warning that the orchestrator's o11y stack picks up.

### 3.10 Decision — vacation-station-14 patches live as a maintained fork patch set, not an upstream PR

- **Why**: Parent bead explicitly says "The fork is OK to maintain (vacation-station-14 is already a community fork; no upstream-PR pressure)." Upstream Space Wizards' production hosting model (per `space-wizards/docs` referenced in zig-zone runbook) explicitly tells operators NOT to reverse-proxy UDP; they're highly unlikely to merge.
- **How**: Patches land on the `main` branch of vacation-station-14 with a `Bead: dotfiles-NNNN` trailer that traces back here. If upstream ever adds a similar feature, we revert the patches and consume theirs. ### 4.2 Wrapper daemon (Go, single binary)

Project layout: `~/dotfiles/ss14/wrapper/`
```
ss14-wrapper/
├── go.mod
├── main.go
├── proxy.go        # UDP+TCP listener, PROXY-protocol parse, forward
├── api.go          # UDS server: LOOKUP, ENUMERATE, HEALTH
├── session.go      # 5-tuple session map with TTL cleanup
└── README.md
```

Pseudocode for the hot path (proxy.go, UDP):

```go
// sketch
func ServeUDP(listenAddr, upstreamAddr string, store *SessionStore) error {
    listener, _ := net.ListenPacket("udp", listenAddr)  // bind tailnet-IP:1212
    upstream, _ := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", upstreamAddr)  // 127.0.0.1:1213
    buf := make([]byte, 65535)
    for {
        n, srcAddr, _ := listener.ReadFrom(buf)
        // nginx prepends a PROXY-protocol header to EVERY UDP datagram
        // (verified /check dotfiles-9cj — nginx 1.28 emits v1 text format on UDP,
        // per-datagram, NOT once-per-session as a v1 of this spec assumed).
        // The go-proxyproto library's autodetecting Reader handles v1 and v2
        // transparently — we parse on every datagram.
        reader := bytes.NewReader(buf[:n])
        hdr, err := proxyproto.Read(bufio.NewReader(reader))  // autodetects v1/v2
        if err != nil { /* malformed header — log + drop, see TC18 */ continue }
        realSrc := hdr.SourceAddr  // net.Addr — *net.TCPAddr in practice (v1 only labels TCP4/TCP6)
        payloadOffset := int(reader.Size()) - reader.Len()
        payload := buf[payloadOffset:n]
        // Session-store maps fan-out-port → real-client-IP for the Robust.Server
        // LOOKUP API. LookupOrCreate is keyed by srcAddr (nginx-side 5-tuple);
        // first sight of a 5-tuple allocates a unique loopback fan-out port.
        sess, _ := store.LookupOrCreate(srcAddr, realSrc)
        // Outbound fan-out socket per session (allocated lazily in LookupOrCreate)
        // gives Robust.Server a unique 127.0.0.1:<fan-out-port> per real client.
        _, _ = sess.FanOut.WriteToUDP(payload, upstream)
    }
}

func ServeReturnPath(store *SessionStore, listener net.PacketConn) {
    // Robust.Server's reply lands on the per-session fan-out socket.
    // Pump it back out the public listener with the original src 5-tuple.
    for sess := range store.AllSessions() {
        go func(s *Session) {
            buf := make([]byte, 65535)
            for {
                n, _, _ := s.FanOut.ReadFrom(buf)
                _, _ = listener.WriteTo(buf[:n], s.PublicSrcAddr)
            }
        }(sess)
    }
}
```

The TCP path is simpler (one PROXY header per connection, no per-packet juggling):

```go
// sketch
func ServeTCP(listenAddr, upstreamAddr string, store *SessionStore) error {
    ln, _ := net.Listen("tcp", listenAddr)
    for {
        conn, _ := ln.Accept()
        go handleTCP(conn, upstreamAddr, store)
    }
}
func handleTCP(client net.Conn, upstreamAddr string, store *SessionStore) {
    // PROXY header (v1 text or v2 binary — library autodetects) is first bytes on the wire.
    // Per /check dotfiles-9cj, nginx's default for TCP is v2 binary, but go-proxyproto's
    // generic Reader handles both transparently — no per-format branching needed.
    reader := bufio.NewReader(client)
    hdr, err := proxyproto.Read(reader)
    if err != nil { client.Close(); return }
    realSrc := hdr.SourceAddr  // *net.TCPAddr
    upstream, _ := net.Dial("tcp", upstreamAddr)  // 127.0.0.1:1213
    // Register session keyed by upstream local port for the LOOKUP API.
    store.AddTCPSession(upstream.LocalAddr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port, realSrc)
    defer store.RemoveTCPSession(upstream.LocalAddr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port)
    bidirectionalCopy(reader, upstream)  // 'reader' starts after the consumed PROXY header
}
```

UDS API (api.go):

```
WIRE PROTOCOL (newline-delimited text, request/response):
  Request:   "LOOKUP <proto> <local-port>\n"            // proto = udp|tcp
  Response:  "OK <real-client-ip>:<real-client-port>\n" // or "MISS\n"

  Request:   "ENUMERATE\n"
  Response:  N lines of "<proto> <local-port> <real-ip>:<real-port>\n" then "END\n"

  Request:   "HEALTH\n"
  Response:  "OK active_sessions=N uptime_s=X\n"
```

Why a text protocol: trivially debuggable (`nc -U /Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock`), no schema-evolution drama, ~zero parse cost vs binary at the volumes involved (one LOOKUP per Robust.Server moderation call, not per packet).

**Default implementation — `Content.Server/Connection/Ss14WrapperRemoteAddressOverride.cs`** (lives in the content layer to avoid polluting Robust.Shared with content-specific dep):

```csharp
// sketch
public sealed class Ss14WrapperRemoteAddressOverride : IRemoteAddressOverride
{
    private readonly string _sockPath;  // "/Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock"
    private readonly ISawmill _log;

    public IPEndPoint? Lookup(string protocol, IPEndPoint observed)
    {
        try
        {
            using var sock = new UnixDomainSocketClient(_sockPath);
            sock.Send($"LOOKUP {protocol} {observed.Port}\n");
            var reply = sock.ReceiveLine();
            if (reply.StartsWith("MISS")) return null;
            if (reply.StartsWith("OK ")) return IPEndPoint.Parse(reply[3..].Trim());
            return null;
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _log.Warning("ss14-wrapper UDS lookup failed (fallback to raw): {Err}", ex.Message);
            return null;  // pass-through; moderation degrades gracefully (§3.9)
        }
    }
}
```

### 4.6 Cutover playbook (atomic-ish)

Phase order:
1. **(off-hours window)** Confirm no players online: `curl https://ss14.zig.computer/status` shows `players: 0`.
2. **On pico**: build wrapper binary, install to `/Users/pico/bin/ss14-wrapper`. Run sanity: `ss14-wrapper --healthcheck` returns 0.
3. **On pico**: install + load `com.zig.ss14-wrapper.plist`. Verify with `launchctl list | grep ss14-wrapper` (status `0` = running clean).
4. **On pico**: patch `config.toml` to `port = 1213` + bindto `127.0.0.1` + connectaddress `udp://ss14.zig.computer:1212` + `[net.wrapper]` block.
5. **On pico**: load `com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist`. Verify Robust.Server bound `127.0.0.1:1213`: `lsof -i :1213 -P | grep LISTEN`.
6. **On zig-computer**: write `/etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf` per §4.1. `sudo nginx -t`.
7. **On zig-computer**: stop existing ss14-watchdog: `sudo systemctl stop ss14-watchdog`. Verify `:1212` free: `ss -tunap | grep :1212` shows nothing.
8. **On zig-computer**: `sudo systemctl reload nginx`. Verify nginx binds `:1212`: `ss -tunap | grep :1212` shows nginx workers.
9. **Verification**: synthetic test from a third tailnet device — `nc -u zig-computer-public-IP 1212 < known-bytes`. tcpdump on pico's wrapper-side confirms PROXY header arrives intact (PROXY v1 text on UDP per /check dotfiles-9cj; PROXY v2 binary on TCP). `nc -U /Users/pico/run/ss14-wrapper.sock` + `ENUMERATE\n` shows the session.
10. **Real-player verification**: connect with SS14 launcher. Issue a test `ban_address` from admin tools. `psql -c "SELECT address FROM ban_address ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"` returns the **real** client IP, not zig-computer's tailnet IP. PASS.
11. **On zig-computer**: `sudo systemctl disable ss14-watchdog`. Move `ss14-replay-rotate.timer` off zig-computer; load `com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist` on pico.

Rollback: stop wrapper + watchdog on pico; on zig-computer remove `streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf`, `nginx -s reload`, re-enable+start `ss14-watchdog.service`. Pre-cutover state fully restored.
