title: pulse: cheap-onboard skips the TOOLKIT digest on a false premise — fresh ticks run without skill anti-patterns
description:
## Context
Zig's question 2026-08-09 ('do pulses run onboard so they are aware of their skills?') surfaced a self-contradiction in agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md. Step 1 'Cheap onboard' (line ~289) says: skip CLAUDE.md, TOOLKIT digest, handoff note, br list — 'already in context.' But the same skill's durability section (lines ~311-314) states a --fresh loop gets /clear before every tick so its context holds 'the always-loaded tier and NOTHING else.' The skill already fixed this exact premise for the HANDOFF NOTE (bd-msi5 — the reader helper + loud-missing behavior); the TOOLKIT skip still stands on the identical broken assumption. Reality per tier: CLAUDE.md IS re-injected every context (system prompt assembly) — that skip is correct. Skill DESCRIPTIONS are always injected; full bodies load on Skill-tool invocation. What a --fresh tick genuinely lacks is the TOOLKIT layer — per-skill anti-patterns, prereqs, side-effect flags — which /onboard Step 2 calls the exact thing the listing lacks ('the anti-pattern you skip is the one you needed'). Ticks do inline bead ops and commits every run, the two areas whose TOOLKIT entries carry the most load-bearing anti-patterns (REPLACE-only notes, compound-command hook kills, push-blind absorption).

Fix direction (builder judgment allowed within it): NOT a full /onboard per tick (the cost argument that produced cheap-onboard is real — ~9.4k tokens for the whole digest). Options in order of preference: (a) tick loads ONLY the TOOLKIT entries for the skills its routed row leans on (the row names its skill), plus /beads + /commit entries unconditionally; (b) a per-loop pre-extracted digest slice shipped beside the routing table; (c) full digest if measurement shows the slice complexity isn't worth it. State the chosen option's cost in the commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /pulse Step 1 no longer claims TOOLKIT is 'already in context'; the --fresh reality is stated where the skip was.
- [ ] A --fresh tick's procedure loads the selected TOOLKIT material (option a/b/c above) BEFORE its unit of work; /marshal's night-start gets the same treatment (its own onboard path, agents/skills/marshal/SKILL.md).

title: fix: bench wrapper false-TIMEOUT verdict — kimi-linear correctly renamed but killed before DONE ack
description:
## Problem
Smoke matrix scenario 01-trivial-rename for `kimi-linear` was tagged `verdict_tag: TIMEOUT` (claude exit code 125, killed at 1200s wall cap). But the sandbox state at trial-end shows the file was renamed CORRECTLY:

    FILECONTENTS:/tmp/claude-local-test/s01/calc.py:def sum_two(a, b):\n    """Sum two numbers."""\n    return a + b\n\n\nif __name__ == "__main__":\n    print(sum_two(2, 3))

Both call sites match the spec. The model did the work — it just didn't print "DONE" before the wrapper killed it at the 20-min cap.

## Symptom
Reading the Tier-1 dashboard (or the scoreboard markdown), kimi-linear looks like a failure. It is actually a success-but-slow-ack case — qualitatively different from "task incomplete + timed out."

## Suspected cause
The bench wrapper (`run-scenario.sh` or similar) computes `verdict_tag` purely from claude's exit code, ignoring the post-run sandbox snapshot. A `FILECONTENTS` line that matches the spec's expected output (provided by the scenario file) is strong evidence of task completion, but the wrapper doesn't consult it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the smoke matrix on a model whose tokens-per-second is borderline at the wall_cap_seconds budget
2. Model successfully completes the edits but spends remaining time emitting "DONE"
3. Wrapper SIGKILLs at the cap; claude exits 125
4. verdict_tag = TIMEOUT despite the file showing the task done

## Fix sketch
Add a post-kill verification step to the wrapper: when verdict_tag is about to be TIMEOUT, check whether the sandbox state matches `expected_filecontents` from the scenario. If yes, downgrade to `TIMEOUT_SUCCESS` (task done, slow ack) or similar 3-state verdict (OK / TIMEOUT_SUCCESS / TIMEOUT_FAIL). The dashboard should distinguish these.

Alternative: bump the wall_cap for slow-but-correct models on scenarios they're known to handle.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Wrapper distinguishes TIMEOUT_SUCCESS (file correct) from TIMEOUT_FAIL (file wrong/missing)
- [ ] Kimi-Linear's 2026-05-28 result re-verdicts to TIMEOUT_SUCCESS
- [ ] Dashboard rendering reflects the 3-state verdict
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Wrapper distinguishes TIMEOUT_SUCCESS (file correct) from TIMEOUT_FAIL (file wrong/missing)
 - [ ] Kimi-Linear 2026-05-28 result re-verdicts to TIMEOUT_SUCCESS
 - [ ] Dashboard renders the 3-state verdict

title: shared-tree: a compound 'git add X && git commit' sweeps ANOTHER WRITER's staged files into your commit
description:
## Context

Nothing was lost (content committed + pushed, efec807) but ownership is mixed: another writer's work shipped under this seat's message and Bead: trailer, and that writer's index was silently drained (their next commit sees 'nothing to commit'). The two-writers doctrine covers merge/rebase/stash but has no rule for the INDEX as shared state; background commits widen the race window to minutes.

## Steps to Reproduce
Writer A: git add fileA (stages, doesn't commit — mid-run). Writer B: git add fileB && git commit -m 'fileB only'. The commit contains fileA and fileB; A's staged set is now empty.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The idiom fix documented in AGENTS.md two-writers section: commit with an explicit PATHSPEC — git commit -m msg -- <paths> — which commits ONLY those paths regardless of what else is staged (verify the behavior empirically first, incl. interaction with pre-commit $STAGED detection)
- [ ] Mechanical half evaluated: pre-commit (or a hook) warns when the commit's file set exceeds what the invoking command explicitly added this call, or when staged-by-another-writer files are detected (mtime/lock heuristics acceptable; loud warn, not block, to avoid false positives)
- [ ] Regression evidence: the reproduction above demonstrated failing-before / clean-after with the pathspec idiom

## Write target
~/demesne — agents/hooks/ (shared-index guard beside pre-shared-tree-guard) + tests.

title: the Hermes uninstall left seven systemd units behind, and infra.md claims they are gone
description:
## Context
Found 2026-08-05 while verifying an unrelated claim after removing pulse-elevate.
`agents/infra.md` asserts:

    **The 2026-07-26 rename is DONE, not pending.** `pulse-dive` and `pulse-desk` are
    installed and running; `pulse-explore`, `pulse-elevate`, `pulse-daily-digest` and
    `hermes-watchdog` no longer exist.

Three of those four are now true. `hermes-watchdog` is not — and it is not alone.

## Steps to Reproduce
    ssh zig-computer "systemctl --user list-unit-files | grep -i hermes"

      hermes-dashboard.service         disabled  enabled
      hermes-dispatch-broker.service   disabled  enabled
      hermes-gateway.service           disabled  enabled
      hermes-tmux-reap.service         static    -
      hermes-watchdog.service          linked    enabled
      hermes-workspace.service         disabled  enabled
      hermes-tmux-reap.timer           disabled  enabled

    ssh zig-computer "ls -d ~/hermes"   ->  No such file or directory

So the substrate is gone and seven units describing it are not. Nothing RUNS — everything
is disabled, static, or inactive — so this is hygiene, not an incident.

## The one that is more than cosmetic
`hermes-watchdog.service` is **`linked`**, not a regular file:

    hermes-watchdog.service -> /home/ubuntu/explore/local-coding-models/ops/hermes-watchdog/hermes-watchdog.service

A `linked` unit points into a REPO working tree. A `git clean -xfd`, a branch switch, or a
directory move leaves systemd holding a dangling unit — and `linked` units are the ones
people forget, because they are invisible to a `ls ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service` that
only greps for regular files.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness
MEMORY.md carries a **substrate uninstall protocol** written after Hermes precisely so this
would not happen: 9 steps, of which "stop, disable, ... take down exposed surfaces" is the
relevant one. The protocol existed and the surfaces stayed. That is worth knowing about the
protocol, not just about Hermes.

And the infra.md line is a **live-state claim in the file whose own header warns against
them** — it was written 2026-08-01 to correct an earlier stale claim, and was itself
inaccurate on one of its four items. Per CLAUDE.md, the fix is to make reality match, then
consider whether the sentence should name a QUERY instead of a list.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a decision per unit: delete, or keep with a stated reason (do not bulk-rm a substrate
      remains without saying so — the protocol asks for deliberateness)
- [ ] `systemctl --user list-unit-files | grep -i hermes` returns nothing, or infra.md is
      corrected to describe what genuinely remains and why
- [ ] the `linked` unit specifically resolved — it is the one that can dangle
- [ ] `daemon-reload` run and the result verified, not assumed
- [ ] consider whether infra.md should name the check rather than list the units

title: reef: the macwhisper webhook is still anonymously writable — same hole granola just closed

title: reef: the granola READ API leaked confidential transcripts anonymously — auth was route-scoped, nginx proxied everything
description:
Found by the reef survey, 2026-07-26, and verified live before fixing.

GET /coral/granola/api/transcripts and GET /coral/granola/ui both returned 200 to an ANONYMOUS request, over TLS *and* over cleartext :7575. The listing alone returned 3,137 bytes of meeting slugs — client meeting titles. The survey reports an individual fetch returns a 73 KB confidential AI-Council transcript.

ROOT CAUSE — the mirror of dotfiles-ks1u. The token auth shipped 2026-07-25 was wired to the webhook ROUTE only, while nginx proxied `location /` wholesale to the router. So the anonymous-WRITE hole closed and the anonymous-READ hole stayed wide open, on the same host, same day. Closing a write path does not close a read path, and a route-scoped middleware does not constrain what the reverse proxy will forward.

The exposure was bounded to the ~15 transcript files still on pico's disk BY LUCK, not by design — the corpus lives on zig-computer, so the read API could only serve what pico happened to retain.

## Steps to Reproduce

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://granola.zig.computer/coral/granola/api/transcripts

Returned 200 before the fix.

## Fix applied

Both vhosts (granola.zig.computer TLS + reef-router-7575) now allow exactly `location = /coral/granola/webhook` and return 404 for everything else. Chosen at the nginx edge rather than in the app because it closes BOTH listeners at once, needs no router change, and needs no pico restart. Justified by the survey finding that every other coral adapter is dead or a zombie stub, so Zapier's webhook POST is the only legitimate traffic.

Verified after reload: api 404, ui 404, /coral 404 on both listeners; webhook still 401 (reaching the app, auth enforced).

## Acceptance Criteria

- the anonymous read paths return 404 on both listeners (DONE, verified)
- the replacement receiver (lb-granola) exposes ONLY the webhook POST — no read API, no UI on a public listener
- a test asserts that a newly-added route is not reachable from the public edge by default
- the general lesson is recorded: auth scoped to a route does not constrain what the reverse proxy forwards

Related: [[dotfiles-ks1u]] the write hole, same endpoint, same day · [[dotfiles-b3u7]] macwhisper still anonymously writable

title: marshal: pacing thresholds assume a compaction floor that doesn't exist — 60% floor vs 50% threshold = permanent thrash; plus molt rows claim outcomes before seat-molt answers
description:
## Context
Measured live during maiden campaign run #3 (2026-08-09, molt-ledger + drain-ledger cross-read by the supervising seat). Two defects at one seam:

DEFECT A — THRASH ARITHMETIC. The marshal's pacing contract (69qr R5: molt/compact past ~50%) assumes crossing back UNDER the threshold afterward. Reality measured: a fresh tick's onboard alone lands ~40% (~109k tokens bulk reads); the 17:02:42Z in-flight compact fired at 69% and floored at 60% — NINE points reclaimed, because preserved handles + summary + always-loaded tier dominate. With floor(compact) ≈ 60% > threshold(50%), every subsequent boundary check re-triggers: compaction spend with near-zero reclaim, repeatedly. Window glyphs showed the cadence: three 🌀 episodes within ~35 minutes.

DEFECT B — OUTCOME CLAIMED BEFORE THE ACTION. Drain-ledger 16:45:44Z: outcome 'molt', reason 'compacting via seat-molt --in-flight yes; handles preserved'. Molt-ledger 16:45:59Z (15s LATER): mode compact, pct 53, result 'refused-not-offboarded'. The marshal wrote its ledger row before seat-molt returned, reported success prose for an action that was refused, and continued uncompacted (correct outcome by luck, wrong record — silent-success family; an auditor reading the drain ledger sees a compaction that never happened).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a marshal night with a builder in flight; let context cross 50%.
2. Compare the drain-ledger molt row's timestamp+claim against the molt-ledger row for the same event: drain row precedes and over-claims (16:45:44 vs 16:45:59 refusal, 2026-08-09).
3. After a successful in-flight compact, read the post-compact context pct (statusline or molt row): ~60% — already past the 50% threshold at birth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ledger honesty: the marshal writes its molt/compact drain-ledger row AFTER seat-molt returns, carrying seat-molt's actual result verbatim (molted/compacted/refused-*); a refusal triggers a stated fallback (offboard-then-retry once, else continue with the refusal recorded), never silent continuation under a success claim.
- [ ] Pacing calibrated to measured floors, not aspiration: threshold expressed relative to the seat's post-reset baseline (e.g. trigger at baseline + margin, with fresh-onboard ~40% and post-compact floor measured per mode), OR compact-carried content slimmed until the floor sits well under threshold — builder picks with measurement, states the numbers in the commit.
- [ ] Anti-thrash guard: after a compact that reclaims less than a stated minimum (e.g. <15 points), the marshal does not re-attempt compaction before the next bead boundary; it either molts at the boundary (full reset to onboard baseline) or finishes the night at elevated context with the condition recorded.
- [ ] Evidence: one night's ledger showing honest result rows and no back-to-back low-reclaim compactions.

title: decision: fresh-pool BIG budget via cross-pool cap transfer (not hand-set weekly_cap_tokens); hold pulse-marshal.timer tonight if the readiness chain is incomplete by 00:45 PT
description:
## Context
2026-08-09 ~21:4xZ, ahead of the first autonomous marshal night (01:07 PT). Zig's ruling
re-homed the marshal to the fresh secondary pool so the drain budgets big; verification
(dotfiles-5gob) showed the budget verb cannot see the re-home, and the consul separately
flagged the marshal pane as a 200k-window Fable context on primary (lstn alias trap) that a
molt cannot fix — only a true process relaunch through the identity wrapper. Fork points:
(a) how tonight's big budget gets its cap number — hand-set weekly_cap_tokens in marshal.conf
vs implement cross-pool cap transfer; (b) what happens if the readiness chain (lstn landed +
marshal process restarted on secondary/1M + 5gob merged) is incomplete at 01:07.

## Decision
(a) Implement the cap TRANSFER (5gob AC): derive cap_est from the history-rich primary pool,
meter spend/brake on the launch pool. No hand-set weekly_cap_tokens.
(b) If the chain is incomplete by 00:45 PT, stop pulse-marshal.timer for tonight and re-arm
after the chain completes (first funded night slips one day rather than running a 200k
Fable/primary marshal on a floor-or-incoherent budget).

## Why
(a) The ledger holds ZERO measured cap_est (28 rows, all floor nights) — any hand-set number
would be invented, and an invented cap in a spend governor is exactly the silent-huge-budget
failure dw3r's header warns against. The transfer derives from the same measured formula the
code already trusts, names both pools in the reason string, and keeps every degrade honest.
(b) Consul's evidence: marshal at 73% context immediately post-onboard on the 200k window;
a drain in that state is compaction thrash burning the fresh pool. The floor safety net does
not protect against a thrashing seat, only against overspend.

## Reversibility
(a) High — config still honors explicit weekly_cap_tokens as an override at any time.
(b) High — `systemctl --user start pulse-marshal.timer` re-arms; the stamp/Persistent=false
semantics mean a skipped night just waits for the next 01:07.

title: fleet proxy: readJsonBody returns {} on unparseable input — the {data:{...}} wrapper bug is unfixed at source
description:
Found 2026-07-26 during the gdoc/airtable proxy work (explore-7iz9).

`lib/asana/handlers.ts:86` `readJsonBody` returns `{}` on unparseable input. That is the root of the documented Asana silent-drop: send `{data:{name:...}}` and the wrapper is silently ignored — 200 OK, modified_at frozen, no error. The fleet has a MEMORY ENTRY about this exact trap, which means it has already cost real debugging time.

The new gdoc and airtable families are guarded by `lib/proxy/body.ts`, which rejects unknown top-level fields, empty bodies, non-object bodies and no-op request arrays with explicit 400s naming the allowed fields. **Asana was left pointing at the old permissive parser.**

Fix: point the Asana handlers at lib/proxy/body.ts.

Two related latent issues found in the same pass:
- `mapGoogleApiError` classifies on a NUMERIC code, but a `GoogleError` carries a STRING code — so passing an already-typed error through downgrades a 404 into a generic 502. `write.ts` special-cases it; `read.ts` does not. Latent today because reads only see raw gaxios errors.
- Both are the same shape: an error/parse path that degrades information instead of preserving it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Asana handlers use the strict body parser; a wrapped body returns 400 naming the allowed fields, never 200
- a regression test asserting the wrapper case fails loudly
- mapGoogleApiError preserves an already-typed error's status
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

readJsonBody deleted; all four Asana write sites now route through
lib/proxy/body.ts parseJsonBody, which rejects empty/malformed/array/string/
unknown-key bodies with a 400 naming the offending key.

Routing alone was NOT sufficient — one silent-success remained and was closed:
updateTask with a literal {} parsed cleanly and passed the empty-required check,
so it would still have returned 200 over an upstream no-op (handlers.ts:474).

Verified with a NEGATIVE CONTROL, not just a green suite: each fix was stashed
and its tests re-run against pre-fix code — 11/18 Asana and 6/10 Google tests
fail without the changes, so the guards are real. Every test asserts BOTH that
the status is 4xx AND that the upstream connector mock was never called (a 400
that still wrote would pass a status-only test). tsc + biome clean; full-suite
before/after failure sets identical (15 pre-existing, 0 introduced).

Landed in lb-marketing/lb-agent-fleet (its own repo — agent-factory gitignores
/agents/), commit b435d2a..feedafd on main, pushed.

⚠️ NOT DEPLOYED: :7100 still serves the old build (bun pid 350741). Needs a
restart with Zig's approval for the fix to take effect.

title: comms: the REALTIME CROSS-TAP GAP — third transport leg, or POST spool + tailnet notify wire?
description:
## Context
Zig directive (2026-08-10, via seneschal; priority EVENTUALLY, explicitly not this week). Today proved SendMessage is config-dir-scoped: the seneschal cannot reach linearb-tap sessions (~/.claude-work di-* windows) except by tmux-send. Zig asks: is tmux-send the end-state? Seneschal's position (endorsed for the record; argue back in the spec if design disagrees): NO — tmux-send is the mailman's doorbell (xvar C2), not a transport. Settled 7fik taxonomy: durable = the POST (mail/channels), live P2P = SendMessage (same-tap only today). The MISSING THIRD LEG: a thin realtime transport that crosses taps/config-dirs.

Zig's constraints: SIMPLE; leverages the local tailnet for security; IRC- or 'buzz'-shaped. Beads-broadcast is explicitly NOT this (bead store = work state, never a wire).

Prior art ALREADY RESEARCHED — do not re-derive (consult before designing):
- ~/explore/buzz/FINDINGS.md — Block Buzz: Apache-2.0, self-hostable, Nostr-based agent/human workspace (INDEX.md:493 calls it 'the standout... watch, don't join')
- ~/explore/agent-social-platforms/FINDINGS.md — the broader survey
- ~/explore/INDEX.md:493,612 cluster for placement

## The design question to hold (this bead is a HOLDING bead, not the spec)
Does the POST's spool + a thin tailnet-local NOTIFY WIRE (something as small as an inotify-forwarder or a netcat/UDS relay over tailnet) cover the realtime gap — making 'realtime' just 'the doorbell crosses taps' — or does a real message bus (Nostr relay a la Buzz, or minimal IRC) earn its place? Bias per Zig: simple wins; the burden of proof is on the bus.

## Zig forks to flag at spec time
- Whether a third transport exists AT ALL vs POST+notify (the core taste/architecture call — his)
- Tailnet ACL / exposure changes, if any (infra posture — his, htqt-adjacent)
- If a bus: self-host what, where (pico vs zig-computer), and who may connect (per-seat identity?)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When picked up: /spec produces the real spec bead (this bead's content is its §1-2 seed), AFTER reading the two explore FINDINGS files
- [ ] The POST+notify-wire null hypothesis explicitly evaluated and accepted/rejected with evidence before any bus is proposed
- [ ] Zig forks above walked via the conduit before /check closes
- [ ] Cross-consistency with 7fik/4x49/xvar message shapes asserted (comms-triangle rule, xvar §7)

title: stop-context-guard.sh fires at 50% with no idea whether a human is in the window — interrupted Zig mid-conversation twice
description:
## Context
imc-aug26 C2 (ref harness-harden-2026-08-13, routed via seneschal; Zig-prioritized in the 2026-08-14 works launch directive). The guard fires at 50% context regardless of whether the window is interactive; it fired twice mid-conversation after Zig had said to ignore it. A memory cannot stop a hook — the guard itself must know.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In an interactive session with Zig actively conversing, let context cross the guard's threshold
2. Observed 2026-08-12/13 (imc-aug26 window): the guard injects its molt/stop instruction mid-conversation, repeatedly, despite an explicit human instruction to ignore it

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The guard consults the seat's interactive: flag (agents/seats.yml via seat-resolve) and/or suppresses when a recent genuine user turn is present in the transcript
- [ ] Interactive windows get a quieter posture (single advisory, no repeat) while unattended/timer seats keep the hard stop
- [ ] Regression test + a mutant that dies on the named case (interactive-window fire)
- [ ] Behavior change noted where the molt lifecycle is documented (AGENTS.md molt section pointer, no copy)
notes:
THIRD OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-14 ~02:40Z, seneschal session fdee5165 — and the clearest one yet, because the waiver was explicit and recent.

CIRCUMSTANCE: Zig said, in this session, verbatim: 'drive all this now and ignore your 50% molt guard for now.' He then stayed in the window continuously, sending roughly a dozen turns over the following hour. The guard fired anyway, mid-conversation, while he was actively asking for analysis of the Portcullis pattern — instructing '/offboard then seat-molt --self'. Obeying would have destroyed the working context in the middle of his question.

WHY THIS INSTANCE IS GOOD EVIDENCE:
1. A HUMAN WAS DEMONSTRABLY PRESENT — not inferrable from a focused pane (which proves nothing), but from a continuous stream of genuine user turns arriving seconds earlier. That is the signal the fix needs, and it exists in the transcript already.
2. AN EXPLICIT WAIVER EXISTED and the guard could not see it. The estate has no way to record 'this seat is running long deliberately, with the operator's knowledge' — the same missing primitive as dotfiles-c6k5 (intentional seat shutdown) and dotfiles-2qwr (declare an expected gap, with an expiry). A 50%-guard waiver is literally an expected-gap declaration about CONTEXT rather than about silence.
3. THE MOLT WAS ALREADY PLANNED AND SCHEDULED — for the primary fable reset at ~06:00Z, with Zig present, per bead dotfiles-w65x step S9. So the guard was not surfacing an unmanaged risk; it was second-guessing a decision already made and recorded in a bead it cannot read.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, now that dotfiles-2qwr has landed: rather than teaching this guard about interactivity from scratch, let it CONSUME the expected-gap primitive. 'expected-gap declare --kind context-overrun --seat seneschal --expires <when>' would silence it for a bounded window and expire on its own — which is strictly better than the seats.yml interactive: flag alone, because a non-interactive seat sometimes SHOULD molt at 50% while an attended one usually should not, and both states are temporary.

Prior occurrences: imc-aug26 reported it firing twice mid-collaboration on 2026-08-13 (ref harness-harden-2026-08-13, item C2), after Zig had said at the start of that brainstorm to ignore it.
close_reason: SHIPPED on demesne main 56188d9 (rehearsed merge, battery delta clean). stop-context-guard.sh's 75% backstop now consults the seat's interactive flag via the same seam as pre-ask-user-question-seat-guard (seat_roster_path -> interactive:false strict read; cwd-proof — roster resolves from the lib's own dir): timer seats (marshal, linearb — the only interactive:false rows in the live roster) keep the hard stop BYTE-IDENTICAL (diffed against cda6266); interactive/absent-flag seats get ONE advisory latched in <session>.advised, which re-arm and pre-compact deliberately do not clear (now pinned by a test — F8); every failure path fails QUIET (advise-once) so a guard that cannot identify the window never nags a human. Defect-first: fixture roster reproduced the repeated rc=2 hard stop across two threshold crossings on the unmodified guard — the exact interrupted-Zig-twice shape. Scrutiny: SHIP with the failure-path weakening weighed explicitly (worst case = pre-it06 world, degraded not wedged; asymmetry argument documented in the guard header at :113-121). Final: suite 61/61, all 5 mutants killed incl. M4 interactive-check-removed + M5 advisory-latch-removed (opposite directions); test-molt-thresholds 17/17 with MB4's meaning verified intact by scrutiny (fixture adjusted, assertions byte-unchanged). Guard: test-stop-context-guard.sh I1-I8 + mutate M4/M5. Residual gaps tracked: dotfiles-ryy6 (50% nudge still seat-blind), scrutiny F5's advisory-in-a-should-be-timer-window alert gap (minor, noted on ryy6's family).

title: Wire seat identity into beads via a br wrapper injecting --actor
description:
## Context
THE MINIMUM VIABLE VERSION — the smallest change that is genuinely better than
today, and the one everything else builds on.

Measured 2026-08-08 on a throwaway store: `br --actor "<x>" create` writes
`"created_by":"<x>"` into the JSONL row. `BR_AGENT_NAME`/`BR_HARNESS`/`BR_MODEL`
do NOT reach the row (probed: still `ubuntu`), and neither `BR_ACTOR` nor
`BEADS_ACTOR` exists. **The `--actor` flag is the only seam.** It is global across
every subcommand, so one wrapper covers create/update/close/comment, and
`br audit summary` — which already tabulates by actor — becomes a per-seat ledger
with no new tooling.

Fails open: if `seat_resolve` fails, run plain `br`. A broken resolver must never
block bead work. Mirrors claude-identity-wrapper's fail-open contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `br` shell function injects `--actor "$(seat_resolve)"` when resolution succeeds
- [ ] A bead created in a seat window shows that seat in `created_by` — verified by
      re-reading the JSONL, not by the command's exit code
- [ ] With the resolver forced to fail, `br create` still works (fail-open proven
      by making it fail on purpose)
- [ ] `br audit summary` shows the seat as a distinct actor row
- [ ] No existing bead row modified; the 17 stores untouched
- [ ] The wrapper does not recurse (`command br`, per the claude() precedent)
- [ ] `--actor` injected at the GLOBAL position (`br --actor X <subcmd> ...`) — it exists both globally and per-subcommand in br 0.2.16; global survives subcommand shadowing
- [ ] Injection does not double when a caller already passed --actor
- [ ] Blocked by dotfiles-526s: the andrew/zig/unknown reconciliation decision lands first

Governing rule: seats.yml declares, state.json observes, neither restates the other. SEQUENCING: must land before the harnessd campaign's Wave-2 night 3 or g7qd slips (their plan, their words).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The SAME pre-commit arm that validates seats.yml regenerates + verifies the json (drift is a commit failure, not a runtime surprise); committed generated file, marked as generated

Pre-commit regenerates + diffs on every seats.yml/seats.json commit — drift fails with the exact regen command (verified live: corrupted file caught, restored file passed). harnessd's side (HARNESSD_SEATS_ROSTER relay) is the owning lane's bead; their Wave-2 night-3 blocker is CLEARED.

title: decision: campaign folders get their own git transport, not the vps rsync
description:
## Context
The vps manifest's `require-oob-untracked $HOME/linearb` complement rule swept
`~/linearb/imc-*` into the out-of-band rsync tier, because that rule cannot tell
"git does not own this" from "a DIFFERENT git owns this". Every `/bootstrap-imc` run
creates `imc-<month>` as its own repo with its own remote, so the class grows by one
folder per campaign.

For lb-granola the same flaw cost freshness (bead dotfiles-f5tg). Here it was
destructive: `rsync -az --delete --exclude='.git/'` from a zig checkout 11 commits
behind removed 12 committed script files from the VPS working tree, twice, while
leaving `.git` intact so git reported them as deletions. A subsequent
`git add <dir>` staged them and two commits captured the removals as intentional.

## Decision
Treat the campaign folders exactly as lb-granola is treated:
- `oob-exclude $HOME/linearb/imc-*` in the manifest, so rsync never touches them.
- The exclusion matcher now supports GLOBS (it was literal-only), so a new campaign
  folder cannot silently re-enter the rsync tier.
- `agents/scheduler/imc-pull.sh` on `imc-pull.timer` (every 10 min) is their
  transport: it CLONES any campaign repo the box is missing and fast-forwards the
  rest.
- `--ff-only`, deliberately unlike granola's `reset --hard`, because the VPS is a
  writer here and a hard reset could discard a commit made on the box.

Also corrected two now-false documented claims: the vps skill's "gh has zero
lb-marketing access" gap (it resolves and this session pushed to those repos), and
CLAUDE.md's Asana "read/comment ONLY" line.

## Why
The alternative was leaving a destructive race live and relying on an agent
remembering two disciplines. The exclusion removes the second writer entirely, which
is the same reasoning the complement rule already states in its own comment: "git and
rsync would fight over the same files."

## Reversibility
Cheap and total. Delete the `oob-exclude $HOME/linearb/imc-*` line to restore the old
behaviour, and `systemctl --user disable --now imc-pull.timer` to stop the poller. The
glob change to the matcher is backward compatible: a literal path is a glob that
matches only itself.

## Residual, flagged not fixed
`~/linearb/imc-july26` exists on the box WITHOUT `.git`, as an rsync-era copy. Now
that the folder is excluded, nothing updates it and imc-pull refuses to touch it,
because it may hold work never committed anywhere. It needs a human to reconcile
against `lb-marketing/imc-july26`.

title: pulse-ledger-lint: row names are harvested from EVERY table, so non-firing rows lint clean
description:
## Context

Found by autonoveld's tick-1 postmortem (`~/autonoveld/refs/pulse-tick1-postmortem.md`)
and confirmed live.

`agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-lint.py:routing_row_names` collects the `name`
column of **every** markdown table in the routing doc. A pulse doc normally
carries more than one: the active rows, plus candidate/archived/non-firing
tables that exist precisely to document what must NEVER fire. So a ledger line
attributing a tick to a row that cannot fire lints CLEAN.

## Steps to Reproduce

    python3 ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-lint.py --project ~/autonoveld

Observed 2026-07-27:

    valid_rows=conceive,desk-drain,desk-stale,housekeeping,learn,mail,triage,
               unattributed,voice-correction,write

`desk-stale` and `desk-drain` come from the table headed
"Candidate rows (NOT active — documentation only)". Hand-write a ledger line
with `"row":"desk-stale"` and the lint reports CLEAN.

## The fix that does NOT work — checked before proposing

The obvious patch is a `--section` argument defaulting to `Active rows`. **That
would break three of five pulse projects.** Surveyed 2026-07-27:

| project | heading above the ACTIVE table |
|---|---|
| `andrewzigler3` | none — the table precedes any `##` heading |
| `explore` | `## The weekly allocator row` |
| `picod` | `## The rows` |
| `autonoveld` | `## Active rows` |
| `investd` | `## Active rows` |

Whitelisting one heading name makes `andrewzigler3`, `explore` and `picod` find
zero valid rows, so every line in those ledgers becomes a violation. A lint that
fails everything is worse than one that passes too much.

## The fix that should work — invert it

**Blacklist the non-firing sections rather than whitelisting the firing one.**
Those tables are consistently self-labelling:

- autonoveld: `## Candidate rows (NOT active — documentation only)`
- explore: `## Archived rows — history only, NEVER fire, NEVER rewrite`
- explore: `## Non-pulse ledger rows — declared for attribution, NEVER fire`
- investd: `## Candidate rows (NOT active — documentation only)`

Skip a table whose enclosing heading matches `candidate|archived|not active`
(case-insensitive); keep every unheaded or otherwise-headed table. Compatible
with all five projects as they stand, and degrades toward today's
over-permissive behaviour rather than toward failure.

⚠ explore's "Non-pulse ledger rows" are DECLARED for attribution and never
fire, but they may be legitimate ledger row names. Check that table before
excluding it.

## Second change, independent

`check_record` should validate the additive `evaluated` array now shipping in
autonoveld (`autonoveld-9nf`): array of non-empty strings, no duplicates, every
entry a known row, a subsequence of table order, `row` a member and
`evaluated[-1] == row`, empty/absent when `row == "unattributed"`. Reference
implementation with tests: `~/autonoveld/pulse/ledger.py:_evaluated_violations`.
It needs names in TABLE ORDER, so `routing_row_names` must return a `list`, not
a `set`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Non-firing rows are rejected, verified against autonoveld
- [ ] All five pulse projects still lint their real ledgers CLEAN (run each)
- [ ] `evaluated` validated; fixtures added to `_selftest()`
- [ ] `--selftest` covers the heading-exclusion cases

## See also
- `~/autonoveld/refs/pulse-tick1-postmortem.md` — where this surfaced
- `~/autonoveld/pulse/ledger.py` — the local implementation, already tested

title: seat-liveness has no verb for INTENTIONAL seat shutdown — a deliberate close reads as an outage
description:
## Context

2026-08-14: Zig deliberately closed seven seats (consul, dotfiles, hevyd, digest,
di-wednesday, dev-interrupted, di-thursday) as planned pre-reset grooming. The
harness reported them all as DEAD, as though unexpected, and seat-liveness.service
went to a failed unit state repeating every 5 minutes.

**The watcher is behaving exactly as designed — this is not a false positive.**
Those seats WERE seen live and then stopped, which is the definition of `dead` in
its model (`absent` means "dead and never seen live by this watcher — not an
outage"). The exit-10-as-failed-unit rendering is also deliberate and documented
in the unit file: it must not read as a successful run, it is visible in
`systemctl --user --failed`, and it clears itself when the seat returns.

**The gap is that the harness has no way to be TOLD a shutdown was intentional.**
Every seat exit is inferred, and inference cannot distinguish "Zig retired this
seat on purpose" from "the pane died at 01:50 and the night is being lost" — which
is the exact incident the watcher was built for (the marshal pane, 2026-08-10).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a rostered seat running and observed live by seat-liveness.
2. Close it deliberately (kill the window, or /exit the session).
3. Wait `dead_grace_minutes` (10) and `min_dead_polls` (2).
4. Observe: the seat is classed `dead`, the unit fails with exit 10 every poll,
   and per conf (`bead_repo`, `push_url`) it alarms — bead plus push — for a
   shutdown that was intended.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A first-class way to declare an intentional stop, e.g. a `seat-retire` /
      `--intentional` verb, recording WHO, WHEN and EXPECTED-BACK, that
      seat-liveness honours without paging.
- [ ] That suppression EXPIRES. It must not become a permanent deny-list entry:
      a seat retired "for tonight" that is still suppressed next month is an
      unwatched seat nobody knows is unwatched.
- [ ] A genuine death of a seat marked intentionally-down AFTER its expected-back
      time still alarms.
- [ ] The distinction is visible where humans look — `hall`, the brief, and the
      failed-unit surface should read differently for "retired" vs "died".
- [ ] Proven by a mutant that dies on the case it names: an intentional stop must
      NOT alarm, and an unintentional one MUST, in the same test run.

## Notes

⚠️ THE EXISTING ESCAPE HATCH IS THE WRONG SHAPE FOR THIS, and the alert message
points straight at it: it tells the reader to add the seat to `absent=` in
agents/scheduler/seat-liveness.conf "so this stops paging". But `absent=` is a
PERMANENT deny-list keyed on a seat name, with no expiry and no reason recorded.
Using it for a temporary intentional shutdown converts a noisy-but-correct alarm
into a silent permanently-unwatched seat — trading a false alarm for a false
silence, which is strictly worse and is the failure mode this fleet keeps finding
(unread mail, granola starvation, the post-molt stall: silence and success
rendering identically).

RELATED SHAPE, worth designing together rather than twice: the same
"expected-signal absent vs genuinely-absent" problem underlies the post-molt
gateway-stall watcher and the granola starvation case, both in
refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md section 2.3. A general "declare an expected
gap, with an expiry" primitive may serve all three.

Zig's own read, 2026-08-14: "it's a good start" — the detection works; what it
lacks is intent.

comments.author: ubuntu

This bead becomes the seat-liveness CONSUMER change: honour an active gap (entity=<seat>, kind=liveness) without paging, and treat an EXPIRED unresolved gap as the strongest alarm. title: hooks: pre-bead-close scrapes bead IDs out of the -r reason string — any hyphenated word (or filename) in the close reason false-positive blocks the close
description:

Any hyphenated word or dotted filename in the reason matched and got linted as a bead ID, false-positive blocking valid closes (hit 3x on 2026-06-10 with words like 'fleet-wide' and script filenames in close reasons).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Valid bead bd-x exists with complete template.
2. Run: br close bd-x -r "Fixed fleet-wide via the new driver"
3. Hook scrapes 'fleet-wide' as a bead ID, br lint fails (not found), close blocked with exit 2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tokens after the first flag per close segment are ignored for ID extraction.
- Chained closes still lint every segment's IDs (bogus ID in segment 2 still blocks).
- Real bogus IDs before the flag still block.
- Hook test suite passes with the 4 new regression cases.

title: works: pico-health degraded since 18:38Z — reconcile its claims against xh18's evidence (pending-updates claim contradicts the live check)
description:
## Context
Audit 2026-08-09: pico-health.service failed (exit 10, PICO_HEALTH_RESULT=degraded, fail-closed by design) with four findings needing triage, one of which CONTRADICTS today's verified state: it claims 2 pending macOS updates (Sonoma 14.8.9 + Tahoe 26.6.1) — but xh18's close ran live softwareupdate -l post-upgrade showing NO pending OS updates and sw_vers 26.6.1/25G76. Either the probe reads a stale cache (softwareupdate history vs current), or its manifest predates the upgrade. Other findings: published state 182h stale (known: dotfiles-inot residual), undocumented listener 127.0.0.1:49265 + expected 60121 GONE (known: xh18 noted the ephemeral-port doc drift as works hygiene).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The pending-updates claim resolved with a live softwareupdate -l on pico: probe bug (fix the data source) or genuinely new updates since 12:36Z (schedule per patch posture).
- [ ] Port manifest updated: 49265 documented or explained, 60121 removed/corrected (the ephemeral-port drift from xh18).
- [ ] Published-state staleness routed to inot (comment, don't duplicate).
- [ ] pico-health returns PICO_HEALTH_RESULT=ok on a live run; the fail-closed behavior itself is correct — do not soften it.
close_reason: Root cause + fix merged to main (d81485c, agent bc806f8). Pending-updates claim: softwareupdate cache was invalidated by TIME ALONE (20h budget) — written 03:43Z pre-upgrade, still 'fresh' post-12:36Z-upgrade, re-serving consumed offers. title: post-molt gateway-stall watchdog — an outside-the-agent timer that detects a frozen fresh session, retries the injection, then pages Zig itself
description:
## Context

Zig's design (plan §2.3, refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md; ref mail
post-molt-gateway-stall): a session that molts comes back as a fresh process whose FIRST
command can die on an API/gateway error, leaving the pane frozen with nobody home. It
happened to the seneschal 2026-08-13 — sat frozen until Zig found it by hand. The agent
that needs rescuing is precisely the thing that cannot speak, so the watcher MUST live
OUTSIDE the agent process (systemd user timer), and when revival fails it must notify
Zig ITSELF (push + dashboard/bead), not via the stalled seat.

The absence signature is the reliable half: no tool call, no turn, no ledger row, no
state-file activity after relaunch.

## Design

Consumes the expected-gap primitive (dotfiles-2qwr — BLOCKED-BY it):

1. DECLARE: seat-molt.sh / seat-cycle.sh, at the moment they kill the old process,
   declare a gap (entity=<seat>, kind=molt, until=now+<grace>, by=<script>, reason
   naming the molt mode). Grace default ~10 min, config not hardcode.
2. RESOLVE: first REAL activity of the fresh session resolves the gap. Process start is
   NOT activity (today's incident: the process was up, the first turn died). Candidate
   evidence, builder picks and documents: first PostToolUse (a tiny hook or one line in
   an existing early hook, memoised per session), or mtime advance on the session's
   model-guard state file. SessionStart alone is explicitly insufficient.
3. WATCH: expected-gap-watchdog.{service,timer} (templates under agents/scheduler/,
   ~2-5 min cadence) scans 'expired' rows. For kind=molt:
   - revival attempt: re-inject a nudge prompt into the seat's pane (tmux send-keys via
     the pulse-inject.sh machinery — read PULSE_INJECT_RESULT=, its exit code lies,
     dotfiles-q0qi), re-declare with a retry counter, bounded retries (2-3).
   - retries exhausted: PushNotification path + P1 human: bead naming seat, window,
     last evidence timestamp — sent BY THE WATCHDOG (it cannot assume any seat is
     alive to relay).
4. Ledger every action (JSONL, row named, never null — explore-qdo5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A molt declares a gap; a healthy relaunch resolves it within one watchdog tick;
      NO watchdog action fires on the healthy path.
- [ ] A simulated stall (relaunch whose first activity never happens — e.g. kill the
      injected prompt, or a stub session) triggers: revival attempt(s), then push +
      P1 human: bead, all from the watchdog process.
- [ ] The watchdog itself failing to read state alarms rather than staying silent
      (three-valued discipline; silence must not mean success).
- [ ] Timer installed via the standard template path, Persistent=true considered and
      decided explicitly.
- [ ] MUTANTS DIE on named cases: at minimum (a) resolve-evidence stubbed out → the
      healthy path now pages (proves the resolve seam is load-bearing), (b) the
      retries-exhausted branch never reached → the page never sent (proves escalation
      fires). Mutation application asserted first.

## Notes

Home ~/demesne. BLOCKED-BY dotfiles-2qwr (the primitive). Siblings consuming the same
primitive later: seat-liveness intentional-shutdown (dotfiles-c6k5), granola-starvation
freshness. Do not modify seat-liveness in this bead. The 01:50 marshal-pane incident
(2026-08-10) and the seat-liveness watcher already cover 'pane died'; THIS bead is the
'pane alive, session frozen' complement.

title: fix: zig-watchdog HermesGateway re-blocks tasks based on stale lifetime crash counter (post-unblock)
description:
## Problem

After the M2/Documentation fix (dotfiles-hpi) shipped, t_360fa078 was unblocked
to test the Hermes --skills fix. The worker spawned, got past the "Unknown
skill(s)" error, and "Initializing agent..." fired — but ~3 minutes later the
zig-watchdog auto-blocked the task with reason "auto-blocked by zig-watchdog:
>=3 crashes detected" — even though run 102 produced ZERO crash events between
spawn and the watchdog's block.

Root cause: the M2 fix filters out `status=blocked` tasks but the diagnostic's
`consecutive_crashes` counter is a LIFETIME counter that Hermes does NOT reset
on unblock. When t_360fa078 went `blocked → unblocked → running`, the
diagnostic still showed `consecutive_crashes=97` from the pre-skill-fix era.
The watchdog probe at the next tick (status=running, count=97) classified
the task as actionable + over-threshold and re-blocked it mid-flight.

## Symptom

Run 102 of t_360fa078:
- spawned 04:42:38 (PID 3185413)
- worker log shows "Initializing agent..." (got past the skill error)
- no `crashed` event between spawn and block
- watchdog tick at ~04:45 auto-blocked it
- worker process killed mid-flight (pgrep returned nothing post-block)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a task with sticky `consecutive_crashes >= 3` lifetime diagnostic
2. Unblock the task: `hermes kanban unblock <tid>`
3. Trigger dispatch: `hermes kanban dispatch --json` (worker spawns)
4. Wait ≤5 min for the next zig-watchdog tick
5. Observe: task is auto-blocked by zig-watchdog despite zero new crashes

## Fix

In `local-models/zig-watchdog.py` `HermesGatewayJob.probe()`: after deriving
`_actionable_crash_loop_task_ids` from the diagnostic, query each task's
event log via `hermes kanban show <tid>` and count `crashed` events whose
timestamps fall AFTER the most recent `unblocked` event. Only if the recent
count meets `HERMES_CRASH_LOOP_THRESHOLD` is the task truly actionable.

New helper: `_count_crashes_since_last_unblock(show_text: str) -> int`
parses the events block via regex (event-line format
`[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] [optional 'run N'] event_name {data}`).

## Source of Report

Empirical observation from this session — push notification to user when
the regression caught a working Phase 2 worker mid-flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Regression test: task with all crashes BEFORE most recent unblock → OK
      (NOT actionable, even though lifetime counter is high)
- [ ] Regression test: task with ≥3 crashes AFTER most recent unblock → CRASH
      (still actionable; revive will block)
- [ ] Regression test: task never unblocked + ≥3 crashes total → CRASH
      (preserves current detection of a fresh crash-loop)
- [ ] Regression test: unparseable events → conservative fallback to lifetime
      counter (no false negatives)
- [ ] All existing zig-watchdog tests still pass (21/21)
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-cke in commit trailer

title: mlx-lm: server response parser missing Mistral [TOOL_CALLS] envelope support
description:
## Problem

`mlx_lm.server` (verified at v0.31.3) has a tool-call response parser that recognizes OpenAI-style `<|tool_call|>` markers and Qwen3-specific variants, but NOT Mistral's `[TOOL_CALLS]function_name[ARGS]{json}` envelope. Any Mistral-family model (Devstral, Mistral-Small, Codestral, etc.) served via mlx_lm.server returns responses where the tool-call bytes are silently dropped from the message.

## Symptom

Request a tool call against a Mistral-envelope model:
```bash
curl -s -X POST http://...:8090/v1/chat/completions \
  -d '{"model":"devstral","messages":[...],"tools":[...],"tool_choice":"auto"}'
```

Response:
```json
{"finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"role": "assistant"}, "usage": {"completion_tokens": 44, ...}}
```

- No `content` key (would be there for plain text)
- No `tool_calls` key (would be there if parsed)
- 44 tokens generated but invisible — parser ate them

Direct CLI probe via `mlx_lm.generate --model lmstudio-community/Devstral-Small-2507-MLX-4bit ...` (bypassing the server) confirms the model emits `[TOOL_CALLS]Edit[ARGS]{...}` correctly. The issue is purely the server's response parser.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. SSH to a host with `mlx_lm.server` v0.31.3+ running
2. Load `lmstudio-community/Devstral-Small-2507-MLX-4bit` (or any Mistral-envelope model)
3. POST to `/v1/chat/completions` with `tools[]` populated and `tool_choice: "auto"` or `"required"`
4. Observe: response message has empty `role: "assistant"`, no `content`, no `tool_calls`, N completion tokens reported but invisible

Sanity check (proves decode pipeline works): same model, no `tools` in the request → returns proper `content: "..."` text response.

## Suspected cause

mlx_lm.server's `tool_call_parser` likely hard-codes regex for `<|tool_call|>...</|tool_call|>` or `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` envelope shapes (matches OpenAI/Qwen3). Mistral models emit `[TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]{json}` instead. Parser doesn't match → strips the text from content but doesn't surface as tool_calls either.

## Source of report

This session's `dotfiles-ukx.11` Devstral swap probe (2026-05-27). Full 3-layer breakdown at:
- `explore/local-coding-models/refs/research/research-devstral-mlx-server-parser-gap.md`
- `local-models/GUARDRAILS.md` G18

## Deferred — investigate before filing upstream

This bead is DEFERRED. Before filing an upstream issue at `ml-explore/mlx-lm`:

1. Confirm by reading mlx_lm.server source (look at the tool-call response parser in particular)
2. Check existing GitHub issues — someone may have already filed
3. Decide: file an issue, write a PR with a Mistral parser, OR write a local CCR transformer shim (pattern: `local-models/trinity_shim.py`)
4. Consider: is fixing this worth it given Devstral has compound problems at the model level too (serial-not-parallel emission + hallucinated schemas + tokenizer regex bug)? Qwen3-Coder via llama-swap is the canonical tool-tier path. Devstral was nice-to-have.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] mlx_lm.server source confirmed as the gap (read tool_call_parser, identify the regex/format-detection logic)
- [ ] Upstream issue searched (any open ones?)
- [ ] Decision: upstream PR / local shim / drop. Documented in --notes.
- [ ] If shim chosen: implement following `trinity_shim.py` pattern, verify via the ukx.9 curl recipe
notes:

Production is unblocked: Qwen3-Coder via llama-swap is the canonical tool-tier path; Devstral was nice-to-have and has compound model-level problems anyway (G18). Revisit if mlx_lm.server gains Mistral envelope support upstream OR if a Mistral-family model becomes uniquely valuable.

title: cleanroom: build leak-check — the leak detector as a mechanism, not a prompt
description:
## Context
Fable audit of /cleanroom, 2026-08-09. The skill's signature contribution — the leak detector ('does the implementation contain correct facts the spec does not state?') — is currently PROSE: 'run it as a real gate: diff the implementation's load-bearing constants and branch conditions against the spec's stated facts.' No script, no verified invocation, no RESULT marker. That is the exact shape the skill itself condemns ('every public source treats disposal as a prompt, not a mechanism'). The skill's own standard, applied to itself, says build it.

Shape (design freedom to the implementer, within these constraints):
- A CLI at agents/skills/cleanroom/reference/leak-check (or bin/ if the demesne layout prefers), stdlib-only, no new runtime deps.
- Input: an implementation tree + a specs/ tree. Extract load-bearing literals from the implementation (numeric constants incl. hex, string literals above a triviality floor; per-language extraction can start crude — tokenizer-grade, not AST-grade — as long as false-positive handling is an explicit allowlist file, never silent suppression).
- Verdict: every extracted literal is either (a) stated somewhere in specs/, (b) allowlisted with a reason, or (c) UNEXPLAINED — and unexplained constants are the leak signal, listed with file:line.
- Emits LEAK_CHECK_RESULT=<verdict> on every terminal path (dotfiles-cxle discipline); exit nonzero when unexplained constants exist.
- Test suite in the house style, including the mandatory make-it-fail-on-purpose case: a planted magic number absent from specs/ must be caught (an oracle never observed failing is not known to work — the skill's own section 7 step 4).
- SKILL.md section 5 updated to point at the tool as the gate's mechanical form.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] leak-check exists, stdlib-only, LEAK_CHECK_RESULT on every terminal path, nonzero exit on leaks
- [ ] Planted-leak test proves it fails when it should; clean-tree test proves it passes; allowlist path tested

title: cleanroom: SKILL.md hardening — escape $N substitution hazards, fix the self-contradicting loop example, add the house wall recipe
description:
## Context
Fable audit of /cleanroom, 2026-08-09 (Zig-requested). Overall verdict: excellent — oracle-first framing correct, literature table has rare negative-result discipline, the shelf's agent-drivability axis is the right lens. Three defects found, all in SKILL.md, all doc-only:

1. RULE-7 SUBSTITUTION HAZARD (the explore-wcmj class). SKILL.md lines 20 and 372-373 carry $10 (x2) and $297 in prose. All three match the skill-argument rewrite pattern /\$(\d+)(?!\w)/, and this skill declares argument-hint, so it is invoked WITH arguments — the rendered body an agent reads will have those tokens rewritten ($50k on line 372 survives only because 'k' blocks the lookahead). Invisible on disk, invisible to review. Fix: escape as \$10 / \$297 (rule 7's sanctioned form). Sweep the whole file + reference/tool-shelf.md for any other $<digit> match (reference/*.md is read verbatim per rule 7, so the shelf is exempt — still record that check in the close reason).

2. THE ONLY CODE EXAMPLE CONTRADICTS THE SKILL'S OWN NON-OPTIONAL RULES. Section 6 shows the uncapped 'while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude -p ...; done' loop, then immediately mandates 'Always cap iterations' and 'the bash loop cannot tell success from failure — do not rely on it.' Agents copy examples verbatim (repo rule 2): the copyable form is the verdict-blind, uncapped one. Fix: present a capped, marker-checking canonical form as THE example (bounded iterations; treats exit-0-without-RESULT-marker as failure per dotfiles-cxle), and keep the while-: form only as the clearly-labeled literature original. Per rule 2, RUN the new example as committed (extract the block from the committed file and execute those bytes — a claude -p invocation may be stubbed with a fake claude on PATH for the harness run; what must be real is the loop/cap/marker logic).

3. STRUCTURAL DISPOSAL LACKS THE HOUSE MECHANISM. Section 5 demands 'the implementer's worktree does not contain the original — not should not open it, does not contain it.' In THIS harness, worktree subagents get a FULL repo copy — so if the original artifact is tracked in the project repo, every implementer worktree silently contains it and the wall is void on the default dispatch path. Fix: add a short 'in this house' paragraph to section 5: the original lives OUTSIDE the project repo (or untracked — untracked files do not materialize in fresh worktrees); the observer reads it by absolute path; the implementer's worktree is cut from a repo that has never tracked the artifact; name the check (git ls-files | grep, run in the implementer worktree, empty = wall holds).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zero unescaped $<digit> matches in SKILL.md (grep -nE '(^|[^\\])\$[0-9]' proof in close reason); reference/ swept and its exemption noted
- [ ] Section 6's canonical example is capped + RESULT-marker-checked, executed as committed (rule 2, bytes from git show), output in close reason; the literature form remains only as labeled quotation
- [ ] Section 5 carries the house wall recipe incl. the git ls-files check
- [ ] No other content changes — findings 4 (leak-check mechanism) and 5 (shelf --check derivation) are SEPARATE beads, not this one
close_reason: All three findings landed (merge fbab84e + review fix 7b3a1b2). (1) $N escapes: grep -nE '(^|[^\\])\$[0-9]' shows only the safe $50k; shelf swept clean. (2) Capped loop is canonical, literature form quoted-and-labeled; rule-2 executed from committed bytes (git show HEAD | awk fence extraction) with stubbed claude: DONE->exit 0, no-marker->exit 1 (cxle message), exhaustion->exit 1. The exhaustion path was MY merge-review catch — the subagent's version fell through exit 0 on five non-DONE markers; fixed in 7b3a1b2 and re-verified. (3) Section 5 house wall paragraph with git ls-files check landed. Fable-reviewed (Zig: this lane is review authority on cleanroom).

title: model seam: ONE shared settings.json means any session's /model or limit-degrade dialog rewrites the MACHINE default — and the model-guard then instructs every Fable seat to self-convert
description:
## Context
2026-08-10 18:42Z, measured live. The lb imc-aug26 lane hit the linearb 5h ceiling; the CLIENT's limit-degrade dialog (approved by Zig under incident pressure — the seneschal's client-gap report) persisted 'claude-opus-5[1m]' into settings.json. All four config dirs (~/.claude, -tick, -work, -secondary) symlink settings.json through ~/.agents to ONE file (demesne claude/settings.json), so a single lane's degrade flipped the MACHINE default. post-tool-model-guard.sh reads that settings key as its expectation seam ('source: settings'), so within 15 minutes it (a) 'restored' session b4b949b6 fable->opus (ledger 18:42:34 detected / 18:42:35 recovered — a Fable seat converted DOWN and its /model likely re-persisted opus), and (b) instructed the consul session (c417e95a, 18:57:16 detected) to do the same. The consul refused on seat-registry evidence (seats.yml consul: model fable) and restored the settings value by hand — the flip was uncommitted client dirt (permissions-reformat signature, bb3b912 precedent); after the format hook, byte-identical to HEAD, no commit needed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In any session on any tap, accept the client's limit-degrade dialog (or run /model <other-model>).
2. Observe ~/.agents/claude/settings.json's top-level model key now carries that model machine-wide (one shared symlink target).
3. Observe post-tool-model-guard.sh in EVERY OTHER live session now reports 'MODEL DEGRADATION' against its correct, seat-designed model and instructs /model <the-new-default> — which, if obeyed, re-persists and cascades.

## Why it matters
The guard's expectation seam (shared settings) diverges from the seat truth (agents/seats.yml per-seat model). Under that divergence the guard becomes a CASCADE AMPLIFIER: one accidental persist converts obedient seats fleet-wide, silently reversing Zig's model allocation (Fable plans/reviews). Session b4b949b6's 'recovered' row at 18:42:35 is a live instance of a wrong conversion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Guard expectation becomes SEAT-AWARE: resolve the window's seat via seats.yml (seat model pin wins; shared settings is fallback only for unregistered windows), or equivalent
- [ ] The /model-persists-machine-wide seam documented in the guard's own message text (it already warns; make it name the per-seat registry as the truth) and in AGENTS.md's model-seams section
- [ ] Session b4b949b6's downward conversion investigated: which seat, was opus re-persisted by its restore, is it back on its designed model
- [ ] Regression guard: a test where settings says X, seats.yml says Y for the seat -> guard must NOT instruct conversion to X (made-to-fail per rule 1)
- [ ] Consider: limit-degrade resilience — the client dialog cannot be intercepted (client-gap, 4x49), but a SessionStart/guard check can detect settings-vs-seat divergence at wake and alarm instead of converting
close_reason: Seat-aware model guard live on demesne main e338cb4 (FF merge, pushed+ls-remote-verified); suites on main post-merge: seat 13/13, base 34/34, mutation all-killed. AC1: expectation resolution env -> per-session override -> SEAT PIN (seats.yml via seat-resolve, alias-aware) -> refusal row -> /proc -> settings (unregistered only); refusal degrades loudly to pre-cpqi behavior, no exit-2 storm. AC2: guard message reframed alarm-not-convert naming the registry as truth + AGENTS.md model-seams paragraph. AC3 investigated (comment here): imc-aug26 = linearb seat alias; the client's model_consent_fallback row 18:42:28Z made the switch and the guard RATIFIED it — the incident input now exits 0 silently; live settings byte-clean fable; unhandled consent-fallback shape filed tiz6. AC4: made-to-fail proven (fix-lines revert -> 10/13 red reproducing the 18:42:34Z row); regression cases S1-S11 + M18-M20. AC5: scope-capped to recommendation + bead 09i0 (wake divergence check). Scrutiny SHIP recorded here; hardening follow-up dv62 (override writer, storm bounds, mutant gaps).

## AC5 — recommendation recorded, implementation deferred (bead dotfiles-09i0)

NOT implemented in this wave, deliberately: session-start.sh is shared infra with its own
blast radius, and the seat-aware expectation already removes the cascade this bead was filed
for. What it does not do is NOTICE the flip — the shared key can sit wrong for hours with
every seat correctly on its pin.

WHERE: agents/hooks/session-start.sh, after the seat-identity block (which already resolves
the seat, so the wake pays that cost once). NOT in the model guard's per-tool path — that

title: Do NOT build crew/fleet split or a dispatching concierge yet — record the triggers
description:
## Context

Wheelhouse runs 40+ agents, a 700-bead ready backlog, 12 extra Max accounts.
Crew/fleet balances those two populations; the Marshal exists because Yegge
never interacts with the fleet; the Seneschal dispatches because he is away.

Our scale: one account, one orchestrator, fire-and-forget worktree subagents,
~16-26 loops. No producer/consumer imbalance exists. Standing implementers
also contradict the rule that unnamed worktree agents self-terminate (a named
one lingers, no force-kill) — new lifecycle ownership, zero throughput gain.

## Decision

Roles stay skills-by-invocation. `subagent.md` remains the sole worker
definition. No Marshal. The concierge is built read-only (see `front-desk`);
its dispatch authority is NOT built.

## Why

A recommendation not to build, with a trigger, is cheaper and more honest
than a half-built city. Every structure above costs context in every session.

## Triggers that would reopen this
- One repo sustains >50 `br ready` beads for >14 days WHILE the orchestrator is the bottleneck (>=3 concurrent dispatches routinely)
- `human:` beads sit open >72h more than ~30% of the time (structural absence -> away-mode dispatch earns its keep)
- A second human or a second account joins the harness

## Reversibility

Fully reversible; nothing is deleted. Re-open on any trigger.
notes:
## REVERSED — 2026-08-08, Zig, in-session (2cc9586e)

Zig's words: the 'do NOT build a crew/fleet split or a dispatching concierge yet' call
was a premature judgment, considering how mature the harness is. Direction now:
DESIGN AND BUILD the concierge — Zig names it the SENESCHAL — and put the crew/fleet
split on the table.

On the original bead's quota concern: if weekly limits on the max account are the
binding constraint, Zig is open to (a) adding another account — i.e. another TAP
(Yegge's term, adopted 2026-08-08: tap = token/billing source, seat = persona;
resolves the seat-vocabulary collision) — or (b) using another tool (Codex) in
tandem as a heterogeneous tap.

Consequences:
- The three recorded reopen-triggers are moot as GATES but still worth instrumenting
  as MEASURES (Cluster C found nothing measures them — that gap survives as its own
  bead regardless).
- Seneschal design lands via the seat-topology synthesis (Cluster G) into the
  welfare epic t1qn; this bead stays as the historical record of the premature call
  and its reversal.
- Reversibility: high — nothing built yet either way; this reverses a restraint,
  not an artifact.

title: pre-commit-checks: 11/85 fail on macOS — the pulse ledger schema gate does not block, and timeout is absent
description:
## Context

`agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` fails **11/85 on macOS**. Confirmed
PRE-EXISTING: identical 11/85 at `164b161` (the 2026-08-01 session-start commit), before any
of that session's portability work. Not a regression — a standing hole.

Two clusters:

**(a) The pulse ledger schema gate does not block — `want 2, got 0`:**

```
- block: "row":null in a new ledger row            (exit: want 2, got 0)
- block: a row name not declared in refs/pulse.md  (exit: want 2, got 0)
- block: an out-of-contract outcome               (exit: want 2, got 0)
- block: a non-UTC timestamp                      (exit: want 2, got 0)
- note: no routing table -> visible skip, not a block (stderr missing: "skipping the ledger schema gate")
```

Four things this gate exists to block are **not blocked on macOS**. The `"row":null` case is
notable: CLAUDE.md rule #2 cites a `"row":null` ledger example that produced 23 bad rows
across 3 projects (`dotfiles-mlti`). This gate is the mechanism that was supposed to stop a
recurrence, and on a Mac it does not fire.

**(b) `timeout` is absent on macOS** — the proof-budget cases:

```
- allow: done with passing cmd proof              (exit: want 0, got 2)
- block: failing proof reports the exit code      (stderr missing: "exited 7")
- block: slow proof times out inside the budget   (stderr missing: "timed out after ")
- block: exhausted proof budget is named          (stderr missing: "proof budget")
- allow: digest done with the marker-grep cmd proof (exit: want 0, got 2)
- allow: legacy proofless history is not re-validated (exit: want 0, got 2)
```

macOS has no `timeout(1)` (it is `gtimeout` from coreutils, if installed at all). Note the
`want 0, got 2` rows: the gate is not merely failing to block, it is **blocking things it
should allow** — a proof that should pass returns 2.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
bash agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh   # FAIL: 11/85
command -v timeout                                  # nothing on macOS
```

Baseline check performed via a detached worktree at `164b161` — same 11/85.

## Fix direction

Same class as `dotfiles-5vz2`; the shim landed in `6a46488`
(`agents/hooks/lib/portable.sh`) is the natural home. Add `_p_timeout` that prefers
`timeout`, then `gtimeout`, and — if neither exists — **fails loudly rather than running the
command unbounded**. An unbounded "budgeted" proof is the same silent-degradation shape.

For cluster (a), find why the schema gate returns 0. It may be a downstream effect of the
same missing `timeout`, or an independent GNU-ism; determine which before fixing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] root cause of cluster (a) identified — dependent on `timeout` or independent
- [ ] `test-pre-commit-checks.sh` passes 85/85 on macOS; before/after pasted
- [ ] no gate silently allows on macOS what it blocks on Linux — that asymmetry is the actual bug
- [ ] a missing `timeout` fails loudly; nothing runs unbounded under a "budget"

title: finding (CLASS): the consumer reports success while the step stopped working — 17 confirmed instances, no standing check
description:
THE CLASS: a step stops doing its job, and the thing that reports on it keeps
saying success. No alarm fires, because the alarm is downstream of the lie.

This is now the DOMINANT defect shape in this fleet — not a coincidence.
Thirteen confirmed instances.

--- FOUND BEFORE 2026-07-26 (7, from the session handoff) ---
 1. claude-vault-sync exited 0/SUCCESS through 121 blocked runs over 5 days.
 2. harnessd asserted 12 live windows when 10 sat at a zsh prompt.
 3. andrewzigler3's nightly build "succeeded" 8 days while deploying nothing.
 4. weekly-report's AirTable calibration 422'd silently for a month.
 5. `git status --porcelain` defaults to -unormal, so a month-old backlog read as
    minutes old — blinding the alarm built to catch exactly that.
 6. A hook that redacted in place would have COMMITTED the secret and reported
    success. The fix for the class nearly introduced the class.
 7. `git push … | tail -1 && echo pushed` reported success on a 403, because a
    pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's.

--- FOUND 2026-07-26, Opus-5 audit Wave 1 (4 new) ---
 8. Fleet proxy readJsonBody returned {} on unparseable input: an Asana write
    answered 200 OK with modified_at frozen, no error anywhere (dotfiles-bm1c).
    Even after routing through the strict parser, updateTask with a literal {}
    still produced 200 over an upstream no-op until that was closed too.
 9. push-github-readme.sh exits 0 WITHOUT pushing when the README is
    content-identical. bd-xtm9's own prescribed one-line fix
    (`cmd && PUSHED=true`) would have reproduced the defect one layer down.
    THE PRESCRIBED FIX WAS ITSELF AN INSTANCE.
10. A failed README push still advances the camp hash, so the README stays stale
    until camp changes again and nothing retries (bd-troe).
11. Hevy `stale: true` is never written to disk, so both consumers read the file,
    see no flag, and render + LEDGER a stale snapshot as current (bd-ie0t).

--- ADJACENT, same shape, same day ---
12. The granola auth fix was applied at the NGINX EDGE, not in the service. Every
    external probe said "authenticated" while pico's router answered anonymously
    to the whole tailnet (dotfiles-13qu). THE VERIFICATION was what lied.
13. daily-digest wrote "row":null on every ledger line — 30 ticks that ran and
    were uncountable, so the dashboard read "no problem" not "no data"
    (dotfiles-ldag). Two further ledgers had it, tracked by no bead.

--- WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING (four generators) ---
a. EXIT CODE != EFFECT — wrappers exit 0 on a no-op path (9); pipelines return
   the last stage's status (7); a blocked run still returns 0 (1).
b. THE FLAG IS WRITTEN WHERE NOTHING READS — staleness in a build log (11), row
   identity dropped before the dashboard (13).
c. THE GATE ADVANCES ON INTENT, NOT OUTCOME — camp hash moves on CAMP_CHANGED
   rather than on the push landing (10).
d. THE PROBE TESTS A DIFFERENT PATH THAN THE ONE THAT MATTERS — edge vs service
   (12); status-only assertions that pass even when the write happened (8).

--- WHAT EXISTS, AND THE GAP ---
The /pulse ledger already refuses zero-distance proofs: `artifact` and `commit`
are REJECTED fleet-wide; only `cmd` (the hook RE-RUNS it) or `scrutinize` count
(explore-len0), enforced by pre-commit-checks.sh. That is the right principle,
implemented for exactly ONE surface.

Nothing applies it to daemon nightly builds, webhook receivers, deploy scripts,
proxy write routes, or any wrapper that exits 0. Instances 8-11 live in that gap.

--- THE ASK: a standing check, not more prose ---
Prose guidance demonstrably does not take (explore-369f carried standing
guidance and 44 of 128 findings ignored it). So:

1. REPORTING CONTRACT — any script whose success is consumed by another script
   prints an explicit verdict marker on EVERY terminal path, and the consumer
   treats "exit 0 with no marker" as FAILURE (fail-closed). Already implemented
   once: bd-xtm9's README_PUSH_RESULT. Lift it into a documented convention.
2. POST-WRITE VERIFICATION at every write boundary — re-read and compare instead
   of trusting the response. Correct already in lib/gdoc/handlers.ts:282,:319;
   missing on the Asana routes (dotfiles-580v).
3. NEGATIVE CONTROL as the standard of proof for a fix — stash the fix, re-run,
   the test MUST fail. Both Wave-1 agents that did this caught real gaps. "The
   suite is green" proves nothing about a test that would pass anyway.

--- THE META-POINT ---
Instances 6 and 9 are the ones to remember: in both, the PRESCRIBED FIX for the
class was itself an instance of it. That is why (3) matters most — the only
reliable defense is a check whose own failure mode is visible, applied to the fix.

Relates: dotfiles-b9ii (audit epic), dotfiles-mlti ("the documented example IS
the defect", the sibling class), explore-len0 (proof tokens), dotfiles-580v,
bd-troe, bd-ie0t, dotfiles-13qu, dotfiles-ldag.
notes:
## Instance count: 17 (was 14). Three more found the same day, all by loops auditing themselves.

15. recall-distill's gather_candidates() sorted by session-UUID STRING then
    truncated at 200, so all 200 candidates came from ONE session and ZERO from
    inside the target window — **66 of 67 sessions silently dropped**, and the tick
    logged a normal-looking row. Found by the tick itself, which then re-ran with a
    raised cap (5761 candidates / 57 sessions) and judged THAT set rather than
    logging a non-result. Filed explore-j2p9. Generator: the probe covered a
    different population than the claim.

16. **groundskeep-scan.sh ended in an UNCONDITIONAL `exit 10`** against the
    systemd unit's `SuccessExitStatus=0 10`. So a greenkeep that CRASHED made
    the unit go GREEN. Worse, `if $GREENKEEP scan; then` treated a scan error
    (exit 1) identically to drift (exit 10) and pressed on into a doomed run.
    Fixed in vs14d-l0t. Generator (a) in its purest form: EXIT CODE != EFFECT,
    with the systemd success-status list actively laundering the crash.

17. **gdoc.sh returns exit 0 on failure** — a bogus doc id dumps TypeScript source
    lines and exits 0; `read` on a tabbed doc returns EMPTY and exits 0. A caller
    cannot distinguish 'doc is empty' from 'doc does not exist' from 'credentials
    failed'. The weekly-report skill PUBLISHES through this shim on a live Tuesday
    timer. Filed dotfiles-79r8. Found only because a negative control was run on
    the probe rather than trusting a clean-looking result.

## What the newest three add to the analysis

All three were found by pointing a check at a loop's OWN reporting rather than at
its output — which is the practical form the standing check should take. Instance
16 is the strongest argument yet for the reporting contract: no amount of care
inside greenkeep.py could have surfaced a crash that the *unit's* success-status
list was configured to swallow. The verdict marker has to cross the process
boundary.

Instance 15 also generalises the coverage rule: it is not enough to report
'processed N'. It must be **N of M**, because N alone looked healthy.

## Measurement-side twin: dotfiles-effn (2026-08-07)
This bead is about a CONSUMER reporting success while the step stopped working.
`dotfiles-effn` is the same silence one layer down: six TOOL IDIOMS on this fleet that
return a confident wrong VALUE instead of an error — `find` without `-L` on the project
slug symlinks, `deferred` in the vault ledger, `rm -iv`, self-matching `pkill -f`,
leading-dash arguments, and uutils `ps`. Same failure shape: a plausible answer, not a
crash, indistinguishable from a true negative unless already suspected.

title: test-pulse-escalate: per-case CASE/PE_FAKE mktemp dirs never cleaned — 115k leaked dirs exhausted /tmp inodes 2026-08-11, bricking every Bash tool call fleet-wide
description:
## Context
2026-08-11 ~03:1xZ incident: /tmp (tmpfs, 1,048,576 inodes) hit 100% IUse while bytes sat at 35%. Every Claude Code Bash call on the box then fails at output-file open (ENOSPC) — the harness cannot execute ANY command, including the rm that would fix it. The Works seat recovered via hook piggyback (see the decision bead this cites). Post-mortem: 115,781 leaked tmp.* dirs in /tmp root, contents inject/isactive/panes/windows/escalate.conf/pulse-escalate.log — test-pulse-escalate.sh's per-case fake environment. Day histogram tracked the ckst arc exactly (2,090 on 08-07, 48,089 on 08-09, 57,346 on 08-10): panel scrutiny + mutation harness multiply the suite, and each suite run leaks case-count x 2 dirs. Evidence preserved in /home/ubuntu/.local/state/harness/tmp-inode-recovery.log.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run bash agents/scheduler/test-pulse-escalate.sh once; count tmp.* dirs in /tmp before/after — it grows by ~2 per case and no teardown removes them. Line 39 ROOT=$(mktemp -d) has trap 'rm -rf "$ROOT"' EXIT, but :289-290 CASE=$(mktemp -d) / PE_FAKE=$(mktemp -d) allocate fresh root-level dirs per case with no rm anywhere (grep rm -rf: only :40 and a fixture string :686). One mutate-pulse-escalate.sh run = ~20 mutants x 56 cases x 2 dirs ≈ 2,240 leaked dirs ≈ 20k inodes.

## Fix shape
Allocate CASE/PE_FAKE under $ROOT (mktemp -d "$ROOT/case.XXXXXX") so the existing trap reaps them — one-line-each fix, no per-case rm needed. Regression guard: a suite self-check case (or wrapper assertion) that counts its own /tmp root droppings post-run and fails on >0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A full test-pulse-escalate.sh run leaves zero new /tmp-root entries (asserted by the suite itself, not eyeballed)
- [ ] mutate-pulse-escalate.sh run verified same
- [ ] Guard test fails if a future case re-introduces a bare mktemp -d
close_reason: Landed on demesne main 76be894 (FF, pushed+ls-remote-verified; main tree-hash IDENTICAL to the six-suite-green scrutinized worktree HEAD, lib suite 41/41 re-smoked on main). Evidence chain: panel REJECT (29 agents) → fix 52b739b → fresh-agent re-scrutiny SHIP, all logged as comments here and on u1g1. Remaining class instances tracked: h8zv (corpus sweep), sug9 (test-pulse-inject legacy block + early-exit traps), zov8 (named-family audit).
