title: cxle instance: 03:5xZ works-gate report claimed 'marshal pane %397 green' after the window was already gone — liveness checks must re-resolve pane ids at check time
description:
## Context
Seneschal finding 2026-08-10, recorded as an unattended-reporting-contract instance (dotfiles-cxle class: success-shaped output from a check that did not observe the real thing). The predecessor Works session's ~03:5xZ gate report claimed 'marshal pane %397 green' — but the marshal window was already gone at the seneschal's 02:43Z listing. The check passed against a STALE cached pane reference: pane ids outlive their meaning, and a liveness check that trusts a stored id reports green on a corpse.

## Concrete fix
Liveness = re-resolve the pane by window/seat NAME at check time (tmux list-panes/list-windows fresh query), assert the process, THEN report. Never carry a pane id across time as the identity of a seat. Applies to: works-gate style checks, the seat-liveness watcher (dotfiles-vbzo), and any gate script that names a pane.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The works-gate check script (and any sibling gate that references a pane) re-resolves by name at check time — audit and patch each site
- [ ] This instance is recorded in the cxle canon (comment on dotfiles-cxle pointing here)
- [ ] A negative control exists somewhere in the gate suite: a check against a killed pane must report RED
close_reason: Landed on demesne main c87e3ef (merge of f4cca6a, pushed+ls-remote-verified); suites re-run on main post-merge: 41/41 + mutation 16/16 all-killed. AC1: full audit of 36 tmux-touching files / 16 classified sites recorded as comment here — 1 defect (api-stall-recover.sh cooldown keyed on bare persisted pane id, the incident's exact shape) patched to fresh session/window/pane triple per run; 15 clean, 5 independently spot-checked by scrutiny. The incident's works-gate itself was never committed code (verified both repos) — stated on the record. AC2: cxle canon comment verified pre-existing (2026-08-10 14:07), not re-filed. AC3: negative controls 17a-17e in test-api-stall-recover.sh (killed-pane/recycled-id must read RED) + existing seat-liveness cases 7/21. Scrutiny SHIP recorded here with before/after reproduction (pre-patch bytes fail exactly 4/41 incl. wrongly-suppressed nudge).

fields, then read each hit for whether the id crosses an invocation boundary.

title: gateway: capture X-Home-Tap / X-Tap-Rollover so a rollover is queryable in request_logs
description:
## Context
dotfiles-kecb's rollover emits two extra headers on a rolled-over launch and ONLY on one:
X-Home-Tap (the tap it came from) and X-Tap-Rollover: 1. Their mere presence is the query. Today
pico's CEL captures neither, so the only durable record of a rollover is the JSONL ledger on the
keep (~/.local/share/fleet-health/tap-rollover.jsonl) plus a stderr line in a pane.

X-Tap already carries the tap that RAN, so nothing is misattributed without this — but a
rolled-over row is byte-identical in request_logs to a launch whose home tap was always that pool,
which means nobody can count rollovers, spot one becoming permanent, or reconcile the keep's
ledger against the gateway's log.

## The seam
frontendPolicies.accessLog.database.add with default()-guarded CEL lines, the same route
dotfiles-7qi7/qmrp used for anthropic.ratelimit.{5h,7d} on 2026-08-09 (hot reload, no restart —
standardAttributes is the path that needs a kickstart, and it is hard-coded to user/group anyway).
Cautions are in infra.md: validate with `agentgateway --validate-only -f <cfg>` paired with a
deliberately-broken control; attributes co-mingle in attributes_json.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] attributes_json carries the home tap and the rollover flag on a rolled-over request, shown
  with a positive control (force a rollover with a fixture conf and watch the row appear) and a
  negative one (an ordinary launch carries neither key)
- [ ] The reconciliation query is written down in refs/probes/gateway-attribution-epoch3.md:
  gateway rollover rows vs tap-rollover.jsonl rows for the same window should agree
- [ ] Hot-reload evidence (the state_manager log line), not an assumed restart

## Write target
pico (agentgateway CEL config) — outside the trio. Hot-reload seam documented in-bead; needs gateway access, do interactively or from a pico-scoped runbook.

title: task: propose-only /triage pulse row — closure must stop depending on Zig noticing
description:
Fix #4 from the beads-lifecycle audit (refs/research/beads-lifecycle-audit.md).
Fixes 1-3 are mechanical hook changes and are being implemented; this one is a
loop and deserves its own decision.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATES IT: closure is purely EPISODIC — 2-3 closes/day
when nobody is watching, versus 50-63 on a sweep day. That is Zig's literal
complaint, quantified. A lifecycle that only advances when an orchestrator happens
to be paying attention is the same shape as this fleet's dominant defect class: it
works until nobody looks, and nothing reports that it stopped.

PROPOSAL: a scheduled, PROPOSE-ONLY /triage row. It never closes anything —
consistent with the propose-never-close rule that /desk already follows for the
same reason (a wrong close is silent AND permanent, and the idea simply
disappears). It surfaces candidates and files them where Zig can act in one pass.

A READY FIRST BATCH EXISTS: the audit found 32 open beads whose OWN BODY says
superseded / obsolete / moot. Those are self-declared dead and need no judgement
to surface.

Also worth folding in, all measured by the same audit:
 - 14 beads stuck in_progress and abandoned, oldest 62 days.
 - JSONL up to 333 HOURS behind the DB in three stores — br sync --flush-only is
   not running where it should.
 - br's native policy.yaml / gate_results machinery is entirely unused; it may
   already do some of what our hooks hand-roll.

Genuine age rot is narrow: only vacation-station-14 (median 88d) and autonoveld
(120d). Everywhere else the backlog is young and simply growing.

Relates: dotfiles-cxle, and the audit doc.

title: pre-commit: the drain gate now costs ~7 min per commit (suite 34s x 12 harness runs) — retune or trim
description:
## Context
`tools/githooks/pre-commit` runs `mutate-marshal-drain.sh` whenever any of
marshal-drain.sh / marshal.conf / test-marshal-drain.sh / mutate-marshal-drain.sh
is staged. Its own comment states the measured cost that justified that scope:

    test-marshal-drain.sh (76 cases, fixture db + fake br)     9s
    mutate-marshal-drain.sh (6 mutants + baseline)            62s

Both numbers are now stale. After dotfiles-5gob the suite is 134 cases / ~34s
and the harness runs 11 mutants + baseline = 12 suite runs, so the gate costs
roughly SEVEN MINUTES on every drain edit. That is still the right gate — every
mutant is killed on the case it names, and CLAUDE.md rule 1 is explicit that a
green suite is not evidence — but a 7-minute pre-commit is where agents start
reaching for `--no-verify`, which is the failure this gate exists to prevent.

## Task
Two independent halves, either is useful alone:
1. Correct the stale measured numbers in the pre-commit comment (a documented
   measurement that is wrong is rule-2 territory: it gets copied).
2. Cut the cost. The suite is subprocess-bound — each `budget` run spawns bash
   + sqlite3 + 3-5 python3 interpreters, and ~100 of the 134 cases run one.
   Candidates: batch the budget cases that share a fixture db; hoist the
   window-math python into a single call; or let the harness run mutants in
   parallel (they are hermetic under separate $TMPDIRs).

Do NOT cut it by dropping mutants or cases — the coverage is the point.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] pre-commit's stated timings match a fresh measurement on this box
- [ ] Either the gate is measurably faster or the cost is documented as accepted
- [ ] mutate-marshal-drain.sh still kills every mutant on the case(s) it names

title: the lexicon-glyph window matcher in pulse-dispatch-remote has no test coverage — the ssh stub answers for the whole lookup
description:
Reported by the dotfiles-77s4 agent as adjacent; filed rather than fixed.

## Context
pulse-dispatch-remote.sh resolves a row window with a remote pipeline:

    tmux list-windows ... | awk ... sub(/^[^a-zA-Z0-9_]+/, "", name) ...

The awk strips lexicon glyph prefixes (✅ 🧠 🔔) so `work:✅ imc-aug26` still matches the
row `imc-aug26`. That matcher is the fix for a real leak — without it a run does not
recognise its own glyph-prefixed window and creates a SECOND one; it previously put two
`weekly-report` windows on the box.

The suite cannot exercise it. The ssh stub answers for the ENTIRE remote lookup
(`list-windows | awk`) as one canned response, so the awk never actually runs. The
matcher therefore has zero coverage today, and a regression in it would be invisible —
while its symptom (duplicate windows on a shared box) is exactly the class of problem
dotfiles-77s4 was filed for.

## Why it is not a quick fix
Covering it means teaching the stub to EXECUTE the awk against a fake `tmux` that emits
realistic `#{window_id} #{window_name}` lines, rather than returning a precomputed id.
That is a stub redesign, not an added case — which is why it was correctly left out of
77s4 rather than bolted on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the stub runs the real awk against synthetic list-windows output
- [ ] glyph-prefixed windows (✅ 🧠 🔔 and a bare name) all resolve to the right row
- [ ] a row whose name is a PREFIX of another does not cross-match
- [ ] a mutant removing the sub() is OBSERVED to fail, mutation asserted applied first
close_reason: The ssh stub now EXECUTES the dispatcher's own awk instead of answering for it. Option (a), sharpened past the drift risk: rsh() sends exactly one word (bash -lc <%q-quoted cmd>), so the stub strips the prefix and re-runs it as bash -c with a synthetic tmux prepended to PATH — non-login on purpose, since -l would reset PATH to the real tmux. Option (b) was rejected for a better reason than the brief gave: the fragile part of that line is its ssh double-quoting round-trip, and calling an extracted function locally would cover the awk while leaving the quoting untested; this covers both. DRIFT IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE, verified by the orchestrator: 0 copies of the awk in the test, 1 in production. Two secondary guards — the fake tmux refuses any -F other than the production format, and the retired WIN_LIST knob exits 3 loudly rather than degrading to a silent no-op. 13 cases: bare name, four glyph prefixes, right row picked from a glyph-laden list, di-mon vs di-monday both directions plus a glyph-prefixed near-miss, glyphs-only matching nothing, unrelated window, empty list. Suite 267 -> 280, production file untouched. Orchestrator independently mutated PRODUCTION (dropped the sub(), test untouched, bash -n clean, mutation asserted applied): 275/5, every glyph case failing with resolved '@99' — the no-match sentinel — instead of the real id, including the 🌀 case, which proves the strip is generic rather than a hardcoded glyph list.

title: model-canon: re-derive the alias to canonical table when the claude CLI version moves
description:
## Context
agents/lib/model-canon.sh (dotfiles-lstn) maps fable/opus/sonnet/haiku to the
full model id the fleet must launch with. That table is a CALIBRATION of
`claude` 2.1.226, not a constant: the client's embedded catalog carries
`latest_per_family`, which moves whenever Anthropic ships a model, and the
`[1m]` asymmetry (haiku has no 1M variant; the tagged form is an HTTP 400) is a
property of today's catalog too.

A stale row does not error. It names a real, older model — so the fleet quietly
runs a previous generation, or quietly drops to a 200k context window, with
every suite green. That is the same silent shape the bead this came from was
about.

## Task
On any `claude` CLI upgrade (mac.upgrade.sh / ubuntu.upgrade.sh bump the
binary), re-derive the four rows and update the header's evidence block. The
probe used on 2026-08-09, one call per candidate id:

    claude -p "47+38" --model '<id>' --tools "" --setting-sources "" --output-format json

reading .modelUsage[<id>].contextWindow (200000 vs 1000000) and
.api_error_status out of the response JSON. Cross-check against the client's
own accepted-alias list, which is a plain string inside the binary: on
2026-08-09 it held sonnet[1m], opus[1m], fable[1m] — and no haiku[1m].

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] each of the four canonical ids re-probed on the current CLI, with the
      measured numbers pasted into the header of agents/lib/model-canon.sh
- [ ] any family that gained or lost a 1M variant reflected in the table
- [ ] bash agents/lib/mutate-model-canon.sh green

## Notes
Deliberately NOT in the table today: claude-opus-4-8 and claude-sonnet-4-6,
both of which carry native_1m in the client's catalog. They are passthrough
(rc 1) so a seat parked on an older model is never silently upgraded. Adding a
row for either is a decision, not an inference.

title: decision: the demesne lexicon — estate, keep/works/roads, seats sit on hosts
description:
## Context
The founding arc ratified the court register (seats, taps, offices, hall, marshal, seneschal, sigils) but the physical layer underneath still spoke a mixed dialect — demesne / zig-zone / infra / hostnames used loosely, with 'demesne' meaning both the estate and the private repo. Zig asked (2026-08-09, separate lane) to settle clean terminology before the seat-world cutover. Three forks were put to him via AskUserQuestion; all three recommendations ratified, plus one correction from Zig.

## Decision
THREE LAYERS, and metaphor binds to ROLES, never to boxes (machines die and services move: marketing-vps decommissioned, granola cutover pico->zig-computer, LinearB rows migrated home).

1. THE DEMESNE = the estate: every device + network Zig owns that the harness reaches with STANDING AUTHORITY. Membership test: Zig's ownership + a standing path + standing authority. NOT synonymous with the tailnet (marketing-vps was estate without ever being a peer). Zig's framing: the hosts share the VPS's public IP when needed, so the estate is 'like one big computer' — and a true grasp/map of the demesne is what makes it a demesne FOR THE SEATS.

2. HOSTS — proper hostnames stay; each holds a ROLE:
   - zig-computer = THE KEEP: VPS; where the court sits (harness, beads, timers, skills) and the public edge (nginx, the shared public IP).
   - pico = THE WORKS: Mac Studio on the home LAN; user-facing production (vs14, ollama) + the agentgateway every court request flows through. Tended FROM the keep over ssh.
   - the tailnet = THE ROADS, and its proper name is ZIG-ZONE (Zig's correction, 2026-08-09: zig-zone names the tailnet itself). Its MagicDNS domain is tailfb4637.ts.net — verified live; any '*.zig-zone.ts.net' DNS reference is drift (infra.md:72 has one).
   - metis = Zig's personal computer (roams; can host sessions).
   - homeassistant = appliance (tagged, managed from ~/picod).
   - iphone-15-pro = client INTO the demesne, not a host within it.

3. THE COURT — seats, taps, offices, hall — ratified in the founding arc; sits entirely in the keep today.

The private repo is THE DEMESNE REPO — the estate's RECORD (charter, roster, map). The estate sense of 'demesne' is primary.

HOSTS DO NOT GET SEATS. Seats are agent identities; hosts are where seats sit. pico hosts zero seats today (no claude CLI) and is first-class estate regardless — it holds the works and the gateway. If an agent ever runs there, the ratified grammar already covers it: pico:<seat>.

Retired: 'infra' as a concept name (the file becomes the demesne map). Clarified: zig-zone-as-DNS-suffix = drift; zig-zone-as-tailnet-name = canonical.

## Why
Every court spec in flight (hall sb6s, seneschal faty, marshal 4d57/69qr, seats.yml uikg) references the physical layer; a settled ground register stops each spec re-inventing it. Roles-not-boxes because the topology churned three times in three weeks.

## Reversibility
Prose + doc titles only. No live-system renames, no hostname changes, no DNS changes. Fully reversible until the map + charter land; cheap even after.

description:

title: Name, visibility, and on-disk location for the agent-brain repo
description:
## Context
Recommendation: `azigler/demesne`, PRIVATE, cloned to `~/demesne`, indirected
through `~/.agents`. The indirection must be a SYMLINK rather than an env var
because systemd --user and launchd do not read shell env — `%h/.agents/...`
works in a unit file, `$AGENTS_ROOT` does not. Shells export
`AGENTS_ROOT="$HOME/.agents"` derived from the symlink, never the reverse.
Open sub-question: does the public bootstrap script name the private repo
(discloses existence, not content) or read `$AGENTS_REPO` from `~/.secrets`?

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Repo name and visibility chosen by Zig and recorded here
- [ ] Symlink-vs-env-var mechanism confirmed or overridden with a reason
- [ ] `$AGENTS_REPO` disclosure question answered
notes:
## Decision — 2026-08-08, Zig via AskUserQuestion (session 2cc9586e)

**Context**: Fork = name/visibility/location for the agent-brain repo; alternatives were (a) as recommended, (b) same shape different name, (c) clone directly to ~/.agents with no indirection.

**Decision**: AS RECOMMENDED — `azigler/demesne`, PRIVATE, cloned to `~/demesne`, indirected through the `~/.agents` symlink.

**Symlink-vs-env-var**: CONFIRMED symlink, on technical grounds — systemd --user and launchd do not read shell env; `%h/.agents/...` resolves in a unit file, `$AGENTS_ROOT` does not. Shells derive `AGENTS_ROOT="$HOME/.agents"` from the symlink, never the reverse.

title: harnessd state-bus.timer + .service are MASKED — the fleet dashboard has served frozen state since 2026-07-29
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
  systemctl --user list-unit-files 'state-bus*'
    state-bus.service   masked  enabled
    state-bus.timer     masked  enabled
  systemctl --user is-enabled state-bus.timer -> masked

Masked, not merely disabled -- someone actively blocked it, and nothing records why.

Downstream (found by the pico audit, dotfiles-5da3): pico's `com.zig.harness` job
serves `state.json` on :10000 with `--auth none`. That file is pushed by
zig-computer's `harness-refresh`, which state-bus.timer drives. With the timer masked,
the dashboard has shown data frozen at **2026-07-29** ever since.

`KeepAlive=true` keeps the pico job green the whole time. **A healthy process serving
stale data is indistinguishable from a working pipeline** -- the dotfiles-cxle class
again, and the third instance found on 2026-08-01 (after pulse-ledger-lint having no
hook caller, and agentgateway-run existing with nothing calling it).

agents/infra.md described this pipeline as "Live now via state-bus.timer" until
corrected today.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Establish WHY it was masked -- masking is deliberate, so there may be a good
      reason (a runaway loop, a cost issue). Check journal + git log around 2026-07-29
      before unmasking anything.
- [ ] Either unmask + verify fresh state lands on pico's :10000, or record the
      decision to leave it off and make the dashboard SAY it is stale
- [ ] The dashboard should fail loud rather than serve a frozen file: a freshness
      stamp with a max-age, so "frozen" renders differently from "healthy"
- [ ] Note the pico side is `--auth none` on a LAN-reachable port (dotfiles-28jw
      records that pico runs without a firewall by Zig's decision)
close_reason: FILED IN ERROR — retracted 2026-08-01 after verifying. The mask is DELIBERATE and documented: harnessd/CLAUDE.md:51 says 'generates in-proc in Go (HARNESSD_GEN_MODE=go); state-bus.timer is masked, so the Python no longer generates.' Masking WAS the migration off the Python generator. Verified live: harnessd.service active, HARNESSD_GEN_MODE=go, http://100.98.174.21:14174/state.json -> HTTP 200 with generated_at 2026-08-01T22:06:51Z (minutes old). The pipeline is healthy. Also verified the mask symlink is dated Jul 7, three weeks BEFORE the 07-29 freeze this bead blamed on it -- which should have been the tell. The narrow real finding (pico's :10000 job serves a frozen copy) is a RETIRED PROTOTYPE, not a break: harnessd/CLAUDE.md:104 says the same-origin Go daemon 'evaporates the rsync-push-to-pico seam the prototype used.' Nothing pushes to pico by design. Refiled as the accurate, much smaller finding.

title: githooks: staging session-start.sh maps to a nonexistent test file, so its suite never gates a commit
description:
## Context

`tools/githooks/pre-commit` runs "the suite matching each staged `agents/{hooks,scheduler,lib,doclint}` script". For `agents/hooks/session-start.sh` it derives
`agents/hooks/test/test-session-start.sh` — **which does not exist**. The real suite is
`agents/hooks/test/test-session-start-merge-driver.sh`.

So editing `session-start.sh` gates on nothing. Found 2026-08-01 while fixing
`dotfiles-1rj5` in that exact file: the suite had to be run by hand, and the commit went
through without it.

This is the gate CLAUDE.md rule #1 describes as the *mechanism* that replaced intention —
so a name-derivation miss here silently returns the repo to intention-only for that script.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `git config core.hooksPath tools/githooks`
2. Stage any edit to `agents/hooks/session-start.sh`
3. Commit — observe the merge-driver suite does not run.
4. `ls agents/hooks/test/test-session-start.sh` -> no such file.

## Fix direction

Name-derivation by convention is the underlying fragility: a suite whose filename does not
match its subject is invisible to it, and nothing reports the miss. Two parts:

1. Map `session-start.sh` to its real suite.
2. **Make an unmatched script loud rather than silent.** Right now "no suite found" and
   "suite passed" are indistinguishable. At minimum warn; better, maintain an explicit
   script->suite map and fail on an entry that names a missing file.

Audit the other `agents/{hooks,scheduler,lib,doclint}` scripts for the same mismatch while
in here — this is likely not the only one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] staging `session-start.sh` runs `test-session-start-merge-driver.sh`, demonstrated
- [ ] a staged script with NO matching suite produces a visible warning, not silence
- [ ] every script in the four gated dirs audited for name mismatch; misses fixed or mapped
close_reason: Fixed in 3fe8494 — seven mismatches found, not one. Staging session-start.sh now runs 4 suites / 65 cases (was 0). Unmatched script prints a stderr banner + trailing warning; a map entry naming a missing file now blocks.

title: decision: the mutation-discipline clauses land in dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1, not /scrutinize
description:
## Context
dotfiles-3afr proposed two clauses — assert the mutation applied, and require a killed
mutant to fail the case it NAMES — and deliberately left the tier as an open question
for Zig: dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1, or /scrutinize. Asked to "fix those remaining beads",
Zig delegated the choice back rather than answering it, so this is a decide-and-proceed.

## Decision
dotfiles/CLAUDE.md **rule 1**.

## Why
- Rule 1 already carries the sentence being refined: "A green suite is not evidence that
  a guard bites; only a mutant that dies is." The clauses are a refinement of that exact
  claim, not a new one. Splitting a claim from its refinement across two documents is how
  dotfiles-x1fn happened this same session.
- Rule 1 is scoped to THIS repo's hook/guard testing, which is precisely where the
  mutation harness lives (agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh,
  agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh). /scrutinize is fleet-wide and owns the
  POST-IMPL AUDIT — stub bodies, composition gaps — a different gate at a different time.
- Cost of the alternative: /scrutinize is a global skill, so the clauses would load into
  every session in every project, to govern a discipline that only applies where a
  mutation harness exists.

## Reversibility
Cheap — it is prose in one file, and the rule points at the reference implementation
rather than restating it, so moving it later moves a pointer.

## What would change my mind
If a second repo grows a mutation harness, the guidance stops being dotfiles-specific and
/scrutinize (or a shared skills/_shared/ doc) becomes the right host.

title: task: the always-loaded staleness warning reaches Zig but not the running MODEL
description:
Known limit of the explore-6wwu fix (dotfiles de54842), flagged by its implementer.

The Stop hook surfaces a stale always-loaded file via systemMessage + stderr +
/tmp/claude-always-loaded/stale.log. That reaches ZIG.

It does NOT reach the running agent. Claude Code only feeds Stop-hook text back
to the model on exit 2 — which BLOCKS — and blocking was explicitly rejected in
decision explore-0z6r (it turns a typo in CLAUDE.md into an interrupted tick).

So a durable pulse window still acts on the stale snapshot; the human is now told,
the agent is not. That is a real improvement (the divergence is no longer silent)
but it is half the loop: the failure explore-6wwu documented was an UNATTENDED
tick escalating to xhigh and losing WebSearch, and an unattended tick has no human
reading systemMessage.

FIX DIRECTION (the implementer's own suggestion, and it is right): a
UserPromptSubmit hook emitting additionalContext. That path DOES reach the model,
does not block, and fires at exactly the moment the agent is about to act.
agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh is already written to be reusable for it.

Relates: explore-6wwu (closed), explore-0z6r (the decision), dotfiles-cxle
(the flag-written-where-nothing-reads generator — this is a partial instance:
written where the HUMAN reads, not where the actor does).

title: hevyd listens on *:14877 (wildcard) while its own docs say 127.0.0.1:14389 — both port and bind drifted
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `ss -ltnp | grep 14877` -> `LISTEN *:14877 users:(("hevyd",pid=995129))`
   A WILDCARD bind (all interfaces), not loopback and not tailnet-scoped.
2. `grep -n '14389' ~/hevyd/CLAUDE.md` -> L164 "systemd user service (hevyd.service)
   on `127.0.0.1:14389`". L109 documents 14389 as the chosen port.
3. `sudo iptables -S | grep -E '14877|14389'` -> no rule for either.
   INPUT policy is DROP, so it is NOT reachable from the internet.

## Assessment -- not an emergency, but two drifts in one
- **Port drift**: docs say 14389, live is 14877. Nothing in ~/hevyd explains the change.
- **Bind drift**: docs say 127.0.0.1, live is `*` -- so it IS reachable tailnet-wide.

hevyd/CLAUDE.md L459-461 records that this EXACT thing already happened once: it bound
`*:14389` since go-live while every doc said 127.0.0.1, and the resolution was that no
ufw rule exists and an off-box probe got REFUSED. So the internet exposure is genuinely
closed both times -- but the wildcard bind has now recurred on a NEW port, which means
the earlier fix did not stick (or was reverted) and nothing detects it.

⚠️ METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: `curl 51.81.33.136:14877` FROM zig-computer
returns 404. That is a loopback artifact -- the packet never traverses the firewall.
Do not read it as proof of public reachability. Probe from off-box (pico via tailnet
is also not the public internet; use a genuinely external vantage point).

Found during the dotfiles-w8xw infra.md refresh, 2026-08-01.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Establish which port is intended and make docs + service agree
- [ ] Bind to 127.0.0.1 or the tailnet IP explicitly, not `*` -- matching the
      documented norm and the earlier fix
- [ ] A check that DETECTS a wildcard bind regression, since this is the second
      occurrence; a doc statement alone demonstrably did not hold
- [ ] Cross-check against dotfiles-6wdw (the open P0 on unauthenticated
      internet->tailnet pivot) -- same hazard class, different port
close_reason: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 — the 'drift' was never the real hevyd. pid 995129 on *:14877 was a LEAKED SCRATCHPAD AGENT ARTIFACT (./hevyd built+run in a Claude scratchpad Jul 27, cwd deleted, reparented to systemd --user) — retired with full verification under hevyd-c9h (kill -TERM, port free, no respawn, unit's 127.0.0.1:14389 intact, intake chain re-probed). The unit's bind never drifted: docs and reality agree at 127.0.0.1:14389. infra.md's ports section corrected same pass. Recurrence check documented in hevyd CLAUDE.md; the systemic fix (reap processes rooted in removed worktrees/scratchpads — 41 more found and reaped on the keep) is the new dotfiles reaper bead.

title: o11y hole: claude sessions launched before their host gained a per-host zshenv route DIRECT and log NOTHING
description:
## Context
Reproducible instance captured live 2026-08-04 on marketing-vps before it could exit.
The earlier sighting (dotfiles-jfqq) vanished before it could be traced and was closed
as non-reproducing — THIS is that reproduction, with a better-supported cause.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On marketing-vps, find a claude process in a pane launched before 2026-08-03:
   `pgrep -af 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'`
2. Read its environment: `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | grep -E 'ANTHROPIC|CC_NO_GATEWAY'`
3. Observed on pid 1623429, pane work:4.0 (window "✅ di-tuesday"),
   cwd /home/andrew/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted:
     ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       -> ABSENT  (so: direct to api.anthropic.com)
     CC_NO_GATEWAY            -> ABSENT  (so: NOT the escape hatch)
     ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS -> "X-Session-Identity: work:di-tuesday" and NO X-Machine-Origin
4. Confirm the absence in the log on pico: no request_logs rows attributed to that session.

## Cause
X-Machine-Origin was added to claude-identity-wrapper.sh in dotfiles-v93v, and
marketing-vps only gained zsh/.marketing-vps.zshenv — the file that exports
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL here — on 2026-08-03. A pane whose claude was launched BEFORE that has
neither: the wrapper it launched under could not supply the base URL and did not yet send
the machine header. Both absences have ONE cause, an old launch. Same shell-age blindness
class as dotfiles-t6to, surviving in already-running processes rather than in config.

## Impact
The session works perfectly and is invisible to pico's request_logs. Per agents/infra.md a
client with no machine header logs group='unknown', indistinguishable from one that never
sent it — and a bypassing session is indistinguishable from an idle one. Confirmed in the
data: 5 rows today carried group='unknown', all agentgateway_user='zig-computer:zsh'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Enumerate every running claude on zig-computer and marketing-vps whose environ
      lacks BOTH ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and CC_NO_GATEWAY, and report the pane for each
- [ ] Zig decides which panes to restart (a restart destroys session context, so it is
      his call — per-pane recipe is in dotfiles-9o46)
- [ ] After restart, confirm the session appears in pico's request_logs with a non-empty
      agentgateway_group, queried with datetime(started_at) not a bare string compare
- [ ] Standing detection documented: any request_logs row with empty/'unknown'
      agentgateway_group is a client that needs restarting

title: weekly-report: the skill's Asana gids and Google Doc id are unverified
description:
Flagged honestly by the dotfiles-gify fix agent, 2026-07-26, as explicitly NOT verified.

The weekly-report skill hardcodes Asana gids (WS, ME, section 1208440192743649, the LinkedIn custom field 1208440192743659) and a Google Doc id. The agent did not verify them because no /tmp/.atok existed, and minting one triggers an OAuth refresh that REWRITES a token store — a write side-effect it had been told not to take. It stopped and said so rather than guessing.

That is the correct call, and it leaves a real gap: the AirTable half of this skill had TWO independent schema drifts (a renamed column AND two field names missing apostrophes, which AirTable silently omits rather than erroring). There is no reason to assume the Asana half is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- every hardcoded gid and doc id in the skill is resolved against the live API and confirmed to point at what its name claims
- anything stale is corrected
- a note on how these get re-verified periodically, since this class of drift is silent by construction
notes:
## Verified — 2026-07-26 (unblocked: tokens live in the agent-factory env)

Resolved every hardcoded id against the LIVE API via the fleet proxy, read-only —
no OAuth token store rewritten, which is what stopped the previous agent.

VERIFIED CORRECT:
- section 1208440192743649 -> resolves, returns real tasks.
- custom field 1208440192743659 -> present on tasks in that section, named
  exactly "LinkedIn" as claimed.
  METHOD NOTE: querying it via /sections/<gid>/tasks returns 'Asana resource not
  found' — because it is a CUSTOM FIELD, not a section. That is the PROBE being
  wrong, not the gid. Verify by expanding custom_fields.gid/name on a task. A
  future re-check using the wrong route will raise a FALSE ALARM.
- Google Doc 1YF_JiO3pcvcFR4x72NNJozGmsB8FMiv30PliJmZqEJk -> resolves; tabs are
  ["OLD", "Jul 22"]. "Jul 22" is a WEDNESDAY, independently corroborating
  dotfiles-r86n's re-derived rule (report Tue T=Jul 21 -> tab T+1 = Jul 22) from
  separate evidence.

NOT VERIFIABLE THROUGH THE PROXY (honest gap, not a pass):
- WS=1178181021060349 and ME=1208749853950521. The proxy exposes only
  attachments/projects/search/sections/tasks — no workspaces or users route.
  Used only as query scoping, so a wrong value surfaces as EMPTY results rather
  than wrong ones — but they remain UNCHECKED.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: gdoc.sh returns exit 0 on failure (dotfiles-79r8).

RE-VERIFICATION (the third acceptance criterion): this drift is silent by
construction, so it needs a periodic re-check. Right home is /housekeeping's
cross-repo state audit — resolve each id and assert the returned NAME matches
what the skill calls it.

title: two skill frontmatters fail a STRICT yaml parse — a stricter reader silently loses the whole routing entry
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
python3 -c "import yaml,re; ..." over agents/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter:

  desk      ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here
  dispatch  ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here

Cause: an unquoted `: ` (colon-space) inside an unquoted YAML scalar. In `desk` it is
`...resourcing memo to Andrew: what to fund...`; in `dispatch` it is
`` `subagent_type: "subagent"` ``. YAML reads the second colon as a new mapping key.

Also found: `beads` and `daemon` have **no `when_to_use` field at all**.

## Why it matters
Claude Code's frontmatter parser is LENIENT, so this has never bitten -- both skills
route fine today. But `description` + `when_to_use` ARE the routing table: they are
what the model sees when deciding whether to load a skill. Any stricter reader (a lint,
a future parser, an external tool, a doc generator) silently drops the field rather
than erroring -- so the failure mode is a skill that quietly stops being routable, with
no error anywhere. Same silent-success class as dotfiles-cxle.

Found by the dotfiles-wstl frontmatter-compression agent, which hit it because it ran a
strict YAML check BEFORE trusting its own A/B -- and discovered its first two edits had
INTRODUCED two new instances. Three pre-existing instances (cdn, dive, scrub-secrets)
were fixed as part of that compression; these two were out of its scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `desk` and `dispatch` frontmatter quoted so a strict `yaml.safe_load` succeeds
- [ ] Decide whether `beads` and `daemon` need `when_to_use` (they may be fine relying
      on `description` -- confirm the routing behavior rather than adding text by reflex)
- [ ] A strict-parse check wired into post-write-skill.sh or the pre-commit doclint, so
      the next unquoted colon is caught at write time rather than by an audit
- [ ] The check must FAIL on a planted bad frontmatter before it is trusted (repo rule 1)

title: marshal budget: DERIVED mode — compute the weekly cap from captured ratelimit utilization; floor only when the data is unusable
description:
## Context
Zig's directive 2026-08-09 ('we need to do this to fix marshall'): the headroom capture is LIVE (7qi7 — anthropic.ratelimit.5h/.7d land per-request in pico requests.db request_logs.attributes_json; first observation 16:23Z: 0.57/0.60), and all four marshal nights today ran the 150k degraded floor because weekly_cap_tokens is deliberately empty. marshal.conf's own text says the cap may be set 'from the captured headers' — this bead wires exactly that, inside budget_compute (agents/scheduler/marshal-drain.sh), as a DERIVED mode between computed and degraded.

## The math (v1, conservative by construction)
- obs = newest row where json_extract(attributes_json,'$."anthropic.ratelimit.7d"') != '' for agentgateway_group = cfg tap, with its started_at. Parse as float u, 0 < u <= 1.
- spend = SUM(total_tokens) for the same tap since the week-reset anchor (window_math already computes it — reuse, including the ISO8601-T datetime() wrapping trap).
- cap_est = spend / u  →  then the EXISTING pipeline runs unchanged (weekly_remaining = cap_est - spend, /days-to-reset, minus zig_daytime_reserve and safety_margin_pct).
- Conservative direction, stated in comments: requests.db sees only gateway-relayed traffic and per-tap spend; if the account pool is broader (16:23Z showed IDENTICAL utilization on personal + zig-computer groups — likely one shared subscription; ifk4 owns the reconciliation), spend underestimates → cap_est underestimates → budget errs LOW. Never the other direction.

## Degrade-to-floor cases (each with its own reason string, never silent)
- no observation / empty value / unparseable / u <= 0.02 (division blowup + implausible)
- observation staler than derive_freshness_hours (new conf knob, default 6)
- spend below derive_min_spend_tokens (new conf knob, default 1000000 — a tiny numerator makes cap_est noise)
- 5h BRAKE: latest 5h utilization >= brake_5h_pct (new conf knob, default 85) → floor regardless, reason brake-5h — protects the live window whatever the week says.
- Existing degrade paths (db unreachable etc.) unchanged.

## Output contract
- MARSHAL_BUDGET=<tokens> status=derived plus a reason carrying the inputs verbatim: derived-cap(u7d=0.60,u5h=0.57,spend=<n>,cap_est=<n>,obs_age_h=<n>) — the ledger night-start row must let a reader re-derive the number by hand.
- All three knobs documented in marshal.conf comments, key=value only (the parser refuses expansion).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] budget_compute implements derived mode + all degrade cases above; existing computed mode (explicit cap / --weekly-cap) takes precedence over derivation.
- [ ] test-marshal-drain.sh: fixture sqlite db with observation rows; cases for fresh->derived (known numbers, assert the arithmetic), stale->floor, empty/zero-u->floor, low-spend->floor, 5h-brake->floor; existing suite green before AND after (repo rule 1 — the pre-commit gate maps this file to its suite).
- [ ] No change to dispatch/merge/record logic; marshal.conf gains only the three commented knobs.
- [ ] Do NOT touch pulse-retry.sh / pulse-inject.sh (t5fj builder owns them tonight) and do NOT implement plan-persistence (29pj owns it).
- [ ] Expected output: a focused diff in marshal-drain.sh + test file + conf comments; report <=400 words with the suite output and a worked example from the REAL db over ssh (read-only query) if reachable, else from the fixture.
close_reason: SHIPPED: budget_compute DERIVED mode live in marshal-drain.sh (merge 04034e3) — cap_est = spend_since_reset/u7d with Fraction-exact arithmetic, freshness/min-spend/plausibility gates + 5h brake, every degrade named, explicit cap still wins. Suite 78->96/96 green on main, 7 mutants killed in the pre-commit gate, shellcheck identical to HEAD. Real-db worked example: u7d=0.72, spend=16,446,116 -> cap_est=22,841,827 -> budget 0 status=derived (reserve exceeds nightly share — honest and conservative; the carry decision is Zig's, pending with the tap-2 rotation). ## Scrutiny — SHIP (independent read-only agent, arithmetic re-derived by hand, real-code-path tests confirmed); 5 non-blocking findings + the bead-gate friction -> dotfiles-vosr (fleet-marked).

title: finding: the Opus-5 guide's remove-list is NARROWER than '80%' but hits /scrutinize HARDER than AGENTS.md's 2026-07-27 reading admits
description:
## Context

Fetched the live vendor guide 2026-08-01 (platform.claude.com .../prompting-claude-opus-5)
during the dotfiles-w8xw audit. Two corrections to standing harness beliefs.

### 1. There is no "80%" in the guide. The remove-list is SPECIFIC, not blanket.

Zig's framing ("Anthropic removed 80% of Opus 5's harness instructions") is
directionally right about the CLASS but wrong about the scale of what the vendor
actually prescribes. The guide opens with: "It performs well out of the box on
existing Claude Opus 4.8 prompts." It then names ~6 targeted removals:
  - explicit verification instructions
  - self-correction / re-check instructions ("double-check", "re-verify")
  - subagent-verification instructions
  - prompt-side VISION workarounds tuned for prior models
  - any rule instructing the model NOT to think/reason (increases tag leakage)
  - carried-over EFFORT defaults (re-run a sweep instead)
and adds ~4 things to ADD (conciseness, written-deliverable length calibration,
scope constraint, delegation caps).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AUDIT: "cut 80%" is not the vendor's recommendation and should
not be the report's frame. The real cut in THIS harness comes from local staleness,
cross-skill duplication and hook-duplicating prose -- which the vendor guide says
nothing about and which is likely the LARGER win.

### 2. The verification sentence is stronger than AGENTS.md records.

AGENTS.md's "Verification: no self-checking, but always evidence at the checkpoint"
section (Zig's call, 2026-07-27, bead explore-8hs7) keeps /scrutinize on the reading
that the guide "never measures" separate fresh-context adversarial review. Verbatim
from the live guide:

  "If your prompt contains explicit verification instructions ('include a final
   verification step for any non-trivial task,' 'USE A SUBAGENT TO VERIFY'), remove
   them: instructions like these cause over-verification on Claude Opus 5, and
   removing them reduces wasted tokens with no loss in quality. THE SAME APPLIES TO
   LEGACY HARNESS SCAFFOLDING THAT ADDS SEPARATE VERIFICATION STEPS."

and in the delegation section:

  "do not use subagents to verify or double-check your own work."

So "use a subagent to verify" and "legacy harness scaffolding that adds separate
verification steps" ARE named. The 2026-07-27 claim that the guide "never measures
the second" is not supportable as written.

NOT proposing /scrutinize be deleted. The conflicted-judge argument in AGENTS.md is
an INCENTIVE argument the vendor never addresses, and the harness has hook-enforced
scrutiny verdicts that a prose change won't move. But the tension is real, it is
Zig's call, and it should be settled by EVIDENCE (how often has /scrutinize actually
changed an outcome?) rather than by re-reading the guide. That evidence sweep is
the sibling bead.

### 3. The harness's dominant instructional idiom may be the weaker one.

  "Positive examples of the communication style you want tend to be more effective
   than instructions about what not to do."

Stated in the narration context, but the harness is overwhelmingly anti-pattern-
driven: every SKILL.md carries a large "Anti-patterns / never do X" block, and
TOOLKIT.md is literally keyed on "the single most load-bearing anti-pattern". If the
generalization holds, a large fraction of the harness's words are in the less
effective form. Worth an A/B before acting -- flagged, not concluded.

### 4. Opus 5 is itself a cause of the bloat being audited.

  "files that Claude Opus 5 writes to disk (reports, Markdown documents, summaries)
   are often longer than on prior models" -> add explicit length calibration.

/desk at 9,772 words, and TOOLKIT.md's note that the old elevate memo grew
1,460->2,190 words, are this documented behavior. A one-line length-calibration
instruction in the always-loaded tier is a cheap structural fix that stops
re-accumulation -- otherwise any cut we make grows back.
close_reason: done

title: vps: make the standing fleet forward DURABLE on the box (it is currently a leftover process)
description:
## Context

Zig decided the box keeps a STANDING forward to zig-computer's fleet proxy
(decision dotfiles-5q7c). But the forward that exists today is not standing by
design — it is pid 1220000, a leftover from a 2026-07-28 self-heal verification
run. Nothing re-establishes it after a reboot, an ssh drop, or a network blip.

That makes the property aspirational: the fleet believes the box always has
proxy access, and the first thing to notice otherwise will be a tick. With the
dotfiles-wv2a fix in place a dropped forward is no longer fatal (the dispatcher
falls back to opening `-R` itself), so this is about honoring the decision and
about the INTERACTIVE /vps path, which has no such fallback.

`ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure` is already idempotent and no-ops on a healthy
port, so it is safe to run on a schedule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A systemd --user unit on marketing-vps (under the `andrew` account) runs
      `~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure` on a timer.
      Interval: minutes, not hours — it must heal well inside a tick's window.
- [ ] `WantedBy` / `Persistent` shaped so it also fires after a reboot, and
      lingering is enabled for the account (`loginctl enable-linger andrew`) so
      user units survive logout. VERIFY linger is actually on; do not assume.
- [ ] The unit does NOT mask a real fault: a `2` (upstream answers non-200 =
      BLOCKED) must not be retried into a false heal. ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh
      already implements the three-valued contract; the unit must not paper
      over its exit code.
- [ ] The unit file is committed to ~/dotfiles (templates dir alongside the
      other scheduler units) even though it is installed on the box, so a
      rebuild is not archaeology. Note in the bead where it is installed.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: kill the forward on the box, show the timer restoring it inside
      one interval, with `curl 127.0.0.1:7100/api/health` -> 200 before and
      after. Paste the commands and output.

## Notes

Shared box — ben, kevin, mike, ubuntu also have accounts. Never `pkill` on port
7100; ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh's teardown is pidfile-scoped for that reason.

title: finding (CLASS): six tool idioms on this fleet that return a confident WRONG answer instead of an error
description:
## Why this is a bead and not a doc paragraph
Filed 2026-08-07 at Zigs instruction. These were originally scattered across a handoff
note (overwritten by the next /offboard), a retreat-scoped doc (deleted when that box is
finished with), and close-reasons on already-closed beads. None of those is queryable and
two are ephemeral. The record for a reusable finding is a bead.

Each item below produced a CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER during the 2026-08-02..07 session — not
an error, not a crash. Several were reported to Zig as fact before being caught.

---

## 1. `find` does not follow symlinks without `-L`
`~/.claude/projects/-home-andrew-*` are SYMLINKS to `./-home-ubuntu-*`, created by
`agents/vault/vps-phase2-symlinks.sh` so an agent whose cwd is `/home/andrew/...` reads the
CANONICAL content.

    find ./-home-andrew-dotfiles -name "*.jsonl" | wc -l   ->   0     (correct POSIX behaviour)
    find -L ./-home-andrew-dotfiles -name "*.jsonl" | wc -l ->  578
    ls -1 -- -home-andrew-dotfiles/ | grep -c jsonl        ->  404

**Damage:** produced BOTH a false all-clear ("0 unique transcripts, nothing at risk") AND,
after I "corrected" it, a false alarm ("2,036 unique transcripts, none in the vault") — on
the question of whether a 6.8G wipe would destroy data. I also declared `find` broken on
that box, which it was not.
**Tell:** `ls` and `find` disagreeing on one directory is a symlink until proven otherwise.

## 2. `deferred` in the vault ledger is HEALTHY when the stamp is fresh
`vault-sync.sh` classifies three ways: deferred + fresh stamp (< `VAULT_SYNC_STALE_HOURS`,
default 6) = exit 0 / `OK (deferred)` / ledger `quiet`; deferred + stale = STALE/blocked;
deferred + no stamp = DEGRADED. The word is printed on the HEALTHY path deliberately, "so
the log never claims a push that did not happen."
**Damage:** I raised it as a data-loss alarm before the final wipe. The retreat docs own
warning ("a deferred row is not a push") is true but is only HALF the test — the stamp is
the other half.

## 3. `rm` is aliased to `rm -iv`
Non-interactively it PROMPTS and then HANGS rather than failing.
**Damage:** a 5-minute command timeout mid-Phase-4, in the middle of severing ssh trust.
**Correct form:** `command rm -f`.

## 4. `pkill -f <pattern>` matches its own shell
The invoking `zsh -c ...` command line contains the pattern, so pkill can kill itself.
**Damage:** truncated a Phase 2 command; the output vanished and looked like a failure.
**Correct form:** resolve the PID first (`ss -tlnp`, `pgrep` + filter) and `kill` by PID.

## 5. Leading-dash arguments — every project slug starts with `-`
`grep "$SLUG"`, `find $SLUG`, `br close -r "-..."` all parse the value as a FLAG.
**Damage:** `grep -c` returned 0 for a slug that was present; ugrep errored with
`invalid argument -m=e-andrew-dotfiles`.
**Correct forms:** `grep -F -- "$SLUG"`, `find ./-home-...`, `br close -r="..."`.

## 6. `ps -eo` / `ps axo` are unreliable on this fleet (uutils)
`error: conflicting format options` on invocations that are valid for procps.
**Damage:** an empty process list read as "no such processes"; I nearly reported an
orphaned claude that had simply already exited.
**Correct form:** read `/proc/<pid>/{cmdline,environ,stat}` directly.

---

## The shape they share
**Every one returns a plausible value instead of an error.** The failure is silent, and it
is indistinguishable from a true negative unless you already suspect it. That is the same
class as `dotfiles-cxle` (the consumer reports success while the step stopped working) —
this bead is its measurement-side twin.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] decide a home for the durable subset — a `/scrutinize` or `/onboard` checklist entry,
      or `agents/lib/` guard notes — so it is not only in this bead
- [ ] items 3 and 4 are mechanically preventable: consider a `pre-bash` hook warning on a
      bare `rm` without `-f` in a non-interactive context, and on `pkill -f` whose pattern
      would match the invoking command
- [ ] item 1 deserves a check in any script that walks `~/.claude/projects`
- [ ] cross-reference from `dotfiles-cxle` so the two classes are findable together
notes: ## Correction — 2026-08-08 (config audit l7sp): item 6's diagnosis is WRONG. The ps failures are caused by OUR alias ps='ps auxf' (bash/.bash_aliases:91) expanding to 'ps auxf -eo ...' — procps-ng handles every quoted invocation fine via `command ps`. The recorded /proc workaround is unnecessary. Fix bead filed (see 'alias ps' bug); item 6's correct form is simply `command ps`.

title: pulse-ledger-watch flags 5 DISABLED units as errors — a false alarm every 2 minutes
description:
## ⚠️ RE-SCOPED and DOWNGRADED P1 -> P2 on 2026-08-07. The first filing was WRONG.

Originally filed as "5 local pulse loops are unregistered, they cannot surface and the
dashboard cannot see them", with an acceptance criterion of **adding manifest entries**.
Investigating before acting showed that would have been a mistake: it would have
registered five DEAD units and made the manifest less honest, not more.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
bash ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-watch.sh > /tmp/lw.txt 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"
cat /tmp/lw.txt      # -> PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_RESULT=staged:0:seeded:0:errors:5

for u in pulse-autonoveld-conceive pulse-autonoveld-mail pulse-autonoveld-voice \
         pulse-autonoveld-write pulse-picod; do
  echo "$u enabled=$(systemctl --user is-enabled "$u.timer") \
        manifest=$(grep -c "$u" ~/harnessd/refs/harness-manifest.json)"
done                 # -> all five: enabled=disabled  manifest=0
```

⚠️ Run the watcher WITHOUT piping to `tail`/`head` — a pipe makes `$?` the pager's exit
code, which caused a misread earlier the same day (see dotfiles-qn4t).

**Observed:** `errors:5` on every run, every 2 minutes, forever.
**Expected:** `errors:0` — a disabled loop cannot fire, so it cannot finish a tick, so
there is nothing to surface. It is not drift.

## What is actually true

All five units are `disabled`/`inactive`. The projects behind them are not dead, which is
what made the first reading plausible:

- `~/autonoveld` IS live — 38 ledger rows, newest today — but driven by the **`daily-ao3`**
  row (`pulse-daily-ao3.timer`, enabled), which IS in the manifest and verifies clean:
  `harness-assert-registration pulse-daily-ao3 daily-ao3` -> `state=healthy`, marker
  matches the newest row exactly. The four `pulse-autonoveld-*` units are superseded legacy
  that write nothing.
- `~/picod` has 22 rows, newest 2026-07-31 — genuinely dormant. `picod-health.timer` is a
  health check, not a pulse loop.

## Why it matters

`pulse-ledger-watch.sh` enumerates `pulse-*.service` without checking whether the timer is
enabled. That is the `explore-4x39` failure mode pointed the other way: **a false alarm on
a healthy system trains you to discount the alarm that will matter.** The error channel is
supposed to mean "a LIVE loop cannot be surfaced." (Demonstrated in practice the same day:
a monitor armed on this log was drowned by these five lines every 2 minutes and missed the
signal it was watching for.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Watcher skips loops whose timer is disabled; keyed on the TIMER, not the service's active state (a oneshot service is inactive between runs by design)
- [x] `bash ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-watch.sh` reports `errors:0` on a healthy box, with staged/seeded unchanged
- [x] A live loop that is genuinely unregistered STILL errors loudly — regression test; do not fix the false alarm by silencing the true one
- [ ] Separately, Zig's call: delete the 5 dormant unit files, or leave them
close_reason: Fixed in 9aeaeb2. pulse-ledger-watch.sh probes 'systemctl --user is-enabled <loop>.timer' after ExecStart classification: disabled|masked|masked-runtime are SKIPPED with a log note (not an error, not counted); every other state takes the normal path. Live verdict verified by me at REAL rc=0 (no pipe): staged:0:seeded:0:errors:0, down from errors:5, staged/seeded unchanged, all 17 live loops still examined -- confirmed pulse-weekly-report still evaluated each run. THE REGRESSION GUARD HOLDS, which was the real risk here: an unclear answer (not-found, empty, failed probe) is treated as LIVE rather than disabled, because reading 'disabled' from an unclear answer would silence a running loop -- the exact failure this script exists to end. Keyed on the TIMER's enabled state, not the service's active state. Suite 76 -> 88 (cases 26-29), verified by me at REAL rc=0, 88/88; test-pulse-retry 26/26 and test-pulse-dispatch-remote 421/421 unaffected. Mutation-checked both directions: breaking the skip fails 8 cases; adding 'enabled' to the skip list fails 60 including 'an ENABLED unregistered loop is still an error' -- the blast radius is the point, since skipping live loops switches the whole mechanism off. NOT DONE, deliberately: the five dormant unit files remain on disk (Zig's call, AC 4); they are now silent skips rather than noise.

title: hooks: nothing logs a hook rejection — 17 exit-2 sites throw away the fleet's best friction signal
description:
## Context
Found by the 2026-08-07 /dream audit while ranking durable pattern seams. There are
**17 `exit 2` sites** across the hook set and **none of them append to any file**. A
rejection is the single most concrete friction event the harness produces — an agent
tried something, a guard said no, and the reason is known at that instant — and it is
discarded every time.

This session alone hit three: the bead-create gate (missing -d), the commit gate (no
Bead: trailer), and the stderr-suppression guard. Each was a real signal about a
mismatch between what an agent expected and what the harness allows. All three are now
unrecoverable except from transcripts.

Ranked #5 of 5 candidate /dream seams on signal-available, but it is the only one whose
data does not exist yet — hence a build, not a read.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hook rejections append one JSONL line: ts, hook, rule, the command//arg shape
      (REDACTED of secrets), cwd slug, and the exit code
- [ ] Append is best-effort and MUST never block or slow the hook it instruments
- [ ] Receipt is git-tracked or explicitly justified as local-only (cf. explore-qd7k:
      a committed receipt can forge its own proof — decide which applies here)
- [ ] /dream gains a `hook-rejections` seam reading it, with a recurrence bar
- [ ] Secret-shaped values never land in the log (reuse scrub-secrets' detectors)

Cross-checked all 13 files: zero jsonl-append-on-rejection anywhere; session-end.sh's jsonl append is vault-redaction, unrelated. Claim confirmed: no hook rejection is logged. title: a seat BLOCKED on a permission dialog is invisible to the harness — it renders 🧠 (thinking), so Zig is never told
description:
## Context

2026-08-14 ~02:30Z: the Works seat (window 2) hit the dangerous-command guard —
an `rm` whose path interpolated a possibly-empty variable (`$PCTDIR/$SID.fired`),
the classic "if the variable is empty this deletes the root" shape. The guard did
its job and opened a Yes/No prompt.

**The seat then sat there, and the harness told Zig it was WORKING.** His words:
"that state was not something that was recognized by the harness, like the glyph
system and the thing that notifies me when an agent needs my attention. It was
hanging there and I didn't know. I just thought it was thinking and working."

It was found only because the seneschal's heartbeat captures pane text and reads
it. Nothing else on the box would have noticed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have any seat run a command that trips a permission/dangerous-command guard.
2. Observe `agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh`: `LEXICON_WINDOW_RE` recognises exactly
   four glyphs — `^(🧠|✅|🔔|🌀)` (thinking / idle / needs-Zig / compacting).
3. There is **no fifth state for "blocked on a modal dialog"**, so the window
   keeps whatever glyph it last had — in practice 🧠.
4. Result: a seat awaiting a human is indistinguishable, in the hall, in the
   glyph, and in every notification path, from a seat mid-thought.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pane sitting in a permission / dangerous-command dialog is DETECTED as a
      distinct state, not inferred from staleness.
- [ ] It surfaces where Zig already looks: the window glyph, `hall`, and the
      notification path that already exists for "an agent needs you".
- [ ] It notifies ACTIVELY — this is the same class as the post-molt stall
      watchdog (dotfiles-cbfc): a seat that cannot speak for itself needs
      something outside it to speak. A blocked seat is a stopped seat.
- [ ] The detector distinguishes BLOCKED-ON-HUMAN from BLOCKED-ON-MACHINE (an API
      stall). They look similar in a pane and need different responses.
- [ ] Proven by a mutant that dies on the case it names: a pane in a dialog must
      NOT read as 🧠.

## Notes

⚠️ **THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNOWS MODAL DIALOGS ARE DANGEROUS — it just has no
glyph for them.** `lexicon-window.sh`'s own header documents the injection
hazard: *"a pane sitting in a modal dialog, because the injected text is eaten by
the dialog and the trailing Enter ANSWERS ZIG'S OPEN QUESTION with the default."*
So the risk is understood at the injection seam and unrepresented at the
observation seam. That asymmetry is the bug.

LIKELY MECHANISM, for whoever picks this up: 🔔 already means "needs Zig" AND
already makes pulse-inject defer. Both behaviours are correct for a
permission-blocked pane, so raising 🔔 may be most of the fix — but confirm that
the deferral semantics are right before reusing the glyph, and consider whether a
distinct glyph is warranted so Zig can tell an open AskUserQuestion (answer in
the pane) from a permission prompt (answer, or rewrite the command) at a glance.

RELATED, STILL OPEN: dotfiles-q18 (36d stale) — "pulse-inject: defer+bounce when
target pane is in choose-tree/copy-mode (pane_in_mode), not just 🔔". Same family:
pane states the harness cannot see. Consider solving them together.

SIBLING BEAD for the other half Zig named — answering the prompt WITHOUT opening
a terminal — is filed separately; this bead is detection and surfacing only.

title: spec: phase 1 local coding-agent stack on pico (Qwen3-Coder + claude-code-router + Ollama)
description:
## 1. Overview

Phase 1 deployment of a Claude-Code-style coding agent backed by a local model on pico (Mac Studio M1 Max, 64 GB). Selects Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as the model, Ollama as the server (current, with 3 env tweaks), claude-code-router as the protocol-translation proxy, and keeps the user on Claude Code as the daily-driver harness. Pi Coding Agent is installed alongside as the kernel for future custom-harness experiments.

What this spec does NOT cover (deferred to a Phase 2 spec):
- LM Studio / MLX A/B test for the 2× decode win
- Aider as the diff-format coding-quality fallback
- GLM-4.5-Air for "quality > speed" runs
- Phoenix observability hookup
- Bespoke per-use-case harnesses (chat / batch / etc.)

## 2. Current State / Baseline

Pico runs Ollama 0.24.0 via a custom LaunchAgent (`com.zig.ollama`). Current env (verified live 2026-05-25):

```
OLLAMA_HOST=100.72.47.4:11434     # tailnet bind, NOT loopback
OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1
OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0
OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=24h
```

Service is healthy: cold model load ~15s, warm calls ~45-200ms TTFT, ~62 tok/s on the existing qwen2.5:7b. Pre-pulled models: `qwen2.5:7b` (4.6 GB base, NOT coding-tuned), `llama3.2:3b` (2.0 GB, too small for coding).

Plist source-of-truth: `~/dotfiles/ollama/com.zig.ollama.plist` with `TAILSCALE_IP_PLACEHOLDER` substituted at install time by `mac.setup.sh` lines 65-74.

Claude Code currently uses Anthropic-hosted Sonnet 4.6 — no local-backend wiring exists yet.

## 3. Changes and Decisions

| # | Change | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Add `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=131072` | Single biggest fix. Default 4K silently truncates and breaks tool loops. 128K matches harnesses-agent recommendation and gives serious coding-session capacity | both serving + harnesses agents flagged independently |
| 3.2 | Add `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2` | 64 GB has headroom for 2 concurrent slots | serving agent |
| 3.3 | Add `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2` | Allows primary + fallback (or embedding) resident simultaneously | serving agent |
| 3.4 | Pull `qwen3-coder:30b` | MoE 30B-A3B (3.3B active) — right architecture for M1 Max's bandwidth profile. 51.6% SWE-bench Verified, tool-calling fixed Aug 2025, ~40-55 tok/s on Ollama | models agent ranking |
| 3.5 | Install `claude-code-router` on pico | Translates Anthropic protocol → Ollama OpenAI-compat. CCR-on-pico keeps the chatty proxy↔model traffic on loopback; one tailnet hop for CC→CCR | harnesses agent |
| 3.6 | New LaunchAgent `com.zig.ccr` | Match existing zig-zone service discipline (own LaunchAgent so env vars don't get clobbered) | mac.setup.sh convention |
| 3.7 | Install Pi alongside (no LaunchAgent) | Pi is interactive CLI; install for experimentation + as fork kernel for bespoke harnesses | user directive + harnesses agent |
| 3.8 | CC client config: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://100.72.47.4:<ccr-port>` | Single env var on the CC client side; reversible (unset to go back to hosted) | claude-code-router docs |

## 4. Formal Specification

### 4.1 Ollama env (plist update)

Target file: `~/dotfiles/ollama/com.zig.ollama.plist` (then re-deploy to pico).

Add to the existing `<dict>` under `EnvironmentVariables`:

```xml
<key>OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH</key><string>131072</string>
<key>OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL</key><string>2</string>
<key>OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS</key><string>2</string>
```

Re-deploy: copy plist to pico, `launchctl unload` + `launchctl load -w`. Verify env via `launchctl list com.zig.ollama` and a smoke test.

### 4.2 Model pull

On pico (or via tailnet API):
```
ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b
```

Expected: ~19 GB download. Disk check before: `df -h /opt/homebrew` (Ollama default model store) should show ≥30 GB free.

### 4.3 claude-code-router install

On pico:
```
brew install node       # if not present (pico's Phoenix path requires Python; check Node first)
npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router
mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code-router
cp ~/dotfiles/ccr/config.json ~/.config/claude-code-router/config.json    # new dotfiles file
```

title: cleanup: the worktree sweep must check for live agents before removing
description:
## Context

2026-08-05, romd session. The orchestrator ran a worktree-cleanup sweep — the one
in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` "Delegation" — over `git worktree list` output while a
dispatched agent was **still running**. It removed that agent's romd worktree,
which was its cwd, and every subsequent Bash call in that agent refused.

The agent had deliberately committed nothing (its dispatch said "report, do not
ship"), so no work was lost. **That was luck, not design.** An agent mid-commit
would have lost real work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a worktree subagent; leave it running.
2. In the orchestrator, run the cleanup block over all worktrees:
   `git worktree list | ... | git worktree remove --force --force`
3. The running agent's cwd disappears; its next Bash call fails.

## Why the existing guard does not catch it

`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` already warns: *"With several agents in flight, name the
path explicitly and re-check `git worktree list` after — a broad cleanup kills a
running agent's tree."*

That is the right warning and it **did not work**, for two reasons worth naming:

1. It says *name the path explicitly*, but the natural way to clean up N finished
   agents is a loop over `git worktree list` — which is exactly the broad sweep
   it forbids. The safe form is more typing than the unsafe one.
2. **`git rev-list --count main..<branch>` returns 0 for a live agent that has not
   committed yet**, which reads identically to "fully merged, safe to remove". The
   check the orchestrator used to prove safety is blind to the case that matters.

The second one is the real defect: a liveness question was answered with a
merge-status query.

## The cross-repo twist

In a cross-repo dispatch the agent's *incidental* worktree (in the orchestrator's
repo) is genuinely disposable, while its *real* worktree (in the target repo) is
not. Both appear in `git worktree list` of their respective repos, and only the
second matters. In this incident the incidental one was removed — which is why
the damage was limited to killing the process rather than losing a branch.

## Fix

Make liveness checkable and check it. Options, none obviously best:

- the orchestrator tracks dispatched agent ids and refuses to remove a worktree
  whose id is still in flight (it HAS this list — it dispatched them);
- check for a live process whose cwd is under the worktree path before removing
  (`lsof +D` / `/proc/*/cwd`);
- a marker file the subagent writes on start and removes at handoff.

Whatever the mechanism, the rule to encode is: **merge status is not liveness.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The documented cleanup sequence cannot remove a worktree belonging to an
      agent that has not returned.
- [ ] Proven by attempting it against a live agent and watching the removal refuse.
- [ ] The safe form is no more typing than the unsafe one, or the unsafe one is
      blocked by a hook.

## Write target
~/demesne — AGENTS.md Delegation cleanup block + a live-agent check in the sweep (agents/lib/ or agents/bin/).
