title: pulse: a dirty checkout must NOT block a tick — proceed, work in the mess, commit your own paths, flag the rest
description:
## Context

Zig, 2026-07-30: *"pulses shouldn't trigger a tripwire if state is dirty. they
should proceed, so they can work in messy repos. then they can check in their
work when they're done and leave the dirty or flag it. then it won't do the
clunky lin-22h parking thing. but yea it shouldn't try to nuke or clean up repos
when they're dirty, they're all WIPs."*

This inverts a currently load-bearing gate, deliberately. Today it cost a full
fleet outage AND a clumsy workaround, both traceable to the same rule:

- An agent on the box edited `benchmarks-2026.md` in `~/linearb` and did not
  commit. `vps-repo-refresh.sh`'s read-only tripwire saw a dirty tracked file,
  wrote NO receipt, and `vps-preflight.sh` fail-closed — blocking **every remote
  row on every project**, not just di-thursday.
- Its remedy text says the file "MUST be reverted" with `git checkout --`. That
  advice would have destroyed verified benchmark-canon work. It survived only
  because the diff was inspected first.
- The orchestrator then could not park the change in zig-computer's working tree
  either, because **`vps-preflight.sh` blocks on uncommitted tracked changes on
  THIS machine too** — so the change had to be encoded into bead `lin-22h` as a
  patch and the tree restored. That is the "clunky parking thing".

## The rule

**Dirty is normal. Dirty is WIP. Dirty never blocks and never gets cleaned up.**

## Required changes

**1. `vps-repo-refresh.sh` — dirty tracked files become a WARN, not a failure.**
The refresh still writes its receipt. The receipt gains a `dirty` field listing
the paths per repo, so downstream can see the state rather than infer it.

**2. `vps-preflight.sh` — same on the zig-computer side.** "uncommitted tracked
changes will NOT reach the VPS" becomes a warning carried forward, not a block.
This is the specific gate that forced the `lin-22h` parking.

**3. NOTHING resets a dirty file. Ever.**
- Remove/neuter the `git checkout --` on harvest paths in step (b). Preserving a
  copy first does not make a reset acceptable under this rule.
- Nothing suggests `git checkout --` or `reset --hard` in any failure text.
- Re-word the tripwire message, which currently instructs the reader to revert.

**4. The pull must tolerate dirt.** `git pull --ff-only` can refuse when incoming
changes touch dirty files. That is NOT a failure now — the tick proceeds against
the older tree. But it MUST be recorded (see 5), because a tick running stale
code is the one thing that produces confidently-wrong output.

**5. Flagging is the price of proceeding — this is the load-bearing half.**
Zig's own standing principle: *"Missing output he catches. WRONG output he
cannot."* Removing the block removes the thing that made staleness impossible, so
the replacement must make staleness VISIBLE:
- the receipt records dirty paths + whether the pull actually advanced;
- the dispatcher surfaces that into the tick's `DISPATCH.md`, so the tick knows
  what state it is working in;
- the ledger row for that tick carries it, so a later reader can tell whether an
  artifact was produced against a clean, dirty, or stale checkout.
A tick that ran against a stale tree and said nothing is the failure mode this
bead must not create.

**6. ⚠️ THE WIP GUARD — the tick commits ONLY its own paths. NAME THE FILES.**
"Proceed on dirty" plus a careless stage equals a tick sweeping Zig'''s unrelated
work-in-progress into its own commit — strictly worse than losing a tick.

The first draft of this guard forbade `git add -A`, `git add .`, and
`git commit -a`, and **that list was incomplete**. Corrected 2026-07-30 by the
marketing-vps agent, which had just been bitten by the gap: the call that staged
12 deletions on the box was `git add refs/doc-scripts` — **a DIRECTORY**, none of
the three forbidden forms.

Verified locally in a scratch repo: with a file deleted from `d/`, plain
`git add d` stages `D d/gone.txt`. `git add <pathspec>` means "make the index
match the working tree there", INCLUDING removals. So any process mutating the
tree behind you — rsync, a sync client, a sibling agent — gets its deletions
folded into your commit under a message claiming you added something.

**The rule is: name the files.** Forbidden: `git add -A`, `git add .`,
`git commit -a`, and **any directory or glob pathspec**. Only explicit file paths.

Belt-and-braces check to run before committing (verified to catch the case above):

    test "$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only | wc -l)" -eq 0 \
      || { echo "ABORT: staged deletions I did not intend"; \
           git diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only; }

State all of this in `DISPATCH.md` in the same breath as the new permission to
commit.

## Interaction with lin-ekx — ORDERING MATTERS

`lin-ekx` (the peer-framing sweep) is IN FLIGHT and edits
`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`, its `DISPATCH.md` contract, and the `/vps` skill —
overlapping files. **Do not start this until lin-ekx has merged.** The two are
complements: lin-ekx grants the box the right to commit its own work; this bead
removes the gate that punished it for having uncommitted work in the meantime.

## Scope decision, recorded not assumed

Zig scoped this to **dirty** (uncommitted). `vps-preflight` assertion **A2**
(local HEAD not the published tip — i.e. COMMITTED but unpushed) is a different
axis and is NOT changed here: it means the box would run genuinely different
code. If Zig wants that relaxed too it is a one-line follow-on, but it was not
what he asked for and it trades away more than dirt does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dirty tracked file in a managed checkout produces a receipt + a warning,
      and the dispatch proceeds to completion.
- [ ] Uncommitted changes on zig-computer no longer block a dispatch.
- [ ] No code path resets, checks out, or stashes a dirty tracked file; no
      failure text recommends it.
- [ ] A pull refused because of dirt is non-fatal AND recorded.
- [ ] Receipt carries `dirty` paths and pull-advanced status; the tick sees it;
      the ledger row records it.
- [ ] `DISPATCH.md` tells the tick to commit its own authored paths explicitly
      and forbids `git add -A` / `git add .` / `commit -a`.
- [ ] Tests for: dirty-but-proceeds, pull-refused-but-proceeds, receipt contents,
      and an assertion that no reset command exists in the refresh path.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: dirty a tracked file on the box on purpose, run a real
      `--dry-run` dispatch, show it reaching `dry-run-ok` with the dirty path
      named in the output — then show the file still dirty and unmodified.
close_reason: done

title: vps-dispatch: oob-exclude directive — stop rsyncing a path that reaches the box by its own transport
description:
## Context

`require-oob-untracked $HOME/linearb` (the complement rule) pushes every top-level
child of `~/linearb` that git does not own. It cannot tell "git does not own this"
from "a DIFFERENT git owns this", so `lb-granola` — a nested independent repo whose
own remote (`azigler/lb-granola`) the box's PAT CAN reach — was being rsync'd as
out-of-band cargo on every dispatch.

Two problems with that, both real:

1. **Freshness.** As OOB cargo the corpus only moved when an unrelated pulse tick
   was dispatched. Measured 2026-07-28: a meeting delivered `17:08:48Z` reached the
   VPS at `18:44:39Z`, 1h36m later, and would have waited days over a quiet weekend.
2. **Two writers.** `rsync -az --delete` over a git working tree dirties it relative
   to HEAD — the same "git and rsync would fight over the same files" argument the
   complement rule's own comment already makes.

Adds an explicit `oob-exclude <path>` directive, pre-scanned so it is order-independent,
and declares lb-granola with it. The VPS now pulls the corpus itself every 2 min
(`~/bin/lb-granola-pull.sh`). Cross-ref: `lbg-y1y` in the lb-granola repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `oob-exclude` directive parsed and honored by the complement rule in
      `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`; declared for lb-granola in `vps-repo-manifest.txt`.
- [x] Order-independent (pre-scan), so the manifest never depends on directive order.
- [x] Regression test: the complement rule STILL ships an untracked child that has its
      own `.git` (the imc-aug26 case), `oob-exclude` drops only the declared child, and
      order does not matter.
- [x] Full suite green (91 PASS / 0 FAIL); negative control confirmed 90/1 with the
      inferred rule injected.

## Notes

Deliberately an EXPLICIT directive, not the tempting inference
`[ -e "$_c/.git" ] && continue`. That inference is wrong and was verified wrong:
`imc-aug26` has its own `.git` AND is untracked by the umbrella, but its remote is
`lb-marketing/*`, which this box's PAT 404s on — rsync is its ONLY possible transport.
Inferring would have silently stranded the August IMC folder, producing exactly the
failure the complement rule's own comment warns about ("a tick drafts confidently
WITHOUT campaign context — wrong output, not missing output"). The regression test
above exists specifically to fail if someone later "simplifies" it back.
close_reason: done

title: tailnet acl: add Taildrop file-sharing grant (bi-directional server↔user)
description:
## Context

Discovered while delivering `stable-diffusion-handoff.md` to the iPhone
via `tailscale file cp /tmp/stable-diffusion-handoff.md iphone-15-pro:`:
the command refused with `cannot send files: peer is owned by a
different user`. Tailscale's default-deny ACL treats Taildrop as a
per-user feature — devices owned by the same user can drop to each
other, but cross-owner (and tag→user) transfers are blocked by default.

zig-computer + pico are tagged `tag:server` (machine identities, no
user). iPhone + metis are owned by `azigler@`. Without a grant, no
file-sharing between them.

## Fix

Added a `grants` block to `tailscale/acl.jsonc` using the
`tailscale.com/cap/file-sharing` capability. Combined src+dst arrays
cover the full server↔user matrix in one rule. Capability-only grant
(no L3 traffic implication beyond what existing acls allow).

After applying via Tailscale admin console paste:
```bash
tailscale file cp <file> iphone-15-pro:    # tag:server → user
tailscale file cp <file> zig-computer:     # user → tag:server (from metis / iPhone)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `tailscale/acl.jsonc` updated with `grants` block
- [x] Comment block documents the rationale + capability syntax
- [ ] User pastes updated acl.jsonc into Tailscale admin console
- [ ] `tailscale file cp /tmp/stable-diffusion-handoff.md iphone-15-pro:`
      succeeds from zig-computer (verification target)
- [ ] Inverse direction tested optionally (drop from iPhone Tailscale
      app to zig-computer)
notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24 — WON'T FIX (Tailscale design limitation)

Tailscale's admin policy editor rejected the grants block with:
"Error: capability name must not be in the tailscale.com domain" —
the namespace is reserved for built-in, non-user-configurable features.

Confirmed via Tailscale docs (kb/1106/taildrop): "Taildrop is currently
limited to sending files between your own personal devices. You cannot
send files to devices owned by other users (even users on the same
Tailscale network)." Hard-locked by design; no ACL grant, nodeAttr,
or admin toggle.

Workarounds documented in zig-zone runbook gotcha #23:
- HTTP over tailnet IP (one-off): `python3 -m http.server` bound to
  `tailscale ip -4`, fetch from any tailnet device
- SSH relay through a user-owned tailnet device (scp → device A,
  Taildrop → device B)
- Untag the source (re-auth as user, breaks the identity model)

ACL revert pushed; comment block updated to document the limitation
so future-me doesn't re-try.
close_reason: done

title: vps-8a9eb245: full checkout + per-host shell files + system-owned tmux
description:
## Context

This box (vps-8a9eb245) had a SPARSE checkout of dotfiles (cone: `agents`,
`claude` only), so the shell tier was still served by `~/marketing-vps` — a
coworker-facing repo, not Zig's own:

    ~/.zshrc     -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/zsh/.zshrc
    ~/.p10k.zsh  -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/zsh/.p10k.zsh
    ~/.tmux.conf -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/tmux/tmux.conf

Both `zsh/.zshrc` and `bash/.bashrc` source `$HOME/.$(hostname -s).{zsh,bashrc}`,
and `sync.sh` symlinks those from `zsh/`/`bash/` when present. Neither existed
for this host, so even a full checkout would have left the box with no PATH /
toolchain env.

tmux ownership (verified): server PID 83840 sits in
`/user.slice/user-1002.slice/session-140.scope` — an abandoned LOGIN-SESSION
scope. It survives logout only by policy default (`KillUserProcesses=no` +
`Linger=yes`), not by ownership. Panes DO escape (tmux 3.6 is linked against
libsystemd and moves them to `user@1002.service/tmux-spawn-*.scope`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git sparse-checkout disable` — full working tree
- [ ] `zsh/.vps-8a9eb245.zsh` written, matching this box's real toolchains
- [ ] `bash/.vps-8a9eb245.bashrc` written
- [ ] `tmux/tmux.service` — systemd USER unit, installed + enabled (NOT started;
      Zig restarts the server himself)
- [ ] `download.sh` + `sync.sh` run clean
- [ ] `zsh -l -i -c exit` exits 0 with no errors — login shell not broken
- [ ] `~/.zshrc` + `~/.tmux.conf` resolve into `~/dotfiles`, not `~/marketing-vps`
- [ ] hourly `vps-repo-refresh.timer` still does an ff-only pull of `~/dotfiles`
- [ ] `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` removal kept in `claude/settings.json`; the pico proxy
      moved to `zsh/.zig-computer.zsh` so zig-computer keeps it
notes:
CLOSED with one criterion installed-but-unproven; that gap is now CLOSED TOO.

tmux ownership PROVEN 2026-07-28 00:29 — Zig ran the cutover himself:

  Name:   tmux: server                 (pid 403325)
  PPid:   83760  ->  /usr/lib/systemd/systemd --user
  cgroup: /user.slice/user-1002.slice/user@1002.service/app.slice/tmux.service

The proof is the SERVER PROCESS's cgroup + parentage, not the unit's
ControlGroup string — a unit always has a cgroup; the question was whether the
daemonized server landed in it, and it did. Direct parent is the user manager.
Old session-140.scope is gone; no session-*.scope remains under user-1002.slice.

Unit: enabled + active, SubState=exited, Result=success (correct for
Type=oneshot + RemainAfterExit). Boot: default.target.wants symlink present,
Linger=yes.

`app.slice` in the path is expected — systemd >= 251 files user services there.
The load-bearing element is `user@1002.service/` before it.

Unplanned benefit: continuum/resurrect are active for the first time (the old
server never loaded them; ~/.tmux/resurrect did not exist). Layout now survives
reboot, not just disconnect.
close_reason: done

title: task: config-mirror contract — the unexercised codex/cursor/gemini vendor tier gets a drift check
description:
## Context

Define the contract: what mirrors (instruction tier), what CANNOT (hooks are claude-runtime-only), what maps (MCP configs per tool); add a drift check to the same seam qvee's symlink-triple assert uses.
## Acceptance Criteria

notes: ## 2026-08-10 (k579 scrutiny finding 1 + live fix): the prune exposed exactly the unexercised-tier risk this bead names. All 7 vendor-arm links (~/.codex/{AGENTS.md,skills}, ~/.cursor/{hooks,skills}, ~/.gemini/{GEMINI.md,hooks,skills}) were DANGLING after the tier moved — 860z only covered ~/.claude. title: model-guard: alias matching accepts within-family downgrades
description:
## Context
post-tool-model-guard.sh same_model() treats a bare alias declaration (fable / opus / sonnet / haiku) as satisfied by any claude-<alias>-* served id, so a seat declared `opus` is happy on claude-opus-5 AND on claude-opus-4-8. That is exactly the observed degradation class: session 2cc9586e was knocked fable-5 -> opus-4-8 AND once fable-5 -> opus-5, and a within-family knock (opus-5 -> opus-4-8) would sail past an alias-declared seat unnoticed. Covered today by case C16, which asserts the permissive behaviour deliberately.

It is a documented tradeoff, not an oversight. An alias is genuinely ambiguous at the client: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_<TIER>_MODEL resolves opus to whatever the vendor points it at (AGENTS.md, the two-seams paragraph), so pinning an alias to one exact id would make the guard fire every time the vendor rolls the alias forward — a false positive on every seat at once, which is the failure mode that gets a guard switched off.

## Task
Decide and implement: keep permissive alias matching, or resolve the alias to an exact id at first observation (cache the first served id per session as the pin, then require exact equality afterwards, so a within-family knock is caught while a vendor roll only costs one session). The second option is cheap and self-calibrating and is the current front-runner, but it needs a case for the vendor-roll scenario before it ships.

## Acceptance Criteria
 - [ ] A decision is recorded (comment or -t decision bead) with the vendor-roll tradeoff stated
 - [ ] If exact-pin is adopted: a within-family knock (opus-5 to opus-4-8) fires the guard
 - [ ] If exact-pin is adopted: a vendor alias roll does not produce a permanent false positive
 - [ ] C16 is updated or replaced to assert whichever behaviour is chosen

title: vault mirror: a git checkout reproduces CONTENT but not identity or time
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Zig, on vps-8a9eb245 after the full-mirror pull:
1. Open `~/linearb/pipeline-website` — no transcript history, though the vault
   demonstrably has it.
2. Look at any mirrored transcript list — everything reads "1 day ago"; all
   recency ordering is gone.

## Context

Two independent defects, one root cause: **a git checkout is not a faithful
mirror.** It reproduces file CONTENT but carries neither the local IDENTITY a
lookup needs nor the TIME the file actually has.

### 1. Identity — 78 projects present but invisible

Claude Code resolves history by a slug derived from `$PWD`, so a box whose unix
user is not the primary's looks for `-home-andrew-foo` while the vault holds
`-home-ubuntu-foo`. `session-start.sh` creates that symlink — but only for the
project a session is STARTING in. That is too late to browse history you have
not opened, and useless for "is my old work here?".

Measured: 91 canonical slugs, 13 aliases. **78 projects fully on disk and
completely unreachable.** The earlier fix made the transform universal but kept
it LAZY; laziness was the remaining half of the bug.

### 2. Time — the whole back catalogue collapsed to one day

git does not record mtimes, so every pulled file is stamped at checkout. The real
time is already IN the file: each session line carries an ISO `timestamp`, and
the last is when the session ended. Strictly better than the git commit date,
which records when the vault happened to sync — on one pipeline-website session
the content ended 2026-07-14 but was committed 2026-07-26, a 12-day error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `agents/vault/restore-mtimes.py` — derives mtime from embedded timestamps.
      Tail-first byte regex (files reach tens of MB; JSONL is append-ordered);
      never parses JSON, so a truncated final line in a live session cannot trip
      it; skips symlinked dirs so aliases cannot double-visit; only `os.utime`.
- [x] Backfill: 7,334 files corrected, largest 183 days. Idempotent (re-run = 0).
- [x] Derivation cross-checked against a full JSON parse — exact match.
- [x] 78 aliases created; pipeline-website resolves to its 2 transcripts.
- [x] Both made durable in `vault-sync.sh` step 1a, peer-guarded, so a slug the
      primary invents is aliased and correctly stamped on the next hourly pull.
- [x] NEGATIVE CONTROLS (not just "ran clean"): deleted 2 aliases -> sync logged
      `aliased 2 new slug(s)` and restored both; forced an mtime to now -> sync
      restored 2026-07-14 23:50:53.

## Notes

`--since 180` bounds the hourly pass to what a pull just touched; a full backfill
stays a manual `restore-mtimes.py` run. 161 files carry no timestamp at all and
are left alone rather than guessed at.
close_reason: done

title: dotfiles runs two durable sessions but has no refs/.handoff-per-window — the notes overwrite each other
description:
## Context
`refs/session-handoff.md` is a single file and `/offboard` overwrites it. `dotfiles` now
demonstrably hosts MORE THAN ONE durable session: this repo is worked from zig-computer
AND from marketing-vps, which is a second writer by design (agents/infra.md).

Nothing is lost — both notes are in git history — but the resume doc is what `/onboard`
actually reads, and it silently presents one session as if it were the whole picture.
The failure mode is not deletion; it is a partial view that looks complete.

## Steps to Reproduce
Observed live 2026-08-04, no synthetic repro needed:

    git log --oneline --all -- refs/session-handoff.md | head -4
      26d08d8  offboard: handoff note (899c6004)          <- marketing-vps session
      4173df7  offboard: note the live second writer
      8f83a4b  offboard: handoff note (188ce668)          <- zig-computer session

    ls refs/.handoff-per-window     -> No such file or directory
    head -1 refs/session-handoff.md -> "# Session handoff — 2026-08-04 899c6004 (marketing-vps)"

Session 188ce668 wrote its note; session 899c6004 wrote its own; the merge took the
latter. The working file now carries only one of the two.

## The documented fix, and why it is not a plain `touch`
`/offboard` already supports this: a project running >1 durable session opts in with
`refs/.handoff-per-window`, and `agents/lib/handoff-path.sh` scopes the note to
`session-handoff--<window>.md`, keyed by the **tmux window name**.

⚠️ Whether WINDOW is the right key here is the open question. `~/explore` uses it for two
windows on ONE machine. dotfiles collides across two MACHINES, and both boxes run a tmux
session called `work` — the same namespace collision `dotfiles-ogkz` had to fix for
agentgateway attribution by adding a machine dimension. Two same-named windows on
different hosts would still clobber each other.

`handoff-path.sh` gained `HANDOFF_WINDOW` and a "stop serving another window's handoff"
fix on 2026-08-04 (`ac0c5f8`, `5981654`) — read those before designing.

## Options
1. opt in as-is, accept window-name collisions across hosts
2. key on `<hostname>--<window>` (mirrors the agentgateway `group`/`user` split)
3. stay single-file and have `/offboard` APPEND a bounded number of prior notes

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] two sessions on DIFFERENT hosts offboard without either note disappearing
- [ ] `/onboard` reads the right one, and can see that others exist
- [ ] a same-named window on two hosts is PROVEN not to collide
- [ ] `agents/lib/test-handoff-path.sh` covers the cross-host case
notes:
## The decision HARVEST collides too, not just the note (2026-08-04)

Observed at the second offboard of session 188ce668. Step 2.5 harvests `-t decision`
beads created since `.claude/last-offboard-session` was stamped. With two sessions
sharing one project, that marker is also shared, so the harvest returns the OTHER
session decisions as if they were this one:

    cut: Mon Aug  4 (marker rewritten by the other session)
    - dotfiles-9o46  kill switch ...        <- marketing-vps session, NOT mine
    - dotfiles-volw  isolation guard ...    <- mine

The marketing-vps handoff hit the mirror image and said so explicitly: its harvest went a
WEEK wide and surfaced eight decisions of which one was its own.

So the fix has to cover BOTH artifacts that key off session identity — the handoff note
AND the last-offboard marker — or the harvest keeps reporting another session work as
this one. That is worse than the note collision: a wrong handoff is visibly one
session view, whereas a contaminated decision list reads as an accurate record of what
this session decided.

Both markers resolve through `agents/lib/handoff-path.sh`, so whichever key is chosen
(window, or `<hostname>--<window>`) should apply to `offboard_pending_path` and
`last_offboard_path` as well as `handoff_path`.

## ABSORBS dotfiles-9w9l (2026-08-05)
`dotfiles-9w9l` (P3, open since 2026-07-28) is the SAME defect, found first:
"handoff-path: window keying cannot distinguish two MACHINES — same-day offboards collide."
I filed this bead without scanning the backlog and rediscovered it. 9w9l is closed pointing
here; this bead keeps the measured evidence (the live 2026-08-04 collision, the contaminated
decision harvest, the three keying options) and 9w9l's P3 is superseded by P2.

9w9l's own worked example is worth keeping, because it shows the workaround people reach for:
a marketing-vps session working on **lb-granola** could not write `refs/session-handoff.md`
without clobbering a NEWER zig-computer note, so it wrote
`refs/session-handoff--marketing-vps.md` beside it by hand and explained why in the header.
That is the correct instinct implemented manually, in a third repo, by one session that
happened to notice. It is evidence the fix belongs in `handoff-path.sh`, not in each
session's judgement.

title: tools/githooks/pre-commit advertises ~90s for the scrutiny-guard harness; it measures ~130s
description:
## Context
Raised by the dotfiles-3137 agent as adjacent. `tools/githooks/pre-commit` tells the
committer the scrutiny-guard mutation harness takes roughly 90 seconds. Measured on
zig-computer during dotfiles-3137: **~130s**, for BOTH the old and the new harness — so
this is not a regression from the hardening, it is drift. The underlying suites grew
(85 + 61 cases).

A wrong duration in a gate message is a small thing that behaves badly: the committer
waits for 90s, concludes the hook has hung at ~100s, and interrupts a gate that was
working. That is the same shape as CLAUDE.md rule 2 — a documented claim that agents and
humans act on.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd ~/dotfiles
    grep -n "90s\|~90" tools/githooks/pre-commit
    time bash agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh
    # measured ~130s (load ~8.7); the advertised figure is ~90s

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the advertised figure matches a fresh measurement, taken on an idle-ish box
- [ ] the message says what it is timing (the harness, not the whole hook) so the next
      drift is attributable
- [ ] the same check applied to the other advertised duration in that file, if any
- [ ] whatever number lands was RUN, not estimated (rule 2)
notes:
## A SECOND stale/absent duration, and the aggregate nobody has looked at (2026-08-05)

The original finding: pre-commit advertises ~90s for the scrutiny-guard harness, measures ~130s.

Added by dotfiles-nnmm: a THIRD mutation gate now runs on pre-commit, for the pulse-inject
seat logic. Measured on a 12-core box and documented honestly in the hook itself:

    test-pulse-inject.sh (full, 113 cases)        107s
    mutate-pulse-seat.sh (5 mutants + baseline)   252s   -> the gate announces "~4.5 min"

Zig 2026-08-05: **~6 min on those three files is acceptable for now.** So this is not a
request to make it faster. It is a request to make the ADVERTISED numbers true, and to
look at the total once.

The aggregate, which no single bead has ever owned:

    ensure-fleet-tunnel      ~63s   (its own trigger paths)
    scrutiny-guards          ~130s  (advertised ~90s  <- the original defect)
    pulse-inject seat        ~252s  (advertised ~4.5 min, close enough)

Each was individually justified when added. Three gates arrived in ~4 days. The risk is not
any one of them — it is that a committer who waits past an advertised figure interrupts a
gate that was working, and that the next addition is argued on its own merits again.

## Acceptance Criteria (superseding the original, which only covered the scrutiny figure)
- [ ] every advertised duration in tools/githooks/pre-commit matches a fresh measurement
- [ ] each message says WHAT it is timing, so the next drift is attributable
- [ ] the file states the worst-case total for a commit touching several trigger sets
- [ ] numbers are RUN, not estimated (CLAUDE.md rule 2)

title: marshal: pin the failure-streak semantics + stop parked beads consuming the wave-1 pick
description:
## Context
Reported by the marshal itself mid-run-5 (2026-08-09, relayed by Zig): 'failure streak stands at 3 rows / 2 distinct beads — one more distinct-bead failure triggers three-strikes,' and wave-1 re-picked the PARKED harnessd-9gvd only to skip it at dispatch. Two defects:

(A) STREAK SEMANTICS UNPINNED. marshal-drain.sh reads the streak off the ledger tail ('consecutive failed rows at the end of tonight', ~line 968), but under kjjf the campaign runs many ledger 'nights' back-to-back, so the tail crosses night boundaries; and the marshal reports the count in two units at once (rows vs distinct beads). Nearly caused a wrong campaign stop earlier tonight (supervisor initially read 2 attempts on one bead as strikes 2 and 3). SUPERVISOR'S RULING to encode (recorded here under kjjf authority; flag in the close if the impl disagrees): the three-strikes counter counts CONSECUTIVE DISTINCT-BEAD failures; multiple failed attempts on one bead = one strike; any merged-AND-closed landing resets it to zero; scope is the ledger tail regardless of night boundaries while a campaign chains runs (a timer night stands alone naturally since the tail ends with it).

(B) PARKED BEADS STILL SELECTED. The planner ranked parked 9gvd as wave-1 and burned the pick on a skip. park-repeat-failure (and any park) must exclude the bead at SELECTION (scheduler feed), not at dispatch — otherwise every subsequent run wastes wave-1 until the human: bead resolves.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Streak computation implements the ruling above with a unit test per clause (multi-attempt-one-bead = 1 strike; close resets; cross-night tail).
- [ ] Ledger/status wording reports ONE unit: 'strikes: N distinct-bead failures (rows: M)'.
- [ ] Parked/blocked-on-human beads are excluded at selection; a skipped-at-dispatch safety check stays as backstop; test proves a parked bead no longer occupies a wave slot.
- [ ] MARSHAL_RECORD_RESULT / three-strikes markers unchanged in shape (consumers exist).

title: CLAUDE.md rule 2: run the example VERBATIM — extract it from the committed file, don't retype it
description:
Standing-practice proposal promoted out of the 2026-08-03 handoff (offboard Step 2.6). Filed rather than edited: rule 1 already took an addition this session, and a second rules change to the same always-loaded file in the same session deserves Zig's eye.

## Context
Rule 2 says: "Before committing an example, run it." That is right and it has a gap —
it does not say run WHAT. Running a retyped or paraphrased version of the example proves
the idea works; it does not prove the bytes in the file work. The two diverge exactly
when a quoting or substitution detail is the thing that breaks, which is the common case
for shell examples in this repo (see rule 7: `$0`/`$N` are rewritten in a rendered
SKILL.md before the agent ever sees them, invisibly to grep and to review).

## The practice worth encoding
Extract the block from the COMMITTED file — by regex or line range — and execute that.
Done twice today and it is meaningfully stronger:
  - dotfiles-xugk: the /commit fix block was pulled out of the committed SKILL.md by awk
    and run under zsh against a throwaway repo. Push rejected -> fallback fired -> merge
    -> push landed -> ls-remote MATCH.
  - dotfiles-3afr: the cited harness path was run rather than eyeballed (28/28).

Neither found a divergence this time. That is not an argument against it — it is what a
guard looks like when it holds.

## Cost
Small. It is a few lines of awk/sed in the verification step, and it replaces a
retyping step that was going to happen anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] rule 2 says to run the example AS COMMITTED, extracted rather than retyped
- [ ] it stays one sentence — rule 2 is already long and this is a refinement, not a
      new rule
- [ ] the worked example cited actually happened
close_reason: Landed in dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 2 (e7865a6) as one sentence appended to its existing imperative: run the example AS COMMITTED, extracting the block from the file by regex or line range (git show HEAD:<path> | awk ...) and executing THOSE BYTES, never a retyped copy — because the detail that breaks an example is usually a quoting or substitution one that retyping silently repairs, which is exactly rule 7's failure mode. The agent practised the technique to prove it: it pulled rule 1's own fenced bash block from the COMMITTED BLOB (git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md, not the worktree copy — the stronger form), cat -A inspected it, and executed it under zsh in a throwaway repo. Orchestrator re-ran that independently: core.hooksPath went (unset) -> tools/githooks, and both cited beads resolve. I considered trimming the closing clause ('neither found a divergence, which is what a guard looks like when it holds, not evidence it is unnecessary') as long for an always-loaded file, and kept it: it answers the first objection a reader raises, and matches the voice of rule 2's existing evidence list.

title: beads: br close on a blocked bead reports 'already closed or not found'
description:
## Context

2026-08-05, romd session. `br close romd-haj --reason "..."` returned:

    Error: Nothing to do: all 1 issue(s) skipped
    Hint: All specified issues were already closed or not found.

`br show romd-haj` immediately after still reported **OPEN**. The real cause was
an open `blocks` dependency (`romd-t0k`), and the fix was `--force`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create bead A and bead B; `br dep add A B -t blocks` so A is blocked by open B.
2. `br close A --reason "..."`
3. Observe: "all 1 issue(s) skipped / already closed or not found" — neither of
   which is true. A is open, exists, and is merely blocked.

## Why it matters more than a wording nit

The message is **success-shaped**. "Already closed" reads as *the thing you wanted
is already true*, so the natural response is to move on. In this incident the
orchestrator nearly did, and only caught it because a later `br show` in an
unrelated check printed OPEN.

That is the `dotfiles-cxle` shape in a tool's own error path: **a step stopped
doing its job while the thing reporting on it said something that reads like
success.** A close that silently does not happen leaves a finished piece of work
open, which is exactly the state the bead lifecycle exists to prevent.

`br close --help` does document `-f, --force  Close even if blocked by open
dependencies`, so the capability is there. Only the diagnosis is wrong.

## Fix

Report the actual reason: `refused: blocked by open dependencies: romd-t0k. Use
--force to close anyway.` Distinguish, in the message, between: already closed /
not found / blocked. They are three different states and only one of them is
success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Closing a blocked bead names the blockers and points at `--force`.
- [ ] "Already closed" is only ever printed for a bead that is actually closed.
- [ ] A negative control: a genuinely-not-found id still says not found.
notes: ## Re-scoped 2026-08-08 (Cluster F): br 0.2.16 is an external binary (~/.local/bin/br), no beads-rust source on this box — unfixable here. br close --help confirms -f/--force ('Close even if blocked by open dependencies') exists; only the diagnosis MESSAGE is wrong. New scope: (a) report upstream; (b) optional thin wrapper intercepting the ambiguous message and re-querying blockers before printing. P3→P4 (upstream-blocked).

title: sketchybar zig-computer click opened a window that closed instantly — the pull dropped the source line for an UNTRACKED alias file
description:
## Context

Clicking the sketchybar `zig-computer` item opened an Alacritty window that closed
immediately without connecting.

Chain, from symptom back to cause — four layers:

1. `sketchybar/hooks/zig-computer.sh:16` sets
   `click_script="$HOOK_DIR/zig-computer.sh open"`.
2. That branch runs `alacritty msg create-window -e zsh -lic zig-computer`.
3. `zig-computer` is a shell **alias**, defined in `bash/.servers.bash_aliases`
   (`alias zig-computer='ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136'`). `zsh/.zshrc:12` sources
   `~/.bash_aliases`, which is what used to pull that file in.
4. The 723-commit fast-forward on 2026-08-01 **replaced** the local `bash/.bash_aliases`
   block `source "$HOME/.servers.bash_aliases"` with origin's `source "$HOME/.secrets"`.
   The alias stopped being defined, `zsh -lic zig-computer` exited non-zero instantly, and
   the window closed with it.

`bash/.servers.bash_aliases` is **UNTRACKED**, which is why upstream had no reason to keep
the line — from upstream's view it sourced a file that does not exist.

## Why it was missed

The migration was **explicitly identified and then not performed.** The pull review flagged
it in writing — "origin sources `~/.secrets`, not `.servers.bash_aliases` — you'd need to
migrate" — recommended taking origin's version, and the migration never happened. Naming a
hazard is not handling it.

This is the second casualty of one root cause in the same pull. The first was
`sketchybar/sketchybarrc` (`dotfiles-22xi`), where an untracked-hooks workaround was read as
pointless drift and dropped. Both were machine-local state that the diff made look
redundant, and both broke silently, two or more layers from the file that changed.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
zsh -lic 'type zig-computer'      # "zig-computer not found"
grep -rn servers.bash_aliases bash/ zsh/   # nothing sources it
ls -la ~/.servers.bash_aliases    # symlink exists, file exists, alias inside
```

Then click the sketchybar item: window opens, closes instantly.

## Fix

Restored the source line in `bash/.bash_aliases`, **guarded** (`[ -f … ]`) so it is a no-op
on any machine without the file — which is precisely why keeping it costs upstream nothing.
Guarded sourcing of machine-local state is the pattern; dropping it because the target is
untracked is the anti-pattern.

Verified end to end, not just resolved:

```
zsh -lic 'type zig-computer'  -> alias for ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136
ssh … 'echo connected'        -> connected: zig-computer
zsh -lic 'zig-computer … '    -> click-path-ok: zig-computer
```

Also confirmed the hook's `ZIG_COMPUTER_SSH_MATCH='ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136'` still matches
the alias target exactly, so the active/inactive icon colour works too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `zig-computer` resolves in a login interactive zsh
- [x] the click path connects, demonstrated end to end
- [x] the source line is guarded so it is portable to boxes without the file
- [ ] **Zig's call:** decide whether the machine-local files orphaned by this pull should be
      tracked — `bash/.servers.bash_aliases` and `sketchybar/hooks/`. Both are currently
      untracked, so both are one fast-forward away from breaking again, and neither exists on
      any other machine. NOTE: `.servers.bash_aliases` contains an SSH target IP and this is
      a PUBLIC repo (cf. `79892d3`), so tracking it is not automatically the right answer.
- [ ] consider a standing check: a guarded `source` whose target is untracked is exactly the
      line a future merge will silently drop again

title: mutate-tap-failover: a NOT-RUN mutant still yields 'all mutants killed' + exit 0 — false-green gate in demesne
description:
## Context
Observed live 2026-08-09 ~21:3xZ on demesne commit b0095ae: M8 (env-bypass-header-strip-disarmed) targets zsh/.zshenv, which does not exist in demesne (zsh/ is outside the demesne-sync set — agents/, refs/, claude/ only), so its mutation could not apply. Per repo rule 1 and the harness's own header discipline, an unapplied mutation is a HARNESS ERROR and must FAIL the run — a NOT-RUN mutant inside a green summary is exactly the dotfiles-8aj5 false-accept class. Same-family fact: the wrapper suite skips T26 in demesne for the same missing file. Transition-state root: demesne cannot fully self-verify the wrapper chain until zsh/ joins the sync set or the cutover flips.

- [ ] A mutant whose mutation does not apply FAILS the harness (nonzero exit, summary names the not-run mutant) — no path from NOT RUN to the all-killed line
- [ ] Explicit-skip is the only sanctioned alternative: a declared, justified per-repo skip list (e.g. M8 demesne-until-zsh-syncs) that prints SKIPPED loudly and is itself asserted (skipping an undeclared mutant fails)
- [ ] Decision recorded: either zsh/ joins demesne-sync so M8+T26 run there, or the skip is declared with the flip as its expiry

title: pulse-stall-reconcile: false 'service-never-ran' verdicts — it compares a fire against the LATEST service start, erasing real earlier fires
description:
## Context
Audit 2026-08-09: the reconciler logged 'skipped-timer-armed-but-service-never-ran' for pulse-digest 8x (17:32-18:42) — FALSE: the journal shows pulse-digest.service ran with PULSE_INJECT_RESULT=injected at 14:00:16 for the 14:00:10 trigger. Cause: it compares fire_ts against service_last_start, which the hardening seat's 15:15:08 post-outage manual re-fire had advanced past the real 14:00 fire — so the reconciler concludes the earlier real fire never happened. Same subsystem also spams: 117 false-skip lines today, 12x/day flags for investd timers, and 33 hall-visit-seneschal not_ready bounces with 'no bounded next_fire' skips — a log nobody can read for signal. q0qi family: a marker (latest start time) consulted instead of the per-trigger reality.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Let a timer fire normally (journal shows service start + injected).
2. Manually start the same service later (systemctl --user start).
3. Watch the reconciler flag the ORIGINAL trigger as service-never-ran on every subsequent cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-trigger matching: a fire_ts is satisfied by ANY service start >= fire_ts (journal InvocationID or a window match), not by comparing against only the latest start.
- [ ] The false-skip class is silenced: known-not-stall states log at most once per trigger, not per cycle.

title: vps-repo-refresh: read-only tripwire misreads a submodule gitlink pin drift as a remote write
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 verifying dotfiles-wv2a, immediately behind dotfiles-0bf2. With
the `oob-exclude` line filtered out of the manifest, the refresh gets further and
then refuses for a second reason:

    REFRESH-FAIL: /home/andrew/linearb has modified TRACKED files the VPS should
    never write:
        pipeline-website

`pipeline-website` is a GITLINK (mode 160000), and the drift is the submodule
checkout being ahead of the umbrella's pin:

    -Subproject commit 2059ca7aa30c0e2c13ebc3dac3a51e2bbd76751e
    +Subproject commit cc73a7dbcf78d8138fbee570034b6e7dae580f51

That is not a write by the VPS. It is ordinary pin drift, and vps-preflight.sh
ALREADY knows this — check_local() passes `--ignore-submodules=all` with a comment
explaining that a gitlink reads as modified whenever the submodule checkout is
ahead of the pin, "which is the NORMAL local state here", and that ignoring it is
non-lossy because those submodules get their own identity check.

vps-repo-refresh.sh's tripwire does not pass that flag, so the two scripts
disagree about what "dirty" means and the stricter one blocks every dispatch with
a message that accuses the box of something it did not do. The message also sends
the reader toward the `.beads/` remedy, which is the wrong diagnosis here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On marketing-vps: `cd ~/linearb && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`
   -> ` M pipeline-website` (a gitlink, per `git diff --submodule=short`).
2. `~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh --manifest <manifest without
   the oob-exclude line> --self-update`
3. Observed: REFRESH-FAIL on modified tracked files; no receipt; every dispatch
   then blocks at A1/A2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The refresh tripwire ignores gitlink-only drift the same way
      vps-preflight.sh does (`--ignore-submodules=all`), so the two scripts agree
      on what dirty means.
- [ ] A real remote write to a tracked file STILL trips it — prove both directions
      in a test; a tripwire that stops firing is worse than one that over-fires.
- [ ] The failure message stops implying `.beads/` when the finding is a gitlink.
close_reason: done

title: test suites: per-case bare mktemp -d leaks /tmp dirs beyond test-pulse-escalate — sweep the whole demesne suite corpus
description:
## Context
Found while patching agents/scheduler/test-api-stall-recover.sh under dotfiles-d5n3. That suite had
the EXACT dotfiles-d5ez shape: a top-level ROOT=\$(mktemp -d) with a reaping trap, and then a
per-case setup_case() calling a SECOND bare `mktemp -d` that nothing ever removes — ~35 leaked
/tmp-root dirs per suite run, multiplied by 17 mutants every time the mutation harness runs. Fixed
in place there (mktemp -d "\$ROOT/case.XXXXXX").

d5ez fixes test-pulse-escalate.sh; zov8 attributes the named-template families found as /tmp
evidence. Neither covers the systematic class: a suite whose PER-CASE temp dir escapes its own
trap. That class is mechanically checkable and is spread across the corpus.

## Steps to Reproduce
Count /tmp-root entries before and after a suite run. Starting heuristic (files where the mktemp -d
count exceeds the reaping-trap count, run in demesne):

  for f in $(grep -rln 'mktemp -d' agents --include='*.sh'); do
    n=$(grep -c 'mktemp -d' "$f"); t=$(grep -c 'trap .*rm -rf' "$f")
    [ "$t" -eq 0 ] || [ "$n" -gt "$t" ] && printf '%s mktemp=%s traps=%s\n' "$f" "$n" "$t"
  done

That heuristic is a STARTING POINT, not a verdict — a single trap on \$ROOT legitimately covers many
mktemp calls that allocate underneath it. The loudest candidates by raw count are
agents/scheduler/test-pulse-inject.sh (28 mktemp / 4 traps), agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh
(13/1) and agents/hooks/test/test-session-start-window.sh (11/1). Confirm each by counting real
droppings, not by the ratio.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every suite under agents/ verified by MEASUREMENT (count /tmp-root entries before/after one
run), not by the grep heuristic
- [ ] Each confirmed leaker allocates its per-case dir under the trap-reaped parent
- [ ] A mechanical guard that catches a future bare per-case mktemp -d (a pre-commit arm, or a
wrapper that fails a suite leaving new /tmp-root entries) — the same guard d5ez asks for, applied
corpus-wide rather than to one file

title: bug: pulse-dispatch-remote A6 silently skips the bead-identity check when local 'br' is off PATH
description:
## Context

Found landing the first remote di-tuesday tick (run 20260728T140030Z-di-tuesday,
2026-07-28). `beads-local.err` in the dispatch state dir contained:

    /home/ubuntu/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh: line 795: br: command not found

Line 795 is the LOCAL half of preflight A6:

    LOCAL_BEAD_JSON=$( cd "$DIR" && br sync --status --json 2>>"$LOCAL_STATE/beads-local.err" )

The dispatch script runs from a shell where `br` is not on PATH, so
`LOCAL_BEAD_JSON` comes back empty and `LOCAL_BEAD_SHA` is empty. The comparison
is then guarded:

    if [ -n "$LOCAL_BEAD_SHA" ] && [ "$LOCAL_BEAD_SHA" != "$REMOTE_BEAD_SHA" ]; then

so the empty local SHA SKIPS the check entirely, and the script still prints

    preflight A6: OK (bead JSONL identical <remote-sha>, index imported)

That line is false: nothing was compared. A6's whole purpose is proving the bead
JSONL is the same file on both machines, and it reports OK while proving only
that the remote could read its own state. This is the silent-degradation shape
the harness guards against. The empty-REMOTE_BEAD_SHA and remote-newer branches
both `fail` loudly, so the local branch is the lone soft spot.

This did NOT harm the 2026-07-28 run (the tick ran end to end, its proof
re-verified locally, ledger + bd-1499 landed), but the assertion it relied on was
never actually made.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` for any row from a shell whose PATH lacks `br` (the scheduled/non-interactive case).
2. Watch the preflight output: A6 reports `OK (bead JSONL identical ...)`.
3. Read `$LOCAL_STATE/beads-local.err` — it holds `br: command not found` for the line-795 local status call.
4. Confirm no two-sided comparison happened: `LOCAL_BEAD_SHA` was empty, so the `[ -n "$LOCAL_BEAD_SHA" ]` guard short-circuited the mismatch branch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `br` resolves in the dispatch script's shell (absolute path, or PATH set explicitly alongside the other tool resolutions)
- [ ] An empty/unreadable LOCAL_BEAD_SHA `fail`s A6 loudly instead of skipping, symmetric with the existing empty-REMOTE_BEAD_SHA branch
- [ ] The "preflight A6: OK (bead JSONL identical ...)" line prints only when a real two-sided comparison happened
- [ ] Re-run a dispatch and confirm `beads-local.err` is empty and A6 reports a genuine match

title: tap-headroom gateway arm: 7d filter hole — a half-populated row can roll INTO a pool at its 7d ceiling

title: zig-zone Phase 4: SS14 game server + watchdog → pico (with feasibility test)
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] SS14 game server runs natively on pico ARM64 (no qemu)
 - [x] SS14.Watchdog runs natively on pico ARM64
 - [x] Client connects through nginx UDP+TCP stream proxy on zig-computer
 - [x] tcpdump verified: client never sees pico's tailnet IP
 - [x] Gameplay works (player tested, admin commands work, postgres writes work)
 - [x] ss14-watchdog systemd unit disabled on zig-computer
 - [x] ss14-replay-rotate timer moved to pico (8th of 8)
 - [x] zig-computer nginx simplified to single proxy / → pico:8080
 - [x] /instances/, /watchdog/, /client.zip routes added to pico nginx
notes:
REVISED CONCLUSION 2026-05-24: SS14 ARM64 build technically works (validated end-to-end with a real player connection), but the deployment model is fundamentally incompatible with reverse-proxied UDP. Per the canonical SS14 architecture (dotfiles-ier research), the game server must live with a public IP that the launcher dials UDP directly. nginx stream{} proxying inverts what Lidgren expects of UDP source addresses. Two intrinsic bugs surfaced: (A) player counter pinned at 0/30 because every client appears as zig-computer's tailnet IP; (B) Lidgren disconnects from Late MsgEntity messages because nginx demuxes UDP into the wrong upstream socket.

ROLLBACK SHIPPED: SS14 game server + watchdog + ss14-replay-rotate timer restored to zig-computer. ARM64 build artifacts preserved on pico (/Users/pico/ss14-watchdog/) in case a future rearchitecture (home-router DNAT for direct UDP, TPROXY, or VPN-based source-preservation) makes SS14-on-pico viable.

Net Phase 4 outcome: SS14 + ss14-watchdog + ss14-replay-rotate STAY on zig-computer permanently. This is a single intentional exception to 'all hostable moves to pico' — justified because zig-computer naturally owns the public IPv4 and SS14's game-server architecture requires that co-location. M1 Max's compute advantages don't help SS14 (latency-bound, not GPU-bound); they DO help the 99% of compute (postgres, LLM, web, builds, obs) which IS on pico.

Spec's Phase 4 wording was sound — the feasibility test result was 'fail'; the spec correctly said 'abort SS14 migration. SS14 stays on zig-computer.'

title: decision: the lb-granola copy on marketing-vps stays (oob-exclude governs future pushes only)
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 while fixing dotfiles-0bf2: `~/linearb/lb-granola` exists on
marketing-vps — 31M, 162 transcripts / 162 payloads / 105 summaries, current to
2026-07-28 21:04, including 1:1 transcripts. The manifest's `oob-exclude`
directive (added 2026-07-28, dotfiles-f5tg) declares that path must never reach
that shared box, and its own comment says the push "was never a DECISION — it
happened because the corpus is untracked by the umbrella."

Measured facts put to Zig, not assumed:
  * NOT world-readable. Dir `drwxr-x--- andrew:andrew`, files `-rw-r-----`, and
    group `andrew` has NO other members.
  * BUT kevin, mike and ben are all in `sudo` on that box, i.e. root-equivalent
    and able to read it at will.
  * zig-computer's copy is identical (162/162/105, same newest files), so the
    box copy is pure redundancy — deleting it would have lost nothing.

## Decision

**Leave it in place.** Zig's call, 2026-07-29, via AskUserQuestion, presented
with the sudo-access caveat above and with deletion offered as the recommended
option.

## Why

Read as: sudo-level access by those three colleagues is acceptable for this
content. They are LinearB teammates, and the box is a LinearB machine.

## Consequences

- No deletion, now or by a future tick. **A later session must not "clean this
  up" as drift** — that is what this bead exists to prevent.
- `oob-exclude` STAYS in the manifest and keeps its meaning, but its practical
  scope is now future pushes only: once dotfiles-0bf2 lands, the dispatcher
  honors it (excludes the path from the out-of-band push) and the refresh stops
  dying on it. Nothing deletes what is already there.
- Therefore the box copy will go STALE from 2026-07-28 onward rather than
  tracking zig-computer. That is a consequence, not a defect — if a tick ever
  needs fresh granola data on the box, this decision has to be revisited
  explicitly.
- The option Zig declined also proposed removing `oob-exclude` from the manifest
  outright. NOT done: the directive still expresses a real intent about future
  pushes, and silently deleting a security declaration is the wrong default. If
  he wants it gone, that is a separate, explicit change.

## Reversibility

Total, in both directions and cheaply. Deleting later is `rm -rf` on a redundant
copy. Re-populating is a single rsync. Nothing here is one-way.

title: pulse-retry: 'no bounded next_fire' skip spam — a bounce source with no timer unit
description:
## Context
Split out of dotfiles-gxqc (the pulse-stall-reconcile false-skip fix). That bead asked
whether the 'no bounded next_fire' skip spam shared a root cause with the reconciler's
false verdicts. It does NOT — different script, different condition:

- gxqc (FIXED): pulse-stall-reconcile.py compared a fire_ts against the LATEST service
  start (ExecMainStartTimestamp), so a later manual start erased an earlier real fire.
  Fixed by per-trigger journal enumeration + a once-per-(timer,fire) log dedup. The
  investd 12x/day flags WERE the same root cause and are cured by that dedup.
- this bead: agents/scheduler/pulse-retry.sh (~line 412) logs
  "skip <loop>: no bounded next_fire (raw='') — unbounded, not retrying" for every
  actionable bounce of a loop that has no bounded realtime schedule.

Measured 2026-08-09: `hall-visit-seneschal` has 33 rows in
~/.local/state/harness/pulse-bounces.jsonl (reason=not_ready), and
`systemctl --user show hall-visit-seneschal.timer -p LoadState` returns
LoadState=not-found — there is NO timer unit at all. So pulse-retry reads an empty
NextElapseUSecRealtime, correctly declines to retry, and says so on every cycle.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Append a bounce row for a loop with no systemd timer unit to
   ~/.local/state/harness/pulse-bounces.jsonl (hall-visit-seneschal is the live case).
2. Run agents/scheduler/pulse-retry.sh.
3. Observe "skip <loop>: no bounded next_fire (raw='')" — and observe it again on the
   next cycle, and every cycle after, with nothing having changed.

## Task
Decide which end is wrong and fix that end, not the log line:
(a) hall-visit-seneschal should not write to pulse-bounces.jsonl if it is not a
    timer-backed pulse loop (that log is pulse-retry's input queue), or
(b) it should have a timer unit, or
(c) pulse-retry should recognise a non-timer-backed bounce source and say so once,
    with the same once-per-state dedup gxqc added to pulse-stall-reconcile.py
    (see log_once / STATE_PATH there for a working, inspectable pattern to copy).

Note the shared SHAPE even though the root cause differs: a steady state re-announced
every cycle. Whatever the fix, the line should not repeat while nothing changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Establish whether hall-visit-seneschal is meant to be a pulse loop with a timer.
- [ ] The 'no bounded next_fire' line stops repeating for an unchanged state.
- [ ] A regression case in agents/scheduler/test-pulse-retry.sh that fails before it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SCOPE ADDITION (Zig, live, 2026-08-09): the interactive court REFRESHES while open — 'immensely better for watching'. Design: the prompt loop becomes a watch loop — render frame, read with timeout (~2s), timeout -> re-render (build the frame off-screen, ANSI home + single write, no flicker; clear-to-end for shrinking rows), keystroke -> existing behavior (seat name visits, Esc/empty closes). Render pauses while a partial seat name is being typed (a redraw mid-typing eats input — buffer the typed prefix and reprint it after each frame, or simply suspend refresh once the first char arrives; builder picks, argues in a comment). Test: frame-stability at a forced width across two renders with a window state change between them.

title: fix: zig-watchdog HermesGateway probe surfaces stale blocked-task crash diagnostics as CRASH + service Documentation= invalid URL
description:
## Problem

Two cosmetic-but-real issues with the freshly-shipped zig-watchdog.

### Bug 1 — sticky HermesGateway=CRASH false positive

The HermesGateway probe matches `repeated_crashes` diagnostics from
`hermes kanban diagnostics` to detect crash-loops. Once a task is already
blocked (manually OR by the watchdog's own revive), the diagnostic counter
stays attached to the task forever — the gateway never clears it on block.
Result: every watchdog tick reports HermesGateway=CRASH and the dashboard
shows a red banner — even though the gateway is healthy.

This is the M2 minor finding from the /scrutinize pass on dotfiles-olh.

### Bug 2 — invalid Documentation= URL

`zig-watchdog.service` line 3 had `Documentation=https://... (bead dotfiles-olh)`.
systemd parses Documentation= as space-separated URLs; the parenthetical
fails URL validation, producing two journal warnings per service start.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Bug 1
1. Have any task with `repeated_crashes` diagnostic AND status=blocked
   (today: t_360fa078 with 97x consecutive_crashes, blocked)
2. Confirm gateway is healthy: `systemctl --user is-active hermes-gateway` → active
3. Run `python3 ~/dotfiles/local-models/zig-watchdog.py`
4. Read `~/.cache/zig-watchdog/state.json` → HermesGateway.last_probe is CRASH
5. Expected: OK (gateway healthy, blocked task is not actionable)

### Bug 2
1. Install zig-watchdog timer: `bash ~/dotfiles/local-models/install-zig-watchdog.sh`
2. `journalctl --user -u zig-watchdog.service --since '2 minutes ago' | grep "Invalid URL"`
3. Two "Invalid URL, ignoring:" lines per service start

## Fix

### Bug 1
In `local-models/zig-watchdog.py` `HermesGatewayJob.probe()`: return CRASH only
when `_actionable_crash_loop_task_ids` (already populated, filters out blocked
tasks) is non-empty. Stale blocked-task diagnostics → OK.

### Bug 2
In `local-models/zig-watchdog.service` Documentation= field: drop the
parenthetical; keep just the URL. Bead reference belongs in commit history,
not in a systemd field that requires URL syntax.

## Source of Report

User noticed dashboard showing "Hermes gateway is in a crashing loop" —
investigation showed gateway healthy but watchdog probe surfacing stale
diagnostic. Plus this session's earlier scrutinize M2 callout flagged it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Bug 1: HermesGatewayJob.probe() returns OK when only blocked-task crash diagnostics exist
- [ ] Bug 1: Regression test: probe with only-blocked-task crashes → OK
- [ ] Bug 1: Regression test: probe with actionable (non-blocked) task crashes → still CRASH
- [ ] Bug 2: systemd journal shows zero "Invalid URL" warnings after service restart
- [ ] All existing zig-watchdog tests still pass
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-hpi in commit trailer

title: spec: the outward-facing gate — what an agent may do to the outside world, and under whose approval
description:
## Context
The safety half, designed BEFORE any endeavor moves: outward actions (send email, publish a site, accept payment, create accounts, post under a name) are a different risk class from anything the harness does today. Generalize harnessd LOCKED #3 machine-wide: server-side allowlists, per-action approval vs narrowly-scoped standing grants (each grant names its scope + expiry), identity rules (what name signs what — Zig's byline rules already exist), and an audit trail (never falsify the record). P1 because it gates the epic and touches trust structure.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Formal spec + test cases; every outward capability enumerated with its gate class
- [ ] Nothing in the epic ships an outward action before this ratifies

## Write target
none (spec authoring). The deliverable is a ratified spec bead, not code; the eventual implementation spans repos and is gated on the spec. Route to a /spec session, not a worktree builder.
design:
# THE OUTWARD GATE — Formal Spec v1 (Fable-authored 2026-08-09)

Article III made mechanical: "Zig is the sole gate for outward acts." This spec defines OUTWARD,
the gate classes, and the machinery — BEFORE any endeavor moves. Design principle throughout: the
gate is server-side and structural where possible (a prompt is not a wall — the cleanroom lesson,
generalized); prose rules exist only where no seam exists to enforce them.

## R1 — WHAT IS OUTWARD (the classification, exhaustive by CLASS not by tool)
An action is OUTWARD iff its effect lands where Zig's estate does not control deletion:
 O1 SPEECH: posting/publishing under ANY name (sites, socials, comments, PR descriptions on
    public repos, package registries, AO3, forums); email/DM to a human.
 O2 IDENTITY: creating/modifying accounts, keys with external authority, OAuth grants, DNS.
 O3 MONEY: accepting/sending payment, subscriptions, listings, anything with a price.
 O4 COMMITMENT: anything that binds Zig or a house (applications, registrations, contracts, ToS
    acceptance beyond read-only browsing).
NOT outward: pushes to Zig-owned repos (public ones ARE outward-visible but are covered by the
existing commit discipline + the depublish rules — carve-out C1, revisit at rung 3); read-only
fetches; tailnet-internal anything; LLM API calls through the gateway.

## R2 — GATE CLASSES
 G0 FORBIDDEN: no grant exists (v1: O3 money, O4 commitment — nothing in the estate may do these).
 G1 PER-ACT APPROVAL: each act needs a fresh, specific Zig approval naming the artifact (the exact
    text/recipient/target), delivered via AskUserQuestion (interactive) or an approval bead Zig
    closes (async). Approval of X is never approval of X'.
 G2 STANDING GRANT, NARROW: a durable grant naming scope + expiry + identity, recorded as a
    decision bead (e.g. "autonoveld may publish chapters to AO3 account <house> until revoked").
    A grant that would not fit in three lines is too broad to be a grant.
 G3 INTERNAL: not outward; existing discipline governs.
Every outward capability that exists today gets enumerated and classed in the ratification pass
(known set: AO3 publishing (G2 candidate — the one live standing grant in spirit), webmentions
(gojamming receives, never sends — G3), gh PR/issue text on public repos (C1 carve-out), push
notifications to Zig (G3, inward). Everything else is G1-until-classed.)

## R3 — IDENTITY RULES (Art. III verbatim, mechanized)
Ventures ship under HOUSE names; Zig's byline is reserved for what he personally makes. Every G1/G2
act names, in its grant or approval, WHICH identity signs. An act under an unnamed identity is
refused. The roster is the identity registry's natural home (seat -> house affiliation, charter).

## R4 — THE MACHINERY (structural, per seam)
 (a) Egress chokepoints: outward-capable credentials live ONLY in named stores (~/.secrets entries
     tagged #outward; harnessd's action endpoints; the AO3 session). No outward credential in an
     agent-reachable default env. The scrub-secrets sweep learns the #outward tag.
 (b) Hook layer: a PreToolUse guard pattern-matches the known outward verbs (gh pr create on
     non-Zig repos, curl POST to non-tailnet hosts with credentialed headers, mail/sendmail, the
     harnessd /act/* endpoints that reach the world) -> exit 2 naming this spec, unless the command
     env carries a grant token (OUTWARD_GRANT=<decision-bead-id>) the guard can check exists+open.
     Fail CLOSED on scan errors (the inverse of the worktree guard's choice — blocking an outward
     act is always safe; justify in the header).
 (c) Server-side where it exists: harnessd action endpoints check the grant registry themselves
     (generalizing LOCKED #3) — the PWA and the hook agree on one registry, never two copies.
 (d) AUDIT: every G1/G2 act appends {ts, actor seat, identity, grant, artifact-hash/pointer} to an
     append-only ledger (~/.local/share/fleet-health/outward.jsonl). The record is never falsified;
     dream reads it; the seneschal brief lists outward acts in a section Zig sees EVERY morning.

## R5 — INTERACTION WITH THE DRAIN + PULSES
Fleet-drain: outward-marked beads are skipped unconditionally (69qr R1e cites this spec). Pulse
ticks: an autonomous loop that reaches an outward decision files the approval bead + push and ENDS
the tick — the existing no-AskUserQuestion-from-timers doctrine, now with a named artifact type.

## TEST CASES
T1 unclassed outward verb hits the hook guard -> blocked naming this spec. T2 a valid grant token in
env -> allowed + audit row written. T3 grant token naming a CLOSED decision bead -> refused (expiry
works). T4 G1 approval of artifact X does not admit modified X' (hash mismatch -> refuse). T5 an act
under no named identity -> refused whatever the grant. T6 audit ledger row appears for every allowed
act (mutant: audit-write-removed must die). T7 fleet-drain skips an outward-marked bead. T8 harnessd
/act endpoint refuses without registry grant even when called directly (server-side half). T9 the
scan-error path fails CLOSED with announcement. T10 G0 classes refuse even WITH a grant token (money
has no grant grammar in v1).

## OQs for /check with Zig
OQ1 ratify the class assignments above (esp. C1 public-repo carve-out and AO3 as the first G2).
OQ2 grant expiry default (none/90d?). OQ3 does the outward ledger live keep-side only, or mirror
into demesne for the record. OQ4 who may FILE approval beads (any seat?) vs who approves (Zig only —
constitutional, not open).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: OQ RESOLUTIONS (Zig, 2026-08-10, AskUserQuestion via seneschal — pm33's htqt half): OQ1 RATIFIED AS SPECCED — all class assignments stand: C1 public-repo carve-out (commit discipline governs, revisit at rung 3), AO3 publishing = first G2, O3 money + O4 commitment = G0 with no grant grammar in v1, webmentions receive-only + push-to-Zig = G3, everything unclassed defaults G1-until-classed. OQ2: G2 grants get a 90-DAY DEFAULT EXPIRY — silent lapse unless renewed; renewal is a cheap re-file of the decision bead. OQ3: the outward ledger MIRRORS INTO DEMESNE via the existing backup pull — the record must survive any single box; dream + seneschal read the mirrored copy. OQ4: approval-request beads are filed by ORCHESTRATOR SEATS ONLY — a subagent/builder that hits an outward need routes the request through its orchestrator (one relay hop, higher request quality); approval itself remains Zig alone, constitutional, unchanged. Spec is /check-clear: all 4 OQs resolved; build may proceed against R1-R5 as written plus these four riders.

title: fix: effort doctrine — move xhigh from session default to per-dispatch escalation (Opus 5 breaks xhigh+thinking-off)
description:
## Context

Opus 5 REJECTS `output_config.effort='xhigh'` when thinking is disabled:

    400 output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is
    disabled on this model. Use effort 'high' or below, or enable thinking.

Claude Code disables thinking on the WebSearch path, so **WebSearch is dead at xhigh on Opus 5**.

## Evidence

agentgateway request log (pico, `~/.local/share/agentgateway/requests.db`):
- `claude-opus-4-8` — 20,578 requests over 10 days, **0** errors
- `claude-opus-5` — first request 2026-07-25T01:28:36Z, **24x HTTP 400, all today**

Controlled A/B, same host + same proxy, 4 minutes apart:
- effort `xhigh` -> 400
- effort `high`  -> real search results; all subsequent requests 200

The 400s begin at the exact minute Opus 5 became the default model (the overnight
`ubuntu.upgrade.sh` run upgraded Claude Code to 2.1.220, whose 2.1.219 made Opus 5
default). This is NOT an apt/package problem.

## Already fixed

`~/.claude/settings.json` `effortLevel`: `xhigh` -> `high` (Zig's call, 2026-07-25).

## What THIS bead fixes

The always-loaded doctrine still pins `xhigh` and will push the setting straight
back, re-breaking search. Zig chose **"session=high, escalate per-step"**
(AskUserQuestion, 2026-07-25).

Note the Opus 5 prompting guide: *"for most tasks, thinking enabled at low effort
performs better than thinking disabled at similar cost."* So the cheap fix is
ALWAYS lower-effort-with-thinking-on, NEVER thinking-off.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `agents/AGENTS.md` effort section: `high` is the DEFAULT (vendor default on Opus 5; identical to omitting the param); `xhigh` is NOT a session setting but a per-dispatch escalation via Workflow `agent(..., {effort:'xhigh'})`; `max` reserved for /elevate + frontier synthesis; `low`/`medium` for mechanical drains
- [ ] `agents/AGENTS.md`: the "proactively ask Zig to bump to xhigh" instruction REMOVED
- [ ] `agents/AGENTS.md`: short explicit note that xhigh + thinking-disabled = 400 on Opus 5, and that the failure is SILENT in a scheduled tick
- [ ] `agents/AGENTS.md`: "ultracode = xhigh + standing permission" decoupled — autonomy must not force an effort level
- [ ] `agents/skills/explore/SKILL.md`: the "Run the research at xhigh" pin REMOVED (this is the skill whose job is searching)
- [ ] `agents/skills/onboard/SKILL.md`: the "recommend bump to xhigh|max" prompt updated to the new ladder
- [ ] `agents/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md`: "Default reasoning: xhigh for research" updated
- [ ] No remaining instruction anywhere in `agents/` telling a session to SET itself to xhigh
- [ ] Committed and pushed on the dotfiles repo
notes:
## DONE — 2026-07-25 (commit 5576ce7, pushed)

Rewrote the effort section of agents/AGENTS.md as "Effort — a per-dispatch choice,
not a session setting". high is the DEFAULT and the only level a SESSION is set to;
xhigh/max are per-dispatch Workflow escalations. Removed the "proactively ask Zig to
bump" instruction. Added the verbatim 400 text + the A/B evidence, and a standalone
paragraph on the silent-in-a-scheduled-loop failure. Decoupled ultracode to an
autonomy grant only.

Skills updated: explore (xhigh pin REMOVED, plus an explicit prohibition on
escalating the search/fetch fan-out — the max ideation pass survives because it
reasons over an already-gathered corpus and does not search), onboard (anything
ABOVE high is now the anomaly to flag), dispatch (per-level table defaulting to
high). elevate cross-references repointed.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by the orchestrator: commit pushed and in sync with
origin/main; every surviving `xhigh` mention in agents/ is either the escalation
mechanism or the 400 warning; no instruction anywhere tells a session to set itself
to xhigh.

## Two things the acceptance criteria MISSED (both caught by the agent)

1. dotfiles/claude/settings.json — the TRACKED template — still pinned
   effortLevel: xhigh. ~/.claude/settings.json is a REAL FILE, not a symlink to it,
   so the hand-fix never propagated. That template is the bootstrap/restore path:
   on a fresh machine or a dotfiles restore it would have silently reinstalled the
   broken config with no signal. Fixed in the same commit; orchestrator confirmed
   both files now read high and both are valid JSON.

2. `max` returns the SAME 400 as `xhigh`. So the rule is "never escalate a step that
   searches", not an xhigh-specific quirk. Both explore and dispatch now say
   xhigh/max.

## Noted for later, not acted on

Anthropic's Opus 5 guidance says effort is NOT a reliable verbosity lever on this
model. The "low/medium are unusually strong" half was folded into the ladder
("cheap is not dumb"); the verbosity half is a separate prompt-tuning matter.

title: directive tracking: a Zig-directed mandate gets a bead at acceptance, closed with evidence at completion — a cleared window can never hide the outcome
description:
## Context
Zig's gap report 2026-08-09: the dotfiles-2 session finished his marshal-prep directive completely (all 106 drainable-type beads assessed, 42 marks, lanes wired — proven) but he could not tell: the session molted, its window was cleared, and its completion note was overwritten in the shared handoff slot by the NEXT session's offboard within the hour (three writers cycled refs/session-handoff.md in one afternoon: 482030c4 -> a491e4bf -> fb9f7a18; the completion was recoverable only from git history, commit 31dc6ec). Completion of directed work reported peer-to-peer but never TO ZIG. The slot-overwrite half is owned by dotfiles-ie5a (demesne handoff layout — today's triple-cycle is fresh evidence, cross-reference it). THIS bead owns the visibility half: directed-mandate lifecycle.

## The shape
When a session accepts a directive from Zig that spans more than one bead of work (a mandate — 'groom all harnessd beads', 'push the drain through', 'depublish the estate'), it opens a `-t task` bead labeled `directive` at acceptance, carrying the mandate verbatim + the accepting session/window. Progress comments land on it at wave boundaries. At completion it closes WITH EVIDENCE (the numbers, the residue, where leftovers went). The seneschal brief already renders recent closes — a `directive`-labeled close is exactly what its 'shipped last 24h' section exists to carry, and an OPEN directive bead is standing brief material ('in flight for Zig'). A session that molts/clears mid-mandate leaves the bead open with a progress comment — the next context (or Zig) reads mandate state from the bead, never from a window that may be gone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The convention documented where sessions will meet it: AGENTS.md gets a short 'Directed mandates' paragraph (bead at acceptance, evidence at close, comment at molt boundaries); /onboard's classify step and /offboard's harvest step each get one line pointing at it.
- [ ] Seneschal brief: verify directive-labeled beads render distinctly (open = 'mandates in flight', closed-today = 'completed for you') — implement the small gather change if not.
- [ ] Retroactive seed: file the completed marshal-prep mandate as a closed exemplar bead citing 31dc6ec's evidence, so the convention has a worked example.
- [ ] Cross-references recorded on ie5a (slot half) and 32mf (spawned seats inherit the convention — a seneschal-spawned seat's directive bead is opened by the spawn procedure).

title: drain integration: consume the garden READY set — trio repos (dotfiles+harnessd+demesne), fleet-first, serialize on WRITE TARGET not home store
description:
## Context
Follow-up wave of the GARDEN spec (dotfiles-vpha; Zig's rulings recorded in its 2026-08-14 comment). Tonight's marshal-garden.sh is standalone; this bead wires the drain to it, under the OQ4 ruling: dispatch repos are the TRIO dotfiles + harnessd + demesne ('demesne's beads store is in dotfiles, so it's a natural trio' — Zig).

## The load-bearing amendment (from the vpha ruling comment — binding)
Serialize on the WRITE TARGET, not the bead's home store. A dotfiles-store bead whose work lands in demesne is the dotfiles-xype shape: the isolation hook cannot see a foreign-checkout write and passes the dispatch; two agents targeting demesne race silently. A per-bead-store lock would wave through exactly that. The garden computes per-bead write_target; the drain LOCKS on it: one live builder per write-target repo at a time (home_repo may keep its swarm semantics). A dispatch candidate with indeterminate write_target is NEEDS-ZIG, never guessed.

## Changes
- marshal.conf repos= gains demesne (name:path; note demesne has NO .beads — selection still reads the dotfiles store; the entry expresses WRITE-TARGET opt-in, and the conf comment must say so)
- marshal-drain.sh selection consumes garden.report.v1's dispatch_candidates (fleet-marked, READY, not stale-avoid, determinate write_target), fleet-first ordering preserved
- Per-write-target serialization lock replaces/extends the per-foreign-repo lock (R2)
- Report/ledger rows name the write target per dispatch

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two candidates with write_target=demesne are provably serialized (test: second waits/defers while first live)
- [ ] A dotfiles-store bead with write_target=demesne dispatches with the demesne-targeted worktree recovery block in its prompt
- [ ] Indeterminate-target candidate never dispatches; appears NEEDS-ZIG
- [ ] test-marshal-drain.sh extended + a mutant that removes the write-target lock and DIES on the serialization test
- [ ] Lands before the Saturday maiden gardened night; consul guard fixes (9qyk/rlpm/2t8o) verified merged first

title: conduit: OQ-11 full health telemetry — fail-open rate + spawn-failure count + /seneschal queue depth
description:

and SPAWN-FAILURE COUNT — plus a /seneschal status line reporting queue depth and

   name it in the conduit section of pulse-escalate.sh's header.
2. Count both in the watcher and add them to the result line.

4. Suite cases + mutants for each new counter (a counter that silently stops
   counting reads exactly like a healthy conduit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both appear on PULSE_ESCALATE_RESULT and in /seneschal status

title: doctrine: two writers share the git INDEX — concurrent staging rides strangers' commits; extend the two-writers rule + an atomic stage-and-commit idiom
description:
## Context
Measured 2026-08-09 ~19:55Z: the Works seat staged .beads/issues.jsonl (+ a pending refs/session-handoff.md rewrite was staged in the shared tree); the hardening seat's concurrent background `git add <2 files> && git commit` swept BOTH staged files into its own commit (efec807) under its message and its Bead: dotfiles-t5fj trailer. Content intact and pushed — but attribution is wrong, the trailer lies about what the commit contains, and the first writer's subsequent commit found 'nothing to commit' (a confusing silent success). AGENTS.md's 'Two writers, one working tree' rule covers pull/merge/stash hazards; it does not cover the INDEX, which is equally shared. A staging race is silent in both directions: the sweeper doesn't know it took extra files; the swept doesn't know its stage emptied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Evaluate a mechanical arm and implement if cheap: a prepare-commit-msg or pre-commit check comparing staged paths against the paths named in the invoking command is NOT generally derivable — so consider instead a post-commit advisory hook that prints the swept file list whenever a commit lands during another live session (pane count heuristic), or explicitly record why no mechanical arm is worth it.
- [ ] The 2026-08-09 instance cited as the measured evidence (efec807).
