title: offboard: the decision harvest drops decisions RESOLVED this session but created earlier
description:
## Context
Found 2026-08-02 running /offboard in ~/coding-jams/ifcomp/2026. The harvest
reported 4 decision beads. Three more — ifcompd-xku (authoring system),
ifcompd-x7s (collaboration model), ifcompd-fmr (repo visibility) — were the
session's MOST consequential decisions, each recorded with full reasoning and
closed during the session. All three were invisible to the harvest.

Cause: Step 2.5 filters on `created_at >= SINCE_EPOCH`. Those beads were created
by a prior session and only RESOLVED in this one.

This is `explore-7ogz` one layer over. That fix added `-a` so a decision created
AND closed inside the session is visible. It did not cover a decision created
BEFORE the session and closed inside it — which is arguably the more common shape,
because a decision bead usually outlives the session that files it. Same silent
failure: the harvest just prints fewer lines, which reads like "fewer decisions".

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Session A: `br create -t decision "..."`. End session.
2. Session B: `br close <id> -r "..."`. Run /offboard.
3. The harvest omits it. The handoff records the session's biggest call as absent.

## Fix options
- Filter on `updated_at`/`closed_at >= SINCE_EPOCH` **in addition to** created_at
  (a decision touched this session is a decision of this session).
- Or emit two groups: "filed this session" and "resolved this session".
  Probably better — they are different things and the handoff reader wants both.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision created in a prior session and closed in this one appears in the harvest
- [ ] The receipt line counts both groups, so a zero is still distinguishable from a failed query
- [ ] /offboard SKILL.md Step 2.5 updated

## Write target
~/demesne — agents/skills/offboard/SKILL.md (Step 2.5 harvest filter).

title: ssh: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 deleted 2026-08-07 17:19 — the metis pull is broken and fetch-camp hides it
description:
## Context

`~/.ssh/id_ed25519` no longer exists on zig-computer. The only `id_ed25519*`
under `/home/ubuntu` is `~/.ollama/id_ed25519`, which is unrelated.

That file was a **default identity** — ssh offers `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`
automatically to any host without needing an `IdentityFile` line. `~/.ssh/local`
has a `Host metis` block carrying only `User andrew`, no IdentityFile, so metis
access depended entirely on that default.

Timeline, from mtimes and the `.bak` files written alongside:

- **03:00 today** — `~/andrewzigler3/in/.camp-fetch-source` records `metis-live`.
  The pull worked. No ssh-agent involved (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK` unset, `ssh-add -l`
  reports no identities), so it was key-file auth via the default identity.
- **17:18** — `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` rewritten (`.bak.2026-08-07` alongside).
  Diff drops a source-restricted `from="15.204.114.210"` agent entry.
- **17:19** — `~/.ssh/local` rewritten (`.bak.2026-08-07` alongside). Diff removes
  the whole `Host marketing-vps` block, which was the only thing in the file
  naming `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
- **23:5x** — `ssh metis`, `ssh andrew@100.106.120.98`, and explicit `-i id_ha` /
  `-i id_rsa_ovh` all return `Permission denied (publickey,password,
  keyboard-interactive)`. Port 22 is open (`nc` succeeds); this is real macOS
  sshd refusing, not Tailscale SSH.

The config edit looks deliberate (a marketing-vps cleanup). **Whether the KEY
FILE was meant to go with it is the open question** — nothing in the dotfiles git
log since 2 days ago touches `ssh/`, and a private key correctly lives outside the
repo, so there is no version-controlled record either way.

## Why P1 — the failure is silent

`~/andrewzigler3/src/scripts/fetch-camp.sh` is explicitly best-effort: any metis
failure logs a warning and falls through to a GitHub sparse checkout of
`azigler/zettelkasten`. The mirror is kept current by metis's own backup cron, so
it is ALWAYS downstream of metis-live.

The next nightly build will therefore succeed, deploy, and report healthy while
serving content that can only ever be staler than the live vault. The script's own
`in/.camp-fetch-source` marker is the detector — it will flip `metis-live` ->
`github-fallback` — but only if something reads it. This is the
`dotfiles-cxle` shape: a fallback converting a failure into a success-shaped
outcome.

Second consequence: **zig-computer now has no credential on metis at all**, which
blocks any agent-side work needing files from that machine.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ls -l ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` → No such file.
2. `ssh -o BatchMode=yes andrew@metis 'echo ok'` → `Permission denied
   (publickey,password,keyboard-interactive)`.
3. `nc -zv 100.106.120.98 22` → succeeds, confirming sshd is up and reachable and
   the refusal is authentication, not connectivity.
4. `cat ~/andrewzigler3/in/.camp-fetch-source` → still `metis-live` from the 03:00
   run, i.e. the marker has not yet been updated by a post-breakage run. Run
   `SKIP_CAMP_FETCH= bash ~/andrewzigler3/src/scripts/fetch-camp.sh` and it should
   flip to `github-fallback` while exiting 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zig confirms whether deleting `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` was intentional.
- [ ] Either the keypair is restored and authorized on metis, OR a replacement is
      authorized (`~/.ssh/id_metis` was generated 2026-08-07 for exactly this and
      is currently unauthorized), AND `~/.ssh/local`'s `Host metis` block names the
      key explicitly with `IdentityFile` rather than relying on a default identity
      that any unrelated cleanup can silently remove.
- [ ] `ssh -o BatchMode=yes andrew@metis 'echo ok'` prints `ok`.
- [ ] `fetch-camp.sh` writes `metis-live` on a real run afterwards — verified by
      reading the marker, not by the script's exit code (it exits 0 either way).
- [ ] A check that makes the silent degradation loud: something reads
      `in/.camp-fetch-source` and reports non-`metis-live` as a real signal. The
      marker already exists (bd-9u3y); what is missing is a consumer.

## Notes

Found 2026-08-07 while trying to fetch Sega CD files from metis for romd's
`/cleanroom` test target. The romd work is blocked on this.

The generalisable lesson, and the reason the config half deserves fixing even if
the key is restored: **a host whose access depends on a DEFAULT identity has an
undeclared dependency.** Nothing named the relationship between `Host metis` and
`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, so a cleanup targeting a different host removed it without
any signal. Name identities explicitly per host.
notes: ## Re-verified 2026-08-08 (Cluster F): the P1 emergency is OVER. ~/.ssh/id_metis exists (created 08-07 23:47Z), ~/.ssh/local Host metis block points at it, live probe ssh -o BatchMode=yes andrew@metis 'echo ok' → ok rc=0. REMAINING (the new scope): (1) re-run fetch-camp.sh and verify ~/andrewzigler3/in/.camp-fetch-source flips github-fallback → metis-live; (2) build the marker-consumer that reports non-metis-live as a real signal. Downgraded P1→P3; sonnet-mechanical, small.
close_reason: Emergency resolved 08-07 (key restored); residuals merged andrewzigler3@831f0b2 and pushed: fetch-camp re-run live (348 camp + 1110 stream files), marker github-fallback -> metis-live verified. Consumer pulse-camp-freshness-status.sh: three-rung contract (SURFACE/QUIET/UNDETERMINABLE), 20-case selftest green, wired as intake row step 6.

title: spec: /pulse — generic per-project heartbeat (extract autonovel /heartbeat; pilot: weekly-reporting)
description:
## 1. Overview  (REVISED 2026-06-09 post-/check — decisions in --notes)

/pulse is a global skill that turns any beads-disciplined project into a self-driving loop: a scheduled tick lands in a DURABLE interactive Claude session -> cheap onboard -> route -> at most ONE unit of work with full discipline -> offboard -> done until the next tick. It generalizes autonovel's /heartbeat (routing table, one-dispatch-per-tick, rate caps, anti-entropy — spec bd-49j) into a project-agnostic skill. It is the Claude-native realization of what Hermes promised (durable, autonomous, learning over time); /heartbeat is the parent and is SUPERSEDED by /pulse after the pilot (autonovel migrates onto a thin routing table; learnings fold back at migration).

## 2. Baseline

- autonovel /heartbeat: proven loop (<=1h tick, routing table, one dispatch/tick, caps).
- weekly-reporting: 4 editorial jobs on systemd user timers driving the Agent SDK — outside the bead/handoff brain. Hermes uninstalled 2026-06-06.
- /onboard//offboard cheap (TOOLKIT ~3k tokens); refs/session-handoff.md + .offboard-pending give continuity; bv --robot-next picks work deterministically; tmux lexicon (🧠/✅/🔔) + AskUserQuestion convention give visibility.
- Ruled out: cloud /schedule (no local harness); claude -p headless (draws from the separate monthly Agent SDK credit pool per docs effective 2026-06-15, and is unwatchable/unsteerable); raw /loop as durability layer (~1-week expiry).

## 3. Changes  (architecture per OQ-1/OQ-3 decisions)

a) SCHEDULER (shipped, wave 1 dotfiles-x1q): agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh — systemd user timer fires the injector; it ensures the tmux session exists (detached creation survives reboot), finds/creates the dedicated scheduler window (lexicon-aware matching) anchored in the project dir, ensures an INTERACTIVE claude session is running (launch + bounded poll), and send-keys the tick command. Per-project unit templates in agents/scheduler/templates/. The session is durable across ticks; Andrew can watch/steer it any time; usage is normal subscription.
b) /pulse SKILL (wave 2): per-project opt-in via refs/pulse.md routing table — rows {trigger, condition-check, action, cap, priority}; tick procedure = Step 0 honor .offboard-pending -> cheap onboard -> evaluate rows top-down -> fire AT MOST ONE (worktree subagents + scrutinize as normal) -> close/commit/push -> offboard (writes handoff; session persists) -> end tick. Quiet tick = log + end.
c) Blocked-on-Andrew protocol: never block on AskUserQuestion in a tick — file P1 'human:' bead + push notification, end tick.
d) COMPACT-AWARENESS (wave 4, per OQ-3): (i) Stop-hook context guard — parse session JSONL latest usage (input + cache_read + cache_creation ~= context), above ~85% exit 2 with 'run /offboard now'; an exit-2 Stop makes the session offboard itself. (ii) PreCompact(auto) backstop — block once with 'offboard first' (marker prevents loops), then allow. Both need empirical verification on 2.1.170 first.
e) /offboard: no successor-booking step needed in the timer model — the recurring timer IS the successor; offboard just leaves clean state for the next tick.

## 4. Formal spec (sketch — refine at wave 2 impl)

- Routing row schema: {name, trigger (time|state|queue), check (bash, exit 0 = fire), action (skill invocation or bv --robot-next), cap (per day/week), priority}. First satisfied row wins; caps enforced via a per-project tick ledger (refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl or bead notes).
- Invariants: one dispatch per tick; all work -> beads + commits + push (always-push); handoff note per working tick; quiet ticks logged not committed.
- Window contract: one dedicated 'pulse' window per tmux session (work session row); the lexicon hook labels it like any other window.

## 5. Test cases (>=10 at /test time)

1. Quiet tick: no row fires -> log only, session intact. 2. Time-trigger cap: fires once despite two ticks in window. 3. Queue trigger takes bv --robot-next top. 4. Dispatch failure -> human: P1 bead + push, tick ends cleanly. 5. .offboard-pending honored first. 6. Two satisfied rows -> higher priority only. 7. Cap exhausted -> next row evaluated. 8. Injector cold-start after reboot (no tmux server) -> tick still lands. 9. Handoff written per working tick. 10. Non-opted-in project -> /pulse refuses with setup guidance. (Injector-level cases 1-7 of wave 1 already pass.)

## 6. Open Questions — ALL RESOLVED 2026-06-09 (decisions + readiness in --notes)

OQ-1 tmux-injection (decided) · OQ-2 weekly-reporting pilot (decided) · OQ-3 compact-awareness design (decided, empirical verification in its impl bead) · OQ-4 digest (deferred by design) · OQ-5 heartbeat superseded after pilot (decided) · location: global paragon set (decided).

## 7. Future

- Morning digest (OQ-4): aggregate human: beads / stale in_progress / markers / 🔔 states across projects; landing spot TBD (Asana vs local+push vs Slack agents). After pilot.
- Fleet control-tower window; per-project lessons bead (the Hermes durable-memory benefit); Slack-agent 🔔 mirroring.
- Hermes carry-forward: when the local-model arc resumes (pico primed), retry Hermes clean-slate and map this contract onto it (see --notes + auto-memory).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Wave 1 scheduler shipped with tests (DONE — dotfiles-x1q, 7/7)
- /pulse SKILL.md ships in dotfiles + TOOLKIT entry
- weekly-reporting pilot: >=1 editorial job runs end-to-end on a pulse tick (bead + commit + push + handoff, no Andrew prompt)
- Tick lands after a reboot (timer Persistent=true + injector cold-start)
- Blocked work surfaces as human: P1 bead + push, never an interactive wait
- Compact-awareness verified empirically before its hook ships
notes:
## Decision: OQ-1 (successor-booking primitive) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

**Decision:** tmux-injection scheduler. NOT claude -p headless.
**Rationale:** (a) headless -p pulls from the monthly use-it-or-lose-it consumption credits rather than normal interactive subscription usage (Andrew's understanding; flag if docs say otherwise — see OQ-3 research item 4); (b) headless is invisible — Andrew can't watch thinking, steer, or give feedback mid-run. An interactive session in tmux is visible to him AND the agent, persistent, steerable, uses the normal subscription, and inherits the 🧠/✅/🔔 lexicon.
**Architecture:** systemd user timer -> injector script -> (1) ensure a DEDICATED window exists in the work session's labeled row (the scheduler window); (2) ensure an interactive claude session is running there in a scaffolded harness folder; (3) tmux send-keys the kick-off command (e.g. '/pulse tick' or the project-specific flow). The window/session is durable; ticks are injected prompts, not new processes.
**Bake-in:** global — injector script + timer templates live in dotfiles (proposed: dotfiles/agents/scheduler/), rigid and deterministic.
**Spec impact:** Sections 3-4 — successor booking becomes 'recurring timer + injector targets the durable window'; per-tick offboard still writes the handoff but the SESSION persists between ticks. Re-dispatch /spec to fold in.

## Decision: OQ-2 (pilot scope) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

## Decision: OQ-4 (morning digest) — DEFERRED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

Later, after pulse proves the per-project loop. Aggregation inputs + landing spot stay open. 'We're getting to this... come back to later once we get more of this implemented.'

## Decision: OQ-5 (autonovel fold-in) — DECIDED 2026-06-09

The toybox 3-project graduation rule is for capability skills, not harness infrastructure.

## Context carry-forward: Hermes

Hermes uninstalled 2026-06-06 (mis-setup, obtuse, no benefit; clean-slate retry intended). No local model currently primed and API-key Claude too expensive, so Hermes is parked. WHEN the local-model arc resumes (pico primed), retry Hermes and map /pulse's contract (routing table, one-dispatch-per-tick, human: bead protocol, injection scheduler) onto it instead of starting over. Also recorded in auto-memory (project_hermes_revisit.md).

## Implementation Readiness — 2026-06-09

**P1 OQs decided:** 2/2 (OQ-1, OQ-2)
**P2:** OQ-3 research in flight (blocks ONLY the compact-awareness feature, not the skill skeleton); OQ-4 deferred by design
**P3:** OQ-5 decided
**New decisions:** skill location (global)

### Recommended impl order
1. Scheduler scaffolding: injector script + dedicated-window convention + timer template (dotfiles)
2. /pulse SKILL.md: routing-table contract + tick procedure + human:-bead protocol (+ TOOLKIT entry)
3. weekly-reporting pilot: first job as a pulse row + its timer
4. Compact-awareness: after OQ-3 research lands
Spec revision needed first: fold OQ-1 architecture into Sections 3-4 (re-dispatch /spec).
## Decision: OQ-3 (compact-awareness) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (research-backed)

**Findings (guide agent, official docs, 2026-06-09):** Hooks do NOT receive context-window % — only the statusline command gets context_window.used_percentage. PreCompact fires before BOTH auto and manual compaction; its payload carries transcript_path but no token counts; it CAN block via decision:"block" / exit 2 (delays compaction). No documented auto-compact threshold, env var, or context-low signal. The session transcript JSONL on disk carries per-turn usage fields. Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md, hooks-guide.md, how-claude-code-works.md.

**Design (both mechanisms need empirical verification on 2.1.170):**
- (a) PRIMARY — Stop-hook context guard: on Stop, parse the session JSONL (latest assistant entry's input_tokens + cache_read + cache_creation ≈ current context), compute %, and above ~85% exit 2 with 'context nearing auto-compaction — run /offboard now, then continue or /compact deliberately.' An exit-2 Stop keeps the agent working WITH that instruction — the session offboards itself, which is exactly Andrew's ideal.
- (b) BACKSTOP — PreCompact(auto) blocks ONCE with reason 'offboard first' (marker file prevents a block loop), then allows.

**Bonus finding for OQ-1:** docs CONFIRM the billing premise — 'Starting June 15, 2026, Agent SDK and claude -p usage on subscription plans will draw from a new monthly Agent SDK credit, separate from your interactive usage limits' (code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md). The tmux-injection decision stands on documented ground. tmux send-keys itself is undocumented-but-generic; the injector should use claude --continue/--resume for session resumption in the dedicated window.

ALL OQs now decided or deliberately deferred: OQ-1 ✓ OQ-2 ✓ OQ-3 ✓ (research-backed design, empirical verification folded into its impl bead) OQ-4 deferred-by-design OQ-5 ✓ + location ✓. Direction confirmed: /heartbeat is the PARENT (pulse is extracted from it); the timing rule is the only reason it stays untouched during the pilot. End state: once /pulse is stable through the weekly-reporting pilot, autonovel MIGRATES onto /pulse with a thin autonovel-specific routing table (mail/daily/write/learn rows), pilot learnings fold in during that migration, and /heartbeat as a separate skill RETIRES. Not "evaluate folding" — superseded after pilot.

Design UPGRADE over §3d: the statusline (not hooks) receives the OFFICIAL context_window.used_percentage — verified live on 2.1.170 (payload also carries session_id, context_window_size, current_usage; the latter validates the JSONL-estimation formula ≈134k ✓ but estimation is now unnecessary).

Fires once per session (marker); stop_hook_active loop-protected; released by a FRESH (<30 min, CONTEXT_GUARD_OFFBOARD_FRESH_SECS) last-offboard-session match — staleness check added after live testing caught yesterday's offboard silencing today's guard.

title: /commit tells you to rebase; AGENTS.md says never rebase — and the reflex chain from rebase's refusal is the DESTRUCTIVE verb
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `grep -n rebase agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md` -> L15 "**Always pull --rebase,
   THEN push** after committing -- unless you're in a worktree"; L96 `git pull
   --rebase origin "$BRANCH"   # ALWAYS. Never push blind.`; L128 defends the choice.
2. `grep -n 'rebase' agents/AGENTS.md` -> L226 "## Two writers, one working tree —
   merge, never rebase, NEVER stash"; L248 "**`git fetch origin && git merge
   --no-edit origin/main`** — NOT `git pull --rebase`."

Both are in the loaded tier. AGENTS.md is always-loaded fleet-wide; /commit's body
loads on invoke, and TOOLKIT.md's /commit entry propagates the REBASE version into
every single /onboard ("**`git pull --rebase` THEN push**").

## Why this is a hazard, not just an inconsistency
AGENTS.md's own measured table (2026-08-01) is:
  git pull --no-rebase -> fails SAFELY
  git pull --rebase    -> fails OBSTRUCTIVELY (rc 128 on ANY unrelated dirty file)
  git stash            -> "succeeds", DESTRUCTIVELY (silently takes the other writer's work)
and it names the trap explicitly: "rebase's refusal is exactly what tempts you
toward it [stash]". So /commit's instruction does not merely disagree -- it routes
the agent onto the rung whose failure mode reflexively suggests the destructive
verb. pre-shared-tree-guard.sh only covers the window where another writer is
PROVABLY mid-run; outside it the verbs are the agent's.

Found in the dotfiles-w8xw audit (audit A). Verified independently by the
orchestrator before filing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zig decides which rule is canonical (they were written for different
      situations -- multi-machine push races vs a second writer in ONE tree -- so
      the fix may be to scope each, not to delete one)
- [ ] The surviving rule stated in exactly ONE place; the other file points at it
- [ ] TOOLKIT.md's /commit entry updated to match
- [ ] A doclint/hook check so the two cannot silently diverge again

title: finding (CLASS): 'the documented example IS the defect' — 4 confirmed instances, one shared fix
description:
Four independent audits on 2026-07-25 each found an instance of the SAME failure
mode, none aware of the others. In a prompt-driven harness, agents copy examples
verbatim. So a wrong example is not a typo — it is a defect that replicates
itself across every project, silently, forever.

THE FOUR CONFIRMED INSTANCES:

1. agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md ~L51 — documents the ledger row as
   {"ts":"…","row":null,"outcome":"quiet",…}. Ticks copied it -> 23 rows across
   THREE ledgers (explore 19, di 1, weekly-reporting 3) with row=null, invisible
   to pulse-cap.py and every per-row analytic. Explore's 19 are repaired
   (explore-qdo5); the SKILL fix is in flight.

2. agents/AGENTS.md:281 — the canonical worktree-cleanup snippet is
   `git push origin --delete worktree-agent-XXXX 2>/dev/null || true`. That
   VIOLATES the same file's own rule at :140-154 AND is blocked by the live
   pre-bash-stderr-guard.sh hook. Every orchestrator copying the documented
   cleanup block hits a hook denial. (The auditor was itself blocked by this
   hook mid-audit, for this pattern. So was the orchestrator, later, in the
   same session.)

3. explore/.claude/practices.md ~L89 — MANDATES the cross-link form
   `[name](name/FINDINGS.md)`, which is a BROKEN hyperlink from inside an
   exploration's own folder. The working form is `../name/FINDINGS.md`.
   Compounding harm: gen-index.py's link regex only matched the BROKEN form, so
   authors who wrote a working link had it silently dropped from the graph.
   Result: LINKMAP reported 69 edges / 85 unconnected when the truth is ~384 /
   ~23. The compendium's knowledge graph has been ~18% VISIBLE.

4. vacation-station-14/CLAUDE.md:194 — a copy-me commit template hardcoding
   `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6`. Agents paste a false model attribution
   into real commit history.

WHY THIS CLASS IS SPECIAL (and worth its own guard):
 - It is INVISIBLE to code review — every file is individually well-formed.
 - It is invisible to tests — nothing tests documentation.
 - It SCALES with adoption: the better the docs are followed, the more damage.
 - It survives fixes downstream: repairing 19 ledger rows does not stop the
   next project reproducing them. Only fixing the example does.
 - Three of the four were found only because four separate auditors happened to
   read four different files on the same day. Nothing systematic would catch it.

THE SHARED FIX (proposed by the config auditor; endorsed):
Add a /housekeeping pass that EXTRACTS every fenced code block and inline
command from SKILL.md files, CLAUDE.md files, and AGENTS.md, and LINTS them:
 - shell blocks -> shellcheck, plus a DRY-RUN against the live PreToolUse hooks
   (the hooks are the ground truth for what is permitted; instance 2 would have
   been caught instantly by running the documented command past the guard that
   blocks it)
 - JSON/JSONL examples -> validate against the schema the consumer actually
   parses (instance 1)
 - markdown links in docs that mandate a link FORM -> resolve them (instance 3)
 - grep for hardcoded model ids / dates / versions in copy-me templates
   (instance 4)
This is the mechanical guard for a class the harness has been fixing one
instance at a time, by luck.

Relates: explore-qdo5 (instance 1 repair), dotfiles-b9ii (epic),
dotfiles-uxj9 (cost), explore-1fd8. Zig's standing preference (memory:
editorial-vs-mechanical-enforcement): hooks for checkable invariants. This is
a checkable invariant.
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

The four instances needed nothing. The real gap was that the doclint guard was BUILT and wired into nothing — a linter nobody ran.

title: pulse-inject: cold-boot injects before the launched TUI is input-ready → keystrokes eaten (ha-portal submit launched claude but /ha-serve was lost; button press into the warm session worked)
description:
ROOT CAUSE: the cold-boot branch waited for pane_current_command==LAUNCH_BASE (LIVENESS — the process exists) then slept a fixed 3s and injected. Claude Code's process name flips within ~1-4s of exec, but the interactive TUI (heavy project: big CLAUDE.md + MCP + skills + hooks) is not READY for composer input for much longer. send-keys 3s after detection landed in the still-initializing TUI and was SILENTLY dropped.

EVIDENCE (/tmp/pulse-inject.log): 2026-07-08T20:01:06 ha-portal nudge cold-booted window 'ha' (@285): launched claude 20:01:07, injected /ha-serve 20:01:14 (only 7s = ~3s after process detection) — EATEN. Later warm nudges 21:36:40 / 21:42:51 injected 0-1s into the already-running session — worked. Every systemd-timer pulse in the log ('injected into @168/@18', no 'launched claude' line) hits a long-lived WARM session, so /pulse + /daily-digest almost never take the cold branch — which is why the weekly report never showed this. The on-demand ha-portal button has no next-tick retry, so it exposes the race.

FIX (agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh): after the liveness poll, poll capture-pane for an input-READY marker (Claude Code composer footer: 'shift+tab to cycle' / '? for shortcuts' / 'for agents' / 'bypass permissions' / 'accept edits on' / 'plan mode on') before injecting, bounded by PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT (default 60s, first-match returns early), then a 2s settle. On timeout, inject anyway (old behavior) so a marker miss degrades to 'try late' not 'never'. PULSE_READY_MARKER overridable; empty disables the gate (non-TUI launches). Verified the default regex matches real ready panes @285/@168/@18.

REGRESSION TEST (test-pulse-inject.sh case 8): slow-TUI launch that prints the marker only after a 4s delay; asserts the cmd lands AND elapsed>=3s (the injector waited for readiness rather than injecting blind). 15/15 pass.

Sibling of dotfiles-q18 (send-keys eaten by a tmux modal). RESIDUAL (not fixed here, noted): stacked warm nudges into a busy session queue multiple /ha-serve commands; and the daemon nudge has no post-inject verify/retry — the readiness gate makes eating unlikely, and maxWorking(480s) still un-wedges the button.
notes: CORRECTION (post-close, Zig): the 'timer pulses reuse a warm long-lived session' claim was WRONG. pulse-inject.log proves weekly-report (pulse-weekly-report.*, same injector) cold-boots a fresh window + fresh claude EVERY week: created window weekly-report @253 (06-30) +4s inject, @279 (07-07) +5s inject — both landed after ready. ha cold-boots: @257 +5s, @276 +6s, @285 +7s (07-08, EATEN). Real root cause = an UNGUARDED timing race (fixed post-detection sleep vs actual composer readiness), variance-driven by boot load + session weight (ha under ~/explore = ~59KB CLAUDE.md vs ~42KB) + attachment (ha=zig-computer ATTACHED 157x71, work=DETACHED). The failing boot waited LONGER (+7s) than the winners (+4/+5s), so sleep length was never the lever — readiness-at-inject-time is. Fix (readiness-marker gate) is unchanged and correct; only the rationale is corrected here + in the code comment.
close_reason: done

title: pulse-inject: PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT=60 is thin enough to EAT a tick on a cold boot
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while building --fresh (dotfiles-6ycc), on a disposable rig.

During a cold boot, `claude` took ~60s to paint its composer — right at PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT=60. The readiness gate timed out, logged "WARN: input-ready marker not seen after 60s — injecting anyway", injected into an empty composer, and the tick was EATEN: 0% context, no work, no ledger row.

This is a concrete mechanism for the "fired but no ledger row" class — the same signature the stale-loop detector (harnessd-h14z) alerts on and the same class as the two explore ticks that vanished over 16 days. It is a silent loss: the injector logs a WARN and proceeds, so nothing downstream knows the tick died.

Caveat on severity, stated honestly: this was a FIRST-RUN-IN-A-NEW-PROJECT boot, which is the slowest possible case. No production regression is claimed. But historical measurements suggested +4-7s of headroom, and the real observation was ~60s — the margin is far thinner than assumed.

Note this interacts with --fresh: a /clear'd session re-paints, so readiness timing on a --fresh loop deserves its own measurement rather than inheriting the warm-path assumption.

Also recorded from the same pass (lower priority, no fix proposed): five same-second timer collisions exist — pulse-explore x pulse-di-digest (Wed 13:00), x pulse-di-thursday (Thu 13:00), x pulse-di-friday (Fri 19:00), pulse-daily-digest x pulse-di-tuesday (Tue 14:00), x pulse-di-wednesday (Wed 14:00). No timer sets RandomizedDelaySec. Staggering would NOT fully close this because pulse-retry.timer fires every 2 min and can start a loop service at any moment; the pid tag shipped in dotfiles-0lm3 is what actually solves the attribution harm.

## Steps to Reproduce

Cold-boot a claude session in a project it has never run in, and inject a tick against a 60s readiness timeout. The composer is not ready, the gate warns and injects anyway, and the tick produces nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- an injection that times out on the readiness gate does NOT inject blind — it either retries with backoff or records an explicit blocked/lost outcome in the ledger
- a tick that produces no work is distinguishable in the ledger from one that never fired
- PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT is measured against real cold-boot and post-/clear repaint times, and set from that measurement rather than assumption
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

pulse-inject.sh:139-158 (shared record_bounce), :250-320 (the gate), :352-358. Timeout now bounces with reason:"not_ready" and exits 0 instead of silently eating the tick; PULSE_READY_ON_TIMEOUT=inject is the escape hatch. The poll now runs to a WALL-CLOCK deadline — the old seq+sleep 1 overshot (the incident logged 'after 60s' a measured 63s later). Success path logs observed elapsed seconds. +7 tests.
AC3 NOT MET, deliberately and honestly: 'measured against real cold-boot times' needs real Claude Code sessions, which the agent was forbidden to start (see the pulse-measure incident). It mined /tmp/pulse-inject.log instead — only 3 gated cold boots exist since the gate shipped (two at +2s, one timing out at 60s); the other 23 predate the gate. So 60->90 is derived from CONSTRAINTS, not data: past the one observed failure, inside the 120s TimeoutStartSec on pulse-retry.service. The new elapsed-seconds log line is what actually closes this criterion over time.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in Wave 1 of the Opus-5 audit.

title: vps-preflight: reports 'HISTORIES DIVERGED' and recommends reset --hard for a repo that is merely BEHIND
description:
## Context

Hit TWICE on 2026-07-29, an hour apart, on `~/linearb`. Both times the repo was
strictly behind origin/main with zero local commits, and both times the preflight
called it a divergence and recommended a destructive remedy.

The message:

    $HOME/linearb: local HEAD 7710c543 is NOT the published tip d4ba7d28 — ...
    Remedy: HISTORIES DIVERGED (an upstream rebase does this). If the published
    tip is authoritative: git -C /home/ubuntu/linearb fetch origin &&
    git -C /home/ubuntu/linearb reset --hard origin/main — this DISCARDS local
    commits, so check 'git log origin/main..HEAD' first

The measured reality both times:

    $ git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main
    0   1                     # 0 ahead, 1 behind
    $ git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main; echo $?
    0                         # HEAD IS an ancestor -> plain fast-forward
    $ git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
    (empty)                   # no local commits exist to discard

Correct remedy in both cases was `git pull --ff-only`, which succeeded instantly.

## Why this matters more than a wording nit

1. `reset --hard` is the one remedy that can LOSE work, and it is being
   recommended for the case where it is never needed. The hedge ("check
   `git log origin/main..HEAD` first") puts the burden on a reader who has
   already been told, authoritatively, that histories diverged.
2. A subagent acting on this message today reported to the orchestrator that
   `~/linearb` histories had diverged and that resolving it was a judgment call
   about which side was authoritative. That was wrong, and it was wrong because
   the tool said so. The cost of a misleading diagnosis is that it propagates.
3. This repo goes stale CONSTANTLY now — marketing-vps commits to it too, so
   `~/linearb` falls behind between dispatches as a matter of course. That makes
   this the single most-seen preflight failure, i.e. the worst one to have
   phrased wrong.

Same defect class as dotfiles-rox7 (pulse-stall-reconcile asserting an injection
that never happened): a backstop that fires correctly but describes the cause
wrongly, spending the reader's attention in the wrong direction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a repo the preflight checks, ensure zero local commits and let origin/main
   advance by one commit (or `git reset --hard HEAD~1`).
2. Run `agents/scheduler/vps-preflight.sh --no-refresh`.
3. Observed: "HISTORIES DIVERGED", remedy is `reset --hard`.
   Expected: "BEHIND by N commits", remedy is `git pull --ff-only`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The check distinguishes the three states and names the one it found:
      BEHIND (`merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`) — remedy
      `git pull --ff-only`, explicitly noted as non-destructive;
      AHEAD (`--is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`) — remedy `git push`, which is the
      genuine "your work is not published" case this assertion exists for;
      DIVERGED (neither) — only here is `reset --hard` mentioned, with its
      warning intact.
- [ ] The commit counts appear in the message (`N ahead, M behind`), so the
      reader can sanity-check the verdict without re-deriving it.
- [ ] `reset --hard` NEVER appears in the BEHIND or AHEAD messages.
- [ ] Tests for all three states.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: paste the three messages produced by three constructed repos.

## Possible follow-on, do NOT do here

Given `~/linearb` now falls behind as normal fleet behavior, consider whether the
dispatcher should `pull --ff-only` the checked repos itself before asserting
(strictly-behind only, never on ahead/diverged). That is a behavior change with
its own risks — file separately if it looks right.
notes: SUPERSEDED and RESOLVED by dotfiles-w16i (2026-07-31). Root cause found and it was deeper than wording: check_local called 'merge-base --is-ancestor' WITHOUT fetching first, so for exactly the commits this machine was behind by, the published tip was not a local object. Both ancestry arms errored, and the code fell through to the else branch that prints 'HISTORIES DIVERGED' and recommends reset --hard. Reproduced in a throwaway repo 2026-07-31: 'fatal: Not a valid commit name <tip>' before fetch, correct BEHIND classification after. That is why every hand-check contradicted the tool - the hand-checks ran git fetch first. Four false firings (7/30 di-wednesday x2, di-thursday, 7/31 di-friday). Now four-state (BEHIND auto-ff / AHEAD / DIVERGED / UNKNOWN) with reset --hard at exactly one executable site.
close_reason: done

title: guard: gateway-health — keep-side probe of the agentgateway with auto-kickstart recovery
description:
## Context
Child of dotfiles-kviw. Routing is deliberately fail-hard (dotfiles-ucl4): when the gateway dies the whole fleet loses claude. pico-health detects (30-min cadence, read-only by charter) but nothing recovers. This guard is the recovery arm, cloned in posture from pico-health.sh (outcome contract, exit codes, ledger) but WRITE-CAPABLE on pico for exactly one verb: restarting the gateway job.

## Design (decided, hardening seat 2026-08-09)
New agents/scheduler/gateway-health.sh + gateway-health.{service,timer} (2-min cadence). Env knobs with defaults, each a test seam: GW_PROBE_URL (http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude/v1/models), GW_SSH (ssh), GW_HOST (pico), GW_JOB (gui/501/com.zig.agentgateway), GW_PLIST (/Users/pico/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.agentgateway.plist), GW_LEDGER (~/.local/share/fleet-health/gateway.jsonl), GW_CURL (curl).
Logic: probe with curl -m 8. ANY http code (401 is the healthy signature — transparent passthrough; see infra.md) = up → GATEWAY_HEALTH_RESULT=ok, exit 0. Connect failure = down → ssh kickstart $GW_JOB; if launchctl says 'Could not find service' → launchctl bootstrap gui/501 $GW_PLIST then kickstart; wait, re-probe (2 tries). Verdicts: restored (exit 10), down-unrecovered (exit 10), pico-unreachable (ssh failed, exit 10). Checker-broken = exit 1, distinct from findings, mirroring pico-health.
NEVER auto-runs gateway-switch.sh — flipping the fleet to direct routing is an operator/orchestrator call; the header must say so.
Ledger: append JSONL on every non-ok verdict and on the first ok after a non-ok (the recovery record); plain ok appends nothing (720 runs/day must not bloat it).
Unit: Type=oneshot, SuccessExitStatus deliberately does NOT include 10, so a finding lands in systemctl --user --failed (the surface the fleet reads — same posture as pico-health).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] agents/scheduler/gateway-health.sh with the outcome contract above; last stdout line always GATEWAY_HEALTH_RESULT=<ok|restored|down-unrecovered|pico-unreachable>
- [ ] gateway-health.service + gateway-health.timer files beside the other scheduler units, modeled on pico-health.{service,timer}
- [ ] Hermetic test suite agents/scheduler/test-gateway-health.sh (fakes on PATH, never real ssh/curl): healthy→ok/exit0/no ledger append; down→kickstart→restored/exit10/ledger row; down+ssh-unreachable→pico-unreachable/exit10; down+kickstart ok but probe still down→down-unrecovered/exit10; 'Could not find service'→bootstrap path invoked then kickstart; ok-after-non-ok appends the recovery row
- [ ] Each failure case shown failing against a deliberately broken variant (guard bites — repo rule 1)
- [ ] No stderr blanket suppression (rule 3); shellcheck-clean like sibling scripts
- [ ] Installation NOT performed by the agent — orchestrator installs/arms after merge
close_reason: Merged f40028d (agent 01433de+90c3777), scrutiny SHIP after FIX-FIRST round. gateway-health.sh: 401-signature probe, curl rc7/rc28+time_connect split (probe-degraded exit10 NO kickstart for slow-but-alive — mutant-confirmed), kickstart→bootstrap-on-missing ladder, pico-unreachable/down-unrecovered verdicts, recovery-row ledger, never touches gateway-switch (static suite assert). 25/25 hermetic, 9/9 mutants killed applied-asserted. Installed retargeted to %h/.agents (post-kvrl convention), timer armed odd-minutes :11, live run: GATEWAY_HEALTH_RESULT=ok HTTP 401. Follow-up: committed mutation harness = dotfiles-w4z9.

Also: fail-open on own crash, unbounded skip-log — both being fixed in same pass.

title: human: the close gate has NO escape hatch while every sibling gate does — and it now blocks 250 real beads
description:
NEEDS ZIG. Surfaced 2026-07-26 by the agent that finished the lifecycle gates, and
it is the sharpest asymmetry in the new setup.

THE ASYMMETRY:
  scrutiny gate (impl beads)      -> has an OVERRIDE escape hatch
  NEW create gate (br create)     -> has '# allow-thin-bead'
  lint gate on br close           -> has NOTHING

So the gate we just BUILT ships with a documented valve, and the gate that now
blocks 250 real beads does not. That ordering is backwards.

THE SCALE, re-measured read-only fleet-wide (counts only for ~/linearb and ~/cfp):
  250 of 469 open beads (53%) fail br lint and cannot close until rewritten
  by priority : P0 2 · P1 26 · P2 155 · P3 67
  by type     : task 202 · bug 26 · epic 18 · feature 4
  missing     : 250 x '## Acceptance Criteria' · 26 x '## Steps to Reproduce'
                21 x '## Success Criteria'
  worst hit   : explore 118/149 (79%) · andrewzigler3 35/37 (94%)
                harnessd 42/59 (71%) · dotfiles 17/24 (70%)

THREE THINGS THAT MAKE IT WORSE THAN THE HEADLINE:
 1. No escape hatch, as above.
 2. **22 have a COMPLETELY EMPTY description** — closing one means authoring the
    whole bead (context, task, criteria) for work you are closing, not doing.
 3. **13 self-declare as superseded / obsolete / moot / already shipped** (10 P2,
    3 P3). These are the absurd ones: you must write acceptance criteria for work
    that will never happen, purely to be allowed to say it never will.

THE MITIGATION IS REAL, and smaller than it looks: the remedy is ONE command, not
two — `br update X --description "…## Acceptance Criteria…" && br close X` passes
the gate in a single call (verified rc=0), and `br update` alone is not gated at
all. So the cost is roughly one authored paragraph per bead: ~155 at P2 where it
plausibly buys something, ~67 at P3 where it plausibly does not.

TO NOTE: fix 1 did not invent a rule. It started ENFORCING one that was already
written down and had been silently bypassed since May. The 250 is pre-existing
debt becoming visible, not new debt.

THE DECISION, three options as I see them:
 (a) Give the close gate an escape hatch matching its siblings (e.g.
     '# allow-thin-close' plus a recorded reason). Cheapest; restores symmetry;
     risks becoming the default.
 (b) Leave it strict and pay the paragraph tax — arguably correct, since the rule
     was always the rule, and 250 paragraphs is a few sweeps.
 (c) Strict, but carve out the self-declared-dead and empty-description cases,
     which are where the rule produces pure ceremony.

I did not choose, and NOTHING was bulk-rewritten. Related: dotfiles-d83p (the
propose-only triage sweep) is the natural vehicle for whichever option you pick.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ZIG'S RULING (AskUserQuestion via seneschal, 2026-08-10): option (c) — the close gate stays STRICT, with carve-outs for the two pure-ceremony cases: (1) beads that self-declare superseded/obsolete/moot/already-shipped, (2) beads with a completely empty description at close time (closing != authoring). Everything else pays the paragraph tax (update+close single call, verified rc=0). Implementation: the lint-gate change is its own bead (filed next, fleet-markable); dotfiles-d83p remains the vehicle for the propose-only sweep of the remaining ~215.

title: spec: a WORK Claude seat on zig-computer via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, for the seven migrated pulse rows
description:
## Overview
The retreat doc specifies WHERE the seven rows run after migration (zig-computer,
`pulse-inject.sh`, one durable window per row) but is silent on WHICH CLAUDE IDENTITY
runs them. This spec covers that gap. Parent: the retreat epic.

## Baseline — why this matters, in the units own words
`pulse-di-monday.service` header, from the 2026-07-27 cutover:

    # CUT OVER TO marketing-vps 2026-07-27 (explore-7iz9, bd-zcxo).
    # Reasoning + drafting run on the LinearB company seat; zig-computer opens the
    # tunnel, refreshes + asserts the box, dispatches, collects the payload, and
    # writes the ledger HERE. The box holds no credentials.

So the cutover existed TO PUT THIS WORK ON THE LINEARB SEAT. Migrating the rows back to
zig-computer without a work credential would run LinearB drafting on Zig PERSONAL
Claude subscription — reversing the reason for the cutover, and doing it silently
(nothing would error; the ticks would just bill and attribute to the wrong seat).

The rollback comment in each unit is ALSO not the target shape — it restores
`--session work --window pulse` (the pre-cutover SHARED conduit window), whereas Zig
2026-08-04 decision is one durable window PER ROW. Copying the rollback line verbatim
would restore the wrong design. Verified across all seven units 2026-08-05.

## The mechanism already exists and is in production here
Claude Code honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and relocates its ENTIRE config tree — verified
2026-07-28 during the tick-jail work: pointed at an empty dir it reports "Not logged in
· Please run /login" and scaffolds `.claude.json` / projects / sessions there.

`zig-computer:~/.claude-tick` EXISTS TODAY with its own `.credentials.json` (22 entries)
and is used by the live `dive` loop through `tick-jailed.sh`. So a second, separate
OAuth lineage on this box is a proven pattern, not a new invention. This spec applies the
same pattern to a `~/.claude-work` seat.

Why a separate config dir rather than an env-var token: an isolated dir carries its OWN
refresh lineage, so a work-seat refresh cannot rotate Zig personal credential out from
under him (the exact failure the tick-jail work measured — atomic rename + inode pinning,
host inode 1121600 vs jail 1134825, every turn 401ing).

## Changes
1. `~/.claude-work/` (0700), holding the work seat OAuth lineage.
2. A way for `pulse-inject.sh` to run a tick under a chosen `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — new
   flag (e.g. `--config-dir`) or an env passthrough. DESIGN OPEN, see OQs.
3. The seven units converted from the remote form to the local form, each pinned to the
   work seat, one durable window per row (`di-monday` … `biweekly-content`).
4. Ledger/attribution: confirm the work seat rows are distinguishable in
   pico agentgateway logs (the `group`/`user` split from dotfiles-ogkz).

## Formal spec — the unit transformation
FROM (current, all seven):
    ExecStart=/bin/bash -c ". %h/.secrets; exec %h/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh \
        --loop %p --row di-monday --dir %h/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted --with-fleet-token --fresh"
TO (target shape, per the doc; the work-seat pinning is THIS spec addition):
    ExecStart=%h/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh \
        --loop %p --fresh --dir %h/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted \
        --session zig-computer --window di-monday --cmd "/pulse tick"
`--row` disappears — row selection becomes the day-guard already in pulse.md condition
column (`date +%u = 1`). The routing tables in each project refs/pulse.md DO NOT CHANGE.

## Test Cases
1. an empty `~/.claude-work` yields "Not logged in", not a silent fallback to the personal seat
2. after login, a tick under `--config-dir ~/.claude-work` reaches Anthropic (200, not 401)
3. the personal `~/.claude/.credentials.json` inode is UNCHANGED after a work-seat token refresh
4. a work-seat tick appears in pico gateway log distinguishably from a personal tick
5. `pulse-inject.sh` with no config-dir flag behaves exactly as today (no regression to dive/desk/dream)
6. the day-guard fires di-monday on Monday and NOT on Tuesday
7. a converted row creates its OWN window, not a shared `work:pulse` pane
8. the ledger row is written on zig-computer with the right loop id
9. `--fresh` still starts a clean context in the per-row window
10. rollback: restoring the remote ExecStart returns the row to the old path unchanged
11. a work-seat 401 fails LOUD (no silent fallback to the personal seat) — cf. dotfiles-ucl4
12. two rows firing near-simultaneously do not collide in the same window

## Open Questions
- OQ1: `--config-dir` flag on pulse-inject.sh, or `Environment=CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=` in the
  unit? The unit-level env is less code and self-documenting in `systemctl cat`; the flag
  is testable in the suite. LEAN: unit-level `Environment=`, plus a pulse-inject assertion
  that the dir exists and holds a credential, so a missing seat fails loudly at dispatch.
- OQ2: does the work seat need the gateway (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` -> pico :17017), or go
  direct? The gateway gives o11y; it is also a fleet-wide SPOF (dotfiles-ucl4 outcome:
  6.5h, claude dead everywhere). LEAN: gateway, consistent with every other row.
- OQ3: does `tick-jailed.sh` apply to these rows? They are LinearB work over trusted
  input, not web crawling — probably not, but the interaction with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
  matters if it ever does.
- OQ4: what happens to the work seat when the andrew account on marketing-vps is deleted —
  is the OAuth lineage tied to the box, the account, or only the Anthropic identity?
  MUST be answered before Phase 5.

## Future
Once all seven are converted, the conduit simplifies away: pulse-dispatch-remote.sh
(~2,300 lines) loses every caller, fleet-creds.sh brokering is unnecessary (a local tick
reads ~/.secrets directly), and the deferred-surface / surface_request round-trip is
deleted for these rows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OQ1-OQ4 answered (via /check) before any unit is edited
- [ ] the 12 cases above are executable tests
- [ ] the pilot row runs on the work seat and is PROVEN not to have used the personal seat
notes:
## DECISIONS (Zig, 2026-08-05)
- **Rollout**: pilot di-monday and FORCE-FIRE it manually (`systemctl --user start`),
  rather than waiting for its real Monday. Fast feedback chosen deliberately.
  ⚠️ Consequence I am carrying forward rather than burying: a manual fire does NOT
  exercise the day-guard or the timer path. Those stay a precondition for PHASE 2a
  specifically (the irreversible step), not for the pilot. Recorded on dotfiles-vwrw.
- **Routing**: through pico agentgateway, consistent with every other row (OQ2 ANSWERED).
  Accepts the pico-SPOF exposure that dotfiles-ucl4 outcome measured (6.5h fleet-wide).
- **End state**: emptied-but-present account, reversible. Full deletion not chosen, so
  OQ4 (what the OAuth lineage is tied to) drops from BLOCKING to worth-knowing.

## OQ1 — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, not preference (2026-08-05)
The lean was unit-level `Environment=CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=`. **That would silently fail.**

Measured on zig-computer, tmux 3.5a:

    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/PROBE tmux -L probe new-session -d -s t -n w "sleep 5"
    tmux -L probe show-environment -t t CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
      -> unknown variable: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR

The caller environment does NOT reach the tmux session. And it is worse than that:
`pulse-inject.sh:358` launches claude with **`send-keys "$LAUNCH" Enter`** — it TYPES the
command into a shell that already lives in the pane, so the launched process inherits the
**tmux server** environment, which was fixed whenever the server started. A unit-level
`Environment=` would be present in pulse-inject own env, never reach the pane, and the
tick would run on Zig PERSONAL seat with nothing erroring. Exactly the silent-success
shape this session has hit repeatedly.

So the seat must be passed EXPLICITLY. Two mechanisms, both available:
  - `new-session -e` / `new-window -e` (pulse-inject.sh:300 and :318) — sets it for panes
    created in that session/window
  - prefix the launch string itself, since the launch is a send-keys anyway

## A SECOND silent-failure mode, found in the same read
`pulse-inject.sh:331` checks `pane_current_command` and REUSES a live claude rather than
launching. So a `di-monday` window that already holds a personal-seat claude would be
reused and would serve the WRONG SEAT with no launch and no error. Setting the env at
launch time is therefore NOT sufficient — the guard must verify the RUNNING claude is on
the work seat, and fail loudly if not.

## Anchors for the implementation
    pulse-inject.sh:300  new-session -d -s "$SESSION" -c "$DIR"
    pulse-inject.sh:318  new-window  -d -P -F "#{window_id}" -t "=$SESSION" -n "$WINDOW" -c "$DIR"
    pulse-inject.sh:331  CURRENT_CMD=$(... pane_current_command)   <- the reuse path
    pulse-inject.sh:358  send-keys -t "$PANE" "$LAUNCH" Enter      <- the launch
Precedent: tick-jailed.sh:134 sets it via bwrap `--setenv` for the `dive` loop, and
`~/.claude-tick` is a live second OAuth lineage on this box today.

## SESSION DECIDED (Zig, 2026-08-05): `work`, NOT `zig-computer`

All seven rows land in the **`work`** session, one window per row:
`work:di-monday` … `work:di-friday`, `work:weekly-report`, `work:biweekly-content`.

This DIVERGES from the retreat doc example (`--session zig-computer`) and from every
native loop (dive/desk/dream/digest all use `--session zig-computer`). Zig call: these are
LinearB rows and he watches them in `work`, which is where their bells surface today via
the relay.

Consequences, verified 2026-08-05:
- **No relay.** They ring Zig DIRECTLY — running in his attached session means
  AskUserQuestion and the 🔔 glyph work natively. The surface_request round-trip exists only
  because a remote tick on an unattended box could not ring a bell.
- **`work:pulse` folds** once all seven are migrated. Verified safe: NO other unit targets
  `--window pulse`; the only other `work`-session loop is `pulse-elevate`, which uses its own
  `elevate` window. `work:🗼 vps` also becomes meaningless after the retreat.
- ⚠️ `--window pulse` remains pulse-inject BUILT-IN DEFAULT. Folding the window does not
  change the default; decide separately whether it should.
- ⚠️ `pulse-retry.sh` also consumes the surface-queue machinery, not just
  pulse-dispatch-remote.sh. Deleting the relay in Phase 7 must not amputate retry for loops
  that still use it. Recorded on dotfiles-35xo.

title: demesne-sync: post-prune the source dirs are gone — refusal is accidental, not designed
description:
## Context
Filed from dotfiles-dotfiles-public-prune-k579 (report-only per that dispatch; the
guard, if one is wanted, belongs in the private tier, which the prune agent may not
write).

`agents/scheduler/demesne-sync.sh` rsyncs SYNCED_DIRS=(agents refs claude zsh tmux)
one way, dotfiles -> demesne, each dir its own `rsync -a --delete`. After the prune,
three of those five no longer exist in the source.

MEASURED, with the script's own documented test seams and a THROWAWAY destination
(demesne itself never written), 2026-08-10:

  1. Real post-prune shape (agents/ survives on disk as gitignored debris —
     __pycache__, node_modules, .ruff_cache — while refs/ and claude/ vanish
     completely):

         ERROR: preflight failed: src-dir-missing:refs
         DEMESNE_SYNC_RESULT=ERROR reason=src-dir-missing:refs   exit=1
         DEMESNE_GATE_RESULT=ERROR reason=src-dir-missing:refs   exit=1
         dest files before=5 after=5

     Fails safe. Nothing is deleted; the rsync loop (lines 312-329) is never
     reached because preflight (lines 250-252) returns first from cmd_sync's
     guard at lines 285-291.

  2. THE COUNTERFACTUAL, same script, only difference being that all five dirs
     happen to exist in the source holding only debris:

         --- agents: 3 item(s) would change
         *deleting   lib/precious.sh
         --- refs: 2 item(s) would change
         *deleting   precious.md
         --- claude: 2 item(s) would change
         *deleting   settings.json
         DEMESNE_SYNC_RESULT=DRYRUN dirs=5 changed=27

     It would empty demesne's agents/, refs/ and claude/ into the shape of the
     pruned source.

So today's safety rests on WHICH directory disappears first, not on a rule about a
source that no longer holds a brain. `agents/` — the biggest of the three — already
fails to trip the check, because debris keeps the directory alive. One `mkdir refs`,
one stray tool, one partially-restored checkout is the difference. The dirty-dest
refusal does not cover this either: it only fires when demesne has uncommitted work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] demesne-sync refuses on a source that does not hold a TIER, tested by content
      (the same marker test sync.sh and bootstrap-agents.sh use — e.g.
      $SRC/agents/AGENTS.md), not by directory existence
- [ ] The refusal is REFUSED (exit 2), not ERROR (exit 1) — a caller must be able to
      tell "correctly declined" from "broken"
- [ ] A test case in agents/scheduler/test-demesne-sync.sh drives the empty/debris
      source and asserts nothing is deleted, so the counterfactual above cannot
      become live silently
- [ ] OR: the script is retired with a note saying so, if the cutover means dotfiles
      is no longer a source at all — an equally good answer, but recorded either way

title: fix: zig-watchdog probes can race kanban dispatcher writes (SQLite corruption risk)
description:
## Problem

Kanban DB at /home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban.db corrupted ~04:53 UTC during this
session ("sqlite refused to open file: database disk image is malformed").
Hermes auto-created 6+ .corrupt.bak files in 30 seconds (same image, sequential
timestamps — the corruption was already present at first backup). `.recover`
yielded schema only (0 INSERT statements) — data unrecoverable. All task
history lost: t_360fa078, t_2d3dcc3e (weekly-reporting), t_093c0add, etc.

## Symptom

`hermes kanban list` (or any kanban CLI) → "Refusing to open corrupt kanban
DB". Gateway log: "kanban dispatcher: board default database ... is not a
valid SQLite database; disabling dispatch for this board". User-facing impact:
Phase 2 substrate down; cross-arc kanban workloads stop dispatching.

## Likely cause

Concurrent writers on a single SQLite file with insufficient coordination:
- gateway-embedded dispatcher tick-loop (every 60s)
- watchdog systemd-timer tick (every 5min), which calls
  `hermes kanban dispatch --dry-run`, `hermes kanban diagnostics --json`,
  `hermes kanban show <tid>` (added in bd-cke fix) per actionable crash-loop
- ad-hoc CLI calls (this session: dispatch / show / block / unblock during
  debugging)
- worker subprocess spawn-crash cycles re-claiming + writing event rows

SQLite WAL mode handles concurrent readers + 1 writer, but multiple
fork/exec processes coordinating via WAL/SHM mmap with stale snapshot reads
can desync. The dispatcher's stuck-FD pattern documented earlier this
session was a symptom of similar pressure.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not deterministically reproducible yet. Best evidence:
1. Long-running hermes gateway (3+ hours)
2. Run zig-watchdog systemd timer firing every 5min on the same kanban DB
3. Add ad-hoc kanban CLI calls during a worker crash-loop scenario
4. After ~30min of mixed activity: `database disk image is malformed`

## Fix (proposed)

Three layers of defense:

### F1 — Watchdog write-coordination
Either (a) skip kanban probes when a dispatcher tick is mid-flight (filelock
on ~/.hermes/.dispatcher-tick.lock), OR (b) increase watchdog interval to
10min (less frequent racing), OR (c) make watchdog probes read-only via
sqlite3 directly with `?mode=ro&immutable=1` URI rather than spawning hermes
CLI subprocesses that may open WAL writers.

### F2 — Backup discipline
The corruption was already present in the FIRST .corrupt.bak. Hermes should
maintain a rolling daily-good snapshot (`kanban.db.daily.bak`) created via
`sqlite3 source ".backup target"` (atomic) rather than just preserving the
corrupt file. The watchdog could own this.

### F3 — Don't issue manual CLI calls while dispatcher is hot
Operational discipline: when investigating, query state via sqlite3 in
read-only mode rather than spawning more hermes CLI processes that contend.

## Source of Report

Empirical observation 2026-05-28 ~04:53 UTC during the dotfiles-cke fix
verification: t_360fa078 worker spawned (PID-tracked), watchdog probe ran a
new kanban-show call, gateway dispatcher continued its 60s tick — within
2 minutes the DB was malformed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] F1 implemented (one of a/b/c) with test
- [ ] F2 implemented + scheduled (daily good-state snapshot)
- [ ] F3 documented in ~/dotfiles/local-models/GUARDRAILS.md as a new G-entry
- [ ] Reproduction recipe captured (or marked as "could not reproduce")
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-ns3 in commit trailer

 - [ ] Bead: dotfiles-ns3 in commit trailer

Phase C-lite stripped that probe entirely; watchdog no longer touches kanban.db. No outside writer = no race. F1/F2/F3 defenses no longer needed.

title: mail: an injected nudge is indistinguishable from a turn typed by Zig
description:
## Context
`pulse-inject.sh` send-keys its `--cmd` into the pane as a REAL USER TURN — a
property `AGENTS.md` calls load-bearing, and it is, for /pulse. But it means any
agent-to-agent nudge arrives wearing Zig's voice. The harness's own rule is that
no agent message is ever the user's consent or approval; a nudge that renders as
a user turn breaks that at the transport layer, BEFORE any messaging feature
ships. Present today, not introduced by this epic.

identifying the sending agent and stating that it is not Zig. `/pulse`'s own
ticks are unaffected — they are the scheduler acting for Zig.

      indication another agent sent it

- [ ] The receiving agent treats enveloped text as an agent message, not as Zig
- [ ] `/pulse` tick injection is unchanged (no envelope, no regression)
- [ ] Verified by injecting an enveloped instruction that the receiver should
      decline, and observing it decline

title: seat-molt: R14 leaks a cross-server pane id — invoker's TMUX_PANE rides to a child targeting a different socket
description:
## Context
Found by the demesne pre-flip commit gate 2026-08-09: test-seat-molt.sh failed 23b2/23b3 in BOTH trees while the same suite passed at pcp8's commit an hour earlier. Root cause: R14 (pcp8) passes the invoker's $TMUX_PANE to the molt child unconditionally, but a tmux pane id is only meaningful on the server that issued it. When the child targets a DIFFERENT socket (the suite's fake server; any cross-server invocation), a colliding id there resolves to an unrelated pane and send-keys types /clear + /onboard into it. Green-vs-red depended on pane-id luck: the fixing session's pane was %344 (no collision on the fake server → green); this session's pane is %3 (collides → red).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a tmux session whose $TMUX_PANE has a small id (e.g. %3), run: bash agents/scheduler/test-seat-molt.sh (pre-fix HEAD)
2. Observe 23b2/23b3 fail — the fake server owns a %3 and the keystrokes landed in the wrong fixture pane.
3. Deterministic: case 23e passes a victim pane's real id as TMUX_PANE with $TMUX naming a different server — pre-fix, the victim's typed-capture contains /clear (23e3 red).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Fix: pane passthrough gated on server identity — only when ${TMUX%%,*} == resolved target SOCKET (production --self derives SOCKET from $TMUX, so the R14 split-window fix is preserved exactly where the id is provably valid)
- [x] Guard: deterministic regression case 23e/23e2/23e3 (victim-pane collision) — red pre-fix (4/56), green post-fix (56/56), demonstrated both directions 2026-08-09
close_reason: Fixed in the same session that found it (R14b block in seat-molt.sh --self). Evidence: pre-fix script = 4/56 red (23b2/23b3 environment-dependent + 23e2/23e3 deterministic — victim pane's typed-capture contains /clear); fixed = 56/56 green. Both runs on this box, file-swap method (git show HEAD: vs fixed copy), no stash/checkout verbs. ## Guard — agents/scheduler/test-seat-molt.sh:23e/23e2/23e3 (deterministic cross-server collision case). Production behavior preserved: --self without --socket resolves SOCKET from $TMUX so equality holds and the R14 split-window passthrough still works; only cross-server invocations (tests, exotic operator calls) lose the pane hint and fall back to window-name resolution, which is the pre-R14 path.

title: harness: shell cwd resets to anchor repo between Bash calls — AGENTS.md standalone-cd merge precondition cannot persist

title: seat-molt: a refusal has NO consumer — refused-not-offboarded leaves the seat wedged at 100% context, silently, indefinitely
description:
## Context
Zig's question 2026-08-09 ('why did the dream session hang and never molt, and why is its context 100% full?') — diagnosed live by the Works seat. The dream tick ran clean (fleet debut, ledger 12:31:32Z, pushed 95e3cc5, scoped handoff note written), then held an interactive walkthrough with Zig and ended its turn announcing 'the molt is armed and will fire when this turn ends.' seat-molt fired at 15:11:51Z and REFUSED: refused-not-offboarded (the post-tick walkthrough made the offboard marker stale — the guard itself judged correctly). The refusal then went NOWHERE: the session's turn was over so it never saw it, nothing retried, nothing escalated, and the seat sat wedged at 100% context for 3+ hours with a ✅ glyph — a lying-✅ (looks idle-and-fine, is actually unable to take its next tick usefully). Recovered manually: verified everything pushed + note durable, /clear'd the pane, 0%.

THE CLASS, third instance today at the same seam: (1) marshal 16:45:59Z refused-not-offboarded while its drain-ledger row claimed 'compacting, handles preserved' (dotfiles-betl defect B — premature claim); (2) hardening's t5fj scrutiny found the lying-🧠 shape; (3) this lying-✅ wedge. AGENTS.md's it06 doctrine says 'a failed/refused molt (twice) is the only context event that summons Zig' — but NOTHING COUNTS REFUSALS; the summon rule has no mechanical arm. The molt-ledger records every refusal and has no reader.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Let a seat end a turn with work after its last offboard (any interactive follow-up after a tick's offboard does it).
2. Arm/fire seat-molt for that seat (mode molt or compact).
3. Observe molt-ledger result refused-not-offboarded; the seat's pane is unchanged, glyph ✅/🧠, no retry, no notification, no escalation. At high context the seat is now wedged until a human notices (dream: 100%, 3+ hours, found only because Zig asked).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A refusal gets a consumer. Preferred shape (coordinate with the hardening lane — pulse-escalate already owns glyph reconciliation and is mid-extension for lying-🧠/🌀): escalate's tick also reads molt-ledger tails for refused-* rows on conf-listed seats; a refusal older than a grace window triggers the ladder — first move: re-run the molt with the missing precondition satisfied (offboard-then-molt for refused-not-offboarded), else climb (supervisor -> seneschal -> P1 human: bead + push).
- [ ] The it06 'refused twice summons Zig' rule gains its mechanical arm: two refused-* rows for the same seat within the window = the summon path fires (bead + push), never silence.
- [ ] The armed-molt announcer ('molt will fire when this turn ends') either verifies the fire or stops promising: whatever arms the molt must check the molt-ledger result and, on refusal, say so IN THE PANE (a visible line) so an idle seat's transcript never claims a molt that was refused.
- [ ] Regression evidence: reproduce the dream shape (post-offboard turn -> refused molt) and demonstrate detection + recovery end-to-end, failure-before/absence-after.
- [ ] Cross-references recorded on dotfiles-betl (premature-claim half), the t5fj/escalate lying-glyph work, and 40ej (the recovery-charter family).

Recorder: every refused/failed seat-molt path writes a reason-carrying ledger row (two paths previously exited PAST the ledger — fixed; EXIT trap catches unhandled deaths; row and log line derive from one source). Consumer: second two-rung ladder in pulse-escalate's tick — first refusal of an episode NOTEs, second within molt_refusal_window_minutes (90m) files a P1 human: bead AND pushes Zig (it06's summon implemented mechanically); idempotent per episode; fleet-wide (running seat-molt IS the opt-in); aborted-modal excluded. Adversarial review: FIX-FIRST (tab-collapse field shift — null-pct rows mangled the summon's context number) → fixed via row_fields() parameter-expansion split → focused re-verify SHIP incl. degenerate shapes + embedded-tab guarantee traced to the flattener. Suites 69/69 + 45/45; 11/11 mutants killed on named cases; five reviewer residues documented in-file as accepted bounds. Merged 21ad7b8 under the guarded sequence, suites re-verified on main, carried to demesne 0ef9183 (gate green with the structural gu0o fix — zsh/tmux joined the sync set so the gate self-verifies), byte-identity verified recursively. title: gateway-switch.sh — one-command per-host kill switch for the pico agentgateway (off|on|status)
description:
WHY
On 2026-08-04 pico lost internet for ~6.5h. Routing is fail-hard with no fallback
(dotfiles-ucl4), so claude died fleet-wide, and flipping the fleet off the gateway took
~15 manual steps across two hosts plus a per-pane fix (dotfiles-9o46). Zig asked for a
real kill switch: one command, symmetric across zig-computer and marketing-vps, easy to
flip on and off.

DELIVERABLE
  agents/scheduler/gateway-switch.sh {off|on|status}
  agents/scheduler/test-gateway-switch.sh
  a short runbook section in agents/infra.md pointing at the script

BEHAVIOUR
`off` — bypass the gateway, talk to api.anthropic.com directly:
  1. comment the `export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=...` line in $HOME/.$(hostname -s).zshenv
  2. if a claude-gateway-tunnel.timer unit EXISTS on this host, `disable --now` it
  3. for every tmux pane whose pane_current_command is zsh or bash, send
     `unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
  4. REPORT (do not touch) every pane holding a running claude/bwrap, since those need
     a manual restart
`on` — restore gateway routing: the same three steps inverted (uncomment; `enable --now`
the timer if the unit exists; `exec zsh` in shell panes -- which is sufficient in THIS
direction because there is nothing left to inherit), then verify.
`status` — report, without changing anything: the file's state and value, the timer state
if the unit exists, the live probe result, and every running claude process with its
actual routing read from /proc/<pid>/environ.

HARD REQUIREMENTS (each one is a real defect paid for already)
 A. THE SYMLINK MUST SURVIVE. $HOME/.<host>.zshenv is a symlink into ~/dotfiles. GNU
    `sed -i` WITHOUT --follow-symlinks replaces it with a regular file and silently
    detaches the host from the repo. Assert the path is still a symlink after every
    write, and cover it with a test.
 B. NEVER send keys to a pane that is not at a shell prompt. Typing into a live claude
    submits a prompt. Gate on pane_current_command and skip anything else. Today an
    input box already held unsent text in 2 of 5 panes.
 C. IDEMPOTENT. `off` twice, or `off` on an already-bypassed host, must be a clean no-op,
    not a double-comment (`## export`) that `on` cannot reverse. Test both directions
    twice in a row.
 D. Do NOT hardcode hostnames for the tunnel step. Key on whether the unit exists, so
    the script is correct on any host including ones that do not exist yet.
 E. Refuse, with a non-zero exit and a message naming the path, if there is no per-host
    zshenv or no export line to act on. Silence is the failure mode to avoid.
 F. No blanket `2>/dev/null` on state-changing or output-bearing commands (repo rule 3).
 G. `status` must be CHEAP -- no LLM calls. Put the real end-to-end request check behind
    an explicit opt-in flag, and when it runs it MUST use `env -u CC_NO_GATEWAY`,
    because a session started with the hatch exports it, every spawned shell inherits
    it, and the request then goes direct while looking like a passing gateway test
    (this exact false pass happened today).

VERIFICATION EXPECTED IN THE REPORT
Run the suite and paste real output. Demonstrate A and C by showing the failure BEFORE
and its absence AFTER (repo rule 1: a fix you cannot demonstrate is a fix you should not
claim). Run `status` on the real host and paste it. Do NOT run `off` against the live
fleet as a test -- use a fixture/fake HOME.

OUT OF SCOPE -- file a bead, do not build
  - restarting live claude sessions automatically (destroys context; Zig's call)
  - any fleet-wide/multi-host driver (rejected: it needs ssh from the box you are on,
    which is the least reliable thing during the outage it exists for)
  - metis (Zig explicitly excluded it; the script will work there generically anyway)
  - reworking the fail-hard no-fallback policy itself (dotfiles-ucl4 is deliberate)
notes:
## Scrutiny — 2026-08-04
Verdict: FIX-FIRST -> addressed -> SHIP

Independent read-only reviewer, dispatched pre-merge. It reproduced 42/42, spot-checked two
of the author's mutants with the mutation asserted applied, and confirmed all seven hard
requirements. It returned FIX-FIRST on one blocker; that blocker and two other findings were
fixed and re-verified before merge, hence SHIP.

  1 BLOCKER (fixed) — `on` un-commented ANY comment containing `export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=`.
    A commented-out example line ended an off/on cycle with TWO active exports, and the
    post-write check passed silently; a prose comment mentioning the variable was rewritten
    into syntax garbage. `zsh -n` ACCEPTS that garbage line — sourcing it fails with
    `no such file or directory: url`, rc 1, on every `ssh host cmd`, i.e. it would have
    broken remote pulse dispatch. Fixed by anchoring `on` to the script's own marker
    (`#gateway-switch:off# `), plus a distinct exit 67 that REFUSES and names the line when
    the only bypassed export was hand-commented, rather than guessing whose comment it is.
  2 (fixed) — no rollback if the post-write invariant failed, leaving a mangled file that
    every shell sources. `cat >` retained deliberately (an `mv` would destroy the symlink,

title: test-pre-commit-checks case 22 is load-sensitive and now gates commits — it can flake-block a commit that is fine
description:
## Context

`dotfiles-jm1c` gave the 32 suites a runner (`tools/githooks/pre-commit` +
`core.hooksPath`). That is the right fix, and it has a side effect worth tracking: a
flaky suite is no longer merely noisy, it **blocks commits**.

`agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` case 22
(`block: slow proof times out inside the budget`) sets
`HARNESS_PULSE_PROOF_BUDGET=1`. Under load the hook burns more than 1s on `jq`/`git`
before it ever reaches the proof, so it emits the **budget-exhausted** message instead of
the **timeout** message and the case fails on `stderr missing: timed out after 1s`.

Measured by the agent that shipped the runner: green 3/3 standalone; fails under a mutant
run at load ~10.5, where it appeared as an over-broad neighbour and had to be diagnosed
before the real mutant result could be trusted.

**Pre-existing, not introduced by the runner** — but the runner is what makes it cost
something.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the box (several concurrent agents, load avg ~10).
2. `bash agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh`
3. Case 22 fails with `stderr missing: timed out after 1s`; the hook emitted the
   budget-exhausted message instead.
4. Re-run on a quiet box → passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 22 is deterministic under load. Two candidate fixes, and this is a judgment
      call: raise `HARNESS_PULSE_PROOF_BUDGET` so the fixed overhead cannot consume it, or
      accept **either** message via a `want_stderr` alternation.
- [ ] State which and why. Accepting both messages tests less; raising the budget makes
      the case slower. Neither is obviously right.
- [ ] Whatever ships, demonstrate it under load — a fix verified only on a quiet box has
      not been verified against the condition that breaks it.

Related: `dotfiles-jm1c` (the runner that raised the stakes), `dotfiles-b9ii` (which added
cases 20-23).
notes:
## Resolution — 2026-08-01 (AC #2: which fix, and why)

Written by the orchestrator; the agent correctly declined to `br update` a bead it did not
create, and left the full rationale in commit `d3df42f` and a 25-line comment above case 22.

### The orchestrator's lean was HALF WRONG, and the measurement is the finding

I briefed "raise the budget, don't accept both messages," reasoning that an alternation
would leave the case unable to tell the two code paths apart. The agent tested it instead
of adopting it and found **two independent defects**, only one of which the bead knew about:

1. The budget is too small under load (the known half).
2. **The assertion pins an exact second count.** The hook prints
   `timed out after ${PROOF_LEFT}s` where `PROOF_LEFT = budget - elapsed`, so raising the
   budget merely *relabels* the flake. Measured at `budget=5`, asserting
   `"timed out after 5s"`: **2/20 red at load 47**, reporting `after 4s`.

So raise-only — my lean — does not fix it. Nobody had noticed defect 2.

### What shipped: both halves

- **Derived budget, not a constant** (the "third option" the brief asked to look for). The
  case runs the hook once with a `cmd: "true"` proof, measures overhead in the same whole
  seconds the hook's own `date +%s` arithmetic uses, and sets
  `SLOW_BUDGET = 2*overhead + 3`. Quiet box → 3; it scales with the box.
- **Assert the phrase `"timed out after "`, not the number.**

### The alternation objection does NOT apply — verified independently

This is the part worth recording, because it is the difference between this fix and the
weaker option the bead offered. Asserting the phrase is **branch-unique**, checked against
the hook source by the orchestrator rather than accepted on report:

    pre-commit-checks.sh:384  (budget exhausted) "... ran out before verifying: ..."
    pre-commit-checks.sh:400  (real timeout)     "  timed out after ${PROOF_LEFT}s ..."

Disjoint strings. A hook that never reaches the proof still goes **red**, so the case
tests exactly what it always tested; only the volatile integer left the assertion. Case 23
was untouched — it is inherently robust because both its paths emit `proof budget`, which
is why 22 was the only flaker.

### Evidence (AC #3 — demonstrated under load, not on a quiet box)

12 cores, synthetic load via 36 `yes` processes.

    baseline flake, full suite      load 28-43   1/10 suites RED
    baseline flake, isolated x30    load 44      4/30 RED
    naive raise-only (my lean)      load 47      2/20 RED  <- disproof
    fix, isolated x20               load 49      20/20 green
    fix, full suite x20             load 52      20/20 green, rc=0
    fix, full suite x8, idle        load 2.9     8/8 green

**Positive control** — mutated a *copy* of `agents/hooks/` (shared checkout untouched):
deleting the `PROOF_RC -eq 124` diagnostic block, and `timeout "$PROOF_LEFT"` → `timeout 60`.
Both make case 22 **fail, and only case 22**. The case can still go red.

**Independent re-verification by the orchestrator**, load avg 1.93:
`bash agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` → **PASS: 69/69, exit 0**.

### Cost + follow-up

Suite 7.6s → 8.8s idle (one extra hook invocation for the probe). No hook change was
needed; `pre-commit-checks.sh` is untouched. No other case flaked across 38 loaded runs.

Filed `dotfiles-wuze` (P3): the mutation-harness commit gate takes **4m24s at load 55**,
not the `~90s` its own comment and user-facing message advertise, with no intermediate
output — a multi-minute silent wait during `git commit` that reads as a hang.
close_reason: done
