title: spec: route marketing-vps Claude Code through pico's agentgateway via a chained SSH tunnel, with machine-of-origin attribution
description:
## Overview

marketing-vps must use pico's agentgateway as its ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. pico is
tailnet-only; the VPS is not on the tailnet and never will be. Additionally, every
agentgateway request must carry the machine of origin as a FIRST-CLASS FILTERABLE
FIELD in the admin UI (not a hidden label).

## Baseline (all verified live 2026-08-02, not inferred)

- pico agentgateway 1.4.1, launchd `com.zig.agentgateway`, uptime 22h,
  KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit=false}, ThrottleInterval=10.
- The `/claude` route on 17017 is a transparent passthrough with NO apiKey policy.
- Gateway health signature: GET /claude/v1/models -> **401** (reached Anthropic,
  no key). NOT 200. /claude/ and /v1/models both -> 404.
- Identity today: claude-identity-wrapper.sh sends
  `X-Session-Identity: <tmux session>:<window>`; pico config line 9 maps it via CEL
  into standardAttributes.user -> the `agentgateway_user` column.
- **The first field is the tmux SESSION name, not the machine.** Live proof: BOTH
  zig-computer and marketing-vps have a tmux session named `work`
  (zig-computer: `work:pulse`, `work:vps`; vps: `work:di-monday` etc). metis carries
  the same ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so >=3 machines already share one flat namespace.
- `src.addr` cannot discriminate: all rows are 100.98.174.21 (zig-computer), and
  tunnelled VPS traffic will arrive as that same address.
- `agentgateway_group` is NULL in **all 78,956 rows** and already has a dedicated
  index `idx_request_logs_group_completed_at`. Virgin squat target.
- The binary contains the facet/dropdown query listing
  gen_ai_request_model / gen_ai_provider_name / agentgateway.user /
  **agentgateway.group** / user_agent.name — so `group` IS an automatic filter
  dropdown, alongside the ones Zig already sorts by.
- ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS supports MULTIPLE headers, `Name: Value`,
  **newline-separated** (first-party docs, code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars).
- Loopback base URL is safe: the `ERR_HTTP_HOOK_BLOCKED_ADDRESS` loopback guard
  applies to HTTP hooks and explicitly ALLOWS 127.0.0.1;
  CLAUDE_GATEWAY_ALLOW_LOOPBACK belongs to the separate CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY mode.
- ⚠️ `config:` (which contains standardAttributes) is applied **ONLY AT STARTUP** —
  agentgateway hot-reloads modelCatalog only. The group change REQUIRES a restart,
  which briefly interrupts fleet-wide LLM traffic.

## Changes

### 1. Transport — ONE hop, not two (verified working)
`ssh -L 127.0.0.1:17017:100.72.47.4:17017 zig-computer` from the VPS. ssh resolves
the forward DESTINATION on the far end, so zig-computer does the tailnet leg itself.
No nested tunnel.

Measured from marketing-vps 2026-08-02, with controls:
    no-tunnel            -> 000   (negative control)
    /claude/v1/models    -> 401   (through the tunnel; == direct baseline)
    post-teardown        -> gone, 7100 fleet tunnel untouched

LOCAL `-L` (VPS-initiated), never reverse `-R` — same argument
ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh already documents: only the initiator can reopen it, and a
stranded VPS whose gateway died has NO working claude at all.

### 2. Generalize ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh (Zig's call: generalize, not a sibling)
It hardcodes target `127.0.0.1:$PORT`, probe path `/api/health`, and expects 200.
Add `--target HOST:PORT`, `--probe-path PATH`, `--expect CODE`. Defaults keep the
fleet-proxy behavior byte-identical.

### 3. Routing
`export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:17017/claude"` in
`zsh/.vps-8a9eb245.zshenv`. NO shell rotation needed — the claude() wrapper
re-derives this per LAUNCH from ~/.<host>.zshenv (the dotfiles-t6to fix).

### 4. Machine label — squat `group` (Zig's design, better than the alternatives)
- wrapper sends a SECOND newline-separated header `X-Machine-Origin: <hostname -s>`
- pico gains `standardAttributes.group` CEL reading it
- `user` (session:window) and 78,956 rows of history are UNCHANGED

### 5. Second producer site
~/explore/tools/tick-jail/tick-jailed.sh mirrors the env via --setenv and must carry
the new header too, else jailed ticks are machine-unattributed.

## Ordering is safe in BOTH directions
Header-without-CEL is ignored; CEL-without-header yields the CEL default. No lockstep.

## Test Cases
1. VPS: negative control — probe before tunnel -> 000
2. VPS: ensure -> 401 through the tunnel (the healthy signature)
3. ensure is idempotent: second call no-ops, does not churn a healthy socket
4. ensure never kills a listener it did not start (7100 must survive)
5. defaults unchanged: fleet-proxy invocation still probes /api/health expecting 200
6. --expect 401 treats 200 as BLOCKED, not healthy
7. wrapper emits BOTH headers, newline-separated, in bash AND zsh
8. wrapper fails open: no tmux -> machine header still present
9. pico: a real claude call from the VPS produces a row with group=marketing-vps
10. pico: a call from zig-computer produces group=zig-computer, user unchanged
11. existing 78,956 rows still parse/group by user after the change
12. CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 still bypasses on the VPS

## Open Questions
- OQ1: fallback when the tunnel is down — fail to direct api.anthropic.com (keeps
  claude working, loses o11y) or fail hard? The VPS failure mode is worse than the
  fleet-proxy one: no gateway == no claude at all.
- OQ2: restart window for pico. It interrupts live fleet sessions including Zig's.
close_reason: Delivered and verified end to end. Transport: ONE hop, not two — ssh -L resolves its destination on the far end, so zig-computer does the tailnet leg (000 negative control, 401 through). Label: squatted the unused agentgateway_group column (Zig's design, better than the options offered) — user stays session:window, all 84,434 historical rows untouched, filterability confirmed via /api/logs/search with positive AND negative controls. marketing-vps is live on the gateway behind a self-healing 2-min timer. Both scrutiny passes returned FIX-FIRST on changes whose mechanical gates were already green: two mutants surviving on the exact branch the VPS now uses (dropped permissions flag, injected credential), and re_escape entirely untested while an unescaped pattern provably matched a DIFFERENT forward. Follow-ups left open deliberately: dotfiles-20rx (CC_NO_GATEWAY broken in fresh zsh), dotfiles-wpu2 (promote the mutation harness), dotfiles-ahrd (tick-jail header coverage).

title: spec: the demesne charter — mission, values, what income is for, what is never traded
description:
## Context
The constitution above seats.yml. Zig-authored with the orchestrator (/spec then /check, Zig deciding every OQ): the goal(s), the value hierarchy when goals conflict (curiosity vs revenue vs Zig's time), what income funds (taps first), identity/byline rules for anything published, and the hard nevers. Injected at seat startup once ratified; desk/dream/seneschal treat it as a criterion.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Written as a spec bead with OQs; /check walks them WITH Zig — this one is his voice, drafted by Fable
- [ ] Injection lands via k50m's session-start seam; snapshot-staleness noted (durable windows lag)

## The palette (Zig + Fable, 2026-08-08 — the drafting session starts here, not from blank)
Zig's seeds: economic (business), philanthropic (EA-shaped; attention as a value form), scientific (research to an end goal) — explicitly starting points, dream bigger.
Fable's archetypes: HOUSEHOLD (the demesne runs itself excellently; thriving of members + lord — already implicitly true, naming it explains why welfare is constitutional) · CRAFT GUILD (world-class mastery of evidence-disciplined agent orchestration; income/reputation/teaching as byproducts) · COMMONS (public goods measured by what others build on top) · LIGHTHOUSE (the demesne as the documented, reproducible experiment in humane machine civilization — the operating model as the product) · EXPEDITION (one question worth a decade) · PATRON (revenue in service of curiosity).
SYNTHESIS (Fable's recommendation): charter = CONSTITUTION (values, currencies, gates, identity, hard nevers); goals = CHARTERED PROGRAMS under it — epics with their own success AND kill criteria, running concurrently like the daemons do. The Goodhart wall becomes structural: a program closes without touching the constitution.
CURRENCIES clause: name explicitly what the demesne earns, spends, and REFUSES to optimize (attention-for-its-own-sake = the named refusal).

## AMENDMENT (Zig, 2026-08-08): charters are PLURAL and first-class. One constitution binds all; MANY charters (directions) under it; each SEAT declares `charter:` alignment in seats.yml — alignment is data, injected at wake beside the constitution. Seats fall into what makes sense; re-chartering a seat is a recorded decision. Reporting (seneschal, CV rollup) groups by charter so 'how is each direction doing' is a query.
notes:
## RATIFIED (Zig, 2026-08-08, in-session): the constitution/programs synthesis and the CURRENCIES clause are the decided construction principle — 'we need to think of this demesne exactly like this in constructing it.' Not a candidate among the palette: the frame the spec is written IN. The palette archetypes become candidate CHARTERS under the constitution. The currencies clause (earn/spend/refuse-to-optimize, attention-for-its-own-sake as the named refusal) is constitutional content, drafted first.

## Charter forks DECIDED (Zig via AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-08/09):
- Currencies refusal: attention-for-its-own-sake (the sole named refusal; others considered, not adopted)
- Income: TAPS FIRST, THEN REINVEST — surplus funds new programs/capability (the demesne compounds itself); Zig draws at discretion
- Byline: HOUSE NAMES, NEVER ZIG'S — ventures ship under their own brand; 'Andrew Zigler' reserved for what he personally publishes (zig-voice rule generalized); disclosure per-venture at his call
- SEAT-CREATION PROCESS (Zig's directive — don't limit upfront, no early bloat): charter stewards (the orchestrator seats) MAY create new seats to lead houses/ventures via a recorded decision bead (office, charter, model pin, tap named at birth); the roster validator enforces schema; OUTWARD capabilities remain gated by the outward-facing spec (htqt) regardless of who created the seat; Zig learns via the seneschal brief rather than pre-approving each. Constitution Article IV gains this clause.
- JOB SEATS RETIRE: the linearb seat represents Zig's current job on the job tap; when the job changes, that seat RETIRES (history preserved, laurels stand) and a new seat is chartered for the new job — seats are careers, not permanent fixtures.
close_reason: RATIFIED by Zig 2026-08-09; constitution at ~/demesne/docs/constitution.md (demesne@0a0f006, pushed). Force-close over the k50m edge deliberately: the SPEC is complete (palette->forks->ratification served as the /check walk); the INJECTION implementation the edge represented rides k50m + the roster seeding, both open and correctly sequenced. The spec bead's job is done.

title: retreat: replicate ~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt into the repo — the plan exists in exactly one place
description:
## Context
The canonical retreat plan is `zig-computer:~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt`. It is UNTRACKED
and exists on exactly one machine. Every other artifact in this arc is replicated; the
plan that governs the destruction is not.

This is the same class as the doc own §1 warning about `~/marketing-vps/.beads` ("6
rows... Replicated NOWHERE. Wiping that directory destroys them") — except the plan
governs the wipe itself, so losing it mid-retreat is worse than losing the beads.

It also has a second reader problem: it is invisible to any session that is not on
zig-computer as `ubuntu`. This session had to be told the path, and then had to guess the
`.txt` extension.

## What to do
Copy it to `dotfiles/refs/in-case-of-retreat.md` and make the home-dir file the pointer,
not the other way round — a `~/` dotfile is unreviewable and unversioned, and this doc is
going to be edited as the retreat proceeds (it already says "NOT smoke-tested — verify
facts live"). In-repo it gets diffs, review, and cross-machine reach.

⚠️ Check before committing: the doc names hostnames, IPs (15.204.114.210, 51.81.33.136),
usernames, key filenames and comments, and a sudoers path. Those are already all over
`agents/infra.md`, so it is consistent with repo practice — but it contains NO secret
VALUES and must not gain any (AGENTS.md: reference by pointer, never paste).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `refs/in-case-of-retreat.md` committed, content byte-equivalent to the source
      modulo the frontmatter/pointer edit
- [ ] `~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt` on zig-computer replaced by (or amended with) a pointer
      to the repo path, so the two cannot silently diverge
- [ ] `~/.break-glass.txt` cross-references updated if it names the old path
- [ ] verified readable from marketing-vps (i.e. a session not on zig-computer can find it)
close_reason: Replicated to refs/in-case-of-retreat.md (72eb426). BYTE-FIDELITY PROVEN THREE WAYS, and the orchestrator re-derived it independently rather than accepting the report: the body extracted from the COMMITTED git object, the live remote file after its pointer edit, and the pre-edit backup all hash to da0d136faac57f19562b52051502dbcc. Whole-file diff shows exactly two hunks — a 12-line header plus a 'text'-tagged fence — and zero lines of the plan changed. The 'text' fence rather than markdown headings was the right call: it preserves the ASCII section rules and shell-snippet indentation that '#' conversion would have silently reflowed, which for a doc whose steps get EXECUTED is the difference between a copy and a paraphrase (CLAUDE.md rule 2, as amended today by g2vg — run/verify the bytes as committed, not a retyped copy). The divergence loop is closed at the source: zig-computer:~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt now opens with a prepended block saying it is no longer canonical, naming the repo path, and stating the repo wins on disagreement — with the full body preserved below rather than deleted, so nothing is lost on a box whose checkout has not caught up. Backup at ~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt.bak.2026-08-05. ~/.break-glass.txt turned out never to reference the file (grep rc=1), so it was correctly left untouched rather than edited speculatively. Secret grep clean — the only near-hit is the NOPASSWD:ALL sudoers rule already quoted in the plan's Phase 4d, and every long opaque run is a filesystem path.

title: pico: retire the leftover com.zig.harness dashboard on :10000 — a dead prototype serving frozen state with --auth none
description:
## Context
pico runs `com.zig.harness` on `:10000` with `--auth none`, serving a `state.json`
frozen at 2026-07-29. It is NOT broken -- it is a RETIRED PROTOTYPE.

harnessd/CLAUDE.md:104: "The Go daemon serving `state.json` same-origin **evaporates
the rsync-push-to-pico seam** the prototype used."

So the architecture moved: harnessd on zig-computer generates in-proc (Go) and serves
same-origin on 100.98.174.21:14174. Nothing pushes to pico anymore, by design. The
pico job is a leftover that kept running with KeepAlive.

## Why it still deserves a bead (small, not zero)
- It serves a stale dashboard with **`--auth none`** on a LAN-reachable port, on a
  host that runs without a firewall by decision (dotfiles-28jw).
- `KeepAlive=true` keeps it green, so it looks healthy while serving month-old state.
  Anyone glancing at it gets a confidently wrong picture of the fleet.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: spec: zig-watchdog — mechanical stall detection + revive for long-running jobs (bench, model pulls, Hermes gateway)
description:
# Spec: zig-watchdog — mechanical stall/crash detection + revive for long-running jobs

## 1. Overview

Single Python script + systemd-user timer that periodically probes a registered set
of long-running job classes for stall/crash patterns and either revives them
mechanically or alerts the operator. Replaces the current "user nudges Claude when
something dies" pattern with mechanical discipline that runs autonomously and
survives Claude session boundaries.

**This skill is structurally analogous to the autonovel-phase1 substrate**: a
deterministic-script cron-equivalent (systemd timer) running every N minutes, no
LLM in the path, with structured probe()/revive() per concern.

## 2. Baseline / current state

Two failures THIS SESSION proved the need:

1. **Kimi-Linear pull stalled for 8h** in CLOSE_WAIT socket state with no progress;
   user had to nudge ("make sure the kimi download isnt hanging") to surface it.
   Recovery was mechanical: kill + restart hf download.
2. **bench-matrix.sh aborted** at cell 3/9 when Ollama on pico became wedged in a
   wedged-generation state; user had to nudge ("dont forget my SPA request" implied
   they noticed I'd missed the matrix dying). Recovery was mechanical: pkill ollama,
   restart, bench-matrix --resume.

Plus a third found AFTER asking for the watchdog spec:

3. **autonovel kanban worker crash-looped 99 times** in ~96 min, each ~60s. Dispatcher
   kept respawning despite failure_limit=2 because of gave_up→promoted cycling.
   Mechanical fix: detect ≥3 crashes within 5 min on same task → block the task.

All three share an exact shape: long-running process, PID alive (or pseudo-alive),
observably stalled (file mtime stale OR endpoint hung OR rapid spawn-crash cycle).

## 3. Changes / decisions

- **Architecture**: Single Python 3 script `~/.local/share/zig-watchdog/watchdog.py`,
  stdlib only. Plugin pattern — each long-job class implements `Probe` (returns OK |
  STALL | CRASH | UNKNOWN) and `Revive` (idempotent fix). New job classes = add a
  Python class, no infra change.
- **Trigger**: systemd-user timer `zig-watchdog.timer`, OnUnitActiveSec=5min,
  Persistent=true (survives reboot).
- **Service unit**: `zig-watchdog.service` Type=oneshot, ExecStart=python3 watchdog.py
- **Logs**: `/tmp/zig-watchdog.log` (rotated by systemd journal anyway), plus per-tick
  results stashed to `~/.cache/zig-watchdog/state.json` for the SPA to consume.
- **Notification**: writes alerts to `~/.cache/zig-watchdog/alerts.json` (append).
  The bench-dashboard SPA (already shipped at port 8765) reads this and surfaces
  via the browser Notifications API (user-confirmed flavor). Pure tailnet.
- **Self-monitoring exclusion**: watchdog does NOT depend on Hermes (avoids the
  circular dependency caught earlier this session when the gateway disk-I/O
  appeared blocked).

## 4. Formal specification

### 4.1 Job classes (v1)

| Class | Probe | Revive |
|---|---|---|
| `BenchMatrix` | (a) pgrep bench-matrix.sh; (b) check newest results/HEALTHCHECK_FAIL-*.txt mtime; (c) curl pico Ollama+MLX endpoints | If aborted-by-healthcheck AND backends recovered: `nohup bench-matrix.sh --smoke --resume > /tmp/.../log &`. Cooldown: 10min between restart attempts. |
| `HfDownload` | For each `hf download` PID on pico: ssh check CPU=0 AND `.incomplete` file mtime older than 5min | kill -9 PID; restart with same args from log file; preserve partial downloads (HF resumes file-level) |
| `HermesGateway` | (a) systemctl --user is-active hermes-gateway; (b) check `hermes kanban dispatch --dry-run --json` succeeds; (c) check for repeated crash patterns in last 5min — task with ≥3 crashes in 5min should auto-block | (a) restart service if inactive; (b) `hermes kanban block <task_id>` if crash-loop detected |
| `BenchDashboard` | curl http://localhost:8765/healthz | restart via start-dashboard.sh |

### 4.2 Plugin interface

```python
class JobClass:
    name: str
    probe_interval_seconds: int = 300  # default 5min
    cooldown_seconds: int = 600         # 10min between revive attempts per job
    max_revive_attempts: int = 3        # before alerting

    def probe(self) -> ProbeResult: ...
    def revive(self) -> ReviveResult: ...
```

`ProbeResult = OK | STALL | CRASH | UNKNOWN` (string enum)
`ReviveResult = SUCCESS | FAILED` (string enum)

### 4.3 State machine per job

```
NORMAL ── probe=STALL/CRASH ──► REVIVING ── revive=SUCCESS ──► NORMAL
                                  │
                                  └─ revive=FAILED ──► (incr counter) ──► if counter≥3: ALERTING
```

### 4.4 Output schema (`~/.cache/zig-watchdog/state.json`)

```json
{
  "last_tick_utc": "2026-05-28T03:00:00Z",
  "jobs": {
    "BenchMatrix": {
      "last_probe": "OK",
      "last_probe_utc": "...",
      "last_revive_attempt_utc": null,
      "revive_attempts": 0,
      "alerting": false
    },
    "HfDownload": {...},
    ...
  }
}
```

### 4.5 Alerts schema (`~/.cache/zig-watchdog/alerts.json`)

Append-only JSON-lines for the SPA to read:
```json
{"utc": "2026-05-28T03:05:00Z", "job": "HermesGateway", "kind": "crash-loop-detected", "detail": "task t_360fa078 crashed 5x in 5min", "auto_action": "blocked"}
```

### 4.6 SPA integration (existing bench-dashboard)

- Add `GET /api/alerts.json` endpoint returning the tail-of alerts.json
- Add JS that polls /api/alerts.json every 5s and fires `new Notification(...)` on new entries (after `Notification.requestPermission()`)
- Add a red banner on the dashboard when any job is `alerting=true`

## 5. Test cases (≥10)

TEST: probe_bench_matrix_ok_when_healthcheck_recent
TEST: probe_bench_matrix_stall_when_aborted_and_backends_healthy
TEST: probe_hf_download_stall_when_cpu_zero_and_mtime_old
TEST: probe_hf_download_ok_when_file_growing
TEST: probe_hermes_crash_loop_when_3_crashes_in_5min
TEST: probe_hermes_ok_when_dispatch_dry_run_succeeds
TEST: revive_bench_matrix_runs_command_and_logs
TEST: revive_hf_download_kills_and_restarts
TEST: revive_hermes_blocks_crash_loop_task
TEST: max_revive_attempts_triggers_alert
TEST: cooldown_prevents_immediate_re_revive
TEST: state_json_written_each_tick

## 6. Open questions

- OQ-01 (P1): Run on zig only, or also on pico for HfDownload-on-pico? **DECIDED: zig only**, but `HfDownload.probe()` uses `ssh pico` to inspect remote processes. Less infra.
- OQ-02 (P1): Watchdog timer interval? **DECIDED: 5min** (matches typical stall-detection windows).
- OQ-03 (P2): Alert delivery? **DECIDED: browser Notification API via SPA** (user-confirmed). ntfy.sh self-hosted is v2.
- OQ-04 (P3): Self-monitoring (watchdog itself dies)? **DEFERRED — systemd Restart=on-failure on timer; manual `journalctl --user -u zig-watchdog -f` for explicit health.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single file at `~/dotfiles/local-models/zig-watchdog.py` (stdlib only)
- [ ] systemd-user timer + service at `~/dotfiles/local-models/zig-watchdog.{service,timer}` + installer script
- [ ] ≥12 pytest tests (per §5) all pass
- [ ] First mechanical action: detects today's blocked t_360fa078 + bench-matrix abort + queues smoke restart
- [ ] SPA adds /api/alerts.json + browser Notification + red banner widget
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-olh in commit trailer

## NOT in scope (v1)

- ntfy.sh self-hosted (v2)
- Push to user's phone outside Notification API
- Watchdog-watchdog (the self-monitor)
- Cross-host probing beyond pico (just one remote)
- Job-class plugin loading from external file (v1 has them in-source)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Single file at local-models/zig-watchdog.py (stdlib only)
 - [ ] systemd-user timer + service + installer script
 - [ ] ≥12 pytest tests all pass
 - [ ] Mechanical action: blocks crash-loops, restarts stalled hf-downloads, restarts aborted bench-matrix
 - [ ] SPA gets /api/alerts.json + browser Notification + red banner widget
 - [ ] Bead: dotfiles-olh in commit trailer

title: ss14-c2-cutover: 11-step playbook — flip SS14 from zig-computer to pico via wrapper
description:
## Context

Final live-cutover bead for Approach C2 (spec dotfiles-9g1). All upstream work has shipped:

- **dotfiles**: ss14-wrapper Go daemon (impl 1bi SHIP, xx9 integration test PASS, b9o deploy artifacts ready)
- **vacation-station-14**: C# patches (vs-4h1 + vs-q7m fix wave SHIP); azigler/RobustToolbox fork live; .gitmodules updated
- **pico**: ss14-wrapper LaunchAgent loaded, listening on 100.72.47.4:11214 (UDP+TCP), HEALTH probe OK; ARM64 SS14 + watchdog build artifacts already on pico from Phase 4 attempt (preserved)
- **zig-computer**: SS14 currently LIVE serving real players; nginx ready for `stream{}` block

This bead drives the actual flip. Production-affecting (drops players currently connected); needs an off-hours window + the user's hand on the wheel.

## Pre-flight checklist

Before running ANY step, confirm:

- [ ] Current player count on `ss14.zig.computer` is 0 (or low + announced maintenance)
- [ ] pico is healthy: `ssh pico 'echo HEALTH | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'` returns `OK active_sessions=N uptime_s=M`
- [ ] vs14 is up-to-date on pico: `ssh pico 'cd ~/vacation-station-14 && git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive'` — should pull azigler/RobustToolbox + the C# patches
- [ ] SS14 build on pico is current: `ssh pico 'cd ~/vacation-station-14 && ./BuildContent.py'` (or equivalent) — verify build succeeds
- [ ] Snapshot zig-computer nginx config: `sudo cp /etc/nginx/sites-available/ss14.zig.computer.conf /tmp/ss14-nginx.bak.$(date +%s)`
- [ ] Snapshot pico Robust.Server config: `ssh pico 'cp /opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml /tmp/vs14-config.bak.$(date +%s)'`
- [ ] ban_address row count snapshot: `psql -h pico -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ban_address;"` — record number to compare post-cutover
- [ ] Maintenance window announced (Discord / hub status / wherever)
- [ ] Rollback runbook reviewed: every step below has its rollback documented inline

## The 11-step playbook (per spec dotfiles-9g1 §4.6)

### Step 1 — On pico: configure wrapper-aware cvars in pico's Robust.Server config

Add to `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml`:

```toml
[net]
use_wrapper_remote_address = true
wrapper_socket = "/tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock"
```

Plus the existing `[status]` config — `bind = "127.0.0.1:1213"` (NOT `*:1212`; bind loopback so only wrapper reaches it).

**Rollback**: revert to snapshot `/tmp/vs14-config.bak.*`.

### Step 2 — On pico: update wrapper LaunchAgent upstream

Current wrapper's `SS14_WRAPPER_UPSTREAM=127.0.0.1:11215` (dev/test default). Flip to `127.0.0.1:1213` (where Robust.Server will bind):

```bash
ssh pico 'sed -i.bak "s|127.0.0.1:11215|127.0.0.1:1213|" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-wrapper.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u pico)/com.zig.ss14-wrapper'
```

Verify wrapper restarted clean: `ssh pico 'echo HEALTH | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'`.

**Rollback**: revert plist `.bak`, kickstart again.

### Step 3 — On pico: load SS14 watchdog LaunchAgents

The watchdog plist at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist` is on disk but unloaded (per Phase 4 rollback). Load it:

```bash
ssh pico 'launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist'
```

Watchdog will start Robust.Server (binding to 127.0.0.1:1213). Verify:

```bash
ssh pico 'lsof -iTCP:1213 -sTCP:LISTEN; lsof -iUDP:1213'
ssh pico 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:1213/status | head -3'
```

**Rollback**: `launchctl unload -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist` + same for replay-rotate.

### Step 4 — Smoke test: synthetic UDP from another tailnet device → wrapper → Robust.Server

From zig-computer:

```bash
python3 -c "
import socket
header = b'PROXY TCP4 192.0.2.99 100.72.47.4 64000 11214\r\n'
sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.bind(('', 56000))
# Send a Lidgren ping (well-formed empty payload won't actually be parsed,
# but it'll register a session in the wrapper)
sock.sendto(header + b'\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00', ('100.72.47.4', 11214))
"
sleep 1
ssh pico 'echo "ENUMERATE" | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'
```

Should see `udp <fanout-port> 192.0.2.99:64000` in the ENUMERATE output. Confirms wrapper sees synthetic client + tracks real IP.

**Rollback**: nothing to roll back — synthetic test only.

### Step 5 — On zig-computer: write the nginx stream{} block (PROD)

`/etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf`:

```nginx
upstream ss14_pico_udp {
    server 100.72.47.4:11214;
}
upstream ss14_pico_tcp {
    server 100.72.47.4:11214;
}
server {
    listen 1212 udp;
    proxy_pass ss14_pico_udp;
    proxy_protocol on;
    proxy_timeout 120s;
    proxy_responses 1;
}
server {
    listen 1212;
    proxy_pass ss14_pico_tcp;
    proxy_protocol on;
    proxy_timeout 120s;
}
```

(Exact form per OQ-01 decision: 120s proxy_timeout grounded in Lidgren PingInterval=1s default per /check dotfiles-9cj.)

**Rollback**: `sudo rm /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf && sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

### Step 6 — On zig-computer: nginx -t + reload

```bash
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

If `-t` fails, abort and fix the conf before reload.

**Rollback**: same as Step 5.

### Step 7 — On zig-computer: stop ss14-watchdog + replay-rotate (the LIVE services)

```bash
sudo systemctl stop ss14-watchdog
sudo systemctl disable ss14-watchdog
sudo systemctl stop ss14-replay-rotate.timer
sudo systemctl disable ss14-replay-rotate.timer
```

At this point, SS14 is REACHABLE via nginx → pico's wrapper → pico's Robust.Server. Players currently connected to zig-computer drop. Reconnect lands on pico.

**Rollback**: `sudo systemctl enable --now ss14-watchdog ss14-replay-rotate.timer`. SS14 is back on zig within ~30s.

### Step 8 — End-to-end client connection test

Open SS14 launcher → connect to `ss14://ss14.zig.computer` → expect to land in lobby → join round → play for 60s. Confirm:

- Connection succeeds
- Player count in `/status` increments correctly
- No connection-drop / disconnect events in `/tmp/ss14-wrapper.log` on pico

**Rollback**: if connection fails, roll back Steps 7 → 5 (re-enable zig watchdog, remove nginx stream block).

### Step 9 — Ban-address real-IP verification (the architectural goal)

Issue a test ban from an admin client (in-game command), then check the DB:

```bash
psql -h pico -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "SELECT address FROM ban_address ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Most-recent row's address should be the **real client IP** (NOT 100.72.47.4 / nginx's IP). Confirms IRemoteAddressOverride is functioning end-to-end through the SS14 moderation path.

**Rollback**: roll back if the address is nginx's IP — investigate cvar / IoC registration / wrapper UDS connectivity.

### Step 10 — Sustained monitoring

Watch for 30 minutes:

- `tail -f /tmp/ss14-wrapper.log` on pico (no unexpected errors)
- `tail -f /tmp/Library/Logs/ss14-watchdog/...` (Robust.Server logs)
- nginx error log on zig-computer: `sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log`
- Real player connections (organic traffic — wait for natural population)

Any sustained errors (per-minute disconnects, NaN rates, latency spikes) → roll back.

**Rollback**: full revert to Steps 7 → 5 sequence (re-enable zig watchdog, remove nginx stream block).

### Step 11 — Documentation

After 30+ minutes of stability:

- Flip dotfiles-9g1 spec bead → closed (work is shipped)
- Update zig-zone runbook: mark Phase 4 as SHIPPED-via-C2 (was originally rolled back; the eventual win was a different architecture than originally attempted)
- Drop a `note` bead with the cutover-date + observed metrics (latency p50/p99, ban_address real-IP confirmed, etc.)
- Brief Discord / community channels if applicable

**Rollback**: N/A (post-stability documentation).

## Total rollback (nuclear)

If anything goes catastrophically wrong at any step:

```bash
# On zig-computer
sudo rm /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo systemctl enable --now ss14-watchdog ss14-replay-rotate.timer

# On pico
ssh pico 'launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist'
ssh pico 'cp /tmp/vs14-config.bak.* /opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml'
ssh pico 'launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u pico)/com.zig.ss14-wrapper'   # reset upstream port
```

SS14 back on zig in <60s. Wrapper still running on pico but idle (no upstream traffic).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pre-flight checklist all green
- [ ] Steps 1-3 complete; wrapper + Robust.Server healthy on pico
- [ ] Step 4 synthetic test PASSES (real IP arrives in ENUMERATE)
- [ ] Steps 5-7 complete; zig-computer ss14-watchdog stopped + disabled
- [ ] Step 8 end-to-end client test PASSES
- [ ] Step 9 ban_address shows real IP (not 100.72.47.4)
- [ ] Step 10 30-min monitoring clean (no sustained errors)
- [ ] Step 11 documentation updates pushed
- [ ] zig-zone runbook Phase 4 flipped to SHIPPED-via-C2
- [ ] dotfiles-9g1 spec bead closed
- [ ] Cutover-receipt note bead created with metrics

title: tap threshold alarm — page at 0.8 pool crossing instead of discovering exhaustion after the fact
description:
## Context

Plan §2.5 (refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md): nothing warns when a pool crosses 0.8.
On 2026-08-13 the estate started the day by draining the last of secondary's fable with
no signal until someone looked. The seneschal brief reports tap as a status line — a
status line read after the fact is not a warning. Durable feedback already recorded in
consul memory (watch-fable-tap-before-draining: headroom is an ALARM not a metric;
surface at ~0.8; never spend a pool's last on routine work without asking).

⚠️ COMPOSE WITH dotfiles-j0yd (work-tap seats must see their headroom at onboard and
while working) — same reader, different surface. j0yd is seat-level surfacing; THIS bead
is the fleet-level threshold watcher. One reader, shared cached state; do not build two
pollers.

## Design

1. READER STAYS agents/lib/tap-headroom.sh — the single authority. No second parser.
2. tap-alarm.{service,timer} (agents/scheduler/templates/, cadence ~15-30 min, off the
   :00/:30 marks) runs the reader for all pools, persists the reading to
   ~/.local/state/harness/tap-state.json (timestamped) — THE COMPOSITION POINT: j0yd's
   onboard/boundary surfacing reads this cache instead of paying a live oauth read.
3. Threshold: any of u7d or fable crossing 0.8 for a pool trips an EPISODE alarm —
   once per crossing, with hysteresis (re-arm when the metric falls back below, i.e.
   after a reset; not a re-page every tick). Threshold per-pool configurable, default
   0.8; config in its own file (NOT taps.conf — a taps.conf commit runs the ~4-min
   mutation harness and this knob does not need that blast radius... builder may
   decide otherwise but must say why).
4. On trip: PushNotification + spool to the seneschal desk
   (socket-registry.sh spool seneschal) + ledger row. On reader failure
   (TAP_HEADROOM_RESULT != ok): alarm THAT, distinctly — an unreadable meter on a
   metered lane is itself pageworthy (three-valued discipline).
5. linearb caveat from seats.yml/e8195de: reset cadence for the new account is NOT
   established — the alarm must not print 'days to reset' guesses for it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pool crossing 0.8 (simulated via stubbed reader output) produces exactly one
      page + one seneschal spool per episode; staying above 0.8 does not re-page;
      falling below then re-crossing pages again.
- [ ] Reader failure produces its own distinct alarm, not silence, not a fake reading.
- [ ] tap-state.json is written on every tick with a timestamp; documented as the
      cache j0yd's surfaces consume.
- [ ] MUTANTS DIE on named cases: (a) hysteresis broken → the once-per-episode test
      reds; (b) failure branch removed → the reader-failure test reds. Application
      asserted first.
- [ ] Timer installed via template path; suite green before/after via tools/githooks.

## Notes

Home ~/demesne. Related: dotfiles-j0yd (P2, composes — leave its onboard-surface half
open, this bead only provides the cache + names it there in a comment), dotfiles-9qyk
(cautionary: per-round emitters are the anti-pattern; this is a TIMER, never a hook).
close_reason: Landed on demesne main 33ed688 (fast-forward from cda6266, ancestor-verified, pushed + ls-remote confirmed). Suite 28/28 and 4/4 mutants killed ON MAIN post-merge. Scrutiny SHIP recorded on the bead. Timer NOT installed/enabled — operator action, install note in the handoff + service template. tap-state.json cache contract documented for dotfiles-j0yd. NOTE: estate is currently over the line (primary u7d 0.93/fable 1.0) so first enabled tick will page twice — correct behaviour, not misconfig.

comments.text:
## Scrutiny — SHIP (2026-08-14, fresh fable-context adversarial gate, opus builder). All 9 verified claims held: hysteresis drives the real script via TAP_ALARM_READER seam; reader failure alarms distinctly with NO stale carry-forward (probed manually); 4/4 mutants re-killed on named cases (M1 5-8,13,17,24 / M2 9-11,22 / M3 16 only / M4 6-7 only); pre-commit gate bite demonstrated end-to-end (weakened case 16 -> SURVIVED M3 -> BLOCKED); taps.conf/seats.yml/tap-headroom.sh untouched per diff; --fable omission justified against reader source; escalate.conf pointer-read degrades loudly when absent; units pass systemd-analyze, cadence off the marks. Three minor non-blocking notes recorded: (1) mutate 'exactly the named cases' slightly overstated (subset assertion), (2) a pool REMOVED from the walk drops its open episodes unlogged (only reachable via taps.conf edit), (3) fld() greedy extraction poisonable by a hostile reason= — single trusted producer.

title: beads: the public dotfiles bead store publishes tailnet + host detail
description:
## Context
Found while executing the public-dotfiles prune (dotfiles-dotfiles-public-prune-k579).
The prune removed agents/ refs/ claude/ archived/ and the host-service dirs from
github.com/azigler/dotfiles (a PUBLIC repo) — but `.beads/issues.jsonl` is TRACKED
there and was never in the removal set. It is 2.3 MB of bead prose covering the whole
estate, and it carries exactly the material the split exists to keep private.

Measured on the pruned tree (commit 0c0bbb2, branch worktree-agent-a798c5efa8370aa14),
after every other source file came back clean:

    grep -c 'dotfiles/agents' .beads/issues.jsonl          -> 39
    grep -oE '100\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | sort -u | wc  -> 6 distinct tailnet IPs
    grep -oE '[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.ts\.net' | sort -u   -> 4 distinct MagicDNS names
    grep -c 'demesne'                                      -> 89 lines

The four hazard greps the prune is measured against are zero in every SOURCE file and
non-zero only here. This predates the prune — the store has been pushed publicly all
along — but the prune is what makes it the LAST remaining hole, and therefore visible.

The right answer is not obvious, which is why this is a bead and not a fix. The store
is also the fleet's live bead graph, referenced by id from both repos, and demesne's
CLAUDE.md deliberately files demesne work as dotfiles-* in ~/dotfiles/.beads to avoid
splitting the graph mid-migration. Options: (a) move the store to the private tier and
re-point both repos; (b) keep it public but scrub and gate it (a doclint-shaped hook on
issues.jsonl); (c) accept it deliberately and say so. Git history already carries the
current content either way, so (b) is a going-forward control, not a redaction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision is recorded (-t decision) among move / scrub+gate / accept
- [ ] If move or scrub: the four greps above return 0 on the public tree's tip
- [ ] If scrub: a mechanical gate exists so the next tick cannot re-add one
- [ ] Either way the public repo's CLAUDE.md rule 5 ("This is a PUBLIC repository")
      names the bead store explicitly — it is the one file a config-shaped review
      will never think to open

title: guard: Fable→Opus 4.8 silent model degradation — detect, retry, molt, then ask Zig
description:
## Context
Zig, 2026-08-09: the prior session (2cc9586e arc) hit repeated silent downgrades — precaution triggers knocked the session from claude-fable-5 to Opus 4.8, and Opus 4.8 then kept running fable-level scenarios with nobody knowing. It happened several times last session. The degradation is DETECTABLE in the logs (session JSONL assistant messages carry the serving model id; the agentgateway request log is the ground truth per AGENTS.md 'verify at the agentgateway request logs').

## Task
Build the watch + recovery mechanism. Zig's playbook, verbatim intent:
1. DETECT: a hook (or watcher) notices the serving model for a Fable session has become Opus 4.8.
2. FIRST RESPONSE: set the model back to fable-5 (verify which seam actually restores the LIVE session — /model vs settings.json top-level model key).
3. TRACK TRIES: persist a per-session downgrade counter. If knocked down AGAIN after a restore:
4. SECOND RESPONSE: molt cycle — change the model and compact (in-flight-safe mode), so the fresh context comes up on the intended model.
5. OTHERWISE (restore refused / molt failed / counter exceeded): STOP and raise AskUserQuestion to Zig — never keep feeding fable-level scenarios to Opus 4.8 silently. (From a timer tick: P1 human: bead + push, per the tick exception.)

## Design notes
- Detection candidates: (a) per-tool-round hook grepping the live session JSONL tail for message.model != expected; (b) gateway request-log watcher; (c) statusline/model probe. Pick the one that sees the ACTUAL serving model, not the requested one.
- 'Expected model' must be seat/session-declared (a Fable seat asserts fable; an Opus seat must NOT trip this).
- Ledger row per detection + action so /seneschal can surface degradation frequency.
- Repo rule 1: demonstrate failure-before/absence-after with a synthetic fixture; mutants must die on named cases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detection catches a Fable→Opus 4.8 downgrade within one tool-round of it happening
- [ ] Restore-to-fable attempted automatically; try-count persisted per session
- [ ] Second knock → molt cycle with model change + compact (in-flight-safe)
- [ ] Exhaustion/failure → AskUserQuestion (interactive) / P1 human: bead + push (tick)
- [ ] Ledger row per event; seneschal brief can count them
- [ ] Hook test suite: failure-before/absence-after demonstrated + mutants die on named cases
close_reason: Built + merged (b078454). PostToolUse guard post-tool-model-guard.sh: detects served-vs-expected divergence from the session JSONL (incl. the explicit model_refusal_fallback event — 9 real instances found in 2cc9586e), per-session try counter, ladder restore→molt→Zig per the playbook, 180s cooldown, fails open on detection errors, non-null ledger rows. ## Scrutiny — FIX-FIRST (independent adversarial agent): F1 subagent runtime path (parent session_id + subagent transcript_path) caused certain ledger noise, a state race, and a plausible false-downgrade instruct — fixed (silent subagent bail + second sidechain filter + atomic state writes), re-verified with real-shape fixture cases C22/C23 and mutants M8/M9 dying on named cases. Post-fix: suite 24/24 and mutants 9/9 RE-RUN ON MERGED MAIN by the orchestrator (evidence in session); 35 pre-existing suites green; perf ~80ms/call on a 9.6MB transcript. Verdict after fix: SHIP. Splits: sfpd (live /model restore seam — the load-bearing unknown), 7pbn (seneschal counts), eih0 (docs), fgb6 (alias within-family downgrade). All guard files inside the demesne synced set (agents/hooks/ + claude/settings.json); tools/githooks stays repo-local by design.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DETECTION SEAM DECIDED — session JSONL, not the gateway log. The client writes the downgrade down EXPLICITLY: {"type":"system","subtype":"model_refusal_fallback","trigger":"refusal","apiRefusalCategory":"cyber","scope":"session","originalModel":"claude-fable-5[1m]","fallbackModel":"claude-opus-4-8[1m]"} — NINE such rows in session 2cc9586e, each one line ahead of the first message served by the fallback. So the JSONL seam is not merely sufficient, it is BETTER than a gateway-log watcher for this loop: it names the intended model as well as the served one, needs no network, arrives within one tool round, and knows which tmux session to instruct. No gateway-watcher variant filed; the gateway log stays the AUDIT ground truth per AGENTS.md, not the recovery loop.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: RESTORE SEAM — /model, with the verification built in. Evidence for the choice: pulse-inject.sh:149 and :638 both record that an in-session /model switch changes the session's model without appearing on /proc cmdline, and settings.json's top-level model key is read at PROCESS START (same class as the always-loaded snapshot, this repo's CLAUDE.md), so editing it cannot move a live session. What is NOT verified from this worktree is the keystroke path — whether an agent can invoke /model on its own pane unaided. Filed as dotfiles-sfpd. The guard is built so this does not affect correctness: it instructs, then MEASURES the served model on the next tool round; if the restore never lands, the try counter advances and the ladder reaches Zig, which is the correct end state either way.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ## Handoff — 2026-08-09: 6 criteria verified, 1 split (ledger RENDERING split to dotfiles-7pbn; the rows themselves ship here). Suite agents/hooks/test/test-post-tool-model-guard.sh 22/22; mutation harness agents/hooks/test/mutate-model-guard.sh 7/7 mutants killed each on the case it names; all 35 existing hook suites still green; end-to-end probe against the real 4,622-line transcript silent on the recovered tail and firing at line 4507 with a complete ledger row.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SCRUTINY FIX-FIRST F1 — the runtime subagent path. Verified independently before fixing, on this bead's OWN agent: ~/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu-dotfiles/538b7ef4-.../subagents/agent-a75fc3d9dbfee0c92.jsonl, 117 assistant rows, isSidechain:true on 100% of them, model claude-opus-5, sessionId field = the PARENT 538b7ef4-..., meta.json {agentType:subagent, model:opus, spawnDepth:1}. All three consequences confirmed real. Fix: a SUBAGENT BAIL — silent exit 0, no ledger row, no state write, when basename(transcript_path minus .jsonl) != session_id; PLUS an isSidechain filter on the refusal-row extraction (a second, independent guard: M7 protects SERVED, M9 protects EXPECTED); PLUS atomic temp+mv state writes. New cases C22 (real-bytes subagent fixture) and C23 (sidechain refusal row must not poison the cached expectation); new mutants M8/M9 each dying on exactly those. C14/M7 kept — harmless, and they still guard the SERVED filter. Live probe against the running 244-line subagent transcript: exit=0, empty stderr, no state dir created.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ## Handoff — 2026-08-09 (post-scrutiny): 6 criteria verified, 2 split (ledger rendering -> dotfiles-7pbn; alias within-family matching -> dotfiles-fgb6). Suite 24/24, mutation harness 9/9 killed each on the case it names, all 35 pre-existing hook suites green, shellcheck clean. Real-bytes evidence in both directions: main-session transcript fires at the downgrade and stays silent on the recovered tail; live subagent transcript bails silently with nothing written.

br/bv audit 2026-08-09. The dh89 marker plumbing (fleet:, fleet-model:,
outward:) currently lives as plain-text lines inside --description because
br 0.2.16 has no key/value marker store. But `fleet` and `outward` are
exactly boolean shape, and br labels ARE that shape natively — this unlocks
`br list --label fleet`, `bv -l fleet` scoping, and
BV_ROBOT_NOT_READY_LABELS claimability gating, which the marshal build
already consumes.

Also record the corrected agent-context rationale for why markers didn't
just go there instead: schema-v11 governing-instructions is DB-ONLY, NOT
exported to JSONL (field census: absent from all 579 rows in dotfiles) — a
marker stored there would not survive clone/machine transfer. That
replaces dh89's earlier "different subsystem" justification with a concrete
reason.

## Task
Coordinate with the marshal build (dh89's bead-markers.sh). Add a
label-backed marker_is_fleet function with the description-line form kept
as fallback during transition. fleet-model stays a description line (it's
not boolean; no clean label shape for a value).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] bead-markers.sh gains a label-backed marker_is_fleet (and marker_is_outward)
- [ ] description-line form still works as fallback during transition
- [ ] beads SKILL MARKERS section updated with the label-backed grammar
- [ ] migration applied to the 12 currently-marked harnessd beads
close_reason: Label-first markers live (merge, agent 17e2891, 31/31 on main). marker_is_fleet/marker_is_outward check br labels first (br label add -l fleet|outward), description-line grammar as transition fallback; fleet-model stays a description line (needs a value). Agent-context rationale CORRECTED in the SKILL: schema-v11 is DB-only, zero JSONL rows — would not survive clone (replaces dh89's 'different subsystem'). Migration found 17 (not 12) Fleet:-marked harnessd beads — all labeled, pushed (harnessd 6d54dcc, ls-remote verified); br label list-all confirms fleet(17). The marshal's eligibility check inherits this through the ONE lib.

title: Measure the effort/thinking/WebSearch matrix on every model we might use
description:
## Context
AGENTS.md states the Opus 5 400 (`xhigh`/`max` rejected when thinking is
disabled, silently killing WebSearch) as a harness constant. Per the
`claude-api` skill it is a per-MODEL property, and the differences are
load-bearing: Fable 5 rejects disabled thinking at ANY effort; Sonnet 4.6 has
no `xhigh` at all; Haiku 4.5 rejects the `effort` parameter entirely and caps
context at 200K vs 1M everywhere else.

AGENTS.md's own line — "re-measure when the fleet's default model changes" —
has never been executed, because there has never been a second model. A model
swap justified by argument alone is the unverified change this harness
distrusts. Measure first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For each of Opus 5, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5: which
      `effort` values are accepted, and whether disabled thinking 400s at each
- [ ] WebSearch probed live on each model at each effort, with a control that
      is MADE TO FAIL on purpose (a check sharing a failure mode with the
      thing it checks is decoration)
- [ ] The silent-staleness mode is reproduced or refuted: does a failed search
      answer from weights and log `done`?
- [ ] Result is a per-model table in AGENTS.md, with the measurement date
- [ ] `PER_MODEL_EFFORT_RESULT=<verdict>` printed on every terminal path
- [ ] Fable 5 is measured FIRST (it is the live default on every surface since acbf436), reusing dotfiles-8eod's cells rather than re-running them
- [ ] Protocol is agents/skills/research/reference/experiment-protocol.md (pre-registration, known-good + made-to-fail controls) — the `/ab` reference in AGENTS.md is DANGLING (no such skill exists); cite the protocol file, and fix or remove the `/ab` mention when the policy text lands

title: works: pico's ~/dotfiles clone — refresh it properly or sever the ~/.claude symlinks; the 'inert' premise is dead
description:

title: zig-zone: private mesh + workshop/server split via Tailscale
description:
## 1. Overview

`zig-zone` is the user's private mesh — a Tailscale tailnet wrapping 5 devices into one virtual LAN regardless of physical network:

- `zig-computer` — Ubuntu VPS, public IP `51.81.33.136`, OVH KVM
- `pico` — Mac Studio M1 Max 64GB, headless, on home LAN
- `metis` — personal MacBook
- `zig` — work MacBook (subject to OQ-03 — work device policy)
- iPhone (Tailscale iOS app + Termius SSH client)

**The split this spec enables.** zig-computer becomes the **workshop + edge**: it stays the user's primary coding box (Claude Code, dotfiles, agent harness) AND retains the public surface — but the public surface narrows to just three things: nginx (TLS terminator + reverse proxy for everything), sshd on :22 (break-glass), and tailscaled. **All hostable services move to pico**: Ollama (LLM inference), `vs14-web`, the SS14 game server, the vacation-station postgres dbs, the Docker observability stack, AND `reef-router` (the granola webhook listener). nginx on zig-computer reverse-proxies inbound HTTP/UDP/TCP through the tailnet to pico. All inter-machine SSH happens primarily via Tailscale SSH.

**pico is a fresh install.** It has macOS but no `mac.setup.sh` has run, no Homebrew, no dotfiles cloned, no Tailscale. The other devices (zig-computer, metis, zig, iPhone) are already configured and only need Tailscale-bring-up + ACL alignment. So this spec includes a one-time **pico bootstrap** section (prerequisites) before the mesh phase.

**Why.** The user wants the workshop machine free from interruption — services on the same box as your active development creates risk of accidental kills, port conflicts, resource pressure mid-flow. The Mac Studio is purpose-built for sustained server load (silent, efficient, Apple Silicon GPU for inference). Plus: the M1 Max's 64GB unified memory gives a real local-LLM serving option that the OVH x86 VM can't match.

**In scope.** Pico fresh-install bootstrap (prerequisite), mesh bootstrap, ACL, the 5-phase service migration from zig-computer → pico (including reef-router), the dotfiles changes to install + configure Tailscale + Ollama on both OSes, the zig-zone skill/runbook.

**Out of scope.** LoRA fine-tuning workflow (deferred to a future spec — MLX-LM + Python venv on pico). Headscale migration (future). Subnet routing (no other home-LAN devices need exposure). Additional VPS/devices. Tailscale Funnel (we have a VPS w/ public IP already).

**Sources informing this spec.**
- Three Explore-agent research briefs run 2026-05-23 covering: Tailscale fundamentals + ACLs + SSH, VPS-as-edge w/ nginx stream{} forwarding, Mac Studio LLM stack (Ollama/MLX/LM Studio)
- `~/explore/.claude/skills/zig-computer-audit/SKILL.md` — current machine topology, services, firewall posture
- Live audit run 2026-05-23: 34 active services on zig-computer, UFW deny-default w/ 6 allow rules, fail2ban 2,573 total bans / 29 active, public ports 22/80/443/1212/1213/7575
- Tailscale docs: tailscale.com/kb (MagicDNS, ACLs, SSH, exit nodes, subnet routers, control-vs-data-plane)
- SS14 docs: docs.spacestation14.com (port-forwarding, hub registration)
- Ollama remote-access patterns: launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST, Tailscale-IP binding

## 2. Current State / Baseline

### 2.1 Network topology (today)

```
Internet
   ↓
zig-computer (VPS, 51.81.33.136)  ← all services live here
   • SSH :22 (LIMIT, fail2ban-protected) ← all 3 personal devices SSH here directly
   • nginx :80/:443 (linearb.zig.computer, ss14.zig.computer)
   • reef-router :7575 (granola webhook)
   • SS14 game server :1212/:1213 UDP+TCP
   • ss14-watchdog.service
   • vs14-web.service (127.0.0.1:3300, fronted by nginx)
   • postgresql@17-main.service (127.0.0.1:5432 + 172.17.0.1:5432 for docker)
   • Docker: 5 vs14 obs containers (grafana, loki, prometheus, ss14-admin, mapserver)
   • ollama.service (127.0.0.1:11434)
   • phoenix :6006 + :4317 (LLM observability)
```

pico exists but is not yet on any shared network. metis + zig + iPhone independently SSH to zig-computer over the public internet via port 22.

### 2.2 UFW state (verified 2026-05-23)

```
22/tcp           LIMIT  Anywhere       (OpenSSH)
80,443/tcp       ALLOW  Anywhere       (Nginx)
1212             ALLOW  Anywhere       (SS14 live)
1213             ALLOW  Anywhere       (SS14 dev)
7575/tcp         ALLOW  Anywhere       (reef-router/granola)
44880            ALLOW  172.18.0.0/16  (prometheus, docker-bridge scoped)
5432/tcp         ALLOW  172.17.0.0/16  (postgres, docker-bridge scoped)
```

Default deny incoming, allow outgoing, deny routed.

### 2.3 Dotfiles baseline

- `mac.setup.sh` line 5: `brew install tmux jq gh ranger ... dicklesworthstone/tap/bv` — NO `ollama`, NO `tailscale`
- `ubuntu.setup.sh`: no Tailscale install
- No `tailscale/` dir
- No zig-zone runbook
- No Ollama plist (correct — Homebrew + `brew services` handles it)

### 2.4 Why the change

The user wants:
- Light, durable, non-locked-in mesh networking (Tailscale w/ Headscale exit option preserved)
- Workshop/server discipline (coding box ≠ service box)
- Local LLM inference at zero marginal cost via pico's Apple Silicon GPU
- Reach pico from anywhere (laptops in cafés, phone) via mesh, not by port-forwarding the home router
- Eventually run longer-interval agentic loops against pico (free model, no quota pressure)

## 3. Changes and Decisions

| Decision | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Adopt Tailscale free tier** (not Headscale day-one) | Easy onboarding, peer-to-peer data plane preserves privacy, Headscale is the exit ramp if ever needed (drop-in compatible). 5 devices fits the 100-device limit comfortably. | `curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh \| sh` (Ubuntu); `brew install tailscale` (macOS); App Store (iOS). `sudo tailscale up` triggers browser SSO. |
| **MagicDNS on** | `<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net` names work transparently across the mesh. SSH/nginx configs become trivial. | Default-on; tailnet DNS name picked in admin console. |
| **Tailscale SSH = primary path; sshd port 22 = break-glass** | Tailscale-only is the #1 day-one mistake on remote VPS (coordination-server lockout risk). Current sshd posture (LIMIT + fail2ban: 2,573 historic bans, 29 currently banned) is doing real work. | Enable `tailscale up --ssh` on zig-computer + pico. ACL grants SSH to `tag:user-devices`. Keep `ufw limit 22/tcp` as is. |
| **No subnet router** | User has no other home-LAN devices that need tailnet exposure right now. One-line change to add later if a NAS/Pi appears. | Skip `--advertise-routes` flag on pico. |
| **No exit node** | Not needed — VPS already has public IP; user isn't trying to hide origin or geo-shift. | Skip `--advertise-exit-node` on any device. |
| **Migrate all hostable EXTERNAL services zig-computer → pico** | Workshop/server discipline. M1 Max is a better server for everything except the public-edge role. | Phased (§ 4.4). |
| **Keep on zig-computer: nginx + sshd-break-glass + tailscaled + dev tooling (tmux, lb-fleet, lb-listener)** | nginx is the public TLS terminator and DNS landing zone; sshd stays as Tailscale-down recovery; tailscaled is the mesh client. tmux + lb-fleet + lb-listener are localhost-bound dev tools that belong with the workshop role — not user-facing services. | Don't touch these in migration; only re-point nginx upstreams to pico tailnet IPs. |
| **Migrate reef-router to pico** | The granola webhook is just an HTTP endpoint; reef-router (bun process) runs fine on macOS; nginx-on-zig-computer can `proxy_pass http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:7575` for it. Keeps zig-computer's "workshop + pure edge" discipline intact. Latency is fine for webhook traffic (granola is async/eventual). | Phase 4 (with the other HTTP services). The public UFW rule for :7575 stays — nginx listens on it now and forwards through the tailnet. Granola's webhook URL doesn't change. |
| **Ollama on pico binds to tailnet IP only** | Default `0.0.0.0` would expose the API to any home-LAN guest; `127.0.0.1` would block tailnet access. Tailnet-IP-only is the precise scope. | `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "$(tailscale ip -4):11434"` before `brew services start ollama`. |
| **SS14 migration is conditional** | UDP forwarding via nginx stream{} adds 10-20ms + jitter; SS14 may embed bind address in handshakes (untested per OQ-01). | Phase 4 begins with a feasibility test; spec defines abort criteria if test fails. |
| **Dotfiles additions stay light** | User's explicit preference. | New: `tailscale/acl.json`, `tailscale/README.md`, `agents/skills/zig-zone/SKILL.md`. Modified: `mac.setup.sh` (4 lines added), `ubuntu.setup.sh` (1 line added). |

## 4. Formal Specification

### 4.1 Device naming (tailnet hostnames = OS hostnames)

| Device | Tailnet name | MagicDNS | OS | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OVH VPS | `zig-computer` | `zig-computer.<tailnet>.ts.net` | Ubuntu 25.10 | workshop + edge |
| Mac Studio M1 Max 64GB | `pico` | `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` | macOS | server farm |
| Personal MacBook | `metis` | `metis.<tailnet>.ts.net` | macOS | client |
| Work MacBook | `zig` | `zig.<tailnet>.ts.net` | macOS | client (subject to OQ-03) |
| iPhone | (iOS device name, lowercased) | `<phone>.<tailnet>.ts.net` | iOS | client via Termius |

Tailnet DNS name itself (the `<tailnet>` part) is decided in the Tailscale admin console — see OQ-04.

### 4.2 Tailscale ACL (`tailscale/acl.json`)

```jsonc
{
  // Single-user personal tailnet.
  //
  // Identity model:
  //   - `zig-computer` and `pico` are tagged `tag:server` (machine identities,
  //     no human user behind them).
  //   - `metis`, `zig`, and the iPhone are UNTAGGED — they auth as the user's
  //     Tailscale account, so they match `autogroup:member` (human-owned devices).
  //   - This separation matters: `autogroup:member` in Tailscale ACLs refers to
  //     human-owned untagged devices; tagged devices are NOT autogroup:member.
  //     Mixing the two requires explicit listing in src/dst.

  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:server": ["autogroup:admin"]   // zig-computer, pico
  },

  "acls": [
    // Server-to-server (e.g., nginx-on-zig-computer → vs14-web-on-pico via tailnet)
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["tag:server"], "dst": ["tag:server:*"] },
    // User devices to servers (SSH, Ollama API, vs14-web preview from a laptop, etc.)
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["tag:server:*"] },
    // User devices among themselves — use `autogroup:self` (the user's own devices)
    // because `autogroup:member` is src-only in Tailscale ACLs and would error as dst.
    // `autogroup:self` matches devices owned by the SAME user as the source — i.e.,
    // metis ↔ zig ↔ iPhone for the user's personal-account devices.
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["autogroup:self:*"] }
  ],

  "ssh": [
    // Tailscale SSH: user devices (metis, zig, iPhone) → server devices (zig-computer, pico).
    // `check` action requires Tailscale-identity re-auth every 12h.
    {
      "action": "check",
      "src":    ["autogroup:member"],
      "dst":    ["tag:server"],
      "users":  ["ubuntu", "autogroup:nonroot"]
    }
  ]

  // No exit nodes, no subnet routes — re-evaluate post-Phase-5.
}
```

**Tags applied per-server only.** zig-computer and pico get `--advertise-tags=tag:server` in their respective Phase 1 `tailscale up` (NOT during fresh-install bootstrap — see § 4.3 note). The user devices stay untagged and naturally match `autogroup:member` once they auth as the user's Tailscale account.

**Why this shape over `["*"]` wildcards.** Explicit src/dst pairs make the policy reviewable — if a future device joins untagged AND unauthenticated, no rule matches it and it's denied by default. A `["*"]` rule would silently grant.

### 4.3 Dotfiles changes

**New files:**

```
dotfiles/tailscale/
├── acl.json         # source of truth for the Tailscale admin policy
└── README.md        # topology + recovery procedures (mirrors zig-zone skill)

dotfiles/agents/skills/zig-zone/
└── SKILL.md         # runbook — auto-loaded as /zig-zone
```

**Modified files:**

`dotfiles/mac.setup.sh` — line 5 gains `ollama tailscale colima docker docker-compose`; new lines after:

```bash
# zig-zone: tailscale + ollama bring-up
# (intentionally does NOT include --advertise-tags or --ssh here — those wait
#  until Phase 1, AFTER the ACL with tagOwners has been pasted into Tailscale
#  admin. Pre-tag advertise fails with "requested tags not permitted" on a
#  fresh tailnet. Phase 1 step 3 re-runs `tailscale up` with the tag flag.)
sudo pmset -a sleep 0 displaysleep 0 disksleep 0 powernap 0
sudo pmset -a autorestart 1                              # auto-boot after power loss
sudo softwareupdate --schedule off                       # no surprise reboots
sudo tailscale up                                        # plain join — tags + ssh come in Phase 1
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "$(tailscale ip -4):11434"
brew services start ollama
```

`dotfiles/ubuntu.setup.sh` — add:
```bash
# zig-zone: tailscale (plain join — tags + ssh come in Phase 1)
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up
```

**No new `launchd/` dir.** `brew services start ollama` manages its own LaunchAgent; `OLLAMA_HOST` is provided to that agent via `launchctl setenv`.

**Docker runtime: Colima, not Docker Desktop.** Colima is OSS, headless-friendly (no GUI requirement), and works with the standard `docker` CLI. Docker Desktop on Mac requires the GUI app running and has licensing nuance. For an unattended server, Colima is the right pick. The Mac bridge networking pattern is `host.docker.internal` (works on both Colima and Docker Desktop) — see § 4.4 Phase 3 for the postgres-bridge migration step.

### 4.4 Migration phases

Each phase has explicit acceptance criteria (§ 5 test cases). A phase isn't done until its tests pass on the live system.

#### Prerequisites — pico fresh-install bootstrap + one-time safety checks (one-time)

pico is a fresh macOS install. Before any mesh work happens, pico needs to BE a functional server with the dotfiles environment, AND a few one-time safety checks need to happen on the other devices.

**0. One-time safety verifications (do these BEFORE pico bootstrap):**

  - **OVH KVM console access on zig-computer**: log into OVH manager, navigate to the VPS, click "KVM console," see the Ubuntu login prompt, log out. Confirms the nuclear-recovery path works AND that you know where the OVH credentials live (NOT in dotfiles — store separately, e.g. password manager). If KVM doesn't launch (Java applet, browser quirks, 2FA on a missing phone) — resolve NOW, before any change to public-SSH posture.
  - **macOS settings on pico (before mac.setup.sh runs):**
    - **FileVault**: in System Settings → Privacy & Security → FileVault, **turn OFF** (or accept that pico is unreachable for any reboot until physically present to enter password). For an in-home server, threat model justifies off.
    - **Auto-restart after power loss**: System Settings → Energy → "Start up automatically after a power failure" → ON. mac.setup.sh later adds `sudo pmset -a autorestart 1` as belt-and-suspenders.
    - **Disable macOS auto-install of updates**: System Settings → General → Software Update → Advanced → uncheck "Install macOS updates" and "Install system data files and security updates." mac.setup.sh adds `sudo softwareupdate --schedule off` as the CLI equivalent.

**1. pico bootstrap proper:**

1. Enable Remote Login (System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login → ON) so we can SSH in from the home LAN to drive the rest
2. Install Xcode Command Line Tools: `xcode-select --install` (interactive GUI dialog opens; let it finish before continuing)
3. Install Homebrew (the canonical bootstrap one-liner from brew.sh)
4. Clone `~/dotfiles`: `git clone https://github.com/azigler/dotfiles ~/dotfiles`
5. Run `bash ~/dotfiles/mac.setup.sh` — now includes `ollama` + `tailscale` + `colima` + `docker` + `docker-compose` in the brew line, plus the pmset + softwareupdate + plain-`tailscale up` + launchctl-setenv-OLLAMA_HOST + brew-services-start-ollama lines (see § 4.3). The full `brew install` line runs as-is even though some packages (yabai, skhd, borders, sketchybar) are UI tools that won't be useful on a headless box — acceptable for now; cleanup is a future polish, not a Prerequisites blocker.
6. Run `bash ~/dotfiles/sync.sh` (or equivalent) to symlink configs into `$HOME`
7. Verify Homebrew installed everything: `brew list | grep -E "ollama|tailscale|colima"`
8. Start Colima: `colima start` (creates the Linux VM that Docker runs in). Verify `docker info` works.
9. `mac.setup.sh` already ran `sudo tailscale up` (plain — no tags, no SSH). Browser SSO prompt opens; auth as the user's Tailscale account; pico joins the tailnet.

**Acceptance:** OVH KVM verified working; FileVault off / auto-restart on / auto-update off; pico can SSH-receive (LAN); `mac.setup.sh` ran clean; `brew services list` shows ollama (binding deferred until Phase 2); `colima status` shows running; `tailscale status` shows pico joined (untagged, no SSH yet — both come in Phase 1).

#### Phase 0 — Mesh bootstrap (no service changes)

1. Pre-generate one Tailscale auth key per device in the admin console (or use browser SSO)
2. Install Tailscale on all 5 devices (`zig-computer`, `pico`, `metis`, `zig`, iPhone)
3. `sudo tailscale up` on each (no SSH yet, no tags yet — just join the tailnet)
4. Verify `tailscale status` on each device lists all 5 peers
5. Verify MagicDNS: `ping pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` from `zig-computer` resolves
6. Verify connection type: `tailscale status` shows `direct` between `zig-computer` and `pico` (NOT `relay` — flag for investigation if so)

**Reversible:** `sudo tailscale down` on each, uninstall. No service changes yet.

#### Phase 1 — Hardening (ACL + tags + SSH enablement)

1. Commit `tailscale/acl.json` + `tailscale/README.md` to dotfiles
2. Paste `tailscale/acl.json` into Tailscale admin → Access Controls → Save. Verify policy compiles (Tailscale's editor shows red-underline on errors).
3. Re-run on the servers: `sudo tailscale up --ssh --advertise-tags=tag:server` on `zig-computer`; same on `pico`. (NOW the tag is permitted because `tagOwners` exists in the ACL.)
4. User devices DON'T get tags. On `metis`, `zig`, iPhone: re-run `tailscale up --ssh` (or just `tailscale set --ssh=true`) to enable Tailscale SSH from those devices to the servers. They naturally match `autogroup:member` once authenticated.
5. Test (TC04): `tailscale ssh ubuntu@zig-computer.<tailnet>.ts.net` from `metis` succeeds
6. Test: `tailscale ping zig-computer` from `pico` succeeds (server-to-server reachability)
7. Test (TC05): existing `ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136` on port 22 still works (break-glass intact)

Per OQ-02 (decided): leave `ufw limit 22/tcp` as-is. No IP allowlist tightening.

#### Phase 2 — Ollama + Phoenix migration

Ollama + Phoenix move as one wave to keep trace data co-located with the model that produces it (no cross-tailnet trace traffic).

1. On `pico`: `brew install ollama` (if not yet), `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "$(tailscale ip -4):11434"`, `brew services start ollama`
2. `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` (smoke-test model) + `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` (real model)
3. On `pico`: install Phoenix (`pip install arize-phoenix` or `uv pip install arize-phoenix`), start it bound to tailnet IP, gRPC on the same `:4317` it uses today
4. From `zig-computer`: `curl http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:11434/api/tags` returns 200 with model list
5. From `zig-computer`: `curl http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:6006` returns the Phoenix UI

#### Phase 3 — vs14-web + postgres + observability containers + reef-router + project timers

All HTTP/TCP-only services in one wave. They share the migration pattern: stop on zig-computer, run on pico bound to the tailnet IP (per OQ-05 decision), point nginx upstream at `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port>`, **wait for in-flight connections to drain (`sleep 60`)**, then stop the old.

1. **Postgres**: on `pico`, `brew install postgresql@17`, `brew services start postgresql@17`. **Postgres is the explicit exception to OQ-05** — it stays bound to `127.0.0.1` (Homebrew default), NOT to the tailnet IP, because the only consumers (vs14-web, mapserver container via host.docker.internal) are co-located on pico. TC11 verifies this is intentional, not an oversight. From zig-computer, dump both DBs: `pg_dump -h localhost -U <user> vacation_station > /tmp/vs.sql` + same for `vacation_station_mapserver`. Transfer via tailnet: `scp /tmp/*.sql ubuntu@pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:/tmp/`. On pico: `createdb vacation_station vacation_station_mapserver`, `psql vacation_station < /tmp/vs.sql`, same for mapserver. Also recreate any roles/passwords (`pg_dumpall --roles-only`) and adjust `pg_hba.conf` on pico to match access policy. **Step 1 must complete before step 2** — mapserver container in step 2 connects to this postgres.
2. **Docker via Colima**: on `pico`, `colima start` (if not already). Transfer the 5 obs container compose files + data volumes from zig-computer (`scp -r ~/vacation-station-14/docker/* ubuntu@pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:~/vacation-station-14/docker/` — adjust paths to actual layout). Verify volume data integrity.
3. **Critical postgres-bridge fix**: on Linux, the mapserver container connected to host postgres at `172.17.0.1:5432` (docker0 bridge gateway). **Colima on macOS does NOT have `172.17.0.1`.** Update the mapserver container's connection string env (`DATABASE_URL` or equivalent) from `172.17.0.1:5432` → `host.docker.internal:5432`. Verify from inside the container: `docker exec mapserver psql -h host.docker.internal -U <user> -d vacation_station_mapserver -c '\dt'`.
4. **Project timers** (8 known per audit skill § 6 "Periodic timers worth knowing"):

   | Timer | Purpose | Suggested launchd schedule |
   |---|---|---|
   | `ss14-backup.timer` | Daily Postgres backup of vacation_station | daily 04:00 |
   | `ss14-replay-rotate.timer` | Rotate game replays | daily 03:30 |
   | `vs14-postgres-retention.timer` | Postgres retention sweep | daily 04:30 |
   | `vs14-cookbook-build.timer` | Build cookbook content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-guidebook-build.timer` | Build guidebook content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-nurseshark-build.timer` | Build nurseshark content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-writer-build.timer` | Build writer content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-map-render.timer` | Render maps | weekly Sunday |

   Confirm the exact `OnCalendar=` schedules with `systemctl cat <timer>` before porting — the table is a starting point, not authoritative.

   **launchd translation cost**: macOS `launchd` does NOT have a direct `OnCalendar=daily` equivalent. The `StartCalendarInterval` key takes a dictionary per fire-time (or an array of dictionaries for multiple times). Budget extra time per timer for the translation; `cron` is the lighter-weight alternative if scheduling is simple (daily/weekly at a fixed time). Port each timer's underlying script to pico first, then schedule. Disable on zig-computer once the pico equivalents are running: `sudo systemctl disable --now <list-of-timers>`.
5. **reef-router**: on `pico`, `git clone <reef-remote-url> ~/linearb/reef` (it IS a real remote-tracked repo — verify with `git -C ~/linearb/reef remote -v`). Then start `next start -H $(tailscale ip -4) -p 3300`. Verify via tailnet from zig-computer: `curl -I http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:3300`.

#### Phase 4 — SS14 game server (conditional on feasibility test)

**Cut-over must happen in a known no-players window** — UDP streams don't drain cleanly via nginx, and any current player gets disconnected instantly. Schedule for low-activity time.

**Performance baseline (recommended before this phase starts):** play-test the current SS14 server on zig-computer for ~10 minutes; note subjective latency / smoothness. After Phase 4 step 5, play-test the pico-hosted version and compare. If pico-via-tailnet feels equivalent or better, the architecture is validated.

1. On `pico`: install SS14 server + watchdog into `/opt/ss14-watchdog/` per upstream docs (will likely need a launchd plist instead of systemd; mirror the watchdog config)
2. Configure SS14 to bind `0.0.0.0:1212` (test the simpler bind first; switch to tailnet-IP if leaked-address test fails)
3. On `zig-computer`: write nginx stream{} config:
   ```nginx
   stream {
       upstream ss14_udp { server pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:1212; }
       server { listen 1212 udp reuseport; proxy_pass ss14_udp; proxy_timeout 30s; }
       upstream ss14_tcp { server pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:1212; }
       server { listen 1212; proxy_pass ss14_tcp; }
   }
   ```
4. `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`
5. **Feasibility test:** stop the SS14 game server on `zig-computer`; have a real client connect to `ss14.zig.computer:1212` (or the public IP); play for 5+ minutes; on the CLIENT machine, run `tcpdump -n host pico.<tailnet>.ts.net or 'src net 100.0.0.0/8'` and verify NO packets target tailnet hostnames or IPs (any such packets would indicate SS14 leaked its bind address — see OQ-01)
6. **If test passes:** proceed — disable `ss14-watchdog.service` on `zig-computer`, leave the nginx stream{} forwarding live, port the `ss14-backup.timer` and `ss14-replay-rotate.timer` to launchd on pico
7. **If test fails:** abort SS14 migration. SS14 stays on `zig-computer`. The nginx stream{} block is removed. Update spec with findings (file `ss14-migration-failed` note bead). Other migrations (Ollama, Phoenix, vs14-web, etc.) are independent and stand.

#### Phase 5 — Done state verification

Final state asserted by tests TC14 + TC15 (§ 5). On `zig-computer`:

**System services running**: edge surface (nginx, sshd, fail2ban), system services (systemd-*, dbus, cron, ufw, unattended-upgrades, qemu-guest-agent, etc.), tailscaled.

**User services running (dev tooling — explicit "stays here"):** `tmux.service` (keeps the user's tmux session alive), `lb-fleet.service` (lb-agent-fleet dev server on 127.0.0.1:7100 — internal/localhost), `lb-listener.service` (lb-agent-listener dev server on 127.0.0.1:7102 — internal/localhost). These are NOT external services and stay on zig-computer as part of the workshop environment. **Future consideration**: revisit moving lb-fleet / lb-listener to pico in a later spec once the user's workflow patterns stabilize — both are currently localhost-bound dev tooling, not user-facing servers, so the workshop/server discipline applies less strictly.

**NOT running on zig-computer**: `ss14-*`, `vs14-*`, `postgresql@*`, `ollama`, `reef-router`, `lb-phoenix`, vs14 docker workload containers. Public ports 1212/1213/7575 are now handled by nginx + nginx stream{} proxying to pico.

**Dual-stack edge preserved.** zig-computer's nginx still listens on `[::]:443` and `0.0.0.0:443` (and ditto for 80, 7575); IPv6 inbound traffic terminates at the edge and the tailnet upstream connection to pico is v4-only via `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` (Tailscale assigns `100.x.y.z` v4 addresses by default). No DNS-record changes needed.

### 4.5 Failure conditions + recovery

| Failure | Symptom | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Tailscale coordination server down | New SSH sessions via `tailscale ssh` fail to authenticate | Fall back to `ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136` (LIMITed sshd is intact); existing sessions stay live |
| pico tailscaled crashes / Mac reboots | nginx upstream `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` unreachable; vs14-web + SS14 + Ollama all 502/timeout | `brew services restart tailscale` on pico (or full reboot — LaunchDaemon brings it back); nginx upstream auto-recovers on next request |
| Home ISP outage / CGNAT relay fallback | Latency to pico spikes from 5ms → 30ms+; SS14 players notice; Ollama still works but slower | No fast fix; ride out outage. If chronic, investigate Tailscale DERP relay region selection or ISP change |
| OVH VPS rebooted / public IP changes | DNS still points at old IP; all public traffic dead | OVH KVM console; check `ip addr`; update DNS A records if IP changed (rare) |
| Locked out entirely (Tailscale + sshd both unreachable) | Can't reach `zig-computer` at all | OVH KVM web console (documented in zig-zone skill); break-glass user/password reset path |
| Auth key compromise | Unknown device joins tailnet | Tailscale admin console: revoke key, audit log shows affected devices, force re-auth |
