title: post-tool-model-guard freezes the seat pin per-session — memo has no invalidation, roster changes are invisible to running windows
description:
## Context

Root cause located 2026-08-13 (refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md §1.3/§2.1, in ~/demesne):
agents/hooks/post-tool-model-guard.sh caches the resolved seat pin into
~/.local/state/harness/model-guard/<session_id>.state (fields seatm=/seatn=), and in
_mg_seat_pin (lines 675-677 as of commit cda6266) a non-empty seatm short-circuits and
returns BEFORE seat_resolve is ever called. There is no TTL on that path — the
SEATTS/cooldown check (line 682) guards only the FAILURE branch. A session therefore
resolves its pin exactly once, at first tool round, and freezes it for life; an
agents/seats.yml amendment is invisible to every running window.

Evidence 2026-08-13: state file 1ae82720-*.state held seatm=fable seatn=linearb while
seats.yml had read opus since 14:43:17Z. Two more sessions frozen the same way.
seat-resolve.sh is INNOCENT — it reads seats.yml live and returns the correct value on
demand (verified: seat_resolve --seat linearb returned opus).

Predecessor bead bd-3sbi lives in the WRONG store (dashboard-dev-interrupted — a LinearB
marketing repo, invisible to harness triage and the marshal) and records a DISPROVED
hypothesis (stale comment-line matching). This bead supersedes it; comment there, do not
build there.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a session in a rostered seat window; let one tool round run (memo written).
2. Change that seat's model: pin in agents/seats.yml (+ regenerate seats.json).
3. Run more tool rounds in the same session.
4. Observe: the guard still enforces the OLD pin — seat_resolve is never re-called
   because seatm= in the state file short-circuits at the top of _mg_seat_pin.

## Design

Record the roster's identity beside the memo — mtime or content SHA of the resolved
seats source (agents/seats.yml, or seats.json if that is what seat-resolve reads) as a
new state field (e.g. seatsrc=). On each tool round, one stat() compares; when it
differs, drop the memo and re-resolve. Cost: one stat per round on the hottest hook in
the fleet — measure and state it.

Also fold in (same seam, same file): print the roster SHA/mtime the guard resolved
against in every fire message, so a frozen-vs-live disagreement is diagnosable from the
block text alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A seats.yml change is picked up by an already-running session within one tool
      round (or one cooldown — state which, and why) without session restart.
- [ ] The memo still short-circuits (no python3 roster parse per round) when the roster
      is UNCHANGED — the memoisation survives, only its invalidation is new.
- [ ] Fire messages name the roster mtime/SHA they resolved against.
- [ ] Proven by a MUTANT THAT DIES on the case it names: e.g. revert the invalidation
      (or stub the stat) and show the named test detecting the frozen pin goes red,
      with the mutation's application asserted first (dotfiles-47nf discipline).
- [ ] Suite test-post-tool-model-guard (or the matching test-*.sh) green before AND
      after; run via the tools/githooks commit gate.

## Notes

Sibling beads, same file, INDEPENDENT fixes (file/keep separate — one bead one builder):
dotfiles-9qyk (no escalation cap — 27+ identical 2KB blocks) and the tap-blind restore
instruction bead. Coordinate at merge time since all touch post-tool-model-guard.sh —
serialize the builders or hand all three to one builder as three commits.
close_reason: Landed on demesne main c6dd96a (rehearsed merge of worktree branch atop 56188d9, ff-only move of shared checkout, pushed + ls-remote verified). Both guard suites + 32-mutant harness green ON MAIN and on rehearsal head; full battery 76 suites with only the two known pre-existing fails. Sessions now pick up a seats.yml re-pin within one tool round via the stamp-file generation check, zero added execve on healthy rounds; fires print the roster identity resolved against (gated to seat-sourced fires per scrutiny F1).

comments.text:
## Scrutiny — SHIP (2026-08-14, fresh-context adversarial gate over the whole trio). Claim-level verification: stamp-file -nt invalidation verified sub-second on tmpfs AND ext4; SEATTS dropped with the memo (S14 red under hand-applied M21 — the exact frozen-memo failure, round 2 still demanding fable after a re-pin); stamp written in exactly one place, escapes the blind-round write_state swallow; roster-path mirror matches seat-resolve branches 1-2, branch 3 degrades keep-memo documented. title: pulse-stall-reconcile: misdiagnoses a REMOTE dispatch failure as an injected-then-died tick
description:
## Context

The 2026-07-29 di-wednesday failure (dotfiles-wv2a) was caught by
pulse-stall-reconcile at 17:30:57Z, ~210 minutes after the 14:00:00Z fire. Good:
the net exists and it did fire. Bad: the row it wrote asserts something that did
not happen, and points the reader at the wrong place.

The row it wrote:

    "outcome":"stalled", "note":"... pulse-inject reported the tick INJECTED,
    but no ledger row landed in the 210m since. The tick did not bounce ... and
    did not block ... it started and died without reporting. ... Check the
    window's pane and the session transcript for the first turn's error."

None of that is true for this failure. Nothing was ever injected. The tick never
started, no remote window was created, no transcript exists to check.
`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` died at step 1 and printed a precise verdict on the
machine Zig watches:

    PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=failed-tunnel   (exit 71)

The reconciler appears to assume the LOCAL `pulse-inject.sh` path, where "the
timer fired and nothing came back" really does imply injected-then-died. For a
REMOTE row the dispatcher's own verdict is available and authoritative, and it
already distinguishes ten failure modes by name.

Consequence: a reader who trusts the note goes looking for a pane and a
transcript that never existed, and the actual cause (a port collision on the
box) is nowhere in the ledger. The row is a true signal wrapped in a false
diagnosis, which is arguably worse than a bare "stalled" — it spends the
reader's attention in the wrong direction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cause a remote dispatch to fail before injection — e.g. bind 127.0.0.1:7100
   on the box so the `-R` forward is refused (the pre-dotfiles-wv2a behavior).
2. Let the timer fire the row and let the stall grace window elapse.
3. Read the row pulse-stall-reconcile appends to refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl.
4. Observed: it claims pulse-inject reported INJECTED and directs the reader to
   a nonexistent pane/transcript. Expected: it reports the dispatcher's actual
   verdict (`failed-tunnel`) and points at the run state dir.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a row whose unit uses `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`, the reconciler reads
      the dispatch verdict rather than assuming the inject path. Sources, in
      preference order: the `PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=` marker in the unit's
      journal (it is the last stdout line, by contract), and the run state dir
      under `~/.local/state/pulse-dispatch/<run-id>/`.
- [ ] The note names the verdict and points at the run state dir (which holds
      `tunnel.err`, and now `tunnel-mode`), NOT at a pane/transcript.
- [ ] A remote failure that never injected must NOT be described as having
      started. Distinguish "never dispatched" from "dispatched and died".
- [ ] Local inject-path rows keep their current wording — do not regress the
      case the reconciler was written for.
- [ ] The 210-minute latency is IN SCOPE to report but NOT to fix here: note in
      the bead what the grace window is and whether it should differ for remote
      rows (a dispatch that fails at step 1 fails in ~1 second and is knowable
      immediately, unlike a genuinely slow tick). File separately if it needs a
      change.
- [ ] Test coverage for both shapes, using the existing harness seams.

## Notes

Related: dotfiles-wv2a inverted `fail()`'s surfacing so a remote infra failure
now rings the 🔔 at work:di within seconds. That is the primary fix; this bead
is about the ledger's own account of what happened being accurate after the
fact, which is a different job (the reconciler is the backstop, and a backstop
that lies about the cause costs more than it saves).

title: a1111: install stable-diffusion-webui on pico, tailnet+LAN reachable
description:
## Context

Set up Automatic1111 stable-diffusion-webui on pico (M1 Max + 64GB,
macOS 14.4) reachable over tailnet AND home LAN — NOT public internet.
Matches the zig-zone pico-service pattern (ollama / phoenix / vs14-web).

User decisions (locked):
- **Auth**: none (network restriction only — tailnet ACL + LAN scope)
- **Model**: skip default download (user adds checkpoints manually)
- **LaunchAgent**: auto-start via ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.a1111.plist
- **mac.setup.sh**: bake in for fresh-Mac reproducibility

## Architecture

- Bind A1111 to 0.0.0.0:7860 via --listen flag → reachable from tailnet
  (pico.tailfb4637.ts.net:7860) AND home LAN (pico's LAN IP:7860)
- NO nginx route on zig-computer — strictly off public internet
  (A1111 has no real auth; Gradio API has had RCE-class bugs)
- Apple Silicon: MPS backend via torch; COMMANDLINE_ARGS needs
  --skip-torch-cuda-test --no-half-vae --use-cpu interrogate per
  A1111's macOS wiki
- Python 3.10 required (system 3.9 won't work; install via brew)

## Tasks

1. brew install python@3.10 + git + wget + cmake + protobuf + rust (A1111 deps)
2. Clone github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui to ~/stable-diffusion-webui
3. First webui.sh run with --listen --port 7860 + Apple Silicon flags;
   verify boot + MPS backend active
4. Verify tailnet access from zig-computer (curl pico.tailfb4637.ts.net:7860)
5. Document LAN IP + macOS firewall posture (user verifies from a
   non-tailnet LAN device themselves)
6. Create ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.a1111.plist; launchctl load -w
7. Template plist into ~/dotfiles/a1111/com.zig.a1111.plist
8. Update mac.setup.sh — brew deps + plist install + repo clone
9. Verify LaunchAgent survives `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.zig.a1111`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A1111 boots cleanly on pico, MPS backend reported in logs
- [ ] webui accessible from zig-computer at http://pico.tailfb4637.ts.net:7860
- [ ] LaunchAgent loaded, auto-restarts on crash, survives reboot
- [ ] ~/dotfiles/a1111/ contains plist template + setup notes
- [ ] mac.setup.sh covers A1111 install for fresh-Mac rebuild
- [ ] No nginx route added on zig-computer (verify ss14.zig.computer.conf
      unchanged)
notes:
## Install gotchas discovered (2026-05-24)

Three first-install quirks not in A1111's macOS wiki — baked into
`webui-user.sh` + `mac.setup.sh` so a fresh-Mac rebuild doesn't trip
on them:

1. **setuptools 80+ dropped `pkg_resources`** (it's now a separate
   namespace). A1111's CLIP install fails with
   `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'`. Fix: pin
   `setuptools<80` in the venv BEFORE first webui.sh launch.

2. **CLIP installs via pip-isolated-build-env**, which downloads a fresh
   setuptools (80+, no pkg_resources). The venv's downgraded setuptools
   isn't visible to the build env. Fix: pre-install CLIP with
   `--no-build-isolation` so it uses the venv's setuptools.

3. **Stability-AI deleted `stablediffusion.git`** sometime in 2026.
   A1111's launch_utils.py defaults to that URL → 404 (masked as 401).
   Fix: `export STABLE_DIFFUSION_REPO=https://github.com/w-e-w/stablediffusion.git`
   (community mirror, same commit hash A1111 pins; documented in upstream
   A1111 PR #17271).

All three baked into `~/dotfiles/a1111/webui-user.sh` (the repo override)
and `~/dotfiles/mac.setup.sh` (the brew-install + setuptools + CLIP pre-
install block).

## State at close

- A1111 LaunchAgent running on pico (PID rotates on restart; check
  `launchctl list | grep com.zig.a1111`)
- Bound 0.0.0.0:7860 → reachable via tailnet (pico.tailfb4637.ts.net:7860)
  AND home LAN (192.168.1.149:7860 — pico's en0 IP)
- SDXL base 1.0 model loaded (`sd_xl_base_1.0.safetensors`, ~6.5GB)
  in `~/stable-diffusion-webui/models/Stable-diffusion/`
- KeepAlive verified: killed python process, LaunchAgent restarted,
  HTTP 200 back in ~10s
- Logs at `/tmp/a1111.log` (StandardErrorPath + StandardOutPath both)
- USER VERIFICATION REMAINING: hit http://192.168.1.149:7860/ from a
  non-tailnet LAN device. macOS Application Firewall may prompt to allow
  inbound on python3.10's first LAN connection — answer Allow.
close_reason: done

title: tmux: commit com.zig.tmux.plist LaunchAgent to dotfiles + wire into mac.setup.sh
description:
## Context
zig-computer runs a persistent tmux server via `~/.config/systemd/user/tmux.service` (Type=forking, ExecStart=`tmux new-session -d -s zig-computer`, Restart=on-failure). User asked for the same on pico.

Set up a LaunchAgent on pico (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.tmux.plist`) that does the equivalent: starts `tmux new-session -d -s pico` at user login, restarts only on non-zero exit (matches `Restart=on-failure` semantics via `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }`). Verified working — `tmux ls` on pico now shows both my `pico` session and the pre-existing tmux-continuum `work` session.

Pico-only setup is fragile (only lives on that one machine). Commit the plist to dotfiles + wire installation into `mac.setup.sh` so any future Mac (or pico rebuild) gets this for free.

## Task

title: spec: the HALL — a tmux-native cockpit; windows become materialized views of the roster
description:
## Context
Zig 2026-08-09: all the parts exist but no terminal viewport — seats/mail/marshal-queue invisible, tmux windows hand-managed (make/rename/close manually = the rename-hazard factory). Yegge built an Emacs rolodex because his terminals were unmanaged; ours have a ROSTER, so the fix is: machinery owns window lifecycle. One command, `hall`:
- `hall` — court view: every seat w/ sigil, office, status glyph, last activity, unread mail, model/tap — rendered from harnessd state.json (the PWA and the terminal are two glasses on one truth)
- `hall <seat>` — jump: window exists -> switch-client; absent -> CREATE correctly (roster cwd, tap config-dir, canonical name). Manual window management ends
- `hall brief` / `hall mail <seat> ...` — seneschal brief + directed mail from the keyboard
- Renames happen via the roster (aliases migrate); the human never renames a window again
Marshal/merge-queue panel rides 69qr's state when it exists. The seneschal is the SWITCHBOARD not the PROXY: status/routing/decisions through it; deep collaborative work stays IN the seat directly.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Formal spec + test cases per /spec; names the state.json contract fields it needs (coordinate with harnessd g7qd/43bp so neither invents fields)
- [ ] Window-lifecycle authority: hall creates/names/retires; a hand-made window shows as UNREGISTERED in the court view, never adopted silently
- [ ] Works degraded when harnessd is down (roster + tmux direct — the cockpit must not die with the daemon)

## Overview (Zig-approved walkthrough, 2026-08-09 — the spec's narrative)
THE INVERSION: seats.yml is truth; windows are cache — machinery creates/names/retires them; hand-made windows show UNREGISTERED, never adopted. SURFACE: `tmux display-popup -E hall` on a keybinding — the court view overlays anything: every seat with sigil/office/status/last-activity/unread-mail/model/tap + a tap headroom meter in the header (shows the CURRENT window's tap; visiting the Factor flips it to tap:work). VERBS: hall (court) · hall <seat> (visit: switch or materialize correctly — roster cwd, tap config-dir, canonical name) · hall brief · hall mail <seat> ... · hall queue (marshal, once 69qr exists) · hall adopt/retire (the only lifecycle verbs, writing THROUGH the roster). STATUS VOCABULARY (emoji-presentation only, per the AGENTS.md glyph rule): 🧠 working · 🔔 needs-Zig · ✅ idle · 💤 asleep · 🛑 disabled · 🚧 unregistered · 🌀 compacting. Dumb glass: verbs+views, no judgment — the seneschal is the person, the hall is the room.

## Tap failover (Zig's requirement, 2026-08-09 — 'the hall can work inexhaustibly')
taps get an ORDERED FAILOVER list (registry-level; per-seat override allowed). At materialization (hall visit OR pulse inject): preferred tap -> headroom check (pico capture, harnessd-4icj) -> dry? next available tap -> session rides the failover tap; NEW sessions return to preferred when it refills; warm panes keep their tap until recycled (R4 — a warm pane never hot-swaps). Every session's serving tap lands in the ledger (honest record of what ran where). Cross-refs: 98v9 (rotation policy) is the pulse-side twin — one resolver serves both.
- [ ] Physical-layer vocabulary comes from the ratified estate lexicon (dotfiles-demesne-lexicon-gadu): the ESTATE (demesne), the KEEP (zig-computer), the WORKS (pico), the ROADS (zig-zone tailnet); hosts do NOT get seats — seats SIT on hosts. Cite, never restate.
close_reason: THE HALL v0 landed (merge 0da434f, agent branch ab9ee624). agents/bin/hall: court view (18 seats, sigil/office/status/last/model/tap, 🚧 for unregistered — never silent adoption), hall <seat> visit (switch or materialize at the seat's ROSTER home: right session, cwd, canonical name; no auto-launch in v0), hall home = seneschal. ONE roster parser — sources seat-resolve.sh and reuses _seat_dump/_seat_strip_glyph, so lexicon regex + YAML subset exist once. R13 held: sessions targeted =name, windows by @id, never colon-joined; every tmux call socket-explicit under env -u TMUX; ZERO send-keys (the hall navigates, never types). tmux.conf: prefix H display-popup + session-created hook materializing the seneschal window (front-desk default). Tap column isolated in hall_tap_cell() as the single v1 failover seam; 📬 legend-only (no invented mail state). ## Guard: 69/69 on main; the court's ACTUAL OUTPUT is fed char-by-char through validate-seats.py's own sigil_violation plus an emoji-count floor (so an ASCII regression can't pass by having nothing to reject) plus a <=78-cell width assert; 5 mutants each died on the case it names — silent adoption of unregistered windows, an em-dash separator, materializing in the caller's cwd, an unguarded attach hook, a send-keys creeping in. NOT ACTIVATED: tmux.conf needs Zig's source-file or a server restart; prefix H currently displaces pain-control's resize-pane -L (his call, surfaced). v1 remains: mail/queue/adopt/retire, tap failover, harnessd state join.

title: Measure whether a different-model reviewer finds different real defects
description:
## Context
`/scrutinize` documents `agent(…, {model:'sonnet'})` as a supplementary lever,
but `scrutinize-panel.workflow.mjs:67,74` passes only
`{label, phase, schema, agentType}` — no model, no effort. The documented
lever has never been pulled. Yegge makes model-swap PRIMARY for review;
our skill (citing Loop Engineering §V.B) makes structural separation primary.

Both defeat different failure modes: fresh context defeats authorship
investment, a different model defeats shared blind spots — which fresh
context cannot touch, since a fresh Opus 5 shares the author's priors. The
proposal is to review on a DIFFERENT and possibly CHEAPER model, inverting
Yegge's upward direction. That is an argument; this bead is the evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The workflow accepts a `model` per hunt agent (default unchanged)
- [ ] Run same-model vs different-model panels over >=3 already-reviewed
      merges; report CONFIRMED (post-refutation) findings per panel, not raw

- [ ] Report token cost of each panel from agentgateway
- [ ] Verdict recorded even if it is "no measurable difference" — a null
      result closes the question and is a success

title: Spec — seat address format, seats.yml schema, and the resolver contract
description:
## Overview

A SEAT is a durable, named agent identity above session and sandbox — adapting
Yegge's Gas Town ("sessions are days, seats are people") to this machine. A seat
accumulates history (handoff lineage, ledger rows, laurels, bead attribution),
carries an execution profile (model pin, effort default), is addressable (mail,
seneschal), and draws tokens from a TAP.

A TAP is a token/quota source — an account credential + config dir. Renamed from
"billing/config seat" (Zig, 2026-08-08) to end the vocabulary collision with
identity seats. Taps today: `personal` (~/.claude), `work` (~/.claude-work),
`tick` (~/.claude-tick). Tomorrow: possibly a second Anthropic account, possibly
Codex — a tap may be heterogeneous in vendor.

Sessions remain ephemeral. Worktree subagents remain sandboxes. NEITHER is a
seat. Pulse rows become scheduled work ASSIGNED to seats (Zig, 2026-08-08).

## Baseline (verified 2026-08-08, cluster reviews B/G/H)

- Six mechanisms claim identity (cwd/slug, beads prefix, memory namespace, tmux
  window, handoff path, process) and disagree; tmux window wins by default with
  no rename migration (the di->pulse incident, bd-msi5).
- created_by is inconsistently full: ubuntu (majority), andrew x38, zig x20
  (dotfiles), unknown x110 (explore). See dotfiles-526s.
- The agentgateway ALREADY emits seat-shaped identity per request:
  `agentgateway.user = zig-computer:desk` (colon form) — the one live consumer.
- 17 active pulse --window values across 24 units; 3 taps; ~/.claude and
  ~/.claude-work symlink the SAME settings.json (no per-tap model pin there);
  ~/.claude-tick diverged (dotfiles-qby3).
- Leaked hook-test tmux servers make session:window tuples non-unique across
  sockets (dotfiles-2v8h).

## Changes

1. `agents/seats.yml` — the single roster (ojjf's roster IS this file; moves to
   the demesne with the agent tier). Read by: seat_resolve (btti), pulse-inject
   (d0bk), harnessd fleet join (harnessd-g7qd), seneschal, laurels.
2. Address grammar `<host>:<seat>` — RATIFIED by Zig 2026-08-08: COLON, matching
   the live gateway dimension byte-for-byte. `zig-computer:desk`.
3. seat_resolve contract (btti implements) — self-resolution, foreign lookup,
   alias migration, loud refusal.
4. Execution profile per seat: `model:` + `effort:`; `tap:` per schedule binding.

## Formal Spec

### seats.yml schema (v1)

```yaml
schema: 1
hosts: [zig-computer]           # future: pico, metis
taps:
  personal: {config_dir: ~/.claude}
  work:     {config_dir: ~/.claude-work}
  tick:     {config_dir: ~/.claude-tick}
seats:
  desk:
    charter: "weekly corpus allocator memo"        # one line, required
    home: ~/explore                                 # default cwd; seats ROAM — home is default, not jail
    model: fable                                    # alias, resolved via settings env pins; required
    effort: high                                    # default per-dispatch effort; required
    history: refs/seats/desk.history.md             # append-only, relative to home; required
    aliases: []                                     # PRIOR window names, for rename migration
    schedules:                                      # zero or more timer bindings
      - unit: pulse-desk
        tap: personal
        window: desk                                # tmux window the tick lands in
  # interactive seats have schedules: [] and are still addressable
```

Rules:
- R1. Seat names: `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,31}`, unique machine-wide, one namespace for
  scheduled and interactive seats.
- R2. Address = `<host>:<seat>`. The bare seat name is a valid local shorthand.
  No subagent address form exists — subagents are sandboxes, not seats (ojjf).
- R3. `model:` values are aliases (fable|opus|sonnet|haiku). Alias->snapshot
  resolution happens at the tap's env (ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL); a seat pins
  the TIER, the fleet pins the SNAPSHOT. Effective model is verified at the
  gateway (gen_ai_request_model), never by reading config back (d0bk AC).
- R4. (Rewritten per Scrutiny-L D1.) `tap:` binds per WINDOW, not per schedule:
  pulse-inject's assert_seat reads the warm launcher's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from
  /proc and hard-fails `failed-wrong-seat` on mismatch, and --fresh sends /clear
  without restarting the launcher — so a differently-tapped schedule landing in
  the same window refuses forever, correctly. A seat wanting two taps uses two
  windows (or an explicit kill-pane step in the unit). The seats.yml validator
  REJECTS two schedules with different `tap:` on the same `window:`. Interactive
  use inherits the launching shell's tap. Tap is derivable from config_dir at
  inject and MUST be logged in the ledger row.
- R5. Resolution (seat_resolve, self): window name -> exact seat match, else
  alias match (returns canonical name + emits a migration notice), else
  UNREGISTERED — loud refusal (exit 3 semantics: cannot-evaluate, never a guess).
  handoff-path.sh refuses on unregistered windows (btti AC).
- R6. Reverse-rename guard: a scoped handoff note carries `seat:` in front
  matter; serving a note whose seat != resolved seat is a loud error
  (dotfiles-tzfr). ABSENT `seat:` (pre-migration notes) => serve + one-line
  migration notice, never an error; M4 backfill deadline: every durable seat's
  note carries `seat:` within one /offboard cycle of roster seeding (Scrutiny-L
  A4).
- R7. (Rewritten per Scrutiny-L A1/A2.) SELF-resolution binds to $TMUX's own
  socket and session — it never searches other sockets. REGISTRY uniqueness is
  a separate validator concern: the seats.yml validator (and `seat_resolve
  --seat`) enumerates /tmp/tmux-$UID/* and refuses loudly on a duplicate
  seat-window tuple across live servers (dotfiles-2v8h). CROSS-SESSION: two tmux
  sessions are live on the default socket TODAY (`work`, `zig-computer`) and
  window names are per-session — a window-name lookup MUST be qualified by the
  schedule's `session:` (recorded per binding in seats.yml) or refuse when the
  name resolves in more than one session. No unstated tie-break.
- R8. Enumeration without tmux: seats.yml is complete on its own — the seneschal
  and laurels read it offline. A seat with no live window is still addressable
  (durable mail queues; nudge fails over per mail-spec c6mp).
- R9. Foreign lookup: `seat_resolve --seat <name>` returns roster row + liveness
  (window up? last ledger row?) without requiring the caller to hold the seat's
  home repo. Unresolvable -> failed-* verdict per c6mp, never silence.
- R10. created_by: new writes use the bare seat name via `br --actor` (d5b9).
  Historical ubuntu/andrew/zig/unknown rows STAND (grandfathered — dotfiles-526s
  decides the mapping doc). Zero store rewrites.
- R11. Commit trailer: `Seat: <host>:<seat>` (b8qx), additive beside
  Claude-Session:; author line unchanged.
- R12. (Rewritten per Scrutiny-L B1 — the prior text misread the evidence.)
  The gateway's `agentgateway.user` is `<tmux session>:<window>` set by
  claude-identity-wrapper.sh (X-Session-Identity), NOT `<host>:<seat>` — the
  host lives in `agentgateway.group` (= hostname -s), and 5 enabled rows emit
  `work:di-*` because Zig deliberately watches them in session `work`
  (2026-08-05 decision in the unit file — do NOT rename that session to make a
  query pretty). The ADDRESS therefore maps to the gateway as: seat -> its
  binding's (session, window) via seats.yml, joined with group=host. Attribution
  queries go through that mapping; nothing requires the user column to equal the
  address. Changing the wrapper's emitted form is a separate decision touching
  78k+ rows of history — out of this spec's scope.
- R13. (Scrutiny-L B2.) An address is NEVER passed to `tmux -t` — the grammar is
  byte-identical to tmux's session:window and a near-miss silently binds the
  wrong session (tmux matches by prefix/fnmatch). seat_resolve returns `session`
  and `window` as SEPARATE fields; every tmux call constructs its target from
  those, never from an address string.

### Migration

- M1. Roster seeding (ojjf): the 17 active windows collapse to ~11 seats;
  di-monday..di-friday -> seat `di` with five schedules, aliases carry all five
  old names. GATED on btti aliases landing first (the di->pulse lesson).
- M2. autonoveld-* -> one seat, four schedules; investd+investd-defi -> one.
- M3. pulse-retry / pulse-stall: jobs, not seats — absent from the roster.
- M4. Handoff notes gain `seat:` front matter lazily (on next /offboard write).

## Test Cases

1. Resolve exact window name -> seat row returned.
2. Resolve aliased old name (di-monday) -> canonical `di` + migration notice.
3. Unregistered window -> loud refusal, exit 3, handoff-path refuses.
4. Reverse rename: note frontmatter seat mismatch -> loud error, note NOT served.
5. VALIDATOR (not resolver, per R7 split): a second live server with a duplicate
   tuple -> validator/`--seat` refusal naming both sockets; SELF-resolution in
   the first server is unaffected.
6. No tmux at all -> `--seat` enumeration and foreign lookup still work.
7. seats.yml schema violation (dup name, bad model value) -> validator fails CI.
8. br create through wrapper -> created_by = seat name; without wrapper on an
   unregistered window -> wrapper refuses (not silent ubuntu).
9. Inject on a schedule with tap=work -> gateway logs user `work:<window>` and
   group `zig-computer`, the work tap's key served it (verify via request_logs
   join per R12's mapping); ledger row carries tap.
10. Seat with schedules: [] (interactive dotfiles) -> addressable, mail
    deliverable on next wake, no timer implied.
11. Model pin fable + tap tick -> effective model at gateway matches pin
    (fails today; passes after qby3 + d0bk).
12. Alias collision: alias equals another seat's NAME or another seat's ALIAS
    -> validator fails (the di->pulse shape is alias-vs-alias; Scrutiny-L A4).
13. (R2) Address grammar: `zig-computer:desk` parses; bare `desk` resolves
    locally; `a:b:c`, uppercase, and >32-char names are rejected.
14. (R11) A commit made through the seat-aware path carries `Seat: <host>:<seat>`
    beside Bead:; pre-merge trailer gate still passes; the Seat: value matches
    seat_resolve output, never hand-typed.
15. (R4) Two schedules with different tap: on one window: -> validator REJECTS
    at commit time, with both schedule names in the error.

## Open Questions (for /check)

OQ1. History file location: refs/seats/<seat>.history.md in the HOME repo vs one
     machine-level dir (demesne refs/seats/)? Roaming seats argue machine-level.
OQ2. Does the seneschal get seat name `seneschal` reserved now (faty says yes)?
OQ3. Interactive windows harnessd/romd/dotfiles: one seat per repo-window, or
     one `zig-interactive` seat with aliases? (G proposes per-window; taste.)
OQ4. Tap credential rotation: does a tap rename/re-auth invalidate history? (No
     by design — history keys on seat, not tap — confirm.)
OQ5. Validator home: pre-commit suite vs harnessd make audit vs both.

## Future

- Second Anthropic tap; Codex as heterogeneous tap (verdict vocabulary already
  vendor-neutral).
- Cross-host seats (pico) — address grammar already carries host.
- Seneschal v1 dispatch authority — behind LOCKED #3-style server-side verb
  allowlist; a seat address in every dispatch record.
- Laurels/CV rollup keyed on seat across all 18 stores (7q80).

## Review-input ACs (per cluster reviews, retained)
- [ ] ADDRESS (corrected 2026-08-08): `<host>/<seat>`, repo NOT in the address. Uniqueness is not free — leaked hook-test tmux servers held duplicate session:window tuples and the resolver passes no -S (dotfiles-2v8h); the spec decides socket-qualification or loud refusal. NO subagent address form is reserved (ojjf rules subagents out of the roster; reserving a form we forbid invites a second grammar)
- [ ] The '9 distinct window names' premise is a stale snapshot — 4 live windows, 17 active pulse --window values, cross-server duplicates observed. Assert distinctness or namespace; never assume it
- [ ] VOCABULARY (Zig, 2026-08-08): identity = SEAT; the billing/config source is a TAP (renamed from 'billing seat', see dotfiles-vvvw). The spec uses both terms consistently and carries the glossary line
- [ ] EXECUTION PROFILE (Zig, 2026-08-08 — pulses rework around seats): seats.yml carries per-seat `model:` and `effort:` (the pin d0bk resolves at inject) and per-binding `tap:` (which account it draws from — ~/.claude, ~/.claude-work, ~/.claude-tick today; a second account or Codex later). Without these fields the roster has nowhere to live
- [ ] seats.yml is the SINGLE roster (ojjf's roster IS this file — no second file) with `charter:` and `history_path:` per seat, enumerable with NO tmux server running (front-desk/seneschal and laurels read it offline)
- [ ] Foreign-seat resolution is specified (mail resolves OTHERS; seat_resolve today resolves SELF) including the no-live-window case — dotfiles-mail-send-axfb blocks on exactly this
- [ ] Migration: the existing andrew/zig/unknown created_by values (dotfiles-526s) and the di-*→one-seat merge (gated on btti's alias mechanism — the di→pulse rename disaster must not repeat) are addressed in the spec's migration section
- [ ] SEPARATOR EVIDENCE (Cluster H, 2026-08-08): the agentgateway ALREADY records live seat-shaped identity as `agentgateway.user = zig-computer:desk` etc. (colon separator, probed via /api/logs/analytics/summary). The spec either adopts `:` or defines the mapping to `/` — the gateway dimension is the one consumer that already exists, don't orphan it
notes:
## Decisions folded in at authoring (2026-08-08, Zig via AskUserQuestion): separator = COLON (matches live gateway dimension); vocabulary seat/tap; execution profile (model/effort per seat, tap per schedule binding) per Zig's pulses-rework-around-seats directive. Spec authored by Fable orchestrator session 2cc9586e; ready for /check to walk OQ1-OQ5.
## Separator RE-RATIFIED on corrected evidence (Zig, 2026-08-08, second AskUserQuestion): COLON stands. Zig's rationale: the tmux session IS the hostname by default on this machine — 'work' is the deliberate exception. So <host>:<seat> and the gateway's <session>:<window> coincide for native rows and diverge only where the session name is intentionally not the host; R12's seats.yml mapping covers exactly those exceptions.

## OQ resolutions — 2026-08-08 (Fable orchestrator, decide-and-proceed; OQ3 stays open for Zig)
- OQ1: MACHINE-LEVEL history dir (demesne refs/seats/<seat>.history.md) — seats roam, so home-repo files fragment a roaming seat's history. Reversible until first write.
- OQ2: BOTH seneschal AND marshal reserved (Zig, second AskUserQuestion + dotfiles-4d57) — seneschal reports, marshal dispatches.
- OQ3: OPEN — interactive seats one-per-window vs one zig-interactive with aliases. Zig's taste call, next decision round.
- OQ4: CONFIRMED — history keys on seat, never tap; tap re-auth/rename does not touch history.
- OQ5: BOTH — validator runs in tools/githooks/pre-commit (data-file arm, dotfiles-lbxa) AND harnessd make audit.
- OQ3 RESOLVED (Zig, 2026-08-08): ONE SEAT PER INTERACTIVE WINDOW — each accrues its own history/laurels/handoff lineage. All five OQs now closed; spec ready for the /test wave.

title: Seat: commit trailer — attribution without touching the git author line
description:
## Context
Gas Town sets `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="gastown/crew/joe"`. **We cannot**: Zig's published
byline is `Andrew Zigler`, and a wrong author line is unfixable without rewriting
history.

- author=seat — rejected, breaks the byline outright.
- committer=seat / author=Zig — rejected: GitHub renders "seat committed", and the
  committer is the signer, so it breaks commit signing.
- **`Seat:` trailer — chosen.** Additive, removable, machine-queryable via
  `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Seat,valueonly)'`, and it matches a convention
  this repo already runs (measured over romd's last 200 commits: `Bead:` ×44,
  `Co-Authored-By:` ×17).

`Co-Authored-By:` is explicitly NOT reused — it is taken by the model and renders
as a GitHub person, which would be a false claim about a human.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/commit` emits `Seat: <host>/<seat>` alongside the existing `Bead:` trailer
- [ ] `git log -1 --format='%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>'` still shows Andrew Zigler for both
- [ ] `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Seat,valueonly)'` returns the seat
- [ ] Trailer omitted entirely when the seat does not resolve — never a placeholder
      or a guessed value
- [ ] Coexists with the EXISTING `Claude-Session:` trailer (x12 in recent history — the session-identity slot): `Seat:` is the durable layer above it, additive, not a replacement
- [ ] pre-merge-worktree.sh's `Bead:`-trailer gate (lines ~68-88) still passes and test-pre-commit-checks.sh stays green

title: Seats — a durable, addressable agent identity above session and sandbox
description:
## Context
Six mechanisms claim to define who an agent is (cwd/slug, beads prefix, memory
namespace, tmux window name, handoff path, process) and they disagree. The tmux
window wins by default — the only one stable across BOTH compaction and `/clear` —
but it has no rename migration, and on 2026-08-03 a `di`→`pulse` rename silently
fed a session a month-stale handoff note with every mechanical gate green.

Bead attribution is already THREE incompatible things (re-measured 2026-08-08): four stores are 100% `ubuntu` (harnessd 314, aaif 117, picod 93, romd 79), but dotfiles' own store holds `created_by: andrew` x38 (2026-07-27..08-06) and `zig` x20, and explore holds `unknown` x110 — set by hand, recently, with no scheme. The field is not empty of identity; it is inconsistently full of it, which is worse.

Adapting Steve Yegge's Gas Town model (MIT/public): *sessions are days, seats are
people.* A seat is a named worker with a permanent identity, above an ephemeral
session and a per-assignment sandbox. Our harness already HAS all three layers —
worktrees, Claude sessions, and an unnamed thing on top. This epic names it.

Deliberate departure: our seats ROAM. His `{rig}/crew/{name}` bakes the repo into
the address; our windows already cross repos (`desk` and `mood` both cwd
`~/explore`; `creaturesd` cwd `/home/ubuntu`; `imc-aug26` in a linearb
SUBdirectory). A repo-scoped address would be wrong on day one.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] A seat has one name, resolvable from any live session without new state
- [ ] New beads record the seat in `created_by`, not `ubuntu`
- [ ] `git log` can answer "which seat produced this commit" without changing the
      author line (`Andrew Zigler` stays author AND committer)
- [ ] A window rename either resolves through a recorded alias or FAILS LOUD —
      never silently serves another seat's handoff note
- [ ] Zero rewrites of the 17 existing bead stores; historical `ubuntu` rows stand

## Acceptance Criteria (added by review 2026-08-08)
- [ ] The existing andrew/zig/unknown actor values are reconciled or explicitly grandfathered (dotfiles-526s) — a fourth form is not added on top

title: What happens when a seat outgrows its scope — the question Gas Town does not answer
description:
## Context
Confirmed NOT-FOUND across Yegge's essays and repo docs: Gas Town has no answer
for an agent whose work drifts past what its name describes. Its seats are pool
slots (Toast, Shadow) with no semantic scope to outgrow. Ours are named for what
they DO (`romd`, `desk`, `dream`), so ours can.

An open design question, not a catch-up item. A starting hypothesis, offered to
be attacked rather than adopted:

1. **Make it observable before making it a rule.** A seat has outgrown its scope
   when its `source_repo` distribution stops matching its bindings — measurable
   from seat-cv-rollup, no judgment call needed to DETECT it.
2. **Resolve by SPLIT with lineage, never by rename.** The old name stays
   resolvable forever (it is in `created_by` history and cannot be recalled);
   `seats.yml` records `split_from:` / `succeeded_by:`; the handoff note is
   COPIED, not moved. Precisely the migration `di`→`pulse` lacked.
3. **Never rewrite historical attribution.** Lineage is a forward pointer, not
   an edit.

Prior art worth checking first: DNS CNAME chains, Git `.mailmap`, and ActivityPub
`movedTo` all solve exactly this — a durable identifier that must keep resolving
after the thing it names has changed.

## Open Questions
- Does a split need Zig's approval, or can a seat propose one and file a bead?
- Does the old seat keep receiving mail after a split (forward, or refuse)?
- Is there a case for a scopeless seat (a pool slot, like Gas Town's) alongside
  the named ones — e.g. for one-off cross-repo work?

title: Promote durable pulse windows to named seats with accumulated history
description:
## Context

The harness already has seats and does not know it. Durable windows
(`pulse`, `dive`, `desk`, `elevate`, `dream`, ...) are standing, named,

and stamped into the gateway as `session:window` by

last overwritten handoff note. The identity track owns the seat record and
addressing; this bead maps existing windows onto it and adds history.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each seat has an append-only history file, distinct from its overwritten handoff note
- [ ] `/onboard` or SessionStart surfaces seat identity + charter — wake with purpose, not amnesia

OFFICE = the title + sigil (the signet layer — ceremonial/semantic, zero migration; seats.yml gains office: and sigil:). title: Measure how often subagent work is amended or reverted after merge
description:
## Context

Portcullis fixed throughput and severed agents from their results; Laurels
repaired that. We have the SAME severance without ever making the trade: a
worktree subagent commits, returns a summary, and is destroyed; the
orchestrator merges, tests, closes, pushes. It never learns whether its work
landed, passed, or was reverted — and cannot, having no future self.

A high rate argues for fewer, longer-lived agents rather than a recognition
system pretending ephemeral workers are seen. A low rate means the severance
is cheap: seats get laurels, subagents do not, and that is fine.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Count merged `worktree-agent-*` commits later amended, reverted, or superseded by a fix bead
- [ ] Report the rate and median time-to-amendment
- [ ] One recommendation: keep ephemeral dispatch, or lengthen agent lifetime
- [ ] Findings on the bead, not in a new doc
- [ ] METRIC CORRECTION (Cluster C, 2026-08-08): the file-touch proxy is NOT the metric — measured 85% (228/269 merges) 'amended', which is ordinary co-evolution, and 5 reverse-merges pollute the denominator. Use instead: (1) explicit reverts (`git log --grep='^Revert|:rewind:'` — measured ~10 total across 8 repos), (2) git-blame line survival via dotfiles-om9z, (3) fix-bead supersession (a -t bug bead touching an agent merge's files within N days)
- [ ] The false-positive class of the naive proxy is stated in the findings so nobody re-derives it

comments.text: Triage 2026-08-10 (Works): NOT fleet-marked deliberately — the METRIC CORRECTION in the ACs (file-touch proxy measured 85% false-positive; a better metric is an open judgment call) plus the 'one recommendation' deliverable make this a thinking seat's task, not a cold build. Blocked-by edge to om9z added (the line-survival primitive it needs, which IS fleet-marked). Re-evaluate for the drain once om9z lands and a metric is ruled.

title: model-guard: verify the LIVE restore seam (/model) end to end
description:
## Context
The silent-degradation guard (dotfiles-p89v) instructs a degraded session to restore itself with the /model slash command, naming the expected model id. That choice rests on real evidence: agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh:149 and :638 both record that an in-session /model switch changes the session model WITHOUT appearing on /proc cmdline, and settings.json top-level "model" is a launch-time seam (read at process start, same class as the always-loaded snapshot) so editing it cannot move a running session.

What is NOT verified from the p89v worktree is the KEYSTROKE PATH: whether an agent can invoke /model on its own pane unaided. The candidates are (a) the agent emitting the slash command itself, (b) a self tmux send-keys into its own pane, which queues the text until turn end the way pulse-inject injects, (c) only Zig can do it, in which case the ladder should escalate to him one rung earlier.

The guard is built so this does not affect correctness: it instructs, then MEASURES on the next tool round. If /model never lands, the per-session try counter advances and the ladder reaches Zig anyway. But rung 1 is wasted effort if (c) is true, and rung 2 (molt with a model change) depends on the same seam.

## Task
Run the experiment on a live, expendable seat: force a degradation (or simulate one with MODEL_GUARD_EXPECTED), then try each candidate path and read the result off the session JSONL assistant message.model field, which is the ground truth the guard already uses. Record which path actually moves the served model.

## Acceptance Criteria
 - [ ] Each candidate path (agent-emitted /model, self send-keys, Zig-only) tried on a live seat and its outcome recorded
 - [ ] The winning path is named in post-tool-model-guard.sh restore instruction, replacing the current generic wording
 - [ ] If NO agent-driven path works, the ladder is shortened so rung 1 escalates instead of instructing
 - [ ] Evidence is the served model id read back from the transcript, not a self-report

## Context

The 2026-08-08 untag landed and the mesh works, but four follow-ups were never
filed. All are the SAME defect class as `dotfiles-metis-key-deleted-l2r8`: an
undeclared dependency that fails silently when something unrelated changes.

**1. pico has NO `~/.ssh/config` at all.** Zero declared outbound identity map —
exactly the shape that cost us metis, where `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` served a host no
config named and a cleanup for a DIFFERENT host deleted it. zig-computer was
hardened this session (every host declares `IdentityFile` + `IdentitiesOnly yes`,
plus a `Host *` catch-all that offers nothing). **pico did not get the same
treatment and is now the weakest link in the demesne.**

**2. pico -> homeassistant is still broken.** `Permission denied (publickey,password)`.
Policy already allows it; the key is missing. Needs pico's pubkey added to the
Advanced SSH & Web Terminal add-on's **`ssh.authorized_keys`** config option — NOT
a plain file, which HAOS regenerates. Confirmed the add-on currently holds exactly
one entry (`claude-code-ha`). `/data/options.json` is root-owned and Supervisor
treats its own DB as source of truth, so a direct edit can be silently clobbered;
the HA UI is the correct path. Deferred by Zig 2026-08-08.

**3. `id_ha` still serves TWO hosts** (pico and homeassistant). Now DECLARED in
`~/.ssh/local`'s key map rather than silent, but the shared-role shape is what
caused the incident. Deleting `id_ha` today breaks both.
⚠️ The `:2222` retirement changed the economics: pico now reaches Tailscale SSH
keylessly, so `id_ha` on pico is only a FALLBACK. Splitting may now be nearly free.

**4. pico's non-interactive PATH lacks `/opt/homebrew/bin`.** `ssh pico "tailscale …"`
fails command-not-found — which is why this session initially and WRONGLY concluded
pico had no tailscale CLI. It runs Homebrew tailscaled 1.98.3 with `RunSSH: true`.
Fix in `~/.zshenv`, not `.zshrc`, which non-interactive shells skip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] pico has a `~/.ssh/config` mirroring zig-computer's hardened `~/.ssh/local`:
      every host declares `IdentityFile` + `IdentitiesOnly yes`, a `Host *`
      catch-all offers nothing, and a key map records which key serves which host.
- [ ] `ssh pico "tailscale status"` works — PATH fixed in `.zshenv`.
- [ ] pico -> homeassistant verified BY USE, not by config inspection.
- [ ] Decide and record whether `id_ha` is split per-host now that pico needs it
      only as a fallback.
- [ ] The `:2222` launchd job on pico is either retired or explicitly kept with a
      stated reason and a date to revisit.

title: decision: PasswordAuthentication is ON for the public-IP box running the agent harness
description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-08 while verifying the untag had not broken plain SSH:

```
port 22 · listenaddress 0.0.0.0:22 · [::]:22
permitrootlogin without-password
pubkeyauthentication yes
passwordauthentication yes      <-- this
```

Root is key-only, which is good. But **regular users can authenticate by password
on a public-IP box** (`51.81.33.136`) that holds `id_ha`, `id_metis`, credentials
in `~/.secrets`, and an autonomous LLM harness with shell access. That is a
continuous brute-force surface against the machine with the most to lose.

Not raised as an emergency: it may be long-standing and deliberate, and something
like fail2ban may already cover it. **That was NOT checked** and should be, before
any change — an existing mitigation changes the answer.

## Why this is a decision and not a fix

`PasswordAuthentication no` is precisely the change that locks you out if any path
depends on it. The public-IP sshd is the demesne's **out-of-band escape hatch** —
the thing that survives a tailnet failure, and the thing that made the untag safe
to attempt at all. Hardening it by breaking it would be the worst available trade.

## Notes

Zig's call. If the answer is "turn it off":

1. Check for fail2ban or equivalent first — it may already be a non-issue.
2. Verify key auth works from metis AND the iPhone BEFORE changing anything.
3. Keep a live session open while making the change.
4. Confirm with `sshd -T`, not by reading the config file — the file is intent,
   `sshd -T` is what the daemon actually resolved.
notes:
## Decision — 2026-08-08, Zig via AskUserQuestion (session 2cc9586e)
KEEP PasswordAuthentication ON. Context: review verified the bead's stated precondition — fail2ban is installed and ACTIVE (1.1.0-8) — which is the compensating control. Zig chose retention (recovery access on a shared box) over key-only hardening, with fail2ban as the active defense. Reversibility: trivial — one sshd_config line + reload, any time the calculus changes (e.g. after the demesne split reduces what the box holds).
close_reason: Zig's decision 2026-08-08: password auth stays ON; fail2ban (verified active) is the compensating control. Full record in notes.

title: tailscale-ssh: iPhone Termius nerdfonts broken via tailnet (works via public IP)
description:
## Problem
iPhone Termius → tailnet → Tailscale SSH server → broken nerdfont/powerline glyph rendering in zsh powerlevel10k prompt. Same client → public IP → OpenBSD sshd renders correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. iPhone Termius connects via tailnet hostname (`zig-computer.tailfb4637.ts.net` or pico) to a tag:server-tagged box
2. zsh powerlevel10k prompt loads inside tmux
3. Observe: glyphs render as missing-character boxes

Compare: same Termius client → `51.81.33.136:22` (public IP, OpenBSD sshd) → glyphs render correctly.

## Investigation status (2026-05-24)

### Confirmed NOT the cause
- **Client font / Termius config** — RULED OUT (public IP path works with same Termius)
- **Env var stripping** — Tailscale SSH (≥1.76) does require `acceptEnv` in ACL to forward env vars. Added `"acceptEnv": ["TERM", "LANG", "LC_*"]` to both SSH rules in `tailscale/acl.jsonc`. Verified `LC_*` show `en_US.UTF-8` and `TERM=tmux-256color` in the broken session.
- **IUTF8 termios flag** — RULED OUT. User verified `stty -a | grep iutf8` shows `iutf8` (set, no minus) on the broken Tailscale-SSH path. Tailscale GitHub issue #4146 was a red herring for this specific symptom.
- **Server-side dotfile regression** — RULED OUT. Session didn't touch zsh/p10k/tmux config.
- **Same shell / tmux session** — both paths land in the same tmux session via `start.sh`.

### Likely cause (unconfirmed)
Something at the SSH protocol / channel layer between tmux's PTY output and Termius iOS's renderer:
- SSH channel data buffering / framing differences (Tailscale's Go server vs OpenBSD sshd C)
- Possible UTF-8 byte boundary issues in packet framing
- Termius iOS's SSH client may handle Tailscale SSH's specific protocol implementation quirks differently
- Terminal-mode bits in pty-req beyond IUTF8 (specific termios encoding flags) that differ between the two server implementations

This requires either: deeper SSH protocol-level capture + comparison, OR Tailscale-side debugging of their PTY proxy code. Beyond the scope of a Sunday-night session.

## Workaround (in use)
Use the public IP path from iPhone Termius for interactive work:
- Termius host entry: `51.81.33.136:22` → OpenBSD sshd → tmux → working glyphs
- Other tailnet devices (macOS Tailscale, CLI tailscale ssh, server-to-server) keep using the tailnet path — they work fine
- No security regression: port 22 is intentionally LIMITed (ufw) + fail2ban (2,573+ historic bans). Public-IP SSH path is the documented break-glass anyway.

## Next-session action
- File issue with Tailscale upstream linking back to this bead — protocol-level PTY data delivery in Tailscale SSH appears to misbehave specifically with Termius iOS client (other tailnet SSH clients work fine).
- If time allows: deeper packet capture / comparison between Tailscale SSH and OpenBSD sshd's framing of the same byte stream.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] ACL `acceptEnv` fix applied + verified env forwarding works
- [x] IUTF8 termios verified as already-set (not the cause)
- [x] Workaround documented (iPhone uses public IP)
- [ ] Runbook gotcha #14 added with "Tailscale SSH + iPhone Termius corner case → use public IP workaround"
- [ ] Optional: file upstream issue with Tailscale

title: two-writers: staged-by-A-committed-by-B — a concurrent committer sweeps another writer's staged work into its own commit
description:
## Context
Recurred twice in one session (2026-08-09, the terminology/design lane): (1) my staged zig-voice reference deletions were swept into the founding lane's marshal-milestone bead commit (03002b8) because 'git commit' commits the shared INDEX, not the paths the committer added — their honest disclosure was the only reason it wasn't silent; (2) the dotfiles jsonl was committed under me between my status check and my add, so my commit found a clean tree and my bead row rode a stranger's commit message. Both benign THIS time; the class is not: writer A stages a half-finished operation, writer B's unrelated commit publishes it mid-thought, and A's blocked/errored commit is the only tell. The existing guards (pre-shared-tree-guard blocks destructive verbs; explicit-path adds) do not cover 'commit picked up someone else's staged entries.'

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Session A: git rm <files> (staged), then pauses (hook block, thinking, anything)
2. Session B in the same checkout: git add <its-paths> && git commit
3. B's commit contains A's deletions under B's message; A's later commit says clean

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A mechanism, not prose: e.g. the commit path warns/refuses when the index contains staged paths the current command did not add this invocation (pre-commit comparing staged set vs the add-list is one shape; a per-writer git worktree for orchestrator sessions is another — evaluate, do not assume)
- [ ] Whatever ships is measured against the two incidents above (reproduce, then show the guard biting)
- [ ] False-positive story stated: bead-jsonl sweeps are the NORMAL shared-file case and must stay frictionless

## Write target
~/demesne — agents/hooks/ (staged-entries commit guard beside pre-shared-tree-guard) + tests.

title: test-pulse-inject: cases 1-17 drive the LIVE default tmux socket, and 28 root-level mktemp dirs sit outside every trap
description:
## Context
Two findings from the dotfiles-u1g1 panel scrutiny (2026-08-11), both pre-existing
debt in agents/scheduler/test-pulse-inject.sh, deliberately NOT fixed in that wave:
the wave refused to ADD to the debt (its new glyph cases were moved into the
file's private-socket discipline as G1-G5) but a full migration is its own job.

FINDING D (major) — NON-HERMETIC. Cases 1-17 run on the DEFAULT tmux socket:
`SESSION="pulse-test-$$"` at test-pulse-inject.sh:24 driven by bare `"$TMUX_BIN"`
with no `-L`, and the EXIT trap at :34 likewise. That is the same server carrying
the live zig-computer estate and its 2-minute api-stall-recover / seat-liveness /
pulse-retry timers. The same file already adopts private-socket discipline from
case 18 onward (PRIV_SOCKDIR / PTMUX with -L, :625-631), so the pattern to migrate
TO is in the file.
Measured by the panel on an unchanged tree: four runs gave FAIL 14/192,
FAIL 15/192, FAIL 16/192 and PASS 192/192, with `can't find pane: %1170` and
`/tmp/tmp.XXXX/pulse-bounces.jsonl: No such file or directory`. Failures included
long-standing cases such as "command injected on cold start" — i.e. ~7% of the
suite is flaky under ordinary box load. dotfiles-u1g1 additionally made this
suite a pre-commit GATE (tools/githooks/pre-commit maps agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh
to it), so the flakiness now blocks unrelated commits and trains people to re-run
until green.

FINDING E (minor, same migration) — TRAP COVERAGE. 28 bare root-level `mktemp -d`
allocations (test-pulse-inject.sh:196, 212, 228, 257, 303, 304, 417, 448, 532,
1115, 1161, 1180, 1196, 1211, 1245, 1261, 1280, 1307, 1328, 1360, 1408, 1424,
1497, 1531, 1620, 1650, 1700 …) are swept by INLINE `rm` statements (:220, 265,
333, 482, 539, 1446, 1736), not by any of the file's EXIT traps (:35, 627, 922,
1487), which reap only $DIR and the private sockets. A completed run cleans up;
a `timeout`, a `set -u` abort or a Ctrl-C leaks up to 28 root-level dirs — the
same class as dotfiles-d5ez, whose 115,781 leaked dirs took /tmp to 100% IUse and
bricked every Bash call on the box on 2026-08-11. Verified during the u1g1 wave:
a SIGTERM'd run of this suite orphaned exactly such a dir.
Fold E into the D migration: a per-section private socket plus one reaped parent
dir removes both problems at once, and the file then earns the leak guard the
escalate and retry suites now carry (a final case asserting zero tagged /tmp-root
droppings).

## Steps to Reproduce
D: run `bash agents/scheduler/test-pulse-inject.sh` four times while the box is
   under normal load (a marshal drain tick, another agent's suite). Expect
   intermittent FAIL 14-16/192 with `can't find pane`.
E: `timeout 20 bash agents/scheduler/test-pulse-inject.sh; ls -d /tmp/tmp.* | wc -l`
   before and after — the inline rms never run, and the traps do not cover them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cases 1-17 run on a private -L socket with their own session names, never the default server
- [ ] The suite is green 5x consecutively under load (the flake is the thing being fixed; one green run proves nothing)
- [ ] Every mktemp in the file is reaped by a trap, not by an inline rm on the happy path
- [ ] The file carries the same leak guard as test-pulse-escalate.sh / test-pulse-retry.sh (a final case asserting zero tagged /tmp-root droppings, `.leak-owner`-stamped)

title: cleanup: pulse-surface-queue.sh's 'remote' origin has no producer and is still the default
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the `dotfiles-y3u8` agent while deleting the marketing-vps conduit, and
deliberately left alone as out of scope.

`pulse-surface-queue.sh` still accepts `--origin remote`, and `remote` **is still
the default** — but the dispatcher that was its only producer is gone. Every live
caller passes `--origin local` explicitly, so nothing is broken today.

It is dead-default config: a knob whose default names a thing that no longer
exists. Harmless now, misleading later — the next reader will reasonably assume a
remote producer exists somewhere.

Related, same origin and worth reading together: the `DISPATCH.md` waiver path now
has **no producer at all** (the dispatcher was the only one), so the anti-runaway
cap is now absolute rather than waivable. That was documented in `pulse/SKILL.md`
rather than left dangling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Either flip the default to `local`, or keep `remote` with a comment stating
      it is reserved for a future non-tailnet box. **Decide; do not default.**
- [ ] If the default changes, confirm no caller relied on the old one — grep, do
      not assume.
- [ ] Suite still passes and the relevant case still bites.
close_reason: Merged 98b854e (agent 9b2ec51): pulse-surface-queue.sh default origin remote -> local (producer retired in y3u8). Sole caller pulse-ledger-watch.sh always passes --origin local explicitly; tests 17/18b/19 now pin the still-supported remote wording explicitly. 88/88 + adjacent suites 26/26, 113/113. Re-verified on main.

title: vault: transcripts cone was an allowlist that only grew for projects opened on THIS box
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. On vps-8a9eb245, look for `~/linearb/pipeline-website` transcripts in
   `~/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu-linearb-pipeline-website/`
2. Observe: only a `memory/` subdir. Zero `*.jsonl`.
3. `git --git-dir=~/.claude/vaults/transcripts.git ls-tree` shows the slug DOES
   exist upstream with 2 top-level transcripts.

## Context — not a bug so much as an expired premise

`agents/vault/vps-peer-bootstrap.sh:18` states the design outright:

    # memory = ALL linearb slugs (memory is tiny); transcripts = ACTIVE slugs only.
    MEM_PATTERNS='/-home-ubuntu-linearb*/'          <- glob
    TR_PATTERNS: four hand-listed slugs             <- allowlist

Sound for a shared coworker-facing peer with limited disk. Wrong once the box
became Zig's own machine (183G free, 6% used).

Full causal chain:
- bootstrap seeded FOUR transcript slugs
- `session-start.sh`'s dynamic-slug hook appended three more as Zig actually
  opened sessions in them here (dashboard-dev-interrupted, agent-factory,
  weekly-reporting) — the cone grew ONLY for projects worked in on this box
- pipeline-website never had a session here, so it was never appended, so it was
  never checked out
- meanwhile memory was a glob from day one, which is why the directory existed
  containing ONLY `memory/`. That is exactly the symptom Zig reported.

Audit at time of fix: 15 linearb slugs + 5 dotfiles sibling slugs missing
(reef 584 transcripts, agent-dev-interrupted 43, reef-fish-meeting-summarizer 84,
dotfiles-local-models 41, dotfiles-claude-sandbox 33, ...). Every IN-cone slug was
complete, so the sync mechanism was never at fault — only cone membership.

## Fix applied (runtime)

Both cones replaced with matching globs and reapplied:

    /-home-ubuntu-linearb*/
    /-home-ubuntu-dotfiles*/

Verified: pipeline-website has its 2 transcripts; a re-audit across 29 slugs
reports zero gaps; the live session's alias and jsonl survived; vault-sync OK.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] pipeline-website transcripts present locally
- [x] all 29 linearb/dotfiles slugs complete (up == local)
- [x] memory and transcripts cones identical
- [ ] DECIDE: should `vps-peer-bootstrap.sh` keep the narrow transcripts default?
      A genuinely shared coworker box probably SHOULD stay narrow — both for disk
      and because Zig's personal transcripts do not belong on one. This box is no
      longer that. Not changed unilaterally: it is a confidentiality/role call.
- [ ] REGRESSION RISK: `.git/info/sparse-checkout` is NOT tracked, so tonight's
      fix is local-only and a re-bootstrap silently reverts it. `vps-peer-bootstrap.sh`
      refuses to run over an existing vault (exit 3), so this needs a deliberate
      re-bootstrap to bite — but nothing warns.
- [ ] Minor: the dynamic-slug hook appends an explicit `/<slug>/` line even when a
      glob already covers it (`grep -qxF` cannot see glob coverage). Idempotent per
      slug and harmless, just cone-file noise. Deliberately NOT fixed — glob-coverage
      logic in a hook that runs at every SessionStart is not worth the blast radius.
notes:
RESOLVED in full — Zig codified the role change 2026-07-28 ("this box has stopped
being that... my peers are not the issue here").

Every open criterion is now closed, not deferred:

- DECIDE narrow-vs-full default -> DECIDED: FULL MIRROR. vps-peer-bootstrap.sh no
  longer writes a sparse cone at all and sets core.sparseCheckout=false explicitly
  so a re-bootstrap cannot inherit a stale one.
- REGRESSION RISK (cone untracked, re-bootstrap reverts) -> GONE. There is no
  narrow cone left to revert TO; the tracked default is now full.
- Minor hook cone-noise -> FIXED. Appends are skipped unless the vault is actually
  sparse.

Went further than the reported symptom, because the symptom was the third
instance of one root cause (allowlist where a transform belonged):
- Pulled ALL 93 slugs, not just linearb/dotfiles. 64 were unmaterialized —
  explore, hevyd, harnessd, cfp, andrewzigler3, aaif, coding-jams, autonovel.
  Zero gaps on re-audit. 1.2 GB -> 4.6 GB worktree, 182 GB free.
- Made the -home-andrew* -> -home-ubuntu* transform UNIVERSAL in session-start.sh.
  It was an allowlist, which is the wrong shape here: a missing entry costs
  invisible data loss, an over-broad match costs an unread symlink.
- Found and migrated 7 ALREADY-STRANDED dirs the allowlist had been silently
  dropping: bare -home-andrew (13 transcripts, merged into -home-ubuntu for 20)
  plus six ~/work/* projects. Committed + pushed as vault e43d1f4
  ("transcripts: 8 slugs"). All 13 -home-andrew* entries are symlinks now.

Evidence: probe over 7 cwds x both sparse states (bare home -> -home-ubuntu, NOT
the nonsense -home-ubuntu--home-andrew that a naive suffix strip produces;
-tmp-* untouched; cone grows only when sparse is on). 22/22 hook tests pass.
93/93 slugs complete. vault-sync OK, 0 unpushed. Live session survived every
migration (jsonl reachable through its alias throughout).

Commits: 6ea8081 (dotfiles), e43d1f4 + 9668925 (transcripts vault).
close_reason: done

title: pulse-surface-queue.sh injected prose hardcodes 'REMOTE ... ran on marketing-vps' — wrong for local surfaces
description:
## ⚠️ RE-RATED P3 -> P1 on 2026-08-07. The original filing was WRONG.

I filed this as "cosmetic, not a correctness bug: the announcement still delivers."
**That was wrong, and the error is instructive: the injected text is not decoration, it
is an INSTRUCTION to the receiving Claude session.** Adversarial review of dotfiles-wqby
caught it hours later.

## Context

`pulse-surface-queue.sh` (lines ~331-336) builds the single-line command that
`pulse-inject.sh` types into the pane. It is hardcoded for the REMOTE dispatcher. Typed
verbatim, for BOTH the 1-pending and n-pending forms:

> "REMOTE PULSE SURFACE (...): a pulse tick that ran on **marketing-vps** has FINISHED
> ... File any bead it names that the remote side did not already file and push, and
> **land the ledger row at `<dir>/refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl`**. Do NOT re-run the tick."

For a REMOTE tick both clauses are right: the box ran the tick, the local session lands
the row (`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` step 6).

For a LOCAL tick staged by `pulse-ledger-watch.sh` (dotfiles-wqby) both are FALSE:
- it did not run on marketing-vps;
- **the ledger row already exists** — the local tick wrote it at wrap (`/pulse` step 5),
  and that row is precisely what the watcher READ in order to stage this announcement.

## The failure, on the happy path

1. Local tick finishes, writes its ledger row.
2. Watcher sees a new row, stages a surface, advances its marker.
3. Drain types the command above into the pane.
4. The session obeys "land the ledger row" and writes a **duplicate** row with a fresh `ts`.
5. Next run (2 minutes later): that row is newer than the marker -> stage -> type -> (4).

Self-sustaining announcement loop, plus ledger corruption in the file the whole mechanism
reads. The only counter-instruction ("do NOT write another") lives in the surface JSON's
`.detail`, which the session reads AFTER the command that contradicts it.

`pulse-ledger-watch.sh` is **gated off by default** as of `975baf4` until this lands
(`PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE=1` forces it on). **This bead blocks dotfiles-wqby.**

## Why the test suite did not catch it

`test-pulse-ledger-watch.sh` case 14 drives the real queue and asserts the surface FILE's
contents — it never asserts what the drain **types**. The gap is the seam between the two
scripts, which is exactly where a shared-prose assumption hides.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The injected command is ORIGIN-AWARE: a local surface never claims marketing-vps
- [ ] A local surface does NOT instruct the session to land a ledger row (the row already exists); the remote form keeps that clause
- [ ] Both the 1-pending and n-pending forms fixed — they carry the text independently
- [ ] `test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` assertions updated in step (8 sites pin the literal string)
- [ ] New assertion on what the drain TYPES for a local surface, not only what the file contains — the gap that let this through
- [ ] Re-enable the watcher in `pulse-retry.sh` (drop the `PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE` gate) and re-run the mutation check on test-pulse-retry case 18
close_reason: Fixed in 3324d1b. pulse-surface-queue.sh's 'stage' now takes --origin remote|local (remote is the default, so pulse-dispatch-remote.sh is untouched) and selects the injected wording accordingly. Verified by direct inspection: the LOCAL branches say 'its ledger row is ALREADY WRITTEN — do NOT write another one. Do NOT re-run the tick.' and grep confirms 0 occurrences of 'land the ledger row' in any local branch, so the duplicate-row -> re-stage -> re-type loop is closed. All three forms handled: 1-pending, n-pending, and a MIXED form for a group holding both origins. REMOTE PROVEN UNCHANGED: the implementer drove the pre- and post-change queue through one fixture and diffed the typed command -- byte-identical at n=1 (601B), n=2 (961B), n=3 (1099B) after normalizing staging stamps; I independently re-ran test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh -> REAL rc=0, 421/421. The test gap that let this through is closed: cases 16-19 now assert what the drain TYPES (both origins, both forms, mixed), not only what the surface file contains. Suite 42 -> 76 cases, verified by me at REAL rc=0, 76/76, with the implementer's mutation checks showing 4/4/4/2 failures when each wording fix is broken.

title: decision needed: Bead-trailer exemption for routine unattended-daemon output commits — 5th gitmoji vs standing-bead convention
description:
## Context
Zig-relayed 2026-08-09 from the digest lane (instance record: digestd-nb9, with digestd-llq as the throwaway-bead workaround it forced twice today). pre-commit-checks.sh requires a Bead: trailer with four exempt gitmojis (:card_file_box: :broom: :dollar: :outbox_tray:); a daemon's routine output commit (:newspaper: digest content + ledger row) has no natural bead, so unattended loops mint-and-close throwaway beads just to commit — ritual compliance that pollutes the bead store and proves nothing. Also to check per the finding: prior :newspaper: commits in digestd history carry no trailer and were NOT blocked — confirm the hook simply postdates them (expected) vs a lost exemption (bug).

## The fork
(a) Add a 5th exempt gitmoji for routine unattended output (:newspaper:, possibly scoped to a repo allowlist so it doesn't become a general escape hatch); (b) standing reusable bead convention (one durable 'routine output' bead per loop, cited by every output commit — keeps the trailer invariant but makes one bead absorb hundreds of commits, diluting 'one bead = one commit'); (c) something better. Documented WHEREVER pre-commit-checks.sh's exemption list lives, so the next daemon doesn't rediscover this.

## Acceptance Criteria (for whoever Zig's ruling lands with)
- [ ] Zig's pick recorded here; implementation in pre-commit-checks.sh + its test suite (rule 1: demonstrate block-before/pass-after for the chosen shape).
- [ ] The history question answered with evidence (hook install date vs the digest commits).
- [ ] digestd-nb9 closed against this; the throwaway-bead pattern (llq) named as the anti-pattern the fix retires.

## Write target

title: answer a blocked seat's permission prompt from the harness app — today it requires opening the terminal
description:
## Context

Zig, 2026-08-14, on finding the Works seat stalled on a dangerous-command prompt:
"we need something in our own harness that gets our attention when the thing is
in this state and then surfaces a way for us to answer it from the harness app. I
have no way of doing that without opening the console and being in the terminal."

The detection/surfacing half is dotfiles-emmk. **This bead is the ANSWERING half**
— once Zig knows a seat is blocked, he currently has exactly one remedy: open the
terminal, find the window, and press a key. That is a poor fit for the way he
actually works (SSH + tmux, often away from the machine), and it means a seat can
sit blocked for as long as it takes him to get back to a console.

## Design

The remedy has two plausible shapes and they are not equivalent:

1. **ANSWER-IN-PLACE** — the app relays a keystroke to the blocked pane.
   Simplest, and preserves the guard's own semantics exactly.
2. **REWRITE-AND-RETRY** — Zig's actual response tonight was not "yes" or "no",
   it was *"I just told her to do a safer version of that."* That is the more
   common real answer to a dangerous-command prompt, and it is a MESSAGE to the
   seat, not a button press. An answering surface that offers only Yes/No would
   have missed what he actually wanted to do.

Worth designing for (2) as the primary and (1) as the fallback, because the guard
fires precisely when the command was ill-formed — so "no, do it differently" is
the expected answer, not the exception.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zig can resolve a blocked seat without opening a terminal.
- [ ] The surface carries enough CONTEXT to decide safely: the full command, which
      variables are unset or empty, and which guard fired — not just the prompt's
      one-line summary. He should never have to approve a command he cannot see.
- [ ] Sending a corrective INSTRUCTION (not just Yes/No) is a first-class action.
- [ ] ⚠️ It is safe against the documented injection hazard (below).
- [ ] The action is attributable and logged — who answered, when, what was sent.

## Notes

⚠️ **THE DANGEROUS PART, and it is already documented in the tree.**
`agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh`'s header records the exact failure this bead could
cause if built naively: *"a pane sitting in a modal dialog, because the injected
text is eaten by the dialog and the trailing Enter ANSWERS ZIG'S OPEN QUESTION
with the default."* So a remote-answer built on blind send-keys can SELECT THE
DEFAULT — which, on a dangerous-command prompt, may be the destructive option.
Any implementation must confirm the pane's state and what it actually sent,
rather than firing keys and assuming.

This is the same reason `pulse-inject` defers on 🔔, and the reason dotfiles-q18
(pane_in_mode) is still open.

DEPENDENCY: dotfiles-emmk (detection) is the prerequisite — you cannot offer an
answering surface for a state the harness cannot see. Sequence emmk first.

CONTEXT ON THE GUARD ITSELF, from Zig, so nobody treats it as noise to suppress:
"I usually see it when an agent writes a command where they're using a variable
as the base of a directory... That means if the variable was empty then it would
cause an rm operation on the root folder or something extremely destructive. It
catches that and it warns against that." The guard is CORRECT and valuable. This
bead is about the response loop being too slow, never about firing less often.
