title: pulse-retry: re-fired a tick whose bounce was already resolved — raced the supervisor, queued /clear behind a LIVE run
description:
## Context
2026-08-09 15:50:55Z, live instance during the marshal campaign: pulse-retry's bounce consumer saw the two blocked_on_andrew bounces (15:47:16, 15:48:32 — pulse-inject deferred on the stale-🔔 marshal window, dotfiles-jisc) and, once the window glyph cleared, re-fired pulse-marshal.service. But the bounce was ALREADY RESOLVED: the supervising session had manually injected at 15:50:51 (night-start ledger row written before the re-fire). The re-fire's pulse-inject typed into the now-🧠 composer, which QUEUES — so a --fresh tick's '/clear' + '/marshal night' sat queued behind the LIVE run-2 tick, set to wipe the running marshal's context at end-of-turn. Under the continuous-push directive this instance is benign (auto-starts run 3 at night-end, nothing in flight); in the general case it is the 3135 family — a /clear landing on a context with in-flight builder handles destroys them, and an abnormal turn-end fires it mid-night.

Two distinct defects:
(a) STALENESS: the re-fire never checked whether the bounced tick was still needed. The evidence was available two ways: the drain ledger's night-start row (15:50:51 < 15:50:55), and the pane's visibly-running tick. A bounce is a claim about the past; re-firing must re-verify the present.
(b) QUEUE-BEHIND-LIVE-TICK: pulse-inject into a 🧠 window queues cleanly by design, but for a --fresh SCHEDULED tick that design assumption inverts — queuing '/clear' behind a running tick of the SAME loop is a delayed context-wipe, not a delivery. pulse-inject (or the retry caller) should treat same-loop-already-running as 'resolved', not 'deliverable'.

Also for the record: the re-fire log line credits itself with the 🔔 clearing ('window cleared 🔔') — it did not clear it; the supervisor's verified rename did (jisc runbook). The engine waited out the 🔔 correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Cause a scheduled tick to bounce blocked_on_andrew (stale 🔔 per jisc).
2. Resolve the blockage manually and inject the tick yourself (supervisor path).
3. Watch pulse-retry re-fire the same loop within its next cycle (~2 min): pulse-inject types /clear + cmd into the live tick's composer, result 'injected'; the pair sits queued to fire at end-of-turn. Journal: 'Aug 09 15:50:52 Starting pulse-marshal.service'; retry log: 're-fired pulse-marshal.service — window cleared 🔔 (bounce 15:48:32)'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Before re-firing a bounced loop, pulse-retry verifies the bounce is still live: same-loop tick not already running in the target pane AND (where the loop has a ledger) no run-start row newer than the bounce. Either signal kills the retry as 'resolved'.
- [ ] pulse-inject --fresh refuses (new verdict, e.g. deferred-already-running) when the target pane's CURRENT turn was started by the same loop's tick — never queues /clear behind a live same-loop run.
- [ ] Demonstrated failure-before/absence-after per repo rule 1, on both arms.
- [ ] Coordination note: 9z3o (pulse-escalate, hardening lane) must integrate with THIS engine, not add a second independent re-fire path — two racing consumers is this bug squared. Cross-linked.
close_reason: Both arms built, adversarially verified, live. (a) STALENESS: pulse-retry step 3d.5 re-verifies a bounce against the present — same-loop delivery row within PULSE_SAME_LOOP_TTL (shared knob, fail-closed on malformed ts) AND ledger run-start newer than bounce both resolve the retry (no re-fire). (b) QUEUE-BEHIND-LIVE: pulse-inject --fresh returns deferred-already-running instead of queuing /clear behind a live same-loop run; failed delivery-row writes are LOUD (PULSE_INJECT_WARN=delivery-unrecorded, separate line, verdict stays last). Failing-before demonstrated on the pre-fix scripts on both arms (builder + independently reproduced by scrutinizer, verdict SHIP 3/3, no new findings). Suites 41/41 + 183/183; 14/14 mutants killed on named cases; gates armed both repos. Merged 009cae4+efec807, carried to demesne 81349a8, all files byte-IDENTICAL, injector hot. 9z3o coordination confirmed from source: escalate filters the underscore literal already_running; escalate owns NO re-fire (single-owner preserved). Watch item: first live fire (Works' next injection or the 01:07 timer) observes the new contract in production.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Third instance of the pattern, from the Works session at run #3 (2026-08-09 ~16:5xZ): a transient run-3 timer was manually stopped as redundant — stale-schedule artifacts re-firing into resolved state now measured three ways in one night (pulse-retry's 2s-late re-fire, the Esc'd-question stale 🔔, the redundant transient timer). Strengthens the staleness-verification AC: any re-fire decision needs a 'has this already resolved' check against ledger/pane truth, not schedule state alone. pulse-escalate (9z3o, closed) deliberately owns NO re-fire for exactly this reason — this bead's pulse-retry + pulse-inject --fresh work is the remaining piece; claimed to the hardening lane, next wave.

title: SECURITY P0: 203 high-confidence secrets across 25 transcript files — transcript vault has been unable to commit for 5 days
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while investigating the VPS report (explore-tkci). Confirmed by reading ~/.claude/vault-sync.log directly, not inferred.

## What is happening

The claude-transcripts vault pre-commit gate (scrub-secrets, explore-r2iq Layer 1) has BLOCKED every hourly sync since 2026-07-21T01:00:30Z — 120 consecutive runs. It is blocking because staged transcript content contains high-confidence secrets.

**The gate is working correctly.** It is doing exactly its job: preventing credentials from entering permanent git history. This bead is not about the gate.

## The two real problems

**1. THE SECRETS ARE ON DISK AND WERE IN CONTEXT. Redaction is not rotation.**

203 findings across 25 files:
   82  slack-token
   54  gateway-sk-key
   14  github-token
   13  aws-akia
   13  anthropic-key
   10  openai-key
    6  google-refresh-token
    5  google-api-key
    3  google-client-secret
    3  bearer-token

By project slug: explore 100, linearb-pipeline-website 49, linearb-agent-factory 26, aaif 13, harnessd 7, linearb-dashboard-dev-interrupted 6, andrewzigler3 2.

One session file alone (-home-ubuntu-explore/6da07a61) carries 61 findings across all 10 types.

Per the standing policy (memory: claude-memory-vault, "redaction != rotation for secrets ever in context"), anything genuinely live here must be ROTATED. Redacting the transcript removes the copy; it does not un-expose the credential.

Triage needed before rotating everything — some are probably not equally severe:
- `gateway-sk-key` (54) is likely the LOCAL agentgateway key, self-issued, low blast radius. Verify.
- `slack-token` (82), `google-refresh-token`, `google-client-secret`, `aws-akia`, `github-token` are the ones that would genuinely hurt.
- `anthropic-key` / `openai-key` — check whether these are real provider keys or example/placeholder strings echoed in tool output.

**2. A 5-DAY SILENT BACKUP OUTAGE, and systemd reported SUCCESS throughout.**

`claude-vault-sync.service` exits **0/SUCCESS** on every run — the push failure happens inside the script and never becomes the unit's exit status. So:
- transcript backups have been dead for five days
- `systemctl status` says everything is fine
- it was found by a human looking, not by any alarm

This is the same class as the vanished pulse ticks and the andrewzigler3 nightly that "succeeds" while deploying nothing. A failure that reports success is worse than a failure that reports nothing.

Note the MEMORY tier is unaffected and syncing fine — only transcripts are blocked.

## Steps to Reproduce

    tail -30 ~/.claude/vault-sync.log        # the BLOCKED banner and the per-file findings
    systemctl --user status claude-vault-sync.service   # reports 0/SUCCESS

## Acceptance Criteria

- every finding triaged as live-credential vs local/self-issued vs false positive, with the list recorded
- every live credential ROTATED (not merely redacted), and the rotation recorded
- the affected transcript files redacted via scrub-secrets --apply so the vault can commit again
- vault-sync propagates its internal failure to the unit's exit status, so a blocked push turns the unit red
- an alarm fires when the vault has not committed successfully for N hours (harnessd is the obvious home — it already has a stale-loop detector)
- a regression test asserting a seeded secret both blocks the commit AND turns the unit red
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-07-26 — Zig: "the secrets are fine." He has accepted the credential exposure as handled and does NOT want future sessions re-raising it.

DO NOT re-file, re-scan-and-escalate, or nag on this. If a future audit finds these same
credential types in transcript history, that is EXPECTED and already adjudicated.

What actually shipped, so the record is complete:
- 20 files / 319 findings redacted across the transcript tree (live session excluded so an
  actively-appended JSONL could not be corrupted). Re-scan: 0 files, 0 matches.
- The vault resumed pushing immediately — first successful transcripts commit since
  2026-07-21 after a 121-run / 5-day outage.
- The gate is now SCRUB-AND-CONTINUE, not block-and-halt (Zig's explicit policy call):
  a redaction is a NOTICE with a row in ~/.claude/vault-redactions.jsonl, exit 0, unit green.
  A broken redactor or a secret surviving re-scan still fails loudly.
- The silent-failure half is fixed independently: vault-sync now propagates tier status to
  the unit exit code, and claude-vault-sync is wired into harnessd's manifest (it had been
  in the invisible 45% — 20 user timers on the box, 11 in the manifest, which is exactly how
  the 5-day outage went unnoticed).

Closing as done. The remaining alarm/observability work stands on its own merit and is not
gated on anything credential-related.
close_reason: done

title: bug: moving ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the .zshenv tier blinded pico's request log — durable panes never re-source
description:
## Context
2026-07-27 23:52Z (2b8d22a) removed ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from the fleet-wide
claude/settings.json `env` block; 23:54Z it landed in the per-host shell tier
(~/.<host>.zshenv). The scoping is RIGHT — vps-8a9eb245 has no route to pico —
but it converted a LAUNCH-time setting (every claude process read settings.json)
into a SHELL-START-time one.

The harness's durable tmux panes hold zsh processes started 2026-07-27 04:46Z,
~19h BEFORE the file existed. They never sourced it, so every claude launched
from them — i.e. every pulse tick in every long-lived window, plus Zig's own
sessions in those panes — talked to api.anthropic.com directly. pico's request
log, the fleet's API-layer instrument (memory reference_agentgateway_request_log),
went blind: last row 2026-07-28T21:56Z, zero since, while sessions ran all night.

Nothing alarmed, and nothing could have: bypassing an o11y proxy is
indistinguishable from being idle. Same family as ~/explore's "name the consumer
in the same change as the producer".

The tick-jail had the same hole from the other direction: bwrap starts from an
EMPTY env and the launcher bypasses the claude() function, so a jailed dive tick
was invisible too.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<any long-lived claude pid>/environ | grep ANTHROPIC
   -> ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS present, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ABSENT.
2. ss -tnp | grep claude -> connections to api.anthropic.com, none to
   100.72.47.4:17017.
3. sqlite3 pico requests.db -> no rows after 2026-07-28T21:56Z.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] claude-identity-wrapper.sh resolves ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL per INVOCATION from
      the per-host file, like it already does for the identity header
- [x] precedence: inherited value wins; CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 opts out; no per-host file
      (the VPS) -> unchanged
- [x] the per-host file's exports do NOT leak into the caller (subshell read)
- [x] verified in BOTH bash and zsh under a clean env (6 cases each, identical)
- [x] tick-jailed.sh mirrors it via --setenv; confirmed inside the REAL jail
- [x] end-to-end: a shell with the var UNSET produces a logged gateway row
- [x] the escape-hatch docs updated everywhere — `unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` no
      longer bypasses anything, CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 does

title: decision: the hook runner keeps full mutant coverage and narrows its trigger to six files, rather than dropping mutants to fit a time budget
description:
## Context

`dotfiles-jm1c` shipped `tools/githooks/pre-commit`. Measured, stopwatch, 12 cores:

| path | time | load |
|---|---|---|
| typical suite (worktree-guard / stderr-guard / require-isolation / hook-helpers) | **138–776 ms** | 1.6–4 |
| `test-pre-commit-checks.sh` alone | 8.4 s @ 1.6 · 11.0 s @ 10.5 | |
| `test-pre-bead-close.sh` alone | 4.6 s @ 1.6 · 10.3 s @ 10.5 | |
| **guard path** (2 suites + `--selftest` + 6 mutants) | **85–88 s** | 2–5 |

85–88 seconds is long enough that "a gate that hurts gets disabled" is a real risk, and
the obvious relief is to drop mutants.

## Decision

**Keep every mutant. Narrow the trigger to six files** — the two gates
(`pre-commit-checks.sh`, `pre-bead-close.sh`), the shared matcher
(`lib/scrutiny-verdict.sh`), the two suites, and the harness itself.

## Why

Those six are the only files whose change can **silently kill the bite**. Everything else
in the repo pays 138–776 ms, which is invisible. So the 85 s is not a tax on ordinary
work; it is a tax on editing the guards — which is exactly when you want it, and which is
rare.

Dropping mutants would buy speed on the one path where speed is worth least, and it would
do it by removing the thing that just caught three dead guards. `dotfiles-jm1c` exists
*because* a green suite hid a live false-accept in the commit gate; a harness trimmed to
fit a budget is how that recurs.

**The trigger includes the TEST files, not just the scripts** — weakening a guard is
frequently an edit to the test alone, and a trigger keyed only on implementation would
miss it.

## Reversibility

One line in `tools/githooks/pre-commit`. Nothing depends on the trigger set; widening or
narrowing it is a local edit with no migration.

## The residual, stated

Five known gaps, all from the shipping agent's own probe of its result, none of them
closed by this decision:

1. **The runner gates everything except itself** — no suite maps to
   `tools/githooks/pre-commit`, so deleting a trigger from it produces zero test failures.
   Confirmed empirically: staging only that file ran nothing.
2. **`core.hooksPath` is per-clone local config.** A fresh clone, a new machine, or one
   `git config --unset` silently disables the whole thing and nothing detects it. Same
   shape as the defect this repo keeps finding: the alarm is the mechanism.
3. `pre-commit-checks.sh` **false-blocks `git commit --amend --no-edit`** (and `-C HEAD`)
   — the `Bead:` trailer lives in the existing message, not in the command text the hook
   greps.
4. **10 suites outside `agents/hooks/test/`** (5 scheduler, 2 lib, 1 doclint, 2 skills) are
   wired in by path mapping but were never run under
   `unset $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)`. Worth one confirming run.
5. `dotfiles-oe80` — a load-sensitive case that can now flake-block a commit.

Recorded per `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` "when you decide-and-proceed, leave a durable record".
The agent that made the measurement flagged that this wanted a `-t decision` bead and
could not create one; this is it.

Related: `dotfiles-jm1c`, `dotfiles-8aj5`, `dotfiles-2dez`, `dotfiles-oe80`, `explore-a3zc`.

title: model-guard: transcript parser misses model_consent_fallback (the limit-degrade row)
description:
## Context
Found while fixing dotfiles-cpqi (read-only investigation of session b4b949b6). The guard's
transcript parser (agents/hooks/post-tool-model-guard.sh, read_facts) extracts exactly one
client-written model fact:

    .type == "system" and .subtype == "model_refusal_fallback"  ->  .originalModel

That is the PRECAUTION-fallback shape (dotfiles-p89v, session 2cc9586e, 9 rows). The
2026-08-10 limit-degrade wrote a DIFFERENT shape, measured verbatim in
~/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu-linearb-imc-aug26/b4b949b6-…jsonl:

    18:42:28.470Z  {"type":"system","subtype":"model_consent_fallback",
                    "content":"Switched to Opus 5 (1M context) — now your default model ·
                               Fable 5 requires usage credits · /model to change"}

It sits one line before the first message the new model served, i.e. it is the client's own,
timestamped record of a switch the guard otherwise has to infer from the served-model tail.

## Task
Decide what the guard should do with `model_consent_fallback` and implement it. Two seams,
and they are NOT symmetric — the reason this is a bead and not a one-liner:
- as EXPECTED evidence it is the opposite of `model_refusal_fallback`: a consent row records
  a switch the USER accepted and the client PERSISTED machine-wide, so its target must never
  become an expectation (that is exactly the dotfiles-cpqi cascade).
- as a DETECTION/ledger fact it is valuable: it names the moment and the reason ("Fable 5
  requires usage credits"), which is what made the cpqi investigation possible at all, and a
  ledger row for it would have surfaced the flip within one tool round instead of 15 minutes.

Check the client's row inventory before designing: `model_consent_fallback` may not be the
only unhandled subtype (grep the fleet's transcripts for distinct .subtype values).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The row's semantics are decided and written down (ledger-only vs expectation input),
      with the cpqi cascade named as the reason for whichever way it goes
- [ ] Fixture is REAL BYTES from a transcript that carries the row (the b4b949b6 one does)
- [ ] A case that fails before the change and passes after, in
      agents/hooks/test/test-post-tool-model-guard.sh, plus a mutant in mutate-model-guard.sh
- [ ] A subtype census across the fleet's transcripts recorded on the bead, so the next
      unhandled shape is a known unknown rather than a surprise

title: pulse-inject assert_seat is jail-blind: it proves the BWRAP process env, not the Claude inside — reported 'seat verified' on wrong-account jailed runs
description:
## Context
Surfaced by the zf2q builder (2026-08-10, ~/explore tick-jail fix): pulse-inject's assert_seat reads /proc/<pid>/environ of the launched process to prove the seat pin. For a JAILED tick that pid is the bwrap launcher, not the Claude inside the jail — so the assert reported 'seat verified' for every wrong-account run during the zf2q investigation, while the in-jail session was actually authenticated as primary. Same defect family as dotfiles-cxle (success-shaped output from a check that did not observe the real thing) and sibling to dotfiles-d5n3.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Pre-zf2q-fix launcher (or any construction where the jail interior resolves a different config dir than the launcher env): fire a jailed tick with a --config-dir pin.
2. pulse-inject's assert_seat reads the bwrap process environ → sees the pin → declares seat verified.
3. Inside the jail, the session's resolved config dir / oauthAccount is a DIFFERENT account. The assert never looked there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Negative control: a deliberately mis-seated jailed launch must fail the assert (watched fail)

title: bug: vault-sync reports a benign flock DEFERRAL as 'blocked — parked on you'
description:
## Symptom
harnessd dashboard shows the claude-vault-sync loop as BLOCKED: "fired 31m ago,
tick BLOCKED - parked on you" (state.json /loops[11], 2026-07-28T14:00:43Z),
while both vault tiers are in fact fully pushed (memory + transcripts each
0/0 vs origin/main; both .last-success-* stamps at 14:00). Nothing is parked
on a human. It is a FALSE ALARM.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have the hourly claude-vault-sync.service and a pulse-dispatch-remote.sh
   loop (its "sync T2/T3 (local push)" step) start vault-sync.sh in the same
   second - both are scheduled on the hour today.
2. The loser of the flock race in agents/vault/transcripts-lib.sh:333
   (`flock -w 10 9 || exit 3`) returns tier status 3 = DEFERRED.
3. Observe: that run prints "== vault-sync DEGRADED - memory=ok
   transcripts=deferred (exit 10) ==" and appends a ledger row with
   outcome "blocked", at the same ts as the winning run's "done" row.
4. Observe the dashboard renders the loop BLOCKED / "parked on you".

Synthetic repro for a test: force one tier's push function to return 3 with a
fresh .last-success-<tier> stamp present, and assert the run's exit code and
ledger outcome.

Live evidence (journalctl --user, 2026-07-28, zig-computer):
  14:00:43 vault-sync[1083379]: == vault-sync DEGRADED - memory=ok transcripts=deferred (exit 10) ==
  14:00:43 vault-sync[1083457]: == vault-sync OK - memory=ok transcripts=ok (exit 0) ==

## Root cause
vault-sync.sh's verdict block (section 4) treats EVERY non-zero, non-inert tier
status as bad (`tier_counts && [ rc -ne 0 ]`), so DEFERRED -> DEGRADED, exit 10,
ledger `outcome:"blocked"`.

Both runs append to the SAME ledger with the SAME ts. harnessd's newestRow()
tie-break (internal/gen/loop.go, outcomeSignificance blocked=2 > done=1 >
quiet=0) then deliberately prefers the `blocked` row over the `done` row -
correct behaviour on its side, fed a wrong row.

2 of the 3 `blocked` rows in the last 200 ledger rows are this false alarm
(note "memory=ok transcripts=deferred"); the third is a REAL secret-gate block.

## Why this matters
This is dotfiles-cxle inverted: a loop that cries wolf. A backup alarm that
fires when nothing is wrong trains its reader to ignore it, which is exactly
how the next REAL 120-run outage gets missed.

## The fix
In vault-sync.sh's verdict block, DEFERRED (tier status 3) must not, on its own,
produce a DEGRADED verdict / non-zero exit / `blocked` ledger row. A deferral
means "another run holds the lock and is doing this work" - a benign no-op, not
a human-blocking condition.

The alarm must NOT be weakened, only re-aimed. Required behaviour:
  - deferred tier + its .last-success-<tier> stamp is FRESH (< STALE_HOURS)
      -> exit 0, verdict word reflects the deferral (e.g. "OK (deferred)"),
         ledger outcome "quiet" (allowed by pulse-ledger-lint ALLOWED_OUTCOMES).
         The `summary` string must still read `transcripts=deferred` so the log
         does not claim a push happened.
  - deferred tier + stamp >= STALE_HOURS old
      -> unchanged escalation: STALE, exit 2x, ledger outcome "blocked".
         (This backstop is what makes the above safe: a permanently wedged lock
         still reddens the unit within STALE_HOURS.)
  - deferred tier + NO stamp at all (never succeeded on this box)
      -> DEGRADED, exit 1x, outcome "blocked" (conservative; matches the
         existing "no stamp => DEGRADED but never STALE" rule).
  - FAILED (1) / BLOCKED (2) tiers: behaviour completely unchanged.
  - memory tier deferral (vault-lib.sh:228, same `flock -w 10 9 || exit 3`)
    is the same class and gets the same treatment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A run in which one tier returns 3 (deferred) with a fresh success stamp
      exits 0 and appends a ledger row whose outcome is NOT "blocked".
- [ ] That run's stdout verdict still names the deferral (grep-able
      `transcripts=deferred`) - no silent "ok".
- [ ] A run in which a tier returns 3 and that tier's stamp is >= STALE_HOURS
      old still exits non-zero (2x) with ledger outcome "blocked".
- [ ] A run in which a tier returns 3 with NO stamp exits 1x / "blocked".
- [ ] All existing cases in agents/vault/test/vault-sync-alarm-test.sh still pass.
- [ ] New regression cases added to that test file, demonstrated FAILING against
      the pre-fix script and PASSING after (paste both runs' output).
close_reason: done

title: tailscale/acl.jsonc: server-to-server SSH rule uses accept (check requires user identity)
description:
## Problem
Just-added server-to-server SSH rule (bead dotfiles-qix, commit 32ea167) used `action: check`. Tailscale admin rejected the policy: `Error: [ssh] "check" action does not support tags in src`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Paste the post-dotfiles-qix ACL into Tailscale admin → Access Controls
2. Click Preview / Save
3. Observe: `Error: [ssh] "check" action does not support tags in src`

## Root cause
Tailscale's `check` SSH action requires the source device to have a human user identity (so they can re-authenticate). Tagged devices (`tag:server`) are machine-only — no human user, nothing to re-auth. Tailscale validates this and refuses the policy.

This was not documented prominently — we discovered it on first paste-attempt. Real Tailscale ACL gotcha worth documenting.

## Fix
Change the server-to-server rule's action from `check` → `accept`. Update the inline comment block to explain the constraint and acknowledge the security trade-off (server compromise has no re-auth gate for SSH'ing into other servers; bounded by the fact that server compromise is already a large problem).

## Regression guard
- Add this gotcha to the `/zig-zone` runbook's "Tailscale gotchas we paid for" section

title: bug: handoff_read_path silently serves another seat's note on a reverse rename
description:
## Context
agents/lib/handoff-path.sh:125-152 warns only when the scoped note is MISSING. The reverse rename — a window renamed ONTO a name that already has a note — resolves, finds the file, and serves another seat's handoff silently. That is the di->pulse failure mode (bd-msi5) with the surviving half unpatched. Found by Cluster B review 2026-08-08.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Two registered seats alpha (window a) and beta (window b), each with a scoped handoff note refs/session-handoff--{a,b}.md
2. tmux rename-window a -> b (the reverse rename: a window renamed ONTO a name that already has a note)
3. From the renamed window, source handoff-path.sh and call handoff_read_path .
4. BEFORE the fix: returns beta's note at rc=0 with EMPTY stderr — the session silently onboards from another seat's private handoff. AFTER: rc=3, empty stdout, loud refusal naming the mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A regression test that FAILS before the fix: rename window A to existing name B, assert loud diagnostic (or refusal) instead of silent serve
- [ ] Mechanism agreed with seat-resolve-lib-btti (a note carries its owner; the resolver compares) — not a parallel invention

title: lexicon: send-keys safety guards read the glyph from the window NAME — blind after ylw2
description:
## Context

Discovered during dotfiles-ylw2 impl (2026-08-11). The ylw2 ruling moves the lexicon
glyph OUT of the tmux window name and into a per-window @glyph option. The ruling
covered NAME RESOLUTION (the _seat_strip_glyph / strip_lexicon helpers stay and become
no-ops on bare names, so both name forms resolve during rollout) — but it did NOT
enumerate the readers that consume the glyph as a FACT, by matching the window name's
leading character. Those go BLIND the moment a window normalizes to bare: every window
reads as "no glyph", i.e. not-blocked and not-busy.

These are SAFETY guards, not cosmetics. Their whole job is to refuse send-keys into a
pane sitting in a modal dialog — typing there answers Zig's open question with the
default.

Inventory (all in demesne, all reading the NAME):
  * agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh:676-677 (in-flight guard) and :1355 (blocked defer)
  * agents/scheduler/pulse-retry.sh:225-226 and :438
  * agents/scheduler/seat-molt.sh:595 (is_blocked) and :599-600 (is_busy)
  * agents/scheduler/api-stall-recover.sh:369 (blocked skip)
  * agents/scheduler/pulse-escalate.sh:788-792 (stale-bell reconciler) and :854

## Steps to Reproduce

On a scratch tmux server (NOT zig-computer), after the ylw2 change lands:

    tmux -L t -f /dev/null new-session -d -s scratch -n marshal
    tmux -L t set-option -w -t '=scratch:marshal' @glyph "$(printf '\U1F514')"

The window name is bare 'marshal' — exactly what tmux-status.sh now produces. Run
pulse-inject (or seat-molt / api-stall-recover) against that window: the guard tests
the NAME prefix, the name is bare, the guard does not fire, and it types into a pane
sitting in a modal dialog. Before ylw2 that window was named with the glyph baked in
and the guard deferred.

## Task

Give each of these a glyph SOURCE that survives the ruling, in this preference order:
  1. tmux show-options -w -t <window> -qv @glyph — the new source of truth;
  2. the window-name prefix — transition fallback for a window no hook has touched yet
     (same rationale as the strip helpers);
  3. optionally the per-session SSoT /tmp/claude-lexicon/<session_id> where the caller
     already has a session id.

ONE shared helper (lexicon_window_glyph <sock> <window> in agents/lib/) beats five
hand-rolled reads — the five existing copies of strip_lexicon are already the warning.

WARNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTER — the false-idle half of ylw2 changes what the working
glyph MEANS to these guards. A session that has ended its turn but is waiting on
background subagents now carries the working glyph (was the ready glyph). pulse-inject's
in-flight guard will therefore defer a tick into such a session where it previously
injected. That is arguably correct (real work is in flight) but it is a BEHAVIOR CHANGE
on the drain's hottest path and must be decided deliberately, not inherited by accident.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each of the five scripts reads @glyph first, name prefix only as fallback
- [ ] Existing suites (test-pulse-inject.sh, test-seat-molt.sh, test-pulse-retry.sh,
      test-api-stall-recover.sh, test-pulse-escalate.sh) stay green, with cases ADDED
      for the @glyph-only (bare-name) window — the post-ylw2 world
- [ ] Made-to-fail: a bare-named window with a blocked @glyph must make pulse-inject
      defer; break the new read and the case goes red
- [ ] The working-glyph-while-waiting-on-subagents behavior change is decided on record
close_reason: Landed on demesne main 76be894 (FF, pushed+ls-remote-verified, tree-identical to scrutinized HEAD). All nine glyph-as-fact reader sites across five scheduler scripts route through agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh (@glyph option first, name-prefix fallback — order-independent with the parked ylw2 merge); runtime-proven with real pulse-inject on a private socket: defers typing NOTHING on both name forms, injects on both controls, fresher-option-wins. Missing-library behavior is now LOUD and honest everywhere: four consumers announce + set LEXICON_READER_MISSING with distinguishing reasons on the real record surfaces (assumed-blocked-no-glyph-reader / deferred-no-glyph-reader / refused-no-glyph-reader, the latter deliberately inside escalate's molt-refusal set :1034), pulse-escalate's rc-78 refusal covered (45b/45c), lib-less environments genuine with controls. New cases hermetic on a private socket (G1-G5); inject 197/197 no-flake at re-scrutiny. Evidence chain: panel REJECT (13 confirmed/11 refuted) → fix 76be894 → fresh-agent SHIP, logged here. Follow-ups: sug9 (legacy non-hermetic block + early-exit traps), txnv (other glyph writers both-surfaces audit). UNBLOCKS dotfiles-ylw2 (parked by tap-conservation directive — see its PARKED comment for the exact resume state).

comments.text:
## Handoff — 2026-08-11, builder (Opus 5), dotfiles-u1g1

COMMIT (demesne, worktree-agent-a07fac99ae27c9686, /tmp/demesne-agent-a07fac99ae27c9686,
UNPUSHED; sequenced AFTER 6dc5ac9 which is dotfiles-d5ez). SHA in the closing note.
20 files: agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh + test-lexicon-window.sh (new), the five
schedulers, their five suites, six mutation harnesses, tools/githooks/pre-commit.

THE HELPER, and why it lives where it does
  agents/lib/lexicon-window.sh — `lexicon_window_glyph <target> [name]` plus
  `lexicon_glyph_is_blocked` / `_is_busy` and the one-call `lexicon_window_blocked`
  / `_busy`. Source order: `show-options -w -t <target> -qv @glyph` FIRST, the
  name's leading glyph as the transition fallback — correct before the ylw2 merge
  and after, in either merge order.
  HOME: agents/lib, not agents/hooks/lib/lexicon-map.sh. lexicon-map.sh is the pure
  WRITER-side map (hook event -> token -> glyph); it touches no tmux, and putting a
  tmux-invoking reader in it would couple every hook to a server. agents/lib is the
  tier the schedulers already source (seat-resolve, handoff-path, tmux-send).
  BUT it SOURCES lexicon-map.sh for LEXICON_STRIP_RE rather than retyping the glyph
  alternation — five hand-rolled copies of that regex is the drift this bead is
  about — with a literal fallback for a tree that lacks the hooks dir.
  ONE I/O SEAM, `_lexwin_tmux`, the tmux-send.sh idiom: seat-molt redefines it to
  its socket-pinned TM, so the socket rule still holds.
  📬 is deliberately NOT in the recognised set: the strip helpers strip it for NAME
  RESOLUTION, but it has never been a lexicon STATE and no guard ever treated it as
  blocked or busy. Reading it as a glyph would be a behaviour change under a refactor.

CONVERTED (no site keeps a private name-glyph read)
  pulse-inject  §3.5 bell defer + _turn_in_flight/_same_loop_running (now take the GLYPH)
  pulse-retry   3d bell skip + turn_in_flight; the window target is `=$session:$name`,
                an EXACT-name target, which is exactly what ylw2's stable names buy
  seat-molt     is_modal/is_busy take the glyph; new win_glyph reads with NO name arg
                (post-ylw2 that is ONE tmux call, two only in the legacy shape);
                win_name deleted, it had no other caller
  api-stall-recover  the bell refusal, keyed off the pane id as a window target
  pulse-escalate     rung 1's "which glyph is lying" + the seneschal guard
  Where the library is missing: four scripts fail CLOSED (constant 🔔 => refuse to
  type). pulse-escalate instead REFUSES TO RUN (verdict failed-no-lexicon-reader,
  exit 78) because its two consumers want OPPOSITE defaults — "assume blocked" makes
  rung 1 claim a reconcile it never did, "assume clear" injects into a blocked
  seneschal. No safe constant exists there, so there is no stub.

SCOPE I ADDED, and why it was not optional
  pulse-escalate's rung 1 now CLEARS BOTH SURFACES (rename + `set-option -w -u
  @glyph`) and verifies by re-reading the glyph over the freshly-listed name.
  Converting only the READ would have been WORSE than the blindness: on a bare name
  the old post-condition ("the name equals its own stripped form") reads true
  immediately, so every tick would log a RENAMED/reconciled it never performed,
  record the episode closed, and `continue` past the whole escalation ladder. Case
  46c is that scenario, driven by a new PE_GLYPH_STICKY knob (the option-surface twin
  of PE_RENAME_NOOP: tmux answers rc 0 and the option does not move).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THE BEAD ASKED TO BE DECIDED ON RECORD
  The bead warns that ylw2's false-idle half makes a session waiting on background
  subagents carry the WORKING glyph, so pulse-inject's in-flight guard would defer a
  --fresh tick where it previously injected. That is NOT decided here and NOT changed
  here: this bead moved the glyph's SOURCE, not its meaning, and the guard's
  predicate is byte-for-byte the same one (🧠/🌀 = busy). The change of meaning
  belongs to ylw2's own merge, where the renderer decides what to paint; nothing in
  this commit alters which token a window carries.

SUITES (all green, real counts)
  agents/lib/test-lexicon-window.sh   41 (NEW) — L1-L9 against a recorder (the only
      way to prove WHICH source answered), L10-L16a against a real tmux on a private
      -S socket (session lexwin-suite, kill-server in the trap)
  test-pulse-escalate.sh  57 -> 63   (46a-46f: the post-ylw2 window shape)
  test-seat-molt.sh       69 -> 74   (10p/10pn/10q, 24b/24bn)
  test-pulse-inject.sh   190 -> 192  (6b/6c, on a real server)
  test-pulse-retry.sh     42 -> 44   (4b/4c)
  test-api-stall-recover.sh 41 -> 43 (4b/4c)
  Every new case has a NON-VACUITY CONTROL beside it — the same bare window with the
  option unset, which must still inject/molt/nudge. Without them a guard that refused
  everything would pass.

MUTATION HARNESSES
  Re-derived against the moved lines: escalate M1/M3/M4/M17, seat-molt M2/M4,
  api-stall M5, t5fj R2/R3/R6/I2/I3. Case-count assertions bumped deliberately
  (EXPECT_ESC_CASES 56->63, EXPECT_MOLT_CASES 69->74).
  FOUR NEW MUTANTS restore the name-only read — escalate M25 (and M26, the option
  never cleared), seat-molt M2b, api-stall M5b — and each dies ONLY on the post-ylw2
  cases while every legacy case stays green. That asymmetry IS the defect's shape.
  Four harnesses (t5fj, pulse-seat, pulse-model, api-stall) gained `ln -sfn
  "$SRC/../lib" "$WORK/lib"`: they copy the script into a scratch dir, and without
  the real lib beside it every mutant would have measured the fail-closed degrade
  instead of the guard.
  All six re-run green: escalate 26/26 mutants, seat-molt 6/6, api-stall 16/16, t5fj
  14/14, pulse-seat 5/5, pulse-model 7/7, o3qj 11/11 — each on the cases it names.

MADE TO FAIL (library level, both passes, short /tmp paths on purpose)
  A scratch tree of SYMLINKED scripts beside a real lib dir, so the reader can be
  swapped with nothing else changed. Control pass (real reader): 416/416 across all
  five suites. Broken pass (a lexicon-window.sh that reads the NAME only): 11 red,
  ALL post-ylw2, every legacy case green —
    inject 6b · retry 4b (x2) · seat-molt 10p + 10pn · api-stall 4b ·
    escalate 46a/46b/46c/46d/46f
  seat-molt 10pn prints the harm literally: `typed: /clear /onboard` into the pane
  holding the dialog.
  ⚠️ FOR THE NEXT PERSON: my first attempt put that scratch tree under the session
  scratchpad and every seat-molt case came back failed-no-window. That was NOT the
  reader — test-seat-molt puts its tmux socket under $TMPDIR and a unix socket path
  is capped at ~108 bytes. A deep TMPDIR silently breaks that suite in a way that
  looks exactly like a regression. Keep scratch trees shallow (/tmp/<short>.XXXXXX).

RUNTIME VERIFICATION (real pulse-inject.sh, real tmux, private -S socket, session
u1g1-demo — never zig-computer, kill-server in the trap, pane runs `cat` so
keystrokes are recorded not executed):
  bare name + @glyph 🔔        name=[pulse]   @glyph=[🔔] -> deferred-blocked-on-human, typed nothing
  control, option unset        name=[pulse]   @glyph=[]   -> injected, TYPED
  legacy 🔔 name, no option    name=[🔔 pulse] @glyph=[]   -> deferred-blocked-on-human, typed nothing
  control, name stripped       name=[pulse]   @glyph=[]   -> injected, TYPED
  stale 🔔 NAME + fresh ✅ option                          -> injected (the option is fresher and decides)

TMUX FINDING worth carrying (pinned as test-lexicon-window L16/L16a and in the
library header): `show-options -qv` on a window that no longer exists answers empty,
rc 0 — but `display-message -p -t <missing> '#{window_name}'` does NOT fail, it
answers the session's CURRENT window name. So the no-name form of the reader can
report a NEIGHBOUR's glyph for a vanished window. Every production caller passes the
name it already resolved; seat-molt's win_glyph is the exception and passes a
concrete pane id, where the failure direction is a refusal to type.

GATE: tools/githooks/pre-commit maps lexicon-window.sh (and its own suite) to all
five consumer suites — the dotfiles-dijt shape exactly: the library's own suite would
stay green while every consumer went blind. It is a slow gate on purpose.

title: an empty hostname -s silently disables BOTH tick attribution AND gateway routing at once
description:
Found by the dotfiles-ahrd agent while exercising the empty-hostname case it was asked to stop reasoning about and actually run. CROSS-REPO (~/explore).

## Context
tick-jailed.sh derives two independent things from the SAME `hostname -s` call:
  - X-Machine-Origin (the attribution header -> agentgateway_group)
  - the per-host env lookup `~/.<host>.zshenv` that supplies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL

Measured with a PATH-shimmed `hostname` printing nothing (exit 0): the launch SURVIVES
(fail-open, no wedge — good), but with no tmux `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` is UNSET, and
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` goes unset too.

## Why this is worse than either half alone
A tick in that state is simultaneously UNATTRIBUTED and OFF-GATEWAY. It does not appear
in pico requests.db at all — not as `unknown`, not as a row with a null group, but as
NOTHING, because it never traverses the gateway. So the one instrument that would reveal
the attribution loss is the same instrument the failure removes from the path.

That is the dotfiles-cxle shape (the consumer reports success while the step stopped
working) with the detector inside the blast radius: an operator looking at pico sees
fewer rows, which is indistinguishable from a quiet period.

## Steps to Reproduce
Shim `hostname` on PATH to print nothing and exit 0, then run a jailed tick through the
TICK_JAIL_EXEC seam. Observe ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS unset AND ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL unset.

## Candidate fix
Decouple the two derivations, and make an unresolvable hostname LOUD rather than
silently degrading — a jailed tick that cannot identify its own machine should still
route through the gateway (falling back to a literal like "unresolved-host" for the
header) so the request remains visible. Losing the label is survivable; losing the
instrument is not.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] an empty/failing hostname still routes through the gateway
- [ ] the attribution header degrades to an explicit sentinel, never to absent
- [ ] the condition is logged loudly at the tick level
- [ ] covered in test-tick-jailed.sh, with a mutant observed failing it
close_reason: Fixed in ~/explore 0e6152a — AND the bead's framing was partly wrong, which the agent pushed back on correctly. MY ERROR: I wrote 'disables BOTH at once' from the previous agent's report. The decoupling was already STRUCTURAL — steps 1 (inherited value) and 2 (CC_NO_GATEWAY) never consult the hostname, so an inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL always survived a hostname failure. The measured failure only looked welded because the repro used 'env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL'. Verified myself against the source. The real deliverable is therefore the sentinel + loudness, not a decoupling: X-Machine-Origin degrades to the literal 'unresolved-host' and is NEVER absent, plus two loud 'tick-jail: WARNING' stderr lines. Case 19 now pins the decoupling that was previously untested. Deliberately NOT done: an /etc/hostname fallback — a second derivation of the machine's name that can disagree with the first inverts this bug rather than fixing it. Also caught, and I had not raised it: the sentinel must never reach the per-host lookup, because '~/.unresolved-host.zshenv' would turn a missing hostname into a plantable path — the gateway block uses raw _host, never sanitized _mhost, and that is now a stated invariant. Honest residual: a box whose only base-URL source is the per-host file stays off-gateway when it cannot name itself; that file cannot be located without a hostname. Three mutants, each asserted applied; the third was added because the second killed case 19 via the header, leaving 19's base-URL half unproven.

title: decision: a VPS gateway tunnel failure fails HARD, no silent fallback to api.anthropic.com
description:
## Context
dotfiles-ogkz puts marketing-vps behind pico agentgateway over a chained SSH tunnel.
If the tunnel dies, the fork is: silently fall back to api.anthropic.com (claude keeps
working, o11y is lost) or fail hard (claude is dead until healed).

Zig was not asked; this was a decide-and-proceed call made while building.

## Decision
Fail HARD. No automatic fallback. Recovery is the self-healing timer
(ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh, VPS-initiated) plus the existing manual hatch CC_NO_GATEWAY=1.

## Why
Silent fallback is not a hypothetical failure mode here — it is the EXACT bug
dotfiles-t6to, where durable panes bypassed the gateway and pico request log went
blind for days with nothing alarming, because "bypassing an o11y proxy is
indistinguishable from being idle." Building an automatic version of that failure
would be shipping the bug on purpose.

## Reversibility
Cheap and local: one branch in the wrapper or the zshenv.

## What would change my mind
If VPS pulse rows start failing on tunnel blips more than the o11y is worth. That is
measurable — count blocked ticks against gateway downtime.
notes:
## OUTCOME — the cost landed within a day (2026-08-04)

This decision was made 2026-08-03 with an explicit "what would change my mind" clause:
*"If VPS pulse rows start failing on tunnel blips more than the o11y is worth."*

That evidence arrived immediately, and larger than the clause anticipated. Per the
marketing-vps session handoff (899c6004, commit 26d08d8): **pico lost its internet for
~6.5 hours** — last gateway request 07:23:49Z, first after 14:00:07Z, **zero rows in
between**. Because routing is fail-hard with no fallback BY THIS DECISION, `claude` died
**fleet-wide**, not just on marketing-vps. A scheduled `pulse-digest` tick was injected
into an API-dead session and lost.

So the blast radius was wider than I reasoned about when I made it: I weighed a dead
TUNNEL (marketing-vps only) and did not weigh a dead GATEWAY (every host that routes
through pico, which is all of them).

## The decision still stands, because the mitigation is better than the alternative
That session shipped `agents/scheduler/gateway-switch.sh` (`off|on|status`, `--dry-run`,
52-case suite) plus `~/.break-glass.txt` on both boxes and an `agents/infra.md` runbook.
That is the right answer, and it is strictly better than the silent fallback this
decision rejected: the bypass is now ONE COMMAND and it is LOUD — a human chooses it,
`status` reports who is bypassed, and nothing silently stops being observed. Silent
fallback would have made the same 6.5h outage invisible, which is the dotfiles-t6to
failure this decision exists to prevent.

## What I would do differently
Name the blast radius in the decision itself. "Fails hard" is not one property — it is
one per host that depends on the failed component, and pico's gateway is a fleet-wide
single point of failure. A decision bead that says "fail hard" should enumerate WHO dies.

## Still true, still watch
`CC_NO_GATEWAY=1` (fixed 2026-08-03, dotfiles-20rx) and now `gateway-switch.sh off` are
the two working escapes. Neither helps a session already wedged mid-turn.

title: dream: d2 laurel placement never commits the seat-history append — dream must finish the stroke
description:
## Context
Routed from the seneschal at Zig's direction (2026-08-09 morning-brief follow-up; Zig + seneschal walked it). The maiden fleet dream (2026-08-09) placed the first laurel — dive / explore-sirc / e99b9db — via seat-history.sh: the append + integrity-hash update were correct on disk, and dream committed its OWN ledger in ~/explore (95e3cc5, 05:31 PT) minutes later, but left refs/seats/dive.history.md sitting dirty in ~/dotfiles. The Master of Works found it at onboard and committed it (dotfiles 7ca11c3).

agents/skills/dream/SKILL.md §d2 (~lines 468–517) specifies placement in full — atomic append, laurels.jsonl row, refusal semantics, ledger count — but never assigns the git commit of the seat-history file. Verified 2026-08-09: no commit/push step anywhere in d2.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a dream tick that places a laurel (dream.py laurels --place per d2).
2. Observe seat-history.sh appends refs/seats/<seat>.history.md in ~/dotfiles and updates the integrity hash — correct on disk, validate-seats passes.
3. Observe the tick commits its own ledger in ~/explore and ends; git status in ~/dotfiles shows the history file dirty. Live instance: 2026-08-09, dive laurel, dirty until 7ca11c3.

## Why dream should finish the stroke
(a) The history file's integrity checksum is validated at COMMIT time — if dream doesn't commit, its write gets validated on some OTHER seat's later commit with zero context; the writer should be the one who trips the gate.
(b) Silent-success class: dream's ledger row says laurels:1 with proof green while the durable record isn't in git — a tree accident loses the laurel the ledger forever claims was placed.
(c) Fleet consistency: seat identity renders from the dotfiles clone, so unpushed means pico shows the seat without its laurel.

## Fix shape
d2 gains a closing step: after `dream.py laurels --place` succeeds, commit the seat-history append with EXPLICIT path (git add refs/seats/<seat>.history.md) + push, per the shared-tree idiom (merge-never-rebase on rejection). Two-writers hazard already covered by existing doctrine — single cross-repo writer, explicit path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] d2 ends with the commit+push step, explicit-path form, citing the shared-tree idiom.
- [ ] The step covers the cross-repo nature (dream runs in ~/explore, the history file lives in ~/dotfiles).
- [ ] TOOLKIT.md /dream entry updated in the same change (post-write-skill.sh nudges).

## Evidence
laurel = dive / explore-sirc / e99b9db · dream ledger row ts 2026-08-09T12:31:32Z in ~/explore/refs/dream-ledger.jsonl · explore commit 95e3cc5 · cleanup commit dotfiles 7ca11c3 · skill text agents/skills/dream/SKILL.md d2

title: claude-code: wire to local models on pico (background tasks + long-running)
description:
## Context (migrated from `~/explore/.beads/explore-sak` 2026-05-25)
Originally tracked as `explore-sak` in the umbrella explore beads. Per bead-location discipline (dotfiles ONLY for true dotfiles work), this work belongs in dotfiles' own `.beads/` because the deliverable is tooling configuration that lives in dotfiles: `claude/settings.json`, environment vars, claude-code-router config, launchd plists for headless mode.

## Goal
Use local models on pico (Qwen3-Coder MLX, Laguna Ollama, Trinity MLX) as alternative backends for Claude Code on zig — specifically for **background tasks + long-running work + 24/7 agents** where Anthropic API token cost matters.

Foundation for downstream arcs:
- `~/explore/.beads/explore-nfc` (24/7 scientific research agent)
- `~/explore/blightmud/.beads/blightmud-hgi` (MUD agent for Cleft of Dimensions)

- NPM-installable
- Translates Anthropic Messages API ↔ OpenAI-compat
- Supports per-scenario routing rules (background / reasoning / long-context / web-search)

title: mlx_lm.server: lazy-load mode doesn't apply chat_template.jinja for tool use (suspected; needs more isolation)
description:
## Context

Suspected mlx_lm.server upstream bug surfaced during Wave 13 G16 root-cause work (dotfiles-ukx.9). When `mlx_lm.server` is started WITHOUT a `--model` flag (lazy-load mode), it appears to NOT apply the model's `chat_template.jinja` correctly for tool-use requests. When started WITH `--model X` (eager-load), the same model's template applies properly and tools work.

## Evidence

Two `mlx_lm.server` processes on pico running same Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B weights:
- PID 45256 :8081 (launchd `com.zig.mlx.plist`) — NO --model flag → tools REFUSED 0/3 trials (deterministic temp=0+seed=42)
- PID 83718 :5802 (spawned by llama-swap for qwen3-coder) — `--model mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit` → tools PASS 3/3 trials

Same model weights, same chat_template.jinja on disk (verified). Same request body shape. Only difference: server's startup `--model` flag.

llama-swap doesn't transform tools (verified via source-read research, ukx.8 + ukx.9). So the divergence is mlx_lm.server-internal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Confirm lazy-load chat-template gap by restarting :8081 with `--model X` flag → expect tools to start working
- [ ] Confirm by toggling: rip --model out → tools refuse; put --model back → tools work
- [ ] Inspect mlx_lm.server source for the lazy-load `_tokenize` path vs eager-load path; identify where templates diverge
- [ ] Check mlx-lm GitHub issues for existing reports
- [ ] If novel bug: file at github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm with minimal repro
- [ ] If known: link to existing issue + workaround status

## Status

DEFERRED — needs more isolation before filing upstream. Per user 2026-05-26: "we can't file a bug until we test it more and I understand it more."

## Don't fix the symptom

The G16 workaround (route via llama-swap, which spawns --model-preloaded instances) IS the production mitigation. This bead is about UNDERSTANDING + UPSTREAM REPORT, not changing routing. Routing is settled per G16.

## See also

- GUARDRAILS G16 — current production routing rule
- refs/research/research-ccr-tool-schema-followup.md — empirical evidence
- refs/research/research-llama-swap-toolshim.md — falsifies "llama-swap shim" hypothesis
- Bead dotfiles-ukx.9 (closed) — sibling research
notes: MOVED 2026-06-06 to local-coding-models-470 (bead-location-discipline pass; mlx-server bugs belong in local-coding-models project tree, not dotfiles infra).

title: ccr: Anthropic→OpenAI tool-schema transformer produces shape llama-swap returns 404 for (smoke-evidence from ukx.3)
description:
## Context

Surfaced 2026-05-26 via `dotfiles-ukx.3` smoke-run (ukx.3 closed). The ukx.3 subagent built the parity smoke-environment, ran scenarios 01/02/05 through both Opus and local backends, and found:

- **Routing works**: CCR's `Router.background` mapping triggers correctly (`claude-haiku-4-5` model → `pico-mlx,qwen3-coder` provider+model). CCR logs confirm: `Using background model for claude-haiku-4-5`.
- **Plain text completion works**: direct curl `{"model":"pico-mlx,qwen3-coder","messages":[...]}` to CCR returns Qwen3 PONG (G16 receipt holds).
- **Tool-using requests through CCR fail**: CCR's transformer outputs `Error from provider(pico-mlx,qwen3-coder: 404)` on every tool-shaped Claude Code request. **The 404 is from llama-swap**, not Anthropic-side.

This is the next-tier blocker the G16 + G17 work didn't surface (those settled raw routing + headless transport). The actual transformation step CCR performs to convert Anthropic Messages tool definitions into the OpenAI Chat Completions shape produces a request that llama-swap returns 404 for.

## Hypothesis (needs investigation)

Possible root causes:
1. **CCR's transformer URL path mismatch** — maybe it POSTs to a path llama-swap doesn't expose (e.g., `/v1/chat/completions` vs `/v1/messages`, or appended `?tools=...` query).
2. **Method mismatch** — POST vs PUT vs the chunked-encoding path.
3. **llama-swap config mismatch** — the alias `qwen3-coder` rewrites correctly for plain text but somehow not for tool-using requests (different `useModelName` resolution path?).
4. **Header issue** — CCR may forward an `x-api-key` or `authorization` header llama-swap rejects.
5. **Tool-schema shape per se** — CCR converts Anthropic tool definitions (Edit, Bash) into a `tools[]` array shape that llama-swap's proxy logic doesn't recognize as a valid Chat Completions request.

(1)+(2) are most likely given 404 specifically (vs 400 = bad request shape, vs 422 = validation). The 404 means "no such endpoint" or "no such model at this endpoint."

## Steps to Reproduce (smoke evidence already captured)

`~/dotfiles/claude/sandbox/results/01-trivial-rename-local-*.md`, `02-easy-add-function-local-*.md`, `05-toolstressy-parallel-local-*.md` all show:
- Routing trace: PASS (CCR logs the right provider+model)
- llama-swap response: `404`
- Wrapper exit code: non-zero

Compare to:
- `~/dotfiles/claude/sandbox/results/01-*-opus-*.md` (PASS via Anthropic)
- Direct curl PONG via llama-swap (PASS, no 404)
- The difference is CCR's transformer in the middle.

## Task

1. **Capture the exact request CCR sends to llama-swap** for a tool-using CC request:
   - Enable `LOG=true` in CCR config (already set per ukx.5 README)
   - Run the smoke `claude/sandbox/run-scenario.sh scenarios/01-trivial-rename.md local`
   - Tail `~/.claude-code-router/claude-code-router.log` for the outgoing POST to llama-swap (full request body + headers + URL)
2. **Test the same request directly via curl** (bypass CCR) to llama-swap with the captured shape — see if 404 still happens
3. **If 404 reproduces**: investigate llama-swap's request routing logic; check `~/.config/llama-swap/config.yaml` for any tool-specific config; compare to plain-text request shape
4. **If 404 doesn't reproduce**: the gap is in CCR's transformer; cross-reference `research-ccr-tool-schema.md` for the transformer source-level analysis, identify what's different for tool-using path
5. **Fix path**: likely either (a) llama-swap config tweak, (b) CCR transformer fix (potentially upstream PR), or (c) custom transformer config in CCR's `transformer: { use: [...] }` for the pico-mlx provider
6. **Verify fix**: re-run scenarios 01/02/05 through local backend, confirm PASS

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Exact CCR-to-llama-swap request shape captured + documented
- [ ] Root cause identified (one of the 5 hypotheses or new finding)
- [ ] Fix applied + verified by re-running smoke scenarios
- [ ] G16 amended: "llama-swap PASSES raw OpenAI tool calls" + "CCR→llama-swap PASSES tool-using CC requests after this fix"
- [ ] Research note at `~/explore/local-coding-models/refs/research/research-ccr-llamaswap-tool-404.md`

## Why this matters

ukx.3 + the smoke environment exists to measure Opus vs local parity. Right now the parity number is **0% for any tool-using scenario** because the routing breaks before the model even runs. That's not a model-quality result; it's a transport bug. Until ukx.12 is fixed, the parity benchmark can't honestly report local performance for Claude-Code-shaped tool work.

## See also
- dotfiles-ukx.3 — the smoke environment that surfaced this (closed)
- dotfiles-ukx.8 — CCR transformer source-level analysis (closed)
- dotfiles-ukx.9 — direct llama-swap probe (PASSES with raw OpenAI tools)
- GUARDRAILS G16 — needs amendment after this fix
- ~/dotfiles/claude/sandbox/results/*-local-*.md — empirical 404 traces

## RESOLVED — 2026-05-26 (Wave 15)

**Root cause**: CCR config had `transformer: { use: ["Anthropic"] }` on the pico-mlx + pico-ollama providers. That tells CCR "this provider speaks Anthropic Messages" → CCR converts outgoing Unified→Anthropic for that provider. But mlx_lm.server (via llama-swap) speaks OpenAI Chat Completions. So CCR was sending Anthropic-shape body (with `input_schema`) to an OpenAI-shape backend. mlx_lm.server's Qwen3 chat template tried `tool.parameters.properties` (OpenAI shape) → `AttributeError: dict has no attribute parameters` → returned 404 with that error in body.

**Empirical proof of root cause**: direct curl to llama-swap with Anthropic-shape tools reproduces the exact same error (`dict object has no attribute parameters`). OpenAI-shape tools direct to llama-swap PASS. The transformation step in the middle is what was upside-down.

**Fix**: REMOVE the `transformer` block from pico-mlx + pico-ollama providers. CCR's default behavior for OpenAI-compat backends correctly invokes `convertAnthropicToolsToUnified` which converts `input_schema → parameters` and wraps in `{type:function, function:{...}}`.

**Verification (live)**: 
- Single tool-use request through CCR → returns Anthropic `tool_use` block correctly
- Parallel Edit + Bash request through CCR → returns 2 tool_use blocks (Edit + Bash) both with correct nested schemas
- Both verified via curl POST to http://127.0.0.1:3456/v1/messages with claude-haiku-4-5 model triggering Router.background → pico-mlx,qwen3-coder

**Supersedes**: 
- ukx.8 + ukx.9 research recommendations that `transformer: { use: ["Anthropic"] }` is correct. Those were source-read-validated but never empirical-wire-tested. The source-reading missed the semantic of what "this provider speaks Anthropic" means in CCR's pipeline.
- ukx.5 README + ukx.6 §4.1 + GUARDRAILS G16 that documented the transformer block as production config — all need follow-up edits.

**Lesson** (per [[preserve-process-artifacts]]): source-read research is necessary but not sufficient — every load-bearing recommendation needs an empirical wire-test before production. This is the 2nd reversal this session (G16-original was the 1st). Pattern is clear.

**Affects upcoming work**:
- ukx.3 smoke env can now produce honest parity data (was blocked on this 404)
- explore-7hh.13 + bd-b5p.4 + nightly-digest.sh: routing now works end-to-end through CCR
- Future CCR provider configs: NO transformer block for OpenAI-compat backends; transformer block ONLY for actual Anthropic backends
