Before: 0 bytes + ENOENT in-jail; after: byte-identical 1917-byte descriptor (cmp IDENTICAL on dispatch path too). Test case 20 is a genuine mutant-kill (22/24 vs pre-fix, exactly the 2 new cases failing). Suite 24/24 on explore main post-merge, pushed 3068e16.

title: AGENTS.md's documented merge-safety check passes trivially when HEAD is already the branch
description:
Hit live 2026-07-25 while merging a cross-repo subagent branch in ~/harnessd.

AGENTS.md "Delegation" documents this cleanup snippet:

    git merge worktree-agent-XXXX --no-edit
    git merge-base --is-ancestor worktree-agent-XXXX HEAD  # safety: abort if not merged

If the working tree is ALREADY CHECKED OUT on the branch being merged, both lines succeed and prove nothing: the merge is "Already up to date" and the ancestor test is trivially true because HEAD *is* that branch. The orchestrator sees a green safety check and reports a successful merge while main has not moved at all. Only a later unrelated error ("cannot delete branch used by worktree") exposed it.

This is another instance of the session's own cross-cutting finding (dotfiles-mlti): the documented example IS the defect, and it self-replicates because agents copy it verbatim.

## Steps to Reproduce

    git checkout some-branch
    git merge some-branch --no-edit                          # "Already up to date."
    git merge-base --is-ancestor some-branch HEAD && echo OK # prints OK

Nothing merged; the guard passed.

## Design

Assert the merge TARGET before merging, not just ancestry after:

    test "$(git branch --show-current)" = "main" || { echo "not on main"; exit 1; }
    git merge worktree-agent-XXXX --no-edit
    git merge-base --is-ancestor worktree-agent-XXXX HEAD

Better still, verify main actually moved (compare the pre-merge and post-merge HEAD sha), which catches the whole class rather than this one instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AGENTS.md's cleanup snippet asserts the current branch is the merge target before merging
- The same fix lands in any skill body that copies the snippet (/orchestrator, /impl)
- The corrected snippet is verified against the live PreToolUse hooks, per the dotfiles-mlti guard proposal
notes:
## Verification — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

AGENTS.md now carries the SHA-comparison merge guard: asserts the target branch, captures BEFORE=git rev-parse HEAD, and requires HEAD to have MOVED plus merge-base --is-ancestor. Both vacuous-pass cases the bead named (merging while on the agent's own branch; an agent that committed nothing) are now caught.

Verified by an independent read-only recon agent against live system state, not
from the bead body. Closing as confirmed-resolved.
close_reason: Verified resolved against live state during Opus-5 audit Wave 1.

title: vps-preflight: auto-fast-forward a strictly-behind checkout instead of blocking (supersedes dotfiles-n16x)
description:
## Context

Zig's call, 2026-07-31, after the fourth blocked tick in two days from the same
cause. Since marketing-vps became a peer that commits and pushes on its own,
**zig-computer falls behind as a matter of routine** — the di-friday block at
19:00Z found this machine 1 commit behind on `~/linearb` and **8 behind** on
`dashboard-dev-interrupted`, all of it the box's own AMD-article work (`bd-hlis`)
pushed while this session was idle. A2 then fail-closes and the tick dies before
dispatch.

The peer model is working; the pull-based preflight has not caught up with it.

## Decision

**The dispatcher fast-forwards the local checkouts itself when they are strictly
behind, then proceeds.** Never on ahead, never on genuinely diverged — those
still block for a human.

## This SUPERSEDES dotfiles-n16x, and absorbs it

`dotfiles-n16x` asked only for a better message. That is now a prerequisite
rather than the deliverable: you cannot auto-ff safely without first
distinguishing the three states correctly, which is exactly what n16x specifies.
Implement n16x's three-state detection, then act on it. Close n16x with this bead.

The misdiagnosis n16x describes has now fired FOUR times (2026-07-30 di-wednesday
x2, di-thursday, 2026-07-31 di-friday). Every instance reported "HISTORIES
DIVERGED" and recommended `reset --hard` for a repo that was 0-ahead/N-behind with
zero local commits. The 19:00Z instance would have hard-reset a repo carrying 8
commits that existed nowhere else on this machine. **The remedy text is the
dangerous part, not the block.**

## Required behaviour

1. Classify each checked repo/submodule with real git, not string comparison:
   - `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` and zero local commits -> **BEHIND**
   - `merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` -> **AHEAD**
   - neither -> **DIVERGED**
2. **BEHIND** -> `git pull --ff-only` (or `merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD`), then
   re-assert identity and proceed. A fast-forward cannot lose work; that is the
   whole safety argument and it should be stated in the code.
3. **AHEAD** -> still blocks. This is the genuine "your work is not published"
   case the assertion exists for; remedy is `git push`.
4. **DIVERGED** -> still blocks. Only here may `reset --hard` be mentioned, with
   its warning intact.
5. If the fast-forward itself fails (dirty tree conflict, network), do NOT force
   anything — warn, and fall through to the existing block.
6. **Record it.** Every auto-ff writes what it did into the preflight report and
   into the tick's ledger row: which repo, from which sha to which. Silent
   catch-up must never hide a case where the box and this machine were
   meaningfully out of step. (Zig chose the plain auto-ff option, but the ledger
   already carries `dispatch.checkout` from dotfiles-f4ub, so this is nearly free
   and preserves the "wrong output is the invisible failure" principle.)

## Scope

`vps-preflight.sh` primarily; `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` only to surface the
record. Do NOT touch the dirty-checkout handling (dotfiles-f4ub, just shipped),
the refresh, or the payload contract.

⚠️ Never edit these scripts while a dispatch is running — bash reads a script
incrementally and an in-place edit can make a live run execute garbage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Three-state classification, exercised by tests for each state.
- [ ] BEHIND auto-fast-forwards and the dispatch proceeds.
- [ ] AHEAD and DIVERGED still block, with correct per-state remedies.
- [ ] `reset --hard` appears ONLY in the DIVERGED message.
- [ ] A failed fast-forward warns and falls through to the block; nothing forces.
- [ ] The auto-ff is recorded in the preflight report and the ledger row.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: construct all three states against real repos and paste the
      three outcomes, including the shas before/after the auto-ff.
close_reason: done

title: investigate+verify: CC 1M context drops to 200K on session RESUME through the pico gateway — test the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=[1m] fix via a virtualized-harness experiment
description:
## Symptom (Zig, 2026-07-15)
A FRESH Claude Code session = Opus 4.8 @ **1M** context. RESUMING a past session comes back at Opus 4.8 @ **200K** — Zig must run /model and re-pick the [1m] variant to restore 1M. Only started after routing CC through the pico gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude).

## Root cause — DIAGNOSED (sourced from official CC docs; this is settled)
1. **"1M" is a beta HEADER, not a model.** On the wire the model is always `claude-opus-4-8`; the 1M window is turned on by `anthropic-beta: context-1m-...`. CC's `[1m]` suffix is a client-side LABEL for "that header is active."
2. **Resume restores the model from the TRANSCRIPT** (docs, sessions.md): "Resumed sessions keep the model they were using when the transcript was saved, regardless of the current model setting." The transcript records only the **bare** `claude-opus-4-8` (the beta is invisible in the API response model field — VERIFIED: every ~/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu-harnessd/*.jsonl records model:"claude-opus-4-8", never [1m]). So resume re-resolves the bare label → no context-1m → 200K.
3. **Behind a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (gateway), CC's automatic 1M upgrade is DISABLED** (docs, model-config.md LLM-gateway section: "when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a gateway, Claude Code can't verify 1M support"). Direct-to-Anthropic, CC auto-re-upgrades a resumed session back to 1M too, silently MASKING the transcript degradation. The gateway removed that safety net → the bug became visible. **The gateway didn't CAUSE the drop; it UN-MASKED it.**
Fingerprint: ~/.claude.json lastModelUsage shows several projects with BOTH `claude-opus-4-8` (200K) AND `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` (1M) usage = resumed-degraded vs fresh sessions in the same project.

## Precedence ladder (CC v2.1.195+, docs)
`--model` flag > `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` env > `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` family > transcript model. Env pins sit ABOVE the transcript → they survive resume.

## Proposed fix (surgical)
`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="claude-opus-4-8[1m]"` — sits above the transcript (survives resume) but only changes what the `opus` ALIAS resolves to, so /model and --model still win for explicit picks. Avoids the blunt `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` pin that Zig's cc-gw note deliberately DELETES (a global ANTHROPIC_MODEL clobbers the /model picker for ALL sessions — see ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases:170-172).
NUANCE TO VERIFY: does DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL override a resumed session whose transcript recorded the CONCRETE `claude-opus-4-8` (not the `opus` alias)? Docs put it above the transcript; confirm empirically.

## THE TEST — Zig's design (virtualized harness; NON-INVASIVE; NO settings.json change)
Set the env var in a THROWAWAY tmux window only; do new→test→close→resume; observe the context window. Clean A/B on the SAME transcript isolates the env var.
1. Scratch CC cwd (fresh project → clean session dir): mktemp -d (or /tmp/claude-*/scratchpad/cc1m).
2. New tmux window: `tmux new-window -d -n cc1m -c <scratchdir>`.
3. CREATE transcript (NO env): `claude` (routes through the gateway via settings.json). Send a tiny prompt ("reply with the single word: ok"). Then `/context` → capture pane (note window size). Exit CC.
4. RESUME control (NO env): `claude --continue` in the same dir → `/context` → capture. EXPECT 200K (reproduces the bug).
5. RESUME treatment (WITH env): `export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="claude-opus-4-8[1m]"; claude --continue` → `/context` → capture. EXPECT 1M if the fix works.
6. Compare 4 vs 5. Treatment=1M & control=200K ⇒ fix survives resume through the gateway.
7. `tmux kill-window -t cc1m`; rm the scratch dir.

Driving notes (executing session):
- claude on PATH (v2.1.210). Inside tmux ($TMUX set; session "work").
- **FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED** by a pre-bash hook. Use `timeout <N>s tail -f /dev/null || true` as a delay (exit 124 = normal), or a background bash / Monitor. Generous waits: ~15s CC boot, ~20s response, ~8s /context render.
- Drive: `tmux send-keys -t cc1m "<text>" Enter`; read: `tmux capture-pane -t cc1m -p -S -300`. Exit CC via "/exit" Enter (or C-c C-c). Do NOT `exec claude` (the shell must persist for the next --continue).
- Observe window size from /context (token budget/limit) + statusline `[MODEL]` display_name + /model current. Grep captures for 1M / 1,000,000 / 200K / 200,000 / [1m].

## DEEPER open question — verify too (the REAL risk)
Even when [1m] is active on a routed session, does the pico gateway FORWARD the context-1m beta so Anthropic actually SERVES >200K? (Untested — ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases:168-169.) If the gateway STRIPS it, [1m] gives a 1M LOCAL budget while the server truncates at 200K → SILENT context overflow. The /context test above only proves the LOCAL budget. To settle SERVING: cross 200K tokens on a routed [1m] session (400 "context exceeded" vs serves?), OR read pico's gateway config (ssh-pico; the :17017/claude proxy) for beta-header handling/allowlist. **Pinning [1m] is only truly correct if the gateway serves 1M.**

## References
- Diagnosis: harnessd session, 2026-07-15.
- cc-gw + Zig's notes: ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases:146-200 (:167 auto-upgrade-disabled behind gateway; :168-169 serving untested; :170-172 why ANTHROPIC_MODEL was deleted).
- CC docs (via claude-code-guide): sessions.md (resume keeps transcript model), model-config.md (LLM-gateway can't verify 1M), env-vars.md (DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL + precedence).
- Evidence: ~/.claude.json lastModelUsage (bare + [1m] per project); harnessd project *.jsonl (transcript records bare model only).
- Gateway: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude (pico); `cc-direct` reverts routing.

## Constraints
NON-INVASIVE until the fix is decided (env var in a throwaway window; no settings.json edit). Don't reroute Zig's primary CC.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Reproduced: resume-through-gateway control (no env) = 200K context
- [ ] Tested: resume with ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=claude-opus-4-8[1m] = 1M (or documented that it does NOT override the concrete resumed model)
- [ ] Answered the deeper question: does the pico gateway actually SERVE 1M (forward context-1m past 200K), or only give a 1M LOCAL budget?
- [ ] Recommendation to Zig on whether/how to apply the fix, with the serving-question resolved
- [ ] Test was NON-INVASIVE (throwaway tmux window + env var; no settings.json change); test window + scratch dir cleaned up
notes:
## EXPERIMENT RUN — 2026-07-15 (harnessd session). Non-invasive throwaway tmux window; cleaned up.
Premise confirmed live: CC routed through the pico gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude
in settings.json; unset in the shell). claude v2.1.210. Same transcript (session d1d53cfd) across A/B/C.

RESULTS (each verified via /context + statusline):
- A. FRESH (no env):            claude-opus-4-8[1m] — 59.2k/1m  (6%)  — statusline [Opus 4.8 (1M context)]
- B. RESUME control (no env):   claude-opus-4-8     — 59.2k/200k (30%) — statusline [Opus 4.8]   <= BUG REPRODUCED
- C. RESUME + ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=claude-opus-4-8[1m]:
                                claude-opus-4-8[1m] — 59.2k/1m  (6%)  — statusline [Opus 4.8 (1M context)]  <= FIX WORKS
Clean A/B: B vs C differ ONLY by the env var (same window/transcript/59.2k tokens). Fix RESTORES 1M on resume.
Settles the nuance: DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL DOES override a transcript recording the CONCRETE claude-opus-4-8.

DEEPER (serving) QUESTION — ANSWERED, high confidence YES (real 1M served, not a false local budget):
- frontier-o11y.md (verified 2026-07-01): Max-subscription OAuth passthrough works through the gateway (200 OK).
  Subscription OAuth REQUIRES anthropic-beta:oauth-... to reach Anthropic -> the gateway FORWARDS anthropic-beta.
- context-1m-2025-08-07 rides as another comma value on that SAME anthropic-beta header -> forwarded with it.
- capability-map.md:267-268: agentgateway forwards headers; strip list = Origin/Sec-Fetch-* ONLY, Anthropic-only.
  config-pico.yaml /claude route: ai anthropic backend, no requestHeaders.remove; 32MiB buffer (no >200k body confound).
- Residual (low): the only unproven path is the ai-backend PARSING anthropic-beta and reconstructing it (drop
  context-1m, keep oauth) — no evidence of such filtering. 100% proof would need a 200k-crossing on a routed
  [1m] session, or reading upstream provider header code. Not done (cost / Zig-gated).

RESOLUTION — APPLIED 2026-07-15 (Zig chose "fold into cc-gw, apply now"):
- dotfiles bash/.bash_aliases: cc-gw now sets .env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=$CC_GW_MODEL (=claude-opus-4-8[1m]);
  cc-direct dels it (+ scrubs it from shell & tmux env). Rationale: degradation happens ONLY behind the gateway
  (auto-upgrade disabled); direct auto-re-upgrades on resume so no pin needed. DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL is surgical —
  survives resume (above transcript) but only changes the `opus` alias; /model + --model still win.
- Applied live to ~/.claude/settings.json (mirrors cc-gw; backup .bak-w1r-*). Takes effect on next CC launch.
- DEPLOYED-FIX VERIFIED end-to-end: a fresh throwaway CC reading the LIVE settings.json (NO shell export),
  create->--continue, came back at claude-opus-4-8[1m] 59.2k/1m — [Opus 4.8 (1M context)]. Confirms the shipped
  mechanism (settings.json .env pin), not just the shell-export form. Full run log: /tmp/cc1m_results.md.
- Remote Control note: orthogonal — cc-gw disables it regardless; Zig is deliberately on the gateway.
close_reason: done

title: PLAN: post-reset harness restoration + seat relaunch sequence (seneschal, executes when primary fable resets)
description:
## Context

Executable runbook for the seneschal to run THE MOMENT the primary fable pool
resets (Thu 2026-08-13 11pm PT / Fri 06:00Z). Written 2026-08-13 while the pool
was still exhausted. Zig asked for a literal step-by-step he can expect executed
flawlessly, plus a mechanical timer watching for the start moment.

TRIGGER: Monitor task b8rfaf28v polls `tap-headroom.sh --pool primary` every
5 min and emits `PRIMARY FABLE RESET` when fable drops below 0.99. It also emits
on reader failure, so silence is not mistaken for "not yet".

WHY THIS EXISTS AS A BEAD: the harness gaps we keep stumbling on have no beads,
and nothing reads seat mailboxes (see refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md 0b), so
this plan would otherwise live only in a spool nobody reads. Full reasoning,
evidence and inventory: refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md in ~/demesne.

ZIG'S RATIFIED DECISIONS (2026-08-13):
- machine default -> claude-fable-5[1m] (canonical, 1M window)
- linearb pin -> SPLIT, fable for drafting rows only. NOT expressible today, so
  the per-schedule override is a PREREQUISITE and linearb STAYS ON OPUS tonight.
  Do NOT revert-then-split: that flaps seven rows twice.

## Design

KEY TOOL: agents/bin/seat-cycle.sh --pane %N [--relaunch CMD] [--cmd PROMPT]
It exits the seat cleanly (/exit + confirm), waits for death, relaunches, gates on
a readiness marker, then INJECTS an opening prompt. Verdict on last stdout line:
SEAT_CYCLE_RESULT=cycled|cycled-no-cmd|failed-*.

TWO TRAPS IT DOCUMENTS, both measured 2026-08-10:
1. A bare `claude` relaunch NEVER trips the wrapper's fable leg (_ciw_fable_launch
   reads ARGV), so the seat silently stays on its config-dir pool. ALWAYS pass the
   canonical literal in --relaunch.
2. A relaunched TUI sits idle forever unless something SUBMITS a prompt. --cmd is
   not optional in spirit; a cycle without one is half a cycle.

PANE IDS as of 2026-08-13 23:50Z (RE-DERIVE before use, panes move):
  %755 seneschal | %752 consul(empty) | %757 dotfiles | %864 hevyd
  %1471 imc-aug26 | %1470 digest | %1473 di-wednesday | %1474 dev-interrupted
  %1475 di-thursday

## Steps

S1. VERIFY THE RESET IS REAL. `bash ~/.agents/agents/lib/tap-headroom.sh`.
    primary fable must be off 1.0000. If not, STOP and wait — every later step
    assumes headroom. Record all three pools in the first report.

S2. FIX settings.json. Edit /home/ubuntu/demesne/claude/settings.json directly,
    set top-level model to exactly: claude-fable-5[1m]
    NEVER via /model (it persists machine-wide from any window; that is what
    caused today's drift). VERIFY: read the file back; confirm the [1m] suffix on
    a full canonical id, not a bare alias (bare = 200k window).
    Commit + push the change in ~/demesne.

S3. LEAVE agents/seats.yml ALONE TONIGHT. linearb stays opus per the split
    ruling. Any pin change waits on the per-schedule override bead. If you do
    touch seats.yml for any reason, you MUST re-run
    `python3 agents/lib/validate-seats.py agents/seats.yml --emit-json agents/seats.json`
    and commit BOTH files — the commit gate blocks on a stale seats.json.

S4. CLEAR STALE MODEL-GUARD MEMOS.
    ls ~/.local/state/harness/model-guard/*.state
    For each, check the owning session pid is DEAD before removing (ps -p).
    Removing a live session's file only loses its try counter, but do it
    knowingly. This is cleanup, NOT the fix — the fix is the memo-invalidation
    bead (S8). Without it the next long-lived session refreezes its pin.

S5. RECYCLE THE STALE SEATS, oldest first, each with an opening prompt.
    Rationale: the always-loaded tier is injected at PROCESS START with no
    invalidation; /offboard+/onboard do NOT refresh it. Today's rulings (seat
    pins, the mechanical-work tap rule, pulse-seats-route-through-seneschal) are
    invisible to every window older than today. Ages at writing: dotfiles 81h,
    hevyd 67h, digest 57h, di-wednesday 33h, dev-interrupted 31h, imc-aug26 24h,
    di-thursday 10h.

    BEFORE EACH: check the seat has no live background work (its own report or
    tmux pane tail). Skip and note any that does. Prefer letting a seat /offboard
    itself first where it is idle-but-dirty.

    ORDER: dotfiles -> digest -> hevyd -> dev-interrupted -> imc-aug26 ->
           di-wednesday -> di-thursday

    RELAUNCH MODEL per seat pin (resolve, do not assume):
      bash ~/demesne/agents/lib/seat-resolve.sh --seat <name>
    dotfiles=fable, digest/hevyd=sonnet, dev-interrupted/imc-aug26=opus,
    di-*=linearb seat=opus tonight. Canonical literals only, e.g.
      claude --model 'claude-fable-5[1m]'   /  'claude-sonnet-5[1m]'  /  'claude-opus-5[1m]'

      it so it must read it by hand, (b) refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md in

    (~/.local/state/harness/post/mail/orator.jsonl, ref cfp-double-assignment)
    and tells it to load /cfp first. Two assignments are waiting there: a

    and the IEEE Software / Nan collaboration (folder ~/cfp/ieee). It reports to

S7. LAUNCH THE CONSUL (window :1 exists but has NO claude running, pane %752).
    Its charter is cross-cutting hardening, guards and taps — i.e. most of the
    repair backlog. Launch with its pin (fable) and kick it off pointed at
    refs/post-reset-plan-2026-08-13.md sections 2 and 7.

S8. FILE THE GAP BEADS. They currently exist only as unread mail. File before
    building; decompose rather than filing one mega-bead (Zig's own live idea,
    idea-bead-decomposition-gate).
      P1 mail readers + per-reader cursor (7fik R1)
      P1 model-guard memo invalidation  -> UPDATE bd-3sbi, do NOT duplicate: its
         recorded hypothesis (stale comment-line matching) is DISPROVED; real
         cause is the per-session .state memo short-circuiting re-resolution at
         post-tool-model-guard.sh lines 675-676 with no TTL
      P1 model-guard tap-awareness + ledger-every-fire + print roster SHA
      P1 post-molt gateway-stall watcher (outside the agent process)
      P1 per-schedule (or per-PHASE) model override — prerequisite for the split
      P2 tap threshold alarm at 0.8
      P2 imc's C1-C5 (five beads): pre-bead-create command-string inspection;
         stop-context-guard interactive-blindness; four doc writers dropping
         shade/border/indent; writer verify lines counting paragraphs only;
         git commit succeeding after a failed git add
      P3 hall marshal tap two-copies + the unwired mail glyph label
    ASSIGN BY CHARTER: consul = guards/taps/watcher; Works = mail readers,
    per-schedule override, C1/C2; imc-aug26 = its own C3/C4.

S9. MOLT THE SENESCHAL — LAST, because it executes S1-S8.
    First TaskStop the background handles: mail Monitor, the hourly heartbeat
    cron, the reset Monitor b8rfaf28v (fired, no longer needed).
    Then /offboard, then
    `agents/scheduler/seat-molt.sh --self --mode auto --in-flight no`.
    The fresh context must come up on claude-fable-5[1m] via the seat pin.
    VERIFY: no model-guard alarm on its first tool round. That ABSENCE is the
    proof S2+S4 took.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] primary fable measured off 1.0000 before any other step
- [ ] settings.json holds exactly claude-fable-5[1m], verified by reading it back
- [ ] seats.yml unchanged tonight (or, if changed, seats.json regenerated and both committed)
- [ ] stale guard memos removed only for dead sessions
- [ ] every recycled seat returns SEAT_CYCLE_RESULT=cycled and comes up on its resolved pin
- [ ] every recycled seat was given an opening prompt naming its mailbox path
- [ ] orator launched and acknowledges the two CFP assignments
- [ ] consul launched and holds the repair backlog
- [ ] gap beads filed, bd-3sbi UPDATED not duplicated
- [ ] seneschal molted last, fresh context on fable, NO guard alarm on first tool round
- [ ] a short report to Zig naming anything skipped and why

## Notes

EVIDENCE STANDARD for the follow-on work: a guard change closes on a MUTANT THAT
DIES ON THE CASE IT NAMES, not a green suite. The mail work closes on a message
sent from one seat and demonstrably READ by another — "it was spooled" is exactly
the claim that turned out hollow on 2026-08-13.

DEADLINE AWARENESS: pulse-di-friday fires Fri 19:00 UTC on the linearb seat and
resolves whatever the pin says then. If the per-schedule override is not built by
then it runs opus — acceptable, state it rather than treating it as a failure.
pulse-seneschal fires Fri 13:44 UTC; the fresh context must find this bead.

pulse-marshal is NOT installed, so the nightly drain is not running and Zig's

title: triage: 'defer until X happens' is a waits-for dep, not a date
description:
## Context
br/bv audit 2026-08-09. `br defer --until` is verified time-only — it cannot
express "defer until event X happens," only "defer until date Y." A
waits-for or conditional-blocks dependency instead leaves the bead out of
`br ready` for a graph-known reason (the blocking bead), and it returns to
`br ready` automatically the moment the trigger bead closes — no calendar
guessing required. This directly extends the existing
defer-needs-trigger memory finding (a dated defer with no trigger is
silent procrastination) by giving it a concrete non-date mechanism.

## Task
Teach /triage the waits-for/conditional-blocks pattern as the correct tool
for event-triggered (not date-triggered) deferrals. Update the
defer-needs-trigger memory file accordingly. Review existing dated defers
fleet-wide for cases that are actually event-triggered and should be
converted to a dependency instead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /triage documents waits-for/conditional-blocks as the event-defer pattern
- [ ] defer-needs-trigger memory file updated with this distinction
- [ ] existing dated defers reviewed; event-triggered ones converted

title: epic: Opus-5 bloat audit — always-loaded tier + 37 global skills + 45 fleet CLAUDE.md
description:
## Context

Zig, 2026-08-01: "Anthropic removed 80% of Opus 5's harness instructions because it
doesn't need it. There's likely a lot of cruft and baggage and bloat and stale info
in all our skills globally and in each home dir and also in the CLAUDE.md files --
thoroughly audit them all, run tests with stripped down skills, and provide a report
so we can decide cleanup and refactor steps."

AUDIT+REPORT phase of dotfiles-b9ii (Opus-5 harness refactor). Deliverable is a
REPORT Zig decides from -- NOT unilateral deletion.

MEASURED SCALE (2026-08-01):
- always-loaded tier: agents/AGENTS.md 5,525 words (~7.4k tok) EVERY session
  fleet-wide, + per-project CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + 37 skill frontmatter blocks
- global SKILL.md bodies: 100,217 words (~134k tok)
- global skill reference/*.md: 165,662 words (gdoc's is node_modules noise)
- TOOLKIT.md: 4,748 words, read every /onboard
- 45 CLAUDE.md files across ~/ (7,738 words at the top: autonoveld)
- 56 project-local skills in 10 repos; 28 hook scripts / 3,764 lines

## The classification every finding must use

  LOCAL-FACT      irreducible; no model knows it (paths, hostnames, API quirks,
                  contract shapes, creds locations). KEEP regardless of model.
  SCAR-TISSUE     a rule written after ONE specific Opus-4.x failure. The strip
                  candidate needing an EMPIRICAL test, not a judgment call.
  MODEL-SCAFFOLD  telling the model how to think / be careful / not be lazy.
                  Opus 5's own guide says this can DEGRADE output. Strip candidate.
  CTX-SCARCITY    exists only because the window was small (dotfiles-q702 thesis).
                  Reconsider under 1M -- but keep q702's nuance: a rule with TWO
                  justifications keeps the surviving one.
  STALE           refers to a thing that no longer exists / a model that changed.
  REDUNDANT       the same rule in 3 places; keep the most-enforced copy.

Constraint from dotfiles-b9ii, Zig's words: "DO NOT clear things just to clear
them. The accumulated beads/explorations are distilled knowledge that gets MORE
relevant as new material lands."

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Every global SKILL.md (37) audited, each finding classified above
- [ ] agents/AGENTS.md audited line-block by line-block (highest leverage/word)
- [ ] All 45 fleet CLAUDE.md files audited for staleness + global-tier redundancy
- [ ] 56 project-local skills + the 165k words of reference/ audited
- [ ] EMPIRICAL A/B (via ~/explore/.claude/skills/ab) on the top strip candidates --
      a stripped variant that still avoids the failure the rule guarded is evidence
- [ ] A single report to Zig with a ranked, costed cleanup plan he decides from

Status: Disabled). On zig-computer, ufw's INPUT DROP makes a bad bind a documentation
smell; on pico there is nothing in front of anything.

## MY MISS — stated plainly
I hardened `config.yaml` (chmod 600 + ${VAR}) and never swept the DIRECTORY for
sibling copies. I fixed the file I was pointed at. The five 644 backups pre-date me
(2026-07-09 .. 2026-07-28), so I did not create the exposure -- but I had the
directory open, ran `ls -la` on it, and did not look. A secret-hygiene fix that does
not sweep for copies is half a fix.

## THIS CHANGES A DECISION ZIG ALREADY MADE
On 2026-08-01 he chose "skip rotation, exposure was local-only" -- correctly, on the
information we had: ONE 644 file, briefly. The real exposure is SIX copies, five
world-readable, for three weeks, on an unfirewalled host. The premise of that call no
longer holds, so it should be re-made rather than assumed to carry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zig re-decides rotation now that the exposure is known to be 6 copies x 3 weeks
- [ ] Delete all five 644 copies + /tmp/agentgateway-restore.yaml (zero benefit; the
      live config works and the 600 backup is the rollback)
- [ ] Decide on my own 600 backup once the fix is trusted
- [ ] Add a sweep step to the secret-hygiene pattern: after hardening a config,
      `ls -la` the directory AND hash every sibling against the live value. This is
      the second time today a fix was found to be one step short of complete (the
      first: agentgateway-run existed and nothing called it)
- [ ] pico's missing firewall is its own finding -- file separately, do not fold in

Verified after: zero files under ~/.config/agentgateway/ contain a credential-shaped literal; the two remaining 644 files have zero key lines; config.yaml.staged is 600 with ${VAR}-only. Gateway healthy throughout (pid 97491, goose 15003/v1/models -> HTTP 200). Zig's call: delete the copies, skip rotation -- pico is not internet-exposed (see the pico-firewall decision bead).

title: suites: 'printf $VAR | grep -q' under pipefail is a flaky false-FAIL — audit the fleet's test suites
description:
## Context
Found while implementing dotfiles-5gob. `test-marshal-drain.sh`'s T1d.1 guard —
"the drain calls the library ID-based marker_is_fleet" — failed intermittently
against a script that plainly contains the string.

Cause: under `set -o pipefail` (which every suite in agents/ sets),
`printf '%s' "$SRC" | grep -q PATTERN` is a RACE. `grep -q` exits the moment it
matches; the still-writing `printf` then takes EPIPE/SIGPIPE and exits 141;
pipefail hands the PIPELINE that status; the `if` reads a PRESENT string as
ABSENT. The failure mode is a red case nobody can reproduce, on a guard that
gets flakier as the file it guards GROWS — i.e. it fires hardest exactly when
the guarded file is under active development.

Measured on this box (zsh 5.9 / bash), 300 trials each, same pattern, same
haystack, only the size varying:

    33,888-byte source (HEAD)      18 / 300 false failures  (6%)
    43,100-byte source (post-5gob) 68 / 300 false failures  (23%)
    herestring form                 0 / 300

Fixed in test-marshal-drain.sh by switching T1d.1 / T1d.2 to
`grep -q PATTERN <<< "$SRC"` (no pipe, no pipefail interaction). THIS BEAD is
the fleet-wide audit that fix implies.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `SRC=$(grep -vE '^\s*#' agents/scheduler/marshal-drain.sh)`  (~43 KB)
2. `set -o pipefail`
3. Loop 300x: `if printf '%s' "$SRC" | grep -q marker_is_fleet; then :; else echo miss; fi`
4. ~23% of iterations print `miss` against a string that is definitely present.

## Task
Grep every `agents/**/test-*.sh` and `agents/**/mutate-*.sh` for
`printf .* | grep -q` (and `echo .* | grep -q`) where the piped value is a
large variable, and convert to a herestring or a `case` match. A guard that
false-FAILS is worse than no guard: it trains the next agent to re-run until
green, or to delete the case.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every occurrence in agents/ audited; large-haystack ones converted
- [ ] A note in the repo's test conventions so the idiom does not come back
- [ ] Spot-check one converted suite with a 300-trial loop: 0 false failures

title: promote the ad-hoc tunnel-ownership mutation harness into agents/scheduler/ and wire it into pre-commit
description:
Raised by the dotfiles-47nf agent as out-of-scope; filed rather than done.

## Context
dotfiles-47nf built a throwaway mutation harness in scratchpad to prove that
ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ownership logic actually bites. It killed 3 real mutants,
including a LIVE cross-kill (bringing up tunnel B printed "closed our local forward"
against tunnel A pid 3101373).

That harness is currently disposable, so the next edit to the ownership logic has a
green suite and no mutant check — which CLAUDE.md rule 1 says is not evidence:
"A green suite is not evidence that a guard bites; only a mutant that dies is."

`agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh` is the existing precedent and is already
wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit. Mirror it as
agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh.

## Also worth encoding: a mutant must die of the bug it NAMES
The 47nf agent's first attempt over-escaped a sed pattern so the mutant matched
NOTHING — the suite failed, but for the wrong reason, which would have been recorded
as "mutant died" by anyone reading only the exit code. A mutation harness should
assert that the mutation actually applied (diff non-empty AND the mutated pattern
still matches the intended shape) before trusting the failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh exists, modeled on mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh
- [ ] it asserts each mutation APPLIED before interpreting the suite result
- [ ] wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit keyed on ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh AND its test
- [ ] observed: harness passes on clean tree, fails on a reintroduced ownership bug
- [ ] case 25 weakness from dotfiles-47nf re-examined (it may be a test that cannot fail)
close_reason: agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh shipped and gated in tools/githooks/pre-commit, keyed on BOTH ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh and its suite. Five mutants (M1 target-blind cross-kill, M2 pre-generalization hardwired, M3 shared pidfile, M4 re_escape neutered, M5 tunnel_down kill-target blind); each mutation is asserted applied FIVE ways before its result counts (target present exactly once pristine, replacement absent before, bytes changed, replacement present once after, bash -n still clean) — any failure is a HARNESS ERROR at rc 2 with the mutant printed NOT RUN, demonstrated by injecting a stale target. Killed mutants must also die on the cases they NAME, so the suite header's map is executable rather than a comment. It also CORRECTED the reviewer's construction: blind our_pid discovery also reddens case 23 (B finds A by discovery and recycle-kills it during setup), so M5 blinds tunnel_down instead, isolating it with both pidfiles correct and both pids non-empty — proving 24/25/27/28 detect ownership rather than empty strings. Orchestrator re-verified independently: harness green on the clean tree with all five killed on their named cases; then deleted case 28 from the TEST ONLY (script untouched) — suite stayed green at 27/27 while the harness caught it FOUR ways (M4 SURVIVED plus M2/M3/M5 MIS-KILLED for no longer dying on the case they name) and exited rc 1, so the gate can actually block. Measured cost: suite 9s, harness 63s, commit 71s — comparable to the existing 88s scrutiny gate.

title: pulse-inject.sh stages no surface — local loops silently lose the always-bell guarantee
description:
## Context

`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` step 7 surfaces **ALWAYS** — every finished tick,
`done`/`quiet`/`blocked` — staging into the deferred-surface queue and raising the
AskUserQuestion from the local session (`dotfiles-5ts2`; Zig 2026-07-31: "there's no
such thing as a low-value bell ... you need to be in charge of making sure I see their
actions and I know when they're ready").

Local loops have **no equivalent**. Any loop moved from the remote dispatcher to a
local timer silently loses the guarantee, and `/pulse`'s "ticks never AskUserQuestion"
rule then stops the tick standing in. Nothing errors; the pane shows the idle glyph
over a deliverable waiting on Zig.

Bit `pulse-weekly-report` on 2026-08-07, five ticks after `dotfiles-1n50` moved it
local on 2026-08-05. Report published clean, tick logged `done`, `PushNotification`
returned "Remote Control inactive" (undelivered), Zig found out by asking.

Patched at the PROSE layer (decision `weekly-reporting-skd`): `refs/pulse.md` declares
`Surfacing: ATTENDED` and the tick raises the dialog itself. Works, but is per-project
and depends on the tick following instructions.

## ⚠️ DESIGN CORRECTION (2026-08-07) — the original framing of this bead was WRONG

This bead first said "teach `pulse-inject.sh` to stage a surface." **That cannot work.**
`pulse-inject.sh` returns as soon as it has typed the command; it does NOT block for the
tick (the `.service` files say so explicitly, and its verdict contract is about whether
INJECTION succeeded — injected / bounced / failed). At the moment it exits, the tick has
not run. Staging there would announce a tick that has not happened.

The dispatcher can surface only because its step 5 **polls `result.json`** and step 6
lands the ledger row — it OBSERVES completion. Nothing observes a local tick's
completion today.

## The actual fix — watch the LEDGER, ride the existing timer

The local tick's durable completion record is **its ledger row**, appended at wrap
(`/pulse` tick procedure step 5) for `done`/`quiet`/`blocked` alike — exactly the set
the dispatcher surfaces. So:

- A watcher compares each local loop's newest ledger row against a per-loop
  "last surfaced ts" marker under `~/.local/state/`, and stages a surface for any row
  newer than the marker.
- Ride **`pulse-retry.timer`** (already every 2 minutes, already drains the queue). No
  new unit, no new daemon — the same reuse argument `pulse-surface-queue.sh` makes for
  its own drain trigger.
- Loop → ledger path → row name comes from `~/harnessd/refs/harness-manifest.json`,
  which already pins `ledger` + `ledger_row` per loop and is already asserted per tick
  by `harness-assert-registration`.

Interaction with the ATTENDED prose fix is fine and needs no special casing: if the
tick already raised its own dialog, the window name starts with the bell glyph,
`pulse-inject.sh` refuses to type into it, and the staged surface stays queued until
the bell clears — the deferred-surface path working as designed. Collapse-per-row means
a loop that ran twice while Zig was away announces only its newest state.

## Check before building

Which loops are local vs dispatched — every local one has this hole right now:
`systemctl --user cat 'pulse-*.service' | grep -E 'ExecStart|^Description'`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ledger-watcher stages a surface for any pulse row whose newest ledger `ts` is newer than that loop's last-surfaced marker
- [ ] Surfaces on `done`/`quiet`/`blocked` alike, matching the dispatcher's always-surface policy
- [ ] Exactly-once per ledger row: marker advances only on successful stage; a bounced drain leaves the entry queued, never dropped or duplicated
- [ ] Invoked from `pulse-retry.sh` (existing 2-minute timer) — no new systemd unit
- [ ] Loop -> ledger/row resolved from the harnessd manifest, not hardcoded
- [ ] Tests alongside `test-pulse-retry.sh` / `test-pulse-inject.sh`, including the exactly-once and bounce cases
- [ ] `/pulse` "ATTENDED loops" section updated to say local loops now surface mechanically
close_reason: Delivered across 413f7ab (build), 975baf4 (same-day gate-off after adversarial review), 3324d1b (blocker fix + hardening) and da6c35a (un-gate). Local pulse loops now surface every finished tick mechanically, via pulse-ledger-watch.sh riding the existing pulse-retry.timer -- no new systemd unit. The gate was RETIRED rather than defaulted-on (a switchable wiring is a second silent way to lose the bell); test-pulse-retry case 18 was inverted to pin that it runs with no flag AND that a stale PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE=0 cannot resurrect it. All four adversarial-review findings fixed: run-level flock (concurrent double-stage), marker RESERVED before staging (a stage could otherwise succeed while the marker write failed, re-staging forever), systemctl rc checked + zero-units is an error + corrupt marker announces instead of silently re-seeding past a finished tick + malformed ts errors (three silent 'nothing new' paths), and a floor marker so a newly-registered loop's FIRST real tick surfaces (the header's '<=2-minute install window' claim was wrong -- it was every new loop, always). Verified by me at REAL exit codes (not through a pipe): test-pulse-ledger-watch 76/76 rc=0, test-pulse-retry 26/26 rc=0, test-pulse-dispatch-remote 421/421 rc=0. Live: watcher runs clean, 17 loops seeded, pulse-weekly-report's marker matches its ledger ts exactly. Blocker dotfiles-sxsv closed first. REMAINING, tracked separately: dotfiles-eh21 (the watcher still reports errors:5 for five DISABLED units -- a false alarm, fix in flight) and dotfiles-qn4t (test-pulse-inject 6/113, pre-existing and unrelated).

title: pico: three launchd jobs have been crash-looping ~240k times each, unnoticed
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-26 while auditing pico for boot persistence. Three separate
launchd jobs were in permanent restart loops, each with a restart count around a
quarter of a million:

| Job | runs | last exit | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `com.zig.vs14-web` | 237,737 | 1 (EADDRINUSE) | **fixed today** — an orphan was squatting :3300 |
| `homebrew.mxcl.tailscale` (user agent) | 242,422 | 78 EX_CONFIG | **fixed today** — duplicate of the system daemon; tailscaled needs root |
| `com.zig.tmux` | ~241,920 | 1 | **open** |

None of them alarmed. `vs14-web`'s loop grew `/tmp/vs14-web.log` to **51 MB**
and the only visible symptom was a log file nobody looks at.

## Why this is a pattern and not three coincidences

All three share the shape in `dotfiles-cxle`: a scheduled/supervised step stops
working while nothing reports it. launchd faithfully does its job — restart on
failure — and a job that can NEVER succeed turns that into an infinite loop that
looks, from every casual angle, like a running service. `launchctl list` shows
the label. `ps` shows a process for the two that had squatters. Only the `runs`
counter tells the truth, and nothing reads it.

**The counter is the tell, and it is free.** A job with `runs` in the hundreds of
thousands is definitionally broken; a healthy long-lived daemon has `runs = 1`
(tailscaled: pid 367, runs = 1, up since May 28).

## Steps to Reproduce

    ssh pico 'launchctl list | awk "\$2 != 0 && \$1 == \"-\""'   # failed, not running
    ssh pico 'sudo launchctl print system/<label> | grep runs'   # the counter

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root-cause `com.zig.tmux` exit 1 and fix or retire it
- [ ] A cheap standing check — any launchd/systemd job whose restart count
      exceeds a threshold is reported. This is the generalisable half and it is
      worth more than the three individual fixes.
- [ ] Consider the systemd equivalent on zig-computer (`NRestarts`) — the same
      blindness applies; nginx there showed `NRestarts=0`, but nothing looks
- [ ] Truncate `/tmp/vs14-web.log` (51 MB, inert now)
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-26. All three loops dead, and the generalisable half shipped.

| Job | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `com.zig.vs14-web` | 237,737, exit 1 | running, counter frozen at 237,744 — an orphan was squatting :3300; killed, launchd took over |
| `homebrew.mxcl.tailscale` (user agent) | 242,422, exit 78 EX_CONFIG | booted out, disabled, plist retired — a duplicate of the SYSTEM daemon, and tailscaled needs root so the agent copy could never start. The real daemon (pid 367, runs=1, up since May 28) untouched. |
| `com.zig.tmux` | 242,224, exit 1 | runs=1, exit 0, not running |

THE TMUX BUG, which Zig diagnosed from the symptom before seeing it: the plist
ran `tmux new-session -d -s pico`, which is NOT idempotent. First run creates the
session and exits 0. Every run after fails `duplicate session: pico` and exits 1
— and `KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit=false}` restarts precisely on nonzero exit.
**The job's own success is what made it fail forever.** 5.5 MB of "duplicate
session" in /tmp/com.zig.tmux.log.

Fixed by making it idempotent: `tmux has-session -t pico || exec tmux
new-session -d -s pico`. KeepAlive was KEPT deliberately — it now means what it
was always meant to (retry if the job genuinely cannot do its work) instead of
retrying because the work was already done. Zig's requirement — one long-lived
system-owned tmux server that survives logout — is satisfied by the server
daemonising and reparenting to launchd (pid 21174, PPID 1, since Jun 5); tmux
has no foreground-server mode, so that is the only shape available.

Verified his live sessions (`work`, 2 windows, attached) survived the change,
after first confirming launchd tracked NO pid for the job so bootout could not
kill the server.

54.5 MB of log reclaimed (5.5 MB tmux + 49 MB vs14-web).

THE STANDING CHECK — `~/dotfiles/agents/bin/restart-loop-check.sh`, and it is
worth more than the three fixes. Covers both hosts (systemd `NRestarts` +
launchd `runs`).

The design decision that makes it trustworthy: **a high count is NOT a loop.**
vs14-web sits at 237,744 and is healthy — launchd does not reset the counter
until re-bootstrap. Flagging that would train the reader to ignore the check,
which is the precise failure this exists to prevent. So it samples TWICE, 15 s
apart, and flags only counts that CLIMBED; high-but-static is reported as `scar`
— history, not fault.

PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, not by a green run: a throwaway `com.zig.looptest`
(/usr/bin/false + KeepAlive) was installed on pico, and the checker caught it —
`runs 7 -> 22 in 15s ACTIVELY LOOPING`, `RESULT=found` — while still classifying
vs14-web as a scar. Then removed.

An earlier version of this script reported `clean` because its own awk quoting
broke and every comparison silently skipped. Caught only because the result
contradicted a known-bad job. That bug WAS the bug class it hunts, committed
inside the hunter, which is why the negative control is not optional here.

Still open: nothing on the three jobs. The check is not yet on a timer — worth a
pulse row or a weekly unit, deliberately left for a session that owns the
scheduler.
close_reason: done

title: githooks: the mutation-harness gate costs 4m24s under load, not the ~90s the runner advertises
description:
## Context

Found while fixing `dotfiles-oe80` (case 22 load-flake), on the same box and under
the same synthetic load used to verify that fix.

`tools/githooks/pre-commit` fires `agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh` when a
commit stages any of six scrutiny-guard files, and both its inline comment and the
message it prints to the committer say **~90s** (measured at load 8.4 on 12 cores).

Measured 2026-08-01 at **load 55 on the same 12 cores: 4m24s** — ~3x the advertised
number, with no output between the "running mutation harness (~90s)" line and the
result. On a box running several agents that is a multi-minute silent wait during
`git commit`, which reads as a hang. It is a cost/UX problem, not a correctness one:
the harness passed (all mutants killed) at that load, and the git pre-commit hook has
no time ceiling to blow.

Not fixed under `dotfiles-oe80` — that bead was scoped to case 22 only.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a 12-core box to ~55 (`for i in $(seq 1 36); do yes >/dev/null & done`).
2. `time bash agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh`
3. Observe 4m24s wall clock, exit 0, "all mutants killed", and no intermediate
   output for minutes at a time.
4. Kill the load, re-run: back to the advertised order of magnitude.

## Task

Decide whether to (a) reword the advertised figure to something load-honest
("~90s on an idle box; several minutes under load"), (b) emit per-mutant progress so
the wait is legible, or (c) both. Do not simply narrow the trigger — the six-file
trigger is deliberate and load-bearing (see the comment above it in the runner).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The committer can tell the difference between "still working" and "hung".
- [ ] Any stated runtime figure names the load it was measured at.

title: pulse-dispatch-remote: adopt a healthy box-side forward instead of hard-failing on the -R bind
description:
## Context

INCIDENT (2026-07-29 14:00 UTC): pulse-di-wednesday.service exited 71
failed-tunnel at step 1. The tick never dispatched; no ad-reads drafted;
NOTHING rang a bell — Zig discovered it by asking hours later.

ROOT CAUSE — two features shipped the same day bind the same port:
  * pulse-dispatch-remote.sh step 1 opens `ssh -R 127.0.0.1:7100:...` to the
    box, ExitOnForwardFailure=yes.
  * ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh (shipped 2026-07-28, the box self-heal) opens
    `ssh -L 127.0.0.1:7100:127.0.0.1:7100 zig-computer` FROM the box.
Both bind 127.0.0.1:7100 ON THE BOX. Whichever is up first wins; the other
gets "remote port forwarding failed for listen port 7100".

A local forward from the box has been up since Jul 28 (pid 1220000, user
andrew) — left behind by last session's self-heal verification. It is
HEALTHY: `curl 127.0.0.1:7100/api/health` from the box returns 200 right now.
So the box had a working path to the fleet proxy, and the dispatch killed
itself rather than use it.

ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh is already the tolerant half ("never fights a healthy
tunnel — if the port answers, do nothing"). pulse-dispatch-remote.sh is the
intolerant half. The asymmetry IS the bug. Step 3's A3 already treats the
box-owned forward as a legitimate state (it calls the self-heal and accepts
the result) — step 1 just dies ~370 lines before A3 can say so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On marketing-vps, open the box-side forward:
   `~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure`
   (or simply observe the one live now: `ss -tlnp | grep 7100`).
2. Confirm it is HEALTHY from the box:
   `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:7100/api/health`
   -> 200.
3. From zig-computer run any remote dispatch, e.g.
   `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh --row di-wednesday --dir ~/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted --dry-run`
4. Observed: exits 71, `PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=failed-tunnel`,
   tunnel.err = "Error: remote port forwarding failed for listen port 7100".
   Nothing is surfaced to work:di. Expected: the dispatch adopts the healthy
   path and proceeds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Step 1 is ADOPT-OR-OPEN, tracking TUNNEL_MODE (owned|adopted):
      (a) try `-R` as today -> owned;
      (b) on bind failure open the control master WITHOUT the forward; if that
          fails the box is genuinely unreachable -> fail failed-tunnel;
      (c) with the master up, probe health FROM THE BOX (rsh, login shell,
          three-valued 200/000/other, same contract as /vps). 200 -> adopted,
          proceed, say so loudly. Anything else -> ask the box to drop only ITS
          OWN forward (`ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh down`, already pidfile-scoped —
          never pkill on a shared box), close the master, retry `-R` ONCE;
          still failing -> fail failed-tunnel with the real reason.
- [ ] TUNNEL_MODE is recorded in the run state dir and in the say/receipt trail.
- [ ] Teardown never kills a forward this run did not create (assert in a test).
- [ ] Cleanup DOES tear down a forward this run caused: when A3's self-heal
      opens a box-side forward mid-run, track it (A3_HEALED=1) and call
      `ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh down` on the box at cleanup in that case only.
      Restores the lifetime-bounded property CLAUDE.md promises. Adopted-mode
      forwards are never torn down.
- [ ] fail() surfacing inverted to cover the class: surface EVERY verdict
      EXCEPT failed-usage / failed-row (operator typos on hand-runs) and except
      --dry-run. Recursion guard and "surface_locally warns, never calls fail"
      must hold.
- [ ] test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh passes with NEW cases: adopt on a healthy
      pre-bound port; reclaim-and-retry on a dead-but-bound port; genuinely
      unreachable box still fails 71; failed-tunnel now surfaces.
- [ ] `bash -n` clean.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: paste a real `--dry-run` against marketing-vps showing
      TUNNEL_MODE=adopted and A3 green. The box's forward is up right now, so
      this is a live reproduction of the exact failing condition.

## Out of scope — file a bead, do not do it

ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh's own logic; the pulse ledger schema; the DI skills;
and the policy question of whether the box should hold a STANDING forward at
all (that is Zig's call, asked separately).
close_reason: done

title: tailnet acl: untag pico, add server→user rules for native Taildrop
description:
## Context

Tailscale Taildrop is hard-locked to same-user transfers (see f7n
WON'T FIX + runbook gotcha #23). User confirmed they want native
Taildrop between pico ↔ iPhone ↔ metis, accepting the trade-off that
pico loses tag:server identity. Hybrid model: zig-computer keeps tag
(public-internet edge, isolation matters); pico moves to user-owned
(internal home-LAN compute).

## ACL changes (this commit)

- Comment block rewritten to document the new identity model
- New L3 rule: `tag:server → autogroup:owner:*` (zig → pico-as-user)
- New SSH rule: `autogroup:member → autogroup:self` with action `check`
  (metis → pico SSH, with 12h re-auth)
- New SSH rule: `tag:server → autogroup:owner` with action `accept`
  (zig → pico SSH; `check` not possible since src is a tag)

## User action (NOT done by me)

1. Open https://login.tailscale.com/admin/acls/file → paste updated
   `tailscale/acl.jsonc` → Preview to confirm intent → don't save yet
2. Open https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines → click `pico` →
   Edit tags → remove `tag:server` → save. (Or via `tailscale set
   --advertise-tags=` on pico, but admin console is simpler.)
3. Save the ACL from step 1 (now that pico's tag matches the new rules)
4. Verify: `ssh pico` still works from zig-computer (rule 4 covers it)
5. Verify: `tailscale file cp /tmp/foo iphone-15-pro:` works FROM PICO
   (this is the new capability)

After step 5 confirms, this bead can close. If anything breaks (SSH to
pico from metis/iPhone, server-to-pico L3 traffic), the ACL preview's
"affected rules" view will say why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] tailscale/acl.jsonc updated with the 4 new rules
- [x] Comment block reflects the new identity model
- [ ] User pastes updated ACL into admin console (preview to confirm)
- [ ] User removes tag:server from pico via admin console
- [ ] User saves the ACL
- [ ] `ssh pico` from zig-computer still works (SSH rule 4 covers it)
- [ ] `ssh pico` from metis still works (SSH rule 2 covers it)
- [ ] `tailscale file cp /tmp/foo iphone-15-pro:` from pico succeeds
notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24 — full bi-directional Taildrop working

Sequence of operations that landed:
1. pico re-authed without --advertise-tags=tag:server → user-owned (azigler@github)
2. ACL rewritten: hosts block aliases pico → 100.72.47.4; L3 rule 4
   (tag:server → pico:*) replaces the old tag:server → tag:server rule
   for pico
3. Tailscale SSH grammar tested: tag-src → user-owned-dst is structurally
   impossible (autogroup:owner / user-identity / group-of-user-identity /
   host-alias / autogroup:self ALL rejected). Documented in
   acl.jsonc comments + zig-zone runbook gotcha #23
4. Alt-port macOS sshd at :2222 via /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.zig.sshd-

7. zig-computer's ~/.ssh/local Host pico block: HostName tailnet FQDN,
   Port 2222, User pico, IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ha, IdentitiesOnly yes,

Verified: ssh pico from zig-computer works via :2222 + key auth (no
Tailscale SSH). Taildrop pico → iphone-15-pro succeeded

title: seat-molt suite: case 26g flakes under gate load — mutate-o3qj S2 MIS-KILLED once, unreproducible standalone
description:
## Context
`agents/scheduler/mutate-o3qj-molt-refusal.sh` mis-killed mutant **S2
[refusal-reason-dropped]** once, inside a `git commit` gate run on 2026-08-10,
during the dotfiles-ckst conduit wave:

```
MIS-KILLED S2 [refusal-reason-dropped] the row lands with an empty reason
           case(s) that had to keep PASSING went red: 26g
           actually failing: 26a 26d 26f 26g 26h 26j
```

Case 26g is `want_verdict 26g "a 🔔 window still aborts" aborted-modal` in
test-seat-molt.sh — a REAL tmux fixture pane with `MOLT_IDLE_TIMEOUT=2`. S2 drops
the recorded REASON, which cannot affect a VERDICT, so 26g going red is the
harness reading a timing artifact as a mutation effect.

## Steps to Reproduce
Not reliably reproducible yet — that IS the bug. What is known:

1. Run a full `git commit` through `tools/githooks/pre-commit` with
   `agents/scheduler/pulse-escalate.sh` staged, so the gate runs ~9 suites and
   `mutate-pulse-escalate.sh` BEFORE reaching `mutate-o3qj-molt-refusal.sh`.
2. Observed once: ARM 1's S2 reports MIS-KILLED with 26g in the
   "had to keep PASSING" list; the gate blocks the commit.
3. `bash agents/scheduler/mutate-o3qj-molt-refusal.sh` standalone: rc=0, all
   mutants killed — three consecutive runs the same hour, one immediately after
   the failure.
4. Synthetic-load attempt (4 busy-loops, 12-core box, loadavg 1.4 -> 5.9),
   3 consecutive `test-seat-molt.sh` runs: 69/69 every time. NOT reproduced, so
   the trigger is sharper than CPU load — most likely contention on the fixture
   tmux server, or the 2s idle timeout racing modal classification.

## Evidence it is not the conduit wave
- `git diff main..HEAD -- agents/scheduler/seat-molt.sh
  agents/scheduler/test-seat-molt.sh` is EMPTY on that branch: both files are
  byte-identical to main.
- The failing arm is the seat-molt RECORDER, which that wave never touched.

## Why it matters
A mutation harness that flakes is worse than one that fails: it gates it06's
"refused twice summons Zig" arm, and a MIS-KILLED verdict blocks a commit for a
reason unrelated to the change being committed. The next person to hit it will be
tempted to re-run until green, which is how a REAL mis-kill gets waved through.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The race is identified and named in the suite (not just retried away)
- [ ] 26e/26g pass under contention — demonstrated with a repro that fails
      BEFORE the fix, not merely N green runs after it
- [ ] mutate-o3qj-molt-refusal.sh green from inside a full `git commit` gate run

title: the guarded merge sequence has NO owner — AGENTS.md and /orchestrator each name the other, and the commands exist in neither
description:
Hit live while merging a dotfiles-ogkz subagent wave, 2026-08-02.

## Context
The 2026-08-01 single-owner consolidation (dotfiles-oec6) pointed these two at each
other and the content fell out between them.

agents/AGENTS.md, "Delegation":
    "The merge / bead-close / worktree-cleanup sequence after a subagent finishes,
     with all of its guards, lives in **`/orchestrator`** — run it, don't retype it."

~/.claude/skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md, "After Subagent Completes":
    "Then run the merge sequence — **single owner: `~/dotfiles/agents/AGENTS.md`,
     "Delegation"** (assert $TARGET -> BEFORE=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -> guarded merge
     -> SHA-moved + --is-ancestor checks -> br close -> commit .beads/issues.jsonl
     -> git worktree remove --force --force + git branch -D -> conditional remote
     delete). That block is loaded in every session; copying it here is how the two
     drift."

Each declares the OTHER the single owner. The runnable commands are in neither.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd ~/dotfiles
    grep -n "is-ancestor\|BEFORE=\$(git rev-parse\|worktree remove" agents/AGENTS.md
    # -> no output. AGENTS.md has none of the guards it is credited with owning.

    sed -n "/^## Delegation/,/^## Beads lifecycle/p" agents/AGENTS.md
    # -> ends by pointing at /orchestrator. No commands.

Then follow the chain as an orchestrator would: AGENTS.md -> /orchestrator ->
AGENTS.md. It terminates in a loop with nothing executable.

## Why this is P1
The ONLY surviving description is /orchestrator's parenthetical step LIST, which is a
summary, not a runnable block. An orchestrator that follows the pointer chain in good
faith finds nothing to run and improvises — landing on exactly the bare
`git merge worktree-agent-XXX` that both documents warn "no-ops SILENTLY on cwd drift
or an agent that committed nothing."

So the guard rule survived the refactor while the guard itself did not, and the
failure is silent by construction. Same shape as dotfiles-cxle (the consumer reports
success while the step stopped working).

This is also CLAUDE.md rule 2 (a documented EXAMPLE is executable): the missing block
is worse than a wrong one, because a wrong example fails loudly.

## Candidate fix
Put the runnable block in exactly ONE place and make the other a pointer that names
the file AND section. Given AGENTS.md is loaded in every session and /orchestrator is
loaded on demand, AGENTS.md is the better host — but either works as long as the
pointer is one-directional. Then add a guard that fails when a "single owner: X"
pointer resolves to a section that does not contain the artifact it claims to own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the guarded sequence exists, verbatim and runnable, in exactly one document
- [ ] the other document points to it one-directionally (no mutual "single owner")
- [ ] the block is RUN once end-to-end before being committed (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
- [ ] a check catches a "single owner" pointer whose target lacks the content
- [ ] the check is OBSERVED to fail against the current circular state before the fix
close_reason: Fixed in parallel by Zig's dc99ec8 while this session ran. Verified: agents/AGENTS.md now carries the runnable guards (--is-ancestor :236, worktree remove --force --force :248) and /orchestrator points at it one-directionally. NOT implemented: a check that fails when a 'single owner' pointer resolves to a section lacking the content it claims to own.

title: bead decomposition gate — re-evaluate bead size at ASSIGNMENT time, not only at writing time (Zig idea 2026-08-13, explicitly not decided)
description:
## Context
Zig's question, routed via seneschal mail (dotfiles.jsonl row 14, ref idea-bead-decomposition-gate, 2026-08-13): what stops agents from making mega-beads? Is a DECOMPOSING STEP missing — something that looks at any bead BEFORE assigning it and splits it into linked sub-beads?

WHAT EXISTS (verified in the mail, do not re-derive): beads/SKILL.md:60 'one bead = one commit'; :508 '4+ criteria or 4+ files = split'; :509 'multiple and-then = split or epic'; epics + child beads supported; /check already emits its readiness summary AS A CHILD BEAD. So the NORM exists, the THRESHOLD is numeric, the CONTAINER exists.

THE GAP, precisely: the split rule is advisory prose, evaluated by the same agent that just wrote the bead, at the moment it is least motivated to notice. Nothing re-evaluates at ASSIGNMENT time — after /spec + /check, when the bead is bigger and better understood, about to be handed to three agents (test, impl, scrutinize) who each inherit the whole scope. On the derive/drop/assert/refuse ladder, '4+ criteria = split' sits at the bottom; Zig's idea moves it to assert (warn at dispatch) or refuse (block).

## Design questions to weigh (from the mail — answers needed, not assumptions)
1. WHERE: /dispatch is the obvious hook, but the marshal selects beads without it — a /dispatch-only gate misses the highest-volume, least-watched consumer.
2. AUTOMATIC vs ADVISORY: auto-decomposition rewrites bead identity and can shred cold-start context; advisory 'this looks like 6 deliverables, split or confirm' may capture most value risk-free.
3. WHO decomposes: cheap mechanical pre-check first (count criteria/files/'and then'), agent only when the count trips.
4. COUNTER-CASE: some work IS one commit with many criteria; a hard refuse trades a mega-bead for a coordination problem. Needs an escape hatch with stated reason (precedent: dotfiles-nneb, the gate with no escape hatch, open 18 days and blocking).
5. WHETHER EPICS ALREADY ARE THE ANSWER: maybe a routing rule (when to reach for an epic) + a check, not new mechanism.

WHY IT MATTERS: mega-bead cost is paid three times downstream; the scrutinizer most needs a bounded surface. Paid precedent: dotfiles-3135 (3-task batch agent's task-2 verified diff lost).

Zig's closing instruction: 'I don't think we should decide now.' File and think, not spec.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A recommendation memo answering the five questions, surfaced to Zig for the decide
- [ ] Explicitly linked to the marshal-gardener design (its TOO-BIG verb is this same predicate)

## Write target
none (study → recommendation memo for Zig). Fable/orchestrator authoring work; the eventual gate implementation would be ~/demesne agents/hooks/ + /dispatch, in follow-up beads after the decide.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: REAL NUMBERS from the garden pass's first machine-wide live run (2026-08-14, GARDEN_RESULT=ok:18:1040 — the vpha build): of 1,040 open beads across all 18 stores, 422 (41%) trip the TOO-BIG predicate — 303 on 4+ AC boxes alone, 67 on 4+ file paths alone, 52 on both; the 'and then' heuristic NEVER trips alone, so the numeric criteria rule is doing all the work. A further 270 (26%) are INCOMPLETE — 250 lack an '## Acceptance Criteria' heading (many have '- [ ]' boxes under other headings), 20 have empty descriptions. Interpretation for the decide: (a) the split norm is honored by roughly a third of the graph at best — the assignment-time gate this bead studies has a large real population to act on; (b) the INCOMPLETE predicate's harshness is itself a fork (heading-match vs boxes-anywhere — one line in marshal-garden.sh's header); (c) any hard refuse at these ratios would block ~40% of the machine on day one, which argues for the advisory/propose rung first, exactly the shape vpha shipped (149 promotion proposals, 0 mutations). Data source: garden.report.v1 from the live run; re-derive with a fresh pass rather than citing these counts as current.

title: reef on pico: REEF_ROOT was unset, so the entire .env.local hierarchy was inert
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while wiring granola webhook auth (dotfiles-ks1u).

The launchd plist com.zig.reef-router set REEF_DIR but NOT REEF_ROOT, so loadReefEnv() resolved \$HOME/reef = /Users/pico/reef — a path that does not exist on pico. Every .env.local in the reef hierarchy was therefore being silently ignored on the box that actually runs the router.

This is a silent-misconfiguration class bug: nothing errored, nothing logged, env-driven config simply had no effect. Any coral adapter relying on .env.local for credentials or tuning has been running on defaults on pico since the router moved there.

Immediate fix applied: REEF_ROOT=/Users/pico/linearb/reef added to the plist (backup at com.zig.reef-router.plist.bak-20260725). Router restarted healthy.

## Steps to Reproduce

Before the fix: on pico, inspect the running router's resolved env root. loadReefEnv() falls back to \$HOME/reef, which does not exist, and no .env.local is loaded. No error is raised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- loadReefEnv fails LOUD (startup error) when its resolved root does not exist, instead of silently loading nothing
- an audit of which coral adapters were running on defaults on pico while REEF_ROOT was unset, and whether any of them silently lost credentials
- the plist change is version-controlled rather than living only on pico's disk
notes:
## Superseded — 2026-07-26 by dotfiles-13qu (the reef retirement)

Zig authorized full retirement of the reef rollback path after evidence that 6 of
7 corals had been dormant 3-5 months and the 7th (granola) had migrated to

title: blightmud: narrow ifmud gag to keepalive-only responses
description:
## Problem
The ifmud keepalive's gag mechanism used a time window (suppress_until) to bypass gagging during manual idle! invocations. Side effect: any user-typed who / idle / w also got silently gagged for 90 seconds after the keepalive, because the trigger matched the User-On-Idle header indiscriminately.

## Fix
Replace the time-based suppress with a boolean gag_next flag set by the keepalive itself. The trigger only gags when the keepalive flagged it; everything else (user-typed socializing commands) flows through naturally. Reset the flag on the End-of-List footer.

Also drop the manual idle! alias — no longer needed; user types idle directly and sees the response.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Keepalive response gagged (no spam every 90s)
- [x] User-typed who/idle/w fully visible
- [x] State backfill handles /load over older state tables
