title: /commit: a push fallback behind a pipe can never fire — the pipe masks git push's exit code
description:
Standing-practice proposal promoted out of the 2026-08-03 handoff note (offboard Step 2.6).

## Context
The orchestrator used this idiom for every push in a long session:

    if ! git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; then
      git fetch origin && git merge --no-edit origin/main && git push origin main
    fi

`if !` tests the exit status of the PIPELINE, which is `tail` — always 0. So the
fetch+merge absorb path CANNOT run, ever. It was written specifically to satisfy the
AGENTS.md "two writers" rule and it satisfied nothing.

This is invisible while pushes succeed. It surfaced only when a real rejection landed
(marketing-vps / another session had pushed four commits): the push failed, the
fallback silently did not fire, and the divergence was caught ONLY by the separate
`git ls-remote` comparison that /commit already mandates as push proof.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd <repo behind its remote>
    if ! git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; then echo "FALLBACK RAN"; fi
    # push fails; "FALLBACK RAN" never prints; exit status of the `if` is tail's 0

## Why it belongs in /commit
/commit already carries the push-proof anti-pattern ("`git rev-parse HEAD` as push proof
— it prints your local head, not what the remote got"). This is the same family one
level down: a guard whose exit code is swallowed before anything reads it. The existing
ls-remote proof is what caught it, which is a good argument for that rule and a good
place to note this.

## Fix
Capture the status without a pipe (`git push origin main; rc=$?`), or use PIPESTATUS.
Then keep the ls-remote comparison regardless — it is the check that actually bit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /commit names this idiom explicitly as an anti-pattern, with the reason
- [ ] the corrected form is shown and has been RUN (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
- [ ] the ls-remote proof stays mandatory — it is what caught this one
close_reason: Landed in agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md (781aef5), immediately after the rev-parse push-proof block, plus one appended sentence on /commit's TOOLKIT anti-pattern line. Named as 'the rev-parse trap one level down — a guard whose signal is swallowed before anything reads it', with the durable tell pinned: the failure mode is SILENCE, which is why it survived a whole session. It states explicitly that the ls-remote proof is NOT redundant with the fallback — it is what catches the fallback itself being broken. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG and the agent caught it: I sanctioned ${PIPESTATUS[0]} as an alternative. It is bash-only and expands EMPTY in this fleet's zsh 5.9, failing open exactly as the bug it would replace — I hit that live, printing 'push succeeded' on a rejected push. It is now documented as a 🚫, not an alternative, with zsh's lowercase 1-indexed $pipestatus shown alongside. The agent also sharpened my own measurement: my pipestatus[1]=0 reading was contaminated, because ANY intervening command clobbers the array; captured immediately it is 1. Orchestrator verified independently: no $N skill-arg substitution hazards (rule 7), TOOLKIT still a digest at 40,169 bytes, and the documented fix EXTRACTED VERBATIM by regex from the committed SKILL.md and executed under zsh against a throwaway repo whose remote had moved — push rejected, fallback fired, fetch+merge, push landed, ls-remote proof MATCH.

title: spec: THE MAILMAN — seneschal-curated delivery to running seats; Granola awareness; external-source registry
description:
## 1. Overview
THE MAILMAN — seneschal-curated delivery of arriving mail to RUNNING seats at
safe boundaries. The reverse direction of THE CONDUIT (dotfiles-4x49: seats
ask upward; here, mail flows downward/inward). Zig's directive (2026-08-10
~10:15 PT, via seneschal): the seneschal watches all seats' mailboxes; when
mail arrives for a running seat it reads the mail, reads what the seat is
doing, and hand-delivers at a safe boundary — "curated delivery, never
mid-flight injection... you become almost like part mailman." Urgency is a
judgment call; some mail correctly waits for next wake.

Also in scope: the GRANOLA TRANSCRIPT AWARENESS seam (work-meeting
transcripts as the first external mail source) and the EXTERNAL SOURCE
REGISTRY (second source: the LinearB Vercel/Slack-reply watcher spool,
building now under Zig's direct delegation).

Sources (1.1): the directive relay (seneschal peer message ~10:15 PT batch);
dotfiles-7fik (POST R1-R6, esp. R3 delivery-at-wake); dotfiles-4x49 +
readiness (message shape, deferred-never-suppressed, advisory doctrine);
dotfiles-mail-spec-c6mp (transport contract); lb-granola-commit.service
(existing Granola→Zapier→box→repo commit path); agents/lib/tmux-send.sh
(text/keys separation, landed ee2cf55); seneschal charter + 4x49's ruled
narrow write grant; the hall-never-types principle.

NOT covered: the POST substrate itself (7fik); upward question routing
(4x49); acting on transcript content (explicitly forbidden without Zig);
LinearB seat topology (seneschal rec is ONE seat identity + task-scoped
lane sessions + top-level spool — recorded here ONLY as
PENDING-ZIG-RATIFICATION, see OQ; nothing in this spec depends on which way
he rules); outward-facing actions (htqt).

## 2. Current State / Baseline
- 7fik R3 (spec'd, unbuilt): delivery at wake, NEVER injection — a seat reads
  its post at /onboard and at natural boundaries; NOTHING pushes into a
  running context. Live urgency = SendMessage or push-to-Zig.
- The hall-never-types principle: no automation types into a live pane; the
  only sanctioned pane-typing path is pulse-inject's --cmd grant (a real user
  turn at window creation) and now tmux-send.sh (text call and key call
  always separate).
- Cross-config-dir gap (live today): SendMessage cannot reach seats on other
  config dirs (~/.claude-work di-* windows) — delivery there is only possible
  via tmux-send.sh. The Vercel/Slack watcher is being built by exactly such a
  seat; its spool will be seneschal-watched.
- Granola: lb-granola-commit.service already commits arriving transcripts to
  the repo. No notification consumer exists — transcripts land silently.
- Seneschal: daily brief + (4x49) conduit answers with the narrow write
  grant; expanded interim heartbeat intercepting 🔔 windows fleet-wide.
- Lexicon glyphs: 🧠 thinking · 🔔 needs Zig · ✅ idle · 🌀 compacting · bare
  name = fresh context awaiting first prompt.

## 3. Changes and Decisions
- C1 R3 AMENDMENT (the load-bearing change): delivery-at-wake remains the
  FLOOR and the default. The mailman adds ONE controlled exception: the
  seneschal may deliver a READ NUDGE to a RUNNING seat at a SAFE BOUNDARY.
  Why: wake-only delivery leaves a running seat blind to arrived context for
  the length of its (possibly days-long) session. Fail-open: if the seneschal
  is down or unsure, mail simply waits for wake — never lost, never forced.
- C2 NUDGE, NEVER CONTENT: what lands in the pane is a one-line doorbell
  ("mail: <n> new for <seat> — read your spool; urgency=<u>"), sent via
  tmux-send.sh as a real user turn. The seat then reads its own spool
  (cursor semantics, 7fik R2). The mailman never pastes mail bodies into a
  context — curation is WHEN to ring, not rewriting the mail. Preserves
  hall-never-types with one narrow sanctioned sender.
- C3 SAFE BOUNDARY (mechanical): pane glyph ✅ or bare-name (idle prompt),
  AND no in-flight subagent/background work visible for that seat in the
  state bus. NEVER 🧠, NEVER 🌀. 🔔 only when the mail plausibly answers the
  blocking question (seneschal judgment, must cite why). If no safe boundary
  appears before the urgency deadline: urgency=now escalates per 4x49
  doctrine (push Zig, deferred-never-suppressed); urgency=wake just waits.
- C4 CURATION CONTRACT: per delivery the seneschal records {mail ref, seat,
  boundary evidence (glyph + ts), urgency, decision: delivered|held|
  escalated}. Held mail obeys deferred-never-suppressed: a hold past the
  source's deadline escalates, it never silently expires. The no-dispatch
  charter holds — delivery is routing.
- C5 GRANOLA AWARENESS SEAM: Works implements a post-commit hook on
  lb-granola-commit.service → appends {source: granola, path, meeting meta}
  to the seneschal's spool. The seneschal reads each transcript on arrival,
  holds the context (brief-ready), and NEVER acts from a transcript without
  Zig. Opportunities: raised to Zig (brief or push per urgency); on his
  approval, delegated to the LinearB seat spawned in the correct ~/linearb
  subfolder — the spawn happens under ZIG'S standing grant, exercised
  per-item on his approval, never seneschal authority.
- C6 EXTERNAL SOURCE REGISTRY: each source declares {name, spool path,
  default urgency, deadline}. Charter entries at spec time: granola
  (urgency=wake default), vercel-slack-watcher (urgency=now default — Slack
  replies age fast). Registry lives beside 7fik's channel INDEX; an
  unregistered spool is an audit finding (7fik R6 extended).
- C7 SEAMS: seneschal skill (mailman duties + curation contract);
  lb-granola-commit.service hook (Works); the watcher spool registration
  (LinearB seat's build, via Works coordination); pulse-escalate (held-mail
  deadline shares the 4x49 conduit watcher); 7fik R3 text amendment rides
  the POST build; tmux-send.sh is the only delivery instrument.

## 4. Formal Specification
DELIVERY DECISION (per arriving mail, seneschal-side pseudocode):
  read mail; read target seat state (glyph, state bus, current work).
  if seat not running → leave in spool (wake floor). done.
  if urgency == wake → leave in spool unless a safe boundary is imminent
     and the mail is context the seat's CURRENT task needs (judgment, cite).
  if urgency == now:
     wait for safe boundary up to source deadline;
     boundary appears → tmux-send.sh nudge (one line, real user turn);
     deadline first → escalate per 4x49 (push, P1 bead if question-shaped).
  record curation row (C4) either way.

SAFE-BOUNDARY PREDICATE: glyph in {✅, bare-name} AND state-bus shows no
in-flight work for the seat AND pane's last line is a prompt (tmux
capture-pane tail). All three; any doubt = not safe.

NUDGE SHAPE (the ONLY thing ever typed): "mail: N new (urgency=U, source=S)
— read your spool". No mail content, no instructions.

GRANOLA FLOW: commit lands → hook appends spool entry → seneschal reads
transcript at its next turn → awareness recorded (one line in next brief:
meeting, participants, load-bearing items) → opportunity? → Zig (never
auto-act) → approved? → LinearB lane delegation under Zig's grant.

LOOP/AUTHORITY SAFETY: the mailman adds no authority — WHO decides anything
is unchanged; only WHEN a seat learns of mail changes. The seneschal's own
mail has no mailman (it reads its spool at its own turns). Delivery to an
interactive window Zig is live in: never nudge — he's there; the mail waits
or he reads the brief.

## 5. Test Cases (≥10)
TEST T1 wake-floor
INPUT: mail for a not-running seat
EXPECTED: sits in spool; seat reads at /onboard; no nudge attempted
RATIONALE: R3 floor unchanged.
TEST T2 safe-boundary-nudge
INPUT: urgency=now mail; target ✅ idle, bus clear
EXPECTED: one-line nudge via tmux-send.sh; seat reads spool; curation row 'delivered'
RATIONALE: the core mailman path.
TEST T3 never-mid-flight
INPUT: urgency=now mail; target 🧠 for entire deadline window
EXPECTED: zero pane writes; escalation fires at deadline; row 'escalated'
RATIONALE: C3 — curation never becomes injection.
TEST T4 nudge-not-content
INPUT: any delivery
EXPECTED: pane receives exactly the one-line doorbell; mail body absent
RATIONALE: C2 — grep the pane capture for body text, must miss.
TEST T5 seneschal-down-failopen
INPUT: mail arrives while seneschal session absent
EXPECTED: spool intact; wake floor serves it; nothing lost
RATIONALE: C1 fail-open.
TEST T6 held-mail-deadline
INPUT: urgency=now held past source deadline (no safe boundary)
EXPECTED: escalation per 4x49; never silent expiry
RATIONALE: deferred-never-suppressed extends to held mail.
TEST T7 granola-awareness-no-action
INPUT: transcript commit lands
EXPECTED: spool entry; seneschal awareness recorded; ZERO actions/spawns/bead-writes from content
RATIONALE: C5 — awareness is not authority.
TEST T8 opportunity-gate
INPUT: transcript contains an actionable opportunity
EXPECTED: raised to Zig; delegation only after his approval; spawn in correct ~/linearb subfolder
RATIONALE: C5 — the grant is Zig's, exercised per-item.
TEST T9 cross-config-dir-delivery
INPUT: mail for a ~/.claude-work di-* seat
EXPECTED: nudge via tmux-send.sh works where SendMessage cannot; same boundary rules
RATIONALE: the gap that makes tmux-send the instrument.
TEST T10 unregistered-spool
INPUT: a spool file with no registry entry
EXPECTED: audit finding (7fik R6 extended); mailman refuses to watch it
RATIONALE: C6 — no shadow channels.
TEST T11 zig-live-window
INPUT: mail for a window with a live Zig conversation
EXPECTED: no nudge; brief/wake path
RATIONALE: §4 authority safety — never interpose on the human.
TEST T12 boundary-race
INPUT: seat goes 🧠 between boundary check and send
EXPECTED: send aborted or lands as queued input the seat reads at ITS next
prompt (tmux semantics); never corrupts an in-flight turn; row records which
RATIONALE: the check-then-send race must be closed or explicitly benign.

## 6. Open Questions (interrogator pass: 16 questions, fresh agent, 2026-08-10 ~17:5xZ)
- OQ-01 (P1, ZIG FORK): The mailman inverts the seneschal charter's core invariant (no send-keys, no state, never types into another window). Separate seat, or charter amendment II?
  - Recommendation: NOT a separate seat — a second Zig-ratified narrow amendment: exactly one sanctioned hand (the validated nudge template via tmux-send.sh) + one durable artifact (the curation ledger). The constitutional trade recorded in seats.yml + constitution cross-ref, as with 4x49's amendment. Spec is inert until ratified.
- OQ-02 (P1): What process watches the spools, at what latency?
  - Recommendation: a systemd .path (or light poll timer) unit, Works-built, that on spool-append nudges/spawns the seneschal via the 4x49 conduit machinery itself. Deadline clock starts at spool-append; registry gains max_watch_latency as part of each source's contract.
- OQ-03 (P1): A nudge into an open AskUserQuestion (🔔) may SELECT AN OPTION — fabricating Zig's answer.
  - Recommendation: v1 FORBIDS 🔔 delivery outright (the draft's 'plausibly answers' clause is struck). Mail for a blocked seat routes to Zig's channel — it is his question. Revisit only after measured TUI behavior.
- OQ-04 (P1): The two-call race (text, sleep, Enter) — seat can flip 🧠 between calls.
  - Recommendation: re-check the boundary between text and Enter; on state change retract (C-u) if possible; if Enter already sent, the row records queued-under-changed-state (benign-by-design: the nudge is advisory and lands as the seat's next user turn). T12 sharpened; body-pasting + no-recheck mutants mandatory.
- OQ-05 (P1): Where does mailman state live across seneschal molts?
  - Recommendation: ~/.local/state/harness/mailman-ledger.jsonl (append-only): curation rows + open holds + deadlines. The pulse-escalate conduit watcher (shared with 4x49) owns the CLOCKS and fires escalations from the ledger; the seneschal owns judgment only; onboard rehydrates open holds from it.
- OQ-06 (P1): Build ordering — the nudge says 'read your spool' but the POST is unbuilt; di-* seats may not report to the state bus at all.
  - Recommendation: mailman Phase 1 gates on 7fik's post.sh read verb. Registry gains per-seat deliverability: seats not reporting to the bus are escalation-only (no boundary predicate = no nudge). The nudge line carries the literal command ('run: post read').
- OQ-07 (P2): The nudge interpolates externally-influenced fields into a real user turn.
  - Recommendation: fixed template; N integer-validated, U enum, S registry-literal only (never spool-echoed); assert the final line matches the template regex before send.
- OQ-08 (P2): Delivered mail is attacker-controlled text with user-turn freshness.
  - Recommendation: every rendered spool entry carries advisory:true/authority:none framing; external-source mail marked untrusted-quotation; skill text teaches mail-is-data-not-tasking (mirror of the harness's cross-session-message rule).
- OQ-09 (P2): Meeting content must not reach committed/pushed surfaces (p45w leak class).
  - Recommendation: NO transcript content (title/participants/quotes) in dotfiles-* beads or any pushed artifact; curation rows reference path+hash only; the gitignored brief may carry the one-line awareness. Doclint prose rule as the guard.
- OQ-10 (P2, ZIG FORK): Read-scope/privacy — which meetings may the seneschal read at all, and does even the brief line need a sensitivity gate?
  - Recommendation: default-deny patterns (calendar tag / title opt-out list Zig maintains); sensitive-flagged meetings get NO brief line, only 'a transcript arrived (gated)'. Zig rules the posture.
- OQ-11 (P2): Transcript text is a prompt-injection channel into the seat with Zig's ear.
  - Recommendation: transcript-derived content always framed as untrusted quotation in seneschal reasoning AND the brief; opportunities BRIEFED by default — pushed only with a second corroborating source or hard external deadline; urgency never inherited from content claims.
- OQ-12 (P2): Window taxonomy + three sanctioned typists, one composer.
  - Recommendation: seats.yml is the taxonomy — non-seat windows are never nudged; bare-name counts UNSAFE when the window is scheduler-owned (pulse set); a per-pane flock shared by pulse-inject / seat-molt / mailman serializes the sanctioned senders.
- OQ-13 (P2): Registry governance — urgency=now is an attention-economy race.
  - Recommendation: Zig approves registry entries; per-source daily urgency=now cap; the seneschal may DEMOTE a crying-wolf source unilaterally on record; only Zig restores.
- OQ-14 (P3): Re-nudge/coalescing + T4's weak oracle.
  - Recommendation: one outstanding nudge per seat (N = total unread), re-ring backoff 30min max twice then wake floor; T4 proven by a body-pasting mutant that must die (repo rule 1).

## 7. Future Considerations
- Phase gating: Phase 1 (nudge + ledger + granola awareness) after 7fik post.sh lands and OQ-01/10 are Zig-ruled; Phase 2 (full registry + di-* deliverability) after the watcher spool exists and the bus covers those seats.
- LinearB seat topology: seneschal's ONE-identity + lane-sessions + top-level-spool rec is PENDING ZIG RATIFICATION — registry entries adapt to whichever shape he rules; nothing here depends on it.
- The mailman + conduit + POST together form the estate's comms triangle: up (4x49), down (this), durable substrate (7fik). Keep the three specs cross-consistent; message shape drift between them is a defect.

- [ ] Section 1.1 sources documented (directive relay, 7fik, 4x49, c6mp, granola service, tmux-send, charter)
- [ ] OQ-01 (charter amendment II) and OQ-10 (transcript privacy posture) walked through the seneschal to ZIG before /check closes them
- [ ] 12 test cases now; the OQ-04/14 mutants (body-pasting, no-recheck) folded at /check
- [ ] Build gates recorded: Phase 1 behind 7fik post.sh + the two Zig rulings; hook seam (lb-granola-commit) to Works only post-readiness
- [ ] Cross-consistency asserted with 4x49 + 7fik message shapes before impl

title: hooks: wire the .offboard-pending marker (documented but never created)
description:
## Problem
/offboard and /onboard both document a `.offboard-pending` marker:
/offboard claims pre-compact.sh + session-end.sh create it, and
/onboard Step 0 checks for it to run /offboard retroactively. No hook
actually creates the file — session-end.sh only flushes bead state.

## Symptom
The retroactive-offboard safety net is dead code. A session that ends
without /offboard is never caught by the next session's /onboard,
because the marker /onboard checks for is never written.

## Cause
session-end.sh was never given marker-creation logic; the skill docs
describe a mechanism that was never implemented.

## Source
Surfaced 2026-05-21 by the harness hooks-analysis review.

## Fix
Wire session-end.sh to drop .offboard-pending at the repo root unless
HEAD committed this session's handoff note (= /offboard ran). Keep
pre-compact.sh out of it — a same-session post-compaction /onboard
would misread its own marker. Correct the /offboard + /onboard docs;
gitignore the marker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] session-end.sh creates .offboard-pending when /offboard didn't run
- [ ] no marker when /offboard ran (HEAD committed the handoff note)
- [ ] skipped inside worktrees
- [ ] /offboard + /onboard docs corrected; .offboard-pending gitignored
- [ ] regression test test-session-end.sh passes

title: hooks: require-isolation guards the WRONG repo on a cross-repo subagent dispatch
description:
## Context
Hit live on 2026-07-27 from a `~/hevyd` session dispatching work into `~/harnessd`
(bead harnessd-zvum).

`~/.claude/hooks/pre-tool-use-require-isolation.sh` blocks any
`subagent_type: "subagent"` dispatch that lacks `isolation: "worktree"`. Its stated
rationale is git-index racing: two subagents in the orchestrator's own working
directory corrupt each other's commits.

But the worktree is created from the ORCHESTRATOR'S repo. When the work lives in a
different repo, satisfying the hook produces a worktree the agent never uses, while
it writes directly to the other repo's shared checkout — exactly the hazard the hook
exists to prevent, now invisible to it. The dispatch reads as guarded and is not.

Single cross-repo agents are fine (no concurrent writer). TWO of them targeting the
same foreign repo would race silently, and the hook would pass both.

Precedent: this project's own history records "ten worktree subagents, two repos"
(hevyd handoff 2026-07-27), so cross-repo dispatch is established practice here, not
a one-off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decide the intended posture for cross-repo dispatch: teach the hook to detect
      it, or document that isolation is orchestrator-repo-scoped and cross-repo
      dispatch must be serialized by the orchestrator
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, the hook's message no longer implies a guarantee it does
      not provide for this case
- [ ] If detection is chosen, a cross-repo dispatch either targets a worktree of the
      RIGHT repo or is refused with a reason
close_reason: done

title: seat-resolve: LC_ALL=C makes tmux mangle its TAB separators — every seat reads live=no
description:
## Context
agents/lib/seat-resolve.sh's liveness enumeration (_seat_live_windows) builds a
TAB-separated tmux format:

    tmux -S <sock> list-windows -a -F "$sock<TAB>#{session_name}<TAB>#{window_name}"

and _seat_resolve_foreign then filters it with awk -F'\t' on $3.

tmux SANITISES its -F output for the CLIENT's locale: in a non-UTF-8 locale it
renders a literal TAB as `_`. So under LC_ALL=C, $3 is empty for every row,
nothing matches the roster, and seat_resolve reports live=no FOR EVERY SEAT ON
THE MACHINE, with rc 0 and no diagnostic. A silent, total, wrong answer.

## Steps to Reproduce
On zig-computer (tmux 3.5a), with a private server and a fixture roster:

    tmux -S /tmp/x.sock new-session -d -s slfix -n scratch sleep 900
    tmux -S /tmp/x.sock list-windows -a -F "A<TAB>#{window_name}" | od -c
        -> A \t scratch            (default locale)
    LC_ALL=C tmux -S /tmp/x.sock list-windows -a -F "A<TAB>#{window_name}" | od -c
        -> A _ scratch             (the TAB became an underscore)
    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 ...             -> A \t scratch again

Then, with SEATS_YML/SEAT_TMUX_SOCKET_DIR pointed at that fixture:

    bash agents/lib/seat-resolve.sh --seat scratch | grep '^live'
        -> live=yes
    LC_ALL=C bash agents/lib/seat-resolve.sh --seat scratch | grep '^live'
        -> live=no                 (the seat is demonstrably up)

## Why this is a live landmine, not a curiosity
`export LC_ALL=C` is the standard preamble of the scheduler's watchers —
pico-health.sh and pulse-escalate.sh both open with it. Any future consumer of
seat-resolve that copies that preamble inherits the bug. dotfiles-vbzo's
seat-liveness.sh hit it during development: under LC_ALL=C it read the entire
fleet as dead, which for that watcher means a P1 human: bead and a push about
every seat at once.

seat-liveness.sh worked around it LOCALLY — it refuses to set LC_ALL=C, repairs a
non-UTF-8 locale to C.UTF-8 when one exists, and exits checker-broken when none
does (test-seat-liveness.sh cases 29/30, mutant M8). That protects one consumer.
The library is still tab-dependent for everyone else.

## Fix shape
Make seat-resolve.sh's own tmux calls locale-proof rather than asking every
caller to be. In rough order of preference: (1) a separator tmux will not
sanitise in any locale, with the awk splitting updated to match; (2) force
LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 for the tmux invocation only, with a fallback when no UTF-8
locale exists; (3) detect the mangling and refuse loudly instead of returning a
confident live=no.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] seat_resolve --seat NAME reports live=yes for a live window with LC_ALL=C exported
- [ ] agents/lib/test-seat-resolve.sh has a case that fails without the fix
- [ ] Every current consumer re-checked for the same tab dependence

title: retreat cruft B: retire the conduit machinery — and pre-commit references it, so check callers FIRST
description:
## Context
Once the seven rows run locally (done 2026-08-05), this machinery has no runtime caller.
Audited 2026-08-05.

    agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh        (~2,300 lines) + test-
    agents/scheduler/vps-preflight.sh
    agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh             + test-
    agents/scheduler/vps-repo-manifest.txt
    agents/vault/vps-peer-bootstrap.sh
    agents/vault/vps-phase2-symlinks.sh
    agents/scheduler/templates/claude-gateway-tunnel.{service,timer}
    agents/scheduler/templates/claude-vault-sync.timer   (verify: peer-only or shared?)

## ⚠️ THE TRAP — deleting these silently weakens a gate
`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` is referenced by **12 non-test files**, including:

    agents/hooks/pre-commit-checks.sh      <- the pre-commit gate keys on it
    agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md
    agents/infra.md

Delete the script without updating `pre-commit-checks.sh` and the gate either errors or —
worse — silently stops covering something while staying green. That is the exact failure
class this repo keeps hitting (`dotfiles-cxle`). **Check every caller before removing any
file here**, and re-run the hook suite after.

`vps-preflight.sh` and `vps-repo-refresh.sh` reference each other and the manifest, so they
come out together or not at all.

## Delete or archive — say WHICH, deliberately
The retreat doc requires the choice be stated, not defaulted. `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`
carries hard-won knowledge (the glyph matcher, the ownership guards, the surface relay);
git history preserves it either way, so deletion is defensible — but say so.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] every caller of each removed file identified and updated FIRST
- [ ] `agents/hooks/test/` suite green after, and the pre-commit gate still bites (prove
      with a mutant, per CLAUDE.md rule 1 — a green suite is not evidence)
- [ ] delete-vs-archive stated per file
- [ ] no dangling reference anywhere, including SKILL.md files and infra.md
close_reason:
DELETED, per Zig's explicit call 2026-08-08 (not archived). Commit f21238e.

8 files / 6,768 lines removed: pulse-dispatch-remote.sh + suite, vps-preflight.sh,
vps-repo-refresh.sh + suite, vps-repo-manifest.txt, vps-peer-bootstrap.sh,
vps-phase2-symlinks.sh.

THE BEAD'S OWN TRAP DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and that matters. It named
agents/hooks/pre-commit-checks.sh as the gate that keys on the script; that file's
only mention is a comment at line 449. The real functional coupling was
tools/githooks/pre-commit, whose mapped_suites_for() named
test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh as a consumer suite for pulse-surface-queue.sh.
Deleting on the bead's stated caller list would have left the real one dangling.

Mutant proof (the bead required it): restoring the old mapping with the suite
deleted produces 'pre-commit: FAIL — the EXPLICIT SUITE MAP names 1 file(s) that do
not exist'. Baseline passed, second mutant also blocked, 11/11 mutants killed.

claude-vault-sync.timer verdict: SHARED, KEPT. systemctl showed it enabled, hourly,
last run 8 minutes before the check; the template header says shared. Deleting it
would have silently stopped the memory vault sync.

Agent's most useful surprise: its FIRST ledger probe was itself the dotfiles-cxle
defect — run with no stdin, the hook read no .tool_input.command, exited 0, and
'proved' the gate was dead. Two false verdicts before the harness was fixed.

title: br 0.1.7 -> 0.2.19 left a stale DB schema: br lint dies, doctor says schema OK, and the close gate blames the bead
description:
## Context

After upgrading `br` 0.1.7 -> 0.2.19 on `zig` (2026-08-01), `br lint` failed outright:

```
Error: Database error: internal error: column 'last_child' not found in table 'child_counters'
```

The 0.1.7 schema was `child_counters(parent_id, next_child_number)`; 0.2.19 expects
`child_counters(parent_id, last_child, …)`. **The migration never ran**, and nothing said so
until a command happened to need the column.

Three separate failures stacked on top of that, and the stacking is the real finding:

**1. `br lint` is dead, not degraded.** Every invocation errors. Any gate built on it is
therefore inoperative rather than lenient.

**2. `br doctor` reports `OK schema.tables` and `OK schema.columns`.** The one diagnostic
whose job is to catch this **passes** on it. Health read `degraded` for unrelated sync
reasons, so even the summary line pointed elsewhere.

**3. `pre-bead-close.sh` blamed the bead.** Closing `dotfiles-22xi` produced:

> Blocked: bead dotfiles-22xi has incomplete template sections.
> Error: Database error: internal error: column 'last_child' not found …

followed by advice to add `## Context` / `## Acceptance Criteria`. The bead **already had
`## Context`, `## Steps to Reproduce`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Fix` and one more**. The
gate ran `br lint`, got a non-zero exit for a reason it never inspected, and asserted a cause
it had not checked — verbatim the `dotfiles-kel5` shape, in a different gate. It does print
the DB error, but buried under a confident wrong headline, which is worse than silence
because it sends you to edit a bead that is fine.

## Steps to Reproduce

With a `.beads/beads.db` created by br 0.1.x, then br >= 0.2.x installed:

```bash
br lint <any-id>          # Database error: column 'last_child' not found
br doctor | grep schema   # OK schema.tables / OK schema.columns
br close <any-id>         # "incomplete template sections" — false
sqlite3 .beads/beads.db '.schema child_counters'
```

## Resolution applied on zig

JSONL is the source of truth and was committed (329 beads), so: backed the DB up to
`.beads/beads-backup-20260802.db`, moved a 143537s-orphaned `.write.lock` aside, deleted
`beads.db` + its `-fsqlite-ns-*` sidecars, and let 0.2.19 rebuild. Result: correct schema,
DB count 329 == JSONL 329 (was 305, i.e. **24 beads behind**), `br lint` clean, doctor
`degraded` -> `healthy`.

**Other machines are exposed.** `marketing-vps` reports br 0.2.16 and `pico` 0.2.11 per the
`dotfiles-1r6k` audit; any box that crossed 0.1.x -> 0.2.x has the same latent mismatch.

Separately, `br delete --hard` did NOT prune the tombstone from the JSONL as its `--help`
claims (`bd-2lcr` persists as `status: tombstone`).

Also a doctor false positive worth a line: it warns `.beads/.gitignore` is "missing expected
pattern(s): .write.lock" while `*.lock` on line 8 already ignores it. It greps for a literal
pattern instead of asking git whether the path is ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pre-bead-close.sh` distinguishes "lint found template problems" from "lint could not
      run" — a non-zero exit it did not inspect must not be reported as a bead defect
- [ ] `br doctor`'s schema check actually detects a missing expected column (it is the
      designated detector and it passed)
- [ ] `br` / `pico` / `marketing-vps` checked for the same stale schema and rebuilt if present
- [ ] the migration gap reported upstream to beads_rust, or a documented rebuild-on-upgrade step added
- [ ] doctor's gitignore check consults `git check-ignore` rather than grepping for a literal

title: conduit: the answer-side producer — socket-registry `answer` verb + the cited-answer contract
description:
## Context
dotfiles-ckst (the 4x49 tick-end subset) landed the ASKING half of the conduit and
the deadline watcher that guards it. The watcher closes a question when a row with
`"status":"answered"` and the same `ref` appears in
~/.local/state/harness/conduit-questions.jsonl — and NOTHING ON THE BOX WRITES ONE
YET. That is correct-but-incomplete by design (the seneschal answer-side is a later
wave, and "no answered row" is exactly "unanswered"), but it means every routed
question currently rides to its deadline and pushes, which is the floor working, not
the conduit working.

agents/lib/socket-registry.sh deliberately ships `register` / `lookup` / `spool` /
`ask` and NO `answer` verb, for the same reason: a producer with no author would
have been a wire format nobody was obliged to honour.

## Task
Build the answer-side producer, alongside the seneschal skill/charter work in 4x49's
impl order (item 4):

1. An `answer` verb on agents/lib/socket-registry.sh appending
   {ts, ref, status:"answered", verdict, citation, advisory-header, as-of} — the
   §4 answer contract (verdict := answered|bounced|escalated; OQ-03 citation roots;
   OQ-07 'advisory: routing / authority: none'; OQ-09 as-of ts).
2. Its cases in agents/lib/test-socket-registry.sh, and the watcher-side cases in
   agents/scheduler/test-pulse-escalate.sh that today hand-build an answered row
   (see the conduit_answered fixture) driving the REAL emitter instead.
3. A mutant in mutate-pulse-escalate.sh for an uncited answer being treated as
   escalate-pending rather than as closed (T7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `answer` verb ships with the full §4 answer shape and its own suite cases
- [ ] test-pulse-escalate.sh's answered-row fixture is produced by the real emitter
- [ ] An UNCITED answer does not close a ref (T7 / OQ-03)

title: pulse-inject: skip injection when target window is 🔔 (blocked on Andrew)
description: State-blind injector bug (diagnosed from Zig's question 2026-06-30). pulse-inject.sh step 4 send-keys the command + Enter UNCONDITIONALLY — it only checks pane_current_command==claude, never the session's interaction state. If a timer fires while the target window is blocked on an AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / permission prompt, the keystrokes feed the MODAL DIALOG (not the message composer): the command text is eaten and the trailing Enter resolves the dialog with the wrong/default answer — losing the tick AND mis-answering Zig's open question. (Not queued — queuing only happens at the composer.) Affects ALL pulse-style timers (explore pulse, daily-digest, elevate, local-coding-models, autonovel) since they all route through this one script. Fix: before the inject, read #{window_name}; the tmux-status.sh hook prefixes '🔔 ' on PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode) + permission Notifications and only clears it on resume (PostToolUse->🧠 / Stop->✅), so '🔔 ' is present exactly for the blocked-modal duration. If the name starts with 🔔, DEFER (log + exit 0); the next timer retries once answered. Guard is 🔔-specific — 🧠 (mid-turn, cleanly queues) / ✅ / 🌀 still inject. Regression test in test-pulse-inject.sh: a 🔔-prefixed window must NOT receive the command; the existing 🌀 case must still inject (proves 🔔-specificity).

title: molt lifecycle: the 75% guard's fired-once marker survives compaction — the backstop dies after the first molt; add the 50% boundary nudge
description:
## Context
Found live 2026-08-09 (Zig noticed 78% with no guard firing): stop-context-guard.sh fired once pre-compaction at 100%, wrote /tmp/claude-context-pct/<session_id>.fired, and the session compacted — same session_id, marker persists, guard permanently dead for the session's remaining life. Every molt/compact resurrects the problem: fresh context, dead backstop. ALSO missing: the doctrine says molt PROACTIVELY at boundaries past ~50%, but nothing nudges — the only mechanical signal was the (dead) 75% backstop.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Session fires the guard (marker written), then compacts (context resets, session_id unchanged)
2. Context climbs past 75 again: guard exits 0 at the marker check — no nudge, ever

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RE-ARM: the marker clears when context DROPS — statusline already writes pct per render; the guard (or a tiny companion) removes .fired when pct < threshold-20 (hysteresis, no flap); alternatively pre-compact.sh + seat-molt clear it explicitly on cycle — pick the mechanism that re-arms on BOTH compact and clear paths, argue it
- [ ] THE 50% NUDGE: a non-blocking Stop-hook line (exit 0, one line, once per N hours per session) at pct>=50: 'context past 50% — molt at your next boundary (offboard + seat-molt --self)'; never fires with the 75% path in the same turn; rate-limited so it is a nudge, not a nag
- [ ] test-stop-context-guard.sh cases: re-arm after drop; nudge fires at 55 once; nudge suppressed inside rate window; 75 backstop still fires after a re-arm
- [ ] Mutants: re-arm-removed (guard stays dead after drop) and nudge-always (nag) both die on named cases
close_reason: Molt lifecycle complete (merge 903a32b, agent 7e048d1). Turn-end stamp (stop-context-guard writes ~/.local/state/harness/turn-end/<sid> before any early exit — the harness TELLS the molt the turn ended); re-arm both paths (pct<threshold-20 + pre-compact clears .fired — dead-backstop-after-molt cannot recur); the 50% nudge (exit-2, 4h rate limit, advisory-degrades-open); seat-molt --self waits on the stamp (stale-pre-t0 refused, modal still refuses with a fresh stamp, --target keeps pane-stability). ## Guard: guard 42/42 + molt 48/48 + thresholds 17/17 on main; 6 molt + 3 guard mutants killed on named cases — M6 proves the pane-stability bug cannot return (23b: a pane stuck on 🧠 forever molts the moment the stamp lands). MB4 isolated from the new nudge at merge. Found live when the orchestrator's own molt sat blind under six builders' counters.

comments.text: FINDING 3, live (Zig's diagnosis confirmed in code): wait_for_idle keys on PANE-TEXT STABILITY (capture-pane hash), and background builders' token counters/spinners redraw every second — so --in-flight yes (the mode that most needs molting) can STRUCTURALLY never read idle; the first live --self run sat blind until killed. THE RIGHT SIGNAL: the Stop hook writes a turn-end timestamp (~/.local/state/harness/turn-end/<session>) — seat-molt waits for a turn-end NEWER than its own invocation instead of inferring from pixels; modal detection stays (an open AskUserQuestion means the turn did NOT end for molt purposes — check ordering). title: lexicon: false-idle ✅ while waiting on subagents → working-glyph; and glyph renames break exact-name tmux targeting
description:
## Context (Zig-routed via seneschal, 2026-08-10)
Two related lexicon defects, decide-once material:

1. FALSE IDLE: a session at rest showing ✅ while WAITING ON A SUBAGENT is mid-work, just not holding the turn — the dotfiles Works window during the 79zy builder waves was the live example. Zig wants those detected and rendered 🧠 (or a distinct working-glyph). Detection candidates: statusline/pane tail shows 'Waiting for N background agent' / the agent-tree lines; or harness state if the renderer can reach it. Likely owner: agents/hooks/tmux-status.sh (the rename-window writer) — verify at impl.

2. NAME-TARGETABILITY: glyph-prefix renames broke exact-name tmux targeting TWICE on 2026-08-10 ('marshal', 'imc-aug26' — external tooling targeting windows by name misses once the glyph lands). Decide ONCE, on this bead: either the lexicon preserves name-targetability (e.g. glyph in pane title / status format, never the window name — or renames preserve a matchable suffix and the fleet idiom greps it) or the fleet idiom moves to index/id targeting everywhere. Note pulse-inject/seat-molt/pulse-escalate all resolve panes — d5n3 already mandates resolve-by-NAME at check time, so whatever is decided must keep a stable resolvable name: a decision that breaks name-resolution collides with d5n3/vbzo. Record the ruling as a decision comment here before impl.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Waiting-on-subagent sessions render a working-glyph, not ✅ (live-verified with a real background agent)
- [ ] The targeting ruling recorded on this bead (preserve-name vs index/id idiom), with the d5n3 name-resolution constraint addressed
- [ ] Whichever ruling: the two broken cases ('marshal'-style seat targeting, external tooling) demonstrably work after
- [ ] Made to fail: a test/negative control for the false-idle detection

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ## RULING — 2026-08-11 (Works seat, decide-and-proceed per this bead's decide-once instruction; recorded before impl). THE GLYPH LEAVES THE WINDOW NAME. Lexicon glyphs render as DECORATION — a @glyph tmux window option displayed by window-status-format/window-status-current-format — and window names stay bare and stable ('dotfiles', 'marshal', 'imc-aug26'). Rationale: (1) exact-name targeting works for ALL tooling permanently, external included — the class that broke twice on 2026-08-10 cannot recur, rather than being one strip-aware grep away in every future tool; (2) the d5n3/vbzo resolve-by-name mandate is satisfied trivially: _seat_strip_glyph and sibling helpers REMAIN for transition compat and become no-ops on bare names, so both glyphed and bare names resolve during rollout and nothing flag-days; (3) api-stall-recover's new cooldown key already stores glyph-stripped windows, so keys are stable across the transition; (4) handoff-path window scoping keys improve (bare names). Rejected alternative: keep renames + make the fleet idiom strip-aware everywhere — leaves the external-tooling miss structurally reachable forever. Reversibility: config-level (tmux.conf format + tmux-status.sh revert). FALSE-IDLE half: waiting-on-subagents renders 🧠 (Zig's own suggested glyph — no new glyph taste decision taken; a distinct working-glyph may be proposed to Zig later), detected renderer-side from the pane's waiting-on-background-agent markers, with a made-to-fail negative control. Visual result for Zig is unchanged: same glyphs in the window list, now painted by the status format instead of baked into the name.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Handoff — 2026-08-11, builder (Opus 5), dotfiles-ylw2 impl of the 05:33Z ruling

TWO COMMITS, both unpushed, orchestrator merges:
  demesne  aab364c  on worktree-agent-ylw2-1786426652  (worktree /tmp/demesne-agent-aa7288b995dbe2336)
           agents/hooks/tmux-status.sh, agents/hooks/test/test-tmux-status.sh,
           agents/hooks/lib/lexicon-map.sh (comment-only: STRIP_RE is now transition compat)
  dotfiles c38b5ab  on worktree-agent-aa7288b995dbe2336
           tmux/tmux.conf

WHAT LANDED
1. Glyph out of the name: tmux-status.sh sets a per-window `@glyph` option instead of
   renaming. apply_glyph() sets it (or `-u` clears it for idle) on BOTH the live-pane
   path and the childed-pid recovery path.
2. One-time transition: a window whose NAME still carries a strip-era prefix is renamed
   back to bare the first time the hook touches it — and ONLY then. An already-bare name
   is never renamed.
3. tmux.conf renders `#{?#{@glyph},#{@glyph} ,}` in TWO places: the two
   window-status-*-format lines (tmux's own defaults + the slot — the plugin-less path)
   and the two @catppuccin_window_*_text options (the themed path, since catppuccin
   overwrites window-status-format on load). Both plain `set` → idempotent on re-source.
4. False idle: on the `ready` token ONLY, one capture-pane of the visible screen, last 40
   lines, matched against `[Ww]aiting for ([0-9]+ )?background agents?`. On a hit the
   TOKEN itself is downgraded to `working` (not just the paint) so the SSoT/statusline
   and the window can never disagree. A 0.2s settle (env
   CLAUDE_LEXICON_FALSE_IDLE_SETTLE, 0 in tests) removes the client-repaint race.

MARKER CHOICE. The client prints `✻ Waiting for 1 background agent to finish` into its
live status region for exactly this state and clears it when the last agent lands. It is
PLAIN ASCII WORDS — no glyph, no colour, no box-drawing — so it survives font/theme
differences and our own Emoji_Presentation rule. Rejected: the agent-TREE panel
(`◹ subagent  <task>  31s · ↓ 68.3k tokens`) — its leading glyphs are decorative and
version-unstable, and its only word-like token is the AGENT TYPE NAME, which is
caller-chosen; matching on it would be matching on user data.

NO NEW GLYPHS. Only the existing four (all Emoji_Presentation=Yes) are used.

RUNTIME VERIFICATION (all on scratch servers, session names ylw2-scratch / ylw2-smoke /
ylw2-committed — never zig-computer; every server reaped in a trap, /tmp root count
22020 before and after):
  AC1 real harness case — at 05:5xZ the live orchestrator window read `✅ dotfiles` while
      `tmux capture-pane` on its pane showed `✻ Waiting for 1 background agent to finish`.
      That IS the false idle. Re-running the hook's exact detection expression READ-ONLY
      against that pane: MATCH → the hook would render 🧠.
  AC1 scratch, real background process (`sleep 41.937 &`, pid observed alive):
      marker absent → name=[marshal] @glyph=[✅] token=[ready]
      marker present → name=[marshal] @glyph=[🧠] token=[working]
      marker gone again → back to ✅ (recovery direction)
  AC3 exact bare-name targeting: `tmux select-window -t '=ylw2-scratch:marshal'` succeeds
      WHILE decorated (@glyph=🧠, name=marshal). Contrast printed in the same run: with the
      pre-ruling baked-in name the same command answers `can't find window: marshal`.
  AC3 transition: name=[🧠 marshal] → one hook event → name=[marshal] @glyph=[✅].
      Also proven on the childed-pid recovery path (C2b).
  AC4 made-to-fail: same screen through a scratch copy with LEXICON_FALSE_IDLE_RE
      replaced → falls back to ✅; and the SUITE run against that copy goes
      `FAIL: 2/101` (the F2 glyph assertion + the F2 SSoT-token assertion).
  tmux.conf smoke, AS COMMITTED (`git show HEAD:tmux/tmux.conf` → `tmux -f`):
      plugin-less HOME  unset → [0:marshal*]   set → [🧠 0:marshal*]
      real HOME (catppuccin) unset → [… 0 …  marshal ]  set → [… 0 …  🧠 marshal ]
      name stays [marshal]; exact-name select OK.

SUITES: test-tmux-status.sh 58 → 101 cases, green (it ran again inside the pre-commit
gate). Neighbours re-run green: test-seat-resolve.sh 124/124, test-handoff-path.sh 17/17.
`bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` clean on all three changed scripts.

⚠️ MERGE-BLOCKING CONSEQUENCE THE RULING DID NOT ENUMERATE — read before merging.
The ruling covered name RESOLUTION (strip helpers stay, become no-ops). It did not cover
the readers that consume the glyph as a FACT by matching the name's leading character.
Those go blind on a bare name:
  * dotfiles-u1g1 (P1, filed, blocked-by ylw2) — pulse-inject.sh, pulse-retry.sh,
    seat-molt.sh, api-stall-recover.sh, pulse-escalate.sh all gate `send-keys` on the
    NAME's 🔔/🧠/🌀. After this lands they read every window as unblocked and not-busy —
    i.e. they would type into a pane sitting in Zig's open dialog. SAFETY, not cosmetics.
  * dotfiles-3os0 (P2, filed, blocked-by ylw2) — agents/bin/hall's hall_status_glyph
    derives every seat's court-view glyph from the name, so `prefix W` would render every
    seat ✅.
Neither was in scope here (both are explicitly out of my file list), and neither is
touched by these commits. My read: u1g1 should land in the SAME session as this merge,
not merely "next" — the drain runs on a timer.

Also recorded on u1g1: the false-idle half changes what 🧠 MEANS to those guards — a
session waiting on subagents now carries 🧠, so pulse-inject's in-flight guard will defer
a tick it previously injected. Arguably right; needs a deliberate decision, not inheritance.

title: pulse-inject: re-source the claude() wrapper before a cold launch (durable panes hold stale function bodies)
description:
## Context
Follow-on to dotfiles-t6to, and the same class of bug one level up. The wrapper fix
lands in claude-identity-wrapper.sh, which a shell reads ONCE at start. The harness's
durable panes hold zsh processes days old, so they keep executing the function body
they read then — a fix reaches Zig's fresh shells instantly and NEVER reaches the
panes that actually launch pulse ticks.

So pulse-inject now re-sources the wrapper immediately before a COLD launch, making
the launched claude pick up the current wrapper regardless of shell age. Guarded to
a `claude` launcher so a jailed / goose launcher is never prefixed; absent file just
prints a line and the launch proceeds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] re-source sent only when LAUNCH_BASE = claude
- [x] test-pulse-inject.sh 65/65, bash -n + shellcheck clean
- [x] the 11 currently-idle panes reloaded by hand (verified: the live function body
      now contains the new CC_NO_GATEWAY branch)

title: dispatch: an interrupted turn's Agent calls can fire invisibly — the duplicate-architect incident
description:
## Context
2026-08-09: a turn was interrupted mid-parallel-dispatch; ONE Agent call had already fired before the interrupt, invisibly (no tool result reached the transcript). The orchestrator re-dispatched the same task on resume -> two architects on one job; the unknown duplicate was never rescoped when a lane conflict arose, and it PUSHED a full campaign into a store another session owned by Zig's explicit mandate. Three writers on one bead store; two competing campaign plans; reconciliation cost an hour of the owning lane's time.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a turn with multiple parallel Agent dispatches queued
2. Interrupt after the first tool call fires but before results render
3. Resume 'where you left off' and re-dispatch: the duplicate exists, unlisted on your board, working the same contract

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mechanism, not vigilance: before any Agent dispatch, a cheap check of live agents (ListAgents or the task dir) for a running agent whose recent start + worktree branch matches the about-to-be-dispatched work; match -> surface, never silently double-dispatch
- [ ] The resume-after-interrupt doctrine line: FIRST action after any interrupted dispatch turn is an agent inventory, before re-dispatching
- [ ] Candidate home: the /dispatch skill (its anti-pattern list) + a line in AGENTS.md Delegation

## Write target
~/demesne — agents/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md + orchestrator discipline (pre-dispatch duplicate check mechanism).

title: always-loaded: _al_mtime uses GNU-only stat -Lc and swallows the error — every mtime is 0 on every Mac
description:
## Context

`agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh:78`:

```bash
_al_mtime() { stat -Lc %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }
```

`stat -Lc %Y` is **GNU-only**. BSD/macOS `stat` has no `-c`. So on every Mac this function
fails on every call, the `2>/dev/null` hides the error, and `|| echo 0` returns **0 as the
mtime of every file**. Staleness detection is silently degraded fleet-wide on macOS.

This is the repo's own rule #3 doing exactly what the rule warns about: the blanket stderr
suppression is what converts a hard portability failure into a plausible-looking `0`. Rule
#3 already says "the hooks themselves have violated it" — this is another instance.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, in the repo root:

```bash
stat -Lc %Y agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh
# stat: illegal option -- c   ; exit 1

stat -Lf %m agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh
# 1785628117                  ; the BSD form works

bash agents/hooks/test/test-always-loaded-staleness.sh
# FAIL: 9/25 test cases failed
```

All three verified on `zig` 2026-08-01. The 9 failures include "names HOW LONG ago",
"MEMORY.md change is detected", and "project CLAUDE.md change is detected" — i.e. the
staleness feature's core behavior, not edge cases.

## Fix direction

Detect once, define the function accordingly — do not stack two suppressed `stat` calls:

```bash
if stat -Lc %Y . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _al_mtime() { stat -Lc %Y "$1" || echo 0; }   # GNU
else
  _al_mtime() { stat -Lf %m "$1" || echo 0; }   # BSD/macOS
fi
```

Keep a fallback, but the fallback must not be reachable merely because the platform is
macOS. While in here, audit `agents/` for other GNU-only `stat`, `date -d`, `readlink -f`,
and `grep -oP` uses — same class as `dotfiles-1rj5`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_al_mtime` returns a real mtime on macOS AND Linux, both demonstrated with output
- [ ] `test-always-loaded-staleness.sh` passes 25/25 on macOS; show the before (9 failing)
      and after
- [ ] the blanket `2>/dev/null` is gone or narrowed to a genuine existence probe
- [ ] `agents/` audited for other GNU-only coreutils idioms; each hit fixed or annotated
close_reason: Fixed in d063a13 — stat flavour probed once; also found declare -A (bash 4) in stop-always-loaded-check.sh. Verified: 9/25 FAIL -> 25/25 on macOS, 25/25 on Linux. _al_mtime now returns a real epoch, deref through symlink intact.

title: ratelimit-recover: ceiling-stall detection, wait-for-reset, then full unattended restart of everything the ceiling killed
description:
## Context
Zig, live 2026-08-09: hitting the subscription API ceiling (unified 5h window / weekly) stalls the fleet exactly like the gateway outage did — sessions die mid-turn, ticks bounce — and today recovery waits for a human. Wanted: detect the ceiling, wait out the reset, then FULLY restart everything without him. The substrate is fresh: the gateway now captures anthropic-ratelimit-unified-{5h,7d}-utilization per request per tap into request_logs.attributes_json (7qi7/qmrp, live 16:23Z), and the restart machinery already exists — pulse-retry re-fires bounced ticks (staleness-verified per t5fj, landing tonight), api-stall-recover nudges killed sessions, pulse-escalate ladders persistent blocks.

## Design sketch (build against, refine in flight)
Detection, two arms like the outage guards: (a) PROACTIVE — read the gateway request_logs utilization per tap (datetime() trap applies, see infra.md); >= warn threshold → ledger + surface; >= 1.0 or observed 429/limit-shape → declare CEILING for that tap, record the reset time; (b) REACTIVE — pane signature for Claude Code's limit-reached state ("Claude usage limit reached... resets at <time>" and 'API Error: 429' shapes; 429 already bells via harnessd, the prose shape does not — corpus rows will accumulate in api-error-captures.jsonl). Wait-for-reset: parse the reset time (pane prose and/or ratelimit headers) and schedule ONE recovery firing at reset+jitter — transient systemd-run --user timer or the 2-min guard cadence gating on now>=reset; no polling storms. Restart = REUSE, don't duplicate (t5fj rule: one owner per verb): mark the affected loops' bounces as ceiling-class so pulse-retry re-fires them at reset; extend api-stall-recover (or a sibling sharing its libs) so limit-killed panes get the resume nudge once the tap has headroom; never nudge while utilization >= ceiling — the upstream-health gate generalizes from "gateway up" to "gateway up AND tap has headroom".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ceiling detection both arms, per TAP (utilization is per-account); ledgered with the same fail-closed posture as the sibling guards
- [ ] Reset-time derivation with evidence (real header/pane fixtures); one scheduled recovery per ceiling episode, idempotent
- [ ] Recovery re-fires bounced ticks THROUGH pulse-retry's staleness-verified path and nudges limit-killed sessions through the api-stall mechanism — zero new re-fire owners
- [ ] Hermetic suites + named mutants per repo rule 1; harness committed alongside (w4z9 pattern, gate arm included)
- [ ] Coordinates with qmrp/4icj (Works lane owns the utilization capture) — integrate, don't fork

title: POST F2: trim/read race can silently lose a message — fix before channel trim ever gets a caller
description:
## Context
Found by the 5z5n scrutiny pass (SHIP verdict, F2, 2026-08-14). _read_or_peek holds no lock across snapshot->render->cursor-advance (post.sh:649-693) while trim decrements cursors under its own flock (post.sh:538-551). Interleaving read-snapshot -> trim+decrement -> read's stale cursor-write leaves cursor > spool length; the clamp at post.sh:611-612 converts that to skip-to-end. Demonstrated live in a scratch dir: a message published in the window (L3-the-victim) was NEVER delivered — POST_READ_RESULT=empty on both subsequent reads, row still on disk.

Why it is latent, not live: (a) nothing anywhere calls channel trim (grep: only post.sh/test/mutate reference it); (b) corrupt/empty cursors safe-restart from 0; (c) a stale-high cursor self-heals on the first read finding nothing new. The race needs manual-trim + concurrent-read + publish-in-the-window. The post.sh header's 'delivered late, never dropped' overclaims until this is fixed (header caveat being added in the landing wave).

## Steps to Reproduce
Scratch POST_ROOT: subscribe a seat to a channel; publish rows past retention; start a read and capture its snapshot; run channel trim (cursors decremented) before the read writes its cursor; publish one more row; read twice — the new row renders never, POST_READ_RESULT=empty, row present on disk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reader takes the channel lock shared across snapshot->advance, OR cursor advance is a compare-and-swap against the value the snapshot was taken at (scrutiny's two suggested shapes — pick with an argument)
- [ ] The scrutiny repro encoded as a test that FAILS on current code and passes on the fix; a mutant reverting the fix dies on it
- [ ] post.sh header claim restored to unconditional once true
- [ ] dotfiles-dbba (trim caller) stays blocked on this

title: works: pico patch posture — 2 Command Line Tools for Xcode updates pending after the 26.6.1 upgrade
description:
## Context
Surfaced while fixing dotfiles-c9yi (pico-health's stale softwareupdate cache). Once the cache
was correctly re-keyed to the running OS build, the TRUE pending set on pico is not the two macOS
offers the stale cache claimed — those were consumed by the 26.6.1 upgrade at 12:36Z 2026-08-09 —
but two NEW ones that appeared after it:

    Command Line Tools for Xcode 26.5   (Recommended: YES)
    Command Line Tools for Xcode 26.6   (Recommended: YES)

Live evidence, `softwareupdate -l` on pico 2026-08-09 21:3xZ, sw_vers 26.6.1 / 25G76. The
installed CLT is `com.apple.pkg.CLTools_Executables` **15.3.0** (pkgutil), i.e. an Xcode-15-era
toolchain on a macOS 26 box — so these are genuine, not the perpetual-phantom-offer case.

`PICO_UPDATES_MAX` is 0, so pico-health is now degraded (exit 10, failed unit) on this finding
alone and will stay that way until someone decides. That is the checker working — but a watcher
left permanently red is the alarm-fatigue failure its own header warns about, so the decision
should not be left to drift.

## Options
1. **Install** — `softwareupdate -i "Command Line Tools for Xcode 26.6"` on pico. Only 26.6 is
   needed (26.5 is the older of the two offers). No restart action listed. Restores updates=0.
2. **Decline and raise the budget** — set `PICO_UPDATES_MAX=2` in pico-health.service WITH a
   comment saying why (the script's own comment mandates exactly this form, and mandates NOT
   deleting the check). Costs: the budget also masks the next two REAL updates.
3. Leave as is — permanently failed unit. Rejected on sight; it trains readers to skip.

## Decision
NOT MADE — this is a patch-posture call on Zig's machine, deliberately not taken by the agent
that found it (dotfiles-c9yi's dispatch said report, do not schedule).

title: decision needed: should post send try the live socket rung before spooling? (send has no live-rung integration)
description:
## Context
From the 5z5n build: socket-registry.sh degrades live->spool on a dead socket, but post send appends straight to the spool without trying lookup first. The 3-layer taxonomy (7fik, settled) says live urgency is SendMessage and the POST is durable-not-immediate — so the current shape may be CORRECT by doctrine, and the ladder belongs in socket-registry (which already has it), not in post.sh. Alternative: post send becomes the single entry point and internally rides socket-registry's ladder.

## Fork
(a) status quo — post send = spool only; senders wanting the ladder call socket-registry.sh spool (which is what existing seats do). (b) post send tries lookup/live first, falls back to spool. (c) post send delegates to socket-registry entirely and becomes an alias.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One option chosen with the doctrine argument recorded here; loser paths named
- [ ] Whichever lands, exactly ONE documented sender idiom in the comms skill (d54d)

title: study: mud-agent arc — local fine-tuned model plays MUDs 24/7 (FUTURE ARC, deferred)
description:
## Bookmark
Deferred until coding-models foundational work (dotfiles-enx + children) lands. Captures the vision so it doesn't get lost.

## Vision
A local fine-tuned model that plays MUDs (primarily Cleft of Dimensions; also cf, dw, ifmud, chatmud, cthulhumud) on pico 24/7 — no token cost, constant training + reinforcement learning. Novel hybrid harness: tmux MUD pane + chat sidebar where user plays / AI plays / they talk.

## Substrate that already exists (don't rebuild)
- `~/explore/blightmud/` — full Rust fork + 15 project-local skills + per-game refs/ + diary/
- `~/dotfiles/blightmud/` — 7 game-specific lua plugins, mapper with BFS pathfinding, automated login (`creds`/`.env.local`), per-game group isolation, auto-reconnect, password-scrubbed `.ts.log` files
- `coplay.sh` — tmux-pane driver (peek/send/talk to MUD panes). Proto-version of the harness UX.
- Logs in `~/.local/share/blightmud/logs/<host>/*.ts.log` — already password-scrubbed, ready for training data

## Planned research streams (when the arc fires)
1. training-data pipeline (.ts.log → SFT/DPO format; scrubbing of non-password sensitive content; volume estimates per game; structure as state→action pairs)
2. fine-tuning toolchain on M1 Max (MLX LoRA realistic? Or cloud-GPU SFT cycles? Periodic vs continuous training?)
3. hybrid harness architecture (trialogue UX: user-plays / AI-plays / talk-to-AI; command schema; intervention model; intercepts via the existing tmux pane)
4. prior art (Jericho, Microsoft TextWorld, GPT-4 plays Pokémon, Voyager, Cradle, AutoNetHack)

## When to fire
After dotfiles-enx (coding-models stack) is operational and the Ollama-vs-MLX A/B verdict is in. The MUD-agent will inherit whatever serving stack the coding work proves out.

## Re-entry
When ready: `br undefer <this-id>`, create the mud-agent epic, set up `~/explore/mud-agent/`, dispatch 4 study subagents per the planned streams above.

title: offboard: the decision harvest labels '(closed this session)' from status alone, so it mislabels
description:
## Context
Found during a real /offboard in ~/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted on
2026-08-05.

Step 2.5's harvest prints `_(closed this session)_` for any decision bead whose
`status == "closed"`. It never compares the CLOSE TIME to the session window. So
every closed decision inside the (deliberately over-wide) cutoff window gets the
label, including ones closed days before the session started.

Measured in that run:
- session start          2026-08-04T14:08:42Z
- cutoff used            2026-08-01T00:42:40Z  (earlier of session start and marker)
- `bd-91xa`  closed      2026-08-03T17:01:29Z  -> labelled "(closed this session)"

bd-91xa was closed a day and a half BEFORE the session began. The label is
simply false, and it is false in the direction that matters: it invents session
activity that did not happen, in the one artifact whose whole job is telling the
next session what this session did.

This interacts badly with the over-wide cutoff by design. Step 2.5 deliberately
prefers `min(session_start, marker)` because "an over-wide window shows you a
bead you can judge and discard; a too-narrow one shows you nothing." That is the
right call for LISTING. But the `(closed this session)` label is not a listing,
it is an ASSERTION, and it is computed as if the window were exact. The wider the
window, the more confidently wrong the label gets.

The skill already tells the operator to judge the list. It does not warn that the
label itself is unjudged, and an operator transcribing the harvest into the note
verbatim (which is what the skill's own template invites) propagates the error.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run /offboard Step 2.5 in a project where a decision bead was closed after the
cutoff but before the session started. Observe the bead printed with
`_(closed this session)_`.

Compare `updated_at` against the printed session-start line:

    br list --type decision -a --json | jq -r '.issues[] | "\(.id) \(.created_at) \(.updated_at) \(.status)"'

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The label reflects the SESSION WINDOW, not `status`. A closed decision
      should only be marked closed-this-session when its close time is at or
      after session start.
- [ ] `updated_at` is a proxy for close time, not close time itself: a closed
      bead edited later reports the edit. Either accept that and say so in the
      output, or find a real close timestamp. Do not silently treat them as equal.
- [ ] When close time cannot be established, print the bead WITHOUT the label
      rather than guessing. An unlabelled true-positive costs a glance; a
      confident false label costs trust in the whole receipt.
- [ ] The two-line receipt keeps working, and gains nothing that reads as a
      verdict the data does not support.

title: ceiling-triggered tap rollover for a RUNNING seat — today only a LAUNCH can roll, so a working seat just stalls
description:
## Context

Zig, 2026-08-14, deciding to leave consul and the Works on secondary rather than
moving them to the fresh primary: *"Let's get them to exhaust all of secondary
first. Then the new guards would ideally see them hit ceiling and trigger a flow
to molt them on a different tap and continue. That's what I'm expecting us to get
to."*

That end-state does not exist yet, and the gap is specific.

## Baseline — what already works, so nobody rebuilds it

- **Launch-time rollover EXISTS and is well tested.** `claude-identity-wrapper.sh`
  consults `tap-headroom` before a launch and rolls onto the next pool when home
  is at its ceiling, emitting `X-Home-Tap` / `X-Tap-Rollover` and a ledger row
  (tests T20–T27, plus G13–G22 in `test-tap-headroom.sh`). It honours
  `seat_home.<seat>` and refuses to roll onto an unmeasurable pool.
- **Detection exists** — `dotfiles-p31a` alarms at a 0.8 crossing and persists
  `tap-state.json`.
- **The running-session guard is now honest** — `dotfiles-2t8o` makes
  post-tool-model-guard say HOLD when the pinned pool is exhausted, instead of
  ordering an unbuyable switch.
- **Context cycling exists** — `seat-molt.sh` (same process, `/clear`+`/onboard`)
  and `seat-cycle.sh` (process restart with a named model and an injected
  opening prompt).

## The gap

**Every piece is present except the one that joins them.** A seat that is ALREADY
RUNNING when its pool hits the ceiling has no path forward: the wrapper's
failover only runs at launch, so it never re-evaluates; the guard correctly says
"hold"; and holding on an exhausted pool means the seat stops doing useful work
until a human notices. The seat cannot roll itself, because rolling requires a
process restart on a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — and the tool that does that
(`seat-cycle.sh`) kills the very process that would invoke it.

So the missing component is an OUTSIDE-THE-AGENT actor that: notices a running
seat's pool hit its ceiling, picks a legal destination pool, offboards the seat
cleanly, and relaunches it on the new tap with its context anchored — then
reports what it did.

## Design notes

- **This is the same shape as `dotfiles-cbfc`** (post-molt stall watchdog): a
  timer outside the agent that acts when the agent cannot act for itself. Build
  it as a sibling, ideally sharing the same machinery, rather than a second
  bespoke watcher.
- **A rollover must OFFBOARD FIRST.** Restarting a seat mid-arc without a handoff
  note loses everything the context held. `seat-cycle.sh --cmd` can carry the
  opening prompt, but the durable anchor has to be written before the exit.
- **Destination choice is not free.** `taps.conf` `order=` and `seat_home.<seat>`
  already encode preference, and `taps.work.failover: []` deliberately forbids
  the LinearB lane from borrowing personal quota. Reuse that resolution — do not
  invent a second policy.
- **Do not roll onto an unmeasurable pool.** The wrapper already refuses this
  (T21/T24, G16/G21); the same refusal must hold here. Rolling on ignorance is
  worse than stalling.
- **Guard against flapping**: a seat that rolls, exhausts the new pool, and rolls
  back is worse than one that stops. Bound the rolls per seat per window and say
  so out loud when the bound is hit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A running seat whose pool reaches its ceiling is detected without a human.
- [ ] It is offboarded (durable anchor written) BEFORE any restart.
- [ ] It relaunches on a legal destination pool, chosen by the existing
      `taps.conf` resolution, naming the canonical model literal in the relaunch
      (a bare `claude` never trips the wrapper's fable leg).
- [ ] It refuses to roll onto an unmeasurable pool, and refuses to flap.
- [ ] The action is reported to the seneschal and appears in a ledger.
- [ ] Proven by a mutant that dies on the case it names: a ceiling must trigger a
      roll, and an unmeasurable candidate must NOT.

## Notes

⚠️ TONIGHT IS THE EXPERIMENT THAT MOTIVATES THIS BEAD. Zig has deliberately left
consul and the Works on secondary to exhaust it while the seneschal moves to the
fresh primary. **Expect them to STALL at the ceiling rather than roll** — that
stall is the experiment's RESULT and the evidence for this bead, not a failure to
be patched over in the moment. Capture what actually happens: which alarm fired,
what the guard said, how long the seat sat, and whether anything noticed.

Secondary at time of filing: u5h 0.60, weekly 0.59, fable 0.72, climbing ~8/hr
weekly and much faster on the 5h window. Its reset is Fri 23:00 PT.
